deployment-probes.json.description: Machine-readable deployment probes for transport- and operator-posture requirements that are not object-model conformance vectors.

probe.success_condition: for high-security or sovereign profile claims, the completed handshake negotiated TLS group X25519MLKEM768; a peer that does not offer that group is rejected rather than downgraded

cases.name: mention_selector
assertions: selector resolution binds the persisted mention subject_id to the agent DID
controller, slug and original text are audit metadata only
slug changes do not rewrite historical mention targets
ambiguous or unavailable selector claims fail closed

cases.name: ceiling_tighten
assertions: Circle and Strand participation ceilings may only drop bits from their parent
a child that enables act_on_behalf below a disabled parent bit is rejected
a Strand that re-enables a Circle-disabled third-party mention bit is rejected

cases.name: effective_intersection
assertions: effective participation is the bitwise meet of the current governance/deployment ceiling and controller selection
the five controller selection bits are independent and are not derived from requested scope
participation is an additional action gate and never materializes a capability grant
act-on-behalf is denied when the current ceiling disables it
tightening the ceiling immediately disables the corresponding action gate
unknown or stale ceiling source fails closed to no effective participation

cases.name: selection_cas
assertions: Account Authority stores the full controller selection without converting it into authority
target action enforcement intersects the stored selection with current governance
a capped selection bit grants no action and creates no capability grant

cases.name: session_overlay
assertions: session scope_details.participation entries are isomorphic to agent_participation_entry
the overlay is a behavior contract and not an authorization boundary
missing backing capability grant still fails the runtime operation

cases.name: third_party_mention_gate
assertions: when accept_third_party_mention is false, non-controller mentions fan out to no agent delivery artifacts
the controller's own mention still delivers
enabling third-party mention later is non-retroactive
subsequent third-party mentions deliver only after the effective bit is true

cases.name: sidecar_mls_bootstrap_binding
assertions: participant authority transcript contains the sorted unique Realm-scoped desired Agent set
Sidecar genesis is Event-derived and MLS binds the native Sidecar scope
server-generated MLS private state and synthetic GroupInfo digests are forbidden
a concurrent losing provisional snapshot is destroyed

cases.name: sidecar_mls_effective_access
assertions: desired membership alone without accepted Add Commit Welcome and target-device consume remains pending
one active authorized Agent device with matching evidence makes the Agent principal effective
current controller device readiness is evaluated separately from effective_agent_ids
desired membership removal stops delivery before the Remove Commit lands
the Principal Server creates a removal obligation but never fabricates an MLS Commit
the dedicated Sidecar view exposes a sorted non-empty authority frontier without creating Circle membership
the controller persists signed Remove events and advances its post-commit snapshot only after accepted submission

cases.name: sidecar_ensure_idempotent
assertions: ensure operation id remains ak.self.agent.sidecar.command.ensure
ensure capability action matches the operation id
prepare returns a closed new or existing branch with Event-derived sidecar id, source context, Event IDs and canonical unsigned draft bytes
the controller may append proofs but any unsigned-byte, payload, Event ID, source context, or refs.after mutation conflicts with zero writes
create and attach produce no Circle membership Strand or Relation object
sidecar profile id remains ak.profile.agent_sidecar.v1

cases.name: sidecar_eligibility_states
assertions: paused agents are removed from the derived desired set and effective sidecar access
deactivated agents are excluded from effective access and trigger native Sidecar MLS removal
desired and effective Agent sets remain distinct until reconciliation completes
default home policy remains context_realm_preferred

cases.name: sidecar_existence_privacy
assertions: callers without sidecar ensure capability receive sidecar_create_denied
an unauthorized caller never learns Sidecar existence; only the authorized controller receives the fixed new|existing prepare branch

cases.name: sidecar_hosted_projection
assertions: track_name and message_id are rejected in ensure context_ref
one native Sidecar context mapping is reused across all source Strand Tracks
display mode is encrypted per-context view state and defaults to context_merged
each source-routed exchange has an independent device-local Event-fold cache and stable anchor order
sidecar-native events create no source echo
merged projection deduplicates the private request Event by Event id

cases.name: sidecar_multi_agent_publish
assertions: ensure, write, exchange control, and publish capability actions all remain Agent Sidecar scoped
the sidecar capability action quartet contains no duplicates and exchange control is controller-only

cases.name: sidecar_exchange_binding_closed_loop
assertions: the routed request event carries a role=request binding with a full request_context, completion_policy=coordinator, and a valid coordinator assignment
the agent runtime learns the exchange identity only from the decrypted request binding; exchange projection is never Account Data or an account-stream object
the runtime executes only when its own principal is addressed, active, eligible, effective, MLS-ready, the Event is the canonical request for exchange_id, and that exchange_id is not already consumed
the runtime persists exchange_id to canonical request_event_id; a later request Event reusing the same exchange_id fails closed and cannot execute again

a validated role=user_facing_response binding with matching exchange_id, request_event_id, causal request ref, native Sidecar scope, source context, and addressed actor is the only path into user_facing_response_event_ids
the accepted request folds to delivered; validated role=internal events keep that state and stay non-echo without producing errors
wrong exchange_id, wrong request_event_id, wrong Sidecar scope, missing causal ref, non-addressed actor, unknown role, and ak:message: shaped request references all fail closed to non-echo
a role=request binding on an agent-authored event is invalid and never consumed
duplicate delivery of the same response event id appends exactly once and the response set keeps canonical (event HLC, event id) byte order

a non-coordinator completes_exchange request never closes the exchange; a valid coordinator request causes the controller to author a durable close control Event, and only that Event advances terminal state

cases.name: sidecar_exchange_projection_recovery
assertions: after local cache loss the controller rebuilds from accepted private Event history without redelivering the agent request
agent-authored role=request bindings are excluded from rebuild by consumer-side actor validation
independent controller devices replaying validation over the same private history produce bit-identical response sets, canonical order, and status
incomparable local folded frontiers are never resolved by HLC or LWW; devices backfill and fold the joined accepted history
folded_frontier carries canonical maximal causal heads, a digest of all contributing Event ids, and max HLC; it is local cache validation metadata only
close or cancel with a non-empty captured response set produces complete; close empty produces controller_closed_empty and cancel empty produces controller_cancelled
agent or control events concurrent with and not causally covered by the winning terminal basis remain private audit history but do not enter the terminal projection

same-sequence control siblings use event-digest bytewise maximum, the first effective terminal control absorbs later controls, and reassignment is valid only before terminal with a matching expected coordinator
delivered requires empty responses, responding/complete require non-empty responses, failed requires empty responses plus failure_reason_code, and non-failed states forbid failure_reason_code

cases.name: sidecar_exchange_binding_containment
assertions: plaintext metadata carrying sidecar_exchange_binding, the binding schema id, or an exchange_id value is a schema_violation hard reject on the wire
binding or control plaintext decrypted from a non-Sidecar scope is invalid and never rendered or folded
explicit publish output is an ordinary shared event carrying no binding, exchange_id, sidecar_id, or private locator
publish output, shared history, Account Data, push previews, notifications, and public telemetry have zero hits for exchange_id, binding schema id, and control schema id

cases.name: sidecar_context_locator_recovery
assertions: all sidecar-list and event-scan pages complete before any locator becomes echo-eligible
only a controller-authored accepted sidecar.context.attach recovers the native context mapping
the mapping points to an already existing canonical source context and creates no Relation
duplicate or conflicting candidates remain unresolved and all exchange events remain non-echo
unauthorized callers receive an indistinguishable empty result

cases.name: sidecar_canonical_sibling_digest
assertions: same actor_seq siblings are decided by the bytewise maximum canonical accepted Event envelope digest
reversing arrival and database order does not change the winner
event id and HLC order are explicit counterexamples and cannot substitute for event_digest

cases.name: sidecar_union_history_frontier
assertions: incomparable device histories trigger full pagination and a refold over their set union
event_ids contains every maximal causal head rather than an HLC winner
event_set_digest covers the sorted unique ids of every participating Event
a missing page or invisible head preserves the old cache and marks backfill pending

cases.name: sidecar_non_disclosure_surface_matrix
assertions: every listed surface has zero disclosure of every forbidden class
private state changes do not alter shared counts ordering unread watch notification or search results
the server neither decrypts nor persists exchange plaintext or fold input

cases.name: sidecar_revoke_fail_closed
assertions: accepted revoke pause or deactivate immediately stops new addressing and delivery
runtime eligibility and authorization freshness are revalidated immediately before execution
old keys sessions and cached projections cannot authorize a new write or response
lifecycle changes never create an implicit exchange terminal

cases.name: sidecar_explicit_publish
assertions: without controller confirmation publication produces zero shared durable output
one confirmation produces exactly one ordinary shared Event from an allowlist builder
the shared Event contains none of the forbidden private identifiers history or locators

cases.name: sidecar_accepted_request_identity
assertions: the runtime persists exchange_id to the accepted request Event id only
response binding request_event_id and top-level after ref equal the same accepted Event id
the controller fold accepts only that Event id
message local-intent and unaccepted Event identities all fail closed

cases.name: sidecar_hosted_ui_matrix
assertions: Chrome and Edge execute the full cross-product against a stable build
realm tree sidecar view and private history seed are asserted before product checks
track and mode switching preserves scroll editor and draft state
switching is incremental and does not replay full history

cases.name: agent_provision
assertions: agent provision operation id remains ak.self.agent.command.provision
agent provision capability action matches the operation id
provision fails without a controller recovery policy before creating any Agent DID, PCR, or grant side effect

controller publishes PCR-independent DID entry 0; prepare validates an exact accepted controller_authority_instance, verifies full_id and returns exact initial_resolution plus allocation without generating DID/private keys or durable Agent/PCR/accountability/selector/pairing/grant side effects, and MUST NOT allocate principal_control_realm_id
the controller recomputes requested_scope_digest and uses the Arkret SDK canonical authoring API for one ak.agent.provision Event
the provision payload carries no nested proof; the Event envelope proof is the only signature
the provision Event passes the ordinary Event proof verifier and admission pipeline; a service-authored or dev-proof substitute is rejected in every mode
one reducer transaction atomically projects provision, accountability and selector cells; partial projection is impossible
an exact commit retry identified by the allocation and one Event id returns the original outcome, while an Event-id byte mismatch conflicts
a crash is recovered by replaying the same Event and never by minting replacement Event ids or proofs
complete returns the Agent PCR binding with pcr_recovery pending and does not pre-write an Agent profile or runtime key authorization
requested_scope is required, immutable and records a global hard ceiling rather than a grant
the accepted Agent DID service entry is a closed four-field binding that fixes only the domain-separated requested_scope digest and contains no complete scope
pairing and grant admission require a controller-signed verifier-bound private requested_scope disclosure whose digest matches the accepted-at DID commitment
provisioning writes one durable fact whose projections include accountability and selector and never materializes Realm grants
a narrower per-key scope is accepted while a wider action/resource scope or omitted mandatory provision constraint is rejected
grant attach accepts a complete controller-authored ak.capability.grant EventInitialSubmission and submits its exact bytes through ordinary Event admission
the ordinary CapabilityGrantBody has no inner proof or signature; the Event envelope proof is the sole durable issuer signature and service signing or proof fallback is rejected
a narrower Realm grant is accepted while an omitted action or out-of-ceiling content resource is rejected with agent_grant_exceeds_requested_scope
missing accountability grants fail with accountability_grant_missing

cases.name: agent_pcr_genesis_forward_declaration
assertions: prepare returns no principal_control_realm_id; the controller derives it from the locally frozen genesis create
the accepted provision returns status=awaiting_pcr_genesis and publishes no DID service entry, pairing handle or list/get visibility
a crash between the two submissions is recovered by replaying the same frozen create bytes; replaying commit returns the same awaiting_pcr_genesis outcome and never authors a second provision
the genesis create is submitted separately and carries no refs entry naming the provision
genesis admission reverse-looks-up an accepted ak.agent.provision whose payload.principal_control_realm_id equals retype of this create event_id
retype of the accepted genesis event_id equals the declared principal_control_realm_id byte for byte
the whole sequence derives without event_id_digest_mismatch, which is the constructibility proof for the named encoding.md 6.0.1 class C exemption

accepting the genesis returns awaiting_did_binding and keeps the Agent invisible; only accepting controller-signed continuous DID entry 1 moves ak.component.agent.status.v1 from uninitialized to active, publishes the pairing handle and returns status=complete
an ak.realm.create whose purpose is not managed_agent_control triggers neither the agent-status write nor the reverse look-up

cases.name: agent_pcr_genesis_same_batch_rejected
cases.submission: ak.agent.provision and its declared managed_agent_control ak.realm.create in one ordered submit batch

cases.name: agent_pcr_genesis_without_declaration_rejected
cases.submission: managed_agent_control ak.realm.create whose retyped event_id no accepted ak.agent.provision declares

cases.name: two_provisions_declaring_one_realm_id_rejected
cases.submission: second ak.agent.provision declaring an already claimed principal_control_realm_id

cases.name: agent_provisioning_abandonment
assertions: the challenge is only issuable while the provision is accepted and its declared managed Agent PCR genesis is not
the confirmation presents fresh credentials and rejects the ones presented when the challenge was issued

one transaction consumes the challenge, releases the agent_slug selector claim and the principal_control_realm_id claim and records the tombstone / audit reservation; any step failing means zero writes
after release the same agent_slug is claimable again by a new provision from the same controller
the abandoned principal_control_realm_id is never reused by a later provision
the accepted ak.agent.provision Event stays in the controller PCR history and is neither deleted nor rewritten
replaying the same request_id returns a byte-identical terminal outcome and exactly one tombstone exists

cases.name: agent_provisioning_abandonment_without_challenge_rejected
cases.submission: abandon_provisioning with no previously issued challenge

cases.name: agent_provisioning_abandonment_replayed_credentials_rejected
cases.submission: abandon_provisioning presenting the same credentials used to issue the challenge

cases.name: agent_provisioning_abandonment_consumed_challenge_rejected
cases.submission: abandon_provisioning reusing a consumed challenge with different canonical intent

cases.name: agent_provisioning_abandonment_after_genesis_rejected
cases.submission: abandon_provisioning after the managed Agent PCR genesis was accepted between issuance and confirmation

cases.name: agent_provisioning_abandonment_replay_has_one_tombstone
cases.submission: abandon_provisioning replayed with the same request_id after success

cases.name: agent_requested_scope_privacy
assertions: the public did:webvh history never contains the complete requested_scope, resource selectors, or constraints
the disclosure validates against agent-requested-scope-disclosure.schema.json and its controller proof payload_digest
the verifier consumes request_id and challenge once and rejects replay, wrong audience, stale proof, and digest mismatch
accepted disclosure is stored only as encrypted verifier-private evidence keyed by agent, digest, verifier, and audience

cases.name: agent_pairing_expiry
assertions: agent key-pair operation id remains ak.gate.account.command.pair_agent_key
expired pairing requests fail with pairing_request_expired
DID mismatch, invalid proof, expired pairing, and deactivated agent errors are all pinned

cases.name: agent_runtime_key_binding
assertions: same stable binding retry retains approval_request_id and notification id and emits action update
a runtime persists and reuses one local key binding for an open pairing_request_id across process restart and channel delete/recreate
a runtime that loses the bound key stops and renews pairing instead of overwriting the pending request with a different key
different stable binding on one open pairing_request_id fails with HTTP 409 agent_runtime_request_conflict without replacement
the possession proof is a closed Ed25519 shape and binds the authoritative pairing handle, pairing secret, service DID, stable runtime binding and no-more-than-five-minute window
public_key.kid, request verification_method and proof verification_method are byte-identical DID URLs controlled by the Agent
final approval recomputes the current stable binding and full ak.agent.key_pairing_request_binding.v1 digest from persistence
the controller approval digest binds the current proof_of_possession_digest so a same-binding proof refresh invalidates a stale prompt
a producer floors typed instants to UTC milliseconds before serializing pairing expiry, and the binding hashes that exact canonical wire string
microsecond and offset wire spellings are schema violations and are rejected before pairing request digest verification
a stale controller approval fails closed
pairing code, proof of possession and attestation bytes never appear in the account notification delta
the authenticated pending_runtime_key_request controller projection is closed and omits pairing_code, requested_scope_disclosure and authorize_event

cases.name: agent_managed_pcr_separation
assertions: agent DID document has one ArkretPrincipalControlRealm service entry binding a non-controller PCR id
agent PCR genesis created_by and notary equal the agent DID and both encryption floors are e2ee_required
controller-authored agent PCR events use actor_id equal to agent DID, executed_by equal to controller DID, and a verified authorization_ref
delegated admission fails when the accepted-at delegation purpose or resource scope does not cover the target Event kind and Agent PCR
agent profile, key authorization and lifecycle events land in the agent PCR
one agent provision Event and its accountability and selector projections land in the controller PCR
pairing requests and approval notifications land in neither PCR
a non-PCR Realm at either principal_control_realm_id fails closed

cases.name: agent_repairing_supersede
assertions: renew_pairing accepts an active or paused agent without changing lifecycle intent, existing keys, or grants before pairing completes
renew_pairing returns pairing_mode replacement and the current pcr_recovery projection without resetting it to pending
issuing a new pairing handle makes every previous handle permanently unresolvable
one controller-signed authorize event carries an exact supersedes set and atomically replaces every prior active authorization dot with reason superseded_by_repairing
stale, partial, extra, or wrong authorized_event_ref supersedes sets fail closed without changing any key
sessions issued from superseded keys fail closed within the revocation freshness window
replacement handle expiry has no side effects and never yields pairing_expired on a previously keyed agent
renew_pairing on a deactivated agent fails with agent_deactivated

cases.name: agent_managed_pcr_recovery
assertions: provision returns the Agent PCR binding with pcr_recovery pending and never pre-authorizes a runtime key
the controller E2EE client, never the server, generates Agent PCR MLS private state
managed Agent PCR MLS state is stored in a controller-owned mls_history envelope encrypted to the controller recovery public key
public contents, plaintext keybag, and AEAD AAD carry the same canonical managed principal binding set
pairing commits only while the active backup tail covers the current Agent PCR Seal frontier and MLS epoch
an accepted pairing advances the Agent PCR frontier, makes recovery stale, and requires a post-commit backup tail before the next pairing
pending, stale, missing, cross-actor, secret-storage-key-only, or binding-mismatched recovery states fail with agent_pcr_recovery_not_ready without consuming the pairing handle
Agent runtime private keys are never backed up or cloned and replacement always generates a fresh local key
a Native Personal Agent has no independent human-facing mnemonic; controller recovery restores PCR continuity but does not bypass current delegation or capability checks

cases.name: agent_longevity_no_expiry
assertions: agent key authorization without expires_at is accepted and remains valid until revoked
same-key re-authorization atomically removes all observed authorization dots and adds one replacement dot
concurrent same-key re-authorizations fold to the intersection of scope and audience and the earliest finite expiry
accountability grant without expires_at is accepted and verifies accountable_principal_ids
low and medium risk agent grants without temporal constraints are accepted
session issuance long after provisioning succeeds while the chain is unrevoked
pause fails closed new sessions and invalidates issued sessions within an independent freshness window of at most 60 seconds
high risk agent grants without expires_at fail with failed_precondition

cases.name: agent_controller_lifecycle
assertions: agent lifecycle operation ids retain canonical namespaces
active to paused to active to deactivated is accepted
deactivated is terminal and resume fails with agent_deactivated
pause while paused fails with agent_paused
deactivation accepts one lifecycle Event and rejects client-authored key or grant revocation bundles
deactivated is a mandatory AND gate for every runtime key, session, pairing handle, grant, KeyPackage, presence and new Event path within sixty seconds
agent views expose lifecycle, readiness blockers and expiring presence as three orthogonal axes
offline never means deactivated, unpaired or direct-conversation missing

cases.name: agent_act_on_behalf
assertions: controller approvals are single-use
approval replay fails with approval_already_consumed
act-on-behalf without authorization_ref, participation, matching grant scope, or fresh approval fails closed
unauthorised sidecar creation fails with sidecar_create_denied

cases.name: agent_session_grant_replay
assertions: session grant issue operation id remains ak.gate.account.command.issue_session_grant
agent_key_proof challenge replay, audience mismatch, and bad signature fail closed
agent session branch rejects invalid proofs, DID mismatch, paused agents, and deactivated agents
accountability grant absence is pinned as accountability_grant_missing

cases.name: agent_human_approval_required
assertions: error details validate against agent_human_approval_error_details
approval_request_id is opaque and is the only runtime-visible correlation handle
controller approval completes out of band
agent retry references accepted approval evidence
no interactive human challenge is returned to the agent runtime

invariants: persist_ledger_before_first_effect
ledger_binds_principal_service_and_admin_actor
exact_replay_resumes_same_ledger
conflicting_replay_has_no_effect
accepted_or_duplicate_steps_are_never_reexecuted
rejected_step_cannot_be_skipped
first_accepted_revoke_event_fences_future_applet_writes
complete_requires_every_planned_step_terminal_success

kdf_contract.expand_with_label_info: uint16_be(Length) || varint(len(utf8("MLS 1.0 " || Label))) || utf8("MLS 1.0 " || Label) || varint(len(Context)) || Context

cases.name: content_key_derivation_sha256_aes128gcm
cases.note: aead_nk is AEAD.Nk of the ciphersuite the group actually negotiated, per encryption-and-audit.md 2.10.1, and 2.10.2 requires aead_profile to be an ACTIVE canonical_id of mls-ciphersuite-registry.json. The only active row is AES-128-GCM, so Nk is 16. The length is an ExpandWithLabel input, so a 16-byte key is not a prefix of a 32-byte one - an implementation following the normative text can never reproduce the latter.

invariants: every mutation MUST produce bytes different from the registered golden value or be rejected before encryption
a content key is scoped to exactly one MLS group epoch and MUST NOT be reused after a Commit

expected.note: threshold controls recovery authorization; eager sealing still targets every configured recovery recipient before GC

receipt policy digest and release eligibility proof agree

request_canonical_digest must cover principal_id, device_id, requested_scope, and audience

fixtures/calendar-notification-fixture.j.description: Server-side schedule notification derivation for ak.profile.calendar_notification_dispatch.v1: one notification per patch per receiver, the pre/post roster union candidate set filtered before generation, the blind-wakeup path for encrypted schedules, and the rule that RSVP writes derive no schedule notification. It deliberately excludes the client authoring, recurrence and RSVP vectors so that requiring this fixture does not pull the client vector closure into a server profile.

notes: These vectors pin CBA dual-plane semantics. DataEvent vectors use signed kind + payload + scope_ref + seal_ref and never use preconditions. Control Move vectors use signed kind + payload + scope_ref + seal_basis and may use preconditions. Every cell write is receiver-projected from the registered reducer contract.

Seal delta entries reference only newly sealed control-plane event digests. Cumulative coverage is derived from predecessor_refs[] plus delta[]. DataEvent digests may appear in data_event_set_root / data_view_root observations, but those roots do not confer control-plane finality.
Cell ids follow ak:cell:ak.component.<facet-path>.v<n>:<subject>; subject placeholders use dot-safe strings to keep examples unambiguous.

vectors.name: data_event_accepts_without_seal_finality
vectors.description: A message DataEvent is locally accepted when signature, actor chain, seal_ref, auth_context, capability and data-plane Lattice validation pass. It does not wait for Seal coverage.

vectors.name: data_event_observation_does_not_seal
vectors.description: A Seal may observe DataEvents through data_event_set_root, but the query grade is observed, not sealed.

vectors.name: control_move_requires_seal_basis_and_seal
vectors.description: A membership ban Control Move uses seal_basis for authorization and preconditions. It remains control_pending until covered by a valid Seal.

vectors.name: same_batch_does_not_advance_authorization_basis
vectors.description: An Event earlier in the same submit batch may resolve bytes and causal refs for later Events, but it cannot create a grant used by a later Event in the same batch.

vectors.name: data_plane_conflict_returns_bottom_without_winner
vectors.description: Concurrent incompatible writes to a data-plane cas_register cell return structured bottom. The reducer must not choose a winner by HLC, actor id, arrival order, or Seal observation order.

vectors.name: seal_delta_excludes_data_event_digest
vectors.description: A Seal delta contains newly sealed control-plane event digests only. Including a DataEvent digest in delta is a seal validation failure.

vectors.name: open_set_compaction_preserves_control_roots
vectors.description: A signed compaction Seal must be equivalent to the deterministic control view of its predecessors and preserve control_event_set_root, state_root and fault diagnostics.

vectors.name: seal_canonical_no_self_reference
vectors.description: Seal canonical bytes are computed from signed top-level body fields only. The Seal id and notary_signature are excluded from the transcript.

vectors.name: cas_mixed_basis
vectors.description: cas_register writes on a non-initial settled value require an explicit CBA basis; null-basis blind overwrites fail closed.

expected.note: Per event-auth-state-resolution.md section 9.3.1 the projector copies the whole-value head_eq into op.from, so the join sees the v1 -> v2 supersession chain and settles on v2 instead of bottom. The blind write above deliberately has no from: it forms a second chain head and the defensive join stays bottom.

vectors.name: auth_context_epoch_pinning_reject
vectors.description: Verifier evaluates key and credential epoch validity at the event seal_ref, not only against the current DID document.

vectors.name: seal_compaction_interval_enforced
vectors.description: Realm seal_compaction_max_interval_ms is a structural obligation: valid full-coverage compaction enables bootstrap, mismatched coverage rejects, and overdue compaction raises health alarms.

vectors.name: inclusion_list_obligation
vectors.description: A multi-signer notary Seal must discharge valid inclusion-list obligations by inclusion, signed reject, or pre-state verification failure proof.

vectors.name: notary_fault_equivocation_quarantine
vectors.description: Two different Seals signed by the same notary in the same slot authorize public equivocation evidence, quarantine the fork, and reject later Seals from that signer.

vectors.name: sealed_control_move_full_digest_collision
vectors.description: Two different canonical preimages recompute to the same event_id under one suite, and the colliding Control Move is already covered by an accepted Seal. Unlike notary equivocation, the sibling event_digest values are byte-identical, so no digest can name the winner.

colliding_identity.note: variant_a and variant_b share this event_id and event_digest byte for byte

resolution_cases.name: cross_suite_discriminator_is_diagnostic_only
resolution_cases.note: blake3 is profile-gated v1_optional_interop, so a peer may be unable to verify it

vectors.name: threshold_forensic_attribution
vectors.description: Threshold notary forensic_attribution must match the quorum-intersection arithmetic rule.

vectors.name: open_set_concurrent_revocation_fail_closed
vectors.description: A DataEvent whose seal_ref is locally valid is re-evaluated against the joined multi-leaf control view when a concurrent revocation branch is observed.

cases.name: late_revocation_leaf_retroactive_removal
cases.description: Ordered sequence, not a single joined-view snapshot: E is first accepted and its reducer-projected write is materialized into data cell X under the initial joined view that has NOT yet joined the revoke leaf R. Dependent event D is then accepted with E as a critical causal dependency and materializes a projected write into data cell Y. R arrives later; once joined, E loses seal_ref authorization, so E and the complete direct/indirect dependency closure rooted at E MUST leave accepted projection inputs. The final state MUST equal that of a receiver that joined {S0,R} from the start, independent of arrival order.

vectors.name: actor_chain_realm_scope
vectors.description: Actor sequence and sibling detection are scoped to (realm_id, actor_id); equal actor_seq values in different Realms do not create a fork.

vectors.name: conflict_recovery_move
vectors.description: A bottom=reject control cell recovers only through a sealed ak.state.conflict_recovery Control Move with recovery_capability and a pre-conflict state_witness. The recovered value is the signed payload.resolved_value, projected by the registered cell_ref + reset form; no other kind may declare that form.

expected.note: reset is legal only on a cell already in bottom; on any other state the write is rejected, so recovery cannot be used as a general overwrite channel.
the state_witness must witness the cell named by payload.target_cell; witnessing a different cell proves nothing about the one being reset.

vectors.name: same_seal_bottom_reject_serialization
vectors.description: Notary admission serializes mutually exclusive writes to one bottom=reject cell within a single proposed Seal, while preserving bottom semantics across unreachable Seal leaves.

vectors.name: realm_alias_single_carrier
vectors.description: A Realm alias has exactly one wire carrier. ak.realm.alias sets ak.component.realm.alias.v1 (cas_register, cell_subject=null, bottom=reject); the closed realm genesis/profile objects carry no alias, and no implementation may keep a fallback input chain over several shapes.

expected.create_time_alias_shape: registered conditional alias slot in the same ordered atomic Realm bootstrap unit
expected.rename_shape: successor set on the same cell carrying whole-value head_eq
expected.release_shape: explicit {tombstone:true} set; effective resolution treats it as absence and the Realm stays addressable only by realm_id
expected.resolution_source: resolve_realm / resolve_target / ak.edge.applet.realm.read.resolve read the effective cell; directory rows are a projection, not a second source of truth

fixtures/cursor-negative-fixture.json.description: Machine-readable negative cursor vectors mirrored from zh/conformance/conformance-vectors.md section 1.16. Complements the positive opaqueness vector ak.vector.encoding.cursor_opaque.core.v1: every case below is a schema-valid-looking ak:cursor: token that a conformant receiver MUST reject before advancing any server-side state. reason_code values are stable codes from error-code-registry.json (invalid_cursor is surfaced under top-level invalid_param).

cases.name: oversized_token
cases.violation: encoded token exceeds the 4KB body cap before any decode work

cases.name: invalid_base64url
cases.violation: token payload is not unpadded base64url

cases.name: malformed_json
cases.violation: decoded body is not valid JSON

cases.name: duplicate_json_key
cases.violation: duplicate JSON key violates canonical JSON ingress rules

cases.name: non_nfc_string
cases.violation: decoded issued_at string value is not Unicode NFC (it carries U+0065 U+0301 instead of the NFC composed form U+00E9); canonical JSON ingress MUST reject. The raw body is intentionally not inlined here so this fixture file itself stays NFC-clean; the base64url token is the authoritative input.

cases.name: inline_positions_rejected
cases.violation: v1 core cursor body carries only the opaque handle; inline position state (s) violates the closed {v,purpose,issued_at,expires_at,h} schema

cases.name: unsupported_version
cases.violation: cursor version is not in supported_versions (v1 core supports only "1")

cases.name: handle_too_short
cases.violation: stateful handle h is shorter than the 22-character minimum (>=128 bits of entropy)

cases.name: non_canonical_timestamp
cases.violation: issued_at must be a canonical UTC Z timestamp; the +00:00 offset form is rejected

cases.name: stream_ttl_exceeds_cap
cases.violation: expires_at - issued_at exceeds the stream-purpose hard TTL cap of 7 days (encoding.md section 8.3 rule 12)

cases.name: barrier_ttl_exceeds_cap
cases.violation: expires_at - issued_at exceeds the barrier-purpose hard TTL cap of 1 hour (encoding.md section 8.3 rule 12)

cases.name: missing_millisecond_fraction
cases.violation: issued_at omits the mandatory three millisecond digits; whole seconds MUST use .000Z

cases.name: retired_t_x_fields_rejected
cases.violation: retired t/x fields are forbidden; issued_at/expires_at are required and no compatibility reader exists

vectors.fixture_freshness_note: All timestamps are pinned so every case stays deterministically rejectable for the spec lifetime: expired cases use year-2020 values (always past), TTL-cap and negative-TTL cases use year-2099 x values (not expired before 2099) with a violation that is checked before any now-relative comparison could differ.
rules: receivers MUST reject every case before advancing subscription position, barrier wait, or any other server-side state

syntax / schema / TTL-bound failures surface as top-level invalid_param with reason_code invalid_cursor; expiry uses cursor_expired; handle lookup or cross-binding failures (not covered here, they need server state) use cursor_integrity_invalid
receivers MUST enforce the 4KB cap on the encoded token before spending base64 or JSON parsing work

TTL bound checks MUST validate issued_at and expires_at well-formedness first, then issued_at <= expires_at, then issued_at not in the future beyond clock skew, then expires_at - issued_at against the per-purpose cap, so a corrupt issued_at cannot bypass the cap

fixtures/did-webvh-witness-fixture.json.description: Conformance vectors for the did:webvh witness rail (identity-did.md §3.4.1-§3.4.3). Two layers are exercised and MUST NOT be conflated. cryptographic_vectors[] contains a field-exact, externally sourced did:webvh v1.0 log and did-witness.json whose entry hash, controller proof and witness proof MUST all be recomputed and verified. method_policy_cases[] cover structural and policy semantics: witness policy is read only from parameters.witness = {threshold, witnesses:[{id}]} whose ids are did:key values that MUST decode to cryptosuite-compatible public keys during parameter validation, proofs come only from the separate did-witness.json keyed by versionId, and every malformed, aliased, unavailable or under-threshold condition fails closed with a registered code instead of degrading to threshold 0. schema_validation_cases[] cover the Arkret-layer carrier: ak.schema.did_webvh_witness_receipt.v1 is a distinct object family from ak.schema.identity_receipt.v1 and the two are returned as a tagged union discriminated on schema. The receipt is a cacheable, auditable observation record; it never substitutes for verifying the standard did-witness.json proofs, the entry hash chain or the controller proof. Placeholder values occur only in the explicitly structural cases; they MUST NOT be substituted for cryptographic_vectors[].

method_policy_cases.name: standard_witness_parameter_is_the_only_policy_source
method_policy_cases.notes: The did:webvh 1.0 shape. threshold is within 1..witnesses.length and every witness id is a unique did:key. This is the only structure an Arkret verifier reads as witness policy.

method_policy_cases.name: absent_witness_parameter_means_no_method_witness
method_policy_cases.notes: Absence is not malformation. A DID that never declared method witnesses is legitimately unwitnessed at the method layer; deployment policy may still refuse to use it on high-risk paths, but that is an overlay decision and not a parse failure.

method_policy_cases.name: aliased_witness_keys_fail_closed
method_policy_cases.notes: The single most dangerous case. A log carrying witnesses / witness_threshold instead of witness was produced against a non-standard dialect, so the true policy is unknown. Reading it as no policy would silently turn a DID that declares two witnesses into one that requires none, which is a fail-open, not a compatibility fallback.

method_policy_cases.name: arkret_overlay_fields_inside_method_parameter_fail_closed
method_policy_cases.notes: profileMinThreshold / structuredWitnesses / watcherEvidence / maxAgeSeconds are Arkret deployment policy. Inside method history they force external verifiers to cope with unregistered keys, make policy rotation require rewriting DID history, and let a holder self-declare both the threshold and the evidence that satisfies it.

method_policy_cases.name: non_did_key_witness_id_fails_closed
method_policy_cases.notes: did:webvh 1.0 constrains witness identifiers to did:key. Any other form describes something that is not a method witness.

method_policy_cases.name: undecodable_did_key_witness_fails_closed
method_policy_cases.notes: The witness id is shaped like a did:key and passes any pattern check, but its multibase payload does not decode to a well-formed public key compatible with the log's Data Integrity cryptosuite. did:webvh 1.0 requires this to be caught during parameter validation, not deferred to signature verification: an undecodable key that is allowed to occupy a threshold slot silently hollows out the threshold, because that slot can never be satisfied by any proof.

method_policy_cases.name: threshold_above_witness_count_fails_closed
method_policy_cases.notes: An unsatisfiable threshold is a declaration error, not an instruction to ignore witnessing.

method_policy_cases.name: duplicate_witness_id_fails_closed
method_policy_cases.notes: A repeated id would let one key be counted twice toward threshold.

method_policy_cases.name: missing_witness_proofs_file_fails_closed
method_policy_cases.notes: Policy is declared but did-witness.json is unreachable or has no entry for this versionId. Unavailable evidence is not absent policy.

method_policy_cases.name: proof_from_unlisted_signer_does_not_count
method_policy_cases.notes: A syntactically fine proof signed by a key outside parameters.witness proves nothing about the declared witness set.

method_policy_cases.name: fewer_valid_proofs_than_threshold_fails_closed
method_policy_cases.notes: One valid proof against a declared threshold of two. Effective threshold is the strictest intersection of the method threshold and the deployment minimum, so a holder can raise this bar but never lower it.

method_policy_cases.name: holder_declared_threshold_cannot_lower_deployment_minimum
method_policy_cases.notes: The log declares threshold 1 while deployment policy requires 2. Effective threshold is 2; otherwise any holder could opt out of the deployment's witnessing requirement by editing its own log.

method_policy_cases.name: same_controlling_organization_does_not_satisfy_distinct_requirement
method_policy_cases.notes: Two distinct witness keys, one operator. Counting keys instead of controlling organizations would let a single operator satisfy a two-organization requirement alone, which empties the requirement of meaning.

method_policy_cases.name: evidence_older_than_max_age_fails_closed
method_policy_cases.notes: Age is measured from observed_at, not from when an Arkret receipt was signed. Re-signing an old observation does not refresh it.

schema_validation_cases.name: did_webvh_witness_receipt_valid
schema_validation_cases.notes: Binds subject DID, exact versionId, witness did:key, its controlling organization and the observation instant. The issuer service DID is the trust root for the receipt itself and is unrelated to the subject DID's controller.

schema_validation_cases.name: registry_consensus_receipt_stays_a_separate_family
schema_validation_cases.notes: The pre-existing family, unchanged. Its witness_role describes a replication role inside a DID registry consensus group and it binds seq + head_event_digest; it says nothing about did:webvh method witnesses. Both families ride ak.root.identity.receipts.read.list and are told apart only by the schema constant.

schema_validation_cases.name: witness_receipt_without_expiry_is_invalid
schema_validation_cases.notes: An Arkret-layer cache record without an expiry is indistinguishable from a permanent assertion, which is exactly how stale witness evidence outlives the state it described.

schema_validation_cases.name: witness_receipt_without_controlling_organization_is_invalid
schema_validation_cases.notes: Distinct-organization policy counts organizations, not keys. A receipt that cannot name the controlling organization cannot be counted toward that requirement, so the field is required rather than optional.

schema_validation_cases.name: non_did_key_witness_in_receipt_is_invalid
schema_validation_cases.notes: witness_did mirrors parameters.witness.witnesses[].id, which did:webvh 1.0 constrains to did:key. A receipt naming another form is describing something that is not a method witness.

schema_validation_cases.name: arkret_overlay_field_on_receipt_is_invalid
schema_validation_cases.first_expected_error: $: Additional properties are not allowed ('max_age_seconds' was unexpected)
schema_validation_cases.notes: The receipt records an observation; it does not carry policy. Letting an issuer attach its own max age would put the freshness bar back in the hands of the party whose evidence is being judged.

schema_validation_cases.name: receipts_tagged_union_accepts_both_families
schema_validation_cases.notes: One response carrying both families. A consumer MUST branch on the schema constant; threshold_met is an Arkret-layer convenience and its absence MUST NOT be read as true.

semantic_cases.name: existing_offline_agent_is_found
semantic_cases.precondition: stable binding exists; agent presence offline and KeyPackage inventory is zero
semantic_cases.action: resolve
assertions: state is found
same Realm and main Strand are returned
no KeyPackage claim occurs
the query-only resolver performs no create phase

semantic_cases.name: repair_dispatch_is_a_non_authorizing_durable_trigger
semantic_cases.precondition: the pair has an accepted binding, one participant has an accepted ak.member.rejoin.own, the MLS group needs a replacement generation, and the peer participant is offline
semantic_cases.action: submit one exact device-or-Native-Agent authorized request through ak.self.direct_conversation.command.repair_dispatch and let the source relay it through ak.peer.direct_conversation.command.repair_relay
assertions: the self request and peer relay use their registered closed operation DTOs; only the destination's internal human-device branch creates DeviceMessageEnvelope values, while a Native Agent branch targets its accepted current runtime endpoint without inventing an ak:device id
the request is not carried on the Signal rail, whose 120 second live envelope cannot reach an offline peer

the request carries no Event bytes, no MLS material and no authority: the peer re-verifies requester identity, the accepted rejoin, both directional Contact heads and generation staleness from the signed event log before authoring anything
the resolver supplies active_mls_generation_ref and sha256(RFC8785_JCS(current accepted active-generation cell whole value)) as one pair in found and in every repairable suspended state
the request copies observed_active_generation_value_digest byte for byte from that resolver value and never hashes the Event ref or scans for a maximum generation
a request whose observed_active_generation_value_digest differs from the peer current whole-value digest is dropped instead of producing a second replacement generation
the source transaction freezes request digest, current destination binding, exact relay bytes and outbox before network delivery; retry and restart never rebuild from newer state

the destination transaction chooses exactly one recipient_target branch: human_principal atomically fans identical canonical content to every current-authorized-device snapshot with distinct stable message ids, or native_agent atomically targets the one current active accepted runtime endpoint

the exact KeyPackage claim uses one closed target selector: a human has exactly one target_device_ids entry; an Agent has target_agent_id, target_agent_verification_method and target_agent_key_authorize_event_id and forbids target_device_ids; both consume exactly requester_keypackage_ref
there is no ack, receipt or refusal code: the durable Commit, Welcome and activation are the only response, and refusal is simply a generation that never advances
concurrent repairers are resolved by the existing candidate fanout cap and security_barrier CAS, with no repair-specific winner rule

semantic_cases.name: repair_relay_destination_atomic_replay
semantic_cases.precondition: one destination accepted the first relay under (Source-Service-ID, request_id) and persisted its terminal outcome
semantic_cases.action: redeliver the exact canonical relay body, then reuse request_id with one changed content byte
assertions: the exact replay returns the original byte-identical outcome without resnapshotting targets or allocating another message id
the changed digest returns duplicate_conflict and writes zero queue entries
a crash before the atomic commit leaves neither the request ledger nor any target queue item; a crash after commit exposes the complete original batch and outcome

semantic_cases.name: repair_relay_human_recipient_snapshot_is_all_or_zero
semantic_cases.precondition: the accepted peer participant is human with three current authorized devices and the third queue write fails
semantic_cases.action: process the peer repair relay
assertions: recipient_target.kind is human_principal
zero messages and zero terminal ledger outcome are committed
a retry may take one new authoritative snapshot only because no first transaction committed; once committed, later device authorization or revocation never mutates the frozen snapshot

semantic_cases.name: repair_relay_native_agent_uses_runtime_not_device
semantic_cases.precondition: the accepted peer participant is a Native Agent with one current active runtime endpoint in accepted Agent key/session binding
semantic_cases.action: process the peer repair relay
assertions: recipient_target.kind is native_agent and enqueued_target_count is exactly one
the target snapshot transcript binds recipient_agent_id, active_runtime_endpoint_ref and stable message_id
no ak:device id, device projection or per-device queue is synthesized
missing, ambiguous, stale or inactive runtime binding fails closed with zero enqueue

semantic_cases.name: repair_exact_keypackage_target_xor
semantic_cases.precondition: claim_purpose is direct_conversation_repair
semantic_cases.action: attempt human, Native Agent, mixed and stale exact selectors
assertions: human accepts only target_keypackage_ref plus exactly one target_device_ids and returns exactly that ref with matching device evidence

Native Agent accepts only target_keypackage_ref plus target_agent_id, target_agent_verification_method and target_agent_key_authorize_event_id and returns exactly that ref with matching AgentSignerEvidence
mixed human and Agent selectors, absent exact ref, another current package, last-resort, consumed, revoked, wrong signer or stale authority all return opaque claim_failed with zero consumption

semantic_cases.name: creation_required_carries_the_authoring_material
semantic_cases.precondition: the pair has an accepted Contact basis and no accepted Direct Conversation Realm; the caller is the founder and the current gates allow creation
semantic_cases.action: resolve the pair through ak.self.direct_conversation.read.resolve
assertions: state is creation_required and next_founding_input is present

next_founding_input member names equal the DirectConversationFoundingUnitSubmission members byte for byte, so the caller copies founder_basis_evidence and source_service_binding across with no renaming map
exactly one founder_basis_evidence branch is returned for this pair, human for a peer Contact founding and controller_agent for an own-Agent founding
the container carries no Event bytes, no coordinates, no idempotency_key and no receipt: the founder still authors and signs all three Events
a service that cannot assemble or verify the material returns temporarily_unavailable instead of a creation_required outcome without the container
the submission re-verifies the material against the service's own current state and never trusts the echoed copy

semantic_cases.name: accepted_service_binding_has_a_non_circular_producer
semantic_cases.precondition: the founder DID and PCR are accepted and the authenticated principal has no current service binding
semantic_cases.action: prepare a frozen binding draft, sign its challenge-bound digest, commit it, then resolve a creation-required pair
assertions: binding establishment runs after DID publication so the service derives current authority_evidence without a future-value dependency
prepare accepts no caller-supplied service metadata, DID evidence, timestamps, challenge or binding core
authorization_challenge equals challenge_id and is inside binding_digest, so an old principal proof cannot complete a fresh challenge
principal proof and service proof use distinct proof_purpose values and created_at equals the frozen accepted_at
current-binding CAS, immutable accepted binding, challenge consumption, service proof and byte-identical replay outcome commit atomically
same-service renewal requires predecessor_binding_digest to equal the complete current binding digest; a CAS loser writes nothing
resolver returns the durable verified binding verbatim, while no binding or unverifiable authority yields temporarily_unavailable

semantic_cases.name: founding_coordinates_are_derived_from_unit_bytes
semantic_cases.precondition: founder authored the three-Event unit in fixed wire order
semantic_cases.action: submit the direct_conversation_founding branch of ak.self.events.command.submit
assertions: realm_id equals retype of the first Event ID and main_strand_id equals retype of the third Event ID
founding_unit_digest is recomputed from the three ordered Event IDs under the ak.direct-conversation.founding-unit.v1 domain
two independent implementations derive the same coordinates, unit digest and receipt semantics
acceptance fixes the caller-derived coordinates and allocates nothing

semantic_cases.name: founding_unit_strand_uses_bootstrap_no_basis_shape
semantic_cases.precondition: the third Event of the founding unit is the Realm's main ak.strand.create and the Genesis Seal covers all three Events
semantic_cases.action: admit the unit
assertions: the Strand carries neither seal_ref, auth_context nor seal_basis and rides the same-batch staged authority-root proof
a no-basis ak.strand.create outside this exact unit is rejected by batch admission
the same Strand carrying seal_ref, auth_context or seal_basis inside the unit is rejected

semantic_cases.name: server_allocated_founding_identifier_rejected
semantic_cases.precondition: a submission asserts a service-allocated realm_id, a reservation handle or a materialization draft
semantic_cases.action: submit the founding unit
assertions: zero Events are written
no coordinator election, reserved state or materializing state exists in the contract

semantic_cases.name: founder_multi_device_concurrency_admits_first_valid_unit
semantic_cases.precondition: two founder devices independently author different valid units for the same pair
semantic_cases.action: both submit concurrently to the same Principal Server slot
assertions: exactly one unit is accepted and three Events are written once
the losing device receives direct_conversation_slot_already_committed with zero writes
both devices then resolve to the same coordinates

semantic_cases.name: exact_unit_replay_returns_byte_identical_receipt
semantic_cases.precondition: the unit was accepted but the response was lost, or the service restarted after receipt persistence or outbox enqueue
semantic_cases.action: replay the same signed bytes with the same idempotency_key
assertions: the stored receipt is returned byte-identically and accepted_at does not advance
no second Event, receipt, slot or outbox entry is produced

semantic_cases.name: same_idempotency_key_different_unit_conflicts
semantic_cases.precondition: the caller reuses one idempotency_key with a different founding_unit_digest
semantic_cases.action: submit the second unit
assertions: zero Events are written

semantic_cases.name: same_and_dual_principal_server_deployments_agree
semantic_cases.precondition: the pair is hosted on one Principal Server in one run and on two Principal Servers in another
semantic_cases.action: run self founding and the federation direct_conversation_founding branch
assertions: both deployments produce the same unit digest, coordinates and admission verdict
the federation branch omits service_binding_ref and binds destination through service DID headers and the source receipt

semantic_cases.name: federation_founding_dependency_missing_is_atomic
semantic_cases.precondition: the Contact basis mirror has not reached the destination Principal Server
semantic_cases.action: deliver the founding unit through the peer direct_conversation_founding branch
assertions: the response is a top-level HTTP 409 with EventsDependencyMissingProblem
zero Events are written and no per-item partial acceptance occurs
the delivery remains retryable and is never permanently rejected

semantic_cases.name: leave_or_directional_contact_terminal_suspends
semantic_cases.precondition: stable binding exists and leave, block, or either directional Contact head/scope gate becomes false; Consent is not consulted
semantic_cases.action: resolve and attempt message
assertions: resolver returns suspended with same coordinates
reason classes are not disclosed
no successor Realm is created

semantic_cases.name: rejoin_uses_same_realm_without_old_keys
semantic_cases.precondition: suspension basis is repaired
semantic_cases.action: resolve and rejoin
assertions: same binding Realm and main Strand are used
new active MLS generation is projected
old epoch keys and history secret are not automatically delivered

semantic_cases.name: generic_navigation_excludes_dm
semantic_cases.precondition: stable DM Realm is synchronized
semantic_cases.action: generic collaboration discovery
assertions: DM Realm is absent
dedicated resolver still returns it

semantic_cases.name: participant_authority_is_symmetric
semantic_cases.precondition: stable binding active membership current authorization basis and active MLS generation are exact
semantic_cases.action: both participants create own messages
assertions: creator and peer use the same participant evaluator
technical root is not an operational owner

semantic_cases.name: third_participant_and_root_governance_denied
semantic_cases.precondition: stable Direct Conversation
semantic_cases.action: add third participant grant admin or modify peer message

semantic_cases.name: agent_reply_requires_conjunction
semantic_cases.precondition: Agent is a stable participant but runtime key or participation policy is not ready
semantic_cases.action: agent reply
assertions: resolver remains found or suspended independently

semantic_cases.name: list_next_prepare_input_authors_scope_update_and_tombstone
semantic_cases.precondition: one accepted non-terminal Contact basis whose issuer-local lineage head is at version 1
semantic_cases.action: read ak.self.contact.read.list and copy next_prepare_input into the prepare phase of ak.self.contact.command.scope_update and of ak.self.contact.command.tombstone
assertions: the accepted row carries next_prepare_input and the three field names are byte-identical to the prepare fields that consume them
version equals current head version plus one and predecessor_event_ref equals the current lineage head Event ID, not the predecessor of that head
both prepare phases are accepted with the values copied verbatim and no client-side renaming, recomputation or derivation occurs
the same row is projected for a glare-derived basis, where predecessor_event_ref is the issuer's own request head
an empty granted_to_peer_scopes replacement keeps contact_state accepted and the row still carries the cursor so a later widen stays authorable

semantic_cases.name: non_authorable_contact_states_omit_next_prepare_input
semantic_cases.precondition: rows in pending_outgoing, pending_incoming, rejected, expired and tombstoned
semantic_cases.action: read ak.self.contact.read.list
assertions: no row in these five states carries next_prepare_input, because the first two have no basis or lineage yet and the last three are terminal
the omission alone expresses that no successor is authorable now and no extra error code or contact_state value is introduced
a client MUST NOT assemble a successor from request_event_ref, response_event_ref or tombstone_event_ref

semantic_cases.name: stale_next_prepare_input_is_refused_and_reread
semantic_cases.precondition: the holder holds a next_prepare_input read before a concurrent accepted successor advanced the lineage head
semantic_cases.action: prepare ak.self.contact.command.scope_update or ak.self.contact.command.tombstone with the stale triple
assertions: prepare is refused with zero writes and a scope replacement whose current proof is stale is refused with contact_scope_stale
the client re-reads ak.self.contact.read.list and retries with the fresh cursor
the client never guesses a lineage head and never retries the same triple

semantic_cases.name: sixteenth_generation_candidate_is_admitted
semantic_cases.precondition: fifteen not-yet-active candidate MLS groups already reference the same active-generation predecessor whole value
semantic_cases.action: submit the sixteenth ak.direct_conversation.mls_generation.activate candidate through ak.self.events.command.submit
assertions: the sixteenth candidate is admitted because the cap is sixteen and not fifteen
no candidate is activated by admission alone; the singleton cell still selects exactly one
the pair coordinates, binding, membership and current active generation are unchanged

semantic_cases.name: seventeenth_generation_candidate_is_refused_with_exact_code
semantic_cases.precondition: sixteen not-yet-active candidate MLS groups already reference the same active-generation predecessor whole value
semantic_cases.action: submit the seventeenth candidate through ak.self.events.command.submit and again through ak.peer.events.command.submit
assertions: both entry points refuse with that exact registered code at HTTP 409 and write nothing
the refusal is never reported as rate_limited and carries no retry_after_ms window, because activating or expiring an existing candidate is the only way forward
a generic failed_precondition or conflict is not an acceptable substitute once the code is registered

semantic_cases.name: generation_candidate_fanout_refusal_does_not_quarantine_the_pair
semantic_cases.precondition: the seventeenth candidate was just refused with mls_generation_proposal_fanout_exceeded
semantic_cases.action: resolve the pair and send an ordinary Message on the current active generation
assertions: the pair is not quarantined and the resolver still returns the same coordinates, active_mls_generation_ref and active_mls_generation_value_digest
the resolver state does not become suspended and no send blocker is added for the refusal
the sixteen existing candidates are retained; the refusal removes none of them

semantic_cases.name: resolver_send_blockers_are_server_verifiable_only
semantic_cases.precondition: the holder blocked the peer in ak.account.blocklist and one historical epoch secret was never installed on this device
semantic_cases.action: resolve the pair through ak.self.direct_conversation.read.resolve
assertions: found.send_blockers[] carries only blockers the service can prove from accepted authoritative state
personal_blocked and history_key_unavailable are absent from the wire enum, so the service cannot report them even if it wanted to
the resolver state stays found; the client-local blockers do not turn it into suspended
the client merges its own client-local blockers on top of the wire set before deciding whether to release the send

semantic_cases.name: resolver_returning_a_client_local_blocker_is_schema_violation
semantic_cases.precondition: a service attempts to report a holder-private or device-private fact on the wire
semantic_cases.action: return found.send_blockers containing personal_blocked or history_key_unavailable
assertions: the closed direct_conversation_send_blocker enum no longer contains either value, so the reply fails schema validation at the client
the client MUST NOT accept the value by tolerating an unknown blocker string
no server-side evaluation of the holder blocklist or of device-local history key installation is protocol evidence

semantic_cases.name: presence_and_keypackage_blockers_are_participant_only
semantic_cases.precondition: the caller is not one of the two exact-pair participants of the requested pair
semantic_cases.action: probe ak.self.direct_conversation.read.resolve for that pair to learn peer presence or KeyPackage inventory
assertions: presence_offline and keypackage_empty are returned only to an existing exact-pair participant of that pair
a non-participant gets the same opaque failure as for a pair that does not exist, so the blockers cannot be used as an enumeration oracle
an existing pair is never hidden from a real participant merely because a peer is offline or has no KeyPackage inventory

semantic_cases.name: pending_incoming_row_authors_respond_and_reject
semantic_cases.precondition: the holder holds one verified mirror of a peer-authored ak.contact.requested plus the request_acceptance_receipt issued by the peer's own source service
semantic_cases.action: read ak.self.contact.read.list and copy request_receipt into the prepare phase of ak.self.contact.command.respond and of ak.self.contact.command.reject
assertions: the pending_incoming row carries the complete signed request_receipt object and the field name is byte-identical to the prepare field that consumes it
both prepare phases accept the receipt copied verbatim, with no narrowing to a reference and no change to the prepare contract
the receipt issuer is the peer's source service, not the holder's own server, so the client verifies the signature itself instead of trusting its server's retelling
the same receipt digest is the one that derives the normal basis, so respond and reject consume the identical bytes

semantic_cases.name: non_pending_incoming_states_omit_request_receipt
semantic_cases.precondition: rows in pending_outgoing, accepted, rejected, expired and tombstoned
semantic_cases.action: read ak.self.contact.read.list
assertions: no row in these five states carries request_receipt, because pending_outgoing has no incoming request to answer and the other four have a consumed slot or a terminal basis
the omission alone expresses that respond and reject are not authorable now; no error code and no contact_state value is added for it

a glare pair never presents a receipt-bearing row: an unconsumed outgoing request in the holder's own slot keeps the row pending_outgoing while glare evidence is still incomplete, and the mechanically derived basis projects accepted, so the row is never pending_incoming and respond and reject stay forbidden throughout

cases.name: advertised_profile_closure
cases.expected: All inherited required endpoints, schemas, event kinds, bindings, fixtures, and required feature-discovery tokens are advertised or locally available.

cases.name: surface_tier_does_not_overclaim
cases.expected: The service does not advertise an operation, profile, or schema excluded by its declared surface tier.

fixtures/encoding-fixture.json.description: Machine-readable encoding & crypto vectors mirrored from zh/conformance/conformance-vectors.md §1.3-§1.13. Conformance runners MUST execute every vector and compare canonical_bytes / digest / order outputs. The crypto.ed25519_detached_jws vector lives separately in crypto-signature-fixture.json; the rank_order vector covers hex-Base32 rank string ordering (LIST item placement).
fixtures/encoding-fixture.json.generator_semantics: Vectors of kind *_reject_generated carry a `generator` object instead of literal input bytes: the runner MUST construct the input at execution time from the generator parameters (e.g. nesting_depth, array_item_count) following the generator.rule text, so the fixture never stores megabyte-scale literals. Rejection is asserted exactly as for literal-input vectors.

rules: an unknown value from an open registry MUST NOT fail deserialization of the containing object
the exact unknown string MUST survive decode and encode
admission may still return unsupported_event_kind or another profile-defined result after parsing
schema-declared x_* and critical extension parameter slots are canonical signed content
unknown nested values MUST be preserved without key filtering, normalization, or reordering beyond canonical encoding
a receiver that does not implement the optional extension still preserves and forwards its exact content
object key MUST be sorted by UTF-16 code unit at every level
array order MUST be preserved as input
string values MUST NOT be rewritten by key sort
hash the exact UTF-8 bytes recorded by expected_input_hex without a trailing newline or Unicode normalization
the digest prefix, lowercase hex length, and Realm digest_algorithm are part of the verified suite contract
implementations declaring ak.profile.hash.blake3.v1 MUST pass the positive KAT and every negative case
NaN / Infinity / -Infinity MUST reject
-0 MUST reject
v1 signed JSON numbers MUST be integers; 1.0 / 1e0 / fractional or exponent decimal spellings MUST reject instead of being canonicalised
signature verification MUST run only after canonicalisation succeeds

rejected_input_categories: duplicate JSON object keys at the same level
lone surrogate or ambiguous escape sequence
non-integer JSON numbers or parser-accepted numbers that cannot be proven to be integers
rules: duplicate keys MUST NOT be silently overwritten by parser default
malformed strings MUST NOT be replaced with U+FFFD before signing
rejection MUST be auditable; reason_code SHOULD be schema_violation, invalid_canonical_json, or invalid_encoding
event digest MUST be derived from canonical bytes after stripping proofs and unsigned, before redaction
event_id MUST appear inside the digest input but does not replace the digest
transport envelope, HTTP headers, sync metadata, and local receive time MUST NOT be hashed
the same event MUST yield the same digest on every Events API and Sync Service

fail_conditions: producer hashes events before canonical set normalization
receiver accepts an unsorted or duplicate signed wire events array
proof field included in receipt digest

rules: proof MUST bind event_digest, actor DID, verification_method, and created_at
cross-service / cross-domain verification SHOULD additionally bind domain or audience
actual ed25519 detached JWS for this binding lives in crypto-signature-fixture.json
HLC MUST sort by (unix_ms, logical, node_id_hash)
implementations MUST NOT compare HLC as raw wall-clock string unless the profile guarantees fixed-width lowercase hex such that string compare equals tuple compare

expected_acceptable_outcomes: wait until unix_ms_hex advances, then emit 01970e589d22-0000-a13f9c2e
return local error hlc_logical_overflow before canonical bytes are produced; caller retries
fail_conditions: logical counter wraps to a smaller value while still emitting events
wall-clock skew is forged to escape overflow at the cost of HLC monotonicity or causality
consumer accepts wrap-around values into accepted history

vectors.fixture_freshness_note: Timestamps are fixed at year 2099 deliberately so the static vector cannot expire during normal spec lifetime. Implementations generating their own conformance cursors MUST use fresh `issued_at`/`expires_at` matching their authority's clock; do NOT reuse this fixture's timestamps on the wire.
client_rules: MUST treat cursor as an opaque string and round-trip it verbatim
MUST NOT parse v / purpose / issued_at / expires_at / h to construct the next page request
MUST handle cursor decode failure by treating cursor as opaque, not by aborting the protocol
server_rules: MUST validate v, purpose, issued_at, expires_at, the full core cursor schema, and h handle binding before honouring cursor
syntax validation failure MUST return invalid_param with reason_code invalid_cursor; TTL failure MUST return cursor_expired; handle lookup or binding failure MUST return cursor_integrity_invalid
fail_conditions: client parses h/expiry and rebuilds a request
core server accepts a cursor body without h

sidecar_case.assertion: a Sidecar scope digests differently from the Realm scope of the same Realm, so ciphertext carried across scopes is detected on decrypt instead of relying on key isolation

mutation_cases.name: kind_only_scope_ref
mutation_cases.note: the whole canonical scope_ref object participates; hashing kind alone would collide every Sidecar in the Realm

rules: implementations MUST NOT hash plaintext payload
implementations MUST NOT omit payload metadata required for routing/decryption; otherwise sync service cannot safely dedupe or audit envelopes
UTF-16 code-unit ordering places the supplementary-plane key before U+FFFF because its high surrogate 0xD83D sorts before 0xFFFF.
duplicate JSON object keys at the same level MUST reject before canonicalisation
non-NFC string input MUST reject before signature verification
U+FEFF / UTF-8 BOM injection MUST reject
malformed HLC strings MUST reject

generator.rule: runner builds a JSON object nested 65 levels deep, e.g. {"a":{"a":{...{"a":1}...}}} where the top-level container counts as depth 1; a mixed object/array variant of the same depth MUST also reject

rules: canonical JSON / deterministic CBOR structure nesting depth MUST NOT exceed 64 (objects and arrays combined, top-level container = depth 1); see zh/conformance/scalability-constraints.md section 2
receiver MUST fail bounded before recursive descent can exhaust the stack (depth-bounded recursion or explicit worklist)
a control input of depth exactly 64 MUST be accepted (the limit is inclusive)
byte string header (0x5a, 4-byte length) declares 4294967295 bytes but only 4 bytes of input remain; declared length MUST be <= remaining input
decoder MUST reject before allocating any buffer sized from the declared length (capacity-bomb resistance)
applies to every hand-written deterministic CBOR structure, including the mls_governance_binding GroupContext extension
input is the indefinite-length map {_ "a": 1} (0xbf ... 0xff); indefinite-length items (map 0xbf, array 0x9f, string 0x5f/0x7f) violate RFC 8949 section 4.2 deterministic encoding and MUST reject
receiver MUST NOT normalise indefinite-length items into definite-length form and continue
applies to every hand-written deterministic CBOR structure, including the mls_governance_binding GroupContext extension

generator.rule: runner emits a definite-length CBOR array header declaring 65537 items followed by 65537 encodings of unsigned integer 0

rules: a single array or map in a hand-written deterministic CBOR structure MUST NOT declare or contain more than 65536 items; see zh/conformance/scalability-constraints.md section 2
decoder MUST NOT preallocate item storage from the declared count before the bound check

vectors.description: Golden vectors for the base58btc multibase encoding of Ed25519 public keys with the 0xed01 multicodec prefix and the resulting did:key identifier. Generated and round-trip verified (encode -> decode) by the reference implementation.
rules: multibase encoding MUST be base58btc with the leading 'z' prefix (multibase table)
the multicodec prefix for Ed25519 public keys MUST be the varint 0xed01, prepended to the 32 raw public key bytes before base58btc encoding

decode MUST round-trip to the original 32 public key bytes; a multibase string whose decoded payload is not exactly 34 bytes (2-byte multicodec prefix + 32 key bytes) or whose prefix is not 0xed01 MUST be rejected
did:key identifiers embed the multibase string verbatim: did:key:<multibase>
base binding fields follow ak.vector.encoding.signature_binding_payload.v1 (event_digest, actor DID, verification_method, created_at)
cross-domain verification binds the target service domain via the optional domain field; the canonical bytes sort it between created_at and event_digest
absent optional fields MUST be omitted from the canonical binding object entirely; a null placeholder changes the canonical bytes and MUST NOT be emitted
base binding fields follow ak.vector.encoding.signature_binding_payload.v1 (event_digest, actor DID, verification_method, created_at)
audience-constrained verification binds a single audience DID via the optional audience field
absent optional fields MUST be omitted from the canonical binding object entirely; a null placeholder changes the canonical bytes and MUST NOT be emitted
