The transformation_rules[] dialect ids are the canonical ak.transform.*.v1 set the profile transformation_rules_v1_grammar declares. Schema ids are the registered reference profiles ak.schema.morph.customer_risk.v1 and its additive extension ak.schema.morph.customer_risk.ext.v1.

vectors.description: Identity transformation preserves all fields and canonical values.
A field-rename transformation: fields.risk_score is renamed to fields.score; the unrelated fields.status passes through untouched. Pure rename, replay-deterministic.

A default-backfill transformation: a new optional field fields.priority is backfilled with the deterministic default "normal" while existing fields.status is preserved. Backfill is idempotent (it never overwrites a present value).
Integer-to-number widening preserves the JSON numeric value while changing its declared schema acceptance set.

assertions.rule: contract-registry operations and generated operation-registry rows form a one-to-one mapping by operation_id.
Every operation-registry operation_id appears exactly once as an OpenAPI operationId and no extra operationId exists.
Every operation not marked http_only_variant=true appears in the parsed non-HTTP binding artifact; every http_only_variant operation is absent.
Every request_schema and response_schema reference resolves to a registered schema artifact.
Every write operation declares idempotency_mechanism and retry_safe; every retry_safe=false operation also declares a machine-actionable uncertain_outcome recovery strategy.
Read-only query and resource-get operations do not invent an idempotency key contract.
Every write operation declares whether success commits an Arkret Event, an actor-private Event, or no Event with a stable rationale; declared event kinds are active and resolvable.

fixtures/organization-registration-fixtu.description: Conformance vectors for registering an external, already-published Organization DID with a deployment (identity-did.md §8.4). The family separates five things that are routinely conflated: resolution, control verification, local registration, Realm relationship and service delegation. Being resolvable or referenceable never yields local administrative authority. Registration is two-phase by decision, not by preference: the registry issues and remembers a single-use challenge, and only then does the caller prove control at a pinned version. The control proof binds local_admin_subject so a captured proof cannot be redirected to another beneficiary, and registration_generation gives the binding an identity that changes across re-establishment so the terminal revoked state and the organization-keyed idempotency stop contradicting each other. Opening a new generation atomically supersedes the previous current generation; old receipts cannot authorize after the current pointer advances even when their immutable signed payload still says active. proof_kind is a closed two-member discriminator over mature DIDs; creating a new Organization DID is a separate ceremony with no member here, so a receiver never has to guess whether a proof asserts existing control or creation. Cases whose schema_only_valid is true satisfy JSON Schema yet MUST be rejected, because cross-field invariants such as the challenge window, scope agreement and quorum sufficiency cannot be expressed in JSON Schema. Placeholder DIDs, digests and JWS strings are structural only and MUST NOT be treated as cryptographic vectors.

schema_validation_cases.name: challenge_valid
schema_validation_cases.notes: Every binding field closes one replay path: purpose separates this signature from any other the organization makes, audience and trust_domain pin it to this deployment, origin pins the HTTP surface, nonce makes it unrepeatable, and the 300-second window bounds how long a captured proof stays useful.

schema_validation_cases.name: ensure_with_resolved_verification_method_valid
schema_validation_cases.notes: Single-signature branch. The pinned version_id plus log_head_digest is what makes the later receipt auditable; without it a receipt would assert control at an unknown point in the DID's history.

schema_validation_cases.name: ensure_with_governance_quorum_valid
schema_validation_cases.notes: Quorum branch with two distinct governance signatures meeting the declared threshold. Per identity-did.md §8.1 a witness attestation is not a quorum and MUST NOT be substituted here: witnessing proves history visibility, quorum proves governance authorisation.

schema_validation_cases.name: receipt_valid
schema_validation_cases.notes: The receipt proves this deployment accepted a local binding and nothing more: it is not a Realm capability, not membership, not a notary designation and not a service delegation. control_proof_kind travels alongside control_key_digest so a later auditor can tell which commitment the digest is over without refetching the request.

schema_validation_cases.name: quorum_threshold_on_single_signature_branch_is_invalid
schema_validation_cases.notes: The discriminator is closed in both directions. A threshold on the single-signature branch would leave a receiver unable to say whether one signature was sufficient or two were promised and one delivered.

schema_validation_cases.name: governance_quorum_without_threshold_is_invalid
schema_validation_cases.notes: Without a declared threshold, any number of signatures could be claimed sufficient after the fact.

schema_validation_cases.name: receipt_without_expiry_is_invalid
schema_validation_cases.notes: An unbounded receipt would let a single first-time control proof authorise the organization relationship indefinitely, which is exactly what the refresh operation exists to prevent.

schema_validation_cases.name: unregistered_scope_is_invalid
schema_validation_cases.notes: The scope vocabulary is closed so a deployment cannot mint administrative authority the organization never consented to.

schema_validation_cases.name: handle_attestation_without_subject_is_invalid
schema_validation_cases.notes: Binding the subject inside the attestation is what stops an attestation issued for one organization from being presented for another.

schema_validation_cases.name: challenge_window_over_300_seconds_is_rejected
schema_validation_cases.notes: Schema-valid but the window is one hour. JSON Schema cannot compare two timestamps, so the receiver enforces the 300-second ceiling; a longer window buys nothing and widens the interval in which a captured proof remains usable.

schema_validation_cases.name: quorum_proofs_below_declared_threshold_is_rejected
schema_validation_cases.notes: Schema-valid: threshold 3, one proof. JSON Schema cannot compare an array length against a sibling integer, so the receiver enforces it and fails closed rather than accepting a partial quorum.

schema_validation_cases.name: ensure_scopes_disagreeing_with_challenge_is_rejected
schema_validation_cases.notes: Schema-valid but the challenge in challenge_valid requested only organization_profile_manage. The same challenge was already consumed by a successful request under a different canonical digest; consumption permits only a byte-identical retry. A scope mismatch means the control proof was produced for different authority than is now being claimed, so the binding MUST NOT be established.

schema_validation_cases.name: refresh_of_revoked_binding_is_rejected
schema_validation_cases.notes: Schema-valid but the stored binding is revoked, which is terminal. Reviving it by refresh would erase the distinction between a withdrawn relationship and a merely stale one, and would let a binding forced to revoked by DID deactivation come back despite the DID no longer being controllable.

schema_validation_cases.name: stale_binding_blocks_high_risk_path
schema_validation_cases.notes: Schema-valid stale receipt after a controller rotation. Low-risk reads may still consume it; a high-risk path MUST fail closed until refresh succeeds. stale rather than auto-invalidation was chosen because auto-invalidation lets an attacker force an unbind by triggering one rotation, while treating it as still valid lets a stolen-then-rotated organization keep its binding.

schema_validation_cases.name: control_proof_redirected_to_another_admin_is_rejected
schema_validation_cases.notes: Schema-valid but local_admin_subject differs from the value bound into challenge_valid and signed over by the control proof. This is the redirection attack the binding exists to stop: a proof that named only the organization and the version would let anyone who obtained it submit ensure naming themselves and receive the organization's administrative scopes. The receiver MUST compare against the stored challenge and reject.

schema_validation_cases.name: replay_of_current_generation_is_idempotent
schema_validation_cases.notes: Byte-identical retry of the request that successfully consumed this challenge: the challenge-consumption ledger digest matches, generation stays 1 and created is false. This is the only ensure replay that is idempotent; merely repeating organization/admin/scopes under a different challenge or request digest does not qualify.

schema_validation_cases.name: re_registration_after_revoke_opens_new_generation
schema_validation_cases.notes: revoke ended generation 1; a later ensure opens generation 2 with created=true. Without the generation, 'revoked is terminal' and 'ensure is idempotent on organization_id' would contradict each other and an implementation would have to pick between returning the old terminal receipt, raising duplicate_conflict, and illegally reviving the terminal state.

schema_validation_cases.name: scope_change_atomically_opens_new_generation
schema_validation_cases.notes: Changing local_admin_subject or the scope set also opens a new generation, because the delegation being granted is not the one the previous receipt attests. Returning created=false here would let a widened delegation hide behind an idempotent replay. Publishing generation 2, terminating generation 1 with organization_registration_superseded and advancing the current pointer are one atomic transition.

schema_validation_cases.name: superseded_active_receipt_cannot_authorize
schema_validation_cases.notes: The immutable generation-1 receipt still says status=active, but the registry current pointer is already 2. A verifier that trusts the signed status without checking the current-generation pointer would let the old admin or old scope set survive replacement. Opening generation 2 atomically terminated generation 1 with organization_registration_superseded, so this receipt no longer authorizes anything.

fixtures/push-notify-outcome-fixture.jso.description: Conformance vectors for the ak.edge.push.command.notify response contract (push-notifications.md §5.2). The response is conserved against notification.devices[]: every input device_id appears in outcomes[] exactly once, none is missing, none is duplicated, and none appears that was not requested. A target-level failure is expanded into one same-reason rejected outcome per input device, so a second response shape never exists. gateway_status accepted/duplicate mean the gateway durably took the route over and the caller MUST NOT resend; only a rejected outcome carrying retry_after_ms transfers the next attempt back to the caller, and only for the two registered caller-retryable reasons. Cases whose schema_only_valid is true but whose semantic_outcome is reject satisfy JSON Schema yet MUST be rejected by a conforming verifier for the listed registered reason code, because conservation is a cross-field invariant JSON Schema cannot express. Placeholder pseudonyms and device ids are structural only and MUST NOT be treated as cryptographic vectors.

request_context.notes: Every response case below is evaluated against this one request. Its devices[] is the conserved input set.

schema_validation_cases.name: all_input_devices_accepted
schema_validation_cases.notes: Both input devices durably taken over. Neither outcome carries reason_code or retry_after_ms; the caller owns no further attempt.

schema_validation_cases.name: partial_rejection_drives_registration_cleanup
schema_validation_cases.notes: Second device has no live registration. Cleanup is addressed by (push_target_id, device_id); the response never returns push_key, so the caller can drop the registration without the raw provider token crossing the wire.

schema_validation_cases.name: target_level_failure_is_expanded_per_device
schema_validation_cases.notes: Unknown push target is a target-level failure. It MUST be expanded into one same-reason rejected outcome per input device rather than collapsing into a target-scoped shape, which is what keeps conservation unconditional.

schema_validation_cases.name: caller_retryable_rejection_carries_backoff
schema_validation_cases.notes: push_gateway_unreachable is one of exactly two caller-retryable reasons. retry_after_ms is the sole wire signal that the caller, not the gateway, owns the next attempt for that device.

schema_validation_cases.name: exact_replay_reports_duplicate
schema_validation_cases.notes: Replay under the same Idempotency-Key and body. duplicate means an earlier request already took the route over and this one produced no new delivery; like accepted it forbids caller resend. It never means the request repeated a device_id, which devices[] uniqueness already forbids.

schema_validation_cases.name: rejected_without_reason_code_is_invalid
schema_validation_cases.notes: reason_code is REQUIRED when gateway_status=rejected; without it the caller cannot tell a terminal rejection from a retryable one.

schema_validation_cases.name: reason_code_on_accepted_is_invalid
schema_validation_cases.notes: A durably accepted route has no rejection reason. Allowing one would reintroduce the ambiguity between acceptance and failure that the closed gateway_status enum exists to remove.

schema_validation_cases.name: retry_after_ms_on_accepted_is_invalid
schema_validation_cases.notes: The gateway retries what it accepted. A backoff on an accepted route would invite the caller to resend and produce duplicate provider delivery.

schema_validation_cases.name: retry_after_ms_with_terminal_reason_is_invalid
schema_validation_cases.notes: push_token_unknown is terminal: the caller must drop the registration, not retry it. Only push_gateway_unreachable and rate_limited may carry retry_after_ms.

schema_validation_cases.name: unregistered_reason_code_is_invalid
schema_validation_cases.notes: reason_code is a closed enum whose members are all registered in error-code-registry.json. A free-form string would let each gateway invent its own failure vocabulary.

schema_validation_cases.name: raw_push_key_in_outcome_is_invalid
schema_validation_cases.first_expected_error: $: Additional properties are not allowed ('push_key' was unexpected)
schema_validation_cases.notes: The outcome object is closed. Returning the raw provider token would contradict the opaque-routing obligation in push-notifications.md §5.1 / §6.2, and the composite identity already addresses registration cleanup.

schema_validation_cases.name: rejected_bucket_response_is_invalid
schema_validation_cases.notes: A rejected-only bucket cannot prove what happened to the devices it omits. The response is a single conserved outcomes[] array; there is no bucketed alternative shape.

schema_validation_cases.name: missing_input_device_violates_conservation
schema_validation_cases.notes: Schema-valid but the second input device has no outcome. The caller cannot tell whether it was taken over or silently dropped, which is exactly the ambiguity conservation removes. JSON Schema cannot express this cross-field invariant, so a conforming verifier MUST enforce it.

schema_validation_cases.name: duplicate_device_id_violates_conservation
schema_validation_cases.notes: Schema-valid but the same device carries two contradictory conclusions. Exactly one outcome per input device_id is required.

schema_validation_cases.name: unrequested_device_violates_conservation
schema_validation_cases.notes: Schema-valid but the third outcome names a device the request never carried. An outcome set that can exceed its input is not a conservation proof and would let a gateway disclose device ids the caller did not address.

schema_validation_cases.name: echoed_push_target_id_must_match_request
schema_validation_cases.notes: Schema-valid but the echo names a different target than the request. The echo exists so an outcome set is self-describing under replay and audit; an echo free to drift provides neither.

schema_validation_cases.name: request_with_repeated_device_id_is_rejected
schema_validation_cases.notes: devices[] is a set keyed by device_id. uniqueItems only rejects byte-identical entries, so this pair differing only in app_id passes JSON Schema; the gateway MUST still reject it. Accepting it would make one input device demand two outcomes and break conservation at the source.

fixtures/reaction-fixture.json.notes: Reducer-level vectors for ak.reaction.add / ak.reaction.remove. The cell ak.component.message.reactions.v1 is the core or_set of reaction assertions: ak.reaction.add and ak.reaction.remove each project exactly one or_set_add, so the remove is itself an assertion rather than an observed-remove. Convergence of the default view is the reaction-specific remove-wins rule keyed on (actor_id, target_ref, key), which zh/models/strand-and-message.md §9.8.3 defines authoritatively as a projection over that set rather than as the or_set join; see §9.8 (Reaction model) and zh/crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md §2.9 (plaintext-vs-encrypted visibility).

cases.name: or_set_dedup_double_add_same_actor
cases.notes: Two add events from the same actor with the same key collapse to one OR-Set membership entry; the per-event audit log retains both.

cases.name: or_set_concurrent_add_remove_remove_wins_in_default_view
cases.notes: Two events from the same actor with no causal_refs between them; default view applies per-actor causal closure — concurrent (add, remove) collapses to the remove because the remove is itself a tombstone for the actor's adds in the concurrent past per OR-Set semantics chosen for ak.reaction.

cases.name: dangling_reaction_before_target_arrives
cases.notes: Reaction whose target_ref has not been observed yet MUST be held in pending; reducer materialises the OR-Set entry only after the target message becomes available.

cases.name: target_redacted_drops_default_view_keeps_audit
cases.notes: When the target message is redacted, the default view summary MUST NOT expose reaction members; the audit view retains the reaction events under the redaction stub.

cases.name: e2ee_routing_digest_dedup
cases.notes: In an E2EE realm the plaintext key is the v1 keyed-HMAC routing tag: HMAC-SHA256(key = MLS-Exporter("arkret-reaction-routing-v1", context = realm_id), data = NFC(canonical_emoji)); see zh/crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md §2.9. The 32-byte tag is carried in `key` as a 256-bit hex digest (the sha256: prefix below denotes the digest wire-encoding, not the derivation). Two adds with the same routing tag from the same actor in the same epoch collapse to one OR-Set membership; the tag differs in a different epoch because the MLS exporter secret rotates on every commit, so it does not dedup across epochs. realm_id is bound via the exporter context, providing defense-in-depth even if mls_group_id is reused across deployments.

cases.name: e2ee_epoch_rotation_breaks_dedup
cases.notes: Same canonical emoji yields a different routing hash after MLS epoch rotation; the new add is a fresh OR-Set entry, not a duplicate of the pre-rotation one.

cases.name: capability_revoked_blocks_subsequent_add
cases.notes: After ak.capability.revoke removes the actor's ak.reaction.add capability, the next add MUST be rejected before reducer state changes; in-flight events accepted before the revoke causal frontier remain in OR-Set state.

cases.name: rate_limit_high_rate_reaction_burst
cases.notes: Servers MAY rate-limit ak.reaction.add per actor; the reducer MUST treat rate-limited events as either rate_limited or quarantine, never as accepted-then-silently-dropped.

fixtures/realm-organization-fixture.json.description: Conformance vectors for the ak.realm.organization statement payload (organization-authorized Realm relationship endorsement / revocation). Validates schema_validation_cases[] against schemas/event-payload.schema.json#/$defs/realm_organization_payload via tools/lint_artifacts.py. The verified organization relationship has two independent authorization layers (realm-and-space.md §2.3.0): Realm-side acceptance (writer holds ak.realm.admin or rides an allowed create-bootstrap batch) and Organization-side consent (payload.authorization proof verifies to the organization DID control state, a threshold governance quorum, or a delegated Account Authority / governance service whose delegation purpose covers ak.realm.organization, the relationship, and the control_scopes). Placeholder signature/proof strings are intentional and MUST NOT be treated as cryptographic vectors. Cases whose schema_only_valid is true but whose semantic_outcome is reject pass JSON Schema yet MUST be rejected by the reducer for the listed expected_reason_code; downstream SDK validators and cotest negative cases MUST assert that exact registered reason code rather than a bare string.

grade_definitions.V: Black-box verifiable by canonical conformance vectors and fixture runner results.
grade_definitions.A: Verifiable by the public SDK API shape and inventory; no implementation-private inspection is required.

sdk_conformance_contract.evidence_coverage_semantics_note: A clause's required_evidence enumerates the ACCEPTABLE evidence kinds for that clause (acceptable-set semantics), not a mandate that every listed kind be present. For a clause claim with result=pass or result=fail: at least one evidence entry MUST be present (already required by the schema when result != not_applicable), and every evidence[].kind MUST be a member of that clause's required_evidence set in this contract. Evidence whose kind falls outside the clause's required_evidence set MUST NOT be accepted as substantiation for that clause. result=not_applicable is exempt from evidence-kind coverage but MUST carry a machine-readable rationale.
rules: Each SDK release claiming Arkret v1 conformance MUST publish one claim object against this exact contract digest.
The claim MUST bind the exact SDK artifact digest and spec revision, and MUST carry an issuer signature over the domain-separated RFC 8785 JCS claim bytes with proof omitted.
Every evidence reference MUST carry a non-zero immutable content digest; consumers MUST verify all digests and the issuer verification method before accepting the claim.
Every applicable clause MUST appear exactly once; not_applicable MUST include a machine-readable rationale.
Evidence references MUST be content-addressed or carry an immutable CI run identifier.

A verifier MUST enforce evidence_coverage_semantics: for every clause claim whose result is pass or fail, it MUST reject the claim unless at least one evidence entry is present and every evidence[].kind is a member of that clause's required_evidence set. A pass/fail clause substantiated only by evidence kinds outside its required_evidence set MUST be rejected. This check is independent of, and applied in addition to, the digest and signature checks above.
Section numbers and table row numbers are not clause identifiers; only clause_id is stable.

profile_sets.test_build_stance_rule: Test/conformance builds are marked solely by the canonical development_mode=true flag on the ServiceDescribe (see zh/sync/service-http-binding.md §2.1.2 and zh/sync/service-surface.md §3.0), which gates the test-only /_arkret/_conformance/* debug namespace and forces verified_profiles=[]. There is no separate ak.profile.* test-build profile: a test build is a deployment stance, not a negotiated interop capability.

profile_set_rules.v1_profile_catalog: Profiles that belong to the v1 stable catalog. This is not a bundle requirement; implementations MUST claim only the profiles, event kinds, schemas, and operations they actually support.
profile_set_rules.v1_minimal_interop_floor: Minimum profile for claiming v1 Event Store interop. Higher-level client, service, federation, blob, push, identity, and sovereign profiles remain independently claimable.
profile_set_rules.extension_profile_implementation: Optional. Tracks implementation profiles outside the v1 minimal interop floor, including evolving external standards (MIMI Internet-Drafts; A2A/ACP/MCP unstandardized agent protocols; Applet registry/audit SLA) and opt-in product/privacy features such as productivity, disappearing messages, calendar events, pins, and search. Implementations claiming v1 core MAY omit these entirely; implementations MUST claim only entries they actually support. When an underlying external standard matures, a replacement profile with stable version pinning can supersede that entry.

profiles/conformance-profiles.json.candidate_profiles_tier_rule: Profiles pairing unregistered candidate workflow concept/action names / capabilities with an explicit fail-closed gate. Receivers MUST treat any capability action whose `profile` points to a candidate profile as unknown (risk_tier=high default) unless they implement the profile. Candidate profiles are NOT part of v1 active conformance and SHOULD be promoted (with paired wire Event.kind values registered under `ak.*`) once their underlying surface is formally registered.
profiles/conformance-profiles.json.profile_roles_rule: Every profile id MUST be annotated with exactly one role from the enum {client, server, gateway, directory, admin, interop}. Roles partition the profile namespace so that an implementation MUST NOT mistake e.g. a gateway profile (push_gateway, blob_node) for a client profile, or a deployment / hardening / vector profile (admin role) for a wire-conformance client / server profile. SDK manifests, client-side feature negotiation, and conformance harness loaders MUST consult `profile_roles` before claiming a profile as locally implemented. Roles in spec layer metadata; the per-profile object in `profile_requirements` MAY ALSO carry a `role` field for convenience, but `profile_roles` is the canonical source.

history_sharing_policy_fixed_baseline.rationale: zh/governance/history-visibility.md section 6 condition 2 requires an effective ak.realm.history_sharing_policy before every ak.realm_key.share; the requirement is unconditional and is not limited to restricted visibility. A Direct Conversation Realm can never publish one: the founding unit is the closed three-Event unit create + peer ak.member.state{join} + main ak.strand.create and a fourth Event MUST reject the whole unit, neither ak.authority.direct_conversation_bootstrap_participant.v1 nor ak.authority.direct_conversation_participant.v1 carries any action that could author a policy facet, and zh/identity/contact-and-direct-conversation.md section 8.3 forbids restoring owner or admin authority after found. This profile therefore supplies the effective value, exactly as ak.profile.principal_control_realm.v1 does for a PCR; key sources and reducers MUST evaluate Direct Conversation history key share against this literal value and MUST NOT raise history_sharing_policy_missing for the absence of an accepted policy Event. Producers MUST NOT declare history_sharing_policy on the Realm object and MUST NOT append a policy Event to the founding unit. Field decisions: default_key_share=event_time_visibility is correct because history_visibility=joined and the peer is a Realm member from Realm Genesis onward (section 6.2), so the event-time judgement alone already releases generation-0 history. allowed_receiver_states=[active_member] is the machine-readable form of the exact-peer-only history sharing baseline, since the profile pins exactly two participants and an active member can only be one of that pair. allowed_key_sources keeps own_device, verified_member_device and key_backup, the last covering a participant restoring across their own devices from their own backup, and deliberately omits archive_node and recovery_service, which are third parties and would break the two-party exclusivity this profile exists to guarantee. post_removal_recovery=deny matches section 8.2, where a returning participant MUST NOT obtain history it had no right to decrypt before rejoining, and the new_mls_generation_history_isolated rule of ak.profile.direct_conversation_repair.v1. restricted_rules is deliberately absent because history_visibility is joined, not restricted, so that rule set is never consulted. Two different meanings of pre-join MUST NOT be conflated. pre_join_history here means before becoming a Realm member; in a Direct Conversation the peer join_frontier is Realm Genesis itself, so no Event in the Realm has a T0 earlier than it, the field is structurally never reached, and deny behaves identically to any allowing value; deny is chosen only to state truthfully that this profile never releases pre-membership history. The pre-join wording in section 6.2 means something else entirely, namely that the peer is not yet an MLS leaf, and that generation-0 history MUST be shared: implementations MUST NOT refuse the generation-0 provisional history key share of ak.authority.direct_conversation_bootstrap_participant.v1 because pre_join_history=deny. No release_range_clamp counterpart is registered here. The PCR clamp exists because its restricted_rules[].range=all_visible_at_t0 is a policy ceiling wider than the interval a newly authorized device may actually receive; this baseline declares no restricted_rules and therefore no range at all, and default_key_share=event_time_visibility delegates the released interval entirely to the section 3 joined event-time judgement, which is already self-clamping because an absence window between leave and rejoin is not T0-visible to the returning participant. The normative conformance vector for this clause is ak.vector.history_sharing.direct_conversation_profile_baseline.v1.

client_local_send_blockers.rationale: The Direct Conversation resolver may only report send blockers it can prove from accepted authoritative state. Two facts are structurally outside that boundary. ak.account.blocklist is holder-private account data that a synchronizing service is required to hold encrypted to holder devices only, so a service that evaluated personal_blocked would have to break that encryption invariant; and whether a given historical MLS secret was ever installed is device-private key state, so a client self-report of history_key_unavailable is a claim, not authority. Both values are therefore removed from the closed wire enum direct_conversation_send_blocker rather than merely annotated there: after removal a service that returns one produces a machine-detectable schema_violation, whereas an annotation would eventually be violated silently. They are carried instead by this closed client-local set, which is evaluated only on the holder's own device from state only that device holds. presence_offline and keypackage_empty stay on the wire because the service does hold provable facts for them, but they are visible only to an existing exact-pair participant of that pair, so they cannot serve as an enumeration oracle. The consequence is deliberate and MUST be documented by implementers: after a block, the fact that sending is refused is known only to the blocking client - not to its own service and not to the peer - and neither of them is entitled to know it. Implementations that habitually ask the server for send state will find the resolver returning found with an empty send_blockers[] and MUST still refuse the send locally. The normative conformance vector for this clause is ak.vector.direct_conversation.send_blocker_authority.v1.
rules: These values MUST NOT appear on any wire surface: not in direct_conversation_send_blocker, not in any operation request or response, not in any Event payload, and not on the peer carrier or federation surface.
A client MUST merge this local set with the server-returned found.send_blockers[] before releasing a send, and MUST fail closed locally when a local blocker applies.

A client-local blocker MUST NOT cause the resolver to return suspended and MUST NOT alter any wire state, so that server state is never polluted by device-local state and two devices of the same holder never disagree about the resolver outcome.
Implementations MUST NOT add any reporting, synchronization or probing channel whose purpose is to make the service or the peer aware that a client-local blocker applies.

binding_invariants: schema_refs MUST contain ak.profile.direct_conversation_realm.v1 and fields.collaboration_role MUST equal direct_conversation; either marker without the other is schema_violation.
content_encryption_floor and metadata_encryption_floor MUST both equal e2ee_required.

The ak.realm.create Event requirements.schema MUST contain ak.profile.direct_conversation_realm.v1 and requirements.critical_extensions MUST contain fail_closed=true id ak.feature.direct_conversation_realm_role.v1 for payload scope.
Exactly the two stable subject DIDs in the immutable binding may be Realm principal members; any third-party join or invite MUST be rejected.
Space events are forbidden in a Direct Conversation Realm with direct_conversation_space_forbidden; additional ordinary Strands remain allowed.
The canonical main Strand MUST be active, belong to the Realm, have no Circle scope, and expose an active primary discussion track.

First creation MUST be the founder's caller-authored three-Event unit submitted through the direct_conversation_founding branch of ak.self.events.command.submit. realm_id and main_strand_id are retyped from the first and third Event IDs, so the service MUST NOT allocate an identifier, issue a reserved or materializing draft, or elect a coordinator; it only verifies the unit, CAS-closes its local (founder_id, trust_domain_id, pair_key) slot and accepts zero or three Events atomically.

The founding slot admits the first valid unit only. A second unit for the same pair MUST be refused with direct_conversation_slot_already_committed and zero writes; a byte-identical replay MUST return the stored receipt without advancing accepted_at; the same idempotency key with a different unit MUST be duplicate_conflict. The slot MUST NOT reopen into creation_required after a committed unit.

Cross-Principal-Server founding MUST NOT depend on the peer service: the founder creates the Realm, activates generation 0 and sends real ciphertext alone. Peer KeyPackage claim is participant-authorized, binds the accepted pair, Realm, main Strand and MLS group, and MUST NOT use a last-resort KeyPackage. Federated delivery of the unit uses the direct_conversation_founding branch of ak.peer.events.command.submit and reports a missing bounded dependency as a top-level retryable dependency_missing with zero writes.

The unit's Genesis Seal MUST cover all three Events, every required founding write of an ordinary Realm create, and the create-locked baseline projection of join_rule=closed, content_scheme=mls_exporter_aead_v1, both e2ee_required floors and history_visibility=joined with exact-peer-only sharing. Sealing the create first and appending the peer join or the Strand afterwards MUST be rejected, and a same-batch facet Event that repeats or overrides a baseline value MUST be rejected.

Between the accepted founding unit and the first legal binding endorsement, pre-binding writes MUST cite authorization_ref=ak.authority.direct_conversation_bootstrap_participant.v1 with exactly one critical refs[] role=direct_conversation_founding_unit reference to the accepted ak.realm.create. The verifier recomputes the mutually exclusive phase from accepted facts; the producer MUST NOT declare it. Both phases retire permanently once the first legal endorsement is accepted.

The binding is immutable and fixes pair_key, participant pair, Realm and main Strand exactly once. It carries no authored lifecycle state or MLS group; current MLS generation is a separate accepted-history projection.

Leave, ban, block, either directional Contact terminal and participant terminal state suspend new writes without destroying the binding or creating a successor Realm. Consent changes never affect Personal DM authority. Recovery reuses the same Realm and MUST NOT automatically redeliver old epoch keys or history secrets.
Principal-private deletion and global content/key erasure retain stable pair, Realm and main Strand identity. The resolver never returns a competing candidate or performs winner selection.

Participant authority and root-owner masking are conjunctive profile admission rules and MUST be evaluated from the same accepted evidence basis as the target action; neither created_by nor membership alone is an authorization source.

The effective ak.realm.history_sharing_policy of a Direct Conversation Realm is history_sharing_policy_fixed_baseline.value, supplied by this profile. Key sources and reducers MUST evaluate every ak.realm_key.share in this Realm against that literal value and MUST NOT raise history_sharing_policy_missing for the absence of an accepted policy Event. Producers MUST NOT declare history_sharing_policy on the Realm object and MUST NOT emit ak.realm.history_sharing_policy into this Realm: the founding unit is closed at exactly three Events so a fourth Event MUST reject the whole unit, neither ak.authority.direct_conversation_bootstrap_participant.v1 nor ak.authority.direct_conversation_participant.v1 carries an action that could author a policy facet, and owner or admin authority MUST NOT be restored after found. history_visibility here is joined, so the baseline declares no restricted_rules and none is ever consulted; the peer is a Realm member from Realm Genesis onward, so pre_join_history is structurally never reached and MUST NOT be used to refuse the generation-0 provisional history key share.

The two client-local send blockers of client_local_send_blockers MUST NOT appear on any wire surface, and the resolver MUST NOT return suspended because one of them applies; the resolver reports only server-verifiable blockers, and personal_blocked or history_key_unavailable on the wire is a schema_violation.

ak.profile.principal_control_realm.v1.description: Realm profile for a principal-scoped durable control stream. PCR genesis is one create-once atomic unit: identity-root-signed ak.realm.create plus founding-device-signed ak.device.authorize. After genesis, device state and recovery policy live in the PCR; the DID is only the identity-root key log and re-anchor fence.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: Receivers that do not understand this v1 profile MUST NOT accept the Realm as principal control state.

rules: Agent PCR events MUST target the Agent DID bound to the Realm; controller execution uses actor_id=Agent DID, executed_by=controller DID, and a verified authorization_ref.

Initial provisioning MUST use one controller-owned ak.agent.provision Event in the controller PCR and atomically project provision, accountability and selector facts; later standalone accountability/selector changes remain controller-owned and MUST NOT move into the Agent PCR.
Pairing requests and account approval notifications MUST NOT be written to any PCR or Collaboration Realm.

history_sharing_policy_fixed_baseline.rationale: A PCR MUST declare history_visibility=restricted, and zh/governance/history-visibility.md section 3 forbids an effective restricted visibility without an accepted ak.realm.history_sharing_policy. But a PCR can never publish one: realm_event_kind_policy is allowlist_only and does not list that kind, PCR genesis is the closed two-Event unit create + ak.device.authorize (managed Agent PCR genesis is a single create), and the post-bootstrap recovery-material gate admits only its own closed write set. This profile therefore supplies the effective value. Implementations MUST evaluate PCR history key share against this literal value; producers MUST NOT declare it on the Realm object (realm.schema.json is closed and has no history_sharing_policy property) and MUST NOT emit ak.realm.history_sharing_policy into a PCR.
history_sharing_policy_fixed_baseline.release_range_clamp: range=all_visible_at_t0 is the policy ceiling, not the released interval. The releasing side MUST additionally clamp to the receiving device's accepted ak.device.authorize frontier per zh/identity/key-management.md section 5.0.1 (PCR history key share release authorization) and MUST NOT release earlier or concurrent-branch epoch keys. Pre-authorize control state reaches a new device through the durable device-list / normalized principal view baseline, not through earlier epoch keys.
history_sharing_policy_fixed_baseline.excluded_key_sources: archive_node and recovery_service are deliberately absent: a PCR is security_class=high_assurance with federation_policy in {closed, restricted, quarantine}, and its history secrets MUST NOT be recoverable through a third-party archive or recovery service. Managed Agent PCR continuity uses the controller-owned mls_history backup, which is a key_backup source.

binding_invariants: realm_id MUST equal the principal_control_realm_id resolved for the principal DID.
fields.purpose MUST be principal_control for human/organization PCRs or managed_agent_control for managed Agent PCRs; schema_refs MUST contain ak.profile.principal_control_realm.v1 in both cases.

Within a Principal Control Realm, ak.policy.set is admitted only for ak.root.identity.recovery_policy.command.publish with canonical payload {policy_id,value}, value.schema=ak.schema.recovery_policy.v1, equal policy ids, and no state/reason; admitting another policy family or bypassing ordinary Event, lease, reducer, allowlist, or Seal processing is non-conformant.
encryption_profile MUST be mls_rfc9420; PCRs MUST NOT use none or external.
content_encryption_floor and metadata_encryption_floor MUST both be e2ee_required; a PCR genesis declaring either floor below e2ee_required MUST be rejected (no plaintext-floor PCR exists in v1).

history_visibility MUST be restricted; new same-principal devices obtain prior control history via durable device-list / normalized principal view baseline and policy-gated MLS history key share, not by joining at the current epoch.
Control events MUST bind principal_id / device_id / session grant audience to the same principal DID or an explicitly trusted recovery/session issuer.

A managed Agent principal_control_realm_id and immutable requested_scope commitment MUST be verified from the unique ArkretPrincipalControlRealm DID service entry at accepted-at; the public entry fixes only realm_id, controller_did, authorization_ref and the domain-separated requested_scope_digest. The complete scope MUST come from a controller-signed verifier/audience/challenge-bound private disclosure whose digest matches that commitment. Implementation-private deterministic derivation or a service-local Agent row is not protocol evidence.
Managed Agent PCR genesis created_by and notary MUST equal the Agent DID; a controller authoring under delegation MUST be recorded as executed_by and MUST NOT synthesize an Agent signature.

A managed Agent PCR genesis carries no anchor ref: delegated_pcr_genesis is selected by payload.object.purpose alone, and admission MUST instead reverse-look-up an already accepted ak.agent.provision in the controller PCR whose payload.principal_control_realm_id equals retype(this genesis event_id). No match means zero writes. The genesis MUST arrive in a submission separate from that provision, because a same-unit or same-batch pair is the unconstructible shape encoding.md 6.0.1 forbids. The managed Agent PCR and its controller PCR MUST be hosted by the same Principal Server, since the reverse look-up and the realm-id claim uniqueness are both local decisions.

The effective ak.realm.history_sharing_policy of a PCR is history_sharing_policy_fixed_baseline.value, supplied by this profile. Producers MUST NOT declare history_sharing_policy on the Realm object and MUST NOT emit ak.realm.history_sharing_policy into a PCR; that kind is absent from realm_event_kind_policy.allowed_event_kinds and the write MUST be rejected with principal_control_event_kind_forbidden.

A PCR MUST NOT carry a Realm alias. ak.realm.alias is absent from realm_event_kind_policy.allowed_event_kinds, so a PCR is addressable only by realm_id; a human-readable alias on an identity-infrastructure control stream would publish the principal's control Realm under a guessable name.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: omit optional feature or return unsupported_feature

prose_requirement_coverage.requirement: discussion history visibility and membership trimming
inline and Blob-backed long-text Content Block boundary, E2EE descriptor and lifecycle

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: return unsupported_feature without dropping encrypted events
return unsupported_feature or omit projection capability
render generic fallback or return unsupported_feature
surface unavailable capability before write
preserve encrypted events and expose key_missing

ak.profile.agent_signer_evidence.v1.description: Portable ordinary-Realm Native Agent signer authorization evidence. Producers publish one Agent authority snapshot with key and Agent-lifecycle witnesses, one privacy-minimal Account Authority controller gate, and a structural XOR between exact-request current observation and destination-signed historical Event admission receipt. Consumers independently verify all three orthogonal gates, reject cross-request replay, preserve accepted Event validity across later terminal transitions, and cross-bind encrypted Events to the historical MLS leaf.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: Do not mark ordinary Native Agent Events Verified. Preserve ciphertext or quarantined plaintext with verification_pending and never fall back to keys/query or ordinary MLS leaf-only trust.

ak.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1.description: Degraded E2EE profile. Allows `mls_send_pause="advisory"` (cf. §2.4.1) so that low-latency interactive scenarios (real-time AV, collaborative editing, in-game chat) do not block message send on MLS commit completion. Cost: removed members can continue decrypting a small window of subsequent messages. NOT for general chat / collaboration / compliance use. MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with ak.profile.mls_governance_binding.full.v1.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: Servers that do not advertise ak.feature.e2ee_relaxed.v1 MUST reject Realm create / ak.realm.policy_bundle writes that set mls_send_pause="advisory" (reason: profile_unsupported / mls_send_pause_advisory_requires_e2ee_relaxed_profile). They MUST NOT silently accept the advisory string without honoring the relaxed semantics.

downgrade_declaration_obligation.policy_declaration_required: Realm create or ak.realm.policy_bundle MUST explicitly declare ak.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1 before mls_send_pause="advisory" is accepted. Out-of-band deployment config, UI-only labels, or a missing governance_binding GroupContext extension MUST NOT be treated as a valid downgrade declaration.
downgrade_declaration_obligation.service_describe_required: The serving implementation MUST advertise ak.feature.e2ee_relaxed.v1 and the claimed profile in ServiceDescribe before accepting advisory writes or projecting the Realm as relaxed to a peer/facade.
downgrade_declaration_obligation.binding_profile_required: Every MLS governance_binding emitted for a relaxed Realm MUST carry binding_profile="ak.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1" and the negotiated reducer_profile. Missing binding_profile, binding_profile="ak.profile.mls_governance_binding.full.v1", or an unsupported profile id is a fail-closed mismatch.
downgrade_declaration_obligation.export_marker_required: Sync metadata, snapshots, backups, exports, and interop mapping receipts that summarize the Realm MUST preserve e2ee_relaxed=true and relaxed_window_max_ms. Consumers that observe advisory semantics without this marker MUST assume the downgrade is undeclared and reject new old-epoch decrypt admission.

client_ui_requirements.banner_warning: Realms declaring this profile MUST display a banner-level warning indicating that kick / ban is not cryptographically immediate; the warning MAY be temporarily collapsed but MUST NOT be permanently dismissable.
client_ui_requirements.invite_warning: When a user invites a new member, the UI SHOULD prompt with 'this Realm uses degraded E2EE' so the invitee can make an informed decision.
client_ui_requirements.export_marker: Sync metadata / backup / export MUST preserve a `e2ee_relaxed=true` marker so downstream consumers know the cryptographic guarantee is relaxed.

downgrade_window_constraint.rationale: Receiving client refuses to admit a message into verified timeline if the gap between receive_at and the most recent membership_change_at exceeds this window with old-epoch decryption.
downgrade_window_constraint.receiver_enforcement: Receiver MUST enforce the hard ceiling independently of any declared deployment value: if a Realm policy event sets relaxed_window_max_ms > absolute_hard_ceiling_ms (300000 ms / 5 min), the reducer MUST reject the policy update with reason_code `relaxed_window_exceeds_ceiling` (mapped from `schema_violation`), and the receiver MUST treat the policy event as failed_precondition. Receivers MUST NOT silently clamp the value to the ceiling, because a silent clamp would let a deployment publish a longer window than receivers honor and split visible policy state across implementations. Negative vector: `ak.vector.e2ee_relaxed.window_exceeds_ceiling.v1` covers (a) reducer reject on policy write > 300000 ms, (b) receiver reject on old-epoch decrypt admission when the gap exceeds the per-policy declared window, and (c) reject when any deployment tries to redefine the ceiling via an unrelated profile.
downgrade_window_constraint.compliance_profile_disabled: Profiles in the compliance / audited tier (ak.profile.attested_audit.e2ee.v1, ak.profile.disclosed_audit.e2ee.v1, and any deployment with active Audit Applet Binding) MUST NOT enable ak.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1. Reducer MUST reject the combination with reason_code `e2ee_relaxed_disallowed_in_compliance_profile`. Rationale: compliance assurance presumes the kick-out semantic is cryptographically immediate; the relaxed window contradicts that presumption.

restricted_requires: each federation peer describes a fanout SLA not exceeding the relaxed window
each federation peer explicitly advertises ak.feature.e2ee_relaxed.v1 when it is expected to accept relaxed old-epoch decrypt admission
federation_guard.interop_floor: Full MLS governance binding (ak.profile.mls_governance_binding.full.v1) remains the federation E2EE interoperability floor. The relaxed profile (ak.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1) is a declared downgrade below that floor and is accepted across federation only for restricted/closed deployments that satisfy the bounded-SLA requirements above.

fail_closed_conditions: combination of ak.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1 with ak.profile.mls_governance_binding.full.v1, compliance-tier E2EE, active Audit Applet Binding, federation_policy=open, or federation_policy=quarantine
restricted federation without peer fanout SLA bounds within relaxed_window_max_ms
governance_binding.binding_profile missing, unsupported, or inconsistent with the Realm downgrade declaration
receiver old-epoch decrypt gap exceeds relaxed_window_max_ms or the absolute hard ceiling of 300000 ms
ak.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1.compliance_unfit: Compliance / regulatory contexts that require 'kick-out is immediately effective' MUST NOT use this profile. Use non-E2EE Realm (encryption_profile="none") + enclave channels instead. Spec deliberately does not allow further relaxation than this profile; deployments needing more leniency are out of v1 E2EE scope.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: return unsupported_feature for managed-only action

ak.profile.directory_service.v1.description: Arkret v1 Directory Service profile. Directory Services index resource-signed discovery state, expose blinded search/resolve endpoints, and support at least one §8 ingest mode without becoming a source of truth.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: omit optional profile or return unsupported_feature without leaking hidden resources
return unsupported_feature
omit optional operation or return unsupported_feature

additional_requirements.invite_claim_reducer_authority_must: ak.invite.claim MUST be decided by the destination Realm reducer, not by Auth Server, verification service, Sync Service ingress, or client projection caches.
additional_requirements.invite_claim_token_commitment_must: Reducer MUST match payload.token_commitment to the pending ak.invite.third_party invite and reject mismatch or already-claimed commitments with no membership proposal.
additional_requirements.invite_claim_allowlist_recheck_must: Reducer MUST re-check binding_proof.verification_service_id against the current effective Realm allowlist and any invite-pinned service DID before accepting subject_proof.
additional_requirements.invite_claim_nonce_dedup_must: Reducer MUST treat (invite_id, claim_nonce) and token_commitment as one-time constraints and reject replay with duplicate_conflict.
additional_requirements.invite_claim_membership_conversion_must: Successful claim MUST atomically transition invite pending -> claimed and materialize only a subject-bound standard invite or membership proposal; final join still requires ak.invite.accept or an explicitly profiled equivalent path.
additional_requirements.invite_claim_expiry_cleanup_must: Reducer MUST expire third-party invites before claim acceptance when expires_at <= now and trigger token material cleanup obligations from third-party-invites.md §6.1.

prose_requirement_coverage.requirement: service DID authentication and destination binding validation
federation transaction idempotency and per-item accepted/rejected/quarantine results
signed Event Envelope verification and authorization
batch, event size and retry rules

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: reject unsupported profile before accepting events

e2ee_mls_interop_floor.applies_when: Any federation transaction carries or depends on encryption_profile="mls_rfc9420", ak.mls.genesis, ak.mls.commit, ak.mls.welcome, MLS-backed E2EE DataEvents, or active MLS security-frontier state.
e2ee_mls_interop_floor.downgrade_admission: Only closed or restricted federation may accept ak.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1, and restricted federation MUST satisfy the bounded-SLA federation_guard in that profile. Open and quarantine federation MUST reject the relaxed downgrade.
e2ee_mls_interop_floor.fail_closed_behavior: A receiver that cannot verify the minimum profile, sees a missing/inconsistent binding_profile or reducer_profile, or cannot prove the relaxed federation guard MUST reject or quarantine the affected MLS artifact/DataEvent before advancing Realm frontier.

ak.profile.service_resolution_mirror.v1.description: Optional Realm-scoped route-availability profile. It implements target-signed planned handover publication and authorized peer mirror resolution without becoming service identity or route authority.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: Omit the profile and both peer operations; normal current-record bootstrap and direct 1:1 handover remain usable when independently implemented, while an unannounced outage without another authorized carrier fails closed.

additional_requirements.target_signature_must: A mirror returns only byte-exact target-service-signed ServiceResolutionRecord and ServiceRouteHandoverNotice values; its own transport signature can never authorize a bare URL.
additional_requirements.visibility_must: Requester and target must both be currently visible in the named Realm through effective binding, sync endpoint or explicit delegation; unknown, unauthorized, invisible and not-held responses are indistinguishable.
additional_requirements.durability_must: Remote record sequence/digest floors, notice revision/digest state and publish acknowledgements survive restart; replaceable TTL route cache is not this safety state.
additional_requirements.bounds_must: Resolve returns at most 32 continuous records and at most 256 KiB canonical response bytes.

ak.profile.signal_message_stream.v1.description: Optional client payload profile for authenticated transient Message generation previews carried inside the encrypted Signal Extension.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: omit live generation previews and continue receiving the final ak.message.create; never place ak.message.stream in durable Event history

additional_requirements.encrypted_only_must: Every ak.message.stream payload MUST be encrypted inside ak.schema.signal_envelope.v1 with signal_class=session; no plaintext branch exists.
additional_requirements.authorization_must: The recipient MUST verify ak.message.stream.send plus ak.message.create for the decrypted Strand at the envelope seal_ref basis before display.
additional_requirements.resource_must: Producer and recipient enforce 16 KiB preview, 5 frames/s, 8 concurrent streams, 15-second keyframes and 10-minute lifetime within the generic 48 KiB plaintext / 64 KiB Signal envelope limits.
additional_requirements.final_binding_must: Only a direct, verified ak.message.create with a message_id matching the complete retyped EventId token, actor, device, security scope, Realm, Strand and discussion track replaces the preview.

ak.profile.signal_peer_relay.v1.description: Optional symmetric Principal Server profile for the encrypted Signal Extension single-hop peer relay. It does not imply durable Event federation and does not advertise any product signal kind.

prose_requirement_coverage.requirement: single-hop peer authentication, current member delivery binding and unchanged producer envelope
bounded batch/body/signature window and drop-unconfirmed retry behavior

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: omit ak.profile.signal_peer_relay.v1 and ak.peer.signal.command.relay; local Signal and durable federation remain independently usable

additional_requirements.encrypted_only_must: Every relayed item MUST be ak.schema.signal_envelope.v1; plaintext or legacy ephemeral inputs fail closed with signal_plaintext_forbidden.
additional_requirements.single_hop_must: A destination MUST NOT relay a peer-received SignalEnvelope to a third service. The original sender-side service performs one direct request per eligible destination service.
additional_requirements.no_kind_advertisement_must: Describe MUST advertise only this profile and operation support; exact product signal kind and target remain encrypted and MUST NOT appear in supported-kinds or routing metadata.
additional_requirements.opaque_outcome_must: A valid authenticated request returns only {accepted:true}; no recipient, binding, capability, count or per-item outcome is exposed.
additional_requirements.retry_must: The operation forbids Idempotency-Key, is retry_safe=false and uses uncertain_outcome.strategy=drop_unconfirmed. A lost response MUST NOT cause automatic request replay.

ak.profile.federation.high_assurance.v1.description: High-assurance / sovereign / regulated / multi-writer federation profile. Adds mandatory proactive frontier exchange with fail-state semantics on top of the ak.profile.federation_minimal.v1 baseline. See zh/sync/federation.md §4.5.3 and zh/sync/sovereign-deployment.md §11.1.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: reject claim of ak.profile.federation.high_assurance.v1 if proactive frontier exchange or stale_peer fail-state is not implemented

additional_requirements.frontier_probe_capability_must: Peer MUST expose capability-gated frontier probe endpoint per federation.md §4.5.1.
additional_requirements.proactive_exchange_must: Per federation-visible Realm, per authorized peer, frontier probe interval MUST be <= 3600 seconds.
additional_requirements.fail_state_must: Three consecutive probe failures (peer unreachable or signature failure) MUST mark the peer as 'stale_peer' for that Realm. Separately, an aggregate-commitment difference MUST first be reduced via per-actor challenge/backfill on the intersection of replicated actors, comparing each (realm_id, actor_id, actor_seq) as a canonical sibling SET of (event_id,event_digest,prev_frontier_digest), not as a single hash. Different event_id/hash siblings at one actor_seq are legal within the event-and-patch.md §2.6 limits and MUST converge by validated set union. A same-event_id/different-digest conflict, an over-limit sibling set, a profile-declared non-joinable sibling conflict, or inconsistent witness payloads for the same complete attestation scope MUST quarantine the affected increments on the FIRST confirmed occurrence and MUST NOT be folded into the three-consecutive-failure window. Raw frontier_root/heads/range-root differences across different scopes, and incomplete subsets of a legal sibling set, MUST NOT alone count as probe failure or witness_disagreement.

Stale status MUST clear after the original evidence is resolved: the disputed event id/digest or over-fork/non-joinable sibling bucket has an authorized canonical resolution and the peer matches that canonical sibling set, or witnesses for the same complete attestation scope again sign one consistent payload. Scope-different peers MUST NOT be required to have globally identical heads.

ak.profile.auth_server.v1.description: Arkret v1 Auth Server profile. Auth Servers verify login factors (password / passkey / OIDC / SSO / recovery), issue short-lived audience-bound `ak.session.grant` artefacts, expose session-grant introspection / revocation, and MAY surface a `ak.self.policy.read.check` decision endpoint. Auth Servers are NOT canonical identity registries (DID documents / key logs live in `ak.profile.identity_registry.v1`) and are NOT principal servers (no Realm-authoritative event acceptance). additional_requirements.session_grant_must_be_short_lived: Auth Server MUST cap session_grant TTL well below the Realm policy review horizon (per device-lifecycle.md §5, typical ceiling is minutes-to-hours, not days).
additional_requirements.audience_binding_must: Every issued session_grant MUST carry an `audience` claim; auth servers MUST refuse to issue grants for audiences they have not been configured to serve.
additional_requirements.session_grant_release_readiness_must: Release readiness MUST cover ak.vector.auth.session_grant_audience_binding.v1, ak.vector.auth.soft_logout_did_proof.v1 and ak.vector.auth.session_grant_issuer_record.v1: proof binds challenge, audience, request_canonical_digest, principal and device; suite-tagged issuer-record ID/JTI recomputation, credential-class holder/bootstrap binding inclusion, canonical JWK, exact replay/conflict/terminal outcomes and DPoP binding are exercised; stranger audiences are rejected; soft_logged_out recovery requires fresh proof; development_mode=true never advertises verified profiles.
additional_requirements.session_grant_issuer_ledger_must: Auth Server MUST be the sole durable authority for immutable SessionGrant issuance records and active/revoked/superseded lifecycle. It MUST derive the suite-tagged grant ID and JWT jti from the complete closed issuance preimage, including the credential-class-selected holder/bootstrap/recovery binding, atomically persist issuance before response, provide durable exact replay for issue, refresh and revoke, and use the same ledger for cascade and introspection. It MUST NOT author ak.session.grant or ak.session.grant.state Events or depend on a Principal Control Realm grant cell.
additional_requirements.session_grant_dpop_binding_must: Issue, refresh, replay retrieval and protected-resource presentation MUST verify current holder/DPoP proof, exact HTTP target and method, issuer/audience and canonical request digest. An S2S HTTP Message Signature authenticates transport only and never substitutes for holder proof or principal/device/notary Event proof.
additional_requirements.session_grant_terminal_replay_must: Exact replay of an expired recorded outcome returns session_grant_replay_expired; exact replay of a revoked or superseded recorded outcome returns session_grant_replay_terminal with grant_id and terminal state. Neither path returns success or issues a new grant. After replay-record retention expires, the same request identity fails closed as indeterminate.
additional_requirements.not_identity_registry_must: Auth Server MUST NOT claim `ak.profile.identity_registry.v1`; any DID document / key-log surface it exposes MUST be declared on `compat_surfaces[]` as `delegated_resolver` rather than self-claimed canonical authority.
additional_requirements.not_principal_server_must: Auth Server MUST NOT claim `ak.profile.principal_server.v1`; Realm event acceptance is the principal server role and is incompatible with auth-server-only deployments.
additional_requirements.verified_profiles_dev_mode_must: When `development_mode=true`, `verified_profiles[]` MUST be `[]` per sync/service-surface.md §3.0; cotest writes verified entries only after a passing verified-profile suite run.
additional_requirements.account_status_publication_must: An Auth Server acting as Account Authority MUST first obtain the PCR-bound issuer actor frontier and accepted Seal frontier through ak.peer.account_status.read.authoring_basis, then sign authority_evidence and publish every ak.account.status transition through ak.peer.account_status.command.submit to the bound Principal Server; it MUST NOT synthesize an empty basis, impersonate a holder session, or use a deployment-private route.
additional_requirements.provisional_identity_abandonment_must: An Auth Server that offers provisional-identity abandonment MUST expose it as the two-step issue_identity_abandonment_challenge + abandon_identity_creation pair and MUST NOT reach the same effect from login, session resume, lease expiry, fence takeover or garbage collection. Both operations are authorized by the account handoff grant alone, because a never-accepted PCR leaves the holder without a principal and therefore without any principal-bound ak.session.grant; the confirmation MUST present a fresh handoff and MUST NOT reuse the grant that obtained the challenge. The challenge is single-use, at most 300 seconds, held in shared durable state, and pins account_subject, holder cnf.jkt, the abandoned principal_id and did_version_id, the identity-creation lease id and fence, and the closed consequence disclosure; expiry and prior consumption remain distinct terminal states. Consuming the challenge, recording the orphan-anchor tombstone / audit reservation, suppressing the reserved_identity_creation checkpoint on every holder-readable surface and releasing the lease MUST commit in one transaction with zero writes on any failure, and replaying the same request_id MUST return the same terminal outcome without a second tombstone. A PCR accepted between issuance and confirmation MUST fail with identity_creation_already_accepted and MUST NOT abandon anything. Re-authentication strength, risk checks, cooldown length, orphan-anchor discovery annotation, handle and namespace release and retention are deployment governance and are not conformance criteria.

ak.profile.circle_conformance.v1.description: Conformance profile pinning the machine-contract surface for Circle (intra-Realm scoped event/message boundary; see zh/models/circle.md). Splits actor content payload (`scope_circle_id` where that object schema defines it), the signed Event `scope_ref`, and the materialized object's `effective_scope`; it also pins the Circle event-kind family, member-state transition table, encryption-profile compatibility, and scope-rebind reducer-reject semantics. feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: implementations that cannot verify the signed Event scope_ref and its equivalence to reducer-derived scope MUST NOT claim ak.profile.circle_conformance.v1; receivers MUST treat any unknown Circle event-kind as schema_violation

additional_requirements.submit_payload_must: Object payload schemas that own scope_circle_id (including Strand, Morph, Relation, and scoped Space create/update shapes) MAY carry only that field as their actor-authored scope selector and MUST reject effective_scope (reason=effective_scope_reducer_managed). Message and structural-operation payloads derive scope from accepted target references and MUST NOT invent a duplicate scope_circle_id; every Event still carries the producer-signed scope_ref.
additional_requirements.canonical_reducer_output_must: The producer MUST sign the tagged Event scope_ref. The receiver MUST derive the effective scope from the frozen pre-state and payload, require exact equality with scope_ref, and materialize the same value as the object's read-only effective_scope. A later scope_circle_id rebind MUST NOT re-interpret historical Events or objects.
additional_requirements.scope_rebind_default_reject_must: Default reducer MUST reject scope_circle_id rebind (None<->Some, Some(A)->Some(B)) with failed_precondition reason=scope_rebind_forbidden. Profile-declared audit-paired rebind MAY be permitted, but MUST emit ak.audit.accessed pairing.
additional_requirements.circle_encryption_profile_floor_must: Circle.encryption_profile may be none or mls_rfc9420. Reducer MUST reject plaintext Circle creation or update when the parent Realm encryption_profile is mls_rfc9420 or the effective content_encryption_floor is e2ee_required (reason=circle_encryption_below_realm_floor).
additional_requirements.circle_content_encryption_floor_must: Circle.content_encryption_floor (allow_plaintext | e2ee_required) is optional and symmetric with Circle.metadata_encryption_floor: when omitted it inherits the parent Realm content_encryption_floor, and the effective floor = max(parent Realm content_encryption_floor, Circle content_encryption_floor). Reducer MUST reject a Circle floor below the effective floor and MUST reject content_encryption_floor=e2ee_required on an encryption_profile=none Circle (reason=circle_encryption_below_realm_floor). See zh/models/circle.md §7.
additional_requirements.encryption_floor_ratchet_must: The effective content_encryption_floor and effective metadata encryption floor of any scope (Realm-default or Circle) are one-way ratchets: monotonically non-decreasing over time. A ak.realm.policy_bundle or ak.circle.update that lowers the effective content floor from e2ee_required to allow_plaintext MUST be rejected (reason=content_encryption_floor_downgrade); one that lowers the effective metadata floor MUST be rejected (reason=metadata_encryption_floor_downgrade). Tightening is always allowed. Vectors: ak.vector.e2ee.content_floor_downgrade_rejected.v1, ak.vector.e2ee.metadata_floor_downgrade_rejected.v1, ak.vector.circle.content_floor_below_realm_rejected.v1, ak.vector.e2ee.in_place_enable.v1.
additional_requirements.circle_membership_subset_must: Circle.members MUST be a strict subset of parent Realm.members; reducer MUST reject ak.circle.member.state -> join when the target actor is not a `join` member of the parent Realm (reason=circle_member_must_be_realm_member).
additional_requirements.scope_invariant_must: Sync Service MUST NOT deliver Events with scope_ref.kind=circle to actors not in that Circle's member frontier at the Event's causal frontier (see zh/models/circle.md §9.3 scope-delivery invariant).

registry/account-data-key-registry.json.description: Canonical registry of standard Account Data key patterns. Account Data is actor/private state written through ak.account_data.set unless a row explicitly lists another actor-private event kind. Every row MUST declare its cross-device merge primitive (merge_strategy) and delete semantics (deletion_mode); see spec/v1/zh/models/account-data.md section 5.
registry_rules: merge_strategy is the machine-readable cross-device convergence primitive for the key. v1 defines exactly one value, cas_register: the key is a server-versioned compare-and-set whole-value register, every write carries expected_revision and the accepted revision is expected_revision + 1. There is no implicit default; a row without merge_strategy is invalid.

Adding an uncoordinated merge primitive requires a new merge_strategy value plus, on the same row, its comparison transcript, tombstone rule and an active conformance vector. Domain rules such as HLC last-writer-wins or delete-wins run inside the client's compare-and-set retry loop over decrypted plaintext; the server sees only opaque bytes and MUST NOT be asked to merge them.

deletion_mode declares how a key stops holding a live value. physical_delete uses ak.self.account_data.resource.delete, which stores a versioned tombstone and MAY garbage-collect it later; the per-key revision high-water mark is retained forever so a stale write can never resurrect a deleted value. value_tombstone means the deleted state is itself a value written through ak.account_data.set and MUST NOT be physically deleted, because the domain requires an unrevivable terminal state that stays observable after tombstone GC.

registry/authority-set-policy-registry.j.description: Canonical registry of authority-set policy symbols and deterministic projections from accepted CBA control state. Registry rows are templates, not authority: each lease carries the concrete AuthoritySetPolicy and its digest, and verifiers rederive it from basis_ref plus CBA closure.
registry_rules: authority_set_id values MUST be unique and MUST match the concrete AuthoritySetPolicy.authority_set_id
A concrete policy MUST use the registered policy_kind and source_kind, then project authorization_rules exactly from fixed_rules or rules_source
authorization_rules MUST be ordered lexicographically by rule_id; each rule's issuers MUST be ordered lexicographically by verification_method and allowed_actions MUST be ordered lexicographically

A lease is authorized only by the unique registered rule whose rule_id equals authorization_rule_id and whose allowed_actions covers action; different rules MAY cover the same action, rules are alternatives, and proofs MUST NOT be combined across rules
authority_set_digest is SHA-256(JCS(the complete concrete AuthoritySetPolicy object))
A verifier MUST rederive source_ref, source_digest, generation_ref and issuer verification methods from the accepted basis; inline policy bytes are portable evidence, not an authority source
A candidate or post-basis control object MUST NOT create authority for a lease evaluated at an earlier basis

policies.rules_source: accepted_recovery_policy.publication_authorization_rules rederived from allowed_proof_kinds and linked accepted state

projection.authorization_rules: one rule per allowed proof kind; principal_signing/recovery_unlock/trusted service use threshold 1, device_quorum uses device_quorum.k, threshold_recovery uses its recovered signing key with threshold 1 (Shamir reconstruction k is not a signature quorum)

registry_rules: A non-grant authorization source is active only when one exact active row is selected by authority_source_id; syntax or an arbitrary Event/cell reference never creates authority.

The evaluator MUST rederive all activation, actor, resource and lifecycle predicates from accepted signed evidence at the Event CBA basis or the current non-event request basis and MUST fail closed on missing, conflicting, non-canonical or freshness-unknown dependencies.
Profile-scoped sources do not enter issuer_authority_refs, cannot authorize ak.capability.grant, and cannot be widened by Realm owner/admin aggregation.

When an Event is directly participant-authored, authorization_ref uses the source wire_ref and refs contains the registered binding_ref_role. When executed_by is present, authorization_ref continues to bind the delegated executor grant/delegation; the profile source is an independent conjunctive evaluator gate and is never replaced by that delegation.
