registry_rules: A calendar schedule MUST carry a signed tzdb_version naming one release row below. Receivers resolve timezone and every derived instant with that release, never with their locally installed release.

Release rows are append-only and each row is frozen once published, including its own required_normalizations table, because historical schedules signed that row. Withdrawing a release is expressed by setting status=deprecated, never by deleting or rewriting the row.

required_normalizations is per release, not global. A later IANA release that changes a Link target expresses that by carrying a different mapping in its own row; the earlier row keeps the mapping that was in force when those schedules were signed. A global table could not represent both at once and would silently break the append-only promise.

Determinism comes from the release tag: IANA tzdata release tags are immutable once published. This registry deliberately does not mirror the full Zone/Link table and does not pin a distribution digest, because a hand-copied mirror would drift from IANA and become a second truth source, and this repository cannot verify third-party distribution bytes. Deployments that additionally need supply-chain pinning verify the distribution in their own build; that pinning is out of scope for v1 interop.

Canonicalization is defined by the Link declarations of the pinned IANA release as published by IANA, in particular its backward and etcetera files: the canonical Zone is the Link target. It is NOT defined by whatever a given platform time zone library happens to expose, since distributions may build the same release with different link handling.

Producers MUST rewrite timezone to the canonical Zone before signing. Receivers MUST NOT re-canonicalize a signed value: an alias that reaches the wire is a producer defect and MUST be rejected, not repaired. The RSVP occurrence key reuses the exact signed timezone value.

Each row required_normalizations is the conformance-required subset that vectors pin for that release. It is not the full alias set; an input outside the table is still canonicalized by that release Link declarations.

Updating a schedule tzdb_version MAY change derived instants but MUST NOT change the signed timezone value or any local occurrence key. When any occurrence instant or end changes, the significant-change table requires RSVP needs_reconfirmation plus a schedule notification.

A service that cannot execute a schedule tzdb_version MUST fail closed with calendar_tzdb_mismatch or unsupported_feature, or mark instant projection unresolved. Falling back to a nearby or newer release is forbidden. Services declare their executable set in ServiceDescribe.calendar_tzdb_versions.

releases.notes: v1 conformance baseline release. Frozen: this row required_normalizations is the mapping schedules pinned to 2025a were signed against.
Appended release; schedules pinned to it expand with its rules only. Its required_normalizations is identical to 2025a because no listed Link target changed between the two releases.

risk_tier_definitions.low: Read, projection, discovery, ack, and account-private affordances. Freshness fail-closed treats unknown / stale as local-pending allowed (capabilities.md §18).
risk_tier_definitions.medium: Object create / update / delete, message authoring, invite issuance, MLS proposal, audit query. Freshness requires recent frontier within freshness_required_ms.
risk_tier_definitions.high: Capability mutation, policy mutation, lifecycle freeze / tombstone / destroy, schema redefinition, MLS commit / welcome / genesis, audit export, moderation decision, admin / hierarchy / upgrade. Freshness MUST be within freshness_required_ms; partition forces local pending with no peer visibility.

registry_rules: Wire capability grant.actions[] entries MUST be drawn from this registry; wildcards / segment globs are statically rejected by capability-grant.schema.json.

Receivers MUST default to risk_tier=high when an action submitted in a grant or evaluated in policy is not present in this registry; this is the freshness fail-closed default required by capabilities.md §18.

required_constraints lists typed-constraint shorthand names that the capability evaluator MUST enforce for the action regardless of the grant author's declarations; absence in this list does NOT disable other declared constraints.

required_evaluator_checks lists non-grant-field invariants (for example actor_eq_target_author or audit_pair_required) that admission control MUST enforce from Event context, reducer state, or paired audit evidence. These are not grant-constraint schema fields.

target_event_kinds links the action to one or more ak.* event_kinds in event_kind_registry. Empty array means the action authorizes a read / projection / signaling path that does not produce a durable reducer-input event. Reducer admission for a listed event_kind MUST verify the actor holds at least one matching action grant.

profile is null for v1 core actions, or a ak.profile.*.v<n> id when the action is only meaningful inside that profile. Receivers without the named profile MUST treat the action as unknown (risk_tier=high default).

Every action MUST declare event_mapping_kind. action == single target_event_kind uses same_name; empty target_event_kinds uses non_event_surface; any other mapping MUST use one of the allowed deviation categories.

grant_authority_actions lists the action ids an issuer holding this action MAY sign a grant for (capabilities.md section 3.2 issuer upper bound). It is a separate namespace from target_event_kinds, which only expresses direct Event admission: several actions can map to one event kind, so an event-kind subset MUST NOT be used to satisfy an action-level grant authority question.

coverage_rule and grant_authority_rule declare how target_event_kinds and grant_authority_actions are derived from the other rows. When a rule is present the materialized list is a cached projection: tools/artifact_pipeline.py generate rewrites it and check rejects any hand edit on either this registry or the generated view.

root_control_only=true marks an action that only the current controller of the Realm authority-root cell may author. It is never grantable and never enters a derived owner authority set. subject_only=true marks a self-service action whose only authority is the target subject's own signature. reducer_only=true marks a record the reducer materializes and no principal may author. The three flags are orthogonal and combinable.

actions.notes: Authorizes the installed Applet service to invoke the closed Ghost Actor provisioning aggregate for one exact effective Realm scope. The operation accepts the caller-signed ak.identity.accountability_grant + ak.profile.create pair atomically; it is not a generic authorization for either Event kind.

Reducer-materialized record of a Realm-link inheritance derivation (zh/models/realm-links.md section 6). No principal authors it and no principal can be granted it, so it is excluded from every derived owner authority set.

Subject-only self-service release of the actor own grant. Authority comes from the target grant subject signature and the reducer target guard, never from a capability, so it is excluded from every derived authority set.

Read-only audit access for a Realm admin NOT in the target Circle. MUST be paired with ak.audit.accessed event. Does NOT yield historical decryption keys unless the admin is formally added to the Circle.

Creates an intra-Realm Circle (scoped event/message boundary; optionally MLS-backed depending on parent Realm floor). NOT in default member bundle by default — Circles should be few and stable. See zh/models/circle.md §8.
Manage an existing Circle. MUST be constrained to specific circle_id selectors; unconstrained Realm-wide grant is not a normal management permission.
Self-service: actor accepts an invite, joins a join_rule=open Circle, or leaves. Reducer enforces payload.actor_id == envelope.actor_id and transition legality. Self-unbanning MUST fail closed.
Cross-actor write (rare). MUST carry ak.audit.accessed pair (same model as ak.strand.watch.set.others).
Invite / remove others. Held by Circle admin. payload.actor_id != envelope.actor_id.

Authorizes only the transaction-bound old-series targets in a fixed SecurityRotationTransaction plan after both replacement active-series pointers are accepted. It never authorizes deleting an active or unplanned backup series.
Direct Conversation participant self-leave only. It never authorizes leave/ban/remove of the other participant or any join transition.

Accepted-at compensation for a self-authored join only. It authorizes one fresh standard leave transition for the exact admission and old membership incarnation; it cannot be transferred or used as ordinary membership authority.

Accepted-at compensation for a delegated/admin-authored join only. It authorizes one fresh standard remove transition for the exact admission and old membership incarnation; it grants no Realm admin capability.

Direct Conversation exact-pair self-rejoin only. It never authorizes a first join, a third participant, or a join authored on behalf of the other participant, and it never authorizes any grant, policy, admin, Strand or binding change.

Authorizes adding an audience_mention node such as @all or @here to a Message create/revise. @here maps to audience="strand_engaged" and is not presence-filtered. This is an additional gate: the actor MUST also be authorized for the underlying message create/revise action. Effective Realm/Circle policy MUST allow the audience and declare finite max_recipients/quota before notification fanout.

Authorizes a decrypted ak.message.stream Signal payload for one discussion Strand. It is an additional recipient-verified gate: the sender MUST also hold ak.message.create. The service cannot inspect or advertise the encrypted payload kind or Strand target.

Narrow Direct Conversation participant authority for welcoming another currently authorized device of the same stable participant. It cannot add a third principal or a device of the other participant.
Authorizes reading an object's discussion / history events (message timeline, redacted-message metainfo, prior revisions). Read / projection surface only; emits no durable reducer event.

Claims, renames or tombstones the Realm's human-readable alias (ak.realm.alias event; projects ak.component.realm.alias.v1). high risk because an alias is the address users type and share: capturing or re-pointing one is a phishing / impersonation primitive. Holding ak.realm.admin (aggregate admin coverage) satisfies admission, or grant this specific action directly. See zh/discovery/object-addressing.md §3.3.

Re-anchors the authority-root capability-action registry digest to a retrievable, recomputable, active snapshot. Changes neither controller nor generation and never retroactively widens an existing grant.
Advances the authority generation, invalidating every grant anchored to the previous one at read time. Destructive root control; never grantable.

Terminal Realm lifecycle. Authored only by the current controller of the Realm authority-root cell with an independent destructive confirmation; it MUST NOT be granted to anyone, so it is excluded from every derived owner authority set.

Highest explicit authority inside one Realm. Held either by the current controller of the ak.component.realm.authority_root.v1 cell (root authority, not a grant) or by an ordinary revocable co-owner grant. Both derived sets are rule-generated; hand edits are rejected by tools/artifact_pipeline.py check.

Rotates the controller binding of the Realm authority-root cell. Authored only by the current controller with successor acceptance; it MUST NOT be granted, so it is excluded from every derived owner authority set.

Sets / changes the Realm's authoritative default discussion Strand pointer (ak.realm.set_default_strand event; projects Realm default_strand_id). Same-name discipline. The Realm authz gate is realm-admin: holding ak.realm.admin (aggregate admin coverage) satisfies admission, or grant this specific action directly. Reducer MUST verify the referenced Strand already exists (failed_precondition otherwise). See zh/models/strand-and-message.md default-Strand discovery section.
Terminal Realm lifecycle with a successor pointer. Same root-control family as ak.realm.destroy: authored only by the current authority-root controller and never grantable.

Authorizes durable history-key delivery after the independent membership, device, history-sharing policy, source_authorization_ref, and recipient checks succeed. This explicit high-risk action is not implied by ak.realm.admin.

event_mapping_kind_definitions.same_name: Action maps one-to-one to an identically named durable event kind.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.non_event_surface: Action authorizes read/projection/signaling behavior that does not emit a durable reducer event.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.aggregate_admin: Action intentionally covers a bounded administrative family of event kinds.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.polymorphic_object: Action covers the same object-lifecycle verb across multiple object event kinds.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.scope_suffix_variant: Action adds actor/scope/role qualifiers while reducer admission targets a shared event kind.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.operation_verb: Action token names an operation/command verb that does not match its target event kind name(s); reducer admission resolves the resulting event kind(s) via target_event_kinds. Literal action matching per the actions[] rule applies; carries no aggregate-admin family semantics.

registry_rules: track_names[] is the canonical source for every Strand.tracks map key; syntax alone never admits a name.
New writes MUST use an active row. Unknown, deprecated, duplicate, or owner-unresolvable names fail closed with schema_violation.
owner.kind=schema requires schema_ref to resolve to an effective reference registered by schema_registry; owner.kind=profile requires profile_id to resolve in conformance-profiles.json.
Profiles MAY add a TrackName only by adding an owned row here, regenerating track-name-registry.json, and updating the versioned Strand schema TrackName enum in the same protocol change.

track_names.description: Message and discussion timeline section of a Strand.
Authoritative structured and narrative synthesis section of a Strand.

registry_rules: A non-grant authorization source is active only when one exact active row is selected by authority_source_id; syntax or an arbitrary Event/cell reference never creates authority.

The evaluator MUST rederive all activation, actor, resource and lifecycle predicates from accepted signed evidence at the Event CBA basis or the current non-event request basis and MUST fail closed on missing, conflicting, non-canonical or freshness-unknown dependencies.
Profile-scoped sources do not enter issuer_authority_refs, cannot authorize ak.capability.grant, and cannot be widened by Realm owner/admin aggregation.

When an Event is directly participant-authored, authorization_ref uses the source wire_ref and refs contains the registered binding_ref_role. When executed_by is present, authorization_ref continues to bind the delegated executor grant/delegation; the profile source is an independent conjunctive evaluator gate and is never replaced by that delegation.

wire_scope_definitions.durable_event: Valid Event Envelope kind for persisted canonical history and reducer input.
wire_scope_definitions.actor_private_event: Persisted actor-private/account-data event; not shared Realm history and not Realm reducer input.

admission_class_definitions.capability_gated: Gated by capability actions. The authorizing actions are exactly the ones whose target_event_kinds list this kind in capability-action-registry; there is no second per-event list. Reducer MUST verify the actor holds a matching action grant. Fail-closed.
admission_class_definitions.conditional: Admission is selected from the event row's closed admission_variants. Receivers evaluate every non-otherwise predicate using admission_predicate_contract: exactly one match selects that variant, more than one match is fail-closed, and zero matches selects the single final otherwise variant. The otherwise branch is a fallback and is not counted as a simultaneously matching predicate. Each selected variant applies its own admission class and capabilities.
admission_class_definitions.crypto_verifiable: Admitted by cryptographic verification of the payload against group/key state (MLS epoch, key material, franking) and its policy preconditions. Reducer MUST verify the cryptographic binding; not a user capability. Fail-closed.
admission_class_definitions.delegated_pcr_genesis: Admitted only for a PCR ak.realm.create with no did_inception ref and with both executed_by and authorization_ref. A purpose=managed_agent_control Native Agent branch MUST carry exactly one critical refs[] role=agent_provision pointing to the accepted controller-authored ak.agent.provision Event; the verifier cross-binds actor_id, realm_id, controller, PCR delegation and provision payload before the reducer materializes the Agent active status cell. An explicitly organization-governed purpose=principal_control branch MUST carry zero agent_provision refs and MUST prove its separate accepted organization authority. The two branches are disjoint; a self-principal or generic realm.create capability substitution is rejected. This class never authorizes a following device-authorize slot by itself.
admission_class_definitions.deny: Explicit fail-closed admission branch. Selection always rejects the Event as failed_precondition/schema_violation and MUST NOT consult capabilities or alternate proof paths.
admission_class_definitions.registration_anchor: Admitted only for self-principal PCR genesis using durable registration-time DID control evidence and one critical did_inception ref. The verifier validates the accepted-at adapter/method evidence and project(full_id)=actor_id; current DID state after registration is irrelevant.
admission_class_definitions.pcr_recovery: Admitted only for ak.device.reanchor under the authority instance's accepted PCR recovery policy/session and monotonic generation CAS. did_root is merely one optional policy-enabled factor. A current DID proof without the matching authority instance and policy cannot enter this class.
admission_class_definitions.direct_conversation_agent_genesis: Admitted only for an ak.realm.create that carries exactly one critical refs[] role=direct_conversation_agent_provision pointing to an accepted ak.agent.provision Event. Used solely for the controller-to-own-Agent Direct Conversation branch, which has no Contact basis. The verifier cross-binds participants to exactly that controller and Agent, requires the Direct Conversation profile rather than a PCR profile, checks the controller binding is current, and fixes founder = controller so the Agent runtime key never needs Direct Conversation founding scope. This role is structurally exclusive with direct_conversation_basis and with the managed-Agent PCR agent_provision role.
admission_class_definitions.direct_conversation_genesis: Admitted only for an ak.realm.create that carries exactly one critical refs[] role=direct_conversation_basis pointing to the portable Contact basis evidence bundle and its continuity chain to the pair's root founder basis. The verifier derives founder from the root basis core (normal branch: the sorted_pair_members entry that is not the request_event_ref issuer, i.e. the responder; glare branch: the requests[0] issuer), then requires created_by == actor_id == founder, recomputes pair_key from sorted_pair_members and the trust domain, and pins the Direct Conversation profile, exact-two participants and the create-locked encryption and history baseline. Accepted-at basis validity and current directional Contact gates are evaluated separately so Event validity never depends on delivery order.
admission_class_definitions.self_authored_proof: Admitted by a proof bound to the subject principal's identity: either the subject's DID-bound signature / proof of possession, or a currently valid delegated-control proof whose authorization_ref is bound by the subject DID Document. Reducer MUST verify actor == subject, executed_by/authorization_ref when delegated, a fresh replay-protected proof, and that the accepted-at delegation purpose/scope explicitly covers the target event kind, resource and operation; mere presence of a DID-bound delegation is never sufficient. No Realm capability grant is consulted. Fail-closed: missing, stale, unbound, purpose-inapplicable or scope-inapplicable proof MUST be rejected.
admission_class_definitions.service_attested: Written by a protocol service component (Auth/Gate server, Events node, applet host, agent runtime) under its service-ID attestation as part of operating the protocol. Reducer MUST verify the issuing service's authority and its binding to the subject/scope; not a user capability. Fail-closed.

admission_predicate_contract.selector_semantics: All selector fields in one non-otherwise when object are ANDed. payload_path is relative to Event.payload; const uses exact JSON value equality, while not_const matches inequality or an absent path. top_level_fields_present requires every listed Event Envelope field. ref_* selectors evaluate Event.refs after schema validation. Unknown selectors, missing companion selectors, multiple matching non-otherwise variants, or evaluation errors are fail-closed.

registry_rules: Every standard ak.* Event.kind admitted through Event Envelope MUST appear in this registry. Signal payload types and DeviceMessageEnvelope message kinds are intentionally outside this Event registry.

Events API, Sync durable history, Federation, and canonical reducers MUST accept only active entries with wire_scope=durable_event unless an implementation profile explicitly defines a private channel for actor_private_event.

Entries with wire_scope=actor_private_event MAY be persisted in encrypted account data or an actor-private stream, but MUST NOT be inserted into shared Realm data-plane history or control-plane Seal history.

lifecycle_modality applies to physical object lifecycle writes, identified mechanically by an fsm_contract whose axis is object_lifecycle, plus explicitly registered reversible Realm lifecycle facets. Every active event kind that writes such a family MUST declare lifecycle_modality. Use reversible for a reversible facet or either member of an archive/restore pair, and terminal for an irreversible transition. Workflow, membership, status, audit, key-material and OR-Set revocation axes are excluded. Reducers and SDKs MUST read this field and MUST NOT infer modality from event-kind spelling.

Every active reducer-input durable kind MUST declare plane, sealed, and a complete machine-readable cell_writes[] contract; no parallel single-target fields or aliases exist. Each entry declares cell_family, cell_subject, lattice, bottom, optional initial_value, and optional condition. A condition marks the target as conditional. Payload conditions use the closed grammar field_present|field_absent|field_equals|any_field_present; a signed semantic-ref condition uses only critical_ref_role_exact_count{role,count}. All are pure functions of the schema-validated signed Event. When the condition holds the target is required and the reducer MUST derive exactly one matching write from kind+payload; when it does not hold the reducer MUST NOT derive that write. See zh/models/event-and-patch.md section 2.4.2. cell_family is a stable ak.component.*.v<n> URI; cell_subject is null, an explicitly sourced payload.* or envelope.actor_id field path, a coalesce descriptor, or a composite descriptor. Bare field paths and other envelope.* fields are invalid. plane MUST be data or control; sealed is a boolean and MUST be true iff plane=control. plane/sealed are the machine-readable authority for DataEvent versus Control Move routing and plane_cross_write validation; payload prose is explanatory. bottom is reject, expose, or inert; inert MUST be used when the lattice cannot produce Bottom. initial_value declares the value the cas_register reports before any reducer write has been applied; declaring `initial_value="__unset__"` combined with `head_eq:"__unset__"` implements singleton-once-set cells.

Every lattice=fsm cell write MUST resolve by cell_family to exactly one fsm_contract. Event-kind parameters MUST NOT duplicate states or allowed_transitions. Template-backed contracts resolve their instance_parameters before transition validation; unresolved templates, parameters or conditional edges fail closed.

Every active wire_scope=actor_private_event kind MUST resolve to exactly one entry in actor_private_contracts.event_writes. Actor-private writes use only the registered actor_private_contracts.cell_families merge contract, never shared Realm plane/sealed routing, CBA fields, reducer_input, or shared cell_contracts.

Protocol-singleton cells MAY take their genesis value from a create payload, but every subsequent write MUST use a registered event_kind. ak.component.notary.v1 and ak.component.realm.reducer_profile.v1 are canonically defined in zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md; their genesis values come from ak.realm.create, and subsequent writes use ak.realm.notary and ak.realm.upgrade respectively.

Lattice MUST be one of the fully specified core types: or_set, mv_register, cas_register, fsm, counter, ordered_log. A new lattice type cannot become active until its join, bottom, op schema, profile gate, and conformance vectors are all registered.

State convergence is defined by CBA: DataEvent writes are projected and locally accepted against seal_ref, Control Move writes are projected and finalized by Seals, and per-cell Lattice join remains deterministic. Event Envelope routing fields MUST NOT be used as ordering authority.

Every active durable reducer-input event_kind MUST have a machine-readable admission source: either at least one capability action targets it (capability_action_registry.target_event_kinds), or it declares an admission class from admission_class_definitions. capability_gated events MUST be listed in at least one action's target_event_kinds - admission has a single direction of truth and no per-event capability list. Enforced by lint_artifacts.py; no active durable reducer-input event may lack an admission source (fail-closed).

A conditional admission MUST use only selectors defined by admission_predicate_contract. All non-otherwise predicates are evaluated independently; exactly one match selects its branch, zero matches selects the final otherwise branch, and multiple matches fail closed. otherwise is never evaluated as an ordinary predicate.

ak.state.conflict_recovery is the single registered exception to literal cell addressing. Its one cell_writes[] entry declares cell_ref (a cell_id sourced from the payload) instead of cell_family/cell_subject, and effect_projection kind=reset instead of a lattice op, and it omits lattice and bottom. That combination is closed: no other kind may declare cell_ref or reset, and this kind MUST declare both together. A recovery addresses one cell of an arbitrary family, so the target cannot be a literal ak.component.*.v<n> URI; and a reset is not a join, so it has no lattice. The safety envelope is not static reachability but zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 9.5: the reducer MUST apply a reset only to a cell already in Bottom, and only when the Event carries refs[] role=recovery_capability and role=state_witness satisfying every condition in that section. On a cell in any other state the write MUST be rejected.

Every active standard Event kind MUST declare exactly one payload_schema_ref. The reference MUST resolve to an existing schema location and MUST equal the single Event Envelope payload dispatch for that kind. Consumers MUST NOT infer payload schemas from Event.kind spelling, schema-name conventions, or fallback definitions.

payload_schema_contract.validation_rule: Every active standard ak.* event kind MUST be validated by the Event Envelope schema and one payload class selected by kind. Unknown standard kind, unmatched active kind, or payload class failure is schema_violation before reducer execution.
payload_schema_contract.non_critical_extension_rule: Unknown non-critical payload fields are preserved in canonical bytes and MAY be ignored by reducers. Unknown critical payload semantics MUST be declared in Event.requirements.critical_extensions and fail closed when unsupported.
payload_schema_contract.explicit_binding_rule: Each active standard event kind declares exactly one payload_schema_ref, and the Event Envelope dispatch selects that exact location. Missing, dangling, duplicate, or divergent bindings fail closed. Consumers MUST NOT infer a payload schema from kind spelling or naming conventions.

Notary equivocation evidence (Control Move). Payload carries signer_id plus the two conflicting Seal wire objects: same (realm_id, notary_seq) slot with different canonical bytes, or a notary_seq=k+1 Seal that does not descend from the same signer's notary_seq=k Seal (authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.1). Admission is verification-only: any Realm member MAY submit and the two conflicting notary signatures are the complete authorization; no capability grant is consulted and reducer MUST NOT require one. Reducer MUST re-verify both signatures and the slot rule, then add a per-signer fault record to the notary_fault cell. Once a fault record is accepted: receivers MUST reject later Seals signed by the fault signer, the two conflicting Seals and their descendants enter fork_quarantine, and Realm-wide pause applies only when no eligible signer remains.

Notary censorship evidence (Control Move). Payload carries signer_id, the signed control-plane receipt, the seal_ref of the Seal that was obliged to include / signed-reject / defer the pending Control Move, a control_event_set_root non-membership proof for the censored event digest, and the missing rejection-or-defer proof (authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.2). Admission is verification-only: the receipt holder MAY submit; the receipt signature plus the non-membership proof are the complete authorization. This evidence does NOT automatically disqualify the notary: reducer adds an audit fault record that MUST raise governance alarms, feeds inclusion-list / recovery obligations, and is evaluated by governance or the genesis recovery path.

Agent signing key authorization. Payload MUST validate as event-payload.schema.json#/$defs/agent_key_authorize_payload and bind agent_id, key_id, verification_method, accountable_principal_id, agent_key_scope, audience, issued_at, and approval_evidence; expires_at is optional (absent means non-expiring, revocation-governed). The agent-key cell is an observed-remove OR-Set. First authorization adds one authorization dot. Same-key re-authorization MUST atomically remove every active authorization dot visible at the Move seal_basis and add the replacement dot; it MUST NOT select a winner by arrival time. Concurrent replacement dots that survive the join are evaluated by the deterministic strictest fold: intersect agent_key_scope and audience, take the earliest finite expires_at (absence is +infinity), and fail closed if accountable_principal_id or verification_method disagree. Key replacement has no dedicated rotate kind: runtime replacement re-pairing authorizes the new key and revokes every prior active key (reason=superseded_by_repairing) in the same accepted transaction.

Agent signing key revocation. Payload MUST validate as event-payload.schema.json#/$defs/agent_key_revoke_payload and bind agent_id, key_id, revoked_at, and revoked_by; the revocation's control-plane basis is the Control Move envelope seal_basis, and its cutoff is the accepted Seal covering the Move.

Controller-authored native personal Agent provisioning fact. Admission atomically projects the provision, accountability, selector and realm-id-claim cells; no nested payload proof or partial two-Event state is valid. The declared managed Agent PCR genesis arrives in a later separate submission whose admission reverse-looks-up this declaration; its acceptance still awaits the controller-signed create-locked DID entry 1.

Controller-owned signed selector statement binding (controller_subject, agent_slug) to one native personal agent DID. Agent lifecycle transition to paused state. Authorization basis is the Control Move envelope seal_basis; payload carries no independent frontier. Auth Server MUST reject new agent session grants for this principal; existing tokens fail closed within an independent pause revocation freshness window of at most 60 seconds, never merely the session maximum TTL. Reversible via ak.self.agent.resume.

Agent lifecycle transition from paused to active. Authorization basis is the Control Move envelope seal_basis; payload carries no independent frontier. At acceptance the reducer MUST use the accepted current control frontier to re-validate controller, agent, key, capability, Realm policy, and accountability_grant freshness; any failure rejects the resume.

Agent lifecycle terminal state. One accepted controller-authorized Event is the unavoidable parent AND gate for every runtime key, session, pairing handle, capability grant, KeyPackage, presence and future submission. Cleanup is asynchronous and MUST NOT synthesize or require child revocation Events. Terminal — no transition out.

concurrency_class_definitions.merge_safe: Operation commutes under its declared lattice and may execute concurrently with other merge_safe operations after ordinary causal validation.
concurrency_class_definitions.exclusive: Operation requires exclusive compare-and-apply for its target cell set but does not globally serialize unrelated security authority.
concurrency_class_definitions.security_barrier: Authority, membership, key, scope, policy, recovery, or identity transition that serializes against every concurrent security_barrier touching the same signed scope.

merge_definitions.server_revision_cas: Whole-value compare-and-set on expected_revision; accepted revision increments by one and the revision high-water mark survives tombstone GC.
merge_definitions.fsm_cas: Closed FSM transition checked against the family table and current revision; concurrent siblings fail closed.
merge_definitions.cas_register: Single actor-private register; concurrent distinct values fail closed rather than using arrival order.
merge_definitions.causal_then_hlc_then_device: Causal dominance wins; only causally incomparable positions compare HLC, and only equal HLC values compare device_id lexicographically.

registry_rules: A schema row with omitted status defaults to active. New or edited rows MUST spell status explicitly.
The only allowed schema status is active. Unknown or any non-active status fails closed; the registry defines no historical compatibility rows.

consumer_binding, when present, is the machine-readable disposition for a logical schema that is not directly named by an operation, Event kind, or another schema. Runtime and dynamic wire bindings MUST declare kind, selector, and normative_ref. A prose_only binding MUST instead declare a non-empty rationale and MUST NOT be counted as wire coverage.

The effective schema reference of a row is the literal concatenation (file + optional fragment): fragment already includes its leading '#', so consumers MUST NOT insert another separator. For example file='schemas/agent-operations.schema.json' plus fragment='#/$defs/agent_pairing_bootstrap' resolves to exactly 'schemas/agent-operations.schema.json#/$defs/agent_pairing_bootstrap'. Consumers MUST resolve that URI-fragment JSON Pointer and MUST NOT bind schema_id to the top-level document of file. When fragment is absent, the effective reference is the top-level document of file. Two schema_id rows mapping to the same file MUST be distinguished by fragment (or one MUST omit fragment to denote the whole document); a consumer that ignores fragment and loads the top-level document for a fragment-bearing row is non-conforming.

fragment, when present, MUST be a non-empty RFC 6901 JSON Pointer in URI-fragment representation starting with '#/'. If the pointer does not resolve within file, or a row that shares a file with another row omits fragment while that other row also omits fragment (ambiguous whole-document mapping), consumers MUST fail closed rather than silently pick a schema.

storage_rules: Protocol wire objects, canonical JSON, signatures, hashes, fixtures, logs, API DTOs, and cross-service references MUST use the full typed form declared by each id_kind row.

Storage implementations MAY store producer-allocated raw 16-byte UUID values (e.g. PostgreSQL `uuid` column) without the ak:<kind>: prefix when the table, column, or explicit kind field already supplies the type context.
Implementations that store raw IDs MUST restore the full typed form before computing canonical JSON, event IDs, payload hashes, detached proofs, federation payloads, sync cursors, or audit logs.
The <kind> segment is part of the signed/canonical wire value. It MUST NOT be changed, inferred differently, or stripped during verification, forwarding, backfill, or replay.

The payload construction MUST be fixed by that kind's id_form and identity_authority columns, never chosen per call site: producer_allocated uses UUIDv7; event_derived uses the creating Event's 33-byte token; suite_tagged_full_digest uses a full uint8 digest-suite code followed by the complete 32-byte digest under its registered kind-specific preimage contract. v1 Event and suite-tagged identities accept only registered active suite codes with high nibble 0x0; this constraint does not give that nibble any meaning beyond the suite code. A UUID version nibble or digest-suite byte alone never proves identity authority.

A producer_allocated UUIDv7 is never a globally sufficient protocol identity. Its canonical identity key is (mint_authority, typed_id), where mint_authority is the DID whose accepted proof authorized the first durable appearance of that ID. Bare typed-ID lookup, cross-authority deduplication, and last-writer-wins collision repair are forbidden.

Storage implementations MAY store producer_allocated UUID values as raw 16-byte UUIDs. Event-derived and suite-tagged full-digest IDs MUST instead store their raw 33-byte token; they MUST NOT use a native UUID column.

The id_form is fixed by registry kind and never chosen per call site: producer_allocated uses RFC 9562 UUIDv7; event_derived uses the same canonical 33-byte token as its creating Event ID; suite_tagged_full_digest uses a full uint8 digest suite code followed by all 32 digest octets. Both token forms serialize as 44 unpadded Base64URL characters.

A database MAY intern any full Realm wire identity in a canonical Realm table and use a database-local surrogate pk for joins, indexes, and foreign keys. That pk is never serialized or signed. The canonical table MUST retain a unique lossless 33-byte Realm identity (or its full typed wire form), and every realm_pk foreign key MUST resolve to the same wire Realm identity carried by the protocol record.

producer_allocated_identity_contract.security_rationale: UUIDv7 randomness and timestamp layout do not authenticate the allocator. Binding every producer-selected ID to the accepted genesis signer prevents an attacker from claiming another producer's ID by copying or predicting the UUID.

issuer_record_identity_contract.v1_suite_code_constraint: The complete uint8 suite wire code is encoded unchanged, but v1 accepts only registered active codes whose high nibble is 0x0; this is not a Realm derivation-class nibble.

issuer_record_identity_contract.signed_claim_binding: Every preimage field except fixed schema is a signed JWT claim, including the required standard holder_binding; kind is the fixed credential kind and jti is the derived typed ID. Verifiers MUST reconstruct the complete preimage from signed claims and recompute jti, so two different holder_binding values cannot share one valid ID.
issuer_record_identity_contract.session_chain_rule: session_id is independently allocated before first issuance, refresh inherits it, and it MUST NOT equal or derive from grant_id
issuer_record_identity_contract.device_id_rule: No independent top-level device_id claim enters the preimage; device scope tokens, the required holder_binding, or optional device_binding carry the binding.

MUST NOT carry any actor-identifying material; only appears in an `ak.call.state.roster_delta` join participant value and in `participant_binding`. The wire value MUST use the canonical UUIDv7-shaped `ak:rtc_participant:<uuid>` form; implementations MAY derive the random bits from the media-service token input, but the version and variant nibbles MUST satisfy the UUIDv7 pattern.
Abstract capability definition reference ID; signed grant objects use ak:grant:<44-char-event-token>.

Circle object ID — intra-Realm scoped event/message boundary. Hosts its own membership (strict subset of parent Realm.members), history visibility, delivery/query/projection boundary, and optional independent MLS group. Does NOT carry federation identity, policy server, or capability registry — those remain on the parent Realm. See zh/models/circle.md.
Agent Sidecar object ID — controller-owned private AI workspace, singleton per (realm_id, controller_id), with derived eligible-Agent access. See zh/models/sidecar.md.
Consent grant/revoke/request identifier shared by Arkret consent events and MIMI interop DTOs.
Strand object ID
Snapshot/blob chunk ID
Claim or attestation ID

Device identifier (ak:device:<uuid>). A device is a typed ID scoped to an owning principal, NOT a DID and NOT an actor principal. Device keys are registered as verification methods under the owning principal DID via ak.device.authorize.
To-device message queue ID
Event Envelope ID
Moderation/filter rule ID
Non-HTTP stream frame ID
Message franking proof ID
Durable signed capability Grant ID derived from the accepted ak.capability.grant genesis Event; distinct from short-lived SessionGrant credentials.

Short-lived signed SessionGrant credential ID derived from the Account Authority's closed immutable issuance record. JWT jti carries this typed ID; it is neither an Event ID nor an ak:grant capability ID.
Invite object ID derived from either directed ak.invite.create or third-party ak.invite.third_party genesis.

Non-secret Principal Server administrative ID for one account-owned online invite locator. The ID is exposed only on the authenticated self management surface and is distinct from the opaque bearer locator_token.
DID/key log event ID
Message object ID
Transient Signal Message preview stream instance ID; never a durable object or Event identity
Morph object ID
Notification projection ID

Identifier for a durable or reserved multi-phase protocol operation instance. It is allocated at reservation time, before the operation's first Event exists, so it can carry no content binding and MUST NOT be parsed for internal semantics; that is what id_form=producer_allocated means here, not a free-form value space.
Actor-private read cursor ID
Policy object ID
Presentation/proof exchange ID
Receipt object ID
Basis-bound AuthorizationLease identifier.

Stable session identifier bound by every proof transcript, backup decrypt proof and MLS Welcome replay during one recovery strand. Referenced by ak.schema.recovery_receipt.v1 and by §15 recovery proofs. See crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §15.
Attestation object ID (e.g. ak.attestation.range_completeness).
Relation object ID
Moderation report ID derived from the accepted ak.self.moderation.report Event.
Moderation queue item ID derived as a second, distinct typed output of the accepted ak.self.moderation.report Event.
Request/correlation ID
Service-local planned route handover chain ID. The target service allocates it once and reuses it across scheduled updates and cancellation revisions for the same handover.
Snapshot manifest ID

Space object ID — structural grouping object inside a Realm (board, list, swimlane, calendar bucket, etc.). Authorization-transparent: never carries its own membership / policy / E2EE group; resolves to the containing Realm.
Directory notification subscription identifier.
Realm object ID — security / sync / auth / E2EE boundary. Always carries membership, policy, history_visibility, MLS group binding, and federation policy.
id_kinds.id_form_note: All Realm IDs are 33-byte Event tokens (encoding.md section 4.1): reserved-zero high nibble, uint4 digest suite, then all 32 digest octets, encoded as 44 unpadded Base64URL characters. The token is byte-identical to its ak.realm.create Event token; retyping only swaps the typed prefix.

id_kinds.description: Durable RecoveryTransaction, SecurityRotationTransaction, federation, or applet transaction identifier.
View object ID
Producer-allocated identity of a principal-private scheduled-send plan. It is not an Event or Message identity and MUST NOT be retyped into either one.

id_kind_registry.uuid_form_rules: The construction is declared per kind by id_form. producer_allocated = RFC 9562 UUIDv7. event_derived = the creating Event's 33-byte token (zero reserved high nibble plus uint4 suite wire_code followed by all 32 octets of its digest), canonically encoded as 44 unpadded Base64URL characters and retyped only by replacing the ak:<kind>: prefix. The token requires strict decode plus canonical re-encode validation; regex alone is insufficient.

operation_registry.description: Canonical operation catalog for generated service operation views and transport bindings.

generated_views.role: HTTP/OpenAPI binding shape aligned to the catalog; not a second operation namespace.
Descriptive operation map and governance notes; excerpt-only unless explicitly marked generated.

high_security_session_authentication_pol.public_projection_rule: Without valid sender-constrained proof, an allowlisted operation may return only its contract-defined public metadata projection and MUST NOT grant session or capability semantics. All other ak.self.* operations fail closed.
high_security_session_authentication_pol.new_operation_rule: A new or unknown ak.self.* operation is protected by default; adding an unauthenticated public projection requires explicit registration in this list and a normative operation contract defining that projection.

registry_rules: New operation_id values MUST be added here before any OpenAPI, HTTP binding table, SDK generator, or alternative transport binding references them.
Generated views MAY change shape, grouping, or field order, but MUST NOT introduce, rename, or remove operation_id values that are absent from this catalog.
Supporting Arkret core does not imply support for every registered operation. Implementations MUST advertise supported_operations and supported_profiles explicitly.

Each surface_groups entry carries a tier (see surface_classes); only the core tier is implied by claiming v1 protocol support. Extension, interop_bridge, and deployment_local surfaces require explicit advertisement.
surface_classes defines the closed tier vocabulary and surface_groups is the sole canonical operation grouping view; generators MUST NOT emit a third top-level surfaces collection.

Profile matrices in artifacts/profiles/conformance-profiles.json define role-level MUST/SHOULD requirements; the surface groups below define machine-readable capability families for discovery, docs, and lint.
Each operation MUST declare success_shape_kind so SDKs can determine success handling without endpoint-name hard-coding.

Operations with typed OpenAPI bodies SHOULD declare request_schema_ref and/or response_schema_ref. The referenced schema fragment is the source for generated DTO docs and MUST match the OpenAPI component referenced by the HTTP binding.

Operations that still bind OpenAPI request/response bodies to OperationRequest or OperationResult MUST declare generic_binding with request/response booleans, reason, profile_gate, and migration_plan; core-tier operations MUST NOT use generic bindings.

operation_id values MUST end with <kind>.<action>. The kind segment MUST be one of read, stream, resource, command, upload, or exchange; the action segment MUST describe protocol semantics and MUST NOT be an HTTP method name. read is the only safe/idempotent computation kind; its exact GET, QUERY, or POST binding is declared by the operation row according to request shape.
An operation row MUST declare exactly one HTTP binding and MUST NOT declare http_compatibility_bindings or unregistered method/path aliases.

resource.replace operations MUST bind to HTTP PUT; resource.delete operations MUST bind to HTTP DELETE; command, upload, exchange, and complex read-body operations SHOULD bind to HTTP POST unless their operation notes define a stricter resource URI replacement contract.

Every write operation (kind command/upload/exchange, and resource.replace / resource.delete) MUST declare idempotency_mechanism (one of idempotency_key, object_id, request_id, canonical_hash, protocol_sequence, none) and retry_safe (boolean). Read-only operations (read/stream/resource.get/resource.head) MUST NOT declare these fields.

An operation that invokes current DID authority MUST carry exactly one did_authority object that byte-matches its did-freshness-profile-registry call_sites row. Operations without a real DID-authority call MUST omit it; risk tier never implies DID freshness.

idempotency_mechanism is the machine-readable source of truth for which idempotency mechanism from api-conventions.md section 6 an operation uses. canonical_hash operations MUST also declare canonical_hash_input as either full_body or an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer. retry_safe=true means a byte-identical full retry of the same request cannot produce duplicate side effects: it returns the original outcome, an equivalent idempotent no-op, or a deterministic conflict. retry_safe=false means blind retries MAY duplicate side effects or consume one-time material; clients MUST NOT retry such operations without out-of-band reconciliation.

Every write operation MUST declare durable_effect. kind=event_log identifies an Arkret Event committed by successful completion and declares either event_kinds[] or an event_kind_source JSON path; kind=actor_private_event declares the actor-private Event kind committed; kind=none declares no Arkret Event and requires a stable rationale. Service-local durable state, identity-method logs, queues, session/material stores, external effects and returned-but-uncommitted Event material all use kind=none with an accurate rationale. Missing, unknown or inactive declared Event kinds fail closed.

Every operation MUST declare body_class, a closed value of non_streaming_json, streaming_ndjson, or binary_stream. body_class=non_streaming_json binds the operation to the general size contract in zh/conformance/scalability-constraints.md section 2.1: canonical request/response body <= 8 MiB, HTTP message content wire bytes <= 16 MiB, Content-Encoding MUST be absent, and every byte overflow maps to payload_too_large. streaming_ndjson and binary_stream operations are excluded from the whole-body limits and MUST define their own per-frame / per-chunk / pending bounds (scalability-constraints section 2.1.7).

max_canonical_body_bytes is OPTIONAL and only for a body_class=non_streaming_json operation whose normative limit is LOWER than the general 8 MiB. It MUST NOT declare a value above 8 MiB, and deployments MUST NOT lower the general interoperability constants through Describe (scalability-constraints section 2.1.6).

max_items is REQUIRED for a body_class=non_streaming_json operation whose request or response carries a top-level array with a normative count bound. max_items and the byte budget are a conjunctive two-dimensional constraint: a count bound never promises that max_items objects of near-maximum size fit in one body, and implementations MUST NOT lower a registered count because a fixture-median product exceeds the byte budget (scalability-constraints section 2.1.5).

surface_classes.core: Base interoperable surfaces implied by claiming Arkret v1 protocol support (service discovery, identity registry, events/account aggregate).
surface_classes.extension: Optional interoperable surfaces that are part of the Arkret specification but require explicit discovery/profile advertisement.
surface_classes.interop_bridge: Adapter surfaces that bridge Arkret to external protocols (MIMI Internet-Drafts, third-party Applet hosts). Implementations advertise these only when the external protocol is supported; bridge operations are not part of any core or extension profile and frequently mirror an in-spec operation via bridges_to.
surface_classes.deployment_local: Deployment-specific, operator, or product-local surfaces that MUST NOT be assumed from core protocol support alone.

source_signature_anchor.node_to_applet: Source-Service-ID current service DID verification method; Destination-Service-ID MUST equal the Applet registration service_id.
source_signature_anchor.applet_to_arkret_inbound: Applet registration webhook_auth.key_ref; its canonical bare full_id MUST be validated by the registered method adapter and project to both Source-Service-ID and the active effective install service_id. Direct full-DID/core-id comparison and did_core_id fragment concatenation are forbidden.

operations.notes: Resource-side appeal against an operator takedown. The appeal packet MUST bind takedown_id, resource id, appellant DID, argument/evidence digest, requested_outcome and created_at, signed by the resource governance key or an authorized advocate; the Directory returns a signed decision receipt. See discovery-directory.md §8.7.

Server-to-server session-grant introspection (RFC 7662-style). The Principal Server validating a presented grant calls this with the grant id or grant_jwt (+ optional audience and optional S2S holder confirmation) and learns whether it is active, plus non-secret grant metadata. The Account Authority MUST read the same issuer ledger used by issue, refresh, revoke and cascade; lifecycle status distinguishes active, revoked, superseded and dynamically expired records rather than consulting a Principal Event/cell. The introspection response MUST include the grant's cnf_jkt (RFC 7638 thumbprint of the bound DPoP holder key) so the Principal Server can verify the per-request DPoP proof on /_arkret/self/* (api-conventions §3.3); clients do not send a separate introspection-proof header on self-path requests. session_public_key is also returned for RFC 9421 PoP verification. READ-ONLY: introspection MUST NOT consume/revoke the grant. Authenticated by the configured session_grant_introspection_bearer (server-local); not exposed over gRPC/MQ.

Account Authority S2S producer operation for Native Agent signer evidence. The request carries agent_authority_service_resolution: the current signed ServiceResolutionRecord, adapter-discriminated method evidence and authenticated normalized DID Document. The receiver independently validates method evidence, document digest, record proof/currentness, project(full_id), and active assertion key before verifying an RFC 9421 signature that covers method, target URI/path, Content-Digest, Source/Destination-Service-ID, operation id and request id. A did_core_id, URL, bearer or caller-supplied public key is never the verification key source; bearer may only be an additional deployment gate. The authenticated source service MUST equal request.agent_authority_service_id and MUST byte-match service_id in request.principal_id's current AcceptedAtServiceBinding; that Principal Server is the Agent PCR authority under the managed-Agent same-server invariant. Ordinary clients and a caller-supplied account identity are forbidden. The Account Authority reads its own authoritative account binding/status projection, selects account_binding_default or account_status_event basis, and signs the closed controller_account_gate_attestation under domain ak.controller-account-gate-v1. issued_at <= expires_at and expires_at-issued_at MUST be <=300s. Unknown principal, missing current service binding, wrong source service and unauthorized caller are indistinguishable not_found outcomes and disclose no account status. Exact request_id plus canonical intent replay returns the byte-identical outcome while retained; same request_id with different principal or service is duplicate_conflict with zero issuance. The attestation is intentionally a reusable short-TTL controller-lifecycle snapshot and omits operation, request_digest, audience and challenge: per-request current_observation and outer_attestation bind its digest to those exact values, so a bare gate replay cannot validate another request. account_id and raw account cells never enter the request, outcome, logs visible to the caller or portable evidence.

Authenticated by Authorization: DPoP <account_handoff_grant> plus a matching DPoP header. The Account Authority verifies the current lease holder and fence, validates the complete unpublished DID operation, derives principal_id, its canonical operation digest, did_version_id, log_head_digest, and control_key_digest, persists the holder-authenticated operation checkpoint, rate-limits same-holder renewal, and issues a <=300s single-use challenge bound to account_subject, holder cnf.jkt, lease/fence, all derived DID pins, audience, origin, trust domain, purpose, and expiry. Repeating the same request_id returns the same unconsumed challenge. Challenge state MUST be shared durable state, not process-local memory; expiry and prior consumption are distinct terminal states.

Issue a single-use challenge for binding an ALREADY-PUBLISHED full_id to the authenticated service account under stable principal_id. Authenticated by Authorization: DPoP <account_handoff_grant> plus a matching DPoP header. Unlike issue_identity_binding_challenge the caller supplies principal_id plus full_id rather than an unpublished DID operation: the Account Authority MUST resolve full_id itself at the high freshness tier (synchronous refresh or fail closed), MUST require the registered adapter to project(full_id)=principal_id, MUST NOT attempt to resolve did_core_id, MUST NOT accept caller-supplied history, and derives did_version_id, log_head_digest and control_key_digest from the resolved current entry. Deployments that do not host the DID MUST additionally require method-native witness / freshness evidence, because accepting registry and Principal Server co-location does not extend trust to third-party DIDs. The <=300s single-use challenge and returned control proof bind account_subject, principal_id, full_id, holder cnf.jkt, the resolved DID pins, audience, origin, trust domain, purpose and expiry. Repeating the same request_id returns the same unconsumed challenge. Challenge state MUST be shared durable state, not process-local memory; expiry and prior consumption are distinct terminal states. This operation performs no PCR genesis and reserves no principal: it only proves current control of an existing DID.

Issue a single-use challenge that authorizes explicitly abandoning a provisional identity whose PCR was never accepted (zh/identity/key-management.md §5.0.2). Authenticated by Authorization: DPoP <account_handoff_grant> plus a matching DPoP header, and by nothing else: the PCR was never accepted, so the holder has no principal and therefore no principal-bound ak.session.grant. The Account Authority verifies the current lease holder and fence, requires principal_id and did_version_id to equal the holder-authenticated reserved_identity_creation checkpoint, and MUST refuse to issue a challenge once that PCR is accepted. The <=300s single-use challenge is bound to account_subject, holder cnf.jkt, the abandoned principal_id, did_version_id, lease id and fence, the closed consequence disclosure, audience, origin, trust domain, purpose and expiry. Repeating the same request_id returns the same unconsumed challenge. Challenge state MUST be shared durable state, not process-local memory; expiry and prior consumption are distinct terminal states. This operation abandons nothing by itself and MUST NOT be reachable from ordinary login, session resume, lease fence advance or any automated flow.

Consume an identity-abandonment challenge and explicitly abandon the provisional identity. Authenticated by Authorization: DPoP <account_handoff_grant> plus a matching DPoP header; the presented handoff MUST be a fresh one and MUST NOT be the grant that was presented when the challenge was issued. Whether that fresh handoff required re-authentication, which risk checks ran and how long any cooldown lasts are deployment governance and are deliberately not specified. One transaction consumes the challenge, records the orphan anchor tombstone / audit reservation, suppresses the reserved_identity_creation checkpoint on every holder-readable surface and releases the identity-creation lease; any step failing means zero writes. If the PCR was accepted between issuance and confirmation the request MUST fail with identity_creation_already_accepted and MUST NOT abandon anything, because removing an established identity is the account deletion path. Replaying the same request_id returns the same terminal outcome and MUST NOT produce a second tombstone. The abandoned entry 0 stays a permanently unusable orphan anchor; its later handling is deployment governance.

Account Authority single-call issuer-ledger session-grant exchange. After validating account-to-principal binding, authentication proof, holder DPoP, audience and scope ceiling, the issuer uses the proof-specific stable request identity and canonical intent digest to atomically persist one immutable issuance record and signed JWT before responding. The grant ID and JWT jti are recomputed from that record under id_kind_registry.issuer_record_identity_contract; no Principal Event is authored. Exact replay revalidates holder/DPoP/target/digest and returns the byte-identical recorded outcome. Same request identity with different canonical intent is duplicate_conflict with zero writes. A replay whose outcome is expired or revoked/superseded returns the registered terminal error and never issues a replacement; an evicted replay record fails closed as indeterminate. The response is the client-visible SessionGrantOutcome and the client presents ak.session.grant directly to /_arkret/self/* with DPoP. For proof_kind=oidc_code_exchange, the Account Authority exchanges and validates the code. For proof_kind=pre_registration_handoff, the DPoP-bound handoff account MUST already be bound to principal_id. The Account Authority never derives a principal DID from OIDC and never obtains or uses a principal/root/device/notary Event-signing key.

Account Authority ordinary hard logout (account-lifecycle §4.1): single client-visible logout entry. The handler validates the current ak.session.grant + DPoP, terminates the Auth-side auth session / grant rotation chain through ak.gate.account.command.logout_auth_session when Auth-side is split out, and completes or durably schedules the Principal-side local account session + device session cleanup and to-device/push removal. Distinct from revoke_session (targeted session-grant revoke). HTTP-only Account Authority op; not exposed over gRPC/MQ.

Account Authority to Auth Server S2S Auth-side logout sub-operation (account-lifecycle §4.1): the Account Authority has already validated the client-visible ak.gate.account.command.logout request, then calls this operation with service-to-service authentication to log out the Auth-side browser/auth session owning the presented ak.session.grant and terminate that session's grant rotation chain. Ordinary clients MUST NOT call this operation; they only call ak.gate.account.command.logout. HTTP-only S2S op; not exposed over gRPC/MQ.

Final native Agent runtime-key authorization. The closed Ed25519 possession proof MUST be byte-identical to the current persisted runtime request and still fresh; the authority rebuilds its server-record-bound transcript, stable runtime binding and ak.agent.key_pairing_request_binding.v1 (including current proof digest) before accepting the controller-signed authorize Event. A stale prompt or any body/record/evidence mismatch fails closed without consuming the pairing handle.

Authorizes a sibling device only after verified current-device confirmation. This operation always produces authorization_binding_kind=accepted_device, so device_signature MUST verify under ak.device-authorize-accepted-device-possession-proof-v1 and registration_anchor/pcr_recovery domains MUST be rejected. The authority recomputes the pairing transcript, verifies exact request/Event equality and submits the current-device-signed Event through ordinary PCR admission; it never resolves current human DID authority.

Issues the replacement device's first Standard grant after a PCR-policy RecoveryTransaction completes. The body carries the terminal device-attested receipt, coordinator attestation, PCR generation and InitialSessionGrantRequest; DID-root evidence is relevant only when that optional factor was enabled.

DPoP-bound issuer-ledger session-grant rotation. The stable request identity is (predecessor_grant_id, refresh_request_digest). Exact replay revalidates current holder/DPoP and returns the recorded successor outcome; conflicting canonical bytes are duplicate_conflict. One issuer transaction creates the active successor with a fresh issuance nonce, preserves the independently allocated session_id, and atomically marks the predecessor superseded with successor_session_grant_id. A replay whose recorded successor is expired or revoked/superseded returns the registered terminal error and never issues another successor. Account Authority-local op; no Principal Event is authored.

Canonical account creation/binding operation. The body selects exactly one branch: an already-published DID control proof, or account-first identity_creation. Both branches submit outer full_id and principal_id; every repeated full_id/principal_id in the selected proof, identity-creation object and PCR genesis initial_resolution MUST equal the outer values byte-for-byte. The Account Authority independently validates the registered method adapter and requires project(full_id)=principal_id. The published-DID proof branch uses the durable challenge pins and creates no identity-creation lease or PCR genesis. In the account-first identity_creation branch the caller MUST additionally present Authorization: DPoP <account_handoff_grant> plus matching DPoP, the current lease/fence, the exact reserved DID inception operation, and a fresh identity-root control proof over the persisted challenge transcript. For did:webvh the verifier takes parameters.updateKeys[0] of the entry pinned by did_version_id (the root is not a DID Document verificationMethod), requires verification_key_multibase to match it exactly, and requires its canonical multikey SHA-256 to equal control_key_digest. For account-first inception that entry is entry 0. The Account Authority CAS-validates account/holder/lease/fence/reservation, consumes the challenge, submits the DID operation internally, accepts only accepted or byte-identical duplicate with a verified head digest, derives pcr_realm_id only by retyping the exact root-signed ak.realm.create event_id, and writes the service-account binding. Account-first PCR genesis persists the same verified full_id, method_history_head and version_id in initial_resolution. Every success returns a signed binding_receipt that binds binding_kind, principal_id, full_id, did_version_id and control_key_digest; identity_creation_lease_id and lease_fence appear only for binding_kind=identity_creation. The (account, principal_id, operation_digest) result is idempotent; published-but-not-yet-bound state is durably completed for that same account and can never be rebound to another account. The operation never accepts recovery words, seed material, or identity-root private keys.

durable_effect.irreversibility_note: Beyond authoring the genesis Events this operation publishes a public did:webvh log entry and commits a one-account-one-principal binding that can never be rebound. Retry and audit logic MUST treat it as cross-service irreversible even though the closed durable_effect kind vocabulary can only name the Event-log half.

operations.notes: Durable issuer-ledger session revocation. The stable request identity binds issuer, operation kind, authenticated principal/session, canonical target selector and canonical request digest. One issuer transaction records the exact outcome and idempotently transitions matching active records to revoked. Same identity and canonical intent replays the byte-identical recorded outcome after current caller authorization is revalidated; the same identity with different intent is duplicate_conflict with zero additional state changes. Introspection is not a substitute for resolving an uncertain mutation outcome.

Optional Account Authority browser redirect landing / handoff for deployments that use an OIDC redirect URI under /_arkret/gate/account. It MUST NOT issue or return SessionGrantOutcome, ak.session.grant, or Principal local session material; client-visible grant issuance remains ak.gate.account.command.issue_session_grant.

Account Authority exchanges an OIDC authorization code for an opaque, short-lived account_handoff_grant bound to the request DPoP key and returns the deployment-local stable account_subject. The handoff is not ak.session.grant, has no refresh-token semantics, and its closed operation allowlist is issue_identity_binding_challenge, issue_did_binding_challenge, issue_identity_abandonment_challenge, abandon_identity_creation, register, issue_session_grant, and issue_recovery_completion_grant. The two abandonment operations are on that list because a never-accepted PCR leaves the holder without a principal, so no principal-bound ak.session.grant can exist to carry them. It returns bound, identity_creation_active, or identity_creation_busy state and atomically acquires, renews, or fences a rate-limited identity-creation lease for the authenticated service account. Busy includes the conflicting live lease expires_at without holder identity. Repeating the same request_id returns the same live outcome. A different holder cannot take an unexpired lease; after expiry, a newly authenticated holder may fence it and must preserve all frozen checkpoints.

Read-only DPoP-bound projection of the current Account Authority identity-creation lease or established binding. The response is rebuilt from durable server state on every call and accepts no client-authored phase, goal, checkpoint, or recovery material. Clients use it to reconcile local onboarding artifacts after reload, callback, process restart, or an uncertain command result.

Runtime-to-controller pending approval request for native personal-agent key pairing. The closed Ed25519 proof binds the local key to the authoritative pairing handle, at-least-128-bit pairing secret, authority service DID, stable runtime binding and no-more-than-five-minute window; the controller still must approve by signing ak.agent.key.authorize bound to the current proof digest. Pairing secret and proof MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string. One open pairing_request_id has at most one pending stable ak.agent.runtime_key_binding.v1 digest: same-binding retries retain approval/notification ids and atomically replace the current freshness proof, while a different binding fails with HTTP 409 agent_runtime_request_conflict without replacement.

Resolves a short-lived agent pairing token carried out-of-band, usually as a URL fragment in a QR/link. The pairing token MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; the response is the six-field agent_pairing_bootstrap.

Runtime-side poll for the controller decision on a previously submitted runtime key request. The pairing_request_id + pairing_code + agent_id triple is the query credential and MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; a record miss and a pairing_code or agent_id mismatch MUST be indistinguishable (both not_found). Once approved, the outcome carries authorized_event_ref plus the authorized key binding; the runtime MUST compare authorized_public_key_digest against its own key and treat a mismatch as paired-by-another-runtime. HTTP responses MUST carry Retry-After; clients wait at least that interval and use 1s/2s/5s/10s then at most 30s backoff, stopping after pairing expiry.

Unauthenticated stage of a device-pairing short-link handoff (device-lifecycle.md §2.1.1). The new device submits a canonical new_device_pubkey and a client_nonce (plus optional display_name / device_metadata) and MUST NOT submit a challenge proof, because the proof must commit to values this call mints; the service mints a fresh device_pairing_request_id, an 8-character Crockford-style 40-bit CSPRNG pairing_code, a gate_audience and a server_nonce, and stores a bounded-TTL account-less record in state pending_authorization. The staged record deliberately carries no hpke_key, no algorithms, no challenge proof and no target attestation: those reach the approving device only over the out-of-band channel, so this anonymous surface never accumulates long-term device key material or a device algorithm fingerprint, and a mirrored copy could never be authoritative anyway. The staged record binds no principal and grants nothing until an authenticated device authorizes it. Stage, resolve and status are rate limited. Each call mints a fresh request, so blind retries duplicate staged records: not retry-safe.

Resolves a device-pairing short-link token carried out-of-band, usually as a URL fragment in a QR/link. The pairing token MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; the response is the DevicePairingBootstrap. The bootstrap carries only server-minted challenge material: it does not carry the challenge proof, the target attestation, or the hpke_key and algorithms that attestation signs, and those MUST NOT be mirrored here. resolve MUST return a uniform not_found for unknown id, pairing_code mismatch, expiry, or a non-pending record so the failing condition is not enumerable. Authorization is unchanged: the returned bootstrap is only consumed by an authenticated device that has independently verified the out-of-band challenge proof and target attestation before driving ak.gate.account.command.pair_device.

Unauthenticated poll for the authorization status of a staged device-pairing record. The device_pairing_request_id + pairing_code pair is the query credential and MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; a record miss and a pairing_code mismatch MUST be indistinguishable (both not_found). While the record is open the outcome carries only state pending_authorization; once an authenticated device has authorized the pairing the outcome carries state authorized plus required device_id and authorized_event_ref; an expired record reports only state expired during a bounded cleanup retention period and becomes not_found after deletion. authorized_event_ref is the entry point for the mandatory pre-assembly check in device-lifecycle.md §5.4.1: the target device MUST fetch that accepted ak.device.authorize and confirm byte-identical device_signature, byte-identical device_public_key / hpke_key / algorithms and an expected principal_id before it assembles the identity locally, and MUST fail closed and warn the user otherwise.

Reads the owner-published current principal resolution evidence from the known Principal Server. history_depth bounds selective history disclosure; after_resolution_event_ref requests only the successor chain after a known ancestor and never exposes unrelated PCR control history. This is a second-hop evidence fetch, not a global resolver or authorization oracle. Sensitive consumers fetch fresh, validate PCR Event/Seal/cell evidence, independently run the registered DID method adapter, and require project(full_id)=principal_id; durable storage of arbitrary remote-principal bindings is not required.

Returns the current signed ServiceResolutionRecord at the stable current_record_url carried by bootstrap material. TLS is transport only. Consumers verify the record proof, method history, project(full_id)=service_id, time ordering, record_sequence/previous_record_digest and describe binding. Same-core successors refresh route caches without Realm rebind; a changed did_core_id requires a new authorized service binding.

Resolves an online invite locator token carried out-of-band, usually as a URL fragment in a QR/link. The locator token MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; the response is a signed principal_locator.

The caller MUST author and sign the exact ak.consent.grant (decision=accept) or ak.consent.revoke (decision=deny or revoke) EventInitialSubmission. The facade verifies the detached operation signature and the Event authority/correlation, then submits the Event unchanged through ordinary Event admission. It MUST NOT synthesize, rebuild or co-sign consent state. A revoke with no matching active observed dots is rejected without disclosing holder state. Exact Event replay returns the same accepted Event reference.

Account Authority or authorized Principal Server publication of exactly one ak.account.status Event into the account principal's Principal Control Realm. The caller uses service-to-service HTTP Message Signature authentication and a required Idempotency-Key covered by the signature. authority_evidence is Account Authority-signed transport evidence binding account_id, principal_id, principal_control_realm_id, issuer service and a live authority_ref; the receiver independently verifies it, the Event proof, exact Event/evidence field equality, current issuer key/delegation and PCR CBA closure. Initial publication carries the Event without an AuthorizationLease; downstream fanout adds receiver-signed account_status_receipts and CbaProofBundle values. AccountStatusReceipt proves local frontier acceptance, contains no AuthorizationLease id, and generic IngressReceipt is forbidden. Same key plus different canonical body is duplicate_conflict. A byte-identical retry returns the latest durable operation state, allowing pending_seal and fanout progress to converge without creating another Event. accepted or duplicate is terminal for the receiving server's frontier; multi-server propagation continues from a durable bounded outbox and never mutates the signed account-status payload.

Read-only service-authenticated Account Authority query for the exact issuer actor-chain frontier and Principal Control Realm Seal frontier needed to sign one ak.account.status Event. The receiver verifies the signed authority_evidence, current issuer delegation and account/principal/PCR binding before disclosure. The response binds RealmActorFrontierView.actor_id to issuer_service_id and both frontier realm_id values to principal_control_realm_id; it grants no authority, accepts no Event and never synthesizes an empty PCR.
