Unique closed XOR delivery carrier for original holder-signed Contact request, normal response, reject, scope replacement, or tombstone facts plus their exact source acceptance receipts and refreshable current proof. It never carries Direct Conversation binding or Realm Events. Branches use byte-identical durable replay; the receiver never re-signs or treats tentative/stale evidence as authority.

Service-authenticated relay for an exact requester-authorized ak.member.repair.request. The source copies request_id, content and detached requester authorization byte for byte from the accepted self dispatch, appends exactly one portable device or Native Agent current-authority evidence branch, and covers the complete body with Content-Digest and RFC 9421. The destination independently binds requester identity, accepted rejoin actor and subject, authorization Event, current evidence and exact requester_keypackage_ref signer. In one transaction keyed by (Source-Service-ID, request_id), it freezes request_digest, resolves the peer participant from the accepted Direct Conversation binding, and atomically chooses one closed recipient branch: snapshot every currently authorized human device and enqueue all stable distinct message ids, or enqueue one stable message id to the Native Agent's current active runtime endpoint from accepted agent-key/session binding. Exact replay returns the stored byte-identical outcome; a different digest is duplicate_conflict. Success proves only durable enqueue, never business repair acceptance.

Service-authenticated hard-erasure receipt fanout. Source-Service-ID MUST equal receipt.issuer. Idempotency-Key is required and covered by the HTTP Message Signature; its scope is (source service, destination service, key). The receiver verifies the closed receipt, issuer authority at receipt.issued_at, every receipt proof, receipt_digest and the exact retained-stub binding before any deletion or durable acceptance. Same key and canonical body returns the byte-identical signed acceptance; different body returns duplicate_conflict with zero writes. An accepted or duplicate acknowledgement closes the sender outbox item.

Service-authenticated exact receipt-package lookup for the issuer, receiver or an explicitly authorized auditor. It is non-enumerating: unauthorized, unknown and hidden receipt identifiers produce the same not_found response. The returned retained stub is the exact object accepted with the receipt and MUST NOT be reconstructed from later state.

Federation peer Event publication. Each EventFederationSubmission carries the original signed Event. Ordinary online publication omits AuthorizationLease and uses an empty ingress_receipts array; explicit delayed/offline publication carries the lease and at least one original lease-bound IngressReceipt. An ak.member.state compensation publication additionally carries the unchanged transport-only membership_compensation_evidence and the receiver applies the same exact admission/incarnation/action/executor/single-use evaluator as initial submission. Request-level CbaProofBundle values provide receiver-relative dependency closure. The receiver independently validates every Event, optional lease, receipt threshold, compensation evidence, bundle object and reducer result. Ordinary missing dependencies use HTTP 200 partial items with reason_code=dependency_missing and non-empty typed missing sets; registered atomic units use top-level HTTP 409 dependency_missing with EventsDependencyMissingProblem and zero writes. A received response terminates that Idempotency-Key; a post-backfill submit uses a fresh key. The caller MUST use service-to-service authentication with Source/Destination service DID and trust-domain headers. Federated ak.invite.claim remains decided by the destination Realm reducer. The request union additionally registers the discriminated direct_conversation_founding branch for the Direct Conversation founding exception of zh/sync/federation.md section 4.0.4: it carries exactly three ordered EventFederationSubmission items, the source DirectConversationFoundingAcceptanceReceipt and bounded dependencies, and it omits service_binding_ref because the Realm does not yet exist at the receiver. The receiver freshly verifies transport source authority over founder_id, cutover/fence continuity when the receipt came from a pre-migration service, destination binding to the local participant, body closure, recomputed founding_unit_digest and coordinates, and the full direct_conversation_genesis admission before admitting the unit at one atomic boundary. A missing Contact basis mirror or other bounded dependency is a retryable top-level HTTP 409 dependency_missing with zero writes, never a per-item partial and never a permanent rejection.
Federation peer Events surface describe. This endpoint describes the server-to-server peer event bindings; it is not a client self/events binding.

Federation peer frontier probe. Requires service-to-service authentication, Source/Destination service DID headers, trust-domain headers, and Realm federation_peer authorization. It returns the federation peer frontier response shape on the dedicated peer trust surface.

Read-only federation dependency resolution for canonical-bytewise sorted exact Event IDs, Event digests, and Seal refs in one Realm. Returns visible Events and receiver-relative CbaProofBundle values under a caller-selected response budget capped at 8 MiB. It never accepts an Event or Seal and never advances a frontier. Every selector is fully accounted for by a returned object or an indistinguishable same-type missing entry; if complete accounting cannot fit the budget, the whole operation returns limit_exceeded rather than a partial success.

Federation peer pull/backfill query. Uses the same selector, cursor, order, and response semantics as ak.self.events.read.scan, but the HTTP trust surface is peer and the caller MUST be an authorized federation peer service.

Private Principal Server to Principal Server invite delivery. Requires service-to-service authentication, Destination-Service-ID equal to invite_address.recipient_service_id, a ak.invite.create event whose invitee equals invite_address.subject_id, and introduction_evidence accepted by the recipient invite_receive_policy.

Atomic cross-Principal-Server KeyPackage claim. The destination KeyPackage authority is the sole CAS authority and MUST validate both requester portable authorization evidence, the requester participant authorization and the outer source-service HTTP Message Signature. Every successful human-device claim record carries complete target_device_signing_key_evidence without a semantic history-entry cap; every Native Agent record instead carries request-bound current target_agent_signer_evidence. The requester independently verifies the returned root/Seal/current authority before installing the KeyPackage; the destination service receipt is transport integrity, not signer authority. Idempotency is scoped by (Source-Service-ID, claim_request_id) and binds the canonical request digest; duplicate transport delivery returns the original byte-identical outcome, but callers MUST use the query operation rather than replaying the command after an uncertain outcome. Success omits inventory counts and per-device failures.

Read-only recovery of the destination authority's durable peer-claim ledger after an uncertain command outcome. It requires the same authenticated source service and exact request_digest and returns only opaque claim state plus the original signed success outcome when one exists.

Read-only service-authenticated retrieval of the exact RFC 9420 GroupInfo and ratchet_tree extension bytes committed by one accepted ak.mls.genesis Event. The provider resolves the Event, verifies every echoed scope/group/epoch/ref/digest selector, hashes raw bytes against both explicit digests and content-addressed refs, and validates GroupInfo/tree consistency before returning an all-or-nothing response. It never returns private tree material, secrets, inferred leaf DTOs or proof-bundle leaves; consumers derive leaf_index only from occupied leaves in the verified RFC tree.

Account Authority transparently relays the exact client-signed PCR genesis unit after authenticating the service account and freezing the account/principal reservation. The outer service signature is transport authentication only. Principal admission independently validates the DID inception root, identity_creation_control_proof, the event-derived PCR id retype(create.event_id) which is never derived from the principal DID or subject and is never server-chosen, empty frontier, ordered root-signed create plus founding-device-signed authorize, single-direction payload digest binding, lease fence and expiry. Acceptance is atomic and create-once at the account dimension: two genesis attempts produce two different realm_id values, so implementations MUST NOT detect concurrency by id equality. Exact replay returns the original pcr_genesis_unit receipt and a conflicting unit performs zero writes.

Realm-scoped service-authenticated publication of exactly one target-signed ServiceResolutionRecord or ServiceRouteHandoverNotice. Idempotency-Key is required, is covered by the HTTP Message Signature, and MUST equal body.request_id. Transport replay is keyed by (Source-Service-ID, realm_id, request_id) and binds the complete canonical request digest: exact replay returns the original ack and a different digest is duplicate_conflict. Artifact integrity is independently keyed by (Source-Service-ID, realm_id, target service_id, artifact family/key/revision): the same artifact key with another digest conflicts with zero overwrite. The receiver validates source peer authority, target visibility, exact artifact_digest, target proof, full_id-to-core projection, sequential record/notice basis, time rules and hard bounds before writing its service-local mirror ledger. The receiver-signed ack cross-binds both keys, request_digest and accepted time; it proves durable receipt of exact bytes only and never makes a URL authoritative or declares a migration safe unless the deployment-required peer set has all acked.

Read-only Realm-scoped recovery of at most 32 continuous target-signed successor records and one active target-signed handover notice within a caller-selected response budget capped at 256 KiB. The authenticated requester must be a current allowed federation peer and must already be authorized to know the target service core through an effective member delivery binding, sync_endpoints or explicit service delegation. Unknown, unauthorized, invisible, not-held and unavailable are outwardly indistinguishable and query/source/target rate limits prevent enumeration. The responder never returns a mirror-signed bare URL. The requester independently verifies every target proof, exact chain, freshness, method history and describe reverse binding; same sequence with different valid target-signed digests enters route-fork quarantine rather than majority, arrival-order or reachability selection.

Optional Signal Extension single-hop peer relay. The source batches original producer-signed encrypted SignalEnvelope values for one Realm and one destination service. The destination independently verifies peer authentication, current delivery binding, envelope proof, scope, Seal, signal_class, TTL and encrypted payload binding, then performs only local live fanout. The request MUST NOT carry Idempotency-Key; uncertain outcomes use drop_unconfirmed. The opaque accepted=true response reveals no Realm, scope, sender, recipient, binding, support, or per-signal result and is not a durable delivery receipt.
Federation peer snapshot manifest head for snapshot-assisted bootstrap. Requires service-to-service authentication and Realm federation_peer authorization.

The wrapper carries one complete DID method-native operation. did_method is the bare method discriminator and MUST equal the DID method component. Controller/update/recovery authorization comes only from the native operation; transport authentication is admission-only. Unsupported methods, generic replace/patch/document fallbacks, stale heads, and sibling forks fail closed. Exact canonical-operation retries are duplicate-success without a second history append.

Establish the local binding for an external, already-published Organization DID. The request MUST carry stable organization_id as did_core_id plus the current published full_id; the receiver independently resolves and validates full_id with the registered method adapter and requires project(full_id)=organization_id. The referenced challenge MUST bind both identifiers, local_admin_subject and the requested scope set, and the method-native control transcript MUST bind organization_id, full_id, the pinned version_id/log_head_digest and that challenge context. The outcome and signed receipt echo both identifiers; the receipt also binds version_id and control_key_digest so the accepted control state remains auditable. Creating a new Organization DID is a separate inception ceremony and has no member here. Idempotency is per generation: replaying the current generation's byte-identical request returns created=false, while a request after revoke, or one that changes local_admin_subject or the scope set, opens registration_generation+1 with created=true. This operation registers a reference and local administrative delegation only: it does not host the DID's method history, make this deployment the controller, or create Realm, membership, notary, capability or service delegation.

Issue a single-use control challenge for an external, already-published Organization DID. The request MUST carry stable organization_id as did_core_id and the current published full_id; before issuing the challenge the registry independently resolves and validates full_id with the registered method adapter and requires project(full_id)=organization_id. The response challenge echoes and binds both identifiers together with purpose, audience, origin, trust domain, nonce, requested scopes, beneficiary local_admin_subject and a window of at most 300 seconds. Two phases are mandatory: the registry remembers this challenge, then ensure supplies a method-native proof over the same control transcript. Folding the challenge into ensure would let the caller supply its own, defeating freshness and single use. The challenge MUST be consumed on first successful use. Deliberately not idempotent: every call mints a fresh nonce, and the caller MUST prove against the newest challenge.

Re-prove control at a newer resolved version and re-issue the receipt, returning created=false. The request MUST carry stable organization_id as did_core_id and the current published full_id; the receiver independently resolves and validates full_id with the registered method adapter and requires project(full_id)=organization_id. The fresh challenge and method-native control transcript bind both identifiers plus the refreshed version_id/log_head_digest. The refreshed outcome and signed receipt echo organization_id and full_id and bind version_id and control_key_digest. A same-core full_id refresh updates resolution/control state, not identity. Scopes are not renegotiated here; a scope change is a new ensure. Refresh exists because a binding pinned to one version stops proving current control after controller rotation and a first-time proof must not authorise the relationship indefinitely.

Withdraw the local binding by stable organization_id did_core_id only, returning the current binding outcome with a receipt whose status=revoked and created=false. No full_id is required because revoke addresses the already-bound local identity rather than resolving or proving fresh external control. This local act does not modify, deactivate or annotate the external DID's method history. revoked is terminal for the generation; re-establishing the relationship requires a fresh ensure with full_id, a new challenge and a new control proof.

Read the local binding by stable organization_id did_core_id without creating or mutating state; returns created=false. The outcome includes the current published full_id and signed receipt, with project(full_id)=organization_id and receipt/control-state bindings defined by OrganizationRegistrationOutcome and OrganizationRegistrationReceipt. Only bindings the caller is authorised to manage or see are returned. A caller with no such authorisation MUST receive the same not-found answer as for an organization that was never registered, so the query cannot enumerate which organizations a deployment has bound.

Publish a signed ak.schema.recovery_policy.v1 genesis policy or rotation as a Principal Control Realm ak.policy.set EventInitialSubmission. The canonical Event payload is {policy_id,value}; value is the complete RecoveryPolicy, both policy ids MUST match, and state/reason MUST be absent. Event actor/scope, value.principal_id, lease and accepted control Seal MUST agree. The command returns success only after the Event is covered by the immutable acceptance_basis; before Seal materialization it returns retry-safe frontier_unavailable for the same Event id.

Read the currently accepted ak.schema.recovery_policy.v1 projection for the authenticated or explicitly selected principal. Returns active_policy=null when no accepted policy exists; does not publish, rotate, or revoke policy state.

did_authority.when: proof_kind == did_root and the accepted PCR recovery policy explicitly enables the factor

operations.notes: Idempotently return or create the service identity bound to the canonical (service_kind, public_base) registration key. The client supplies full_id plus the client-controlled signed did:webvh inception operation; the Provider verifies the proof, requires state.id=full_id, projects full_id to the returned service_id did_core_id, and never receives private key material. Provider persistence MUST enforce UNIQUE(service_kind, public_base) and MUST reject an existing hosted document that declares the same key even when the mapping row is absent.
Read the service registration bound to the canonical (service_kind, public_base) key without creating or mutating identity state.

High-assurance optional endpoint to revoke a previously issued cursor authority. Revocation hits return cursor_revoked and MUST NOT advance account subscribe position, barrier wait, or dropped recovery state. To-device queue deletion is decoupled from cursors entirely and happens only via ak.self.device_messages.command.ack.

Carries exactly one holder-signed profile_event EventInitialSubmission and no unsigned patch. event.realm_id is the exact PrincipalAuthorityInstance PCR selector; accepted-profile presence is evaluated only in that PCR lineage. If it has no accepted Actor Profile, the Event must be ak.profile.create; its actor_profile ID is derived by retyping the create Event ID and payload.object must omit id. If it has an accepted Profile, the Event must be ak.profile.update, payload.target_ref must equal that create-derived ID, and the signed patch remains limited to display_name, avatar_blob_ref and profile_fields.<key>. Both branches bind realm scope to the same PCR and event.actor_id to the session principal. On create payload.object.principal_id must equal that principal; on update the accepted target profile's materialized principal_id must equal it. Direct holder proof is required without executor or Applet provenance. Event preconditions are empty; update concurrency uses only optional signed payload.expected_state_digest. The service forwards the exact bytes through ordinary Event admission without authoring, rebuilding, co-signing, choosing an ID or adding a concurrency guard. Until the Control Move has accepted Seal coverage the operation returns frontier_unavailable; exact retry after coverage returns the byte-identical stored outcome. The single accepted effect advances the holder account-aggregate projection once; it creates no Directory announcement or account-data Event.

Holder-bound one-shot read of the current principal account projection. Returns principal_id, account lifecycle state, device summaries, optional ActorProfile, and signed handle-claim evidence or refs. Because the operation has no authority-instance selector, profile is present only when exactly one accepted profile is unambiguous across the principal's PCR lineages; multiple accepted lineages fail closed by omitting profile, never by choosing an implicit current PCR. It MUST NOT return an unsigned bare handle as authoritative identity. Naming: the trailing segment 'viewer' is intentionally outside the api-conventions.md §2.4 read-verb taxonomy; it follows the GraphQL 'viewer' convention (the authenticated subject's own projection). The target is located by the holder-bound session rather than an external id, so 'get' does not apply, and 'viewer' (subject identity projection) stays distinct from 'describe' (service capability metadata).

Streaming push of cross-Realm account-aggregate deltas (cross-Realm frontier, to_device queue, account_data, device_lists, unread / notification counts). Signal envelopes use the Signal Extension live rail and are not account aggregate state. Connection is long-lived; server pushes NDJSON frames as new data becomes available.
Lists the authenticated actor's account_data entries. content is stored verbatim and is opaque to the server.

Submits the caller-signed tombstone ak.account_data.set Event. The actor-private cell subject is composite[envelope.actor_id, payload.key], so only the holder may sign it and the service MUST NOT author it under its own DID. expected_revision is the Event payload's; it is no longer a query parameter. deletion_mode=value_tombstone keys MUST still be refused here.

Reads one account_data entry by account_data_key key, including its compare-and-set revision. Returns not_found when the key is unset or holds a tombstone; the not_found error.details carry account_data_cas_conflict_details so the caller still learns current_revision.

Builds a ak.account_data.set actor-private write as a compare-and-set whole-value replacement: expected_revision must equal the accepted revision (0 to create) and the stored revision becomes expected_revision + 1. A mismatch returns cas_conflict with account_data_cas_conflict_details and stores nothing, so a stale offline retry can never overwrite a newer write. Controller-private registered types reject agent / applet / service principals. content is stored verbatim; clients own canonical encoding and (for sensitive keys) client-side encryption.

Consume an agent-provisioning abandonment challenge and explicitly give up an accepted ak.agent.provision whose declared managed Agent PCR genesis will never be submitted (zh/identity/key-management.md section 3.6.3). Authenticated by the controller user_session; the presented credentials MUST be fresh and MUST NOT be the ones presented when the challenge was issued, while re-authentication strength, risk checks and cooldown are deployment governance. One transaction consumes the challenge, releases the agent_slug selector claim and the principal_control_realm_id claim, records the tombstone / audit reservation and suppresses every holder-readable trace of the allocation; any step failing means zero writes. If the genesis was accepted between issuance and confirmation the request MUST fail with agent_pcr_genesis_already_accepted and MUST NOT abandon anything, because an established Agent is retired through ak.self.agent.command.deactivate. Replaying the same request_id returns the same terminal outcome and MUST NOT produce a second tombstone. The accepted provision Event stays in the controller PCR history and the abandoned realm id MUST NOT be reused.

Issue the single-use challenge that authorizes explicitly abandoning an accepted ak.agent.provision whose declared managed Agent PCR genesis was never accepted (zh/identity/key-management.md section 3.6.3). Authenticated by the controller user_session. The service requires agent_id, principal_control_realm_id and allocation_handle to equal the authenticated controller's accepted provision, and MUST refuse to issue a challenge once that genesis is accepted. The <=300s single-use challenge is bound to the controller account_subject, holder key, agent_id, agent_slug, the declared principal_control_realm_id, the allocation, the closed consequence disclosure, audience, origin, trust domain, purpose and expiry. Repeating the same request_id returns the same unconsumed challenge. Challenge state MUST be shared durable state, not process-local memory; expiry and prior consumption are distinct terminal states. This operation abandons nothing by itself and MUST NOT be reachable from lease expiry, garbage collection or any automated flow.

Controller-only caller-signed ak.capability.revoke Control Move. Path grant_id, payload grant_id/grant_ref, path Agent subject, target Realm, authenticated actor, the exact authority instance selected by the session, and the sole signed head_eq guard on the complete grant-cell head are all admission invariants. The service never authors the Event or appends CAS after signing; exact replay returns event.created_at as revoked_at.

Controller-only full replacement of one Account-Authority-owned per-scope selection. The authenticated bearer+DPoP session is the authority proof. First write uses expected_version=0; each accepted write increments the exact agent/scope slot by one. Governance ceilings and ordinary Agent capabilities are evaluated at action time and are not copied into this record.

Prepare fixes the new|existing branch, every reducer-derived coordinate, Event ID, canonical unsigned Event bytes and digest. It returns two controller-signing drafts for a new Sidecar and only an attach draft for an existing Sidecar. Commit accepts only proofs appended to those exact drafts. First ensure atomically admits exactly [ak.sidecar.create, ak.sidecar.context.attach]; attach must reference the reserved create Event with role after. The parent-Realm bootstrap exception is scoped only to create.

Controller-only paginated Sidecar list, optionally filtered by realm_id. Returns only Sidecars owned by the authenticated controller and never ordinary Circles or another controller's existence stubs.

Controller-only dedicated Sidecar read surface. Returns the typed Sidecar plus read-only owned/effective Agent sets, native MLS context and reconciliation readiness. Unauthorized, nonexistent, and foreign-controller IDs use one indistinguishable not_found envelope.

Closed selector XOR. current_admission binds the actual operation, request digest, verifier, audience and challenge and may authorize first live Signal evidence through current shared context. historical_event binds Event id, digest and receiver service and returns only the destination-signed admission receipt persisted when that exact Event was accepted; current state never reconstructs historical validity.

Read-only pre-admission of final signed Events followed by one authority-issued publication lease per Event. The operation never commits an Event or advances a frontier. Ordinary Events bind an accepted seal_ref/seal_basis; only complete registered genesis units may bind the ordered anchor_unit digest. Idempotent retry returns byte-identical leases.

Issues a short-TTL, single-blob, read-only pre-signed URL whose authorization material rides in the URL itself (query string). Used as a deliberate carve-out of the no-credentials-in-URL rule (server-threat-model.md S21) so that browser primitives like /

Media service token exchange operation. Issues a short-lived (TTL <= 600s) backend_token + participant_binding for joining a focus declared in ak.realm.media_service.foci[]. Same wire across all backend types (livekit / mediasoup / janus / arkret_native); only backend_token shape is type-specific. Token issuer DID MUST be one of the Realm-authorized media service DIDs; clients reject otherwise (token_issuer_unauthorised). See zh/crypto-media/media-service-binding.md §3.

Submits the caller-signed ak.circle.archive Event carried in lifecycle_event through ordinary Event admission; payload.target_ref MUST name the path Circle. Transition follows the Circle lifecycle matrix (reducer rejects illegal transitions with circle_not_active). The service MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event.

Submits the caller-signed ak.circle.create Event carried in create_event through ordinary Event admission; the parent Realm is create_event.event.realm_id. The Circle id is retype(create_event.event.event_id), so the service MUST NOT mint it, and MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event. Reducer-locked fields (mls_group_ref, state) MUST NOT be actor-supplied; encryption_profile='none' is allowed only when the parent Realm policy floor permits plaintext.

Submits the caller-signed ak.circle.restore Event carried in lifecycle_event through ordinary Event admission; payload.target_ref MUST name the path Circle. Transition follows the Circle lifecycle matrix (reducer rejects illegal transitions with circle_not_archived). Restore re-enables new writes after pending MLS membership removals are settled. The service MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event.

Rotates the Circle's bound MLS group. MUST NOT acknowledge a rotation without actually changing the cryptographic scope; returns unsupported_feature until the MLS genesis/commit/welcome cascade is wired end-to-end.

Submits the caller-signed ak.circle.tombstone Event carried in lifecycle_event through ordinary Event admission; payload.target_ref MUST name the path Circle. Terminal: the lifecycle matrix admits no transition out, so the signed Event is the whole record of who ended the Circle. Response surfaces the terminal state with empty members. The service MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event.

Submits the caller-signed ak.circle.member.state Event carried in member_event through ordinary Event admission; payload.circle_id MUST equal the path circle_id. Moving another actor to join requires ak.circle.member.manage narrowed to this Circle, evaluated against projected grants rather than asserted by the request, and the target MUST already be a joined parent-Realm member (strict-subset invariant); a self-join is gated by join_rule. The service MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event, nor add a capability verdict to the closed payload.

Submits the caller-signed ak.circle.member.state Event carried in member_event through ordinary Event admission. The Event membership MUST be leave and payload.expected_membership MUST carry the concrete current membership as its signed head_eq guard; payload.circle_id and payload.actor_id MUST equal the two path identifiers, and event.realm_id MUST equal the path Circle's parent Realm. Removing another actor requires ak.circle.member.manage narrowed to this Circle. The service MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event.
Lists Circles the caller may see within one parent Realm (required realm_id query). Directory visibility is enforced per Circle; non-members of a 'members'-visibility Circle MUST NOT see it.
Reads one Circle projection. Returns not_found when the Circle is invisible to the caller rather than disclosing existence.

Submits the caller-signed ak.consent.grant Control Move carried in grant_event through ordinary Event admission. payload.consent_id is the producer-allocated cell subject and the or_set add dot is 'ak:event:<enclosing event_id>:<write_index>', so the service chooses neither and MUST NOT synthesize the Event. The authenticated actor MUST be authorized to write the holder's consent (holder or an explicitly authorized controller/agent).

Submits an opaque consent-contact request from the authenticated peer. peer_principal_id defaults to and MUST equal the actor. The response is identical for missing holders, policy denial, rate limiting, silent drop and quarantine acceptance; the operation never returns a consent cell.

Submits the caller-signed ak.consent.revoke Control Move carried in revoke_event through ordinary Event admission. Its payload.observed_dots MUST enumerate the active grant dots being removed for the (consent_id, peer, consent_scope), read back from consent_cell_view.active_grant_dots. Revoking consent_scope=any cascades all concrete scopes and MUST still enumerate every dot; revoking a concrete scope leaves others intact.
Lists holder-private consent cells for the authenticated holder only. Peer actors MUST NOT receive cell state, dots, expiry or request timestamps.
Reads one holder-private consent cell. The authenticated actor MUST equal holder_principal_id or be an explicitly authorised holder controller; peers never receive this DTO.

Two-phase holder-local terminal reject. The service accepts only the holder-signed ak.contact.rejected Event bytes reserved for the exact current request slot, signs the matching rejection acceptance receipt, and provides durable exact replay/conflict semantics independently from normal accept responses.

Two-phase holder-local acceptance of one holder-signed ak.contact.requested fact. The accepted source receipt, peer closed XOR, full directional scope set and issuer-local slot lineage are durable replay inputs; no Private Consent Event is written or consulted.

Two-phase holder-local normal accept response. The service accepts only the holder-signed response Event bytes reserved for the current request slot, signs the matching normal-response acceptance receipt, and never writes Private Consent. Reject uses the separate ak.self.contact.command.reject operation. Glare is mechanically derived from two causally concurrent request receipts and forbids this operation.

Two-phase prepare/commit carrier for one holder-signed ak.contact.scope.update full-set directional replacement. Request/response establishes the issuer-local version 1 genesis; every scope replacement is version >= 2, exactly current+1, and references the exact issuer-local current head. Expansion and narrowing are both explicit signed replacements.
Holder-signed issuer-local lineage terminal. It consumes the Contact basis and generation; it does not carry scope replacement and does not write or revoke Private Consent.

Holder contact projection from source-signed request/response receipts, issuer-local Contact lineages and current signed head leases. An accepted row also carries the closed next_prepare_input cursor whose basis_id, version and predecessor_event_ref are copied verbatim into the prepare phase of ak.self.contact.command.scope_update or ak.self.contact.command.tombstone; every other contact_state omits it, and the projected request/response/tombstone event refs are never authoritative lineage heads. A pending_incoming row likewise carries request_receipt, the complete signed request_acceptance_receipt copied verbatim into the prepare phase of ak.self.contact.command.respond or ak.self.contact.command.reject; it is signed by the peer's source service rather than by this server, so the client verifies it independently instead of trusting this server's retelling. Every other contact_state omits it, because pending_outgoing has no incoming request to answer and accepted, rejected, expired and tombstoned have a consumed admission slot or a terminal basis; a glare pair is never pending_incoming, so the glare ban on respond and reject needs no extra code. Private Consent and account-data notes are never Contact authority.

Issue one immutable current-authority authority Ack for a fully signed Control Move. Local device/Agent authorities use the same typed request and outcome without an HTTP hop. A caller canonically sorts distinct authority Acks and may submit the resulting receipt set only when the current notary profile quorum and common-window rules are satisfied.

Explicit, cumulative, monotonic to-device delivery acknowledgement (client-sync.md §10.1). Queue deletion happens only here; stream cursor advancement (account subscribe after=, device_messages after=) is read-only and MUST NOT prune the queue. Re-acking the same or an older token is a legal no-op. Unknown / expired / cross-bound tokens are rejected with invalid_param (reason invalid_ack_token) without deleting anything.

Enqueues caller-supplied DeviceMessageEnvelope targets into recipient device queues. Each target carries a sender-assigned message_id copied unchanged into the stored envelope; the service deduplicates logical messages by (sender_principal_id, sender_device_id, message_id), returning the existing outcome for identical canonical target content and duplicate_conflict/message_id_conflict for different content. HTTP batch replay is additionally deduplicated by (sender, Idempotency-Key). Queue pruning is only via ak.self.device_messages.command.ack.

Query-only resolver for the pair's single stable Direct Conversation. It never creates: a Direct Conversation Realm is created solely by the founder derived from the pair's root Contact basis (normal branch takes the responder, glare branch takes the requests[0] issuer) through the direct_conversation_genesis admission variant of ak.realm.create. Outcomes are evaluated in a fixed order and expose creation_required, creation_blocked, awaiting_founder, provisional, found, suspended or temporarily_unavailable. Whenever an accepted active-generation singleton exists the response carries active_mls_generation_ref and sha256(RFC8785_JCS(current accepted cell whole value)) as one pair; found always carries both, and a repairable suspended state never hides them. Waiting never grants create authority to the non-founder and there is no timeout fallback or takeover.

Authenticated requester command for durable Direct Conversation replacement-repair delivery. The caller supplies one request_id, exact non-authorizing repair content and a closed device-or-Native-Agent detached authorization, but never recipient targets. In one source transaction keyed by the authenticated requester and request_id, the service validates current participant/rejoin/contact/generation gates, freezes request_digest plus the current destination Principal Server binding, persists the byte-identical peer-relay body and outbox state, and returns only after the destination has durably atomically enqueued its frozen closed human-device-fanout or Native-Agent-runtime target. Exact replay returns the original byte-identical outcome; a changed digest is duplicate_conflict. No Event or repair acknowledgement is synthesized.

Authenticated principal session requests one durable frozen AcceptedAtServiceBinding core after DID publication and PCR acceptance. The service derives current DID authority evidence, its own service metadata/key/origins and timestamps; the caller supplies none of them. Omitting expected_current_binding_digest is create-if-absent, supplying it is same-service renewal CAS. The service-generated challenge is copied into binding_draft.authorization_challenge and therefore binding_digest. Same request_id and intent replays the same unconsumed draft; different intent conflicts.

Commit the exact durable binding draft with a principal proof whose method is valid at accepted_at. The service recomputes both transcripts and atomically CAS-installs the immutable accepted binding, signs the service-acceptance proof, consumes the challenge and stores the byte-identical outcome. Exact request replay returns that outcome; challenge reuse, expiry, digest/proof mismatch or a moved current pointer writes nothing.

Initial durable Event publication uses EventInitialSubmission: the signed Event remains the only business fact, while AuthorizationLease and optional CbaProofBundle values are independently verified publication evidence outside the Event digest. The ingress MUST persist and return the original IngressReceipt before lease expiry; byte-identical retry returns the stored receipt without changing received_at. For ak.invite.claim, the receiving Realm reducer remains the authoritative state machine and re-checks token commitment, allowlist, replay, proposal and expiry state. The request union additionally registers the discriminated direct_conversation_founding branch, the only carrier for a Direct Conversation founding unit: the founder authors all three Events itself, realm_id and main_strand_id are retyped from the first and third Event IDs, and the service allocates no identifier and issues no draft. That branch requires exactly three ordered EventInitialSubmission items, closed XOR founder basis evidence and an idempotency_key, accepts zero or three Events inside one slot transaction, and returns DirectConversationFoundingAcceptanceOutcome with the source-signed receipt. Same key plus the same unit replays the byte-identical receipt without advancing accepted_at; same key plus a different unit is duplicate_conflict; a slot already closed by another unit for the same pair is slot_already_committed. All four outcomes write zero Events on failure.

Submit a client-signed Seal. Except for the canonical genesis exception, the signature MUST satisfy the predecessor governance state's ak.component.notary.v1 membership and threshold rules; Realm visibility or device ownership is insufficient. The receiver recomputes the Seal id, recursive coverage, completeness_root, state_root, signer authority and signature.

Return one bounded, manifest-committed chunk of a complete_control_state_v1 proof bundle for one authenticated, caller-visible Realm/scope. The request MUST name an exact locally trusted_anchor_seal_id and chunk_index; later chunks pin expected_bundle_digest. The service MUST build from that anchor and return mls_governance_anchor_unreachable instead of substituting another anchor. From one accepted Seal view it supplies enough complete state to rederive the closed key-access projection in mls-security-frontier-registry.json; callers cannot supply roots or choose frontier members. Responses bind canonical acquisition identity with proof_request_digest, commit all chunks under chunks_root, and use bundle_digest rather than accepted_seal_id as the logical content address. Each response is at most 4 MiB; the logical bundle is at most 256 MiB, 1024 chunks, 4096 Seals, 1048576 covered digests, 262144 control leaves and 128 frontier Events. Exceeding a total bound returns mls_governance_proof_bounds_exceeded with no partial output. Implementations MUST enforce Realm/scope visibility before materialization and MUST fail closed when any covered Event, control state, Seal path, chunk commitment, signature authority, or reducer profile cannot be reconstructed.
Dereference a known set of event_id / event_digest references to full EventEnvelope objects. Point lookup by identifier, not a range scan — use ak.self.events.read.scan for selector-based reads.
Canonical safe and idempotent Events range scan. HTTP uses RFC 10008 QUERY with typed JSON content.

Long-lived per-Realm / actor event stream with optional bounded catch-up replay. `dropped` and `resync_required` control frames MAY carry `reconnect_after_ms`, a server-directed minimum delay before opening another subscription for the same caller/selector scope; early reconnects are rejected with rate_limited / Retry-After.
Issues a fresh opaque locator for the authenticated principal. subject_id and recipient_service_id are server-derived; the raw bearer token is returned exactly once and MUST NOT be persisted.
Idempotently revokes one locator owned by the authenticated principal. A same-principal retry returns the original revoked_at. Unknown, consumed, or cross-principal locator ids return not_found.

Atomically revokes one authenticated-principal-owned locator and issues a new opaque token. The old token becomes indistinguishable from unknown tokens before success is returned. After an uncertain transport outcome, the client MUST first idempotently revoke the old locator_id and only then issue fresh material; directly issuing without that revocation can leave the old token active.

Read the authenticated subject's private invite-receive policy. Returns the recommended default when no explicit override is stored; the response is never written into the target Realm durable event log.

Replace the authenticated subject's private invite-receive policy. The body MUST set subject_id equal to the session actor; the override shares the same store as ak.self.contact.command.tombstone(block_peer) denied_subjects writes.

Transaction-bound monotonic erasure of the exact old secret_storage and mls_history series reserved by a SecurityRotationTransaction. Partial outcomes persist per series/object; exact retry never resurrects or rewrites an erased item. A complete outcome carries the sole canonical erase confirmation.

Issues the durable, single-use, short-TTL (<=300s) challenge that every high-risk backup delete proof must sign over. While a challenge for the same (principal_id, backup_id, request_id) is still valid the service returns the same challenge; a different request_id mints a new one. See key-management.md section 7.8.1.

High-risk delete guarded by a server-issued single-use challenge and the shared high-risk authority proof family (key-management.md section 7.8/7.8.1). The challenge is consumed atomically with the first successful delete; a byte-identical retry returns the stored terminal outcome, and the same request_id with a different canonical digest is a duplicate conflict.

Requester-signed self KeyPackage claim. Exactly one holder_acceptance detached-JWS proof binds the complete proof-free request, authority service DID, requester and at-least-128-bit claim_nonce. The authority atomically commits KeyPackage CAS, (requester, claim_nonce, payload_digest) ledger and byte-identical terminal outcome; exact retries return that outcome and conflicting digest reuse fails before inventory lookup.

Carries exactly one direct-holder signed report_event EventInitialSubmission and no unsigned report fields. The Event kind is ak.self.moderation.report; this self endpoint accepts only absent/self provenance and forbids source_provider, delegated executor, Applet and MIMI-facade provenance. event.actor_id and payload.reporter must equal the authenticated session principal. There is no path Realm: event.realm_id, payload.realm_id, signed scope_ref and the accepted target's derived governance scope must match exactly. Realm-default reports may omit payload.effective_scope; Circle reports must sign the exact Circle scope. The target must be accepted and visible to the reporter; absent, invisible and scope-mismatched targets use the same not_found response. This DataEvent carries seal_ref plus auth_context and cannot carry seal_basis or preconditions. The service forwards exact signed bytes through ordinary Event admission and never authors, rebuilds, co-signs, maps an operation ref to another target or adds a concurrency guard. report_id is derived by retyping the accepted Event id and the stored submit outcome has status=submitted. Exact replay returns that byte-identical outcome without a second log or queue append; the same Event identity with different bytes returns duplicate_conflict. routed_to is omitted for an ordinary reporter and may be returned only when the caller independently holds moderation/governance capability for the exact scope.
Extension read surface listing reducer-maintained Morph lifecycle rows for a Realm. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.

Optional extension read surface returning the authorized document body, version, relation, comment, and cursor-presence read-model for a single document Morph addressed within its Realm. Canonical truth remains the Morph/Relation/Message event history.
Canonical HTTP binding is POST /_arkret/self/policy/check. Paths carry no version segment; protocol version is negotiated via *.describe / supported_operations (see sync/api-conventions.md).

Accepts exactly one caller-signed ak.read_cursor.advance actor-private Event. The Event payload is the complete ak.schema.read_cursor.v1 cursor; envelope.actor_id and payload.actor_id MUST equal the authenticated holder, payload.device_id MUST equal the authenticated session device, and envelope.realm_id MUST equal payload.realm_id. The service validates and forwards the exact Event bytes and MUST NOT mint the cursor id, choose updated_at, rebuild the payload or co-sign. Multi-device convergence is causal-first per zh/discovery/read-receipts.md section 6.5: a position that causally dominates the other wins regardless of HLC; HLC max applies only to causally concurrent positions, and device_id lexicographic order only breaks equal HLCs. The cursor is never published into shared Realm history.
Lists the authenticated actor's read markers, optionally filtered by the realm_id query param.

Submits the caller-signed ak.realm.archive Move carried in lifecycle_event through ordinary Event admission; event.realm_id MUST equal the path realm_id. The archived facet changes when the lifecycle event is accepted into the Realm event log; archived=false clears the archived facet unless a terminal lifecycle state already applies. The service MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event.

Submits the caller-signed terminal ak.realm.destroy Move carried in lifecycle_event through ordinary Event admission; event.realm_id MUST equal the path realm_id. The destroyed state changes when the lifecycle event is accepted into the Realm event log; later ordinary writes fail with realm_terminal_state. The service MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event.

Submits the caller-signed ak.realm.freeze Move carried in lifecycle_event through ordinary Event admission; event.realm_id MUST equal the path realm_id. The frozen facet changes when the lifecycle event is accepted into the Realm event log; frozen=true rejects ordinary non-exempt writes with realm_frozen and frozen=false clears the freeze facet unless a terminal lifecycle state already applies. The service MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event.

Submits the caller-signed terminal ak.realm.tombstone Move carried in lifecycle_event through ordinary Event admission; event.realm_id MUST equal the path realm_id and payload.successor_realm_id is required. The tombstoned state changes when the lifecycle event is accepted into the Realm event log; later ordinary writes fail with realm_terminal_state. The service MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event.
Reads only the profile-private submit/read/review/cancel/invite-consume audit trail for one application. Applicant, eligible reviewer, or explicitly authorized Realm auditor only.
Candidate-profile private applicant cancellation. The caller and detached receipt signer must both be the original applicant.

Candidate-profile private reviewer decision. The reviewer-signed receipt binds the exact application revision and a capability grant/frontier proof; stale, expired or unauthorized decisions fail closed.

Candidate-profile private application intake. The applicant-signed receipt binds the accepted knock, policy/revision/private-body digests and applicant DID. The receipt and private body commit atomically and never enter shared Realm history.
Lists candidate application metadata. Reviewers and each matching applicant receive the protected body; other Realm members receive only application_pending placeholders.
Reads one candidate application for its applicant or an eligible reviewer. Every successful private-body read emits ak.audit.accessed.
Returns the organization-inherited effective moderation policy view: inheritance chain, organization policy layers, the Realm's own override, and merged effective rules.

Carries exactly one caller-signed ak.realm.moderation_policy EventInitialSubmission. The request contains moderation_policy_event and no unsigned policy projection; the closed Event payload contains only value, whose value is the complete policy object. event.realm_id must equal the path Realm, event.actor_id must equal the authenticated session actor, and the exact submitted bytes pass ordinary Event admission without service authorship, rebuilding, co-signing or precondition injection. The Event carries exactly one signed head_eq against ak:cell:ak.component.realm.moderation_policy.v1:null naming the complete settled value or null when absent. Admission follows the capability registry and accepts ak.realm.moderation_policy or ak.policy.manage; Realm ownership alone grants no write authority. Organization-approval constraints and any extra action capability required by policy contents are evaluated during admission. Exact byte replay of an accepted Event returns the byte-identical stored outcome; identity/body conflict, stale head, Bottom or multiple applicable CAS guards fails closed with zero additional writes.
Full event-log + operation dump for a Realm (schema ak.export.realm.v1). Caller must be authorized to read the Realm; payload visibility still follows Realm policy.
Reads the Realm lifecycle projection (owner + members + deleted). Returns not_found when the Realm is invisible to the caller.

Submits the caller-signed ak.realm.link Control Move from realm_id -> target_realm_id; the service MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize it. The edge is event.payload and the source Realm is event.realm_id, which MUST equal the path realm_id. General directed cycles are valid and traversal uses a visited set; admission rejects only self-reference, invalid kind, invalid payload, or an illegal FSM transition. Self-reference returns schema_violation with reason_code realm_link_self_reference; an illegal transition returns failed_precondition with reason_code realm_link_invalid_transition.

Returns the merged effective policy after walking governed_by / inherits_policy_from ancestors per the Realm's ak.realm.inheritance_policy. inheritance_mode=none when no inheritance policy is projected (implicit inheritance is forbidden).
Lists typed cross-Realm links projected from ak.realm.link. direction is outbound/inbound/both; link_kind_allow is a comma-separated allowlist of canonical link kinds.

Submits the caller-signed tombstoning ak.realm.link Move (payload.status=tombstoned) for the (realm_id, target_realm_id, link_kind) triple; the service MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize it. link_kind is named in the signed payload rather than a query parameter, because a query parameter is outside the bytes the caller signs; payload.target_realm_id MUST equal the path target_realm_id. Removing an edge is the same durable Event kind as creating one, so this operation keeps its event_log effect.

Returns the projected ak.realm.organization relationship statements for the Realm (active / revoked / expired, latest-per-(organization_id, relationship)) plus declared owning_organizations hints with no verified statement. The caller must be authorized to read the Realm. A relationship is only verified when lifecycle_phase=verified_active; declared_organization_hints are unverified claims and MUST NOT be rendered as official / governed / endorsed.

After ak.policy.manage admission, a settled direct declaration is deleted by the caller-signed durable ak.realm.policy_server Move with the exact payload {"tombstone":true} and head_eq for the complete declaration; the service MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize it, which is why this DELETE carries a request body the way ak.self.keys.backups.resource.delete already does. The registered cas_register effect sets that value in the per-Realm cell; effective reads then ignore the direct binding and resume governed_by fallback or local-only capability evaluation. Repeating DELETE against a settled tombstone is an idempotent empty success and MUST NOT change the cell or state_root. A never-written or inherited-only direct cell returns not_found and MUST NOT mutate an ancestor.
Reads the projected ak.realm.policy_server config. Returns not_found when neither the Realm nor its governed_by ancestor chain declared one. from_org_fallback=true marks an inherited config.

Submits the caller-signed durable ak.realm.policy_server declaration Move (admission capability ak.policy.manage); the service MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize it. The declaration is event.payload and the Realm is event.realm_id, which MUST equal the path realm_id. Reducer validates the DID, canonical HTTPS policy-check URL and on_timeout enum. When the direct cell already has a settled declaration or tombstone, the Move MUST carry head_eq for that complete value and the caller attaches it, because preconditions are inside the signed bytes; an absent direct cell is the only initial write.

Continues only the stored next_required_step. request_digest, prepared_plan_digest and expected_next_step MUST equal the resource; the endpoint is not a generic step or Saga executor. Client attestation is required only for issue_terminal_receipt or local_commit and must bind transaction/request/plan plus the pre-reserved output_ref. When all coordinator-owned recovery steps are accepted but the device is offline, the resource remains awaiting_device_attestation rather than completed.

Creates exactly one durable RecoveryTransaction or SecurityRotationTransaction. The coordinator MUST atomically persist canonical request bytes, request_digest, the closed typed prepared_plan and prepared_plan_digest, all reserved public ids, and the initial resource before the first irreversible side effect. Recovery create also CAS-binds one already verified recovery session to this transaction. Same transaction_id plus identical bytes returns the recorded resource; different bytes returns duplicate_conflict.

Authoritative durable progress query by transaction_id. It MUST return the stored binding, accepted step prefix, next action, and terminal outcome and MUST NOT synthesize state from a short-lived HTTP idempotency cache.

Encrypted-only Signal Extension send rail for ak.schema.signal_envelope.v1. Exact signal type and product target remain inside ciphertext. It MUST NOT persist the envelope as a durable Event or advance actor_seq / Realm frontier.

Authenticated encrypted-only Signal Extension receive rail. Frames carry SignalEnvelope objects or bounded transport control frames; exact signal type and product target remain inside ciphertext. No catch-up or durable delivery guarantee.
Extension read surface listing reducer-maintained Space lifecycle rows for a Realm. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.
Extension read surface listing reducer-maintained Strand lifecycle rows for a Realm. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.

Optional extension read surface that materializes a View{kind=collection} projection such as board/list/table/calendar. The response is a derived read model computed from signed Events, reducer profile, View definition, and the returned frontier; it is not a canonical truth source.

success_shape_kind_definitions.service_describe: ServiceDescribe object returned by a describe endpoint.
success_shape_kind_definitions.schema_resource: Response body is a canonical artifact JSON Schema resource.
success_shape_kind_definitions.inline_response: Endpoint-specific inline object schema in OpenAPI.
success_shape_kind_definitions.operation_result: Generic OperationResult envelope; operation row MUST carry generic_binding.
success_shape_kind_definitions.event_stream: Long-lived event stream rather than a single JSON success body.
success_shape_kind_definitions.metadata_headers: Metadata-only success expressed through HTTP headers.

risk_tier_definitions.low: Read, projection, discovery, ack, and account-private affordances. Freshness fail-closed treats unknown / stale as local-pending allowed (capabilities.md §18).
risk_tier_definitions.medium: Object create / update / delete, message authoring, invite issuance, MLS proposal, audit query. Freshness requires recent frontier within freshness_required_ms.
risk_tier_definitions.high: Capability mutation, policy mutation, lifecycle freeze / tombstone / destroy, schema redefinition, MLS commit / welcome / genesis, audit export, moderation decision, admin / hierarchy / upgrade. Freshness MUST be within freshness_required_ms; partition forces local pending with no peer visibility.

registry_rules: Wire capability grant.actions[] entries MUST be drawn from this registry; wildcards / segment globs are statically rejected by capability-grant.schema.json.

Receivers MUST default to risk_tier=high when an action submitted in a grant or evaluated in policy is not present in this registry; this is the freshness fail-closed default required by capabilities.md §18.

required_constraints lists typed-constraint shorthand names that the capability evaluator MUST enforce for the action regardless of the grant author's declarations; absence in this list does NOT disable other declared constraints.

required_evaluator_checks lists non-grant-field invariants (for example actor_eq_target_author or audit_pair_required) that admission control MUST enforce from Event context, reducer state, or paired audit evidence. These are not grant-constraint schema fields.

target_event_kinds links the action to one or more ak.* event_kinds in event_kind_registry. Empty array means the action authorizes a read / projection / signaling path that does not produce a durable reducer-input event. Reducer admission for a listed event_kind MUST verify the actor holds at least one matching action grant.

profile is null for v1 core actions, or a ak.profile.*.v<n> id when the action is only meaningful inside that profile. Receivers without the named profile MUST treat the action as unknown (risk_tier=high default).

Every action MUST declare event_mapping_kind. action == single target_event_kind uses same_name; empty target_event_kinds uses non_event_surface; any other mapping MUST use one of the allowed deviation categories.

grant_authority_actions lists the action ids an issuer holding this action MAY sign a grant for (capabilities.md section 3.2 issuer upper bound). It is a separate namespace from target_event_kinds, which only expresses direct Event admission: several actions can map to one event kind, so an event-kind subset MUST NOT be used to satisfy an action-level grant authority question.

coverage_rule and grant_authority_rule declare how target_event_kinds and grant_authority_actions are derived from the other rows. When a rule is present the materialized list is a cached projection: tools/artifact_pipeline.py generate rewrites it and check rejects any hand edit on either this registry or the generated view.

root_control_only=true marks an action that only the current controller of the Realm authority-root cell may author. It is never grantable and never enters a derived owner authority set. subject_only=true marks a self-service action whose only authority is the target subject's own signature. reducer_only=true marks a record the reducer materializes and no principal may author. The three flags are orthogonal and combinable.

actions.notes: Authorizes the installed Applet service to invoke the closed Ghost Actor provisioning aggregate for one exact effective Realm scope. The operation accepts the caller-signed ak.identity.accountability_grant + ak.profile.create pair atomically; it is not a generic authorization for either Event kind.

Reducer-materialized record of a Realm-link inheritance derivation (zh/models/realm-links.md section 6). No principal authors it and no principal can be granted it, so it is excluded from every derived owner authority set.

Subject-only self-service release of the actor own grant. Authority comes from the target grant subject signature and the reducer target guard, never from a capability, so it is excluded from every derived authority set.

Read-only audit access for a Realm admin NOT in the target Circle. MUST be paired with ak.audit.accessed event. Does NOT yield historical decryption keys unless the admin is formally added to the Circle.

Creates an intra-Realm Circle (scoped event/message boundary; optionally MLS-backed depending on parent Realm floor). NOT in default member bundle by default — Circles should be few and stable. See zh/models/circle.md §8.
Manage an existing Circle. MUST be constrained to specific circle_id selectors; unconstrained Realm-wide grant is not a normal management permission.
Self-service: actor accepts an invite, joins a join_rule=open Circle, or leaves. Reducer enforces payload.actor_id == envelope.actor_id and transition legality. Self-unbanning MUST fail closed.
Cross-actor write (rare). MUST carry ak.audit.accessed pair (same model as ak.strand.watch.set.others).
Invite / remove others. Held by Circle admin. payload.actor_id != envelope.actor_id.

Authorizes only the transaction-bound old-series targets in a fixed SecurityRotationTransaction plan after both replacement active-series pointers are accepted. It never authorizes deleting an active or unplanned backup series.
Direct Conversation participant self-leave only. It never authorizes leave/ban/remove of the other participant or any join transition.

Accepted-at compensation for a self-authored join only. It authorizes one fresh standard leave transition for the exact admission and old membership incarnation; it cannot be transferred or used as ordinary membership authority.

Accepted-at compensation for a delegated/admin-authored join only. It authorizes one fresh standard remove transition for the exact admission and old membership incarnation; it grants no Realm admin capability.

Direct Conversation exact-pair self-rejoin only. It never authorizes a first join, a third participant, or a join authored on behalf of the other participant, and it never authorizes any grant, policy, admin, Strand or binding change.

Authorizes adding an audience_mention node such as @all or @here to a Message create/revise. @here maps to audience="strand_engaged" and is not presence-filtered. This is an additional gate: the actor MUST also be authorized for the underlying message create/revise action. Effective Realm/Circle policy MUST allow the audience and declare finite max_recipients/quota before notification fanout.

Authorizes a decrypted ak.message.stream Signal payload for one discussion Strand. It is an additional recipient-verified gate: the sender MUST also hold ak.message.create. The service cannot inspect or advertise the encrypted payload kind or Strand target.

Narrow Direct Conversation participant authority for welcoming another currently authorized device of the same stable participant. It cannot add a third principal or a device of the other participant.
Authorizes reading an object's discussion / history events (message timeline, redacted-message metainfo, prior revisions). Read / projection surface only; emits no durable reducer event.

Claims, renames or tombstones the Realm's human-readable alias (ak.realm.alias event; projects ak.component.realm.alias.v1). high risk because an alias is the address users type and share: capturing or re-pointing one is a phishing / impersonation primitive. Holding ak.realm.admin (aggregate admin coverage) satisfies admission, or grant this specific action directly. See zh/discovery/object-addressing.md §3.3.

Re-anchors the authority-root capability-action registry digest to a retrievable, recomputable, active snapshot. Changes neither controller nor generation and never retroactively widens an existing grant.
Advances the authority generation, invalidating every grant anchored to the previous one at read time. Destructive root control; never grantable.

Terminal Realm lifecycle. Authored only by the current controller of the Realm authority-root cell with an independent destructive confirmation; it MUST NOT be granted to anyone, so it is excluded from every derived owner authority set.

Highest explicit authority inside one Realm. Held either by the current controller of the ak.component.realm.authority_root.v1 cell (root authority, not a grant) or by an ordinary revocable co-owner grant. Both derived sets are rule-generated; hand edits are rejected by tools/artifact_pipeline.py check.

Rotates the controller binding of the Realm authority-root cell. Authored only by the current controller with successor acceptance; it MUST NOT be granted, so it is excluded from every derived owner authority set.

Sets / changes the Realm's authoritative default discussion Strand pointer (ak.realm.set_default_strand event; projects Realm default_strand_id). Same-name discipline. The Realm authz gate is realm-admin: holding ak.realm.admin (aggregate admin coverage) satisfies admission, or grant this specific action directly. Reducer MUST verify the referenced Strand already exists (failed_precondition otherwise). See zh/models/strand-and-message.md default-Strand discovery section.
Terminal Realm lifecycle with a successor pointer. Same root-control family as ak.realm.destroy: authored only by the current authority-root controller and never grantable.

Authorizes durable history-key delivery after the independent membership, device, history-sharing policy, source_authorization_ref, and recipient checks succeed. This explicit high-risk action is not implied by ak.realm.admin.

event_mapping_kind_definitions.same_name: Action maps one-to-one to an identically named durable event kind.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.non_event_surface: Action authorizes read/projection/signaling behavior that does not emit a durable reducer event.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.aggregate_admin: Action intentionally covers a bounded administrative family of event kinds.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.polymorphic_object: Action covers the same object-lifecycle verb across multiple object event kinds.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.scope_suffix_variant: Action adds actor/scope/role qualifiers while reducer admission targets a shared event kind.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.operation_verb: Action token names an operation/command verb that does not match its target event kind name(s); reducer admission resolves the resulting event kind(s) via target_event_kinds. Literal action matching per the actions[] rule applies; carries no aggregate-admin family semantics.

registry_rules: A calendar schedule MUST carry a signed tzdb_version naming one release row below. Receivers resolve timezone and every derived instant with that release, never with their locally installed release.

Release rows are append-only and each row is frozen once published, including its own required_normalizations table, because historical schedules signed that row. Withdrawing a release is expressed by setting status=deprecated, never by deleting or rewriting the row.

required_normalizations is per release, not global. A later IANA release that changes a Link target expresses that by carrying a different mapping in its own row; the earlier row keeps the mapping that was in force when those schedules were signed. A global table could not represent both at once and would silently break the append-only promise.

Determinism comes from the release tag: IANA tzdata release tags are immutable once published. This registry deliberately does not mirror the full Zone/Link table and does not pin a distribution digest, because a hand-copied mirror would drift from IANA and become a second truth source, and this repository cannot verify third-party distribution bytes. Deployments that additionally need supply-chain pinning verify the distribution in their own build; that pinning is out of scope for v1 interop.

Canonicalization is defined by the Link declarations of the pinned IANA release as published by IANA, in particular its backward and etcetera files: the canonical Zone is the Link target. It is NOT defined by whatever a given platform time zone library happens to expose, since distributions may build the same release with different link handling.

Producers MUST rewrite timezone to the canonical Zone before signing. Receivers MUST NOT re-canonicalize a signed value: an alias that reaches the wire is a producer defect and MUST be rejected, not repaired. The RSVP occurrence key reuses the exact signed timezone value.

Each row required_normalizations is the conformance-required subset that vectors pin for that release. It is not the full alias set; an input outside the table is still canonicalized by that release Link declarations.

Updating a schedule tzdb_version MAY change derived instants but MUST NOT change the signed timezone value or any local occurrence key. When any occurrence instant or end changes, the significant-change table requires RSVP needs_reconfirmation plus a schedule notification.

A service that cannot execute a schedule tzdb_version MUST fail closed with calendar_tzdb_mismatch or unsupported_feature, or mark instant projection unresolved. Falling back to a nearby or newer release is forbidden. Services declare their executable set in ServiceDescribe.calendar_tzdb_versions.

releases.notes: v1 conformance baseline release. Frozen: this row required_normalizations is the mapping schedules pinned to 2025a were signed against.
Appended release; schedules pinned to it expand with its rules only. Its required_normalizations is identical to 2025a because no listed Link target changed between the two releases.

registry_rules: Only an active adapter row can validate a full_id or project it to did_core_id. DID syntax alone never admits a method.
project is a method-defined semantic transform over a canonical bare full_id, not generic string concatenation or prefix removal. Receivers compare the complete projected did_core_id byte-for-byte.

Every adapter validates method-native control, deactivation, currentness and history evidence according to its trust profile before returning a verified projection. Unknown methods and unknown adapter versions fail closed.

A new full_id is an update of an existing principal or service only when the same active adapter projects it to the identical did_core_id. A method or core change creates a new identity and cannot inherit authorization through a continuity assertion.
DID URLs are constructed and compared from the verified full_id under the adapter's DID URL rules. A did_core_id is never used as a DID URL base.

A full_id is a canonical bare DID and therefore contains no path, query or fragment. Each active adapter deterministically emits method_history_head, version_id and service_resolution_event_ref according to its registered rules, including synthetic values for methods without native history.

For a generic Event proof, the verifier extracts the canonical bare full_id base from proof.verification_method, validates the active adapter and key at the cited accepted-at method history, projects that full_id, and compares the resulting did_core_id to executed_by when present or actor_id otherwise. registration_anchor and pcr_recovery are the only registered special admissions and never convert current DID control into generic human PCR authority.

A principal resolution update is admitted only in its derived identity-control Realm and only when one exact head_eq precondition guards ak:cell:ak.component.identity.resolution.v1:null. The guarded whole resolution_projection MUST equal the accepted current cell and MUST cross-bind payload.previous_resolution_event_ref and payload.previous_method_history_head.

checks: principal_genesis_event.kind == ak.realm.create and principal_genesis_event is resolution head 0
every post-genesis event is ak.identity.resolution.update with actor_id == principal_id and realm_id == principal_control_realm_id

if current_resolution_event is principal_genesis_event then predecessor_resolution_events is empty; otherwise predecessor_resolution_events[0] is the current Event's guarded immediate predecessor when history_depth is nonzero

the supplied resolution events form a contiguous immediate-predecessor segment backward from current_resolution_event under the exact guarded whole-cell values; if the segment reaches head 0 it terminates at principal_genesis_event, otherwise the oldest guarded predecessor is the next audit cursor and omitted history is never treated as absent
accepted_seal.realm_id == principal_control_realm_id and accepted_seal recursively covers both principal_genesis_event.event_digest and current_resolution_event.event_digest
resolution_cell_proof.cell_value equals the registry projection of current_resolution_event
method_history_evidence boundary and currentness validate under the adapter selected by cell_value.full_id

adapters.version_id_rule: The exact method-native versionId of that same verified current did:webvh log entry, serialized as a non-empty string.
adapters.service_resolution_event_ref_rule: did-webvh-entry-sha256:<the same 64 lowercase hex octets carried by method_history_head after sha256:>
