An `ak.call.state` event requested a `recording_transition` or `transcript_transition` not listed in the per-capture controlled state machine (e.g. transitioning out of terminal `ready` / `failed`, `stopped → failed`, or attempting to enter a capturing state without a new `ak.call.recording.start`). The reducer MUST `failed_precondition`. The same code covers both orthogonal capture dimensions. See zh/crypto-media/call-state.md §4.2.
Conflict-recovery witness's state_root does not contain (or contains a divergent value for) the recovery_capability cell referenced by the grant. See zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md §9.5.
Recovery evidence does not bind the current transaction, recovery session, principal, replacement device or prepared-plan digest.
A recovery policy publish is the first accepted policy for the principal but does not use `version=1`. Genesis recovery policies MUST start at version 1.

A key-backup envelope or recovery proof references a `recovery_policy.policy_id` / `policy_version` that is not the currently accepted policy for the principal. Recovery strands MUST surface this to the user as 'update recovery policy' rather than silently continuing. Dual-registered as a reason_code and a top-level service code (see codes[]). See zh/identity/key-management.md §7.5.4 / §7.7 and zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §15.
A non-genesis recovery policy rotation omits `supersedes` or names a predecessor other than the currently accepted policy_id for the principal. Servers MUST reject with 409 Conflict.
A recovery policy publish or rotation uses a `version` that is not strictly greater than the currently accepted policy version for the principal. Servers MUST reject with 409 Conflict.

A recovery policy or recovery session request targets a principal_id different from the authenticated principal or authorized recovery coordinator scope. Servers MUST reject without revealing the target principal's recovery state.

A recovery policy, receipt, or proof names a proof kind outside the ak.schema.recovery_policy.v1 allowed_proof_kinds enum. Producers MUST use one of principal_signing, recovery_unlock, device_quorum, trusted_recovery_service, or threshold_recovery.

A recovery proof echoes a challenge value that does not exactly match the server-issued challenge for the referenced recovery_session_id. Servers MUST reject the proof before completing device recovery. See zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §15 and artifacts/schemas/recovery-session.schema.json.

A recovery-session submit_proof or a new RecoveryTransaction binding targeted a recovery session that is already in a terminal state (`completed` / `rejected` / `expired`). Terminal recovery sessions are immutable; servers MUST reject with top-level `failed_precondition` carrying this reason_code. Recovery sessions have no public complete operation. See zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §15 and artifacts/schemas/recovery-session.schema.json.
Closed generic Agent readiness blocker: the controller-owned PCR recovery material no longer satisfies the current recovery policy or active runtime-key state.

An ak.state.conflict_recovery reset named a target_cell that is not in ⊥. The reset replaces a cell rather than joining into it, so allowing it on a live cell would make recovery a general overwrite channel that bypasses every lattice and every precondition. This is the converse of cell_in_bottom_state, which rejects an ordinary write against a cell that is in ⊥. See zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md §9.5.
Conflict-recovery Move's inclusion proof cannot reconstruct the witness's `state_root`. See zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md §9.5.
Conflict-recovery Move is missing the required `refs[role=state_witness]` reference. See zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md §9.5.

Conflict-recovery witness frontier has a causal path from one of the sibling Moves that triggered the bottom — i.e., the witness is not strictly pre-conflict. See zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md §9.5.

Conflict-recovery witness is older than the permitted freshness window, or local frontier has observed a revoke / supersede for the referenced recovery_capability after the witness frontier. Receivers MUST reject stale witness replay. See zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md §9.5.

The reducer projection required by the registered contract cannot be derived uniquely from `kind`, signed envelope fields, schema-validated payload, and frozen pre-state. Receiver MUST reject the entire Event; projected writes are reducer output and never producer-selected Event fields. See zh/models/event-and-patch.md §4.3.1.
Event Envelope refs[] exceeds the v1 maximum of 128 semantic refs. Receiver MUST reject with schema_violation. See zh/conformance/scalability-constraints.md.

`ak.relation.tombstone` / `ak.relation.update` / equivalent Relation write rejected because the target Relation is already in the terminal state `tombstone`. In particular, `ak.relation.update` targeting a tombstoned Relation MUST be rejected with this reason_code.

The number of concurrent candidates (winner + losers) under a single Relation dedupe key exceeded the conflict fanout limit (v1 public profile: 16, aligned with the sibling fork limit in zh/models/event-and-patch.md §2.6). The reducer rejects the whole candidate group rather than retaining unbounded loser records; reconvergence requires a repair Event/Control Move on the latest CBA query basis. See zh/models/relation.md §6.

Sub-reason for schema_violation when a direct ak.relation.create / update / delete targets a derived-projection contains shape (Space(board) -> Space(list) or Space(list) -> Strand). Truth sources are the ak.component.space.parent.v1 and ak.component.strand.position.v1 cells written via ak.space.parent / ak.strand.move / ak.strand.reorder Moves; only the non-derived object-composition contains form is directly writable. See zh/models/relation.md §3.2 and zh/models/realm-and-space.md §3.5-§3.6.

Sub-reason for schema_violation when a direct ak.relation.create / update / delete targets relation_kind=watches. The watches Relation is a derived projection only: its truth source is the ak.component.strand.watch.v1 cell written via the ak.strand.watch.set durable event, never a direct Relation write. See zh/models/relation.md §3.2 and zh/models/strand-and-message.md §8.

RelationProfile registration/update was rejected because its `cardinality` and `max_to_per_from` / `max_from_per_to` express contradictory bounds (e.g. one_to_one with max_to_per_from > 1, or many_to_one with max_to_per_from > 1), or a `max_*` value is <= 0. `max_*` may only tighten within the direction implied by `cardinality`. See zh/models/relation.md §5.

A Relation write with `relation_scope` in {space, board} was rejected because the reducer could not resolve the participating endpoints' owning board/space (`board_space_id`) used as the dedupe/cardinality key — the endpoint belongs to no board/space, or the owning board/space is tombstoned. The reducer MUST NOT silently downgrade to realm-scope dedupe. See zh/models/relation.md §5.

A ak.realm.policy_bundle write under ak.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1 declared relaxed_window_max_ms greater than the spec hard ceiling (300000 ms / 5 min). Reducer MUST reject the policy update and receivers MUST NOT silently clamp; otherwise visible policy state splits across implementations. See artifacts/profiles/conformance-profiles.json#ak.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1.downgrade_window_constraint.

Sub-reason for failed_precondition when a Realm moderation-policy override would relax an action forbidden by inherited organization policy without embedding a valid organization approval. See zh/sync/service-http-binding.md §2.3.

Revocation / grant freshness cannot be established for a high-risk, cross-domain, or delegated action. Receiver MUST fail closed and return freshness diagnostics instead of treating missing revoke evidence as allow.
Concurrent grant/revoke ordering cannot be deterministically resolved with currently available history; recipient SHOULD backfill or escalate to manual review rather than picking a winner.

A capability revoke-undo (rollback) references a revoke whose signature does not verify. The undo MUST fail closed and the original revoke stays in effect. See authz/capabilities.md and fixtures/capability-fixture.json.

Recovery-session `rejection_reason_code` value: a server-side risk policy rejected the session. Closed value set defined in artifacts/schemas/recovery-session.schema.json and zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §15.

entry.schedule_basis_refs is not a subset of the envelope causal_refs[], or is empty, duplicated, or not sorted in ascending canonical byte order. This shape admission is decidable without resolving the referenced Events and MUST reject rather than pend. See zh/models/calendar-event.md.

payload.occurrence is neither JSON null nor a canonical instance key (YYYY-MM-DD for all-day, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS[Zone] for timed), including when its date component is not a real proleptic-Gregorian date. Receivers MUST reject instead of rewriting the key, since the cell subject derives from the signed value. See zh/models/calendar-event.md.
Closed generic Agent readiness blocker: no active accepted runtime key exists. It is durable subject-level readiness state and MUST NOT be inferred from a missing session or target-Realm grant.

The observed Calendar schedule revision frontier exceeds the 128-entry bound shared with causal_refs, so entry.schedule_basis_refs cannot express it. The producer MUST converge the schedule before responding and MUST NOT truncate the basis. See zh/conformance/scalability-constraints.md. It is raised by the authoring client when the observed frontier itself exceeds the bound; a wire Event that actually carries more than 128 refs is instead rejected by schema maxItems as schema_violation.

A grant or delegation set `scope_expansion_allowed=true`. v1 does not permit a child to expand beyond the parent's resources/actions; the reducer MUST reject (schema_violation) because the field directly conflicts with the §10.1 `resources MUST ⊆ parent` invariant. See zh/authz/constraint-schema.md §7 / zh/authz/capabilities.md §10.1.

Sub-reason for failed_precondition when a structural relation, parent, position, cascade, or reverse-projected fact would need to span two sibling Circle scopes in the same Realm. v1 reducers MUST NOT choose either Circle, union them, or promote the fact to Realm-default. See zh/models/circle.md §6.1.

Sub-reason for failed_precondition when scope_circle_id rebind is attempted without an explicitly profile-permitted audited-high-risk path. Default reducer rejects rebinds to prevent silent historical-discussion migration. See zh/models/circle.md §6.1.

The signed Event `scope_ref` does not equal the security scope deterministically resolved from the target or referenced accepted object state. Receiver MUST reject the Event and MUST NOT rewrite or reducer-stamp the signed scope. See zh/models/circle.md §6.1.

Sub-reason for failed_precondition when an object write references an effective scope whose Circle or parent Realm has been tombstoned/destroyed and cannot accept new writes. Projections may surface the same string as a non-error status marker. See zh/models/realm-and-space.md §2.6.1 and zh/models/circle.md §9.2.
Streaming-chunked AEAD attachment: a per-segment AEAD tag fails to verify. Receivers MUST reject the segment and abort the stream. See zh/crypto-media/media-and-blob.md §3.3.6.

Streaming-chunked AEAD attachment: a segment index is out of range, a segment length violates `segment_bytes`, or `segment_count` disagrees with the observed stream. Receivers MUST reject. See zh/crypto-media/media-and-blob.md §3.3.
Streaming-chunked AEAD attachment: a segment index appears more than once in the stream. Receivers MUST reject. See zh/crypto-media/media-and-blob.md §3.3.6.
Streaming-chunked AEAD attachment (`ak.blob.stream_aead.v1`): segment indices arrive out of order, skip a value, or leave a gap. Receivers MUST reject. See zh/crypto-media/media-and-blob.md §3.3.6.

Streaming-chunked AEAD attachment: the stream ended without a valid final segment (last_segment_flag never observed, or fewer segments than `segment_count`). Receivers MUST reject to resist truncation. See zh/crypto-media/media-and-blob.md §3.3.6.
The resource selector attempted to use actor:*. v1 actor selectors MUST name a concrete DID; universal subject grants are not accepted.

Governance-plane resource selector wildcard (e.g. policy:*, schema:*, or a governance object:* selector) was used without the required mitigation (denied by deployment policy, or constrained with max_authority_depth=0 plus bounded expiry plus admin approval). Receiver MUST reject.

Resource selector or constraint exceeds parser hard limits defined in resource-selector-grammar.md §3.3 (string length, resources[] length, token count, nesting depth, single-field length, required_claims item count, constraint nesting). Distinct from invalid_param so audit / abuse-detection can separate suspected parser-DoS attempts from ordinary format errors. Dual-registered as a reason_code and a top-level service code (see codes[]).

Invite delivery to the private target failed after the delivery service exhausted the retry budget. Used as a stable invite transition reason for ak.invite state projections; see zh/models/governance-objects.md and zh/sync/third-party-invites.md §6.1.

ak.schema.key_backup.v1 envelope chain failed verification: a `supersedes_digest` does not match the canonical_json digest of its predecessor, or a non-genesis envelope is missing a predecessor accessible to the caller. See zh/identity/key-management.md §7.6 and zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §12 / §12.1.

`ak.schema.key_backup.v1.supersedes` references a backup_id that is unknown to the server, deleted, or owned by a different actor / series. Wire endpoint returns 409 Conflict; receivers MUST treat the chain as broken. See zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §12.1.

A PUT /_arkret/self/keys/backups/{backup_id} request whose `series_seq` is not strictly greater than the current maximum sequence within the same (actor_id, series_id), or whose genesis envelope sets series_seq != 0. See zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §12.1.

Federation idempotency replay outcome: a cached federated request was re-evaluated and the origin service's signing key is now revoked, so the cache hit is treated as historical_only and MUST NOT bypass current key-state verification. See zh/conformance/conformance-vectors.md §9 (ak.vector.federation.idempotency_after_key_revoke.v1).
Service is not in the Realm's plaintext_visible_services policy; plaintext-bound operation refused.

A service did:webvh inception or rotation omitted the sole next-key commitment, supplied more than one update/next key, or failed to open the previous nextKeyHashes commitment. Providers and resolvers MUST fail closed as service_registration_rejected.

A subsequent `ak.call.state` event attempted to write a `session_focus` value different from the already-committed one. The reducer MUST `failed_precondition` — `session_focus` is write-once per call lifecycle; in-session focus migration is not supported in v1. See zh/crypto-media/call-state.md §4.1.

The committed `ak.call.state.session_focus` is authoritative and write-once: once it exists, a connect / token-exchange failure against that focus MUST be surfaced as focus-unavailable (`focus_unavailable_for_client`) and clients MUST NOT silently fall back to a different focus to keep the media path up. Naming the invariant explicitly closes the split-brain attack where two subsets of a conference converge on different SFUs. See zh/crypto-media/media-service-binding.md §5 and §2 (`foci[].health_endpoint`).
Closed target-specific Direct Conversation readiness blocker: the otherwise authorized Agent has no current session for the requested send path. It MUST NOT appear in generic Agent readiness.

A threshold-recovery share submitted during reconstruction does not match the `share_commitment{algorithm, commitment_b64u}` declared in the active recovery policy. Coordinator MUST notify the user which holder submitted an invalid share. See zh/identity/key-management.md §7.5.4 / §8.

Agent Sidecar ensure was denied without revealing whether the controller's native Sidecar or requested source-context mapping already exists. Returned as a generic failed_precondition sub-reason to avoid existence side channels. See zh/models/sidecar.md §3 and §7.

Sub-reason for failed_precondition when any legacy plaintext broadcast envelope is submitted or received. Signal is encrypted-only in every scope; implementations MUST fail closed and MUST NOT advertise Signal for a scope unless they can verify its MLS basis, AAD, and proof. See zh/crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md section 2.9.1.

Snapshot signer's authority (Realm owner / admin / trusted snapshot issuer / witness quorum membership) was revoked at or before the manifest's `created_at`, or revoke freshness cannot be sealed within the verifier's revocation_freshness_window_ms. Client MUST quarantine or reject the snapshot. A revoke that takes effect strictly after `created_at` does not retroactively invalidate a previously valid snapshot.

An Event or reducer input is held in a reversible soft-failed state pending causal backfill, authorization material, policy evidence, or asynchronous verification. It may later upgrade to accepted or roll back to rejected, but accepted MUST NOT degrade to rejected without a new governance event. See zh/sync/operations-sync.md §4.4.
`ak.space.tombstone` rejected because the target Space is already `tombstoned`.
`ak.space.tombstone` cannot proceed because the target Space still has active `contains` Relations or non-tombstoned child Spaces. See zh/models/realm-and-space.md §3.4.
`ak.space.archive` rejected because the target Space is not in `active` state (per zh/models/realm-and-space.md §3.3).
`ak.space.restore` rejected because the target Space is not in `archived` state; `tombstoned` is a terminal state and MUST NOT be restored.

A `match_scope=subtree` / `children` selector required resolving the target Space's ancestor chain under the authorizing operation's CBA basis, but the `ak.space.parent` cell was in a multi-head / bottom (⊥) state. The subtree authorization branch MUST fail closed rather than pick an arbitrary head, otherwise the same grant could authorize divergently across receivers (split authz). See zh/authz/resource-selector-grammar.md §6.
`ak.space.parent` would create a cycle in the Space ancestor chain (self-loop or chain loop). Reducer MUST reject (zh/models/realm-and-space.md §3.5).

The effective Space parent chain cannot be read or verified at the operation basis. Parent-dependent placement, default-Realm resolution, and subtree authorization MUST fail closed rather than treating the Space as a root. See zh/models/space-hierarchy.md section 4.
Standard moderation reason: spam content.
Local state does not match the authoritative frontier; client SHOULD reconcile via backfill or snapshot before continuing.
Capture artifact persistence or deletion failed in the Arkret blob pipeline.
A `ak.redaction` event targeting a Strand is rejected because the target Strand is already in terminal state `redacted`. Strand terminal state is reached via ak.redaction.
`ak.strand.archive` / `ak.strand.update` rejected because the target Strand is not in `active` state (per zh/models/common-fields.md §5.1).
`ak.strand.restore` rejected because the target Strand is not in `archived` state.

A canonical JSON or deterministic CBOR structure exceeds the v1 maximum nesting depth of 64 (objects and arrays combined, top-level container = depth 1). Receiver MUST reject (top-level schema_violation) before recursive descent can exhaust the stack, and MUST NOT truncate or partially parse. See zh/conformance/scalability-constraints.md section 2.

Recovery-session `rejection_reason_code` value: the session was superseded by a newer recovery session for the same principal / device. Closed value set defined in artifacts/schemas/recovery-session.schema.json and zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §15.

Reducer audit reason stamped when one controller-signed ak.agent.key.authorize runtime-replacement Event atomically observe-removes every prior active authorization dot named by its exact supersedes[] set and adds the new authorization. No synthetic ak.agent.key.revoke Event is authored. Sessions issued from superseded keys MUST fail closed within the revocation freshness window. See zh/identity/key-management.md §3.6.1.

A 3PID invite claim arrived with the invite_token sourced from a URL query string or path segment instead of from a URL fragment or out-of-band code, in violation of zh/sync/third-party-invites.md §3.2. The verification service MUST reject and SHOULD invalidate the token to prevent referer / log replay.

A media backend join token presented at connect time is past its `expires_at` (e.g. a LiveKit JWT whose `exp` has elapsed, distinct from `proof_invalid` which covers a structurally bad / wrong-issuer signature). The client MUST re-run the media-service-binding §3 token exchange instead of reusing the stale token; clients MUST NOT extend or replay an expired backend token. See zh/crypto-media/bindings/livekit.md §8 and zh/crypto-media/bindings/arkret-native.md.

A media token's `service_signature.kid` or `participant_binding.issuer_kid` resolves to a service DID that does NOT appear in the current epoch `ak.realm.media_service.service_id` (or the foci[]-aligned token endpoint seal). Clients MUST reject — this closes the attack where any service can forge a focus join token. See zh/crypto-media/media-service-binding.md §3.

A backend attempted to deliver a transcription artifact outside the Arkret-side blob pipeline, or used a key not derived from the MLS-Exporter label `ak.rtc-transcript-key/v1` (e.g. reused the SFrame / recording label or an empty Context). Clients MUST fail closed. See zh/crypto-media/call-state.md §5.1 and zh/crypto-media/media-service-binding.md §8.1.

Call transcription was requested without `ak.call.transcribe` capability, or the Realm policy forbids transcription. Issuer / reducer MUST reject; parallels `recording_denied` for the transcribe dimension. See zh/crypto-media/call-state.md §5.1.
A bounded-lifetime artefact (member application, reservation cell, presign envelope, runtime gate proof, etc.) is past its declared `expires_at` / TTL window. See per-feature spec sections.
Event kind does not appear in any known registry entry; treat per non_critical_extension_rule (preserve canonical bytes, ignore in reducer) unless declared in critical_extensions.

Current parser rejected an Event carrying a top-level or payload field not declared by the closed schema for its kind (including removed / renamed fields in artifacts/registry/forbidden-wire-fields.json). Distinct from `schema_violation` in that it pinpoints an unrecognized field rather than a constraint violation on a known field. See zh/spec-map.md §1.2.1.

A `ak.realm.media_service.foci[].type` value is not in the v1 registered set (`livekit` / `mediasoup` / `janus` / `arkret_native` / `moq_relay`) or is registered but not supported by this client / issuer. Clients MUST fail closed instead of forwarding the token to an arbitrary SDK. See zh/crypto-media/media-service-binding.md §2.

Current parser rejected an Event whose `kind` is not an active registered v1 kind. Sync, federation, snapshot, SDK, and conformance paths MUST fail closed and MUST NOT perform payload-shape disambiguation or alias lookup. See zh/spec-map.md §1.2.1 and zh/overview/evolution-and-compatibility.md.

A projected RSVP head references a schedule basis that cannot be resolved, is invisible, or is not on the target Strand's schedule revision DAG. The head is retained for audit, excluded from the effective response, and MUST NOT be guessed into currency. See zh/models/calendar-event.md.

Receiver does not recognise `encryption.aead.aead_profile` (or sees a reserved-but-unpublished profile such as `ak.aead.hybrid_kem.*`). Receivers MUST fail closed; inferring parameters from `aead.name` alone is forbidden. See zh/identity/key-management.md §7.9.

An encrypted-attachment envelope carries a `scheme` value the receiver does not recognise. Receivers MUST fail closed rather than guess a decryption form. See zh/crypto-media/media-and-blob.md §3.2/§3.3.
Per-item algorithm-agility failure: a critical digest prefix is not an active digest-suite registry row. Receiver MUST fail closed. Dual-registered with the top-level service code.
Event kind is not active in the receiver's profile or registry; receiver MUST NOT silently drop, MUST report this code.
Implementation does not advertise the feature requested; caller SHOULD downgrade or pick another peer.

HPKE suite id on an application-layer sealed surface (key-backup recipient_method=recovery_public_key, ak.secret.send, member-application encryption_envelope, file-transfer key_envelope) is not an active row in artifacts/registry/hpke-suite-registry.json (unknown, inactive, or reserved-but-not-activated). Receivers MUST fail closed rather than infer suite parameters from the AEAD name. Dual-registered as a reason_code and a top-level service code (see codes[]). See zh/identity/key-management.md §7.5.2.
Proof / event signature `alg` is not in the conformance signature-algorithm allowlist. Dual-registered as a reason_code and a top-level service code (see codes[]). See zh/conformance/encoding.md.

A key-backup envelope signature verifies cryptographically but the signer is not an active accepted device in the current generation, or is revoked, unauthorized, or generation-mismatched. Receivers MUST reject it even if the series chain and ciphertext_digest are self-consistent. See zh/identity/key-management.md §7.4.1.

A request supplied a `verification_method` whose DID component does not bit-identically match the target principal id after stripping fragment/query. Surfaces in two places. (1) `ak.gate.account.command.pair_agent_key`: `verification_method` vs `agent_id`. (2) `ak.gate.account.command.issue_session_grant` agent branch (`proof.proof_kind="agent_key_proof"`): `proof.verification_method` vs request `principal_id`. Endpoints MUST fail closed before invoking the proof validator so that mismatch is reported as this code rather than as a generic signature failure. See zh/identity/key-management.md §3.6.1.

An ak.view.update or ak.view.reconcile targeted a View whose accepted lifecycle state is tombstoned, or attempted to restore that View to active. Tombstoned shared Views are terminal. See zh/models/views.md §3.1.

`ak.strand.watch.set` writing `level_public=true` for another actor is rejected — publishing one's own subscription level is an opt-in personal disclosure and MUST be written by the target actor themself. `ak.strand.watch.set.others` writes MUST omit `level_public` or set it to `false`. See zh/models/strand-and-message.md §8.4.

`ak.strand.watch.set` may only set the watch state of the submitting actor; cross-actor writes require `ak.strand.watch.set.others` (audit / accessibility scope). See zh/models/strand-and-message.md §8.4.

`ak.strand.watch.set` writing `level="muted"` for another actor is rejected — `muted` suppresses mention / moderation / workflow notifications and MUST be opt-in by the target actor themself. `ak.strand.watch.set.others` only authorizes writing `level ∈ {mentions_only, participating, all}` for other actors. See zh/models/strand-and-message.md §8.4.

A `ak.strand.watch.set` write that uses `ak.strand.watch.set.others` to set another actor's watch state was rejected because it lacked refs[role=audit_pair] to a same-batch `ak.audit.accessed` event, or the paired audit payload did not identify the same writer DID, target actor DID, cell id, paired event id/digest, and before/after heads. See zh/models/strand-and-message.md §8.4.

A did:webvh resolver cache entry exceeded the per-entry maximum evidence age, even if the global cache-only outage window has not expired. High-risk writes, service delegation, capability reconstruction, and snapshot witness acceptance MUST fail closed. See zh/identity/identity-did.md §5.

did:webvh resolution is in cache-only degraded mode and either the requested operation is outside the closed low-risk read-only set, or no sealed, controller-proof-verified cache evidence is available. Resolver MUST fail closed rather than treat unresolvable as valid.

A deployment profile requires witnesses from distinct controlling organizations, but the controlling organization of at least one witness cannot be verified, or two witnesses resolve to the same organization. Counting unverifiable or colliding organizations would let one operator running several witness keys satisfy a distinct-organization requirement alone; the verifier MUST fail closed on high-risk paths. See zh/identity/identity-did.md §3.4.2.

Witness evidence is older than the effective max age set by deployment / Realm policy, measured from when the proof was observed rather than from when any Arkret receipt was signed. Re-signing an old observation does not refresh it. See zh/identity/identity-did.md §3.4.2.

parameters.witness is present but is not the did:webvh 1.0 shape {threshold, witnesses:[{id}]}: threshold outside 1..witnesses.length, a duplicated witness id, a witness id that is not a did:key, a did:key whose multibase/multicodec payload does not decode to a well-formed public key compatible with the log's Data Integrity cryptosuite, or an unregistered extension key. Key decoding happens during parameter validation, not at signature time; accepting a witness id on string shape alone would let an unverifiable key occupy a threshold slot and hollow out the threshold. Also raised when parameters carries a look-alike key such as witnesses, witness_threshold or witnessThreshold, because that shape is evidence the log was produced against a non-standard dialect and the true policy is therefore unknown. A verifier MUST fail closed and MUST NOT fall back to treating the DID as unwitnessed: silently reading a malformed or aliased declaration as threshold 0 turns a DID that declares witnesses into one that requires none. See zh/identity/identity-did.md §3.4.1.

A witness proof in did-witness.json fails signature verification, is signed by a key outside the witness listed in parameters.witness, or does not bind the versionId it is offered for. The proof does not count toward threshold and the entry MUST be treated as under-witnessed. See zh/identity/identity-did.md §3.4.1.

parameters.witness declares a witness policy but the did-witness.json proofs file is unreachable, unparseable, or contains no entry for the versionId under evaluation. Unavailable evidence is not absent policy; the verifier MUST fail closed on high-risk paths rather than proceed as if no witnessing were required. See zh/identity/identity-did.md §3.4.1.

Valid distinct witness proofs for the versionId are fewer than the effective threshold, which is the strictest intersection of the method-native parameters.witness.threshold and the deployment / Realm policy minimum. A holder-declared policy can raise this bar but MUST NOT lower it. See zh/identity/identity-did.md §3.4.1 and §3.4.2.

`ak.mls.welcome.payload.claim_ref.capabilities_digest` does not match the claimed KeyPackage capabilities, or the Welcome requires capabilities outside the claimed subset. Receivers MUST reject before decrypting the Welcome. See zh/crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md §2.6.

Confirmed fork/witness evidence: two distinct canonical Event preimages independently recompute to the same complete suite-tagged event_id (full-hash collision evidence); a validated per-actor sibling set exceeds the registered single-bucket or per-position limit; a profile declares the observed sibling combination non-joinable; or witnesses required to sign the same complete (realm_id, from_frontier, to_frontier, actor_seq_ranges, root, count) attestation payload return inconsistent values. A carried event_id whose recomputed digest differs is only event_id_digest_mismatch and MUST be rejected before quarantine. Different valid event_id values at the same (realm_id, actor_id, actor_seq) are not by themselves disagreement: event-and-patch.md §2.6 permits a bounded legal sibling set, which peers MUST reconcile by validated set union. Raw frontier_root / heads / range-root differences across different replication, disclosure, or attestation scopes also are not disagreement. The verifier MUST quarantine only the affected evidence scope and fail closed; recovery requires raw replay, an aligned same-scope quorum, or operator-approved fork resolution. See zh/sync/operations-sync.md §12 and zh/sync/federation.md §4.5.1.

Internal route evaluator diagnosis for a notice whose exact record basis is not the receiver's durable floor. It MUST NOT be serialized by ak.peer.service_resolution.read.resolve; the outward response is the blinded not_found/capability-denied or universal failure surface.
Internal route evaluator diagnosis for a notice revision/digest fork or duplicate-key conflict. It MUST NOT be serialized by the blinded peer resolve surface.
Internal route evaluator diagnosis that a candidate belongs to an accepted cancelled notice. It MUST NOT be serialized by the blinded peer resolve surface.
Internal route evaluator diagnosis that the signed handover validity window has expired. It MUST NOT be serialized by the blinded peer resolve surface.
Internal route evaluator diagnosis that no exact formal successor record is available at the candidate or authorized mirror. It MUST NOT be serialized by the blinded peer resolve surface.

Internal anti-rollback diagnosis for distinct valid target-signed artifacts at the same sequence/revision; the service route is quarantined. It MUST NOT be serialized by the blinded peer resolve surface.
Internal peer-response diagnosis for a non-contiguous successor chain. It is a requester-local validation result and MUST NOT appear in the responder's wire error.
Internal peer-response diagnosis for the 32-record, 256-KiB or caller-selected budget limit. It MUST NOT be serialized by the blinded peer resolve surface, which uses the universal size failure.

wire_scope_definitions.durable_event: Valid Event Envelope kind for persisted canonical history and reducer input.
wire_scope_definitions.actor_private_event: Persisted actor-private/account-data event; not shared Realm history and not Realm reducer input.

admission_class_definitions.capability_gated: Gated by capability actions. The authorizing actions are exactly the ones whose target_event_kinds list this kind in capability-action-registry; there is no second per-event list. Reducer MUST verify the actor holds a matching action grant. Fail-closed.
admission_class_definitions.conditional: Admission is selected from the event row's closed admission_variants. Receivers evaluate every non-otherwise predicate using admission_predicate_contract: exactly one match selects that variant, more than one match is fail-closed, and zero matches selects the single final otherwise variant. The otherwise branch is a fallback and is not counted as a simultaneously matching predicate. Each selected variant applies its own admission class and capabilities.
admission_class_definitions.crypto_verifiable: Admitted by cryptographic verification of the payload against group/key state (MLS epoch, key material, franking) and its policy preconditions. Reducer MUST verify the cryptographic binding; not a user capability. Fail-closed.
admission_class_definitions.delegated_pcr_genesis: Admitted only for a PCR ak.realm.create with no did_inception ref and with both executed_by and authorization_ref. A purpose=managed_agent_control Native Agent branch MUST carry exactly one critical refs[] role=agent_provision pointing to the accepted controller-authored ak.agent.provision Event; the verifier cross-binds actor_id, realm_id, controller, PCR delegation and provision payload before the reducer materializes the Agent active status cell. An explicitly organization-governed purpose=principal_control branch MUST carry zero agent_provision refs and MUST prove its separate accepted organization authority. The two branches are disjoint; a self-principal or generic realm.create capability substitution is rejected. This class never authorizes a following device-authorize slot by itself.
admission_class_definitions.deny: Explicit fail-closed admission branch. Selection always rejects the Event as failed_precondition/schema_violation and MUST NOT consult capabilities or alternate proof paths.
admission_class_definitions.registration_anchor: Admitted only for self-principal PCR genesis using durable registration-time DID control evidence and one critical did_inception ref. The verifier validates the accepted-at adapter/method evidence and project(full_id)=actor_id; current DID state after registration is irrelevant.
admission_class_definitions.pcr_recovery: Admitted only for ak.device.reanchor under the authority instance's accepted PCR recovery policy/session and monotonic generation CAS. did_root is merely one optional policy-enabled factor. A current DID proof without the matching authority instance and policy cannot enter this class.
admission_class_definitions.direct_conversation_agent_genesis: Admitted only for an ak.realm.create that carries exactly one critical refs[] role=direct_conversation_agent_provision pointing to an accepted ak.agent.provision Event. Used solely for the controller-to-own-Agent Direct Conversation branch, which has no Contact basis. The verifier cross-binds participants to exactly that controller and Agent, requires the Direct Conversation profile rather than a PCR profile, checks the controller binding is current, and fixes founder = controller so the Agent runtime key never needs Direct Conversation founding scope. This role is structurally exclusive with direct_conversation_basis and with the managed-Agent PCR agent_provision role.
admission_class_definitions.direct_conversation_genesis: Admitted only for an ak.realm.create that carries exactly one critical refs[] role=direct_conversation_basis pointing to the portable Contact basis evidence bundle and its continuity chain to the pair's root founder basis. The verifier derives founder from the root basis core (normal branch: the sorted_pair_members entry that is not the request_event_ref issuer, i.e. the responder; glare branch: the requests[0] issuer), then requires created_by == actor_id == founder, recomputes pair_key from sorted_pair_members and the trust domain, and pins the Direct Conversation profile, exact-two participants and the create-locked encryption and history baseline. Accepted-at basis validity and current directional Contact gates are evaluated separately so Event validity never depends on delivery order.
admission_class_definitions.self_authored_proof: Admitted by a proof bound to the subject principal's identity: either the subject's DID-bound signature / proof of possession, or a currently valid delegated-control proof whose authorization_ref is bound by the subject DID Document. Reducer MUST verify actor == subject, executed_by/authorization_ref when delegated, a fresh replay-protected proof, and that the accepted-at delegation purpose/scope explicitly covers the target event kind, resource and operation; mere presence of a DID-bound delegation is never sufficient. No Realm capability grant is consulted. Fail-closed: missing, stale, unbound, purpose-inapplicable or scope-inapplicable proof MUST be rejected.
admission_class_definitions.service_attested: Written by a protocol service component (Auth/Gate server, Events node, applet host, agent runtime) under its service-ID attestation as part of operating the protocol. Reducer MUST verify the issuing service's authority and its binding to the subject/scope; not a user capability. Fail-closed.

admission_predicate_contract.selector_semantics: All selector fields in one non-otherwise when object are ANDed. payload_path is relative to Event.payload; const uses exact JSON value equality, while not_const matches inequality or an absent path. top_level_fields_present requires every listed Event Envelope field. ref_* selectors evaluate Event.refs after schema validation. Unknown selectors, missing companion selectors, multiple matching non-otherwise variants, or evaluation errors are fail-closed.

registry_rules: Every standard ak.* Event.kind admitted through Event Envelope MUST appear in this registry. Signal payload types and DeviceMessageEnvelope message kinds are intentionally outside this Event registry.

Events API, Sync durable history, Federation, and canonical reducers MUST accept only active entries with wire_scope=durable_event unless an implementation profile explicitly defines a private channel for actor_private_event.

Entries with wire_scope=actor_private_event MAY be persisted in encrypted account data or an actor-private stream, but MUST NOT be inserted into shared Realm data-plane history or control-plane Seal history.

lifecycle_modality applies to physical object lifecycle writes, identified mechanically by an fsm_contract whose axis is object_lifecycle, plus explicitly registered reversible Realm lifecycle facets. Every active event kind that writes such a family MUST declare lifecycle_modality. Use reversible for a reversible facet or either member of an archive/restore pair, and terminal for an irreversible transition. Workflow, membership, status, audit, key-material and OR-Set revocation axes are excluded. Reducers and SDKs MUST read this field and MUST NOT infer modality from event-kind spelling.

Every active reducer-input durable kind MUST declare plane, sealed, and a complete machine-readable cell_writes[] contract; no parallel single-target fields or aliases exist. Each entry declares cell_family, cell_subject, lattice, bottom, optional initial_value, and optional condition. A condition marks the target as conditional. Payload conditions use the closed grammar field_present|field_absent|field_equals|any_field_present; a signed semantic-ref condition uses only critical_ref_role_exact_count{role,count}. All are pure functions of the schema-validated signed Event. When the condition holds the target is required and the reducer MUST derive exactly one matching write from kind+payload; when it does not hold the reducer MUST NOT derive that write. See zh/models/event-and-patch.md section 2.4.2. cell_family is a stable ak.component.*.v<n> URI; cell_subject is null, an explicitly sourced payload.* or envelope.actor_id field path, a coalesce descriptor, or a composite descriptor. Bare field paths and other envelope.* fields are invalid. plane MUST be data or control; sealed is a boolean and MUST be true iff plane=control. plane/sealed are the machine-readable authority for DataEvent versus Control Move routing and plane_cross_write validation; payload prose is explanatory. bottom is reject, expose, or inert; inert MUST be used when the lattice cannot produce Bottom. initial_value declares the value the cas_register reports before any reducer write has been applied; declaring `initial_value="__unset__"` combined with `head_eq:"__unset__"` implements singleton-once-set cells.

Every lattice=fsm cell write MUST resolve by cell_family to exactly one fsm_contract. Event-kind parameters MUST NOT duplicate states or allowed_transitions. Template-backed contracts resolve their instance_parameters before transition validation; unresolved templates, parameters or conditional edges fail closed.

Every active wire_scope=actor_private_event kind MUST resolve to exactly one entry in actor_private_contracts.event_writes. Actor-private writes use only the registered actor_private_contracts.cell_families merge contract, never shared Realm plane/sealed routing, CBA fields, reducer_input, or shared cell_contracts.

Protocol-singleton cells MAY take their genesis value from a create payload, but every subsequent write MUST use a registered event_kind. ak.component.notary.v1 and ak.component.realm.reducer_profile.v1 are canonically defined in zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md; their genesis values come from ak.realm.create, and subsequent writes use ak.realm.notary and ak.realm.upgrade respectively.

Lattice MUST be one of the fully specified core types: or_set, mv_register, cas_register, fsm, counter, ordered_log. A new lattice type cannot become active until its join, bottom, op schema, profile gate, and conformance vectors are all registered.

State convergence is defined by CBA: DataEvent writes are projected and locally accepted against seal_ref, Control Move writes are projected and finalized by Seals, and per-cell Lattice join remains deterministic. Event Envelope routing fields MUST NOT be used as ordering authority.

Every active durable reducer-input event_kind MUST have a machine-readable admission source: either at least one capability action targets it (capability_action_registry.target_event_kinds), or it declares an admission class from admission_class_definitions. capability_gated events MUST be listed in at least one action's target_event_kinds - admission has a single direction of truth and no per-event capability list. Enforced by lint_artifacts.py; no active durable reducer-input event may lack an admission source (fail-closed).

A conditional admission MUST use only selectors defined by admission_predicate_contract. All non-otherwise predicates are evaluated independently; exactly one match selects its branch, zero matches selects the final otherwise branch, and multiple matches fail closed. otherwise is never evaluated as an ordinary predicate.

ak.state.conflict_recovery is the single registered exception to literal cell addressing. Its one cell_writes[] entry declares cell_ref (a cell_id sourced from the payload) instead of cell_family/cell_subject, and effect_projection kind=reset instead of a lattice op, and it omits lattice and bottom. That combination is closed: no other kind may declare cell_ref or reset, and this kind MUST declare both together. A recovery addresses one cell of an arbitrary family, so the target cannot be a literal ak.component.*.v<n> URI; and a reset is not a join, so it has no lattice. The safety envelope is not static reachability but zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 9.5: the reducer MUST apply a reset only to a cell already in Bottom, and only when the Event carries refs[] role=recovery_capability and role=state_witness satisfying every condition in that section. On a cell in any other state the write MUST be rejected.

Every active standard Event kind MUST declare exactly one payload_schema_ref. The reference MUST resolve to an existing schema location and MUST equal the single Event Envelope payload dispatch for that kind. Consumers MUST NOT infer payload schemas from Event.kind spelling, schema-name conventions, or fallback definitions.

payload_schema_contract.validation_rule: Every active standard ak.* event kind MUST be validated by the Event Envelope schema and one payload class selected by kind. Unknown standard kind, unmatched active kind, or payload class failure is schema_violation before reducer execution.
payload_schema_contract.non_critical_extension_rule: Unknown non-critical payload fields are preserved in canonical bytes and MAY be ignored by reducers. Unknown critical payload semantics MUST be declared in Event.requirements.critical_extensions and fail closed when unsupported.
payload_schema_contract.explicit_binding_rule: Each active standard event kind declares exactly one payload_schema_ref, and the Event Envelope dispatch selects that exact location. Missing, dangling, duplicate, or divergent bindings fail closed. Consumers MUST NOT infer a payload schema from kind spelling or naming conventions.

Notary equivocation evidence (Control Move). Payload carries signer_id plus the two conflicting Seal wire objects: same (realm_id, notary_seq) slot with different canonical bytes, or a notary_seq=k+1 Seal that does not descend from the same signer's notary_seq=k Seal (authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.1). Admission is verification-only: any Realm member MAY submit and the two conflicting notary signatures are the complete authorization; no capability grant is consulted and reducer MUST NOT require one. Reducer MUST re-verify both signatures and the slot rule, then add a per-signer fault record to the notary_fault cell. Once a fault record is accepted: receivers MUST reject later Seals signed by the fault signer, the two conflicting Seals and their descendants enter fork_quarantine, and Realm-wide pause applies only when no eligible signer remains.

Notary censorship evidence (Control Move). Payload carries signer_id, the signed control-plane receipt, the seal_ref of the Seal that was obliged to include / signed-reject / defer the pending Control Move, a control_event_set_root non-membership proof for the censored event digest, and the missing rejection-or-defer proof (authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.2). Admission is verification-only: the receipt holder MAY submit; the receipt signature plus the non-membership proof are the complete authorization. This evidence does NOT automatically disqualify the notary: reducer adds an audit fault record that MUST raise governance alarms, feeds inclusion-list / recovery obligations, and is evaluated by governance or the genesis recovery path.
Realm membership state

Realm-scoped MemberIdentity segment replacement event. Append-only log entry that may supersede prior ak.member.identity.update events via payload.replaces[] without overloading ak.profile.update patch semantics.

Strand business-progression stage transition. Single source of truth for mutating Strand.stage / Strand.stage_changed_at; ak.strand.update patch on those paths MUST be rejected (forbidden-wire). Default invariant: payload.watcher_actor_id MUST equal envelope actor_id, unless writer holds ak.strand.watch.set.others. The watches Relation (actor --watches--> strand) is a derived projection of this cell, not a separate truth source — direct ak.relation.create relation_kind=watches MUST schema_violation. Agent signing key authorization. Payload MUST validate as event-payload.schema.json#/$defs/agent_key_authorize_payload and bind agent_id, key_id, verification_method, accountable_principal_id, agent_key_scope, audience, issued_at, and approval_evidence; expires_at is optional (absent means non-expiring, revocation-governed). The agent-key cell is an observed-remove OR-Set. First authorization adds one authorization dot. Same-key re-authorization MUST atomically remove every active authorization dot visible at the Move seal_basis and add the replacement dot; it MUST NOT select a winner by arrival time. Concurrent replacement dots that survive the join are evaluated by the deterministic strictest fold: intersect agent_key_scope and audience, take the earliest finite expires_at (absence is +infinity), and fail closed if accountable_principal_id or verification_method disagree. Key replacement has no dedicated rotate kind: runtime replacement re-pairing authorizes the new key and revokes every prior active key (reason=superseded_by_repairing) in the same accepted transaction.

Agent signing key revocation. Payload MUST validate as event-payload.schema.json#/$defs/agent_key_revoke_payload and bind agent_id, key_id, revoked_at, and revoked_by; the revocation's control-plane basis is the Control Move envelope seal_basis, and its cutoff is the accepted Seal covering the Move.

Controller-authored native personal Agent provisioning fact. One Event proof binds the controller-supplied accepted Agent DID entry-0 commitment, the forward-declared managed Agent PCR realm id, controller delegation, immutable requested-scope digest, accountability scope and selector. Admission atomically projects the provision, accountability, selector and realm-id-claim cells; no nested payload proof or partial two-Event state is valid. The declared managed Agent PCR genesis arrives in a later separate submission whose admission reverse-looks-up this declaration; its acceptance still awaits the controller-signed create-locked DID entry 1.

Controller-owned signed selector statement binding (controller_subject, agent_slug) to one native personal agent DID. The Event belongs in the controller Principal Control Realm, never the Agent PCR or a Collaboration Realm. Concurrent distinct current values remain visible and make selector resolution ambiguous/fail-closed.

Agent lifecycle transition to paused state. Authorization basis is the Control Move envelope seal_basis; payload carries no independent frontier. Auth Server MUST reject new agent session grants for this principal; existing tokens fail closed within an independent pause revocation freshness window of at most 60 seconds, never merely the session maximum TTL. Reversible via ak.self.agent.resume.

Agent lifecycle transition from paused to active. Authorization basis is the Control Move envelope seal_basis; payload carries no independent frontier. At acceptance the reducer MUST use the accepted current control frontier to re-validate controller, agent, key, capability, Realm policy, and accountability_grant freshness; any failure rejects the resume.

Agent lifecycle terminal state. One accepted controller-authorized Event is the unavoidable parent AND gate for every runtime key, session, pairing handle, capability grant, KeyPackage, presence and future submission. Cleanup is asynchronous and MUST NOT synthesize or require child revocation Events. Terminal — no transition out.

Agent-initiated action request. Carries proposed_action, target descriptor, and content digest. Awaits controller approval before generating shared event.

Controller approval of a draft / action request. Binds draft_id, content digest, target descriptor, proposed_action, approved payload digest, approval expiry, and single-use nonce. Publish executor MUST atomic-consume the nonce; reuse fails closed (reason=approval_already_consumed).
Controller rejection of a draft / action request. Draft transitions to rejected; agent runtime MUST NOT continue publish attempts.

Holder-signed normal Contact acceptance: closed peer XOR, exact request/receipt digest, stable basis, lineage version 1 and full granted_to_peer_scopes. It never reads or writes Consent.

Participant endorsement of the settled Direct Conversation coordinates and of the first exact-pair MLS generation. It does not enforce uniqueness: at most one Realm can exist per pair because only the founder derived from the pair's root Contact basis may author the founding unit. Selects which already-established MLS group currently holds send authority in a Direct Conversation Realm. It never creates a group: the producer first establishes candidate state with ordinary ak.mls.genesis and Add Commit and durably stores its own private state, and the activation then references those accepted public facts. Generation 0 is the founder's sender-only provisional exporter group. Generation 1 MUST be authored by the joiner, because no portable proof exists that the peer Principal Server durably accepted the Welcome and only the joiner can truthfully assert it. Generation 2 and above are post-binding repair and require generation = current + 1 with predecessor_active_value_digest matching the current value.

The facade MUST NOT author actor_id as the reporter principal. One accepted Event derives exactly one report and one moderation_queue_item; their full typed IDs differ although both retype the same complete event_id token.

Closes the appeal from submitted / under_review / decided via reviewer close, appellant withdrawal, or a deployment's authorized close service. close is a manual/authorized action; the protocol does not mandate any auto-close timer or cool-off duration (deployment/Realm policy decides). concurrency_class_definitions.merge_safe: Operation commutes under its declared lattice and may execute concurrently with other merge_safe operations after ordinary causal validation.
concurrency_class_definitions.exclusive: Operation requires exclusive compare-and-apply for its target cell set but does not globally serialize unrelated security authority.
concurrency_class_definitions.security_barrier: Authority, membership, key, scope, policy, recovery, or identity transition that serializes against every concurrent security_barrier touching the same signed scope.

merge_definitions.server_revision_cas: Whole-value compare-and-set on expected_revision; accepted revision increments by one and the revision high-water mark survives tombstone GC.
merge_definitions.fsm_cas: Closed FSM transition checked against the family table and current revision; concurrent siblings fail closed.
merge_definitions.cas_register: Single actor-private register; concurrent distinct values fail closed rather than using arrival order.
merge_definitions.causal_then_hlc_then_device: Causal dominance wins; only causally incomparable positions compare HLC, and only equal HLC values compare device_id lexicographically.

registry/exporter-label-registry.json.description: Canonical registry of all normative MLS-Exporter and MLS ExpandWithLabel domain-separation labels in Arkret v1. Each label is a wire-breaking security parameter: implementations MUST use the exact label string, primitive, and Context field shape, and MUST NOT migrate or reuse keys across distinct labels without a new profile. MLS-Exporter entries MUST NOT derive with an empty Context; an ExpandWithLabel entry follows its registered context_encoding, including an explicitly registered empty context. Domain separation is defined by exact label inequality; forbid_reuse_with is a non-exhaustive human/tooling hint and MUST NOT be interpreted as an allow-list or require symmetric closure. Per-entry defined_in points to the normative source. See zh/crypto-media/media-service-binding.md §8 and conformance/conformance-vectors.md §12.7.

labels.label: ak.content-v1
labels.purpose: Per-epoch content AEAD key derived from history_secret for mls_exporter_aead_v1
labels.context_encoding: empty byte string, exactly as specified by the registered ExpandWithLabel derivation
labels.output_bytes: AEAD.Nk for the active MLS ciphersuite

labels.label: ak.history-v1
labels.purpose: Per-epoch history_secret root for mls_exporter_aead_v1 content encryption; may be retained and re-sealed to authorized later joiners via ak.realm_key.share
labels.context_encoding: realm_id UTF-8 bytes exactly as serialized in the enclosing Realm id string
labels.output_bytes: KDF.Nh for the active MLS ciphersuite

labels.label: ak.rtc-frame-key/v1
labels.purpose: SFrame per-sender media frame key (E2EE media frames)
labels.context_encoding: canonical JSON (RFC 8785 JCS) bytes of the context_fields object {realm_id, call_id, focus_id, epoch_id, participant_identity, device_id}; empty or epoch-only Context MUST fail closed

labels.label: ak.rtc-recording-key/v1
labels.context_encoding: canonical JSON (RFC 8785 JCS) bytes of the context_fields object {realm_id, call_id, focus_id, recording_id, media_service_id, recording_start_event_id}; empty Context MUST fail closed

labels.label: ak.rtc-transcript-key/v1
labels.purpose: Encryption key for a call transcription artifact (transcribe pipeline, distinct from media frame and recording keys)
labels.context_encoding: canonical JSON (RFC 8785 JCS) bytes of the context_fields object {realm_id, call_id, focus_id, recording_id, media_service_id, transcript_start_event_id}; empty Context MUST fail closed

labels.label: ak.signal-v1
labels.purpose: Per-epoch, per-sender-device Signal AEAD key for the ak.signal_exporter_aead.v1 construction. Sender key separation prevents a 32-bit AES-GCM sender_nonce_prefix collision from becoming same-key nonce reuse.
labels.context_encoding: canonical JSON (RFC 8785 JCS) bytes of {sender_device_id}; empty Context is forbidden
labels.output_bytes: AEAD.Nk for the active MLS ciphersuite

labels.label: arkret-aead-sender-nonce-prefix-v1
labels.purpose: Per-sender AEAD nonce prefix for every AEAD-bearing v1 envelope (nonce = sender_nonce_prefix || device_nonce_counter_be64); canonical derivation defined once in encoding.md, domain documents only declare their `purpose` value
labels.context_encoding: canonical-bytes of the JSON object {"key_ref", "epoch", "device_id", "purpose", "aead_profile"} (not a bare string)

labels.label: arkret-mention-routing-v1
labels.purpose: Keyed-HMAC key for the opt-in mention routing sidecar tag in E2EE Realms (mention_routing_hmac_v1 = HMAC-SHA256(key, utf8(mentioned_did)); the exporter output is the HMAC key; Sync Service MUST NOT derive, receive or persist the exporter secret)
labels.context_encoding: realm_id UTF-8 bytes exactly as serialized in the enclosing Realm id string

labels.label: arkret-reaction-routing-v1
labels.purpose: Keyed-HMAC key for the plaintext reaction routing tag in E2EE Realms (reaction_routing_hmac_v1 = HMAC-SHA256(key, utf8(canonical_emoji)); the exporter output is the HMAC key)
labels.context_encoding: realm_id UTF-8 bytes exactly as serialized in the enclosing Realm id string

Each entry pins the context (top-level envelope, specific payload class, etc.) because a name may be legal elsewhere. cotest scanner walks Event Envelope / payload bytes and flags any occurrence outside the entry's allowed_contexts.

rejection_levels.hard_reject: Reducer / parser MUST fail with schema_violation when the field appears in the listed context.
rejection_levels.migration_only: Readers MAY tolerate the field during a bounded migration window but writers MUST NOT emit it.
rejection_levels.compat_only: Allowed only on explicit interop / compatibility surfaces.
rejection_levels.docs_only: Removed from machine surfaces; survives in CHANGELOG / migration notes.

allowed_context_definitions.changelog: Reference in CHANGELOG or migration documentation.
allowed_context_definitions.legacy_migration: Reference in time-bounded migration code that rewrites stored legacy bytes.
allowed_context_definitions.interop_module: Reference in an explicit interop binding (e.g., MIMI interop) where the cross-protocol mapping requires the field.
allowed_context_definitions.negative_test: Reference in negative fixtures / cotest drift tests that assert rejection.

When the plaintext counterpart is `content`, the encrypted counterpart is `encrypted_content` (Strand, Message, Morph). Generic `encrypted_payload` remains valid for non-content carriers such as identity and reaction payloads.

Extensible user metadata fields live under metadata.fields, or inside encrypted_metadata when the effective metadata profile requires encryption.
Realm is the v1 boundary. 'room_kind' MUST NOT appear on the wire outside an explicit MIMI / Matrix interop module.

Strand payload field 'kind' (or any analogous discriminator) MUST NOT carry the literal value 'room'. Use 'realm' / 'strand' / canonical Realm.kind values. Interop translation lives in an opt-in interop module only.

Strand payload MUST NOT carry 'discussion_space_ref'. Discussion privacy is represented by Circle-scoped Strand objects and confidential_discussion_of Relation facts; the field-level Circle identifier is 'scope_circle_id' (see schemas/strand.schema.json, zh/models/circle.md).

entries.replacement: parent_space_id / default_realm_id / default_scope_circle_id / retention_policy_id / disclosure_policy_id / rate_limit_policy_id / policy_id
entries.notes: Single concrete protocol object identifiers use `_id`; `_ref` is reserved for causal, proof, schema/profile, content-addressed, or polymorphic reference material. Event.scope_ref is a valid polymorphic signed reference. The old fields parent_ref, default_realm_ref, default_scope_ref, retention_policy_ref, disclosure_policy_ref, rate_limit_policy_ref, and Policy-object policy_ref MUST NOT appear on current v1 wire.

entries.notes: Capability grant constraints that contain one concrete identifier kind use `_ids`, not `_refs`. The old fields allowed_view_refs, allowed_strand_refs, allowed_circle_refs, denied_strand_refs, allowed_space_refs, denied_space_refs, realm_refs, and approval_actor_refs MUST NOT appear on current v1 wire. Polymorphic container constraints allowed_from_container_refs / allowed_to_container_refs remain `_refs` because they may identify Space, Strand, or Morph containers.
The abbreviated media participant typed ID prefix was expanded to the full snake_case kind. Current v1 wire MUST use ak:rtc_participant:<uuid>; ak:rtcpart:<uuid> is rejected.
Key backup KDF params use digest_algorithm for PBKDF2/derived digest selection. The old params.hash selector is ambiguous with digest bytes and MUST NOT appear on current v1 wire.

member_delivery_binding references the policy revision Event that authorized a delivery binding, not a Policy object. The field therefore carries explicit event-reference semantics as policy_event_ref.
The child_scope_policy discriminator now names the concrete field it requires: scope_circle_id.

Range-completeness event_range, audit RYW receipt, and POST /events response MUST use 'realm_frontier'. The replication and security boundary covered by this frontier is the Realm, not an in-Realm Space container. 'space_frontier' MUST NOT appear on the current wire as a frontier object property.

Relation MUST carry rank at the top level, not nested under fields. The dual-source (top-level rank vs fields.rank) ambiguity is closed: writers MUST emit top-level rank only, and readers MUST reject fields.rank with schema_violation. See zh/models/relation.md §2.
Space MUST carry rank at the top level. Mirrors the relation_payload constraint; closes the dual-source ambiguity uniformly. See zh/models/realm-and-space.md §3.2.

entries.replacement: ak.realm.create genesis or dedicated Realm security facet
entries.notes: Space is a container, not a security boundary. A legacy space-create / space-update payload carrying Realm-level security_class is the pre-inversion Space-as-boundary shape and MUST be rejected; migrate it to Realm payload fields.

entries.replacement: ak.realm.join_rule or ak.realm.policy_bundle join policy facet
entries.notes: Join policy is Realm-scoped. Space payloads MUST NOT carry join_rule; this closes the current Space container model versus removed pre-inversion payload-shape ambiguity.
History visibility is Realm-scoped. Space payloads MUST NOT carry history_visibility.
Policy server attachment is Realm-scoped. Space payloads MUST NOT carry policy_server.
Delivery binding policy is Realm-scoped. Space payloads MUST NOT carry delivery_binding_policy.

ak.message.create payload MUST NOT carry revision_root. The reducer initializes revision_root to the new message_id; only ak.message.revise (and subsequent revise events) may set revision_root, and only to the create's revision_root. See zh/models/strand-and-message.md §9.

ak.message.create payload MUST NOT carry a second identity. The reducer materializes Message.id by retyping the creating Event's full 33-byte / 44-character content-bound token. See zh/models/strand-and-message.md §9.

The Agent Sidecar exchange binding (ak.schema.agent_sidecar_event_exchange_binding.v1), exchange control plaintext (ak.schema.agent_sidecar_exchange_control.v1), and exchange_id are legal only inside MLS-encrypted payload/metadata of events whose effective scope is the native Sidecar. They MUST NOT appear in plaintext metadata, account-data keys, shared Realm/Circle event payloads, publish output, push previews, notifications, telemetry, or any other shared/public surface. Shared-wire-visible occurrences are schema_violation; material decrypted from a non-Sidecar scope is invalid and never rendered or folded. See zh/models/sidecar.md §7.2.

Composite Content Block MUST use the field name `parts` (matching schemas/message.schema.json, schemas/event-payload.schema.json, schemas/strand.schema.json, and schemas/morph.schema.json). The temporary `blocks` spelling was rejected because it over-constrained the concept to document layout blocks; the canonical wire name is `parts`, and `blocks` MUST NOT appear in current content_block_composite wire. See zh/models/content-types.md §4.10.

Encrypted Envelope MUST NOT carry `cleartext_commitment`. The bare plaintext hash is dictionary-attackable offline against low-entropy plaintext; v1 E2EE producers MUST NOT emit it and receivers MUST reject any envelope that carries it (top-level `not.required` in schemas/encrypted-envelope.schema.json). Future profiles needing plaintext commitment MUST define a keyed/salted form rather than this bare hash.

File transfer account-data values MUST NOT carry a bare plaintext file hash. The only digest field for the stored Blob is ciphertext `content_digest`; plaintext digest aliases such as `cleartext_sha256`, `plaintext_sha256`, or `plaintext_digest` are rejected.

Strand MUST carry stage at the top level (required field). Strand stage_changed_at is reducer-derived and lives at the top level. It MUST NOT be smuggled under metadata.fields.* and MUST NOT be supplied by actor on wire (reducer overwrites with the triggering ak.strand.stage.set event's created_at). See zh/models/common-fields.md §5.3.3 rule 3.

entries.replacement: stage (top-level Strand field) or state (physical lifecycle)
