registry/hpke-suite-registry.json.description: Canonical HPKE (RFC 9180) suite vocabulary for v1 application-layer public-key sealing surfaces that are NOT carried inside MLS: key-backup `recovery_public_key` envelopes, to-device sealed material (`ak.secret.send`), member-application reviewer envelopes and file-transfer key envelopes. An HPKE suite names the (KEM, KDF, AEAD) triple; its canonical_id is the wire scheme / `hpke_suite` selector value. The KEM (DHKEM-X25519-HKDF-SHA256), the KDF (HKDF-SHA256) and the application-layer seal/open transcript are standard RFC 9180 base mode (SetupBaseS / SetupBaseR): the RFC 9180 key_schedule with LabeledExtract / LabeledExpand derives key, base_nonce and exporter_secret from the DHKEM shared secret and the caller `info`, and the AEAD nonce is the internally derived base_nonce XOR seq (single-shot seq=0), NOT carried on the wire. This is the fourth algorithm-agility registry, symmetric to signature-alg-registry.json, digest-suite-registry.json and mls-ciphersuite-registry.json. MLS group messages keep their own HPKE internals via mls-ciphersuite-registry.json and are out of scope here.
registry/hpke-suite-registry.json.suite_id_grammar: suite_id = 'ak.hpke_' kem_id '_aead_' aead_id '.v' major ; each id segment matches [a-z0-9]+ . The canonical_id is the full wire string; it is NOT freely composed from parts — only suites present as rows below exist, and only status=active rows are valid on wire.
registry_rules: Only suites present as rows in this registry exist. Implementations MUST NOT compose KEM/KDF/AEAD ids freely; only status=active rows are valid on wire.

A suite id not present as an active row MUST fail closed with unsupported_hpke_suite when it appears in an HPKE-sealed surface (key-backup recipient_method=recovery_public_key, ak.secret.send, member-application encryption_envelope, file-transfer key_envelope). Receivers MUST NOT infer suite parameters from the AEAD name alone.

Schema enum values for HPKE suite selector fields (e.g. ak.schema.key_backup.v1 encryption.hpke_suite, the ak.secret.send / member-application / file-transfer envelope `scheme` const) MUST be generated from active rows' canonical_id only when publishing a new schema version, then frozen for that schema version. Activating a reserved/new suite requires a new schema version and profile negotiation; registry activation MUST NOT expand an existing schema enum in place (zh/conformance/schema-registry.md §6.1 b.1).

When a surface carries both an explicit `hpke_suite` selector and an AEAD `name`/profile field, the AEAD MUST equal the selected suite's aead; a mismatch MUST be rejected (schema_violation). A surface MAY omit the selector only where a single default-MUST suite is pinned by its defining document, in which case the absent selector denotes that row.

status=reserved rows pin the wire id and profile gate but MUST NOT appear on wire until every activation_requirements entry is met and the row is flipped to active in a registry release. Receivers MUST fail closed (unsupported_hpke_suite) on a reserved suite id seen on wire before activation.

Every status=active row MUST declare kat_vector_id naming an active vector-registry entry; every status=reserved row MUST instead declare kat_absence_reason and MUST NOT declare kat_vector_id. tools/lint_artifacts.py enforces this binding.

The registry is intentionally minimal: new KEM families (post-quantum / hybrid), new KDFs and new AEADs enter additively as new rows with their own profile gates and conformance vectors; the ak.hpke_*_aead_*.v* wire form needs no rewrite. Nonce handling is RFC 9180 key-schedule-derived, uniformly across every HPKE-sealed surface (`recovery_public_key` envelopes, the to-device `ak.secret.send` seal, member-application and file-transfer key envelopes): the AEAD nonce is base_nonce XOR seq (single-shot seq=0) and MUST NOT be carried on the wire; each seal mints a fresh ephemeral key, so base_nonce is unique per envelope. See zh/identity/key-management.md §7.5 for the symmetric (non-HPKE) key-backup nonce-uniqueness rules.

kem_strength_order.note: Classical KEMs are treated as equal classical strength; the hybrid xwing row is strictly stronger (adds ML-KEM-768 post-quantum confidentiality). Consumed by any future no-downgrade rule on suite transition.

suites.security_note: All-RFC-9180 suite for key-backup recovery_public_key envelopes on platforms with AES hardware acceleration. Classical.

v1 default-MUST application-layer HPKE suite: all-RFC-9180 base mode DHKEM(X25519, HKDF-SHA256) + HKDF-SHA256 + 96-bit-nonce ChaCha20-Poly1305 (SetupBaseS / SetupBaseR, key_schedule-derived base_nonce, no wire nonce). Software-friendly (constant-time, no AES hardware needed), the default for the recovery_public_key / to-device / member-application / file-transfer envelopes. Classical (not post-quantum).
P-256 KEM for WebAuthn/FIDO2/PKI key-agreement interop, mirroring the ECDSA-P256 signature row. Profile-gated; receivers not advertising ak.profile.hpke.p256.v1 fail closed. Classical.

suites.kat_absence_reason: The X-Wing HPKE construction remains reserved until the profile and per-suite KAT activation requirements are complete.
activation_requirements: ak.profile.kem.hybrid_xwing.v1 fully specifies draft-connolly-cfrg-xwing-kem-10 and HPKE KEM id 0x647A; any incompatible draft change requires an explicit registry release and refreshed KAT digest before activation
Per-suite HPKE conformance vectors published (KEM encap/decap, key schedule, sealed bytes)

Coverage-priority alignment recorded: key-backup envelope before MLS KeyPackage (static ciphertext backups are the primary Harvest-Now-Decrypt-Later target; reuses the reserved ak.aead.hybrid_kem.* namespace)
suites.security_note: Reserved post-quantum hybrid KEM (X25519 + ML-KEM-768) per the encryption-and-audit.md §2 PQ roadmap. The KEM identifier is the IANA-assigned HPKE value 0x647A and the exact construction is pinned to draft-connolly-cfrg-xwing-kem-10. Hybrid confidentiality: secure if either X25519 or ML-KEM-768 holds. Not on wire until the profile and KAT activation requirements are complete.

storage_rules: Protocol wire objects, canonical JSON, signatures, hashes, fixtures, logs, API DTOs, and cross-service references MUST use the full typed form declared by each id_kind row.

Storage implementations MAY store producer-allocated raw 16-byte UUID values (e.g. PostgreSQL `uuid` column) without the ak:<kind>: prefix when the table, column, or explicit kind field already supplies the type context.
Implementations that store raw IDs MUST restore the full typed form before computing canonical JSON, event IDs, payload hashes, detached proofs, federation payloads, sync cursors, or audit logs.
The <kind> segment is part of the signed/canonical wire value. It MUST NOT be changed, inferred differently, or stripped during verification, forwarding, backfill, or replay.

The payload construction MUST be fixed by that kind's id_form and identity_authority columns, never chosen per call site: producer_allocated uses UUIDv7; event_derived uses the creating Event's 33-byte token; suite_tagged_full_digest uses a full uint8 digest-suite code followed by the complete 32-byte digest under its registered kind-specific preimage contract. v1 Event and suite-tagged identities accept only registered active suite codes with high nibble 0x0; this constraint does not give that nibble any meaning beyond the suite code. A UUID version nibble or digest-suite byte alone never proves identity authority.

A producer_allocated UUIDv7 is never a globally sufficient protocol identity. Its canonical identity key is (mint_authority, typed_id), where mint_authority is the DID whose accepted proof authorized the first durable appearance of that ID. Bare typed-ID lookup, cross-authority deduplication, and last-writer-wins collision repair are forbidden.

Storage implementations MAY store producer_allocated UUID values as raw 16-byte UUIDs. Event-derived and suite-tagged full-digest IDs MUST instead store their raw 33-byte token; they MUST NOT use a native UUID column.

The id_form is fixed by registry kind and never chosen per call site: producer_allocated uses RFC 9562 UUIDv7; event_derived uses the same canonical 33-byte token as its creating Event ID; suite_tagged_full_digest uses a full uint8 digest suite code followed by all 32 digest octets. Both token forms serialize as 44 unpadded Base64URL characters.

A database MAY intern any full Realm wire identity in a canonical Realm table and use a database-local surrogate pk for joins, indexes, and foreign keys. That pk is never serialized or signed. The canonical table MUST retain a unique lossless 33-byte Realm identity (or its full typed wire form), and every realm_pk foreign key MUST resolve to the same wire Realm identity carried by the protocol record.

producer_allocated_identity_contract.security_rationale: UUIDv7 randomness and timestamp layout do not authenticate the allocator. Binding every producer-selected ID to the accepted genesis signer prevents an attacker from claiming another producer's ID by copying or predicting the UUID.

issuer_record_identity_contract.v1_suite_code_constraint: The complete uint8 suite wire code is encoded unchanged, but v1 accepts only registered active codes whose high nibble is 0x0; this is not a Realm derivation-class nibble.

closed_encoding.audience: canonical_bare_resource_service_did; never an HTTP origin or endpoint URL
closed_encoding.credential_binding: v1 fixes credential_class=standard and requires holder_binding

issuer_record_identity_contract.signed_claim_binding: Every preimage field except fixed schema is a signed JWT claim, including the required standard holder_binding; kind is the fixed credential kind and jti is the derived typed ID. Verifiers MUST reconstruct the complete preimage from signed claims and recompute jti, so two different holder_binding values cannot share one valid ID.
issuer_record_identity_contract.session_chain_rule: session_id is independently allocated before first issuance, refresh inherits it, and it MUST NOT equal or derive from grant_id
issuer_record_identity_contract.device_id_rule: No independent top-level device_id claim enters the preimage; device scope tokens, the required holder_binding, or optional device_binding carry the binding.

lifecycle.refresh: one issuer transaction creates active successor and supersedes predecessor with successor_session_grant_id

realm_token_layout.event_derived_retype_compatibility: Realm and Event token headers are identical, so an ak.realm.create Event token is byte-identical to its Realm token and retyping only swaps the ak:event: / ak:realm: prefix. v1 Realm identity is fixed to SHA-256, so only a creating Event with header 0x01 is Realm-eligible.
realm_token_layout.high_nibble_carries_no_category: The high nibble is reserved zero and carries no category information. Realm purpose lives in the signed create payload; implementations MUST NOT infer purpose from realm_id.

registry/id-kind-registry.json.uuid_form_rules: The construction is declared per kind by id_form. producer_allocated = RFC 9562 UUIDv7. event_derived = the creating Event's 33-byte token (zero reserved high nibble plus uint4 suite wire_code followed by all 32 octets of its digest), canonically encoded as 44 unpadded Base64URL characters and retyped only by replacing the ak:<kind>: prefix. The token requires strict decode plus canonical re-encode validation; regex alone is insufficient.

registry/mls-ciphersuite-registry.json.description: Canonical MLS (RFC 9420) ciphersuite vocabulary for v1 KeyPackage cipher_suites[] negotiation and server describe surfaces. Completes the algorithm-agility registry symmetry with digest-suite-registry.json, signature-alg-registry.json and hpke-suite-registry.json.
registry_rules: Schema / describe enum values for MLS ciphersuite fields MUST be generated from active rows' canonical_id only when publishing a new schema/describe contract version, then frozen for that version. Activating a reserved/new suite requires a new contract version and profile negotiation; registry activation MUST NOT expand an existing schema enum in place (zh/conformance/schema-registry.md §6.1 b.1).

A ciphersuite not present as an active row MUST fail closed in KeyPackage claim / group negotiation (unsupported ciphersuite); receivers MUST NOT accept unregistered suites even if the underlying MLS library supports them.

New suites (e.g. ChaCha20-Poly1305 for AES-accelerator-less devices) enter additively as new rows with their own profile gates and conformance vectors; the registry stays minimal for classical suites, but pre-registers post-quantum hybrid rows as status=reserved to match the HPKE / TLS PQ pre-registration discipline (hpke-suite-registry.json, transport-bindings.md §5).

status=reserved rows pin the canonical_id, profile gate and activation_requirements but MUST NOT appear on wire until every activation_requirements entry is met and the row is flipped to active in a registry release. Receivers MUST fail closed (unsupported ciphersuite) on a reserved suite seen in KeyPackage cipher_suites[] or group negotiation before activation — same discipline as encryption-and-audit.md 'MLS 内容 KEM 边界'.

Every status=active row MUST declare kat_vector_id naming an active vector-registry entry; every status=reserved row MUST instead declare kat_absence_reason and MUST NOT declare kat_vector_id. tools/lint_artifacts.py enforces this binding.

registry/mls-extension-registry.json.description: Canonical registry of Arkret-defined MLS (RFC 9420) GroupContext extensions occupying the MLS private-use ExtensionType range 0xF000-0xFFFF. Maintained so SDKs and conformance tooling have a single machine-readable entry for each active Arkret MLS extension codepoint.

private_use_range.reference: RFC 9420 §17.6; IANA MLS Extension Types registry (private-use range)

extensions.name: mls_governance_binding
extensions.carries: Arkret Realm/Circle governance binding inside the MLS GroupContext

registry/mls-security-frontier-registry..description: Closed machine contract for the accepted state that changes current or historical MLS key access. Producers never choose frontier members. Verifiers project these inputs from one accepted Seal view and the RFC 9420 group state, then compare the resulting digest with the governance binding.

cell_entry_shape.ordering: Sort by UTF-8 bytes of cell_family, then canonical JCS bytes of cell_subject, then projected_value_digest; reject duplicates.

digest_input.digest_rule: security_frontier_digest = sha256(JCS({profile_id,effective_scope,cell_entries,mls_leaf_set_digest})). accepted Seal ids, ordinary Event seal_ref values and producer-supplied Event lists are not digest members.

cell_rules.include_when: The subject is in the effective Realm scope. invite and knock do not create an MLS leaf and are excluded.
The cell subject names the effective Circle. invite and knock are excluded.
The principal owns a current or pending MLS leaf and the effective terminal status changes leaf eligibility.
The Agent owns a current or pending MLS leaf and status=deactivated changes leaf eligibility. pause alone is an admission gate and is excluded.

cell_rules.projection: Effective authorization set for the exact principal/device keys referenced by current or pending MLS leaves.
cell_rules.include_when: At least one current or pending leaf references the exact device key. Unreferenced devices are excluded.

cell_rules.projection: Effective device generation for principals that own a current or pending MLS leaf.
cell_rules.include_when: The generation fence changes validity of a key referenced by a current or pending leaf.

cell_rules.projection: Effective authorization set for exact Agent runtime keys referenced by current or pending MLS leaves.
cell_rules.include_when: At least one current or pending leaf references the exact Agent key. Unreferenced Agent keys are excluded.

cell_rules.scope: Realm-default and parent floor for Circle MLS scopes
cell_rules.include_when: Only these fields are projected. Other bundle fields remain protected by Event/CBA/Seal admission but do not force rekey.

cell_rules.scope: Realm-default and parent floor for Circle MLS scopes
Realm-default and parent floor for Circle MLS scopes
cell_rules.projection: Fields that determine current or historical key eligibility.

cell_rules.scope: Realm-default and parent floor for Circle MLS scopes
cell_rules.projection: Service principals and data classes permitted to receive current or historical plaintext/key material.
cell_rules.include_when: A value change expands or contracts actual plaintext/key recipients; endpoint-only metadata is excluded.
Only the effective patched history_visibility value is projected. Display and directory metadata are excluded.

mls_tree_rule.input: The canonical current/pending RFC 9420 leaf set for the effective group, including leaf credential and referenced device/Agent key identity but excluding tree-shape-only metadata.
mls_tree_rule.digest: mls_leaf_set_digest = sha256(JCS(canonical_leaf_entries)). Leaf entries are sorted by their canonical JCS bytes and duplicates are rejected.
mls_tree_rule.commit_rule: For a Commit, compute the next frontier against the post-Commit winning leaf set and the accepted control state selected by the Commit authoring basis. The governance binding is inside the same RFC 9420 transcript; the key-schedule cell containing that binding is never recursively included.

always_excluded: message, Strand, display and directory metadata
media or routing endpoint metadata that does not change plaintext/key recipients
contact, consent, block or pause facts whose accepted effect does not remove an MLS leaf
ordinary Event seal_ref and accepted Seal identifiers
producer-supplied Event, Seal, root or frontier member lists

registry/morph-kind-decision-table.json.describes: Canonical merge precedence for the four declaration sources that can contribute to 'what a Morph is and what it allows'. Mirrors morph.md §4. Reducers, capability checks, query/projection paths, and conformance tests MUST follow this table.

precedence.notes: Declares the field set, types, requiredness, transition rules. Always read for field validation.

Tightens the order-1 declaration inside a single Realm (allowed facets subset, writable fields subset, required schema_refs, required capability actions). MUST NOT widen order-1; widening attempts produce `schema_violation` at Realm accept time.
Wire-stable string key. Create-locked so capability grant selectors do not silently break.
Pure hint. Reading facets to make a security / state-machine / interop decision is a conformance bug.

conflict_resolution.rationale: Facet is a hint, not a contract.
Field + capability are truth; facet is presentation hint only.

conformance_must_test: Reading order-4 facets to decide authorization → MUST fail.
Reducer field validation that ignores order-2 tightening → MUST fail.
Mutating morph_kind after create → MUST fail with `morph_kind_immutable`.
Order-2 morph_kind_profile that widens order-1 schema → MUST be rejected at Realm accept time with `schema_violation` / `morph_profile_widens_schema_ref`.

registry/normative-clause-registry.json.description: Canonical reverse-coverage registry for testable normative clauses. Each row pins one protocol obligation to a stable clause_id, an exact prose anchor, a digest of that section's current text, and the evidence that proves it. It closes the direction vector-registry.json cannot: from prose obligation to executable proof. See spec/v1/zh/conformance/conformance-suite.md section 2.

coverage_scope.rule: This registry covers the high-risk observable obligation set named in included_categories. It is deliberately not a numbering of every normative sentence under spec/v1/zh; mechanically numbering prose would manufacture meaningless MUSTs. A green release gate proves that every registered clause has live evidence and that no registered section changed without review. It does NOT prove that every MUST in the specification is registered.
coverage_scope.extension_rule: Adding a normative obligation inside an included category requires adding or updating a clause in the same change. Because section_digest pins the current text of every registered anchor, editing a registered section fails the release gate until the clause and its evidence are re-reviewed.

registry_rules: clause_id values are stable and MUST NOT be reused after a clause is retired; retire a clause by setting status=deprecated instead of deleting the row.
source_anchor MUST be a repository-relative markdown path plus an existing heading slug. section_digest MUST equal the sha256 of that heading's section text as computed by tools/lint_artifacts.py.

testability_grade=vector rows MUST list evidence_refs containing active vector ids from vector-registry.json. testability_grade=api_shape or audit rows MUST instead declare test_plan describing the non-vector proof.
A clause MUST NOT claim evidence it does not have: an obligation with no executable proof stays out of this registry rather than pointing at an unrelated vector.

clauses.requirement: Canonical JSON serialization (key order, number form, NFC strings, duplicate-key rejection) is the single encoding used for every digest, signature and canonical comparison.
Digest suite identifiers, canonical event digest computation and the bytewise tie-break order are fixed; implementations MUST NOT substitute another hash encoding or comparison direction.

The signature carrier MUST cryptographically protect its algorithm selection, and the binding payload MUST bind domain and audience; a signature valid for one algorithm, domain or audience MUST NOT verify for another.

HLC well-formedness, logical-counter overflow handling and the causal-first usage boundary: HLC breaks ties between causally incomparable items only and MUST NOT select a winner in shared protocol state.
Cursors are opaque server-issued tokens bound to their query scope; clients MUST NOT parse or forge them and cross-scope replay MUST be rejected.
Encrypted envelopes carry a pre-encryption immutable header; AAD digest and ciphertext digest are computed over fixed transcripts and any mismatch MUST fail closed.
Transport encoding bounds: Content-Encoding is forbidden on non-streaming JSON operations and every size limit MUST be enforced before the body is fully buffered or parsed.
Every operation_id ends with <kind>.<action> drawn from the closed kind set, and the action MUST describe a protocol effect rather than an HTTP method name.
clauses.test_plan: Enforced mechanically by tools/lint_artifacts.py: every operation_id in operation-registry.json is checked against the closed kind set and against forbidden HTTP-method action names. There is no runtime vector because the obligation is on the published contract, not on request handling.

clauses.requirement: Every write operation declares a machine-readable idempotency mechanism and retry safety; clients MUST NOT be left to guess the recovery path of an uncertain outcome.
Protected current-v1 endpoints require sender-constrained proof of possession; a bare bearer session grant MUST NOT authenticate a protected request.

MLS integration boundary: only registered active ciphersuites reach the wire, Welcome and KeyPackage binding is verified byte-exactly, every peer claim returns branch-matched portable target signer evidence that the requester independently verifies without DID-document device-key or service-projection fallback, encryption floors MUST NOT be downgraded, an encrypted envelope MUST NOT disclose an AAD event id wider than the Realm aad_visibility ceiling, every encrypted envelope MUST commit its exact scope_ref through the unconditional domain-separated aad.scope_digest and receivers MUST recompute it on decrypt, every MLS epoch MUST bind the independently re-derived security frontier for its accepted key-access state, and epoch-0 leaf indices MUST be recovered only from digest-verified RFC 9420 GroupInfo/ratchet-tree bytes committed by the accepted genesis.
Read-trigger expiry anchors derive from anonymous aggregate contributions, converge under replay and reordering, and MUST NOT reveal reader identity or reader counts.
Directory resolution failures are indistinguishable: unauthorized, non-existent and policy-denied targets MUST NOT be separable by error code, field set or timing.

A Control Move MUST carry a CBA basis covered by an accepted Seal except in the two closed anchor-unit contexts; same-batch events MUST NOT advance their own authorization basis, and basis-free anchor Events remain Control Moves with Control Proposal Acks and pending-index obligations. Ordinary Collaboration bootstrap uses the ordered machine-registry facet closure with an explicit final creator membership and no implicit creator membership. The mutually exclusive Direct Conversation branch is exactly create, explicit peer membership, and one basis-free main ak.strand.create; its fixed baseline and founder membership are reducer projections. Batch admission MUST reject both no-basis shapes anywhere else.

Seal canonical bytes exclude self-reference and DataEvent digests, compaction preserves control roots, Realm reducer selection comes from the authenticated singleton control cell, equivocating notaries are quarantined instead of silently merged, and a full-digest collision under a sealed Control Move is normalized by canonical bytes rather than by an ambiguous digest.

A grant stays within the union of the authorities its issuer_authority_refs name and within their per-action validity window; cycles over grant refs and inactive refs MUST fail closed rather than widen the effective permission set.
Revocation rolls back downstream grants and forces a re-check of dependent decisions; a revoked grant MUST NOT keep authorizing pending or cached writes.
Lattice joins are idempotent, commutative and associative per family; data-plane conflicts return structured bottom instead of electing a winner by arrival order or HLC.
Field patches apply atomically against the declared pre-state; a partially applied patch or an unbound pre-state MUST be rejected.
Every reducer-input event kind declares a closed cell contract (cell family, subject, lattice, bottom, effect projection); an unregistered projection MUST NOT be improvised.
Call state transitions follow the registered matrix, terminal states are absorbing, replaying the same state is a no-op, and concurrent siblings resolve to bottom.
Invite claim is a state machine: a consumed token MUST NOT be re-subjected, expiry uses canonical time, and the membership transition is atomic with the claim.

Account Data keys are server-versioned compare-and-set registers: a stale write MUST fail with cas_conflict, the revision high-water mark never goes backwards, and domain merge runs client-side on plaintext.
Multi-device read cursor merge is causal-first: a causally dominating position wins regardless of HLC, HLC decides only concurrent positions, and device_id only breaks equal HLCs.
To-device delivery executes each durable handler effect exactly once: redelivery is deduplicated by sender-scoped message id and queue removal happens only on explicit ack.
Member delivery binding never silently downgrades: a stale binding frontier, an expired handover grace window or an unresolvable binding MUST fail closed instead of routing to the previous service.

A revoked authorization observed inside the configured freshness window remains deterministically accepted-but-stale for reducer input; a deployment may hide it locally but MUST NOT reject it from the canonical join.
Every accountable principal on an Actor Event must have an active matching accountability grant; any missing grant rejects the whole Event without a stripped projection.

Realm proposal configuration must leave a realizable decision schedule: decision window does not exceed the absolute deadline, equality is valid only when deferral is disabled, and invalid create/update writes reject without state change.
Optional nullable fields normalize absent and null unless a conditional branch requires the field or x-arkret-presence-semantics=distinct explicitly assigns three business states.
clauses.test_plan: tools/gen_property_presence_manifest.py must classify every tristate audit target with zero unresolved dispositions; the Rust SDK draft202012_runtime and Circle payload tests pin the sole distinct target and its Missing/Null/Value round-trip.

clauses.requirement: An accepted ordinary-Realm or managed-Agent closed-anchor Control Move, its Control Proposal Ack and pending index are committed atomically; the covering Seal atomically applies lineage and cell effects and marks every covered pending digest sealed, rolling back if any digest is absent. The separately specified human self-principal PCR authority-authored path omits the Ack but not the pending index or covering-Seal obligation.

Fields inside the event_digest preimage MUST NOT commit to the enclosing Event's own event_id, event_digest or any retype of them, nor to the identity of a not-yet-formed sibling Event in the same atomic unit or ordered submit batch; those two classes have no fixed point, MUST be rejected as event_id_digest_mismatch, and MUST NOT be exempted by any registry. Commitments of that kind MUST instead use the counterpart's payload digest or a structure outside the preimage (proofs, receipts). A one-way forward declaration naming a later Event from a separate submission whose canonical bytes the author already froze is constructible and MUST be allowed only when preimage-identity-exemption-registry.json carries an active row for exactly that field and the field's own description declares the forward commitment.

A client MUST NOT admit a Seal into its local MLS governance trust store because a service reported it as a head, because a proof bundle self-reported it, or because an error suggested it. A candidate is admissible only when the client verifies it locally: for an event-derived Realm, the genesis Seal must cover the ak.realm.create Event derived from realm_id and be signed by the notary named in that create payload; for a Principal Control Realm, the genesis Seal must cover the principal's critical did_inception root anchor; otherwise only a Seal verified as a descendant of an already-trusted anchor may replace the pin.

registry/operation-clause-registry.json.description: Canonical selector-based normative-clause coverage registry for service operations. A profile conformance claim computes its inherited required_endpoints closure and MUST satisfy every active clause whose selector matches each operation. This registry complements operation-registry shape; it does not create a second operation namespace.

clauses.requirement: The canonical operation id and every advertised HTTP binding shape MUST match contract-registry, generated operation-registry, OpenAPI and operation schema index.
Protected operations MUST enforce the OpenAPI security declaration and sender-constrained proof rules before any durable side effect or sensitive response.
Every write operation MUST expose machine-readable idempotency, retry safety, and an uncertain-outcome recovery strategy when blind retry is unsafe.
HTTP headers, aggregate headers, path/query and canonical request envelopes MUST obey the v1 transport bounds and reject generated over-limit inputs before unbounded allocation.
Operation-specific and universal failures MUST use registered error codes and preserve the minimal-disclosure error envelope.
Stream operations MUST implement the registered frame ordering, dropped/resync recovery, cursor binding and reconnect cooldown behavior.
Batch and fanout operations that admit partial outcomes MUST account for every input item and define safe partial retry identity.
Privacy-sensitive operations MUST preserve indistinguishable failures and the minimum response/metadata disclosure defined by their profile.

registry/operation-registry.json.description: Canonical operation catalog for generated service operation views and transport bindings.

generated_views.role: HTTP/OpenAPI binding shape aligned to the catalog; not a second operation namespace.
Descriptive operation map and governance notes; excerpt-only unless explicitly marked generated.

high_security_session_authentication_pol.public_projection_rule: Without valid sender-constrained proof, an allowlisted operation may return only its contract-defined public metadata projection and MUST NOT grant session or capability semantics. All other ak.self.* operations fail closed.
high_security_session_authentication_pol.new_operation_rule: A new or unknown ak.self.* operation is protected by default; adding an unauthenticated public projection requires explicit registration in this list and a normative operation contract defining that projection.

registry_rules: New operation_id values MUST be added here before any OpenAPI, HTTP binding table, SDK generator, or alternative transport binding references them.
Generated views MAY change shape, grouping, or field order, but MUST NOT introduce, rename, or remove operation_id values that are absent from this catalog.
Supporting Arkret core does not imply support for every registered operation. Implementations MUST advertise supported_operations and supported_profiles explicitly.

Each surface_groups entry carries a tier (see surface_classes); only the core tier is implied by claiming v1 protocol support. Extension, interop_bridge, and deployment_local surfaces require explicit advertisement.
surface_classes defines the closed tier vocabulary and surface_groups is the sole canonical operation grouping view; generators MUST NOT emit a third top-level surfaces collection.

Profile matrices in artifacts/profiles/conformance-profiles.json define role-level MUST/SHOULD requirements; the surface groups below define machine-readable capability families for discovery, docs, and lint.
Each operation MUST declare success_shape_kind so SDKs can determine success handling without endpoint-name hard-coding.

Operations with typed OpenAPI bodies SHOULD declare request_schema_ref and/or response_schema_ref. The referenced schema fragment is the source for generated DTO docs and MUST match the OpenAPI component referenced by the HTTP binding.

Operations that still bind OpenAPI request/response bodies to OperationRequest or OperationResult MUST declare generic_binding with request/response booleans, reason, profile_gate, and migration_plan; core-tier operations MUST NOT use generic bindings.

operation_id values MUST end with <kind>.<action>. The kind segment MUST be one of read, stream, resource, command, upload, or exchange; the action segment MUST describe protocol semantics and MUST NOT be an HTTP method name. read is the only safe/idempotent computation kind; its exact GET, QUERY, or POST binding is declared by the operation row according to request shape.
An operation row MUST declare exactly one HTTP binding and MUST NOT declare http_compatibility_bindings or unregistered method/path aliases.

resource.replace operations MUST bind to HTTP PUT; resource.delete operations MUST bind to HTTP DELETE; command, upload, exchange, and complex read-body operations SHOULD bind to HTTP POST unless their operation notes define a stricter resource URI replacement contract.

Every write operation (kind command/upload/exchange, and resource.replace / resource.delete) MUST declare idempotency_mechanism (one of idempotency_key, object_id, request_id, canonical_hash, protocol_sequence, none) and retry_safe (boolean). Read-only operations (read/stream/resource.get/resource.head) MUST NOT declare these fields.

An operation that invokes current DID authority MUST carry exactly one did_authority object that byte-matches its did-freshness-profile-registry call_sites row. Operations without a real DID-authority call MUST omit it; risk tier never implies DID freshness.

idempotency_mechanism is the machine-readable source of truth for which idempotency mechanism from api-conventions.md section 6 an operation uses. canonical_hash operations MUST also declare canonical_hash_input as either full_body or an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer. retry_safe=true means a byte-identical full retry of the same request cannot produce duplicate side effects: it returns the original outcome, an equivalent idempotent no-op, or a deterministic conflict. retry_safe=false means blind retries MAY duplicate side effects or consume one-time material; clients MUST NOT retry such operations without out-of-band reconciliation.

Every write operation MUST declare durable_effect. kind=event_log identifies an Arkret Event committed by successful completion and declares either event_kinds[] or an event_kind_source JSON path; kind=actor_private_event declares the actor-private Event kind committed; kind=none declares no Arkret Event and requires a stable rationale. Service-local durable state, identity-method logs, queues, session/material stores, external effects and returned-but-uncommitted Event material all use kind=none with an accurate rationale. Missing, unknown or inactive declared Event kinds fail closed.

Every operation MUST declare body_class, a closed value of non_streaming_json, streaming_ndjson, or binary_stream. body_class=non_streaming_json binds the operation to the general size contract in zh/conformance/scalability-constraints.md section 2.1: canonical request/response body <= 8 MiB, HTTP message content wire bytes <= 16 MiB, Content-Encoding MUST be absent, and every byte overflow maps to payload_too_large. streaming_ndjson and binary_stream operations are excluded from the whole-body limits and MUST define their own per-frame / per-chunk / pending bounds (scalability-constraints section 2.1.7).

max_canonical_body_bytes is OPTIONAL and only for a body_class=non_streaming_json operation whose normative limit is LOWER than the general 8 MiB. It MUST NOT declare a value above 8 MiB, and deployments MUST NOT lower the general interoperability constants through Describe (scalability-constraints section 2.1.6).

max_items is REQUIRED for a body_class=non_streaming_json operation whose request or response carries a top-level array with a normative count bound. max_items and the byte budget are a conjunctive two-dimensional constraint: a count bound never promises that max_items objects of near-maximum size fit in one body, and implementations MUST NOT lower a registered count because a fixture-median product exceeds the byte budget (scalability-constraints section 2.1.5).

surface_classes.core: Base interoperable surfaces implied by claiming Arkret v1 protocol support (service discovery, identity registry, events/account aggregate).
surface_classes.extension: Optional interoperable surfaces that are part of the Arkret specification but require explicit discovery/profile advertisement.
surface_classes.interop_bridge: Adapter surfaces that bridge Arkret to external protocols (MIMI Internet-Drafts, third-party Applet hosts). Implementations advertise these only when the external protocol is supported; bridge operations are not part of any core or extension profile and frequently mirror an in-spec operation via bridges_to.
surface_classes.deployment_local: Deployment-specific, operator, or product-local surfaces that MUST NOT be assumed from core protocol support alone.

source_signature_anchor.node_to_applet: Source-Service-ID current service DID verification method; Destination-Service-ID MUST equal the Applet registration service_id.
source_signature_anchor.applet_to_arkret_inbound: Applet registration webhook_auth.key_ref; its canonical bare full_id MUST be validated by the registered method adapter and project to both Source-Service-ID and the active effective install service_id. Direct full-DID/core-id comparison and did_core_id fragment concatenation are forbidden.

operations.notes: Resource-side appeal against an operator takedown. The appeal packet MUST bind takedown_id, resource id, appellant DID, argument/evidence digest, requested_outcome and created_at, signed by the resource governance key or an authorized advocate; the Directory returns a signed decision receipt. See discovery-directory.md §8.7.

Server-to-server session-grant introspection (RFC 7662-style). The Principal Server validating a presented grant calls this with the grant id or grant_jwt (+ optional audience and optional S2S holder confirmation) and learns whether it is active, plus non-secret grant metadata. The Account Authority MUST read the same issuer ledger used by issue, refresh, revoke and cascade; lifecycle status distinguishes active, revoked, superseded and dynamically expired records rather than consulting a Principal Event/cell. The introspection response MUST include the grant's cnf_jkt (RFC 7638 thumbprint of the bound DPoP holder key) so the Principal Server can verify the per-request DPoP proof on /_arkret/self/* (api-conventions §3.3); clients do not send a separate introspection-proof header on self-path requests. session_public_key is also returned for RFC 9421 PoP verification. READ-ONLY: introspection MUST NOT consume/revoke the grant. Authenticated by the configured session_grant_introspection_bearer (server-local); not exposed over gRPC/MQ.

Account Authority S2S producer operation for Native Agent signer evidence. The request carries agent_authority_service_resolution: the current signed ServiceResolutionRecord, adapter-discriminated method evidence and authenticated normalized DID Document. The receiver independently validates method evidence, document digest, record proof/currentness, project(full_id), and active assertion key before verifying an RFC 9421 signature that covers method, target URI/path, Content-Digest, Source/Destination-Service-ID, operation id and request id. A did_core_id, URL, bearer or caller-supplied public key is never the verification key source; bearer may only be an additional deployment gate. The authenticated source service MUST equal request.agent_authority_service_id and MUST byte-match service_id in request.principal_id's current AcceptedAtServiceBinding; that Principal Server is the Agent PCR authority under the managed-Agent same-server invariant. Ordinary clients and a caller-supplied account identity are forbidden. The Account Authority reads its own authoritative account binding/status projection, selects account_binding_default or account_status_event basis, and signs the closed controller_account_gate_attestation under domain ak.controller-account-gate-v1. issued_at <= expires_at and expires_at-issued_at MUST be <=300s. Unknown principal, missing current service binding, wrong source service and unauthorized caller are indistinguishable not_found outcomes and disclose no account status. Exact request_id plus canonical intent replay returns the byte-identical outcome while retained; same request_id with different principal or service is duplicate_conflict with zero issuance. The attestation is intentionally a reusable short-TTL controller-lifecycle snapshot and omits operation, request_digest, audience and challenge: per-request current_observation and outer_attestation bind its digest to those exact values, so a bare gate replay cannot validate another request. account_id and raw account cells never enter the request, outcome, logs visible to the caller or portable evidence.

Authenticated by Authorization: DPoP <account_handoff_grant> plus a matching DPoP header. The Account Authority verifies the current lease holder and fence, validates the complete unpublished DID operation, derives principal_id, its canonical operation digest, did_version_id, log_head_digest, and control_key_digest, persists the holder-authenticated operation checkpoint, rate-limits same-holder renewal, and issues a <=300s single-use challenge bound to account_subject, holder cnf.jkt, lease/fence, all derived DID pins, audience, origin, trust domain, purpose, and expiry. Repeating the same request_id returns the same unconsumed challenge. Challenge state MUST be shared durable state, not process-local memory; expiry and prior consumption are distinct terminal states.

Issue a single-use challenge for binding an ALREADY-PUBLISHED full_id to the authenticated service account under stable principal_id. Authenticated by Authorization: DPoP <account_handoff_grant> plus a matching DPoP header. Unlike issue_identity_binding_challenge the caller supplies principal_id plus full_id rather than an unpublished DID operation: the Account Authority MUST resolve full_id itself at the high freshness tier (synchronous refresh or fail closed), MUST require the registered adapter to project(full_id)=principal_id, MUST NOT attempt to resolve did_core_id, MUST NOT accept caller-supplied history, and derives did_version_id, log_head_digest and control_key_digest from the resolved current entry. Deployments that do not host the DID MUST additionally require method-native witness / freshness evidence, because accepting registry and Principal Server co-location does not extend trust to third-party DIDs. The <=300s single-use challenge and returned control proof bind account_subject, principal_id, full_id, holder cnf.jkt, the resolved DID pins, audience, origin, trust domain, purpose and expiry. Repeating the same request_id returns the same unconsumed challenge. Challenge state MUST be shared durable state, not process-local memory; expiry and prior consumption are distinct terminal states. This operation performs no PCR genesis and reserves no principal: it only proves current control of an existing DID.

Issue a single-use challenge that authorizes explicitly abandoning a provisional identity whose PCR was never accepted (zh/identity/key-management.md §5.0.2). Authenticated by Authorization: DPoP <account_handoff_grant> plus a matching DPoP header, and by nothing else: the PCR was never accepted, so the holder has no principal and therefore no principal-bound ak.session.grant. The Account Authority verifies the current lease holder and fence, requires principal_id and did_version_id to equal the holder-authenticated reserved_identity_creation checkpoint, and MUST refuse to issue a challenge once that PCR is accepted. The <=300s single-use challenge is bound to account_subject, holder cnf.jkt, the abandoned principal_id, did_version_id, lease id and fence, the closed consequence disclosure, audience, origin, trust domain, purpose and expiry. Repeating the same request_id returns the same unconsumed challenge. Challenge state MUST be shared durable state, not process-local memory; expiry and prior consumption are distinct terminal states. This operation abandons nothing by itself and MUST NOT be reachable from ordinary login, session resume, lease fence advance or any automated flow.

Consume an identity-abandonment challenge and explicitly abandon the provisional identity. Authenticated by Authorization: DPoP <account_handoff_grant> plus a matching DPoP header; the presented handoff MUST be a fresh one and MUST NOT be the grant that was presented when the challenge was issued. Whether that fresh handoff required re-authentication, which risk checks ran and how long any cooldown lasts are deployment governance and are deliberately not specified. One transaction consumes the challenge, records the orphan anchor tombstone / audit reservation, suppresses the reserved_identity_creation checkpoint on every holder-readable surface and releases the identity-creation lease; any step failing means zero writes. If the PCR was accepted between issuance and confirmation the request MUST fail with identity_creation_already_accepted and MUST NOT abandon anything, because removing an established identity is the account deletion path. Replaying the same request_id returns the same terminal outcome and MUST NOT produce a second tombstone. The abandoned entry 0 stays a permanently unusable orphan anchor; its later handling is deployment governance.

Account Authority single-call issuer-ledger session-grant exchange. After validating account-to-principal binding, authentication proof, holder DPoP, audience and scope ceiling, the issuer uses the proof-specific stable request identity and canonical intent digest to atomically persist one immutable issuance record and signed JWT before responding. The grant ID and JWT jti are recomputed from that record under id_kind_registry.issuer_record_identity_contract; no Principal Event is authored. Exact replay revalidates holder/DPoP/target/digest and returns the byte-identical recorded outcome. Same request identity with different canonical intent is duplicate_conflict with zero writes. A replay whose outcome is expired or revoked/superseded returns the registered terminal error and never issues a replacement; an evicted replay record fails closed as indeterminate. The response is the client-visible SessionGrantOutcome and the client presents ak.session.grant directly to /_arkret/self/* with DPoP. For proof_kind=oidc_code_exchange, the Account Authority exchanges and validates the code. For proof_kind=pre_registration_handoff, the DPoP-bound handoff account MUST already be bound to principal_id. The Account Authority never derives a principal DID from OIDC and never obtains or uses a principal/root/device/notary Event-signing key.

Account Authority ordinary hard logout (account-lifecycle §4.1): single client-visible logout entry. The handler validates the current ak.session.grant + DPoP, terminates the Auth-side auth session / grant rotation chain through ak.gate.account.command.logout_auth_session when Auth-side is split out, and completes or durably schedules the Principal-side local account session + device session cleanup and to-device/push removal. Distinct from revoke_session (targeted session-grant revoke). HTTP-only Account Authority op; not exposed over gRPC/MQ.

Account Authority to Auth Server S2S Auth-side logout sub-operation (account-lifecycle §4.1): the Account Authority has already validated the client-visible ak.gate.account.command.logout request, then calls this operation with service-to-service authentication to log out the Auth-side browser/auth session owning the presented ak.session.grant and terminate that session's grant rotation chain. Ordinary clients MUST NOT call this operation; they only call ak.gate.account.command.logout. HTTP-only S2S op; not exposed over gRPC/MQ.

Final native Agent runtime-key authorization. The closed Ed25519 possession proof MUST be byte-identical to the current persisted runtime request and still fresh; the authority rebuilds its server-record-bound transcript, stable runtime binding and ak.agent.key_pairing_request_binding.v1 (including current proof digest) before accepting the controller-signed authorize Event. A stale prompt or any body/record/evidence mismatch fails closed without consuming the pairing handle.

Authorizes a sibling device only after verified current-device confirmation. This operation always produces authorization_binding_kind=accepted_device, so device_signature MUST verify under ak.device-authorize-accepted-device-possession-proof-v1 and registration_anchor/pcr_recovery domains MUST be rejected. The authority recomputes the pairing transcript, verifies exact request/Event equality and submits the current-device-signed Event through ordinary PCR admission; it never resolves current human DID authority.

Issues the replacement device's first Standard grant after a PCR-policy RecoveryTransaction completes. The body carries the terminal device-attested receipt, coordinator attestation, PCR generation and InitialSessionGrantRequest; DID-root evidence is relevant only when that optional factor was enabled.

DPoP-bound issuer-ledger session-grant rotation. The stable request identity is (predecessor_grant_id, refresh_request_digest). Exact replay revalidates current holder/DPoP and returns the recorded successor outcome; conflicting canonical bytes are duplicate_conflict. One issuer transaction creates the active successor with a fresh issuance nonce, preserves the independently allocated session_id, and atomically marks the predecessor superseded with successor_session_grant_id. A replay whose recorded successor is expired or revoked/superseded returns the registered terminal error and never issues another successor. Account Authority-local op; no Principal Event is authored.

Canonical account creation/binding operation. The body selects exactly one branch: an already-published DID control proof, or account-first identity_creation. Both branches submit outer full_id and principal_id; every repeated full_id/principal_id in the selected proof, identity-creation object and PCR genesis initial_resolution MUST equal the outer values byte-for-byte. The Account Authority independently validates the registered method adapter and requires project(full_id)=principal_id. The published-DID proof branch uses the durable challenge pins and creates no identity-creation lease or PCR genesis. In the account-first identity_creation branch the caller MUST additionally present Authorization: DPoP <account_handoff_grant> plus matching DPoP, the current lease/fence, the exact reserved DID inception operation, and a fresh identity-root control proof over the persisted challenge transcript. For did:webvh the verifier takes parameters.updateKeys[0] of the entry pinned by did_version_id (the root is not a DID Document verificationMethod), requires verification_key_multibase to match it exactly, and requires its canonical multikey SHA-256 to equal control_key_digest. For account-first inception that entry is entry 0. The Account Authority CAS-validates account/holder/lease/fence/reservation, consumes the challenge, submits the DID operation internally, accepts only accepted or byte-identical duplicate with a verified head digest, derives pcr_realm_id only by retyping the exact root-signed ak.realm.create event_id, and writes the service-account binding. Account-first PCR genesis persists the same verified full_id, method_history_head and version_id in initial_resolution. Every success returns a signed binding_receipt that binds binding_kind, principal_id, full_id, did_version_id and control_key_digest; identity_creation_lease_id and lease_fence appear only for binding_kind=identity_creation. The (account, principal_id, operation_digest) result is idempotent; published-but-not-yet-bound state is durably completed for that same account and can never be rebound to another account. The operation never accepts recovery words, seed material, or identity-root private keys.

durable_effect.irreversibility_note: Beyond authoring the genesis Events this operation publishes a public did:webvh log entry and commits a one-account-one-principal binding that can never be rebound. Retry and audit logic MUST treat it as cross-service irreversible even though the closed durable_effect kind vocabulary can only name the Event-log half.

operations.notes: Durable issuer-ledger session revocation. The stable request identity binds issuer, operation kind, authenticated principal/session, canonical target selector and canonical request digest. One issuer transaction records the exact outcome and idempotently transitions matching active records to revoked. Same identity and canonical intent replays the byte-identical recorded outcome after current caller authorization is revalidated; the same identity with different intent is duplicate_conflict with zero additional state changes. Introspection is not a substitute for resolving an uncertain mutation outcome.

Optional Account Authority browser redirect landing / handoff for deployments that use an OIDC redirect URI under /_arkret/gate/account. It MUST NOT issue or return SessionGrantOutcome, ak.session.grant, or Principal local session material; client-visible grant issuance remains ak.gate.account.command.issue_session_grant.

Account Authority exchanges an OIDC authorization code for an opaque, short-lived account_handoff_grant bound to the request DPoP key and returns the deployment-local stable account_subject. The handoff is not ak.session.grant, has no refresh-token semantics, and its closed operation allowlist is issue_identity_binding_challenge, issue_did_binding_challenge, issue_identity_abandonment_challenge, abandon_identity_creation, register, issue_session_grant, and issue_recovery_completion_grant. The two abandonment operations are on that list because a never-accepted PCR leaves the holder without a principal, so no principal-bound ak.session.grant can exist to carry them. It returns bound, identity_creation_active, or identity_creation_busy state and atomically acquires, renews, or fences a rate-limited identity-creation lease for the authenticated service account. Busy includes the conflicting live lease expires_at without holder identity. Repeating the same request_id returns the same live outcome. A different holder cannot take an unexpired lease; after expiry, a newly authenticated holder may fence it and must preserve all frozen checkpoints.

Read-only DPoP-bound projection of the current Account Authority identity-creation lease or established binding. The response is rebuilt from durable server state on every call and accepts no client-authored phase, goal, checkpoint, or recovery material. Clients use it to reconcile local onboarding artifacts after reload, callback, process restart, or an uncertain command result.

Runtime-to-controller pending approval request for native personal-agent key pairing. The closed Ed25519 proof binds the local key to the authoritative pairing handle, at-least-128-bit pairing secret, authority service DID, stable runtime binding and no-more-than-five-minute window; the controller still must approve by signing ak.agent.key.authorize bound to the current proof digest. Pairing secret and proof MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string. One open pairing_request_id has at most one pending stable ak.agent.runtime_key_binding.v1 digest: same-binding retries retain approval/notification ids and atomically replace the current freshness proof, while a different binding fails with HTTP 409 agent_runtime_request_conflict without replacement.

Resolves a short-lived agent pairing token carried out-of-band, usually as a URL fragment in a QR/link. The pairing token MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; the response is the six-field agent_pairing_bootstrap.

Runtime-side poll for the controller decision on a previously submitted runtime key request. The pairing_request_id + pairing_code + agent_id triple is the query credential and MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; a record miss and a pairing_code or agent_id mismatch MUST be indistinguishable (both not_found). Once approved, the outcome carries authorized_event_ref plus the authorized key binding; the runtime MUST compare authorized_public_key_digest against its own key and treat a mismatch as paired-by-another-runtime. HTTP responses MUST carry Retry-After; clients wait at least that interval and use 1s/2s/5s/10s then at most 30s backoff, stopping after pairing expiry.

Unauthenticated stage of a device-pairing short-link handoff (device-lifecycle.md §2.1.1). The new device submits a canonical new_device_pubkey and a client_nonce (plus optional display_name / device_metadata) and MUST NOT submit a challenge proof, because the proof must commit to values this call mints; the service mints a fresh device_pairing_request_id, an 8-character Crockford-style 40-bit CSPRNG pairing_code, a gate_audience and a server_nonce, and stores a bounded-TTL account-less record in state pending_authorization. The staged record deliberately carries no hpke_key, no algorithms, no challenge proof and no target attestation: those reach the approving device only over the out-of-band channel, so this anonymous surface never accumulates long-term device key material or a device algorithm fingerprint, and a mirrored copy could never be authoritative anyway. The staged record binds no principal and grants nothing until an authenticated device authorizes it. Stage, resolve and status are rate limited. Each call mints a fresh request, so blind retries duplicate staged records: not retry-safe.

Resolves a device-pairing short-link token carried out-of-band, usually as a URL fragment in a QR/link. The pairing token MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; the response is the DevicePairingBootstrap. The bootstrap carries only server-minted challenge material: it does not carry the challenge proof, the target attestation, or the hpke_key and algorithms that attestation signs, and those MUST NOT be mirrored here. resolve MUST return a uniform not_found for unknown id, pairing_code mismatch, expiry, or a non-pending record so the failing condition is not enumerable. Authorization is unchanged: the returned bootstrap is only consumed by an authenticated device that has independently verified the out-of-band challenge proof and target attestation before driving ak.gate.account.command.pair_device.

Unauthenticated poll for the authorization status of a staged device-pairing record. The device_pairing_request_id + pairing_code pair is the query credential and MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; a record miss and a pairing_code mismatch MUST be indistinguishable (both not_found). While the record is open the outcome carries only state pending_authorization; once an authenticated device has authorized the pairing the outcome carries state authorized plus required device_id and authorized_event_ref; an expired record reports only state expired during a bounded cleanup retention period and becomes not_found after deletion. authorized_event_ref is the entry point for the mandatory pre-assembly check in device-lifecycle.md §5.4.1: the target device MUST fetch that accepted ak.device.authorize and confirm byte-identical device_signature, byte-identical device_public_key / hpke_key / algorithms and an expected principal_id before it assembles the identity locally, and MUST fail closed and warn the user otherwise.

Reads the owner-published current principal resolution evidence from the known Principal Server. history_depth bounds selective history disclosure; after_resolution_event_ref requests only the successor chain after a known ancestor and never exposes unrelated PCR control history. This is a second-hop evidence fetch, not a global resolver or authorization oracle. Sensitive consumers fetch fresh, validate PCR Event/Seal/cell evidence, independently run the registered DID method adapter, and require project(full_id)=principal_id; durable storage of arbitrary remote-principal bindings is not required.

Returns the current signed ServiceResolutionRecord at the stable current_record_url carried by bootstrap material. TLS is transport only. Consumers verify the record proof, method history, project(full_id)=service_id, time ordering, record_sequence/previous_record_digest and describe binding. Same-core successors refresh route caches without Realm rebind; a changed did_core_id requires a new authorized service binding.

Resolves an online invite locator token carried out-of-band, usually as a URL fragment in a QR/link. The locator token MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; the response is a signed principal_locator.

The caller MUST author and sign the exact ak.consent.grant (decision=accept) or ak.consent.revoke (decision=deny or revoke) EventInitialSubmission. The facade verifies the detached operation signature and the Event authority/correlation, then submits the Event unchanged through ordinary Event admission. It MUST NOT synthesize, rebuild or co-sign consent state. A revoke with no matching active observed dots is rejected without disclosing holder state. Exact Event replay returns the same accepted Event reference.

Account Authority or authorized Principal Server publication of exactly one ak.account.status Event into the account principal's Principal Control Realm. The caller uses service-to-service HTTP Message Signature authentication and a required Idempotency-Key covered by the signature. authority_evidence is Account Authority-signed transport evidence binding account_id, principal_id, principal_control_realm_id, issuer service and a live authority_ref; the receiver independently verifies it, the Event proof, exact Event/evidence field equality, current issuer key/delegation and PCR CBA closure. Initial publication carries the Event without an AuthorizationLease; downstream fanout adds receiver-signed account_status_receipts and CbaProofBundle values. AccountStatusReceipt proves local frontier acceptance, contains no AuthorizationLease id, and generic IngressReceipt is forbidden. Same key plus different canonical body is duplicate_conflict. A byte-identical retry returns the latest durable operation state, allowing pending_seal and fanout progress to converge without creating another Event. accepted or duplicate is terminal for the receiving server's frontier; multi-server propagation continues from a durable bounded outbox and never mutates the signed account-status payload.

Read-only service-authenticated Account Authority query for the exact issuer actor-chain frontier and Principal Control Realm Seal frontier needed to sign one ak.account.status Event. The receiver verifies the signed authority_evidence, current issuer delegation and account/principal/PCR binding before disclosure. The response binds RealmActorFrontierView.actor_id to issuer_service_id and both frontier realm_id values to principal_control_realm_id; it grants no authority, accepts no Event and never synthesizes an empty PCR.

Unique closed XOR delivery carrier for original holder-signed Contact request, normal response, reject, scope replacement, or tombstone facts plus their exact source acceptance receipts and refreshable current proof. It never carries Direct Conversation binding or Realm Events. Branches use byte-identical durable replay; the receiver never re-signs or treats tentative/stale evidence as authority.

Service-authenticated relay for an exact requester-authorized ak.member.repair.request. The source copies request_id, content and detached requester authorization byte for byte from the accepted self dispatch, appends exactly one portable device or Native Agent current-authority evidence branch, and covers the complete body with Content-Digest and RFC 9421. The destination independently binds requester identity, accepted rejoin actor and subject, authorization Event, current evidence and exact requester_keypackage_ref signer. In one transaction keyed by (Source-Service-ID, request_id), it freezes request_digest, resolves the peer participant from the accepted Direct Conversation binding, and atomically chooses one closed recipient branch: snapshot every currently authorized human device and enqueue all stable distinct message ids, or enqueue one stable message id to the Native Agent's current active runtime endpoint from accepted agent-key/session binding. Exact replay returns the stored byte-identical outcome; a different digest is duplicate_conflict. Success proves only durable enqueue, never business repair acceptance.

Service-authenticated hard-erasure receipt fanout. Source-Service-ID MUST equal receipt.issuer. Idempotency-Key is required and covered by the HTTP Message Signature; its scope is (source service, destination service, key). The receiver verifies the closed receipt, issuer authority at receipt.issued_at, every receipt proof, receipt_digest and the exact retained-stub binding before any deletion or durable acceptance. Same key and canonical body returns the byte-identical signed acceptance; different body returns duplicate_conflict with zero writes. An accepted or duplicate acknowledgement closes the sender outbox item.

Service-authenticated exact receipt-package lookup for the issuer, receiver or an explicitly authorized auditor. It is non-enumerating: unauthorized, unknown and hidden receipt identifiers produce the same not_found response. The returned retained stub is the exact object accepted with the receipt and MUST NOT be reconstructed from later state.

Federation peer Event publication. Each EventFederationSubmission carries the original signed Event. Ordinary online publication omits AuthorizationLease and uses an empty ingress_receipts array; explicit delayed/offline publication carries the lease and at least one original lease-bound IngressReceipt. An ak.member.state compensation publication additionally carries the unchanged transport-only membership_compensation_evidence and the receiver applies the same exact admission/incarnation/action/executor/single-use evaluator as initial submission. Request-level CbaProofBundle values provide receiver-relative dependency closure. The receiver independently validates every Event, optional lease, receipt threshold, compensation evidence, bundle object and reducer result. Ordinary missing dependencies use HTTP 200 partial items with reason_code=dependency_missing and non-empty typed missing sets; registered atomic units use top-level HTTP 409 dependency_missing with EventsDependencyMissingProblem and zero writes. A received response terminates that Idempotency-Key; a post-backfill submit uses a fresh key. The caller MUST use service-to-service authentication with Source/Destination service DID and trust-domain headers. Federated ak.invite.claim remains decided by the destination Realm reducer. The request union additionally registers the discriminated direct_conversation_founding branch for the Direct Conversation founding exception of zh/sync/federation.md section 4.0.4: it carries exactly three ordered EventFederationSubmission items, the source DirectConversationFoundingAcceptanceReceipt and bounded dependencies, and it omits service_binding_ref because the Realm does not yet exist at the receiver. The receiver freshly verifies transport source authority over founder_id, cutover/fence continuity when the receipt came from a pre-migration service, destination binding to the local participant, body closure, recomputed founding_unit_digest and coordinates, and the full direct_conversation_genesis admission before admitting the unit at one atomic boundary. A missing Contact basis mirror or other bounded dependency is a retryable top-level HTTP 409 dependency_missing with zero writes, never a per-item partial and never a permanent rejection.
Federation peer Events surface describe. This endpoint describes the server-to-server peer event bindings; it is not a client self/events binding.

Federation peer frontier probe. Requires service-to-service authentication, Source/Destination service DID headers, trust-domain headers, and Realm federation_peer authorization. It returns the federation peer frontier response shape on the dedicated peer trust surface.

Read-only federation dependency resolution for canonical-bytewise sorted exact Event IDs, Event digests, and Seal refs in one Realm. Returns visible Events and receiver-relative CbaProofBundle values under a caller-selected response budget capped at 8 MiB. It never accepts an Event or Seal and never advances a frontier. Every selector is fully accounted for by a returned object or an indistinguishable same-type missing entry; if complete accounting cannot fit the budget, the whole operation returns limit_exceeded rather than a partial success.

Federation peer pull/backfill query. Uses the same selector, cursor, order, and response semantics as ak.self.events.read.scan, but the HTTP trust surface is peer and the caller MUST be an authorized federation peer service.

Private Principal Server to Principal Server invite delivery. Requires service-to-service authentication, Destination-Service-ID equal to invite_address.recipient_service_id, a ak.invite.create event whose invitee equals invite_address.subject_id, and introduction_evidence accepted by the recipient invite_receive_policy.

Atomic cross-Principal-Server KeyPackage claim. The destination KeyPackage authority is the sole CAS authority and MUST validate both requester portable authorization evidence, the requester participant authorization and the outer source-service HTTP Message Signature. Every successful human-device claim record carries complete target_device_signing_key_evidence without a semantic history-entry cap; every Native Agent record instead carries request-bound current target_agent_signer_evidence. The requester independently verifies the returned root/Seal/current authority before installing the KeyPackage; the destination service receipt is transport integrity, not signer authority. Idempotency is scoped by (Source-Service-ID, claim_request_id) and binds the canonical request digest; duplicate transport delivery returns the original byte-identical outcome, but callers MUST use the query operation rather than replaying the command after an uncertain outcome. Success omits inventory counts and per-device failures.

Read-only recovery of the destination authority's durable peer-claim ledger after an uncertain command outcome. It requires the same authenticated source service and exact request_digest and returns only opaque claim state plus the original signed success outcome when one exists.

Read-only service-authenticated retrieval of the exact RFC 9420 GroupInfo and ratchet_tree extension bytes committed by one accepted ak.mls.genesis Event. The provider resolves the Event, verifies every echoed scope/group/epoch/ref/digest selector, hashes raw bytes against both explicit digests and content-addressed refs, and validates GroupInfo/tree consistency before returning an all-or-nothing response. It never returns private tree material, secrets, inferred leaf DTOs or proof-bundle leaves; consumers derive leaf_index only from occupied leaves in the verified RFC tree.

Account Authority transparently relays the exact client-signed PCR genesis unit after authenticating the service account and freezing the account/principal reservation. The outer service signature is transport authentication only. Principal admission independently validates the DID inception root, identity_creation_control_proof, the event-derived PCR id retype(create.event_id) which is never derived from the principal DID or subject and is never server-chosen, empty frontier, ordered root-signed create plus founding-device-signed authorize, single-direction payload digest binding, lease fence and expiry. Acceptance is atomic and create-once at the account dimension: two genesis attempts produce two different realm_id values, so implementations MUST NOT detect concurrency by id equality. Exact replay returns the original pcr_genesis_unit receipt and a conflicting unit performs zero writes.

Realm-scoped service-authenticated publication of exactly one target-signed ServiceResolutionRecord or ServiceRouteHandoverNotice. Idempotency-Key is required, is covered by the HTTP Message Signature, and MUST equal body.request_id. Transport replay is keyed by (Source-Service-ID, realm_id, request_id) and binds the complete canonical request digest: exact replay returns the original ack and a different digest is duplicate_conflict. Artifact integrity is independently keyed by (Source-Service-ID, realm_id, target service_id, artifact family/key/revision): the same artifact key with another digest conflicts with zero overwrite. The receiver validates source peer authority, target visibility, exact artifact_digest, target proof, full_id-to-core projection, sequential record/notice basis, time rules and hard bounds before writing its service-local mirror ledger. The receiver-signed ack cross-binds both keys, request_digest and accepted time; it proves durable receipt of exact bytes only and never makes a URL authoritative or declares a migration safe unless the deployment-required peer set has all acked.

Read-only Realm-scoped recovery of at most 32 continuous target-signed successor records and one active target-signed handover notice within a caller-selected response budget capped at 256 KiB. The authenticated requester must be a current allowed federation peer and must already be authorized to know the target service core through an effective member delivery binding, sync_endpoints or explicit service delegation. Unknown, unauthorized, invisible, not-held and unavailable are outwardly indistinguishable and query/source/target rate limits prevent enumeration. The responder never returns a mirror-signed bare URL. The requester independently verifies every target proof, exact chain, freshness, method history and describe reverse binding; same sequence with different valid target-signed digests enters route-fork quarantine rather than majority, arrival-order or reachability selection.

Optional Signal Extension single-hop peer relay. The source batches original producer-signed encrypted SignalEnvelope values for one Realm and one destination service. The destination independently verifies peer authentication, current delivery binding, envelope proof, scope, Seal, signal_class, TTL and encrypted payload binding, then performs only local live fanout. The request MUST NOT carry Idempotency-Key; uncertain outcomes use drop_unconfirmed. The opaque accepted=true response reveals no Realm, scope, sender, recipient, binding, support, or per-signal result and is not a durable delivery receipt.
Federation peer snapshot manifest head for snapshot-assisted bootstrap. Requires service-to-service authentication and Realm federation_peer authorization.

The wrapper carries one complete DID method-native operation. did_method is the bare method discriminator and MUST equal the DID method component. Controller/update/recovery authorization comes only from the native operation; transport authentication is admission-only. Unsupported methods, generic replace/patch/document fallbacks, stale heads, and sibling forks fail closed. Exact canonical-operation retries are duplicate-success without a second history append.

Establish the local binding for an external, already-published Organization DID. The request MUST carry stable organization_id as did_core_id plus the current published full_id; the receiver independently resolves and validates full_id with the registered method adapter and requires project(full_id)=organization_id. The referenced challenge MUST bind both identifiers, local_admin_subject and the requested scope set, and the method-native control transcript MUST bind organization_id, full_id, the pinned version_id/log_head_digest and that challenge context. The outcome and signed receipt echo both identifiers; the receipt also binds version_id and control_key_digest so the accepted control state remains auditable. Creating a new Organization DID is a separate inception ceremony and has no member here. Idempotency is per generation: replaying the current generation's byte-identical request returns created=false, while a request after revoke, or one that changes local_admin_subject or the scope set, opens registration_generation+1 with created=true. This operation registers a reference and local administrative delegation only: it does not host the DID's method history, make this deployment the controller, or create Realm, membership, notary, capability or service delegation.

Issue a single-use control challenge for an external, already-published Organization DID.
