consumer_binding, when present, is the machine-readable disposition for a logical schema that is not directly named by an operation, Event kind, or another schema. Runtime and dynamic wire bindings MUST declare kind, selector, and normative_ref. A prose_only binding MUST instead declare a non-empty rationale and MUST NOT be counted as wire coverage.

The effective schema reference of a row is the literal concatenation (file + optional fragment): fragment already includes its leading '#', so consumers MUST NOT insert another separator. For example file='schemas/agent-operations.schema.json' plus fragment='#/$defs/agent_pairing_bootstrap' resolves to exactly 'schemas/agent-operations.schema.json#/$defs/agent_pairing_bootstrap'. Consumers MUST resolve that URI-fragment JSON Pointer and MUST NOT bind schema_id to the top-level document of file. When fragment is absent, the effective reference is the top-level document of file. Two schema_id rows mapping to the same file MUST be distinguished by fragment (or one MUST omit fragment to denote the whole document); a consumer that ignores fragment and loads the top-level document for a fragment-bearing row is non-conforming.

fragment, when present, MUST be a non-empty RFC 6901 JSON Pointer in URI-fragment representation starting with '#/'. If the pointer does not resolve within file, or a row that shares a file with another row omits fragment while that other row also omits fragment (ambiguous whole-document mapping), consumers MUST fail closed rather than silently pick a schema.

registry/service-kind-registry.json.description: Canonical service_kind vocabulary. A service_kind names one deployed wire role. This registry is the single source of valid values and per-context eligibility for Service Describe, Realm sync endpoints, Realm join candidates, ServiceRegistrationKey, and the MIMI provider directory. Consumers MUST derive their closed value space from active rows whose valid_in includes the applicable context.
registry_rules: A service_kind id matches [a-z][a-z0-9_]* and is lowercase snake_case. Only ids present as rows in this registry exist; only status=active rows are valid on wire.

Value spaces are NOT interchangeable. Each row declares valid_in, the set of contexts the id may legally appear in. A service_kind valid for Service Describe is not thereby valid as a Realm sync endpoint class or as a ServiceRegistrationKey component. Consumers MUST derive their enum from the rows whose valid_in contains that consumer's context, never from the full row list.

Schema enum values for every service_kind selector field MUST be generated from active rows filtered by valid_in; tools/lint_artifacts.py check_service_kind_registry asserts each declared JSON pointer.

service_registration_key is the most restrictive context: it admits only service types that are a standalone deployment owning a service DID under a canonical public base. Adding a row to this context means that service type can hold a service identity and appear in ak.root.identity.service_registration.* operations.

The registry is additive. New service types enter as new rows with their own valid_in set; existing wire values never change meaning. Widening an existing row's valid_in is a registry release, not an implementation decision.

service_kind is a role name, not a product name. Deployment or implementation identifiers (for example a binary called soland or starid) MUST NOT be registered. A single physical deployment MAY fill more than one role, but each ServiceDescribe document describes exactly one role. Co-located roles sharing a public binding are selected with GET /_arkret/describe?service_kind=<registered-id>; each response advertises only that role's exact supported_operations, profiles, authentication metadata, limits and plaintext visibility. Compound service_kind values are forbidden.
This registry governs service_kind selector fields, including the policy source_service_kind attribution field.

registry/signature-alg-registry.json.description: Canonical signature algorithm vocabulary and explicit per-standard mappings for v1 JOSE, Arkret raw signatures, and RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signatures.
registry_rules: A JWS protected header MUST use the standard JOSE member alg and its value MUST equal the active row's jose_algorithm. Arkret MUST NOT rename members inside a JOSE object.
An Arkret-owned raw-signature carrier MUST use signature_algorithm and its value MUST equal an active row's raw_signature_algorithm. It MUST NOT use the JOSE abbreviation alg as an Arkret field name.
An RFC 9421 Signature-Input alg parameter MUST use http_message_signature_algorithm. JOSE names such as ES256 are not HTTP Signature Algorithms registry names and MUST NOT be substituted.

Activating a reserved/new algorithm requires a new schema version and profile negotiation; registry activation MUST NOT expand an existing schema enum in place (zh/conformance/schema-registry.md §6.1 b.1).
Algorithms not present as active rows MUST fail closed with unsupported_signature_alg on critical proofs.

Every status=active row MUST declare kat_vector_id naming an active vector-registry entry; every status=reserved row MUST instead declare kat_absence_reason and MUST NOT declare kat_vector_id. tools/lint_artifacts.py enforces this binding.

A reserved hybrid row is a single negotiated verification policy over two independent proof entries, not a new unregistered compact signature encoding. Both components MUST bind the same canonical payload and proof purpose; accepting a stripped single component as hybrid-verified is forbidden.

algorithms.security_note: Classical Ed25519 default signature suite; not post-quantum.
Classical ECDSA P-256 suite for WebAuthn/FIDO2 and PKI interop.

NIST FIPS 204 ML-DSA category 3 suite for post-quantum hardening profiles. JOSE/JWK serialization follows RFC 9964: alg=ML-DSA-65, kty=AKP, required pub, optional private seed in priv, and empty ML-DSA context.

algorithms.kat_absence_reason: Reserved hybrid policy has no canonical proof-set ordering or anti-stripping KAT until all activation_requirements are complete.
activation_requirements: Publish canonical proof-set ordering and duplicate-component rejection rules
Publish anti-stripping vectors proving that both components bind identical canonical payload bytes and proof purpose and that either missing/invalid component fails hybrid verification
Define verifier capability tiers and downgrade display semantics without ever reporting a single-component result as hybrid verified
Publish a new negotiated proof contract release; reserved policy MUST NOT widen frozen JOSE or raw-signature enums in place
algorithms.security_note: Reserved hybrid verification policy. Before activation, the canonical_id itself is not a wire alg and MUST fail closed if presented as one; active Ed25519 and ML-DSA-65 proofs retain their independent existing semantics.

risk_tier_definitions.low: Read, projection, discovery, ack, and account-private affordances. Freshness fail-closed treats unknown / stale as local-pending allowed (capabilities.md §18).
risk_tier_definitions.medium: Object create / update / delete, message authoring, invite issuance, MLS proposal, audit query. Freshness requires recent frontier within freshness_required_ms.
risk_tier_definitions.high: Capability mutation, policy mutation, lifecycle freeze / tombstone / destroy, schema redefinition, MLS commit / welcome / genesis, audit export, moderation decision, admin / hierarchy / upgrade. Freshness MUST be within freshness_required_ms; partition forces local pending with no peer visibility.

registry_rules: Wire capability grant.actions[] entries MUST be drawn from this registry; wildcards / segment globs are statically rejected by capability-grant.schema.json.

Receivers MUST default to risk_tier=high when an action submitted in a grant or evaluated in policy is not present in this registry; this is the freshness fail-closed default required by capabilities.md §18.

required_constraints lists typed-constraint shorthand names that the capability evaluator MUST enforce for the action regardless of the grant author's declarations; absence in this list does NOT disable other declared constraints.

required_evaluator_checks lists non-grant-field invariants (for example actor_eq_target_author or audit_pair_required) that admission control MUST enforce from Event context, reducer state, or paired audit evidence. These are not grant-constraint schema fields.

target_event_kinds links the action to one or more ak.* event_kinds in event_kind_registry. Empty array means the action authorizes a read / projection / signaling path that does not produce a durable reducer-input event. Reducer admission for a listed event_kind MUST verify the actor holds at least one matching action grant.

profile is null for v1 core actions, or a ak.profile.*.v<n> id when the action is only meaningful inside that profile. Receivers without the named profile MUST treat the action as unknown (risk_tier=high default).

Every action MUST declare event_mapping_kind. action == single target_event_kind uses same_name; empty target_event_kinds uses non_event_surface; any other mapping MUST use one of the allowed deviation categories.

grant_authority_actions lists the action ids an issuer holding this action MAY sign a grant for (capabilities.md section 3.2 issuer upper bound). It is a separate namespace from target_event_kinds, which only expresses direct Event admission: several actions can map to one event kind, so an event-kind subset MUST NOT be used to satisfy an action-level grant authority question.

coverage_rule and grant_authority_rule declare how target_event_kinds and grant_authority_actions are derived from the other rows. When a rule is present the materialized list is a cached projection: tools/artifact_pipeline.py generate rewrites it and check rejects any hand edit on either this registry or the generated view.

root_control_only=true marks an action that only the current controller of the Realm authority-root cell may author. It is never grantable and never enters a derived owner authority set. subject_only=true marks a self-service action whose only authority is the target subject's own signature. reducer_only=true marks a record the reducer materializes and no principal may author. The three flags are orthogonal and combinable.

actions.notes: Authorizes the installed Applet service to invoke the closed Ghost Actor provisioning aggregate for one exact effective Realm scope. The operation accepts the caller-signed ak.identity.accountability_grant + ak.profile.create pair atomically; it is not a generic authorization for either Event kind.

Reducer-materialized record of a Realm-link inheritance derivation (zh/models/realm-links.md section 6). No principal authors it and no principal can be granted it, so it is excluded from every derived owner authority set.

Subject-only self-service release of the actor own grant. Authority comes from the target grant subject signature and the reducer target guard, never from a capability, so it is excluded from every derived authority set.

Read-only audit access for a Realm admin NOT in the target Circle. MUST be paired with ak.audit.accessed event. Does NOT yield historical decryption keys unless the admin is formally added to the Circle.

Creates an intra-Realm Circle (scoped event/message boundary; optionally MLS-backed depending on parent Realm floor). NOT in default member bundle by default — Circles should be few and stable. See zh/models/circle.md §8.
Manage an existing Circle. MUST be constrained to specific circle_id selectors; unconstrained Realm-wide grant is not a normal management permission.
Self-service: actor accepts an invite, joins a join_rule=open Circle, or leaves. Reducer enforces payload.actor_id == envelope.actor_id and transition legality. Self-unbanning MUST fail closed.
Cross-actor write (rare). MUST carry ak.audit.accessed pair (same model as ak.strand.watch.set.others).
Invite / remove others. Held by Circle admin. payload.actor_id != envelope.actor_id.

Authorizes only the transaction-bound old-series targets in a fixed SecurityRotationTransaction plan after both replacement active-series pointers are accepted. It never authorizes deleting an active or unplanned backup series.

Authorizes adding an audience_mention node such as @all or @here to a Message create/revise. @here maps to audience="strand_engaged" and is not presence-filtered. This is an additional gate: the actor MUST also be authorized for the underlying message create/revise action. Effective Realm/Circle policy MUST allow the audience and declare finite max_recipients/quota before notification fanout.

Authorizes a decrypted ak.message.stream Signal payload for one discussion Strand. It is an additional recipient-verified gate: the sender MUST also hold ak.message.create. The service cannot inspect or advertise the encrypted payload kind or Strand target.
Authorizes reading an object's discussion / history events (message timeline, redacted-message metainfo, prior revisions). Read / projection surface only; emits no durable reducer event.

Claims, renames or tombstones the Realm's human-readable alias (ak.realm.alias event; projects ak.component.realm.alias.v1). high risk because an alias is the address users type and share: capturing or re-pointing one is a phishing / impersonation primitive. Holding ak.realm.admin (aggregate admin coverage) satisfies admission, or grant this specific action directly. See zh/discovery/object-addressing.md §3.3.

Re-anchors the authority-root capability-action registry digest to a retrievable, recomputable, active snapshot. Changes neither controller nor generation and never retroactively widens an existing grant.
Advances the authority generation, invalidating every grant anchored to the previous one at read time. Destructive root control; never grantable.

Terminal Realm lifecycle. Authored only by the current controller of the Realm authority-root cell with an independent destructive confirmation; it MUST NOT be granted to anyone, so it is excluded from every derived owner authority set.

Highest explicit authority inside one Realm. Held either by the current controller of the ak.component.realm.authority_root.v1 cell (root authority, not a grant) or by an ordinary revocable co-owner grant. Both derived sets are rule-generated; hand edits are rejected by tools/artifact_pipeline.py check.

Rotates the controller binding of the Realm authority-root cell. Authored only by the current controller with successor acceptance; it MUST NOT be granted, so it is excluded from every derived owner authority set.

Sets / changes the Realm's authoritative default discussion Strand pointer (ak.realm.set_default_strand event; projects Realm default_strand_id). Same-name discipline. The Realm authz gate is realm-admin: holding ak.realm.admin (aggregate admin coverage) satisfies admission, or grant this specific action directly. Reducer MUST verify the referenced Strand already exists (failed_precondition otherwise). See zh/models/strand-and-message.md default-Strand discovery section.
Terminal Realm lifecycle with a successor pointer. Same root-control family as ak.realm.destroy: authored only by the current authority-root controller and never grantable.

Authorizes durable history-key delivery after the independent membership, device, history-sharing policy, source_authorization_ref, and recipient checks succeed. This explicit high-risk action is not implied by ak.realm.admin.

event_mapping_kind_definitions.same_name: Action maps one-to-one to an identically named durable event kind.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.non_event_surface: Action authorizes read/projection/signaling behavior that does not emit a durable reducer event.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.aggregate_admin: Action intentionally covers a bounded administrative family of event kinds.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.polymorphic_object: Action covers the same object-lifecycle verb across multiple object event kinds.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.scope_suffix_variant: Action adds actor/scope/role qualifiers while reducer admission targets a shared event kind.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.operation_verb: Action token names an operation/command verb that does not match its target event kind name(s); reducer admission resolves the resulting event kind(s) via target_event_kinds. Literal action matching per the actions[] rule applies; carries no aggregate-admin family semantics.

data_versions.precis: RFC 8264 derived-property tables at Unicode 6.3.0 plus RFC 8265 UsernameCaseMapped; mapping, normalization, and bidi tables at Unicode 17.0.0

registry/string-profile-registry.json.upgrade_rule: Changing Unicode, PRECIS, UTS #39, or UTS #46 data is a reviewed v1 artifact update. Existing canonical identifiers and signed bytes are never rewritten. UTS #39 upgrades rebuild authority-local derived collision indexes; newly assigned code points are rejected by receivers whose pinned profile does not yet recognize them.

profiles.name: arkret_human_identifier
profiles.canonical_equality: exact prepared Unicode code point sequence
profiles.authorization: may be uniquely indexed but is not a principal identifier
profiles.registration_collision: optional authority-local UTS #39 Highly Restrictive assessment and skeleton index; never canonical equality

profiles.name: arkret_external_string
profiles.canonical_equality: delegated to external standard, DID method, or provider profile
profiles.authorization: Arkret-wide NFKC or case folding is forbidden

registry_rules: track_names[] is the canonical source for every Strand.tracks map key; syntax alone never admits a name.
New writes MUST use an active row. Unknown, deprecated, duplicate, or owner-unresolvable names fail closed with schema_violation.
owner.kind=schema requires schema_ref to resolve to an effective reference registered by schema_registry; owner.kind=profile requires profile_id to resolve in conformance-profiles.json.
Profiles MAY add a TrackName only by adding an owned row here, regenerating track-name-registry.json, and updating the versioned Strand schema TrackName enum in the same protocol change.

track_names.description: Message and discussion timeline section of a Strand.
Authoritative structured and narrative synthesis section of a Strand.

registry/vector-registry.json.description: Canonical registry of conformance vector identifiers. Every ak.vector.* identifier referenced by prose or fixtures MUST appear here, and every row MUST point at the prose or fixture source that defines it.

vectors.description: Security sequences for registration-only human DID authority, PCR-instance anti-substitution, optional DID-root recovery, outage isolation and exact freshness call-site registration.

The Realm ak.realm.policy_bundle aad_visibility.event_id component is a disclosure ceiling over the encrypted-envelope aad_visibility_event_id discriminator: an equal or narrower envelope is accepted, a wider one is rejected with aad_visibility_policy_violation, and an absent component means the hidden ceiling rather than no constraint.
Personal blocklist whole-value CAS updates, target closure, shared-history receive-before-filter behavior, unblock projection rebuild and non-enumerable holder-side filtering.

Account Data keys are server-versioned compare-and-set registers: a stale byte-identical retry after a newer write is rejected with cas_conflict, concurrent delete/update elects exactly one winner, opposite arrival orders reach the same final state, the revision high-water mark survives tombstone GC so deleted values cannot be resurrected, and value_tombstone key patterns refuse physical delete.

The two registered typed-id account-data namespaces are closed: ak.views.private.<view_id> and ak.notifications.inbox.<notification_id> accept only a full typed id tail, reject the bare namespace instead of falling through to the permissive unregistered-key branch, refuse plaintext content, bind the decrypted private View to visibility=private and its own view_id while the shared ak.view.* surfaces reject visibility=private, close the inbox value to dismissed/archived with an HLC-then-device_id merge, and delete physically without allowing revival.
Account Authority evidence, PCR-scoped ak.account.status publication, idempotent pending-to-accepted operation state and bounded Principal Server fanout.

Actor Profile accountability admission is deterministic: every declared principal needs an active matching grant, any missing grant rejects the whole Event, and field-stripped acceptance is non-conformant.
Actor-chain sequence and sibling buckets are Realm-scoped; cross-Realm equal sequence values are independent, while same-Realm conflicting siblings fork and cross-Realm predecessor references fail.
Realm-scoped actor frontiers bind realm_id and actor_id, start at actor_seq 0, retain the complete sorted sibling head set, and hash the closed realm_actor transcript deterministically.
Byte-level MLS-Exporter KAT for arkret-aead-sender-nonce-prefix-v1, including the exact JCS context, AES-GCM prefix length, counter concatenation, and context-field negative mutations.

Controller-owned recovery_public_key backup of managed Agent PCR MLS state, canonical managed-principal binding across public/plaintext/AAD views, pairing recovery-readiness gate, and prohibition on Agent runtime private-key backup or per-Agent human mnemonic.
Managed-agent DID-to-PCR binding, controller delegated authoring attribution, control-fact placement, and rejection of non-PCR Realms at either principal control id.

Native Agent MLS KeyPackages bind exclusively to the current accepted ak.agent.key.authorize Event and its runtime signing key, never to a controller delegated-device authorization; stale, mixed, cross-principal, revoked, superseded, expired, or key-mismatched bindings fail closed.

Managed Agent bootstrap is constructed in one acyclic order: controller-signed PCR-independent DID entry 0 -> exact initial_resolution -> frozen genesis create -> realm_id=retype(event_id) -> accepted provision -> accepted PCR -> controller-signed create-locked DID entry 1. Covers awaiting_pcr_genesis and awaiting_did_binding invisibility, exact durable commitment comparison, activation only after entry 1, and rejection of same-batch submission, undeclared genesis, duplicate claim, service-chosen realm id, cross-server split or wrong DID update key/tuple.

Explicit two-step abandonment of an accepted ak.agent.provision whose managed Agent PCR genesis will never arrive: a single-use challenge pins the agent, slug, declared realm id and allocation, and one transaction consumes it, releases both claims and records exactly one tombstone. Covers slug reuse after release, the permanently unusable realm-id claim, replay returning one terminal outcome, and rejection without a challenge, with replayed credentials, after expiry, after consumption, and once the genesis is accepted.

Provision requested_scope is a required immutable global ceiling rather than a grant; narrower key scopes and Realm grants are accepted, while action/resource/mandatory-constraint widening fails closed and provisioning emits no Realm grant.

The public managed-Agent DID history contains only the requested_scope commitment digest; complete scope disclosure is controller-signed, verifier/audience/challenge-bound, short-window private evidence, and public-copy, mismatch, stale, wrong-audience, and replay variants fail closed.
Stable runtime key binding digest, same-binding idempotent retry, different-binding HTTP 409 conflict, and stale approval fail-closed behavior.

Executes the portable Agent signer evidence transcript across exact-request current admission, destination-receipted historical verification, three orthogonal lifecycle gates, canonical witnesses, MLS cross-binding and tamper cases.

High-risk agent session scope returns claim_required with closed details {reason_code=human_approval_required, approval_request_id}; controller approval is out of band and CAPTCHA, OTP, password, and browser challenges are forbidden on the runtime path.
Request-key canonical body conflict, scope binding, canonical_hash_input and 24-hour retention semantics.

Deterministic Applet registration_epoch recomputation from the closed normalized transcript, UTF-8 domain separator, JCS bytes, and SHA-256; covers set sorting and duplicate rejection, optional omission, DID method version evidence, and security-field rotation.

Caller-signed Applet revoke plan binding, durable pre-effect ledger bound to principal service and admin actor, exact replay, conflict rejection, non-skip partial outcomes, restart recovery, and first-accepted-event write fencing.

Applet transaction push source signature anchor: per-delivery RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signature covering method/target/authority/content-digest/source-service-id/destination-service-id/idempotency-key, source_signature_anchor persisted into the idempotency/replay record, duplicate body/anchor conflicts fail closed, and source service authentication does not replace Event actor/applet/capability checks.
Release requires an active binding, unexpired authorization, and accepted session head notice; suspended, revoked, expired, or wrong-stage inputs fail closed.
Audit binding is a closed control-plane FSM: active and suspended may transition as registered, revoked is terminal, and same-basis conflicting siblings produce Bottom.
Same-basis close dominates release, earlier accepted releases must be frozen in close release_refs, post-close releases fail, and ordered_log ordering is deterministic.
Release recipient actor and public key must exactly match authorization and resolve to the same authorized audit actor; substitution fails closed.
Release is bounded by binding activation, first_auditable_epoch, encryption-time eligibility, sealed epoch state, and sealed_by_commit_ref.
Release material output is gated on accepted release plus a profile-valid RYW receipt, matching policy digest, and independent witnesses where attested hardware is claimed.
Audit session stages follow the registered request-authorize-notice-close FSM, permit explicit early close, reject skipped stages, and make close terminal.
field_access.sensitive_fields read projection handling: redact/hash/omit remove original values, hash uses keyed/salted digest discipline, and unenforceable handling falls back to omit.
Closed SessionGrant issuance preimage, typed ID/JWT jti derivation, holder/recovery binding, canonical public-JWK normalization, durable exact replay, conflict and terminal outcomes.
Authority lease issuance, ordered batch delivery, exact idempotent refresh, founding anchor basis, stale/quorum failure and cache-clearing boundaries.

Executable closed WebSocket discovery and frame bytes, application-context DPoP KAT and replay binding, account/events/signal multiplex isolation, duplicate/unknown/oversize negatives, reauth, drain, close-code traces and mandatory HTTP fallback.

Streaming AEAD declared-bounds negatives (declared fields only, no multi-MiB payload materialised): segment_count above 2^20, segment_bytes below 1 KiB or above 8 MiB, and segment_count inconsistent with ceil(size_bytes / segment_bytes) MUST all be rejected fail-closed (schema_violation, reason_code segment_bounds_invalid) before key derivation or any segment download.
Streaming AEAD ordering: out-of-order / skipped / gapped segment_index MUST be rejected with segment_sequence_invalid; a repeated segment_index MUST be rejected with segment_replay.

Streaming chunked AEAD (ak.blob.stream_aead.v1) happy path: multi-segment plaintext with a short final segment is split, per-segment AEAD encrypted, segment-wise downloaded and incrementally verified, and the top-level ciphertext_digest is recomputed and matches per media-and-blob.md section 3.3.

Streaming AEAD scheme closure: an unknown attachment scheme MUST fail closed with unsupported_attachment_scheme (no fallback decrypt); an envelope carrying both whole-file nonce and chunked nonce_prefix/segment_* fields MUST fail blob.schema.json encrypted_attachment oneOf validation.

Streaming AEAD truncation: a dropped final segment, a last segment whose flag stays 0x00, or segment_count exhausted without last_segment_flag=0x01 MUST be rejected with segment_stream_truncated and buffered plaintext discarded.

calendar.attendees is the single canonical roster: actor ids are unique, the omitted role defaults to required, at most one organizer exists, and roster membership creates no Realm or Circle membership and widens no history access.

One schedule patch derives exactly one notification per receiver over the pre/post roster union filtered by post-state access, mute, DND and push rules; encrypted schedules only produce the profile-defined blind wakeup; RSVP changes derive no schedule notification.

Calendar Strands activate exactly one way: Strand.schema_refs carries ak.schema.calendar_event.v1 and metadata.fields.calendar co-occurs in both directions on the post-patch object, the container self-schema is refused in schema_refs, legacy flat schedule fields and metadata.fields.profile/profile_refs impostors are refused, and writes bind the schema in requirements.schema[].

Nonexistent and ambiguous local times both resolve with the offset in effect before the transition, so a fixed local meeting time does not drift across a DST boundary and the overlap emits exactly one occurrence.

RFC 8984 subset defaults, base start as the first occurrence counted against count, implicit inheritance of base time and weekday components, count/until typing and exclusivity, by_* companion preconditions, and the paginated expansion with its candidate-period scan budget and revision-bound continuation.
Excluded recurrence rules, recurrence overrides, RDATE/EXDATE, per-instance reschedule or cancellation, and the JSCalendar @type discriminator all fail closed instead of being silently ignored.

RSVP admission is capability-based rather than attendee-based, refuses cancelled events, and layers basis checks so that e2ee and plaintext Realms accept the identical canonical set: shape admission rejects without resolving anything, target admission reads only the referenced Events plaintext envelope and pends on dependency_missing, and basis validity is projection-only. It also fails closed above the 128-entry frontier bound and keeps missing, invisible, cross-Realm and non-calendar targets externally indistinguishable.

RSVP derives a typed composite subject from payload event_ref, nullable occurrence, and the explicitly sourced envelope actor_id; causal successors dominate while concurrent mv_register heads remain exposed independently of HLC.

Instance heads override series fallback without unioning them into a false conflict, causal successors dominate independently of arrival order and HLC, missing keys project encrypted_unresolved instead of a fabricated status, and equal decrypted plaintext is not a conflict merely because ciphertexts differ.
RSVP occurrence key canonicalizes recurrence instance local wall-clock start in the event timezone.

The RSVP response branch follows the effective scope encryption floor: plaintext is refused under an e2ee floor, permitted only with the declared rsvp_response data class otherwise, never silently downgraded, and the routing-visible metadata set is disclosed explicitly.

ak.rsvp.set declares one deterministic reducer projection, set(payload.entry): an implementation that omits the registered write, projects an extra target, or derives a value different from the canonical payload entry fails conformance. Those writes are reducer-local output and never producer-selected Event fields.

Identity-affecting schedule edits orphan instance RSVPs and mark series RSVPs needs_reconfirmation, non-calendar updates are not schedule revisions, divergent concurrent heads block RSVP until a resolution Event, and byte-identical concurrent heads settle without picking a winner.

all_day selects the date branch and its negation the whole-second LocalDateTime branch for start, end and recurrence.until; intervals are half-open so end is strictly later than start; UTC timestamps, offsets, bracketed zones and fractional seconds are refused.

Producers canonicalize Link aliases to the canonical Zone before signing, receivers refuse non-canonical signed zones, a schedule-signed tzdb_version outside the executable set fails closed, and a release bump may move derived instants without changing the signed timezone or any local occurrence key.
Same-basis sibling transitions to different states return fsm bottom instead of selecting a winner.
Accepts the three legal first call states and rejects active or terminal first states.
Moderator kick/ban requires ak.call.moderate (call_moderation_unauthorised otherwise); the call moderation effective OR-Set gates token re-issue with call_participant_removed.

P2P calls converge to SFU when participants exceed two, reusing the oldest_membership no-vote session_focus election; mode does not auto-downgrade, and ak.call.summary is gated on a terminal call state (call_summary_invalid otherwise).

Recording ready results MUST carry ak.schema.call_recording_artifact.v1 metadata bound to the recording start event, Arkret blob pipeline, recording exporter label/context, retention policy, deletion audit trigger, and erasure receipt.

Recording retention: audit_lock blocks deletion (legal_hold_active) regardless of retention_expires_at, and ak.call.recording.start cannot enter a capturing state without an atomically persisted consent_confirmed result.
Same-basis replay of the same from/to transition is idempotent and does not create a divergent head.
Terminal call states reject every attempted outgoing transition with call_state_terminal.

Transcription requires ak.call.transcribe (transcription_denied otherwise), and transcript artifacts MUST use the ak.rtc-transcript-key/v1 exporter label with a dedicated Context (transcription_artifact_pipeline_bypassed otherwise).
Covers every legal call lifecycle transition and representative non-terminal illegal transitions.
Profile-declared non-event grant authority permits only exact Realm-admin-to-active-bridge-registration ak.applet.ghost.provision grants and rejects owner shortcuts or binding drift.

Multi-parent authority audit materialization derives maximum depth plus canonical sorted and deduplicated root identities; missing parents remain dependency-pending and independent reducers produce the same state-root input.

A multi-level authority chain built from one grant shape: each grant records the grant it was issued under in issuer_authority_refs, and revoking an ancestor invalidates its descendants at read time without any cascading write.
Delegation cycle rejection across direct, multi-hop, revoke/redelegate and atomic batch variants.
A fixed authority expiry seal prevents rolling renewal and stops a re-granted authority from widening the window of the refs that cover it.

Grant-ref liveness follows upstream revocation without cascade writes, root refs survive controller transfer but fail after generation reset, and root-control terminal events reject ordinary grant-based authorization.
Reducer-only ak.capability.derived follows the unified issuer-authority rules while retaining Realm-link inheritance behavior and remaining unauthorable by principals.
Direct Conversation participant authority is a profile-scoped non-grant source, survives root generation changes, requires the pair's unique immutable binding, and cannot issue child grants.
Risk-tier freshness matrix fails closed and keeps unknown low-risk pending outcomes local.
Global cross-grant decision merge prevents any allow from bypassing deny, quarantine or review.
Issuer effective-authority and freshness-unknown fail-closed checks for first-issued grants.
Static depends_on_moderation_state requirement rejects missing or false declarations.

Subject-only relinquish needs no revoke grant, rejects non-subjects and root-cell targets, and both revoke and relinquish stay dependency-pending without prewriting tombstones when the target grant is unresolved.

The unified grant form preserves depth, expiry-seal, cycle and constraint inheritance, permits unbounded low/medium-risk multi-hop agent grants, and requires finite expiry for high-risk agent or service grants.
Effective grant validity-window intersection rejects empty windows.
External authority authority Ack issuance, canonical receipt-set assembly, common-window calculation, threshold deduplication, exact replay and decision-chain binding.
Control Proposal Ack deadlines, at most two immutable-horizon signed defers, decision-overdue evidence, and acceptance of a later cryptographically valid Seal.
Realm proposal decision windows are ordered and realizable: decision <= absolute, equality is accepted only with zero defers, and invalid configurations fail before any Realm state write.
cas_register writes on non-initial state require an explicit CBA basis: Control Move preconditions or equivalent DataEvent causal/lattice proof; null-basis blind overwrites fail closed.
bottom=reject control cell recovery accepts only a sealed conflict-recovery Move with valid recovery_capability and pre-conflict state_witness; negative cases pin recovery_witness_* reasons.
open_set concurrent revocation is evaluated against the joined control view; revoked or bottom authorization cells fail closed without a freshness window.
Seal canonical bytes exclude id and notary_signature; verifier recomputes the typed id and signature payload digest from signed top-level fields only.
directory_visibility=realm_members exposes only the Realm-member preview field set and gives non-Realm callers the same locked stub/timing bucket as members-only circles.

Circle lifecycle is evaluated at the Event CBA basis; linear archive uses the revocation freshness window, tombstone and concurrent archive fail closed immediately, and restore never rehabilitates a pre-archive basis.

Hard quota counters use one logical linearizable authority across every service node: a race for the last slot cannot overshoot, idempotent retries count once, unavailable authority fails closed, and calendar-month periods are rejected.

Temporal action gates are neutral for unrelated actions according to effect, while edit/redact windows use the verified target created_at and the fixed verification time/skew to accept inside the deadline and fail closed outside or on missing target time.

Authority-surface coverage for ak.authority.direct_conversation_repair.v1, whose action_allowlist is exactly ak.member.rejoin.own. A self leave -> join ak.member.state under the repair source matches that action and reports it as the matched authority source; joining on behalf of the other participant, carrying a first join, admitting a third participant, presenting ak.member.leave.own under the repair source (daily self-leave belongs to the participant authority) and running rejoin.own backwards as join -> leave all fail closed. Behavioural rejoin vectors that never name the action or the authority source would stay green with an empty allowlist and therefore do not cover this.

The ak.self.contact.read.list projection carries the closed next_prepare_input successor cursor: an accepted row MUST carry it and the five non-authorable contact_state values MUST NOT, its basis_id, version and predecessor_event_ref are copied verbatim into the scope_update and tombstone prepare phases, version is the next Event's version and predecessor_event_ref is the current lineage head rather than that head's predecessor, and a stale cursor is refused with contact_lineage_conflict or contact_scope_stale and MUST be re-read rather than guessed or retried unchanged.

The ak.self.contact.read.list projection carries the complete signed request_receipt on a pending_incoming row, so respond and reject become authorable: the field name is byte-identical to the prepare field that consumes it, it is copied verbatim and never narrowed to a reference, and because it is signed by the peer's source service rather than by the holder's own server the client verifies it independently instead of trusting its server's retelling. pending_outgoing, accepted, rejected, expired and tombstoned rows MUST NOT carry it, a glare pair is structurally never pending_incoming so respond and reject stay forbidden without a new code, and a consumed receipt is refused by prepare with zero writes and MUST be re-read rather than cached or replayed.
KeyPackage upload, entry upload, consume, and revoke signatures use one byte-exact operation-id domain plus typed unsigned-request JCS transcript shared by ordinary devices and Native Agent runtimes.

accepted_device pairing signs a closed target-owned possession attestation under ak.device-authorize-accepted-device-possession-proof-v1 whose only replay boundary is the pairing challenge transcript digest: the approving device and the Account Authority each rebuild it independently, it is the sole authority for hpke_key and algorithms, short-link and to-device share one schema and one domain, transcripts never cross between root_anchored and accepted_device, and the target device fails closed before local assembly when the accepted Event does not match its attestation or the expected principal_id.

document_digest is sha256:lowercase_hex(SHA-256(RFC8785_JCS(normalized DID Document projection))): any raw JSON property reordering keeps the digest identical, changing any controller / verification relationship / service / security-relevant extension property necessarily changes it, and raw response bytes are never carried in document_digest (they use raw_document_digest).

evidence_digest is recomputable from the retained canonical evidence receipt (ak.did.binding_evidence.v1): a proofless method degrades to an empty method_proofs array rather than a placeholder, webvh witness rows are sorted by witness_did with duplicates rejected, any method evidence change changes the digest, and unknown method or proof kinds fail closed.

policy_digest is recomputable from the retained canonical resolver policy snapshot (ak.did.resolver_policy.v1): required core dimensions (accepted_did_methods, fail_mode, trust_roots) plus the profile-closed profile_policy, registered wire tokens only (language-native debug renderings rejected), and flipping any security-relevant field necessarily changes the digest while unknown profiles or fields fail closed.

Byte-exact KAT for the receiver-derived off-wire Direct Conversation binding digest: fixed v1 domain separator, closed normalized binding object, unordered participant and authorization-ref normalization, created_at and Event-context exclusion, and semantic-field mutation separation.

Registering an external Organization DID separates resolution, control verification, local registration, Realm relationship and service delegation; being resolvable or referenceable yields no local administrative authority. prepare/ensure is two-phase by decision: the registry issues and remembers a single-use challenge bound to purpose, audience, origin, trust domain, nonce, local_admin_subject and a window of at most 300 seconds, and the control proof binds that beneficiary to block redirection. Challenge consumption atomically records the canonical request digest and outcome, so only a byte-identical retry is idempotent; the same challenge under a different digest fails closed. proof_kind is a closed two-member discriminator over mature DIDs, witness attestation is never a governance quorum, requested scopes MUST match the challenge, and quorum proofs MUST meet the declared threshold. registration_generation reconciles idempotency with terminal revocation: replacement atomically terminates the old current generation and advances a monotonic current pointer, so an old receipt cannot authorize after supersession. Status is the closed triple active/stale/revoked with rotation mapping to stale and DID deactivation forcing revoked, and revoked is terminal against refresh.

Root-committed FoundingDeviceDescriptor, device possession, one-way authorize payload digest binding, ordered atomic create-once PCR genesis unit, extended identity creation transcript, exact replay and mutation rejection.

Failure-indistinguishability vector covering both the third-party claim endpoint and the invite-locator resolve endpoint; each endpoint's failure classes MUST share one external response shape and bounded timing distribution.

Last-resort KeyPackage Realm affinity, optionality, and profile gating: cross-intended_realm_id reuse MUST be rejected with last_resort_realm_affinity_violation; a server not declaring the feature MUST fail closed on an empty pool and MUST NOT return a last_resort package, with explicit last-resort fallback returning last_resort_not_supported; high_security_organization and sovereign_deployment Realms MUST treat last-resort as forbidden even when the service supports the feature.

Last-resort KeyPackage (ak.feature.mls_last_resort_keypackage.v1): when the normal pool is empty, claim MAY return last_resort=true; the package is reused across multiple Welcomes within the same intended_realm_id, consume is idempotent (stays published, never keypackage_already_consumed), and each consumption emits an append-only audit record per encryption-and-audit.md section 2.6.2.

Last-resort KeyPackage forced rotation: on next online the holder MUST publish fresh init key material, transition the old package to revoked with revocation_reason=keypackage_rotated, and trigger an MLS self-update Commit on every group joined via it to advance the epoch and close the forward-secrecy weakening window.

Cross-Principal-Server KeyPackage claim linearization and uncertain-outcome recovery: claim CAS, request ledger and serialized result commit atomically; same source/id/digest replays byte-identically; another digest conflicts without a second claim; query recovers the original outcome.

Peer KeyPackage claim requires both a participant signature bound to the exact request/service destination and the source-service HTTP Message Signature. Destination authority, both directional Contact heads/scopes, capability, freshness and Direct Conversation no-last-resort gates fail closed behind one claim_failed surface without inventory leakage; Consent is not queried.

cas_register join is the pure maximal-chain function over set ops carrying from: a sequential governance lifecycle (declaration -> whole-value head_eq tombstone -> re-declaration) joins to the single terminal value instead of bottom; two ops with the same from and different values form two maximal chains and join to bottom; a non-initial op whose from matches no covered value is a dangling supersession and fails closed to bottom; duplicate (value, from) sets are idempotent; supersession binds by value, so ABA reuse is the documented value-CAS semantic and families needing generational distinction embed a monotonic component in the value.
counter join/validate_op convergence for the same CBA Event set.

mv_register join/validate_op convergence for the same CBA Event set.

Blind-index stale postings after revocation, visibility tightening, redaction, expiry, or epoch rotation MUST not produce unauthorized recall.
Search hit is not an authorization proof; unauthorized or unverifiable hits return non-enumerating stubs.
Directory search, privacy-preserving search, and bridge interop surfaces stay separated and do not leak private plaintext.
Recovery A/B and SecurityRotation crash, response-loss, restart, exact/conflicting replay, staged-secret loss, terminal replay and multi-backup-kind erase ordering.

FLOW-GAP-015 closure for target-signed planned service-route handover and Realm-scoped mirror recovery: exact current basis and time ordering, cancellation continuity, no notice-authorized business traffic, same-core formal successor validation, durable publish acknowledgement and replay conflict, bounded visibility-blinded resolve, fork quarantine, durable anti-rollback floor with replaceable TTL cache, delivery-binding rebind boundary, and bilateral cross-ack cutover.

Production current-v1 protected endpoints MUST reject bare Authorization: Bearer unless it is bound by DPoP, an RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signature, detached JWS, mTLS, or equivalent sender-constrained proof; high-security profiles additionally require RFC 9421 PoP for every protected ak.self.* operation; a PoP signature whose created/expires falls outside the replay window MUST be rejected.
A DPoP/RFC 9421 grant-binding session key must not reuse bytes, fingerprints, thumbprints, or key identifiers from the long-term device identity key; reuse fails closed.

DPoP htu binds scheme, authority, and path: cross-authority/scheme reuse, untrusted forwarding headers, and missing authority are rejected; only a configured trusted proxy with scrubbed headers may reconstruct the external URI.

Sender-constrained session PoP: a write request with a valid RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signature (kid = current grant session_public_key, covering @method/@target-uri/@authority/content-digest) is accepted; a signature whose transcript mismatches the method/path/body digest fails verification and is rejected per api-conventions.md section 3.2 and service-http-binding.md section 2.5.
Runtime producer and controller consumer bind exchange identity only to the accepted request Event id and reject message, local-intent and unaccepted identities.
Same-sequence request and control siblings choose the bytewise maximum canonical accepted Event envelope digest, never Event id, HLC, arrival or database order.
Controller-only complete pagination and structural Event pairing recover private Sidecar context locators without adding a disclosure endpoint.

Explicit response closed loop with runtime addressed/self eligibility and restart dedupe gates, coordinator completion policy, causal request refs, controller validation, fail-closed non-echo handling, and controller-authored durable close control.

Containment: plaintext or shared-scope occurrences of exchange binding/control schema ids or exchange_id are hard rejects/invalid; publish output, Account Data, and public/shared surfaces carry no exchange material.

Event-fold and local-cache recovery: rebuild from accepted private history, causal folded-frontier validation, no Account Data merge, controller control ordering/sibling resolution, terminal absorption, reassignment, action-by-response-set mapping, and projection schema state invariants.
Only explicit controller confirmation creates one allowlisted ordinary shared Event, with zero private identifiers, history or locators.
Chrome and Edge execute the hosted multi-track, multi-mode, multi-device, multi-Agent and responsive UI matrix with preserved state and incremental switching evidence.
Every shared list, expansion, activity, export, URL, log and telemetry surface discloses no Sidecar locator, identity, content or fold input.
Accepted Agent revoke, pause or deactivate immediately stops new delivery, execution and writes without implicitly terminating exchanges.
Incomparable device histories require complete backfill and union refold with maximal causal heads and a digest over all contributing Event ids.

Signal verification uses two independent state domains: seal_ref selects only the Realm/scope authorization basis, while device authorization resolves against each verifier's current accepted device directory. A device authorized after seal_ref but currently active passes the device check; a device active at seal_ref but currently revoked/fenced/conflicted is rejected; a verification_method whose full value is not byte-identical to sender_actor_id#sender_device_id is rejected; a missing current directory key or missing Tier-2/service-attested trust anchor is rejected; a currently active device whose sender lacks scope send eligibility or the signal_class action under the Realm seal_ref is rejected.

Byte-level ak.history-v1 -> ak.signal-v1 ExpandWithLabel KAT for per-sender-device SignalEnvelope AEAD keys, including JCS({sender_device_id}), distinct valid-device keys under a forced equal nonce, and label/context/device/epoch negative mutations.
Encrypted Message preview keyframe/delta/abort state machine, identity derivation, attempt fork handling, resource limits, and direct final binding.

Signal payload_sequence is a durable per-device/per-canonical-scope u64 high-water: forward gaps from reservation/crash/failure are accepted, repeat or rollback is stale, exact envelope replay is diagnosed separately, and scopes remain independent.

High-assurance snapshot inclusion-challenge sampling verifies sufficient event_id and actor_seq_range coverage, recomputes the RFC 6962 domain-separated event-set Merkle root (0x00 leaf / 0x01 node), rejects the legacy unprefixed root, rejects commitment-root mismatch, and rejects silent actor sequence gaps.
Canonical filter/query-scope cursor binding and cross-scope replay rejection.
Opaque delivery ack token, monotonic cumulative acknowledgement, binding rejection and lost escalation.

Client events.query backfill with include_completeness=true detects withheld actor branches via ak.attestation.range_completeness verification; feature-less servers ignore the parameter; single_source attestation does not satisfy high-assurance realms.
Deterministic limited-timeline window-start state basis with safe omission on unresolved bases.

Account and events NDJSON stream trace conformance: catchup completion ordering, cursor-bearing frame closure, dropped-versus-resync branching, and reconnect position advancement are evaluated over complete traces rather than isolated frame schemas.

DeviceMessageEnvelope requires a sender-assigned message_id; unacknowledged byte-identical redelivery executes durable handler effects once, conflicting reuse fails with duplicate_conflict/message_id_conflict, and distinct ids remain distinct logical messages.

reports/event-reference-field-inventory..description: Complete schema-property inventory for Event ID/ref/digest fields. EventId is itself the complete suite-tagged cryptographic identity; no companion-digest wrapper or truncated identity class exists. External protocol event identifiers are classified separately and never enter the Arkret EventId value space.

reports/property-presence-manifest.json.description: Per-property wire presence contract derived from the schema documents. required, nullable and default are independent axes; presence_class is their normative combination. An SDK MUST reproduce the class exactly: a tristate property needs an explicit SDK disposition: the protocol-wide default normalizes absent/null, conditional requiredness is enforced by the Draft runtime, and only x-arkret-presence-semantics=distinct requires Missing / Null / Value. Repeated conditional schema occurrences are also grouped into semantic audit targets by shape and instance path so SDK audits do not count the same DTO field multiple times.

presence_class_definitions.required: must be present and never null.
presence_class_definitions.required_nullable: must be present and may be null; absent and null are different wire facts.
presence_class_definitions.tristate: optional, nullable, no default; absent, explicit null and a value are three accepted wire spellings whose semantics require a disposition.
presence_class_definitions.optional_defaulted: optional with a schema default; omission means the default.

sdk_disposition_definitions.distinct: business semantics distinguish Missing / Null / Value; SDK must preserve all three.
sdk_disposition_definitions.condition_guarded: missing is invalid in an applicable conditional branch and is enforced before typed decoding.
sdk_disposition_definitions.absent_null_equivalent: v1 default normalization; SDK uses an optional value and canonical output omits None.

reports/schema-consumer-coverage.json.description: Per-logical-schema consumer coverage. A schema that only compiles has no proven wire consumer; this report separates operation request/response binding, admitted Event contracts, structural $ref use and conformance vector coverage so an unused schema cannot hide behind a startup compile.

consumer_definitions.inbound: bound as an operation request body, or an admitted Event envelope/payload contract.
consumer_definitions.outbound: bound as an operation response body.
consumer_definitions.schema_reference: referenced by another schema document, so it is a structural component; local self-reference is not a consumer.
consumer_definitions.event_kind: bound by the Event kind registry, so a durable Event selects it by kind.
consumer_definitions.declared_wire: explicit machine-readable runtime, dynamic, nested-value or alias binding declared by the canonical schema registry.
consumer_definitions.prose_only: explicitly declared as having no whole-object v1 wire admission surface.
consumer_definitions.vectors: required by a conformance profile or vector group, or referenced by a fixture.
consumer_definitions.prose: named by the normative text, which is where a runtime-dispatched contract is defined.
consumer_definitions.startup_compile: a schema registry row, compiled by the startup catalog gate.

binding_kind_definitions.exact: the reference targets this logical schema itself.
binding_kind_definitions.fragment: the reference targets a $defs fragment of the same document.
binding_kind_definitions.registered: the schema ID appears in the Event kind registry.
binding_kind_definitions.required_schema: listed in a conformance profile or vector group required_schemas.
binding_kind_definitions.fixture: the schema ID appears in a conformance fixture.
binding_kind_definitions.normative_text: the schema ID appears in the normative prose.
binding_kind_definitions.declared: the canonical schema registry carries an explicit disposition.

vector_coverage_disposition_definitions.direct: named by a conformance profile/vector group or fixture.
vector_coverage_disposition_definitions.operation_e2e_owned: the logical schema is an operation catalog/DTO whose instance cases belong to the listed request/response E2E owners.
vector_coverage_disposition_definitions.composed_schema_owned: the schema is only admitted inside the listed higher-level logical schemas.
vector_coverage_disposition_definitions.event_envelope_owned: the payload is selected by Event kind and is covered only inside signed Event admission.
vector_coverage_disposition_definitions.runtime_dispatch_owned: the schema is selected by an explicit dynamic/runtime binding in the canonical schema registry.
vector_coverage_disposition_definitions.no_v1_wire_instance: the canonical registry explicitly declares that v1 has no whole-object wire instance.
vector_coverage_disposition_definitions.unresolved: no direct vector or reviewed higher-level coverage owner has been identified; this is a release blocker.

schemas/account-data-encrypted-value.sch.title: Arkret Account Data Encrypted Value
schemas/account-data-encrypted-value.sch.description: Principal-private Account Data value sealed client-side. Services validate and store this envelope but never receive the account secret or plaintext.

schemas/account-data-operations.schema.j.title: Arkret Account Data Self-Management Operation DTOs
schemas/account-data-operations.schema.j.description: Closed request/response DTOs for the self-surface actor-private account_data operations (ak.self.account_data.*). PUT builds a ak.account_data.set actor-private write; the server stores content verbatim (clients own canonical encoding and, for sensitive keys, client-side encryption). Every key is a server-versioned compare-and-set whole-value register: writes carry expected_revision and the accepted revision is expected_revision + 1, so concurrent multi-device writes converge instead of silently overwriting each other. See spec/v1/zh/models/account-data.md §5. account_data_key keys are dot-delimited namespaces validated against account-data-key-registry.json.

account_data_key.description: Dot-delimited account_data namespace key (e.g. ak.contacts.realm.<realm_id>, ak.account.blocklist). Control chars / whitespace / path separators are forbidden so the key is URL- and log-safe.

revision.description: Monotonic per-key revision counter. 0 means the key has never been written. Each accepted write or delete stores expected_revision + 1. The counter is a high-water mark: it MUST NOT go backwards, not even after a tombstone is garbage-collected, so a stale offline write can never resurrect a superseded value.
Revision of this stored value. Pass it back as expected_revision to replace or delete the entry.

content.description: Caller-supplied opaque payload, stored verbatim. Any JSON value.

account_data_replace_request_body.description: Carries the caller-signed ak.account_data.set Event and nothing else. The actor-private cell subject is composite[envelope.actor_id, payload.key], so the subject *is* the owner: the Event MUST be signed by the holder and the service MUST NOT author it under its own DID. key, expected_revision, and body / encrypted_payload live exclusively in set_event.event.payload and MUST NOT appear at the request top level. A tombstone payload is rejected here: erasure goes through ak.self.account_data.resource.delete, which enforces the registered deletion_mode.

account_data_delete_request_body.description: Carries the caller-signed tombstone ak.account_data.set Event and nothing else. Same subject rule as the replace body: composite[envelope.actor_id, payload.key] makes the holder the only legal signer. expected_revision is the payload's, not a query parameter -- one CAS precondition, one place. deletion_mode=value_tombstone keys MUST still be refused on this endpoint.

revision.description: Revision of the stored tombstone (expected_revision + 1). Recreating the key requires this value as the next expected_revision.

account_data_cas_conflict_details.description: Closed error.details payload for cas_conflict and not_found on ak.self.account_data.resource.*. It always carries the current revision so the caller can decrypt, re-apply its domain merge rule and issue exactly one new compare-and-set write without a second round trip.

current_entry.description: Present only when the key currently holds a live value. Omitted when the key is unset or holds a tombstone; current_revision is still authoritative in that case.

schemas/account-operations.schema.json.title: Arkret Account Operation DTOs
schemas/account-operations.schema.json.description: Closed request and response DTOs for account self-service operations, service-authenticated Account Authority PCR authoring basis discovery, and Account Authority to Principal Server account-status publication.

account_subject.description: Deployment-local, non-reversible stable account subject: SHA-256 over utf8('ak.account-subject.v1\n') followed by RFC 8785 JCS of {account_authority_id, service_account_id}. It binds one authenticated service account into the identity-root transcript without disclosing the raw local account id.

dpop_jkt.description: RFC 7638 SHA-256 JWK thumbprint of the holder key, encoded base64url without padding.

handle_claim_ref.description: Opaque reference to a signed ak.schema.handle_claim.v1 claim, such as an event ref, issuer-local receipt ref, or content-addressed artifact ref.

audience.description: Stable target-service authorization identity. A complete service DID used for signature verification is supplied separately and MUST project to this did_core_id.

expires_at.description: Lease expiry. Issued lifetime MUST be no greater than 15 minutes; 15 minutes is also the v1 default.

account_registration_control_proof.description: Closed control proof for binding an already-published full_id to principal_id through account register. OIDC, passkey, or agent authentication alone is insufficient to establish DID control. The Account Authority resolves full_id at high freshness, requires project(full_id)=principal_id, and selects the current active update key of the entry pinned by did_version_id from verified method history rather than from request-supplied key material. The signature covers every field except signature as canonical JSON with domain separator ak.account-registration-control-proof-v1 and MUST replay the durable challenge issued by ak.gate.account.command.issue_did_binding_challenge.

request_canonical_digest.description: SHA-256 over RFC 8785 JCS of the complete account_register_request_body with proof.request_canonical_digest and proof.signature omitted.

account_subject.description: Service account subject this identity is being bound to. Signed so the proof cannot be replayed to bind the same identity to a different account.

principal_id.description: Stable did_core_id echoed by the challenge and equal to project(full_id).

full_id.description: Complete DID resolved by the Account Authority and signed by the holder; it MUST equal the register request full_id byte-for-byte.

did_version_id.description: Adapter-defined versionId of the entry whose current active update key signed this proof.

control_key_digest.description: SHA-256 over the canonical multikey bytes of the verified current active update key.

dpop_jkt.description: DPoP holder thumbprint echoed by the durable challenge.

expires_at.description: Issued lifetime MUST be no greater than 300 seconds.

verification_method.description: Current active update-key DID URL under full_id. The verifier parses its bare DID component with the registered adapter and requires the projected did_core_id to equal principal_id; it never appends a fragment to principal_id.

witness_evidence.description: Method-native witness / freshness evidence digest for the external DID, required by deployments that do not host the DID themselves.

account_handoff_authentication_proof.description: OIDC authorization-code exchange proof used only to create a DPoP-bound account handoff. The signature is made by the same Ed25519 holder key as the request DPoP proof over utf8('ak.account-handoff-authentication-proof-v1\n') || RFC8785_JCS(this object with signature omitted).

challenge.description: Account Authority-generated challenge persisted with the OIDC authorization transaction and consumed by this exchange.

request_canonical_digest.description: sha256:<lowercase-hex> of SHA-256 over RFC 8785 JCS bytes of the complete account_handoff_request_body with proof.request_canonical_digest and proof.signature omitted.

signature.description: 64-byte Ed25519 signature encoded base64url without padding.

reserved_identity_creation.description: Server-persisted identity-creation checkpoint, readable only by the authenticated current holder of the owning service account's identity-creation lease. It is NOT public: an unfinished reservation would otherwise leak that a specific account is mid-registration, and abandoning it would leave a permanent public trace. Once registration completes the public artifact is the published DID log entry itself, so this checkpoint never needs to become public. It contains the exact unpublished or already-published DID operation, never recovery words, seed material, private keys, or an encrypted root export.

operation_digest.description: sha256:<lowercase-hex> of SHA-256 over RFC 8785 JCS bytes of the complete did_operation object.

state.description: Account-Authority-authored durable identity-creation saga state. Clients MUST derive their onboarding phase from this value and MUST NOT infer a phase from local checkpoint presence. reserved_identity MUST be absent only in active and present in every later state.

expires_at.description: Lease expiry. Issued lifetime MUST be no greater than 15 minutes; 15 minutes is also the v1 default.

reserved_identity.description: Holder-authenticated identity-creation checkpoint carried while a reservation exists. It MUST be omitted once the provisional identity has been explicitly abandoned through ak.gate.account.command.abandon_identity_creation: after abandonment the checkpoint MUST NOT remain readable on this or any other holder-readable surface, because leaving it would keep publishing that some account once tried to create an identity. That is a security property, not a cleanup policy.

expires_at.description: Expiry of the conflicting live identity-creation lease. The client uses this authenticated upper bound for waiting UI; it conveys no holder identity or authority.

account_handle.description: Canonical handle of the authenticated service account. This unsigned UX hint is only for display and local artifact naming; it MUST NOT be treated as principal identity evidence, authorization, or a service-account-to-principal binding.

account_subject.description: Stable subject for the authenticated service account. The client freezes this value from the DPoP-bound handoff and MUST require the identity-binding challenge to echo it byte-for-byte before signing.

preferred_locale.description: Optional private UI-language preference of the authenticated service account. It is returned only in this DPoP-bound handoff response so the client can continue the just-completed authentication flow in the selected language; it MUST NOT be copied into a public actor profile.

account_handoff_grant.description: Opaque, short-lived credential bound to the request DPoP key. It is not ak.session.grant and has no refresh-token semantics.

allowed_operations.description: Closed set of operations this handoff may be presented at. The two abandonment operations are members because a never-accepted PCR leaves the holder without a principal, so no principal-bound ak.session.grant can carry them; membership here does not widen the handoff into a session credential.

requires_fresh_authentication.description: Authoritative Account Authority decision. true means the current handoff is the challenge-issuing handoff and confirmation requires a new authentication; clients MUST NOT infer this by comparing locally persisted credentials.

full_id.description: Complete standard DID whose registered method adapter MUST project to the principal_id derived from did_operation.

identity_binding_challenge_outcome.description: Persisted, single-use server challenge. The client copies every field from challenge_id through expires_at into identity_creation_control_proof, adds proof_kind and verification_key_multibase, and signs that complete proof object with signature omitted. request_id is idempotency metadata and is not part of the root-control transcript.

operation_digest.description: sha256:<lowercase-hex> of SHA-256 over RFC 8785 JCS bytes of the complete request did_operation object.

did_version_id.description: Validated did:webvh inception versionId copied into the root-control transcript.

log_head_digest.description: SHA-256 over RFC 8785 JCS bytes of the exact method-native inception log entry.

control_key_digest.description: SHA-256 over the canonical multikey bytes of the current active update key (parameters.updateKeys[0]) of the DID entry pinned by did_version_id; never private key material or a next-key commitment. For account-first inception that entry is entry 0; for an already-published DID it is the entry current at binding time, so a spent inception key is never required.

pcr_genesis_unit_kinds.description: Closed ordered declaration copied into the identity-root creation transcript.

identity_creation_control_proof.description: Fresh proof signed by the did:webvh inception operation's parameters.updateKeys[0] identity root. The verifier selects that key from did_operation and MUST NOT treat a request-supplied key or a DID Document verificationMethod as authority. Signature covers every field except signature as canonical JSON with domain separator ak.identity-creation-control-proof-v1.

pcr_realm_id.description: Principal Control Realm id obtained only by retyping the exact root-signed ak.realm.create event_id; it is not derived from principal_id and MUST equal the pcr_genesis_unit create Event's retyped id.

realm_create_payload_digest.description: Canonical digest of the ak.realm.create payload only. Event ids and envelope digests are forbidden from this transcript.

founding_authorize_payload_digest.description: Canonical digest of the founding ak.device.authorize payload only. Event ids and envelope digests are forbidden from this transcript.

initial_session_request_digest.description: SHA-256 digest of RFC 8785 JCS InitialSessionGrantRequest. The embedded session_public_key MUST thumbprint to dpop_jkt; this binds the first Standard grant intent without turning it into a separate root-signed object.

signature.description: 64-byte Ed25519 identity-root signature encoded base64url without padding.

registration_did_evidence_draft.description: Dedicated registration-time control proof and frozen method evidence. It is distinct from identity_creation_control_proof and MUST bind the exact did_operation pins.

binding_kind.description: Discriminates the already-published DID proof branch from account-first identity creation.

full_id.description: Verified complete DID whose registered adapter projects to principal_id.

did_version_id.description: Adapter-defined version identifier pinned when the account binding was accepted.

control_key_digest.description: Digest of the verified current control key that authorized this binding.

identity_creation_lease_id.description: Present only when binding_kind=identity_creation. The published_did branch creates no identity-creation lease.

head_event_digest.description: DID registry log head digest for the exact did:webvh inception entry accepted during this binding saga; it is not a PCR Event head.

proof.description: Account Authority detached proof. payload_digest is SHA-256 over RFC 8785 JCS of the complete receipt with proof omitted, including binding_kind, principal_id, full_id, did_version_id, control_key_digest, operation/head digests, and the identity-creation lease/fence only when that branch applies. JWS signs canonical_json({context:'ak.account-binding-receipt-proof-v1', payload_digest, account_authority_id, account_subject, principal_id, full_id, did_version_id, control_key_digest, verification_method, created_at}); proof.created_at MUST equal issued_at and verification_method MUST be an assertion method of account_authority_id valid at issued_at.

propertyNames.description: ak.self.account.command.update_profile only accepts display_name, avatar_blob_ref, and profile_fields.<key>. The bio is carried as profile_fields.bio.

account_materialized_profile.description: Materialized Actor Profile returned on the account surface. id is the actor_profile ID derived by retyping the accepted ak.profile.create Event ID; realm_id is the exact Principal Control Realm that carries the profile Event lineage.

profile.description: Present only when the authenticated principal has exactly one unambiguous accepted Actor Profile across its authority-instance PCR lineages. Because this request has no authority selector, multiple accepted lineages MUST fail closed by omitting profile; the service MUST NOT choose an implicit current PCR.

is_server_admin.description: True when the authenticated principal is a deployment server administrator (the server's configured admin principal set). Operator-only product surfaces (e.g. organization creation) gate their UI on this. Reducer/config-derived, not a stored account field; absent or false means non-admin.

account_register_request_body.description: Canonical account binding request. Exactly one branch is required: proof binds an already-published full_id, while identity_creation carries the account-first DID operation and PCR genesis unit. In either branch every repeated principal_id and full_id in the selected proof/creation objects and genesis initial_resolution MUST equal the outer values byte-for-byte, and the Account Authority MUST independently require project(full_id)=principal_id before any write.

full_id.description: Required for both externally created and account-first identities. The server verifies the method evidence and project(full_id)=principal_id before persisting the PCR resolution state.

preconditions.description: This account self-service surface forbids Event preconditions. ak.profile.update concurrency is expressed only by the optional signed payload.expected_state_digest.

account_profile_event_submission.description: Holder-signed Actor Profile Control Move. event.realm_id is the exact PrincipalAuthorityInstance PCR selector, and accepted-profile presence is evaluated only within that selected PCR lineage. With no accepted profile there the exact Event MUST be ak.profile.create and its materialized actor_profile ID is derived by retyping event.event_id; the create payload MUST NOT carry id. With an accepted profile there the exact Event MUST be ak.profile.update and payload.target_ref MUST equal that accepted create-derived ID. In both branches realm scope identifies the same PCR, and event.actor_id identifies the session principal. On create payload.object.principal_id MUST equal that principal; on update the accepted target profile's materialized principal_id MUST equal it. Holder direct proof is required without executed_by, authorization_ref or Applet provenance. Event preconditions MUST be empty; update concurrency uses only the optional signed payload.expected_state_digest. The service submits the exact bytes through ordinary Event admission and MUST NOT author, rebuild, co-sign, choose an ID or add a concurrency guard. A valid Control Move not yet covered by an accepted Seal returns frontier_unavailable; after coverage, exact retry returns the stored outcome.

account_update_profile_request_body.description: Carries exactly one holder-signed profile create-or-update Event and no unsigned profile patch.

account_update_profile_outcome.description: Stored outcome after the profile Control Move is accepted and its effect is materialized. profile.id is the create-derived ActorProfile ID, profile.realm_id is event.realm_id, and an update projects updated_by/updated_at from event.actor_id/event.created_at. Exact Event replay returns the byte-identical stored outcome and emits no second account-aggregate delta.

account_status_authority_evidence.description: Account Authority-signed, transport-only evidence binding one service account, principal, Principal Control Realm and authorized Event issuer. It is not a public identity fact and MUST be disclosed only to Principal Servers that already hold or are about to hold state for this account/principal. The proof uses context ak.account_status.authority_evidence.v1 and payload_digest over RFC 8785 JCS of every field except proof.

binding_version.description: Monotonic Account Authority-local binding generation. A receiver MUST reject rollback relative to evidence already accepted for the same (account_authority_id, account_id).

authority_ref.description: Account Authority DID service/delegation URL authorizing issuer_service_id to sign ak.account.status for this account. For a direct Account Authority issuer this is its own account-authority service entry; for a delegated Principal Server it is the live delegation entry.

account_status_publication.description: Constrained carrier for exactly one ak.account.status Event. Initial Account Authority publication carries event only; fanout of an already accepted Event carries the same event plus account_status_receipts. AuthorizationLease and generic IngressReceipt are forbidden because this high-risk status publication is admitted against current authority state.
