account_status_receipt.description: Principal Server-signed transport receipt proving that one ak.account.status Event was accepted into that receiver's local account-status frontier. It is not an offline-publication IngressReceipt, contains no AuthorizationLease id, and grants no authority. proof uses context ak.account_status.ingress_receipt.v1 and payload_digest over RFC 8785 JCS of every field except proof.

cba_proof_bundles.description: Receiver-relative Principal Control Realm CBA closure for receipted fanout. Initial publication MAY omit it when the destination already has the current PCR dependencies.

account_status_authoring_basis_request_b.description: Service-authenticated, read-only request for the exact actor-chain and Principal Control Realm Seal frontiers needed to author one ak.account.status Event. The signed authority evidence is verified before any frontier is disclosed.

account_status_authoring_basis_outcome.description: PCR-bound authoring coordinates for one authoritative account-status producer. actor_frontier supplies actor_seq and prev_refs; seal_frontier supplies the sole seal_basis leaf. Both variants MUST exactly match authority_evidence and are read-only observations, not authority grants.

account_status_publication_outcome.description: Durable operation state. accepted/duplicate are terminal for this receiver's account-status frontier; pending_seal is retryable with the same Idempotency-Key and byte-identical request until the Event is accepted or rejected. propagation_state reports this receiver's downstream fanout obligation without mutating the signed Event payload.

did_binding_challenge_request_body.description: Request a single-use challenge for binding an ALREADY-PUBLISHED full_id to principal_id. Unlike identity_binding_challenge_request_body this carries no unpublished did_operation and no PCR genesis digests: the DID already exists, and the Account Authority resolves full_id at high freshness, requires project(full_id)=principal_id, and never attempts to resolve did_core_id directly.

principal_id.description: Stable did_core_id to bind. It is not directly resolvable.

full_id.description: Already-published complete DID. The Account Authority MUST resolve it at the high freshness tier, require project(full_id)=principal_id, and MUST NOT accept caller-supplied DID history.

did_binding_challenge_outcome.description: Persisted, single-use server challenge for binding an already-published full_id to principal_id. The client copies every field from challenge_id through expires_at into account_registration_control_proof, adds proof_kind, request_canonical_digest and verification_method, and signs the closed proof with the current active update key of the entry pinned by did_version_id. The client MUST byte-compare principal_id, full_id and every other echoed field against what it expects before signing and MUST fail closed on any mismatch. request_id is idempotency metadata and is not part of the signed transcript.

account_subject.description: Service account subject that will own the binding. Signed so the proof cannot be replayed against another account.

full_id.description: Server-resolved full_id echoed into the signed proof transcript; it MUST project to principal_id.

did_version_id.description: versionId of the entry the Account Authority resolved as current; the proof MUST be signed by that entry's active update key.

witness_evidence.description: Method-native witness / freshness evidence digest resolved for this DID. Deployments that do not host the DID MUST require it: same-origin trust between registry and Principal Server does not extend to third-party DIDs.

expires_at.description: Issued lifetime MUST be no greater than 300 seconds.

identity_abandonment_challenge_request_b.description: Request the single-use challenge that makes abandoning a provisional identity explicit. It applies only while the Principal Control Realm was never accepted and the identity root is lost, so the caller can sign nothing and the account handoff grant is the only available credential. principal_id and did_version_id pin exactly which reservation is being given up.

principal_id.description: Provisional principal recorded in the holder-authenticated reserved_identity_creation checkpoint. The Account Authority MUST reject any other value and MUST NOT issue a challenge for a principal whose PCR is already accepted.

did_version_id.description: versionId of the published entry 0 that becomes the orphan anchor. Pinning it lets the confirmation detect a PCR acceptance that landed after the challenge was issued instead of abandoning a live identity.

identity_abandonment_consequence_disclos.description: Closed ordered set of consequences the client MUST present before it may submit the confirmation. The protocol fixes which consequences must be disclosed; the localized wording is deployment-owned. This list is not a self-asserted acknowledgement receipt, which would be forgeable; the anti-automation property comes from the challenge itself, which no login, session resume, lease fence advance or other automated flow ever fetches.

identity_abandonment_challenge_outcome.description: Persisted, single-use server challenge for provisional identity abandonment. It is the evidence that the abandonment was an explicit user action: the identity root is lost, so the holder cannot sign a confirmation. Challenge state MUST be shared durable state, not process-local memory; expiry and prior consumption are distinct terminal states.

lease_fence.description: Identity-creation lease fence at issuance. The confirmation MUST be rejected when the current fence differs, so a concurrent holder cannot have its reservation abandoned underneath it.

expires_at.description: MUST be at most 300 seconds after issued_at.

identity_abandonment_request_body.description: Confirm the explicit abandonment of a provisional identity. It MUST present a fresh account handoff grant and MUST NOT reuse the grant presented when the challenge was issued; how strong the authentication behind that fresh handoff is, which risk checks run and how long any cooldown lasts are deployment governance and are deliberately not specified here.

request_id.description: Idempotency identity of the abandonment. Replaying it returns the recorded terminal outcome and MUST NOT produce a second orphan-anchor tombstone.

identity_abandonment_outcome.description: Recorded terminal outcome of an explicit abandonment. One transaction consumed the challenge, recorded the orphan-anchor tombstone / audit reservation, suppressed the reserved_identity_creation checkpoint on every holder-readable surface and released the identity-creation lease. There is exactly one success terminal; every other terminal is an error reply. Whether the orphan anchor is annotated on a discovery surface, when its handle and namespace are released and how long the reservation is retained are deployment governance and are not carried here.

principal_id.description: The abandoned provisional principal. Its published entry 0 is now a permanently unusable orphan anchor: it MUST NOT be reused and continuity MUST NOT be claimed over it.

schemas/account-subscribe-frame.schema.j.title: Arkret Account Subscribe Frame
schemas/account-subscribe-frame.schema.j.description: Single NDJSON frame on the ak.self.account.stream.subscribe streaming channel (GET /_arkret/self/account/subscribe, Content-Type: application/x-ndjson). Each newline-delimited line is one frame object. Discriminated by the `kind` field: `delta` carries account-aggregate data (cross-Realm frontier, to_device, account_data, device_lists, notifications, unread counts); the other kinds are control frames that mirror ak.self.events.stream.subscribe (`catchup_complete`, `frontier`, `heartbeat`, `dropped`, `resync_required`, `unauthorized`). Encrypted broadcast signals use the optional Signal Extension rail and never appear in this durable/account aggregate stream. `dropped` and `resync_required` MAY carry `reconnect_after_ms` as a server-directed minimum delay before opening another account subscribe stream for the same principal/device/filter scope.

cursor.description: Stream cursor (purpose='stream'). On `delta` / `catchup_complete` / `frontier` frames it points to the position covered by this frame; pass back as `after=` on the next subscribe call to resume. REQUIRED on `dropped` frames as the account-aggregate catch-up start for `GET /account/subscribe?after=<cursor>&catchup=true`. MUST be present on `delta` / `catchup_complete` / `frontier` / `dropped`; absent on `heartbeat` / `resync_required` / `unauthorized`.

realms.description: Per-Realm map on `delta` frames. Keys are `ak:realm:*`; values are that Realm's aggregate timeline/state/account-data entry. Membership lifecycle (`join` / `invite` / `knock` / `leave`) is carried by the events inside the Realm entry.

device_lists.description: Principal DID sets whose authoritative device list changed or left the caller's visibility scope on `delta` frames.

account_data.description: Account-scoped private data updates on `delta` frames.

notifications.description: Account-private notification projection deltas on `delta` frames. These are not Realm Events and are authorized by the authenticated account context rather than realm_id visibility.

agent_signer_evidence_bundle.description: Bounded signer-evidence sidecar for Agent-authored Events in this delta. Clients MUST verify each evidence item before caching or using it.

partial.description: When true on a `delta` frame, the per-Realm timelines are limited (truncated); client SHOULD backfill via ak.self.events.read.scan for any Realm whose timeline carries `limited=true`.

priority.description: Optional server-side priority hint for the frame (UX scheduling).

reconnect_after_ms.description: Optional server-directed minimum delay, in milliseconds, before opening another `ak.self.account.stream.subscribe` stream for the same principal/device/filter scope. MAY appear only on `dropped` and `resync_required` frames. This is a stream reconnect hint, not a generic error retry field; it does not apply to unrelated API calls. Clients MUST wait at least this delay before reconnecting, and servers MUST reject earlier reconnect attempts with `429 rate_limited` plus `Retry-After`.

notification_kind.description: Closed notification type. Agent runtime approvals reuse the registered notification type `agent`.

ack_token.description: Server-issued opaque acknowledgement token, REQUIRED whenever messages[] is non-empty. Bound server-side to (principal_id, device_id, queue high-water position of this batch) and covering this batch plus all previously delivered messages. NOT a cursor: no ak:cursor: wire form, no cursor schema/TTL/purpose. The client passes it verbatim to ak.self.device_messages.command.ack AFTER durably persisting the batch payloads; queue deletion happens only through that explicit ack, never through stream cursor advancement (client-sync.md §10.1).

lost.description: SHOULD be set true when the server has dropped unacknowledged messages for this device (expiry or capacity) since the device's last acknowledged position. Clients SHOULD trigger key recovery paths (key backup / key re-request) and MUST NOT silently assume the queue was complete.

limited.description: True when this account subscribe to_device batch is truncated because the device queue exceeds the stream frame budget. When true, `next_cursor` is REQUIRED and the client MUST continue with ak.self.device_messages.read.list?after=<next_cursor>; the top-level account stream cursor MUST NOT be used as the to-device queue pagination cursor.

next_cursor.description: Read-only to-device queue continuation cursor for ak.self.device_messages.read.list?after=... . It is not an acknowledgement and MUST NOT delete queued messages; queue deletion happens only through `ack_token` passed to ak.self.device_messages.command.ack.

ordered_log_conflict_diagnostic.description: User-visible audit diagnostic for an ordered log issuer equivocation. The loser remains in canonical history but is excluded from timeline.events and the joined state leaf.

prev_cursor.description: Stream cursor pointing backward in the timeline for backfilling history before this batch.

preview_only.description: Fallback path of client-sync.md §5.2: when timeline.limited=true and the server does not return realm_sync_entry.state_at_window_start, it MUST set preview_only=true. Clients then render window-start events as preview only.

ordered_log_conflicts.description: Audit-visible ordered log equivocations affecting this timeline window. Clients MUST NOT render loser events as ordinary messages; they MAY expose these records in conflict/audit UI.

members.description: Lightweight roster hint derived from effective ak.member.state, effective ak.member.identity.update references, and currently visible handle-claim evidence. Entries MUST NOT carry display fields or naked handle strings directly; handle strings may appear only inside signed ak.schema.handle_claim.v1 objects.

members_limited.description: True when members[] is truncated and MUST NOT be treated as the complete Realm roster.

members_next_cursor.description: Optional pagination cursor for continuing member roster retrieval.

event_states.description: Per-event protocol-state views (event_id + event_state) for reducer-input events carried by this entry. The 'bottom' detail object lives separately in 'bottoms' below — keyed by cell, not duplicated per event — so wire body is not doubled. Receivers correlate event_state=failed_bottom with the cell-level bottom diagnostic via the cells listed in bottom.cells[]. See zh/sync/service-surface.md §5.3.

event_state_reason_code.description: Optional short reason code (e.g., 'recovery_witness_missing'). For failure detail beyond the enum.

bottoms.description: Structured Bottom diagnostics for cells whose effective Lattice join resolved to ⊥ under the current CBA query basis. Each entry pins (cell, status, bottom). See zh/sync/service-surface.md §5.3.

state_at_window_start.description: Derived projection-only state at the timeline window start. NOT part of state hash, frontier, or causal graph.

collaboration_role.description: Projection-only strong Realm role, emitted only after the server validates the registered Realm profile and discriminator.

subject_id.description: Optional disclosed principal / holder did_core_id for this member. Omit when subject disclosure is only available inside encrypted MemberIdentity or not authorized for the caller. Required whenever handle claim evidence or digest hints are included.

identity_event_ids.description: Effective ak.member.identity.update event ids for this actor after replacement refs are applied.

member_display_state_digest.description: Digest over the effective identity event references plus the current visible handle claim digest set for this roster entry.

identity_events.description: Optional inline effective ak.member.identity.update Event envelopes. When present these are the original events, not query-time re-encryption or projection rewrites. MUST be omitted unless subject_id is disclosed, because plaintext or decryptable identity events can disclose the same member subject.

handle_claim_digests.description: Digests of currently visible effective ak.schema.handle_claim.v1 objects for this member in the current Realm context. MUST be omitted unless subject_id is disclosed, because stable claim digests are linkable across contexts. Absence is not proof that the member has no handle.

handle_claims.description: Optional inline signed handle claim evidence. MUST be omitted unless subject_id is disclosed, and every included claim MUST have claim.subject equal to subject_id. Services may omit this for privacy, size, or freshness; clients can backfill by subject via ak.find.directory.read.list_handles_for_subject.

handle_claims_limited.description: True when handle_claims[] is truncated or replaced by digest-only hints. Clients MUST NOT interpret missing claims as no handle.

oneOf.description: Catch-up replay or initial baseline completed; no data fields are allowed.
Cursor-only frontier advancement; no data fields are allowed.
Account stream gap signal; cursor is the account catch-up start. No data fields are allowed. `reconnect_after_ms` MAY be present to enforce a server-directed reconnect holdoff.
Keepalive frame; cursor and data fields are forbidden.
Hard reset signal; cursor and data fields are forbidden. `reconnect_after_ms` MAY be present to enforce a server-directed reconnect holdoff.
Authorization-loss signal; cursor and data fields are forbidden.

schemas/accountability-grant.schema.json.title: Arkret Accountability Grant
schemas/accountability-grant.schema.json.description: Issuer-signed endorsement used to verify Actor Profile accountable_principal_ids entries. This is the payload contract for ak.identity.accountability_grant.

issuer.description: Stable principal did_core_id accepting accountability for subject. Verifiers MUST take the proof verification-method DID URL's bare controller full_id, validate it with the registered method adapter, and require project(full_id) to equal issuer; direct full-DID/core-id string comparison is forbidden.

accountability_scope.description: Non-empty duplicate-free closed set used only for display and accountability governance; never grants authorization. A string is the singleton-set wire form. Array order has no semantic meaning. Canonical authors emit singleton sets as strings and multi-value sets in ascending raw UTF-8 byte order; receivers accept every schema-valid ordering and normalize only for cell-subject derivation, domain equality, and projection union.

expires_at.description: Optional: absent means the accountability grant is non-expiring and governed by grant_status revocation and controller lifecycle cascade.

proof.description: Detached proof by issuer over utf8('ak.accountability-grant-v1\n') || canonical_json(the object with proof omitted).

id.description: Present on the materialised object. MUST be absent from the create Event payload: zh/models/common-fields.md derives it from the create Event's own event_id (retyped), so a payload-supplied id would be a second, forgeable truth.

actor_kind.description: Directory / UX classification only. MUST NOT participate in authorization, reducer acceptance, capability resolution, or any wire-protocol decision: those MUST consult DID + Grant + Constraint exclusively. Implementations are free to use actor_kind for icon selection, directory filtering and presentation, but a wrong value MUST NOT widen or narrow what a principal can do. Does NOT include 'device': a device is not an actor principal and has no DID of its own; its identity is device_id (ak:device:<uuid>) plus a verification method under the owning principal DID. See zh/models/actor.md.

handle.description: Arkret canonical handle string: <localpart>:<domain>. The @ mention sigil is not part of the handle.

agent_slug.description: Projection hint for a controller-scoped selector slug backed by ak.schema.agent_selector_claim.v1. Only valid when actor_kind=agent under ak.profile.personal_agent_provisioning.v1; it is not a global handle and MUST NOT be used for authorization, attribution, or Directory discovery. The mention input token @<controller-handle>/<agent_slug> resolves to this actor's principal_id before persistence only after selector claim validation.

status.description: Public projection of the account lifecycle status values defined in zh/identity/account-lifecycle.md §3. Implementations MAY hide or coarsen this field in projection views, but the wire enum mirrors ak.account.status.

resolution.description: Read-only current principal full_id projection derived from the PCR identity resolution cell. It is not writable through Actor Profile create/update patches and is not an authorization root.

schemas/agent-operations.schema.json.title: Arkret Account Pairing and Agent Operation DTOs
schemas/agent-operations.schema.json.description: Closed request and response DTOs for account pairing and native personal agent management operations.

agent_slug.description: Required controller-scoped native personal agent selector slug. Used only as the right-hand component of @<controller-handle>/<agent_slug>; not a global handle or authorization subject. Provisioning services MUST issue or update a ak.schema.agent_selector_claim.v1.

opaque_local_id.description: Deployment-local short-lived account/auth artifact id. It is not a ak:<kind> protocol object id.

pairing_secret.description: One-time CSPRNG pairing secret carrying at least 128 bits of entropy. It is transmitted only in JSON bodies, never in URLs or logs.

device_pairing_code.description: Eight-character human-readable Crockford-style code carrying 40 CSPRNG bits, bound to a short-lived SAS/QR transcript and protected by a ten-failure lockout.

agent_runtime_key_possession_proof.description: Closed Ed25519 proof that the submitter controls the proposed native Agent runtime key and possesses the authoritative pairing secret. Canonical transcript, equality, freshness, and final-commit re-verification rules are defined in key-management.md section 3.6.2.

audience.description: Stable target-service authorization identity; any verification_method remains a DID URL whose bare full DID MUST project to this did_core_id.

signature.description: Unpadded base64url encoding of the 64-byte raw Ed25519 signature over the canonical transcript.

public_key.description: Canonical PublicKey DTO. Defined once in public-key.schema.json so device, agent and account surfaces share one definition.

agent_runtime_public_key.description: Closed v1 Native Agent runtime signing-key profile. Ed25519 is the fully-specified JOSE algorithm identifier from RFC 9864; polymorphic algorithm identifiers are rejected.

agent_status.description: Controller lifecycle intent axis. Closed enum; only the controller's pause / resume / deactivate lifecycle events change it. Pairing and key facts are reflected through the generic readiness axis and open-handle fields, never through a fourth generic state axis (key-management.md §3.6.1).

agent_runtime_state.description: Operation-local diagnostic enum used only by agent_runtime_approval_status_outcome on the unauthenticated pairing poll. It is mechanically derived from the polled handle and key facts, is never writable, and MUST NOT appear in generic Agent list/get/key_state projections: no active accepted key authorization with an unexpired bootstrap handle is pending_runtime_key; no active key with the bootstrap handle expired is pairing_expired; an active key with no unconsumed replacement handle is ready; an active key with an unexpired replacement handle is replacing.

agent_presence.description: Short-lived reachability signal only. It never substitutes for lifecycle or readiness and does not use a protocol-wide fixed five-minute refresh interval.

realm_id.description: Realm that owns the capability grant cell and therefore the required ak.capability.revoke write surface.

key_state.description: Controller-private key, pairing-handle, authorization and PCR-recovery material for a generic Agent view. This object deliberately carries no lifecycle, readiness, presence or runtime_state field: the only three generic status axes are siblings on agent_projection, while pairing poll alone exposes its operation-local runtime_state diagnostic.

requested_scope.description: Controller-private projection of the required immutable global Agent key/session ceiling captured at provision time, not a grant. Content actions are the maximum actions that later key scopes, Realm-scoped grants and sessions may allow; an omitted action cannot be added later. Participation is a separate action-time deny gate and cannot add authority. Provisioning never materializes content grants from this field. Operation/service resources constrain the service surface; explicit content resource selectors only further narrow later grants. Receiver authority comes from a valid agent-requested-scope-disclosure whose digest matches the accepted-at Agent DID commitment, not this service projection.

requested_scope_digest.description: sha256 digest of the domain-separated Agent requested_scope commitment fixed in the accepted Agent DID ArkretPrincipalControlRealm service entry; the public entry does not contain the complete scope.

pairing_request_id.description: Current unconsumed, unexpired pairing handle. Its presence means pairing is open. Services MUST omit this field and its pairing_mode / pairing_code / pairing_expires_at siblings immediately after the handle is consumed or expires.

pairing_mode.description: Durable branch discriminator for the current open handle. bootstrap is valid when the Agent has no active accepted runtime-key authorization; replacement is valid when it already holds an active authorized key and lifecycle is active or paused. This field is pairing material, not a fourth generic status axis.

pairing_expires_at.description: Authoritative pairing expiry instant in the shared byte-canonical UTC millisecond profile. The projection and ak.agent.key_pairing_request_binding.v1.expires_at use the same exact string; offset or sub-millisecond wire spellings are schema violations and MUST NOT be normalized by a verifier.

agent_pcr_recovery_state.description: Controller-visible recovery readiness for the managed Agent Principal Control Realm. pending means no accepted controller-owned managed-PCR backup exists; ready means the current controller recovery policy and Agent PCR sealed MLS frontier are covered by the active mls_history series tail; stale means an older backup exists but no longer covers the current policy, delegation, Seal frontier, or MLS epoch. Runtime pairing commits require ready at the pre-commit frontier; the accepted key-authorization Event then advances the frontier and makes this projection stale until a post-commit backup tail is accepted.

challenge_proof.description: Structured proof of possession of new_device_pubkey. The Account Authority MUST recompute the signing transcript itself and MUST NOT settle for byte equality against a stored copy. Which transcript applies is fixed by the request shape: with device_pairing_request_id it is ak.device-pairing.challenge.v1 rebuilt from the staged record; with challenge_transcript it is ak.device-pairing.challenge.to_device.v1 rebuilt from those inputs plus the Account Authority own gate_audience origin. The digest of that recomputed transcript is also the value the target device_signature commits to, so one recomputation gates both proofs. A mismatched transcript_digest, a transcript name that does not match the request shape, a kid other than new_device_pubkey.kid, or a failing signature MUST NOT authorize a device.

hpke_key.description: New target device X25519 HPKE public key. It MUST be byte-identical to authorize_event.event.payload.hpke_key and is never generated or substituted by the service. Its authority is the out-of-band device_pairing_target_attestation the approving device verified, not the staged record: the unauthenticated staging surface never carries this value.

device_signature.description: Target-device Ed25519 possession proof over ak.device-authorize-accepted-device-possession-proof-v1: this operation always produces authorization_binding_kind=accepted_device, so registration_anchor and pcr_recovery possession domains MUST be rejected here. It MUST be byte-identical to authorize_event.event.payload.device_signature and verify under new_device_pubkey.

authorize_event.description: Fully signed ak.device.authorize initial submission authored by a current accepted device. The service MUST admit this exact Event through the ordinary Event validation/reducer path; it MUST NOT mint an Event id, rewrite the Event, or directly insert a device projection. The payload MUST name the target new_device_pubkey.kid, hpke_key and device_signature from this request, set authorization_binding_kind=accepted_device, and name the approving current device id in authorized_by. The proof.verification_method bare DID component MUST project through its registered adapter to principal_id and its fragment MUST equal authorized_by; appending a fragment to did_core_id is forbidden. That Event proof, not the target device_signature, binds principal_id, authorized_by, not_before, expires_at and scopes, because only the approving device knows those values.

device_pairing_request_id.description: Server-mediated short-link request id. Present exactly for the short-link path. The Account Authority MUST atomically authorize only the still-pending staged record whose pairing_code and new_device_pubkey exactly match this request, and MUST verify challenge_proof against the ak.device-pairing.challenge.v1 transcript rebuilt from that record (device_pairing_request_id, pairing_code, gate_audience, expires_at, server_nonce, client_nonce, new_device_pubkey digest). A record whose proof does not verify MUST NOT authorize a device.

challenge_transcript.description: Transcript inputs for the to-device path, where there is no staged record for the Account Authority to rebuild from. Present exactly when device_pairing_request_id is absent.

pairing_request_id.description: Single-use pairing artifact id returned by agent_provision_outcome. Profile-local, short-lived and not a durable protocol object ref.

requested_scope_disclosure.description: Controller-signed private disclosure addressed to the authoritative pairing verifier. The endpoint MUST consume its presentation challenge once, match agent/controller/audience, recompute the public DID commitment digest, and use the disclosed scope for the subset check. It MUST NOT copy the disclosure into authorize_event or any durable/public history.

signing_key_binding.description: Controller-signed minimal public binding created in the same approval action. Its agent/method/raw-key/authorization id and both digests MUST match the runtime request and authorize_event exactly.

authorize_event.description: Fully-signed ak.agent.key.authorize initial submission approved by the controller or policy engine. Its Event MUST target the Agent Principal Control Realm, carry actor_id equal to agent_id, executed_by equal to the controller DID, authorization_ref equal to the controller delegation DID URL bound by the Agent DID Document, and a proof verification method belonging to the controller or one of its currently authorized devices. The submission MUST carry ordinary publication authority evidence without rewriting the Event. Its payload.agent_key_scope MAY be narrower than, but MUST be an actions/resources/constraints subset of, the immutable provision requested_scope; every provision constraint remains mandatory. Required so key activation never depends on an unaudited pairing side effect. authorize_event.event.event_id is the pair operation idempotency identity.

activation_state.description: Two-phase pairing result. awaiting_accepted_frontier means the exact authorization Event is durable but is not yet authorization state; the controller MUST close it into a managed Agent-PCR Seal and retry the identical idempotent request. active means portable signer evidence can be built from an accepted Seal and only then may the runtime be treated as authorized.

agent_runtime_approval_request_body.description: Runtime-to-controller pending approval request for native personal-agent key pairing. The runtime proves possession of the local key and the short pairing code; the controller still must approve by signing ak.agent.key.authorize and submitting agent_key_pair_request_body. The service computes ak.agent.runtime_key_binding.v1 from agent_id, pairing_request_id, verification_method, public-key digest and attestation digest. One open pairing_request_id has at most one pending stable binding: same-binding retry is idempotent and refreshes the full request while retaining approval/notification ids; a different binding fails with HTTP 409 agent_runtime_request_conflict without replacement.

pairing_request_id.description: Single-use pairing artifact id returned by agent_provision_outcome. Profile-local, short-lived and not a durable protocol object ref.

agent_runtime_approval_controller_projec.description: Authenticated controller-safe projection of the pending runtime key request. It is deliberately not agent_runtime_approval_request_body and not agent_key_pair_request_body: pairing_code is exposed only by the sibling controller key_state field, while requested_scope_disclosure and authorize_event do not exist until the controller approves. Services MUST also omit any other runtime secret or unregistered field.

agent_human_approval_error_details.description: Closed error.details shape returned by ak.gate.account.command.issue_session_grant when an agent_key_proof request needs out-of-band controller approval. The enclosing ErrorEnvelope.error.code MUST be claim_required. The agent runtime MUST NOT be given CAPTCHA, OTP, browser-login, or other interactive human challenge material.

agent_runtime_approval_status_request_bo.description: Runtime-side poll for the controller decision on a previously submitted runtime key request. The pairing_request_id, pairing_code, and agent_id triple is the query credential and MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string. A record miss and a pairing_code or agent_id mismatch MUST be indistinguishable (both not_found). HTTP responses MUST carry Retry-After; clients wait at least that interval and stop polling after pairing expiry.

pairing_request_id.description: Single-use pairing artifact id returned by agent_provision_outcome. Profile-local, short-lived and not a durable protocol object ref.

agent_runtime_approval_status_outcome.description: Controller-decision status for one runtime key pairing request. runtime_state is an operation-specific pairing diagnostic, not a fourth general Agent status axis. While the polled pairing is open it is pending_runtime_key (bootstrap) or replacing (replacement). Once the controller has approved this exact pairing, authorized_event_ref plus the authorized key binding fields are present; the runtime MUST compare authorized_public_key_digest against its own key. Presence and digest match of those fields — never lifecycle, readiness, presence or runtime_state alone — is the approval signal. An expired bootstrap reports pairing_expired; an expired replacement reports ready with no authorization fields for this request.

authorized_public_key_digest.description: SHA-256 of the decoded 32-byte Ed25519 public key, computed with agent_signing_public_key_digest. This is not the canonical runtime-request PublicKey DTO digest.

agent_provision_request_body.description: Controller-authored managed-Agent bootstrap. Before prepare, the controller publishes a signed, PCR-independent did:webvh inception whose document contains the managed-controller delegation but no ArkretPrincipalControlRealm service. prepare receives that full_id, verifies the accepted inception and returns its exact initial_resolution plus an opaque allocation. The controller freezes the managed-Agent PCR genesis with that commitment, derives principal_control_realm_id, and commits one ak.agent.provision Event. After PCR acceptance, the controller publishes the pre-rotation-authorized DID update containing the create-locked Realm binding. The service exposes the Agent and pairing handle only after that update is accepted.

full_id.description: Controller-authored Agent did:webvh whose accepted inception is independent of the future PCR Realm id.

controller_authority_instance.description: Exact authenticated controller PCR instance in which provision_event will be authored. The service MUST validate the canonical digest and match this object byte-for-byte to its durable principal-resolution record; selecting a PCR from principal_id alone is forbidden.

principal_control_realm_id.description: Agent PCR realm id the controller derived as retype(event_id) of the managed Agent PCR ak.realm.create envelope it froze locally, and signed into provision_event. A service MUST NOT choose it; commit MUST reject any value that differs from the provision payload byte for byte. It is distinct from the controller PCR that carries provision_event. This transport field is not inside any digest preimage; the ordering the controller MUST follow is key-management.md 3.6.3 and the named encoding.md 6.0.1 exemption on the payload field.

requested_scope.description: Required immutable global Agent key/session ceiling, not a grant. Later key scopes, Realm grants and session requests MUST NOT exceed its actions, resource selectors or mandatory constraints. Participation is an independent action-time deny gate and cannot restore authority omitted here. Provisioning never materializes content grants from this field. Operation/service resources constrain the service surface; explicit content resource selectors only further narrow later grants.

agent_provision_outcome.description: Four-stage outcome. prepare returns awaiting_controller_event with an accepted inception commitment. An accepted ak.agent.provision moves it to awaiting_pcr_genesis. PCR acceptance moves it to awaiting_did_binding until the controller-authored continuous WebVH update publishes the exact Realm service entry. The Agent, pairing handle and list/get projection become visible only at complete.

full_id.description: Complete Agent DID whose registered adapter projection is agent_id; managed-Agent PCR genesis initial_resolution MUST commit this value and its verified method head.

initial_resolution.description: Exact verified accepted inception position. It is immutable across all provisioning outcomes and is copied byte-for-byte into managed-Agent PCR genesis.

principal_control_realm_id.description: Agent PCR realm id the controller derived locally as retype(event_id) of the managed Agent PCR genesis it froze, and declared in the provision payload. Until that genesis is accepted this is a claim, not a live Realm.

controller_realm_id.description: Authenticated controller PCR in which the provision Event must be authored. Present only while status is awaiting_controller_event.

allocation_handle.description: Service-signed opaque allocation binding returned only by prepare and presented unchanged by commit.

requested_scope_digest.description: Digest of the complete immutable requested_scope commitment in the Agent DID accepted create-locked bootstrap history (entry 1); only this digest, not the complete scope, is public. The client MUST recompute it from its submitted scope, returned agent_id and authenticated controller DID.

agent_provisioning_abandonment_challenge.description: Request the single-use challenge that makes abandoning an accepted-but-never-genesised Agent provisioning explicit. It applies only while ak.agent.provision is accepted and the declared managed Agent PCR genesis has not been accepted, so the Agent has no PCR, no DID service entry, no pairing handle and no list/get projection. agent_id, principal_control_realm_id and allocation_handle pin exactly which provisioning is being given up.

principal_control_realm_id.description: Realm id the accepted provision declared. The service MUST reject any other value and MUST NOT issue a challenge once the genesis for it is accepted.

agent_provisioning_abandonment_consequen.description: Closed ordered set of consequences the client MUST present before it may submit the confirmation. The protocol fixes which consequences must be disclosed; the localized wording is deployment-owned. It is not a self-asserted acknowledgement receipt, which would be forgeable; the anti-automation property comes from the challenge itself, which no ordinary flow ever fetches.

agent_provisioning_abandonment_challenge.description: Persisted, single-use server challenge for abandoning an Agent provisioning whose PCR genesis never arrived. It is the evidence that the abandonment was an explicit controller action. Challenge state MUST be shared durable state, not process-local memory; expiry and prior consumption are distinct terminal states.

expires_at.description: MUST be at most 300 seconds after issued_at.

agent_provisioning_abandonment_request_b.description: Confirm the explicit abandonment of an Agent provisioning whose PCR genesis never arrived. It MUST present fresh credentials and MUST NOT reuse the ones presented when the challenge was issued; how strong that re-authentication is, which risk checks run and how long any cooldown lasts are deployment governance and are deliberately not specified here.

request_id.description: Idempotency identity of the abandonment. Replaying it returns the recorded terminal outcome and MUST NOT produce a second tombstone.

agent_provisioning_abandonment_outcome.description: Recorded terminal outcome of an explicit provisioning abandonment. One transaction consumed the challenge, released the agent_slug selector claim and the principal_control_realm_id claim, recorded the tombstone / audit reservation and suppressed every holder-readable trace of the allocation. There is exactly one success terminal; every other terminal is an error reply. The accepted ak.agent.provision Event itself stays in the controller PCR history and is never deleted or rewritten.

principal_control_realm_id.description: The abandoned realm-id claim. It MUST NOT be reused by a later provision, and no Realm will ever exist at it.

agent_renew_pairing_request_body.description: Re-open bootstrap pairing or replace an agent runtime. The service issues a fresh one-time pairing_request_id + pairing_code; every previously issued pairing handle for the agent becomes permanently unresolvable. An Agent with no active accepted runtime-key authorization re-opens bootstrap pairing; an Agent holding an active authorized key (lifecycle active or paused) performs runtime replacement re-pairing. Lifecycle intent, existing keys and grants stay untouched until the new controller-signed authorization with an exact supersedes set is accepted atomically, and completion preserves lifecycle intent. deactivated rejects.

agent_renew_pairing_outcome.description: Fresh pairing handle plus the current managed Agent PCR recovery projection. Unlike initial provisioning, pcr_recovery can already be ready or stale; pair commit still requires ready.

requested_scope_digest.description: Unchanged digest of the immutable requested_scope commitment in the Agent DID binding; the complete scope remains controller-private.

agent_pairing_bootstrap.description: One-time bootstrap material handed to a personal agent runtime after provisioning. This is not a session grant, capability grant or long-term secret.

agent_pairing_resolve_request_body.description: Body-only resolver input for short agent pairing handoff links. The token is obtained from a URL fragment or equivalent out-of-band channel and MUST NOT be sent in URL path or query.

lifecycle_event.description: Closed ak.self.agent.pause Event authored in the Agent PCR and executed/signed by the authenticated controller delegation. The service submits these exact bytes through ordinary Event admission and never synthesizes an Agent-authored Event. Its optional payload.reason MUST equal the request reason exactly (both absent or the same string).

Closed ak.self.agent.resume Event authored in the Agent PCR and executed/signed by the authenticated controller delegation. Sidecar desired membership is re-derived from accepted lifecycle and exact Realm membership after admission; the request carries no writable Sidecar roster or acknowledgement.

The single controller-authorized terminal ak.self.agent.deactivate Event. Once accepted, lifecycle is an unavoidable AND gate that makes every subordinate runtime key, session, pairing handle, capability grant, KeyPackage, presence and future submission ineffective. Cleanup Events are not part of this request. Optional payload.reason MUST equal request reason.

grant_event.description: Complete controller-authored ak.capability.grant initial submission. event.payload.grant is a closed CapabilityGrantBody without an inner proof; the Event envelope proof is the sole durable issuer signature. Admission MUST verify that event.actor_id, event.realm_id, payload.grant_id, grant.id, grant.issuer, grant.subject and grant.realm_id match the authenticated controller, path Agent and governed Realm as applicable. Every action and resource must be covered by the requested_scope disclosed in the verifier-bound private sidecar, and provision constraints remain mandatory. A violation fails with agent_grant_exceeds_requested_scope. The service MUST submit these exact bytes through ordinary Event admission and MUST NOT synthesize the Event or fall back to a body-local signature.

requested_scope_disclosure.description: Fresh, controller-signed private ceiling disclosure addressed to the grant admission verifier. It is transaction evidence only and MUST NOT be copied into the Realm-scoped grant or Event history.

agent_grant_detach_request_body.description: Carries the caller-signed ak.capability.revoke Control Move and nothing else. The path grant_id MUST equal payload.grant_id and optional payload.grant_ref; the target grant subject MUST equal the path Agent; event.realm_id MUST equal the target grant Realm. The service submits the exact signed Event through ordinary Event admission and MUST NOT rebuild it, synthesize a revoke Event, or attach a precondition after signing.

revoke_event.description: Complete controller-authored ak.capability.revoke initial submission. The Event MUST carry exactly one signed head_eq precondition on ak:cell:ak.component.capability.grant.v1:<payload.grant_id>, naming the complete observed grant-cell head. event.actor_id is the authenticated controller and admission binds its proof to the session-selected exact authority instance. Ordinary capability target guards remain authoritative: only the target issuer or current root controller of the target grant Realm may revoke it. Exact replay is idempotent; stale CAS, unsigned requests, and same-Event-ID different-body attempts fail closed.

agent_sidecar_context_ref.description: Existing shared Strand or Relation used only as the UI/source context for a native Sidecar projection. It does not create or identify a private Strand.

control_frontier.description: UTF-8 byte-lexicographically sorted accepted refs for Sidecar genesis, ownership, Agent lifecycle/runtime-key authorization, and exact Realm membership. It excludes action grants, participation selections, and MLS/key-readiness results.

current_controller_device_ready.description: True only when the authenticated controller session device is the accepted genesis creator device or has completed matching Welcome and KeyPackage consume evidence.

desired_agent_ids.description: Read-only projection derived at the accepted frontier: active, runtime-key-authorized Agent principals owned by the Sidecar controller and also active members of sidecar.realm_id. It is not caller-authored or reducer-stored and cannot be edited through Sidecar operations.

effective_agent_ids.description: Desired Agent principals that are members of the current accepted Sidecar MLS epoch and have completed target-device Welcome/KeyPackage consumption and key readiness. Reducer/service MUST enforce this set is a subset of desired_agent_ids. The controller is represented by sidecar.controller_id and is not duplicated in either Agent array.

version.description: Account Authority CAS version for this exact agent/scope selection.

expected_version.description: Value to echo verbatim into the next participation replace for this exact agent/scope selection.

next_replace_input.description: Verbatim prepare input for the next ak.self.agent.participation.resource.replace of this entry; member names match the replace request byte-for-byte per the service-http-binding.md 2.2.2 echo-container discipline. A first-ever selection has no entry row and uses expected_version 0.

schemas/agent-provision.schema.json.title: Arkret Agent Provision
schemas/agent-provision.schema.json.description: Controller-authored payload that creates one native personal Agent provisioning fact and atomically projects its accountability and controller-scoped selector bindings. The containing Event proof is the only signature; this payload carries no nested proof.

principal_control_realm_id.description: Agent PCR realm id this provision forward-declares. The controller freezes the managed Agent PCR ak.realm.create envelope locally, computes its event_id and writes retype(event_id, "realm") here; that genesis Event is not yet submitted when this payload is authored, and it MUST be submitted separately afterwards rather than alongside this Event. This is the named class C exemption ak.exemption.preimage_identity.agent_provision_principal_control_realm_id.v1 registered under encoding.md 6.0.1: the genesis preimage carries no reference to this Event, so the dependency stays one-way. Genesis admission reverse-looks-up this declaration; a service MUST NOT choose the value.

accountability_scope.description: Canonical closed accountability scope. The former singleton-array compatibility shape is not valid v1 wire.

schemas/agent-requested-scope-disclosure.title: Arkret Agent Requested Scope Disclosure
schemas/agent-requested-scope-disclosure.description: Controller-signed, verifier-bound private disclosure of a managed Agent's immutable requested_scope. This object is authorization evidence, not a grant. It MUST travel only over an authenticated confidential presentation/operation channel and MUST NOT be written to a public DID Document, durable Realm Event, public registry, pairing code, or notification. The verifier consumes request_id/challenge once, validates the short presentation window, verifies a current controller proof, recomputes requested_scope_digest against the accepted-at Agent DID commitment, and then applies the Agent ceiling subset rules. After successful one-time admission, an implementation MAY retain the object only as encrypted verifier-private evidence keyed by (agent_id, requested_scope_digest, verifier_service_id, audience).

request_id.description: Identifier of the signed ak.identity.presentation_request or an equivalent authenticated private challenge request. It is single-use at verifier_service_id.

requested_scope.description: Complete immutable Agent ceiling disclosed only to the bound verifier. It does not grant any action or resource.

requested_scope_digest.description: MUST equal sha256(RFC8785/JCS({agent_id, controller_id, kind:'ak.agent.requested_scope_commitment.v1', requested_scope})) and the digest in the accepted-at Agent DID service binding.

verifier_service_id.description: Exact verifier named by the presentation request. A different verifier MUST NOT accept or forward this disclosure as its own evidence.

audience.description: Exact origin, service audience, or canonical operation audience requested by verifier_service_id.

challenge.description: Verifier-generated unpredictable challenge. The (verifier_service_id, request_id, challenge) tuple is single-use; replay MUST fail closed.

expires_at.description: Presentation admission expiry. expires_at MUST be later than issued_at and expires_at - issued_at MUST NOT exceed 300 seconds. It does not change the immutable ceiling; it only bounds disclosure delivery/replay.

proofs.description: At least one current controller proof. The proof verification method MUST belong to controller_id or one of its currently authorized devices. payload_digest is sha256(canonical_json(this object with proofs omitted)); detached JWS signs canonical_json({context:'ak.agent-requested-scope-disclosure-proof-v1', payload_digest, agent_id, controller_id, verifier_service_id, audience, challenge, verification_method, created_at}).

schemas/agent-selector-claim.schema.json.title: Arkret Agent Selector Claim
schemas/agent-selector-claim.schema.json.description: Signed claim binding a controller-scoped native personal agent selector slug to an agent principal DID. It powers @<controller-handle>/<agent_slug> compose-time resolution without making the agent carry a public handle.

controller_subject.description: Controller principal DID that owns the selector namespace.

agent_slug.description: Controller-scoped slug used as the right-hand side of @<controller-handle>/<agent_slug>.

subject.description: Native personal agent principal DID selected by (controller_subject, agent_slug).

issuer.description: DID that signs this selector claim. It is normally controller_subject; a delegated issuer MUST be authorized by controller_subject and bound in source_refs or proof evidence.

issuer_service_id.description: Service DID that served or vouched for this selector claim when distinct from issuer.

visibility.description: Disclosure boundary for selector resolution. Restricted/private claims require audience and requester policy checks before returning subject.

audience.description: Audience binding for restricted selector disclosure, such as a Realm ID, verifier domain, or service DID.

claim_scope.description: Optional scope such as realm_id, organization_id, purpose, allowed_operations, or disclosure policy tags.

source_refs.description: Optional refs to accountability_grant, actor profile, provisioning, delegation, or revocation evidence.

schemas/agent-sidecar-event-exchange-bin.title: Arkret Agent Sidecar Event Exchange Binding
schemas/agent-sidecar-event-exchange-bin.description: Closed typed binding that ties one native-Sidecar-scoped Message event to one source-routed exchange. It is legal only inside encrypted metadata plaintext of an event whose scope_ref.kind is sidecar. It is the only normative way to declare an explicit user-facing response; invalid or absent bindings are non-echo. See zh/models/sidecar.md.

exchange_id.description: Opaque controller-private idempotency identity copied verbatim from the request binding. It is not a Sidecar locator and MUST NOT appear in shared events, plaintext metadata, publish output, push previews, notifications, public telemetry, account-data keys, or any public/shared surface.

role.description: Closed disposition. request: the controller's private request event itself. user_facing_response: an Agent response the controller MAY echo after validation. internal: exchange-scoped Agent collaboration/tool output that MUST NOT be echoed. Consumers MUST fail closed to non-echo on any value not listed here.

request_event_id.description: Accepted Event id of the private request event of the same exchange. Event id is the only canonical reference form; Message ids MUST NOT be used here.

completes_exchange.description: Optional coordinator completion request; legal only with role=user_facing_response. It does not itself make the exchange terminal. A controller device validates the actor against coordinator_assignment_event_id and, on success, authors a durable ak.agent.sidecar.exchange.control Event with action=close.

coordinator_assignment_event_id.description: Request Event id for the initial coordinator assignment, or the accepted reassign_coordinator control Event id. Required only when completes_exchange=true.

request_context.description: Write-once exchange identity carried only on role=request. It is the single durable source of the projection's write-once fields: any controller device rebuilding the projection copies these values verbatim, so cross-device bit-identity is anchored to the accepted request event instead of device-local state. Forbidden on response/internal roles.

completion_policy.description: Closed v1 completion policy. Only the effective coordinator may ask the controller to close the exchange.

coordinator_agent_id.description: Initial coordinator. It MUST be one of addressed_agent_ids. It MAY be omitted only when addressed_agent_ids contains exactly one item, in which case that sole item is implied.

schemas/agent-sidecar-exchange-control.s.title: Arkret Agent Sidecar Exchange Control
schemas/agent-sidecar-exchange-control.s.description: Closed plaintext encrypted inside the payload of ak.agent.sidecar.exchange.control. Only the Sidecar controller may author this durable private-Strand Event. It is the sole source of coordinator reassignment and terminal exchange state.

basis_event_ids.description: Canonical UTF-8 byte-order sorted maximal causal heads of exchange facts observed when this control was authored. The outer Event refs MUST contain role=after for every id, and the request Event must be causally covered.

response_event_ids.description: Exact canonical set of validated user-facing response Event ids causally covered by basis_event_ids. Required for every terminal action, including an empty array.

failure_reason_code.description: Required only for action=fail. close/cancel derive empty-response failure codes controller_closed_empty/controller_cancelled.

coordinator_agent_id.description: New coordinator for action=reassign_coordinator. It MUST be addressed by the request and eligible at authoring time.

schemas/agent-sidecar-exchange-projectio.title: Arkret Agent Sidecar Exchange Projection
schemas/agent-sidecar-exchange-projectio.description: Disposable controller-device-local cache for one source-routed native Sidecar exchange. Every field is a deterministic fold of accepted Sidecar-scoped Events. This object is not wire truth, is not Account Data, is never merged across devices, and may always be deleted and rebuilt.

terminal_event_id.description: Controller-authored ak.agent.sidecar.exchange.control Event that produced complete or failed.

exchange_id.description: Opaque controller-private idempotency identity; it is not a Sidecar locator and MUST NOT be copied into shared events.

folded_frontier.description: Local cache coverage. event_ids are the canonical sorted maximal causal heads of all contributing accepted exchange facts. event_set_digest commits to the canonical sorted complete contributing Event-id set. max_hlc is display/cache metadata only and never proves causal dominance.

schemas/agent-sidecar-view-state.schema..title: Arkret Agent Sidecar View State
schemas/agent-sidecar-view-state.schema..description: Controller-private encrypted account-data plaintext for one hosted Sidecar context. It changes only private presentation and never mutates either Strand, Track, access, read state, notifications, search, or event ownership.

schemas/agent-sidecar.schema.json.title: Arkret Agent Sidecar
schemas/agent-sidecar.schema.json.description: Controller-owned private AI workspace bound one-to-one to (realm_id, controller_id). Agent Sidecar is a first-class native protocol scope, not a Circle profile, backing Circle, or editable membership container. See spec/v1/zh/models/sidecar.md.

encryption_profile.description: Agent Sidecar is always protected by an independent MLS group; plaintext fallback is invalid.

schemas/agent-signer-evidence-operations.title: Arkret Agent Signer Evidence Operations
schemas/agent-signer-evidence-operations.description: Authenticated, anti-enumeration operation shapes for producing and resolving portable Native Agent signer evidence.

principal_id.description: Controller principal whose Account Authority lifecycle gate is being attested.

agent_authority_service_id.description: Native Agent PCR authority service assembling signer evidence. It MUST equal both the authenticated S2S caller and service_id in the controller principal's current AcceptedAtServiceBinding.

agent_authority_service_resolution.description: Current signed route and method-native control evidence for the Agent PCR authority. The Account Authority verifies this carrier before using its RFC 9421 keyid; a did_core_id, URL, bearer token or self-asserted public key is never a key source.

controller_account_gate_attestation_issu.description: Closed S2S request for the Account Authority-owned controller lifecycle gate. Agent state, account_id and raw account cell material are deliberately absent.

normalized_did_document.description: Exact normalized DID Document whose canonical digest equals method_history_evidence.evidence.document_digest. Its id MUST equal service_resolution_record.record.full_id; the record proof and HTTP Signature keyid MUST name a currently authorized assertionMethod in this document. The method-native evidence evaluator, not this caller assertion, authenticates the document.

authenticated_service_resolution.description: Self-contained verification input for high-risk inbound service authentication. The receiver validates method evidence against the document and signed record, enforces record freshness/currentness and only then verifies the RFC 9421 request.

controller_account_gate_attestation_issu.description: Byte-stable issuance outcome. The embedded attestation is the only Account Authority material admitted into AgentSignerEvidence.

schemas/agent-signer-evidence.schema.jso.title: Arkret Agent Signer Evidence
schemas/agent-signer-evidence.schema.jso.description: Closed portable evidence for one Native Agent signer. Current admission and historical Event verification are structurally disjoint. Historical validity is fixed by a destination-signed admission receipt; it is never reconstructed from a later current snapshot.

admission_evidence_digest.description: SHA-256 over RFC 8785 JCS of exactly {agent_authority_snapshot, controller_account_gate_attestation}. It never includes itself, a receipt or an outer attestation.

snapshot_digest.description: SHA-256 over RFC 8785 JCS of core only.

seal_lineage.description: Complete duplicate-free predecessor closure needed to connect the key and Agent-status witness Seals to frontier_seal_id. Every Seal is in principal_control_realm_id.

agent_snapshot_lease.description: Authority signature over domain ak.agent-authority-snapshot-v1 and every sibling field except proof.jws. Current admission checks the lease at verifier-now; historical verification checks it at the receipt accepted_at.

basis_digest.description: Digest of the Account Authority-private binding/status projection selected by basis. The portable object never carries a service-local account_id or raw account cell.

controller_account_gate_attestation.description: Privacy-minimal Account Authority gate. The authority signs domain ak.controller-account-gate-v1 and every field except proof.jws. account_id and raw account cell material are forbidden by the closed schema.

current_observation.description: Fresh request binding for new admission. All basis digests and Seal ids must match admission_evidence exactly; this object never appears in historical evidence.

event_admission_receipt.description: Destination-signed immutable record of the exact three-gate evidence used when this Event was accepted. The proof domain is ak.agent-signer-admission-receipt-v1 and covers every field except proof.jws.

core_digest.description: SHA-256 over RFC 8785 JCS of the complete top-level evidence with outer_attestation omitted.

outer_attestation.description: Anti-malleability assembly signature. It binds the tagged mode, request or receipt, admission evidence and optional transparency without replacing underlying authority proofs.

authorization.description: Key authorization only. Parent Agent/account gates never rewrite this interval and no cross-Realm valid-until scalar exists.

key_cell_value.description: Canonical resolved OR-set entries sorted by tag bytes. Raw or implementation-private JSON is not a valid state value.

realm_create_event_id.description: Accepted managed Agent PCR genesis ak.realm.create that materialized the first active status. This evidence object is assembled after both Events are accepted and never enters either digest preimage.

agent_provision_event_id.description: Accepted ak.agent.provision in the controller PCR whose payload.principal_control_realm_id equals retype(realm_create_event_id). The genesis create carries no reference to it, so a verifier resolves it by that reverse look-up.

schemas/agent-signing-key-binding.schema.title: Arkret Agent Signing Key Binding
schemas/agent-signing-key-binding.schema.description: Controller-authored minimal public binding between one Native Agent signing verification method, its raw Ed25519 key, and the accepted ak.agent.key.authorize Event. The authorize Event payload commits the digest of this object's binding core before agent_key_authorize_event_id and controller_proof are appended; those two fields are materialized only after the Event full identity is known, avoiding self-reference. Private pairing, scope, PoP, attestation, and capability material MUST NOT appear in this object.

agent_key_id.description: Exact payload.key_id of the bound ak.agent.key.authorize Event; used with agent_id to derive the authoritative agent-key cell subject.

public_key_digest.description: SHA-256 of public_key.key after base64url decoding to exactly 32 bytes, computed with agent_signing_public_key_digest; verification_method and alg are not in this digest domain.

agent_key_authorize_event_id.description: Complete identity of the already accepted authorize Event. This field is excluded from the binding core committed by that Event payload and is appended only after Event identity verification.

expires_at.description: Present iff the authorization itself declares expires_at. JSON null is forbidden.

key.description: Base64url without padding of exactly 32 Ed25519 public-key bytes.

schemas/applet-edge-operations.schema.js.title: Arkret Applet Edge Operation DTOs
schemas/applet-edge-operations.schema.js.description: Closed request/response DTOs for Applet edge and bridge operations.

applet_transaction_request_body.description: Body for ak.edge.applet.command.transaction. Transport-layer requirements are mandatory but not body fields: RFC 9421 Signature/Signature-Input, Source-Service-ID, Destination-Service-ID, Content-Digest, Idempotency-Key, received_at audit metadata, and a persisted source_signature_anchor. See zh/extensions/applet-integration.md section 7.3.1.

source_service_id.description: Must exactly match the Source-Service-ID header and the signed source-service-id component. It identifies the source service only; each Event still requires independent actor/applet/capability signature verification.

signals.description: Optional encrypted Signal Extension envelopes. Exact applet payload types and targets remain inside ciphertext.

schemas/applet-ghost-operations.schema.j.title: Arkret Applet Ghost Actor Operation DTOs
schemas/applet-ghost-operations.schema.j.description: Closed request/response DTOs for ak.self.applet.ghost.command.provision. An installed Applet service / bridge submits a complete service-signed accountability Event and delegated Ghost profile Event for one external user. The Principal Server MUST re-check their applet / service / realm / namespace / capability bindings and commit the pair atomically; it MUST NOT mint either proof with a server notary key.

ghost_actor_provision_request_body.description: Request body for ak.self.applet.ghost.command.provision. ghost_actor_id MUST fall inside the actor namespace declared by the applet_id registration; protocol / tenant / external_user_id identify the external principal being mirrored.

accountability_grant_event.description: Complete ak.identity.accountability_grant Event signed by the installed Applet service DID. Its nested accountability proof MUST be signed by the same service identity.

profile_event.description: Complete ak.profile.create Event for ghost_actor_id, delegated and signed by service_id. authorization_ref MUST identify the active ak.applet.ghost.provision capability grant and refs MUST bind the accountability Event.

ghost_actor_provision_outcome.description: Response for ak.self.applet.ghost.command.provision. Carries the durable event refs the Principal Server atomically accepted (or re-confirmed on an identical idempotent replay). authorization_ref is the active Applet provisioning capability grant used by the submitted pair; the accountability grant is not an authorization grant for later Ghost actions.

schemas/applet-install-operations.schema.title: Arkret Applet Install Operation DTOs
schemas/applet-install-operations.schema.description: Closed request/response DTOs for ak.self.applet.install.command.preview, ak.self.applet.command.install, and ak.self.applet.command.revoke. The InstallPlan body itself is defined in applet-install-plan.schema.json.

registration_event.description: Caller-signed formal registration Event. actor_id MUST equal the authenticated install admin, payload MUST exactly equal the registration derived from applet_package, and the controller proof copied into payload.proof remains independently required.

capability_grant_events.description: Caller-signed formal capability-grant Events. Each Event actor and grant issuer MUST equal the authenticated install admin; subjects, actions, resources and applet_authority constraints MUST exactly match the recomputed install plan and effective_scope.

capability_revoke_events.description: Exactly one caller-signed ak.capability.revoke initial submission for every active grant in the recomputed plan.

membership_state_events.description: Caller-signed membership removals in the plan, or an empty array when the install owns no managed membership.

proof.description: Required when revoke_mode includes delegated session revocation in production. The proof signs the canonical ak.gate.account.command.revoke_session transcript reconstructed from the active applet install selector.

schemas/applet-install-plan.schema.json.title: Arkret Applet InstallPlan
schemas/applet-install-plan.schema.json.description: Canonical plan returned by ak.self.applet.install.command.preview and recomputed by ak.self.applet.command.install before commit. plan_digest is calculated over the canonical InstallPlan object with plan_digest omitted.

schemas/applet-package.schema.json.title: Arkret Applet Package
schemas/applet-package.schema.json.description: Controller-signed package used to install an Applet. The package is a distribution object, not Realm history truth and not a grant. Principal Server / authz service derives ak.applet.registration and capability grants during ak.applet.install.

package_id.description: Distribution identifier only. Not a grant subject.

proof.description: Controller DID detached proof over the canonical package or derived registration object. proof.payload_digest MUST equal package_digest (proof over canonical package) or the derived registration object digest. Empty object is invalid.

detached_proof.description: Controller-DID detached-JWS proof shape, aligned with event-envelope.schema.json#/$defs/proof (the generic non-Event signed-object proof). Non-Event objects bind their canonical payload via payload_digest; Event proofs MUST instead use event_digest and event_proof.

webhook_auth.description: HTTP message signature verification seal for transaction push. key_ref is the Applet service DID URL used as the app/bridge->arkret inbound source signature anchor. Verifiers MUST take its bare controller full_id, validate it with the registered method adapter, and require project(full_id) to equal service_id (did_core_id); direct full-DID/core-id string comparison is forbidden. The key is bound to the effective registration_epoch. accepted_signature_algorithms pins the acceptable RFC 9421 signature algorithms.

key_ref.description: DID URL under an Applet service full_id whose registered adapter projection equals service_id. For app/bridge->arkret inbound transaction push, Signature-Input keyid MUST equal this value. Node->Applet pushes verify the Arkret source service full_id/key binding selected by the Source-Service-ID did_core_id, not this field.

endpoint_policy.description: Supported Applet API endpoints and their auth requirement.

limits.description: Service-side resource hints derived into the registration manifest.

ghost_policy.description: Ghost Actor support and accountability template. enabled defaults to false semantics; an explicit boolean is required.

delegation_policy.description: Delegated native-user acting request. Defaults to false; enabled MUST be explicit.

e2ee_policy.description: MLS join request. Defaults to false; enabled MUST be explicit.

widget.description: Optional Applet widget declaration. When present, it MUST validate ak.schema.applet_widget_declaration.v1.

schemas/applet-registration-epoch-transc.title: Arkret Applet Registration Epoch Transcript
schemas/applet-registration-epoch-transc.description: Closed, normalized security transcript hashed to produce an Applet registration_epoch. The hash input is the UTF-8 domain separator arkret-applet-registration-epoch-v1\n followed by the JCS bytes of this object.

full_id.description: Complete service DID whose adapter projection MUST equal derived_registration.service_id.

schemas/applet-widget-declaration.schema.title: Applet Widget Declaration
schemas/applet-widget-declaration.schema.description: Closed declaration for an Applet UI widget origin, CSP, scoped token capability scope, and consent gate.

widget_origin.description: HTTPS origin only: scheme, host, and optional port; no path, query, or fragment.

csp.description: Content-Security-Policy that the host client MUST enforce for the widget document.

token_scope.description: Maximum capability scope for the short-lived widget token.

schemas/applet.schema.json.title: Arkret Applet Protocol Object
schemas/applet.schema.json.description: Schema-registry object for applet protocol metadata snapshots. Event payloads for ak.applet.* MUST use the typed payload definitions in event-payload.schema.json; this object is not a loose transport envelope and is closed at the top level except for x_* extensions.

applet_id.description: Stable applet identifier. MUST be either a did_core_id or the registered typed-id form ak:applet:<uuidv7>. Arbitrary opaque strings are not valid wire identifiers; bridge-specific aliases belong in namespace / external_ref fields.

service_id.description: Stable did_core_id of the service that hosts the applet runtime; current resolution is supplied by its authenticated service definition.

manifest.description: Applet manifest snapshot at registration time (capability requirements, supported intents, etc.).

schemas/audit-release-attestation.schema.title: Arkret Audit Release Attestation
schemas/audit-release-attestation.schema.description: Structured remote attestation for an audit applet release service under ak.profile.attested_audit.e2ee.v1. This is the wire form behind audit_assurance_class=attested_hardware: a verifier MUST be able to validate release-service measurement, attestation chain trust root, attestation key freshness, operator identity, Realm/Circle binding, and audit release policy digest without trusting prose declarations. The attestation binds the controlled output path for ak.audit.release; it does not add the applet to MLS and does not grant signal plaintext access. See zh/crypto-media/audited-e2ee.md §6.

realm_id.description: Realm this attestation evidence is valid for. Verifier MUST require realm_id to match the MLS Welcome / Event Envelope Realm being joined or audited; identical audit_policy_version_digest values across Realms do not make evidence portable.

audit_service_actor_id.description: Stable did_core_id of the audit release service / applet actor whose controlled output path this evidence attests. MUST match the recipient_audit_actor_id or service actor accepted by the active ak.audit.applet_binding.

service_id.description: Stable operating service did_core_id hosting the audit applet or release service. MUST match the service_id in the active ak.audit.applet_binding / ak.audit.release chain.

family.description: Attestation family. 'software_test_only' is for conformance fixtures and MUST be rejected by deployments declaring attested_hardware assurance.

measurement.description: What is actually running inside the enclave / HSM / equivalent controlled output boundary. Verifiers compare this measurement to the measurement allowed by the active audit applet binding and release policy.

code_digest.description: Hash of the audit release service binary / image / policy bundle that the enclave loads. MUST be reproducible (signed by vendor build pipeline).

policy_version.description: Release service's compiled-in policy version (e.g. semantic version or git tag). MUST appear in the Realm/Circle audit binding's allowed release-service policy versions at issued_at.

report_data.description: Optional REPORTDATA-equivalent that binds the attestation to the release service public key or output-encryption key. Lowercase hex encoding of a 32–64 byte byte-string (pattern enforces an even hex length: each byte is exactly two hex characters; total 64–128 hex characters). Receivers MUST validate this binding when present.

attestation_chain.description: Ordered attestation evidence chain: leaf attestation (signed by the enclave) → intermediate (e.g. PCK certificate, AK certificate) → root (vendor attestation root certificate). Each item is base64url-encoded DER / CBOR per platform format. Verifier MUST validate signature chain and trust the root against the Realm-declared trust root list.

attestation_key.description: The attestation public key (extracted from the leaf of attestation_chain). ak.audit.release proofs and RYW receipt validation MUST be cryptographically bound to this attested output path when audit_assurance_class=attested_hardware.

verification_method.description: DID URL the receiving verifier uses to resolve attestation_key. MUST live under audit_service_actor_id's DID Document or a DID Document explicitly delegated by the active audit binding. Fragment characters are constrained to the ASCII set `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]` (a strict subset of RFC 3986 unreserved, excluding `~`, plus `:`) for stable byte-comparable key ids; see the Arkret verification-method DID URL profile in identity/did-usage-and-verification.md section 2.2. DID method-name normalized to lowercase per W3C DID 1.0.

validity.description: Validity window of THIS evidence. Verifier MUST reject evidence outside the window. For evidence presented under audit_assurance_class=attested_hardware (ak.profile.attested_audit.e2ee.v1), the verifier MUST reject evidence whose window (expires_at - not_before) exceeds 90 days; Realm/service policy MAY cap it lower. Evidence with a longer window MUST be treated as an elevated-risk signal and rejected by profile policy rather than silently accepted.

revocation.description: How the verifier should check whether attestation_chain leaves / intermediates have been revoked. Required when platform supports revocation (sgx_pccs CRL, tdx PCS, etc.).

operator_principal_id.description: DID of the controlling organization actually operating this enclave / HSM. This intentionally keeps the _did suffix because it is raw external DID material being compared against service_id and Realm policy, not a protocol actor_id/principal_id alias. MUST match what the Realm policy lists as the allowed audit operator. Distinct from service_id when the operating org is different from the technical service DID (e.g. service hosted by org A on behalf of org B).

audit_purpose.description: Why this audit applet release service may output audit material. MUST match the active binding/session purpose; mismatch → audit_purpose_mismatch.
