audit_policy_version_digest.description: Same definition as ak.audit.ryw_receipt.audit_policy_version_digest — fixed sha256 over canonical JSON {realm_id, trust_domain, audit_binding, release_policy, release_window_policy, activation_frontier_digest, first_auditable_epoch} at the Realm policy frontier at issued_at. Lets verifier O(1) check that the policy classification this evidence was issued under matches the current binding/session state, cannot be reused across Realms, and cannot retroactively expand eligibility for already encrypted messages. This field is intentionally not hash-agile in v1; a future algorithm change requires a new schema/profile. See encoding.md §2 (canonical JSON) and audited-e2ee.md §6.

proofs.description: Detached signature(s) over the canonical evidence bytes (all fields except `proofs`), signed by operator-controlled keys distinct from the enclave attestation key. Two-key separation: the enclave attests its own measurement; the operator separately attests that this enclave is the one they intend to deploy.

schemas/audit-ryw-receipt.schema.json.title: Arkret Audit RYW Receipt
schemas/audit-ryw-receipt.schema.json.description: Read-Your-Writes receipt issued by an Events API node, witness, or peer Principal Server confirming that a ak.audit.release or other audit envelope has reached accepted state. Required by ak.profile.attested_audit.e2ee.v1 and ak.profile.disclosed_audit.e2ee.v1 before an audit applet release service may output wrapped material or plaintext evidence (see zh/crypto-media/audited-e2ee.md §6). The audit_assurance_class field MUST match the active Audit Applet Binding; mismatch fail closed.

trust_domain.description: Deployment trust domain for the Realm at the receipt frontier. Verifiers MUST require this to match the current receive context and the enclosing audit Event Realm context before using audit_policy_version_digest.

realm_operator_organization.description: DID of the Realm operator's ultimate controlling organization at this receipt frontier. Verifiers MUST derive and verify it from the Realm service/operator DID control chain; it is not a self-attested label. For federation_witness_attested, every witness controlling_organization MUST be distinct from this value and from any organization under the same ultimate controller.

kind.description: Attestation kind derived from witnesses[]. 'federation_witness_attested' MUST be used iff witnesses[] contains >= 2 distinct entries (distinct issuer.did AND distinct controlling_organization AND distinct verification_method), each issuer.did is listed by Realm policy under audit.ryw_witnesses[], and no witness controlling organization equals or is ultimately controlled by realm_operator_organization. 'single_source' MUST be used iff witnesses[] contains exactly 1 entry. Any mismatch between 'kind' and the witnesses[] cardinality / distinctness / Realm policy listing / operator independence MUST be rejected with audit_receipt_invalidated. The value is externally verifiable from the witness list, not a self-claim.

issuer.description: Service DID of the witness that produced this receipt.

verification_method.description: DID URL of the key the witness used to sign (e.g. did:web:...#key-1). MUST be distinct from other witnesses' verification_method values for 'federation_witness_attested' to be valid.

controlling_organization.description: DID of the organization that controls the witness. This value is not self-attested: verifiers MUST resolve issuer DID Document and confirm its controller / service ownership chain matches controlling_organization. For 'federation_witness_attested', all witnesses' controlling_organization values MUST be pairwise distinct and MUST NOT equal the audit actor's controlling organization or realm_operator_organization, including common ultimate controllers.

attested_at.description: Time at which this witness attested. Receivers MAY use the latest attested_at across witnesses as the effective receipt timestamp.

witnesses.description: Externally verifiable list of witnesses attesting that the audit_event_id+audit_event_digest reached accepted state. The 'kind' field MUST be derivable from this list per the rules in §4.1.1.

witness_attestation.description: Witness attestation block. The receipt's independence is externally verifiable from the witnesses[] list rather than self-claimed via a single enum. See zh/crypto-media/audited-e2ee.md §4.1 / §4.1.1.

audit_assurance_class.description: Audit assurance class propagated from the active Audit Applet Binding. attested_hardware = ak.profile.attested_audit.e2ee.v1 (TEE/HSM/enclave controlled release required). disclosed_policy = ak.profile.disclosed_audit.e2ee.v1 (process-only disclosure, NOT cryptographically enforced). Release services MUST propagate the binding-declared value verbatim; receivers MUST fail closed when this field disagrees with the binding/policy state at the receipt's frontier.

audit_policy_version_digest.description: Canonical hash of the Realm-bound audit release policy tuple from the receipt frontier. Computed as fixed sha256 over canonical JSON {realm_id: <id>, trust_domain: <trust_domain>, audit_binding: <object>, release_policy: <object>, release_window_policy: <object>, activation_frontier_digest: <hash>, first_auditable_epoch: <n>}. Lets verifiers atomically check that the receipt's claim matches the active binding/policy at this frontier without replaying events and prevents cross-Realm reuse or retroactive expansion of identical policy text. MUST match the receipt frontier's policy state and ak.audit.release.eligibility_proof; mismatch MUST fail closed (audit_receipt_invalidated). Required field — missing receipts MUST be rejected to prevent silent policy drift. This field is intentionally not hash-agile in v1; a future algorithm change requires a new schema/profile.

recovery_reason_code.description: Optional machine-readable code, set only when this RYW receipt covers a ak.audit.accessed Event emitted via the Late Key Recovery path (see zh/crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md §2.3.5 and zh/crypto-media/audited-e2ee.md §4.1). Payload value, not an error-code-registry reason_code. Used by audit projections to distinguish late-key-triggered accesses from first-access reads. When absent, the receipt covers a normal (first-access) ak.audit.accessed Event.

schemas/authority-set-policy.schema.json.title: Arkret Authority Set Policy
schemas/authority-set-policy.schema.json.description: Canonical, basis-resolvable authority policy bound by AuthoritySetRef. authority_set_digest is SHA-256(JCS(the complete object)).

schemas/authz-operations.schema.json.title: Arkret Authorization Operation DTOs
schemas/authz-operations.schema.json.description: Closed response DTOs for authorization query operations that need operation-specific list envelopes.

schemas/availability-receipt.schema.json.title: Arkret AvailabilityReceipt
schemas/availability-receipt.schema.json.description: Signed holder commitment that Event bytes are available until retention_expires_at. Digest membership roots do not prove byte availability; CBA models availability independently.

payload_digest.description: Hash of canonical AvailabilityReceipt bytes with signature omitted.

schemas/blob-operations.schema.json.title: Arkret Blob Operation DTOs
schemas/blob-operations.schema.json.description: Closed request/response DTOs for blob service operations whose wire shape is not the full blob metadata resource.

kid.description: DID URL of the concrete issuer verification method. Bare DID is not accepted because the receipt must pin one already accepted service key binding.

content.description: The binary blob content part in multipart/form-data. This field is not JCS-canonicalized as JSON; content_digest covers the bytes.

key_ref.$comment: MUST stay identical to encrypted-envelope.schema.json#/properties/key_ref and encryption-and-audit.md §2.3.1. Closed MLS group-binding object; not an opaque string.

oneOf.description: Reference to accepted ak.mls.genesis / winning ak.mls.commit event.

group_state_ref.description: v1 MLS group state lookup hint. MUST point to accepted ak.mls.genesis / winning ak.mls.commit / equivalent group state proof. Does NOT replace MLS transcript verification.

oneOf.$comment: whole-file AEAD form: single nonce, single ciphertext_digest
streaming chunked AEAD form (STREAM / OAE2): per-segment AEAD, per-object random nonce_prefix

not.$comment: byte counts use size_bytes
content hashes use content_digest with an algorithm prefix

realm_id.description: Owning Realm for authorization, asset privacy policy enforcement, retention and GC. MAY be omitted only for global / cross-Realm service blobs (e.g. avatar previews) explicitly authorized by the Blob Service deployment policy.

schemas/bottom.schema.json.title: Arkret Bottom Diagnostics
schemas/bottom.schema.json.description: Structured diagnostic for cell join values that resolve to bottom (⊥). Surfaced on /account/subscribe, /events, and state query responses when a cell's effective Lattice value is undefined under the current CBA query basis. See spec/v1/zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md §5.1.

kind.description: Why the join produced bottom. 'conflict' = concurrent cas_register / fsm divergence on safety-critical cell. 'invalid_transition' = fsm op violates allowed_transitions. 'missing_dependency' = event ref to absent / failed prior event. 'unauthorized' = event issuer lacks capability for the op (verifier-side). 'notary_split' = multiple Seal leaves diverge on next-seal authority. 'schema_error' = lattice op or value violates declared cell schema.

cells.description: Cell ids participating in the bottom diagnostic. Multi-cell when a multi-cell Control Move atomically failed across linked cells.

event_ids.description: Reducer-input event ids whose effects (or precondition checks) produced this bottom. Empty allowed when the cell's bottom is structural (e.g. notary cell schema_error) and not tied to a specific event.

seal_view.description: Seal leaves and control frontier under which this bottom was observed. Diagnostics MUST pin this so the receiver can reproduce the join without ambiguity.

state_root.description: Control-plane state_root at observation time (recompute from Seal leaves). Optional when the diagnostic is emitted before state_root is computable.

heads.description: When kind=conflict and the cell's lattice exposes multiple candidate heads (mv_register, or_set with conflicting tag values), the candidate values. Implementations MUST NOT pick a winner from this array; it is for UI / audit only.

details.description: Free-form structured details specific to the diagnostic kind. Producers SHOULD use stable keys per kind (e.g. invalid_transition: from/to/expected_transitions; schema_error: schema_id/violation_path). Receivers MAY display but MUST NOT use for authorization decisions.

escalated_at.description: When the cell first crossed Realm.bottom_escalation_after_ms. Absent when within the grace window. Implementations SHOULD raise an out-of-band notification to admins / recovery governance once set.

schemas/calendar-event.schema.json.title: Arkret Calendar Event Profile Fields
schemas/calendar-event.schema.json.description: Schedule subtree carried at Strand metadata.fields.calendar and activated by ak.schema.calendar_event.v1 in Strand.schema_refs. Both directions of that binding are enforced by strand.schema.json. All intervals are half-open [start, end). Timed events carry RFC 8984 LocalDateTime wall-clock anchors resolved through timezone plus tzdb_version; this schema never carries an absolute instant.

start.description: Inclusive lower bound of the event interval, and the recurrence anchor. Narrowed to local_date when all_day is true and to local_date_time when it is false.

end.description: Exclusive upper bound of the event interval, in the same shape as start. MUST be strictly later than start in both branches; a single all-day event spells end as the following date. JSON Schema cannot express the cross-field comparison, so reducers and profiles enforce it with schema_violation.

timezone.description: Canonical IANA Zone name in the release named by tzdb_version. Producers MUST resolve Link aliases to their canonical Zone before signing per calendar-timezone-registry.json; this pattern only constrains shape.

tzdb_version.description: IANA TZDB release tag (for example 2026a) whose rules resolve timezone and every derived instant. Signed with the schedule so receivers never silently substitute their locally installed release.

all_day.description: True selects the date branch of start/end/recurrence.until; false selects the whole-second LocalDateTime branch.

status.description: Whole-event schedule status. Required with no implicit default; distinct from the generic Strand stage and state axes. cancelled rejects new RSVPs and is schedule-relevant for notification.

call_id.description: Soft reference to an Arkret call session. It never widens access: an unresolvable or invisible call_id MUST NOT leak call state.

attendees.description: The single canonical schedule roster. Membership and invite projections are producer inputs only, never a second projection truth source. actor_id uniqueness is enforced by the reducer; at most one organizer is enforced here by maxContains.

allOf.$comment: All-day branch: start, end and recurrence.until are Gregorian dates.
Timed branch: start, end and recurrence.until are whole-second LocalDateTime values.

recurrence.description: RFC 8984 RecurrenceRule snake_case subset. Omitted interval means 1, omitted first_day_of_week means mo, rscale is Gregorian and skip is omit; the JSCalendar @type discriminator is implied by this schema and MUST NOT appear on the wire. Unlisted RecurrenceRule members, excluded rules, overrides, RDATE and EXDATE are rejected rather than ignored.

until.description: Inclusive termination bound compared against the occurrence local start with <=. Narrowed to the same branch as start/end by all_day, and MUST NOT be earlier than the base start.

allOf.$comment: nth_of_period selects an occurrence within a month or year and is meaningless for daily/weekly recurrence.
by_month_day filters a month position and cannot combine with weekly recurrence.
by_set_position selects from a candidate set and requires at least one candidate-producing by_* rule.

role.description: Attendance role. Omitted means required. organizer is display and scheduling semantics only and grants no capability.

display_name_snapshot.description: Identity-revealing display snapshot. It MUST be encrypted together with the rest of the schedule whenever Strand metadata is encrypted.

schemas/call-recording-artifact.schema.j.title: Arkret Call Recording Artifact
schemas/call-recording-artifact.schema.j.description: Canonical metadata for a call recording artifact after it has entered the Arkret blob pipeline. It binds the blob, recording start event, MLS exporter recording key context, retention policy and deletion audit surface without introducing a ak:recording or ak:artifact storage key.

content_digest.description: Digest published by the Arkret blob pipeline for the stored recording object.

ciphertext_digest.description: Digest of encrypted recording bytes. This MUST match encryption.ciphertext_digest and the referenced encrypted blob metadata.

produced_by.description: Media service DID or recorder service DID that produced the encrypted recording bytes.

recording_initiator_capability_ref.description: Capability grant reference proving the recording was initiated by an actor holding ak.call.record.

deletion_audit.description: Present only after a delete attempt is scheduled, completed, or blocked. The referenced erasure receipt remains the durable audit proof.

call_recording_retention.description: Retention contract for a recording or transcript capture artifact. retention_expires_at is the earliest deletion time; deletion_trigger declares the only accepted purge cause; audit_lock blocks all purge paths until an audit-grade release is accepted; consent_confirmed records the required second client-side capture confirmation.

retention_expires_at.description: Earliest time the artifact MAY be purged. Absent = governed by retention_policy_id. MUST NOT be in the past at write time.

audit_lock.description: When true the artifact is under audit / legal hold; purge MUST be rejected with legal_hold_active until the lock is released by an audit-grade action.

consent_confirmed.description: Records that the second client-side confirmation required before recording or transcript capture was obtained.

trigger_event_id.description: Durable event that caused this delete attempt, when the trigger is event-backed.

erasure_receipt_ref.description: ak.audit.erasure_receipt event, ak.schema.erasure_receipt.v1 object, or digest proving the deletion outcome.

schemas/call-signal-plaintext.schema.jso.title: Arkret Call Signal Plaintext
schemas/call-signal-plaintext.schema.jso.description: Closed top-level plaintext object carried inside a SignalEnvelope encrypted_payload for ak.call.signal. The signal_kind-specific data object is validated by the corresponding normative branch in zh/crypto-media/webrtc-signaling.md.

payload_sequence.description: Strictly increasing but non-contiguous u64 within (sender_device_id, canonical scope_ref); arbitrary forward gaps are accepted. It is independent of seq, the per-call anti-rollback sequence monotonic over (realm_id, call_id, actor_id, device_id).

data.description: Signal-kind-specific payload. Producers and consumers MUST additionally validate the closed field rules for the selected signal_kind in webrtc-signaling.md; this extension point is encrypted end-to-end and is not interpreted by the Signal service.

subject_authority_instance.description: MUST be present when subject is a human principal did_core_id. It freezes the PCR lineage this grant accepts; a same-core proof from any other instance cannot exercise or inherit the grant. Omitted for condition selectors and roles governed by a different explicit authority contract.

items.description: Canonical action vocabulary. MUST be of the form ak.<segment>.<segment>... matching capabilities.md §5. Bare names without the ak. prefix are not permitted; consult capabilities.md before introducing new action names. Wildcards within a segment are not permitted in this schema; the resource selector controls scope, not action expansion.

capability_action_registry_digest.description: JCS SHA-256 digest of the complete canonical capability-action-registry.json snapshot used to expand aggregate_admin actions. Required by the reducer whenever actions[] contains an action whose registry row has event_mapping_kind=aggregate_admin; optional and audit-only otherwise. Unknown or unavailable snapshots fail closed with capability_registry_basis_unavailable.

constraints.description: Constraints applied to this grant. Re-grant control MUST be expressed via constraint_kind='authority_control' and max_authority_depth (see capabilities.md §10). A top-level 'delegable' field is forbidden and MUST be rejected as schema_violation. With no authority_control constraint the grant cannot be re-granted (equivalent to max_authority_depth=0).

issued_at.description: Grant issuance time — carries the 'creation time' semantics for a Capability Grant in place of the generic created_at (models/common-fields.md §3.2). Retention / audit / ordering queries MUST use issued_at / expires_at / revoked_at rather than falling back to created_at.

not_before.description: Top-level grant validity start. Authorization evaluates this together with temporal constraints: effective_not_before = max(not_before, every temporal.not_before present).

expires_at.description: Top-level grant validity end. Authorization evaluates this together with temporal constraints: effective_expires_at = min(expires_at, every temporal.expires_at present). A grant MUST NOT outlast the effective_expires_at of the refs that cover a given action.

updated_by.description: Reducer-derived actor that produced the most recent grant lifecycle update. Ordinary grant body fields remain immutable; revocation still uses revoked_by/revoked_at.

updated_at.description: Reducer-derived timestamp for the most recent grant lifecycle update. Ordinary grant body fields remain immutable; revocation still uses revoked_by/revoked_at.

issuer_authority_refs.description: The authority this grant was issued under. Every grant has one: a root controller’s grant anchors on the authority-root cell, and any further grant anchors on the grants its issuer already holds. The typed ref is the only distinction within the unified grant shape. Authorization is recomputed from these refs on every decision, so revoking an ancestor invalidates its descendants at read time without any cascading write.

oneOf.description: A grant the issuer holds. The issuer MUST be that grant's subject, and the ref MUST be active at evaluation time; its capability, resources and constraints all bound this child.

controller_epoch_at_issuance.description: The controller epoch under which this grant was issued. It proves the issuer controlled the root at issuance and nothing more: it is issuance audit, not a liveness version. Comparing it to the current epoch would make ak.realm.owner.transfer kill the whole authority tree.

authority_generation.description: The authority generation this grant is anchored to. Unlike the epoch this IS compared to the cell's current value: ak.realm.authority.reset advances it precisely so an entire authority tree stops resolving.

oneOf.description: The Realm authority-root cell. A rooted terminal: it never contributes an edge to the cycle check. realm_id is explicit rather than inherited from the envelope because ak.capability.derived can carry roots from another Realm.

authority_depth.description: Reducer-derived absolute distance from the authority root: a realm_root ref counts 0, so a root controller's grant is 1 and a member's re-grant is 2. Derived from the refs, never author-declared, so it cannot be misreported — which is what makes it safe to answer 'how far did this authority spread' with a single field instead of a recursive join. Taken at issuance and not recomputed on revocation; a later chain may be shorter than the recorded value, which is the conservative direction for a max_authority_depth decision.

authority_root_refs.description: Reducer-derived set of roots this grant ultimately descends from: the direct realm_root refs plus the union of every grant ref's own roots. Plural because multiple parents, and ak.capability.derived inheritance across a Realm link, can reach different roots or generations. Deduplicated on (realm_id, cell_ref, authority_generation) and sorted canonically by unsigned-byte order; controller_epoch_at_issuance is per-grant issuance audit and is deliberately not part of the identity key.

allOf.$comment: Lint condition (2) from capabilities.md §18.1: grants whose actions[] include moderator-role actions MUST carry a constraint with depends_on_moderation_state=true. Conditions (1) and (3) (subject condition selector referencing moderation state, constraints referencing moderation queue/cell) are reducer-side lint and not enforced here.

schemas/cba-proof-bundle.schema.json.title: Arkret CBA Proof Bundle
schemas/cba-proof-bundle.schema.json.description: Unsigned receiver-relative dependency container for exactly one target_seal_ref. Every embedded object MUST belong to the target Realm, be reachable from the target Seal dependency graph, appear in canonical id/digest bytewise order without duplicates, and be independently verified; the bundle itself is not authoritative. A bounded verifiable superset is allowed, but unrelated objects are a schema violation. inclusion_proofs and availability_proofs together MUST contain no more than 2048 items; this cross-property aggregate and the dependency path depth limit of 4096 are semantic validation rules in addition to each array's local JSON Schema bound.

control_moves.description: Control Move Event envelopes only. Semantic validation MUST reject DataEvent, Anchor Unit, actor-private, or unknown non-control Event shapes even when the generic Event Envelope schema is otherwise valid.

inclusion_proofs.description: Inclusion proofs. The combined item count of this array and availability_proofs MUST be no greater than 2048.

availability_proofs.description: Availability proofs. The combined item count of this array and inclusion_proofs MUST be no greater than 2048.

schemas/circle-operations.schema.json.title: Arkret Circle Self-Management Operation DTOs
schemas/circle-operations.schema.json.description: Closed request/response DTOs for the self-surface Circle administration operations (ak.self.circle.*). Every write operation carries the caller-signed ak.circle.* Event and the service submits those exact bytes through ordinary Event admission; the durable Circle object model is circle.schema.json. See spec/v1/zh/models/circle.md and spec/v1/zh/sync/service-http-binding.md.

circle_view.description: Circle projection row returned by create/get/lifecycle operations. Field set mirrors circle.schema.json; reducer-managed fields (mls_group_ref, state, members, created_at) are read-only outputs.

profile_ref.description: Create-locked Circle semantic profile discriminator. Ordinary Circles omit it; profile-specific Circles expose it so clients can apply mandatory filtering.

mls_group_ref.description: Reducer-derived MLS group reference; present only when encryption_profile='mls_rfc9420'.

member_count.description: Exact count of active Circle members. Present only when the caller is an active Circle member; directory-only previews MUST omit it and use the privacy-bucketed preview contract instead.

viewer_membership.description: The caller's own Circle membership state when one exists.

members.description: Active Circle member DIDs (strict subset of parent Realm.members). Empty after tombstone.

circle_create_request_body.description: Carries the caller-signed ak.circle.create Event and nothing else. The Circle id is retype(create_event.event.event_id), so the service cannot name the Circle and MUST NOT synthesize the Event: every actor-supplied field lives in create_event.event.payload.object, and the parent Realm is create_event.event.realm_id. See spec/v1/zh/models/circle.md and spec/v1/zh/sync/service-http-binding.md.

create_event.description: Closed ak.circle.create Event authored and signed by the authenticated caller. The service MUST submit these exact bytes through ordinary Event admission and MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event, nor accept a body-local signature fallback. Admission MUST verify that event.actor_id is the authenticated caller, that event.realm_id names the parent Realm the caller holds ak.circle.create in, and that payload.object carries neither id nor the reducer-derived mls_group_ref. encryption_profile='none' is allowed only when the parent Realm policy floor permits plaintext.

circle_member_request_body.description: Carries the caller-signed ak.circle.member.state Event and nothing else. The target actor and the membership value live in member_event.event.payload; the Circle is payload.circle_id and MUST equal the path circle_id. The service MUST NOT add a capability verdict to the payload it submits: circle_member_state_payload is closed, and the ak.circle.member.manage decision is the admission path's, evaluated against projected grants rather than asserted by the request.

member_event.description: Closed ak.circle.member.state Event authored and signed by the authenticated caller. The service MUST submit these exact bytes through ordinary Event admission and MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event. Admission MUST verify that event.actor_id is the authenticated caller and that payload.circle_id names the path Circle. Moving another actor to join requires ak.circle.member.manage narrowed by allowed_circle_ids, and the target MUST already be a joined parent-Realm member; knock requires join_rule=knock. A self-service join is gated on the Circle join_rule instead.

circle_member_delete_request_body.description: Carries the caller-signed ak.circle.member.state leave Event and nothing else. The path circle_id and actor_id MUST respectively equal member_event.event.payload.circle_id and payload.actor_id; member_event.event.realm_id MUST equal the path Circle's parent Realm. The service submits the exact signed Event through ordinary Event admission and MUST NOT rebuild it or synthesize a leave Event.

member_event.description: Closed ak.circle.member.state Event authored and signed by the authenticated caller, with membership fixed to leave and expected_membership carrying the concrete current membership as the signed head_eq guard. Admission MUST bind the Event proof to the exact authority instance selected by the authenticated session; matching only the caller DID is insufficient. Removing another actor requires ak.circle.member.manage narrowed to the path Circle; self-service leave uses ak.circle.member.add.

note.description: Reducer-emitted reason code on Ignored / Rejected, or unsupported-feature note while MLS scope rotation is not wired end-to-end.

circle_archive_request_body.description: Carries the caller-signed ak.circle.archive Event and nothing else. The target Circle is lifecycle_event.event.payload.target_ref and MUST equal the path circle_id; an optional human-readable reason is payload.reason. Archive, restore and tombstone take separate request defs because each pins its own Event kind.

lifecycle_event.description: Closed ak.circle.archive Event authored and signed by the authenticated caller.

circle_restore_request_body.description: Carries the caller-signed ak.circle.restore Event and nothing else. Same shape as circle_archive_request_body with the Event kind pinned to restore.

lifecycle_event.description: Closed ak.circle.restore Event authored and signed by the authenticated caller.

circle_tombstone_request_body.description: Carries the caller-signed ak.circle.tombstone Event and nothing else. Tombstone is terminal: the lifecycle transition matrix admits no transition out of it, so the Event the caller signs is the whole record of who ended the Circle.

lifecycle_event.description: Closed ak.circle.tombstone Event authored and signed by the authenticated caller.

circle_lifecycle_event_submission.description: Shared submission shape for the three Circle lifecycle Events. Its payload is object_lifecycle_payload, so the target Circle is single-sourced by target_ref. The service MUST submit these exact bytes through ordinary Event admission and MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event; admission MUST verify that event.actor_id is the authenticated caller, that payload.target_ref names the path Circle, and that the reducer's lifecycle transition matrix admits the transition from the Circle's current state.

schemas/circle.schema.json.title: Arkret Circle
schemas/circle.schema.json.description: Circle — intra-Realm scoped event/message boundary. Hosts its own membership (strict subset of parent Realm.members), history visibility, and delivery/query/projection boundary. It may be plaintext delivery-only or MLS-backed depending on encryption_profile and parent Realm policy floor. It does NOT carry federation identity, policy server, or capability registry — those remain on the parent Realm. Circle is NOT a principal Group; principal-set capability narrowing belongs on Group / capability constraint / resource selector. See spec/v1/zh/models/circle.md.

id.description: Present on the materialised object. MUST be absent from the create Event payload: zh/models/common-fields.md derives it from the create Event's own event_id (retyped), so a payload-supplied id would be a second, forgeable truth.

realm_id.description: Parent Realm. create-locked; Circle never re-binds to another Realm.

profile_ref.description: Optional create-locked Circle semantic profile discriminator. Ordinary Circles omit it. Profile-specific creation paths MUST persist their registered profile id. Agent Sidecar is a separate ak.schema.agent_sidecar.v1 object and MUST NOT be represented by this field.

directory_visibility.description: Who may see this Circle exists as a directory entry. 'members' means only Circle members see its title/display/member_count. 'realm_members' exposes directory metadata only and does NOT grant event or history access.

join_rule.description: How an actor becomes a Circle member. 'public' lets any active parent-Realm member self-join; it does not make the Circle globally discoverable. 'knock' requires the application/approval flow. 'invite' requires Circle admin add or invite.

history_visibility.description: Circle's own history visibility. Effective visibility MUST NOT be wider than the parent Realm's policy floor. See zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md §6.

content_encryption_floor.description: Optional Circle-local content encryption floor. When omitted, the Circle inherits the parent Realm's content_encryption_floor. Effective floor = max(parent Realm content_encryption_floor, this field). May only tighten, never widen, the parent Realm floor, and the effective floor is a one-way ratchet: once e2ee_required has been accepted it MUST NOT be lowered back to allow_plaintext (reducer rejects with content_encryption_floor_downgrade). e2ee_required is only meaningful when encryption_profile='mls_rfc9420'; a Circle with encryption_profile='none' MUST keep allow_plaintext. See zh/models/circle.md §7.

metadata_encryption_floor.description: Optional Circle-local metadata encryption floor (binary, symmetric with content_encryption_floor: allow_plaintext | e2ee_required). When omitted, the Circle inherits parent Realm's metadata_encryption_floor. May only tighten, never widen, parent Realm floor; the effective floor is a one-way ratchet (reducer rejects a lowering write with metadata_encryption_floor_downgrade).

agent_participation.description: Optional wrapped five-bit Agent ceiling. When present every bit is explicit and may only tighten the parent Realm ceiling.

encryption_profile.description: Circle content encryption profile. create-locked. 'none' means plaintext delivery/query/projection isolation only and is allowed only when the parent Realm policy floor allows plaintext. 'mls_rfc9420' means the Circle owns an independent MLS group and MUST NOT derive its keys from the Realm-default MLS group.

mls_group_ref.description: Reducer-derived reference to the independent MLS group bound to (realm_id, circle_id). Present only when encryption_profile='mls_rfc9420'. Populated by ak.circle.create reducer; not actor-supplied on wire.

state.description: Circle lifecycle state. v1 defines active, archived, and tombstoned only; Circle has no independent freeze or destroy state because parent Realm freeze/destroy applies at the Realm boundary.

short_name.description: Human-facing short name. Unique per (realm_id, short_name) case-insensitive — reducer-enforced. Circle naming has no Sidecar-reserved prefix because Sidecar is a separate native scope.

color_token.description: Color token from the spec-controlled palette. Clients MUST map token -> theme color (light/dark/high-contrast) consistently across devices; clients MUST NOT reassign tokens.

schemas/common-ids.schema.json.title: Arkret Common ID and Reference Definitions
schemas/common-ids.schema.json.description: Shared ID and reference pattern $defs referenced cross-file by multiple object schemas so a single form change propagates without inline drift. Defs-only: not an object or event schema. See zh/models/common-fields.md and artifacts/registry/id-kind-registry.json for the authoritative ID kind registry.

event_id.description: Complete Arkret Event cryptographic identity. The suffix is the canonical unpadded Base64URL encoding of exactly 33 octets: one registered active digest-suite wire_code followed by all 32 octets of the Event digest. Regex validation is only lexical; receivers MUST decode, require 33 octets, canonical re-encode, and verify the suite code and full digest before use.

did_core_id.description: Canonical stable DID-derived identity core. The lowercase DID method name follows ak:did_core:, and the remaining method-adapter-defined core is opaque to generic consumers. The did:web v1 adapter uses the complete canonical method-specific-id, never a digest or truncated host. Principal, actor and service identity equality is byte-for-byte equality of the complete did_core_id. A did_core_id is not a DID and cannot be resolved without a full_id or ServiceResolutionRecord.

did_full_id.description: Canonical bare DID used for registration, DID method resolution and owner-published current resolution. It contains no path, query or fragment and MUST project through the registered method adapter to exactly one did_core_id.

webvh_full_id.description: Canonical bare did:webvh identifier used at method-native registration, document and evidence boundaries. Role admission is enforced separately.

human_principal_full_id.description: Canonical bare DID for a v1 human principal anchor. The method set is derived from role_requirements.human_principal_anchor; capability checks for relocation, DID-root recovery and ongoing governance are separate.

managed_agent_full_id.description: Canonical bare did:webvh identity of a durable managed Agent. Its accepted bootstrap history is controller-authored and must contain a continuous inception followed by the create-locked PCR binding update.

ephemeral_pairwise_full_id.description: Realm-local ephemeral pairwise actor identifier. It is MLS LeafNode-bound and can never create a Principal Control Realm.

did_key_full_id.description: Canonical bare did:key identifier used at method-native key and witness evidence boundaries. This is a registered method-specific DidFullId subtype, not a business ActorId and not a DID URL.

did_url.description: Arkret verification-method DID URL profile (identity/did-usage-and-verification.md section 2.2): lowercase method name, no query, required fragment, fragment limited to ASCII [A-Za-z0-9._:-]. Every verification_method-family field and every kid/key_ref a schema declares to be a DID URL MUST resolve to exactly this definition; values compare byte-for-byte with no URI normalization or percent-decoding.

schemas/consent-operations.schema.json.title: Arkret Consent Cell Self-Management Operation DTOs
schemas/consent-operations.schema.json.description: Closed request/response DTOs for holder-private consent cells. Only holders/controllers receive consent_cell_view; peer request submission returns an opaque outcome and never exposes cell state.

active_grant_dots.description: Currently-active grant dots (not yet observed/revoked, within validity window).

consent_grant_request_body.description: Carries the caller-signed ak.consent.grant Control Move and nothing else. consent_id, peer, consent_scope, not_before and expires_at all live in grant_event.event.payload; the holder is taken from the path. consent_id is producer-allocated, so the caller mints it: it is the cell subject (ak:cell:ak.component.consent.grant.v1:<consent_id>), and the or_set add dot is 'ak:event:<enclosing event_id>:<write_index>' (zh/identity/consent-model.md section 3.2). A service that wrote this element itself would be putting consent into replicated cell state that no Event in the log explains.

grant_event.description: Closed ak.consent.grant Event authored and signed by the holder, or by a controller/agent whose authorization scope explicitly covers consent writes and whose payload carries replayable holder approval evidence; a general PCR write capability is never such an authorization. The service MUST submit these exact bytes through ordinary Event admission and MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event. Admission MUST verify that event.realm_id is the holder's principal control Realm and that the path holder is the consent holder; a grant submitted by any other actor is rejected unauthorized.

consent_revoke_request_body.description: Carries the caller-signed ak.consent.revoke Control Move and nothing else. Its payload.observed_dots MUST enumerate every active dot that becomes inactive, and the caller reads those dots back from consent_cell_view.active_grant_dots: an observe-remove OR-Set revoker has to name the exact dots or two concurrent revokes race, one removing the old dot and the other the new one while the UI reports success (zh/identity/consent-model.md section 3.2). A consent_scope=any cascade is no exception.

revoke_event.description: Closed ak.consent.revoke Event authored and signed by the holder or an explicitly consent-write-authorized controller/agent. Its payload.consent_id MUST equal the consent_id of the ak.consent.grant being revoked. The service MUST submit these exact bytes through ordinary Event admission and MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event.

consent_request_request_body.description: Body for opaque contact/consent request submission. peer_principal_id defaults to the authenticated actor and MUST equal it. Holder existence is deliberately not a precondition visible to the caller.

consent_request_outcome.description: Constant anti-enumeration response. Missing holder, denial, rate-limit drop and quarantine acceptance all return this exact shape; no cell id, state, dots, timestamps or expiry are exposed.

schemas/contact-operations.schema.json.title: Arkret Contact and Direct Conversation Operation DTOs
schemas/contact-operations.schema.json.description: Closed request/response DTO bundle for the Contact lifecycle: request, respond, reject, scope replacement, tombstone, the portable basis evidence bundle, acceptance receipts and the peer Contact carrier, plus the contact-list projection.

control_proposal_ack.description: External-authority receipt set for this Contact Control Move when the receiving Principal Server cannot itself produce the complete current authority quorum.

subject_id.description: Principal DID whose private Contact projection receives this fact.

principal_authority_instance.description: Immutable PCR lineage selected for this Contact participant. principal_id and principal_server_id MUST equal subject_id and recipient_service_id.

recipient_service_id.description: Stable Principal Server service did_core_id that hosts subject_id and accepts this delivery.

route_assistance.description: Optional transport-only hints for recovering the same recipient_service_id route during Contact delivery bootstrap. They are not part of the signed Contact Event, Contact projection, Realm member cell or authority state; they do not extend any token/receipt TTL or authorize delivery.

previous_terminal_basis_id.description: Absent only for a root Contact basis. On recontact it is copied from every signed request fact and request acceptance receipt in this bundle and points to the immediately preceding terminal basis. The bundle field is derived convenience, never independent authority.

terminal.description: Signed current-head classification. true means head_event_ref is an accepted ak.contact.tombstoned terminal head for this basis; false means the basis remains non-terminal. A historical predecessor in a recontact continuity chain requires true from both directional proofs.

request_receipt.description: Closed prepare input for answering one incoming Contact proposal, carried only by the ak.self.contact.read.list projection. It is the complete signed request_acceptance_receipt object, not narrowed to a reference, and the field name is byte-identical to the request_receipt field of the prepare branch of ak.self.contact.command.respond and ak.self.contact.command.reject, so a client copies it verbatim; the prepare contract is unchanged and a client MUST NOT rename, rebuild or re-derive the receipt, and MUST NOT assemble one from request_event_ref, which is a projection summary. Unlike next_prepare_input this receipt is issued and signed by the PEER's source service rather than by the holder's own server, which is exactly why handing the object itself to the holder client has real cross-server verification value: the client verifies the issuer signature, the issuer service key at accepted_at and the receipt's binding to the exact request Event ref and digest on its own, instead of unconditionally believing its own server's retelling. Presence is fixed by contact_state: a pending_incoming row MUST carry it, and a pending_outgoing, accepted, rejected, expired or tombstoned row MUST NOT, because pending_outgoing is the holder's own outstanding proposal with no incoming request to answer and the other four have a consumed admission slot or a terminal basis. A glare pair is therefore never receipt-bearing: the holder's own unconsumed outgoing request keeps the row pending_outgoing while glare evidence is incomplete, and the mechanically derived glare basis projects accepted, which matches the rule that the glare branch forbids respond and reject. Absence is the sole encoding of 'respond and reject are not authorable now'; no extra error code and no extra contact_state value expresses it. When the slot has moved on, prepare refuses with zero writes; the client MUST re-read this operation rather than cache, guess or replay a consumed receipt.

effective_scopes.description: Optional shorthand. When present, MUST equal bidirectional_scopes.

peer_service_id.description: Optional stable Principal Server service did_core_id hosting the peer. Omitted for same-Principal-Server contacts.

peer_service_resolution.description: Required bootstrap material whenever peer_service_id is present. It MAY be refreshed without changing peer_service_id.

contact_next_prepare_input.description: Closed successor cursor for the holder's own issuer-local Contact lineage, carried only by the ak.self.contact.read.list projection. The container name carries the tense: version is the version the NEXT Event carries, that is current head version plus one, hence the minimum of 2; predecessor_event_ref is the current lineage head Event ID, that is the predecessor the next Event must name, and never the predecessor of the current head. The three field names are byte-identical to the prepare-phase fields of ak.self.contact.command.scope_update and ak.self.contact.command.tombstone and MUST be copied verbatim; a client MUST NOT rename, recompute or derive them, and MUST NOT assemble a successor from request_event_ref, response_event_ref or tombstone_event_ref, which are projection summaries and not authoritative lineage heads. Presence is fixed by contact_state: an accepted row MUST carry it, and a pending_outgoing, pending_incoming, rejected, expired or tombstoned row MUST NOT, because the first two have no basis or lineage yet and the last three are terminal. Absence is the sole encoding of 'no successor is authorable now'; no extra error code or contact_state value expresses it. A stale cursor is refused by prepare with contact_lineage_conflict or contact_scope_stale; the client MUST re-read this operation and retry with the fresh values, and MUST NOT guess a head or retry the same triple.

previous_terminal_basis_id.description: Immediate previously accepted terminal Contact basis for a recontact request. The Principal Server MUST require an exact local terminal-basis match when present and MUST require it when a terminal predecessor exists.

control_proposal_ack.description: External-authority receipt set for this Contact Control Move when the receiving Principal Server cannot itself produce the complete current authority quorum.

contact_prepared_event_draft.description: Service-fixed canonical Event bytes without the holder proof. The client may only append the proof; after removing that proof the commit Event must equal these bytes, ID and digest exactly.

control_proposal_ack.description: External-authority receipt set for this Contact Control Move when the receiving Principal Server cannot itself produce the complete current authority quorum.
External-authority receipt set for this Contact Control Move when the receiving Principal Server cannot itself produce the complete current authority quorum.
External-authority receipt set for this Contact Control Move when the receiving Principal Server cannot itself produce the complete current authority quorum.

direct_conversation_summary.description: Contact-list projection of an already materialized stable Direct Conversation. Coordinates and binding identity are immutable; state only says whether the same conversation is currently sendable. Creation progress is exposed only by direct_conversation_resolve_outcome; there is no durable creation operation, draft or reservation.

glare_concurrency_attestation.description: Source-signed evidence that the issuer had accepted both directional request receipts while neither request slot had yet been consumed by a normal response or rejection. Exactly one attestation from each pair member is required by the glare evidence bundle.

peer_contact_authoritative_mirror_receip.description: Only an accepted or duplicate mirror receipt proves that the immutable signed Contact fact is durably mirrored. A deferred receipt is never authority for proof refresh or glare finalization.

result_digest.description: H('ak.peer-contact.control-result.v1',{request_digest,result_kind,glare_concurrency_attestation?,current_proof?}) over the exact closed successful result.

peer_contact_control_receipt.description: The recipient signs every field except signature. This receipt is only for proof_refresh or glare_finalize and cannot stand in for a signed Event mirror receipt.

peer_contact_event_submit_outcome.description: Only the five signed Contact Event request kinds use this branch. The receipt event coordinates and result_kind must match the submitted Event exactly. Request/response may return a current proof; accepted or duplicate scope/tombstone must return one; reject and deferred never do.

previous_terminal_basis_id.description: Present exactly when this accepted request starts a recontact after a prior accepted basis became terminal. It MUST equal the requester-signed ak.contact.requested payload field and is covered by receipt_digest/signature. It is distinct from slot_predecessor, which is the issuer-local request-slot CAS predecessor and can also follow a rejected proposal.

schemas/content-block-poll.schema.json.title: Arkret Poll Content Block
schemas/content-block-poll.schema.json.description: Canonical content-block schema for ak.content.poll and ak.content.poll.response.

poll_answer.description: One visible answer option. answer.id values MUST be unique within a poll; reducers and conformance vectors enforce that cross-item constraint.

poll_body.description: Poll configuration. max_selections is validated against responses by reducers because JSON Schema cannot compare a response to its referenced poll message.

schemas/control-proposal-decision.schema.title: Arkret Control Proposal Ack and Decision
schemas/control-proposal-decision.schema.description: Quorum-capable Control Proposal Acks and signed reject/defer decisions for CBA Control Moves. Deadlines provide bounded authority decisions, never acceptance or Seal finality.

authority_acks.description: Canonical ascending verification_method order. Distinct valid members, not array length, determine quorum.

proofs.description: Canonical ascending verification_method order. Every proof signs the same decision payload and the set independently satisfies the Control Proposal Ack authority quorum.

control_proposal_ack_issue_request.description: Typed authority input used by a local signer or the registered HTTP operation to issue one immutable authority Ack.

schemas/cursor.schema.json.title: Arkret Cursor
schemas/cursor.schema.json.description:
Single opaque cursor type. Used as both stream continuation token (incremental sync, list pagination — 'after', 'before', 'prev_cursor', 'next_cursor') and barrier token (read-your-writes wait — 'X-Arkret-Wait-For'). Wire form is always ak:cursor:<base64url(canonical_json)>. Clients MUST treat the wire form as opaque; only the issuing server reads the inner structure.

Integrity contract (normative, see client-sync.md §12 and encoding.md §8 / §8.3.1): v1 core uses the stateful opaque-handle form only — body is {v, purpose, issued_at, expires_at, h} where 'h' is an unguessable server-side handle that the issuing server resolves to the bound (principal_id, device_id, service_id, filter_digest, purpose, positions, target?, expiry) tuple. Server-side handle lookup IS the integrity check; there is no inline transcript binding to verify on the client side. Servers MUST reject unknown / expired / cross-binding handles with cursor_integrity_invalid.

purpose.description: Cursor purpose. 'stream' = continuation cursor for incremental sync / list pagination. Used as 'after' on /account/subscribe, 'before' / 'after' in the JSON content of ak.self.events.read.scan and ak.peer.events.read.scan (including its service-to-service federation binding QUERY /_arkret/peer/events), and as response 'prev_cursor' (older direction) / 'next_cursor' (newer direction). prev_cursor / next_cursor carry absolute directional meaning regardless of how the request was issued — see api-conventions.md §7.0. 'barrier' = read-your-writes / wait-for-event cursor (use in X-Arkret-Wait-For header to block until local frontier covers target.event_id). The handle binding (resolved server-side) carries positions for 'stream' or target for 'barrier'; the wire body does not.

issued_at.description: Cursor issuance instant in the canonical Arkret UTC millisecond profile.

expires_at.description: Cursor expiration instant. MUST be in the future when issued. TTL upper bounds (expires_at - issued_at): barrier cursors MUST have TTL ≤ 3,600,000 ms (1 hour); stream cursors MUST have TTL ≤ 604,800,000 ms (7 days).

h.description: Server-side opaque handle. The issuing server MUST bind this handle to (principal_id, device_id, service_id, filter_digest, purpose, positions, target?, expiry) and MUST be able to revoke it. The handle MUST be unguessable (≥ 128 bits entropy after base64url decoding); minLength=22 enforces that floor mechanically (base64url packs 6 bits per character so 128/6 ≈ 21.33 → at least 22 chars of the [A-Za-z0-9_-] alphabet). Servers MUST reject any unknown / expired / cross-binding handle with `cursor_integrity_invalid`. Handle lookup IS the integrity check — there is no MAC or signature to verify inline. This is the moral equivalent of Matrix `next_batch` / MSC4186 `pos` and satisfies the integrity contract without crypto. Servers SHOULD keep the handle → binding map durable across process restarts (see client-sync.md §12.1): a memory-only table is still integrity-correct (unknown handles fail closed) but turns every restart into a fleet-wide forced full resync. For production-grade deployment profiles (small_team / organization / high_security_organization / sovereign_deployment / sovereign_enclave / isolated_sovereign_network) this durability plus TTL GC is a MUST per client-sync.md §12.1; only personal_node keeps it at SHOULD.

^_[A-Za-z0-9_]*$.description: Server-private auxiliary fields (e.g. `_compress` / `_kid` flags). Names MUST start with underscore. In v1 core there is no `_mac` / `_sig` integrity field — handle lookup IS the integrity check — so the underscore namespace is private to the issuing server. `_mac` and `_sig` themselves are explicitly excluded by the top-level `not` clause: a cursor body carrying either MUST be rejected (encoding.md §8.3).

schemas/delivery-binding-stale.schema.js.title: Arkret Delivery Binding Stale Error Body
schemas/delivery-binding-stale.schema.js.description: Canonical error body for the delivery_binding_stale federation signal. A receiver that has accepted a member delivery-binding rebind handover returns this when a sender still delivers under the pre-handover binding. Carries new_recipient_service_id, handover_frontier, and a verifiable handover_proof binding the accepted ak.member.state{membership=join} rebind Move. High-risk redirect: senders MUST cross-verify handover_frontier via a non-destination witness and validate handover_proof (reachability, seal-frontier finalization, allowed_recipient_services membership, trust-domain guard) before following. See zh/sync/federation.md §4.1 and registry/error-code-registry.json (delivery_binding_stale / delivery_binding_handover_proof_invalid).

new_recipient_service_id.description: Stable target Principal Server service did_core_id after rebind. MUST be within the current effective allowed_recipient_services / delivery binding policy allow set.

new_service_resolution.description: First-hop material for new_recipient_service_id. A sender verifies the handover and this resolution record before following the redirect.

handover_frontier.description: Handover frontier F that triggered the rebind. MUST equal handover_proof.frontier.

handover_proof.description: Verifiable proof binding the accepted ak.member.state{membership=join} rebind Move that produced the new binding.

actor_id.description: Rebind target principal; MUST equal target_principal_id.

witness.description: Event digest / state witness / inclusion proof of the rebind Move. Sender MUST verify reachability in the Realm Event graph and policy, and that the Move is seal-frontier finalized.

message_id.description: Sender-assigned stable identity of one logical to-device message. Queue services MUST preserve it byte-for-byte across retries and redelivery. Receivers deduplicate by (sender_principal_id, sender_device_id, message_id).

sender_principal_id.description: Sender Principal DID. Intentionally NOT named sender_actor_id: device messages are out-of-band per-device transport envelopes that travel principal-to-principal outside any Realm context, so the Realm-scoped Actor identity used by message.schema.json / event-payload.schema.json does not apply here. Pair with sender_device_id and verify it against the accepted PCR device projection.

recipient_principal_id.description: Recipient Principal DID. Same naming rationale as sender_principal_id — device messages are not Realm-scoped, so Actor identity is not used. Pair with recipient_device_id for targeted device delivery.

device_proof.description: Optional per-device transport proof block (typical sub-fields: device_authorize_event_id, sender_device_key_fingerprint, signature_over_content_digest). It MUST NOT replace MLS authentication of the enclosing envelope and MUST NOT be trusted in isolation.

unsigned.description: Optional non-authenticated metadata block (transport-layer hints only). Receivers MUST NOT trust any field here for authorization, ordering, or cryptographic verification. Typical sub-fields: progress (delivery progress hint), error_context (transport-layer error diagnostics), retry_after_ms. By convention this block is excluded from the signed transcript of the enclosing transport envelope and is dropped on persist.

secret_request_content.description: ak.secret.request to-device content (device-lifecycle.md §10.7). A newly authorized device asks an existing authorized device to hand over an account-scope secret over HPKE. Carries no secret material itself.

request_id.description: Caller-generated random correlation id; MUST NOT be reused after the request is answered or cancelled.

secret_id.description: Opaque identifier of the requested secret, e.g. example_mls_account_secret.

from_device.description: Requesting (new) device; MUST equal envelope sender_device_id.

recipient_hpke_public_key.description: base64url X25519 HPKE public key the requesting device controls and the responder seals to. It MUST be byte-identical to the hpke_key registered for from_device in the current accepted device projection. A responder MUST fail closed on any mismatch and MUST NOT accept an ephemeral key merely because it appeared in a bound SAS verification transcript; SAS authenticates device signing keys, not HPKE sealing keys.

secret_send_content.description: ak.secret.send to-device content (device-lifecycle.md §10.7). The existing authorized device returns the requested secret HPKE-sealed to the requester's recipient_hpke_public_key. The plaintext is never visible to the queue service.

request_id.description: Correlates to the pending ak.secret.request; MUST equal the request_id authenticated inside the sealed plaintext and HPKE AAD. Receivers MUST drop sends that do not match a locally pending request_id.

secret_id.description: Opaque requested secret identifier; MUST equal the secret_id authenticated inside the sealed plaintext and HPKE AAD.

from_device.description: Authorizing (existing) device; MUST equal envelope sender_device_id and MUST be a non-revoked device of the recipient principal.

ciphertext.description: base64url HPKE AEAD ciphertext over the secret plaintext. The plaintext MUST carry the requested secret body, version, request_id and secret_id. The HPKE AAD is the RFC 8785 JCS canonical JSON of {message_id, kind, sender_principal_id, sender_device_id, recipient_principal_id, recipient_device_id, request_id, secret_id, expires_at}; expires_at is the exact already-validated canonical Arkret UTC millisecond string from DeviceMessageEnvelope and MUST NOT be converted to a second epoch field. Freshness for server-assigned sent_at is bound by the sender-assigned message_id plus the one-time request_id authenticated inside the sealed plaintext and AAD.

realm_key_request_content.description: ak.realm_key.request to-device content (device-lifecycle.md §13.2). A read-eligible receiver asks a concrete key source to evaluate policy and, if authorized, deliver historical history_secret material via durable ak.realm_key.share or an equivalent policy-authorized recovery path. Carries no key material itself.

recipient_hpke_public_key.description: Recipient device HPKE public key (KeyPackage init key or equivalent) the key source MUST verify as an authorized device key for recipient_principal_id before sealing history_secret.

requested_source_kind.description: Source class this request targets. key_backup is intentionally excluded because it is retrieved via ak.self.keys.backups.command.unlock.

target_source_ref.description: Concrete source this request is routed to: a device_id for own_device / verified_member_device, or a service DID for archive_node / recovery_service. Service-targeted reuse of this to-device kind is valid only when ServiceDescribe exposes a concrete recipient_device_id / queue target for the service DID; otherwise the service MUST expose a dedicated operation.

target_principal_id.description: Principal that owns target_source_ref (the to-device queue is addressed by (principal, device_id)). Carried so the relay routes directly without scanning Realm members to reverse-lookup the device's principal.

effective_scope.description: Tagged scope of the requested key material. Realm-default history uses {kind:'realm', realm_id}; Circle history uses {kind:'circle', realm_id, circle_id}.

policy_digest.description: Optional requester-observed policy digest hint. The key source MUST recompute the effective policy from accepted history before sharing.

membership_frontier_digest.description: Optional requester-observed membership frontier hint. The key source MUST recompute recipient eligibility from accepted history before sharing.

member_repair_request_content.description: ak.member.repair.request to-device content (contact-and-direct-conversation.md 8.2.1). A participant that has rejoined membership asks the current peer participant to author the MLS Remove/re-add Commit and Welcome that a replacement generation needs, because no actor may sign for another. Same non-authorizing trigger shape as ak.realm_key.request: it carries no Event bytes, no MLS material and no authority, and the peer MUST re-verify every gate from the signed event log before authoring anything.

realm_id.description: The pair's immutable Direct Conversation Realm. Repair never creates a successor Realm, Strand or binding.

requester_principal_id.description: MUST equal the principal bound by the selected device or Native-Agent authorization/evidence branch: no actor may ask for repair on another participant's behalf.

requester_device_id.description: Human-device branch only. MUST equal the detached repair authorization and portable device evidence device_id, and the exact KeyPackage selected by requester_keypackage_ref MUST belong to this current authorized device.

requester_agent_id.description: Native-Agent branch only. MUST equal requester_principal_id and the actor/subject of the accepted rejoin Event.

requester_agent_verification_method.description: Native-Agent runtime verification method that signed the repair authorization and the exact KeyPackage. It MUST match current AgentSignerEvidence byte for byte.

agent_key_authorize_event_id.description: Native-Agent branch current accepted ak.agent.key.authorize Event. It MUST match the current AgentSignerEvidence and the exact KeyPackage claim record.

requester_keypackage_ref.description: The single KeyPackage the peer claims for the re-add, so exactly one KeyPackage is consumed and the peer never has to guess which of the requester's packages to use.

observed_active_generation_value_digest.description: SHA-256 of RFC 8785 JCS for the complete accepted ak.component.direct_conversation.active_mls_generation.v1 cell value the requester observed, copied byte for byte from active_mls_generation_value_digest returned by the resolver. It is never derived from or replaced by active_mls_generation_ref. A peer that sees a different current whole-value digest MUST drop the request instead of authoring a second replacement.

rejoin_event_id.description: The requester's accepted ak.member.rejoin.own Event. The peer MUST verify it is accepted and subject-matched; an unaccepted or absent rejoin means there is nothing to repair yet.

purpose.description: Optional verification purpose. Omitted means generic device key verification. same_principal_device_authorization is used when a fresh device asks already authorized devices of the same principal to approve device authorization.

pairing_code.description: Eight-character human-readable Crockford-style device-pairing code bound into a same-principal authorization transcript. It is short-lived, one-time, and locked after ten failed submissions.

new_device_pubkey.description: Canonical PublicKey for the requesting device when purpose=same_principal_device_authorization. kid MUST be the requesting ak:device:<uuidv7> id and the key material MUST be carried in key. The legacy {kid, alg, public_key} spelling is not canonical wire and MUST be rejected. The object is later consumed verbatim by ak.gate.account.command.pair_device.

challenge_proof.description: Fresh requesting-device proof of possession over the ak.device-pairing.challenge.to_device.v1 transcript, which commits to {expires_at, gate_audience, new_device_pubkey_digest, pairing_code, request_canonical_digest, transaction_id}. The receiving authorized device MUST recompute the transcript from the values it displays to the user and verify the signature before treating the requesting device as pairable; it is later submitted verbatim to ak.gate.account.command.pair_device.

target_attestation.description: Closed accepted_device possession attestation of the requesting device when purpose=same_principal_device_authorization, and the only authority for its hpke_key and algorithms. It is the same schema and same domain the short-link path uses, because it binds only pairing_challenge_transcript_digest and each path already closes its own challenge transcript. The receiving authorized device MUST rebuild and verify it after the challenge proof, requiring device_id to equal new_device_pubkey.kid, device_public_key to decode to the same key as new_device_pubkey.key, and pairing_challenge_transcript_digest to equal the transcript digest it just recomputed; only then may it read hpke_key and algorithms from it and copy device_signature verbatim into the ak.device.authorize payload. It travels only on this out-of-band message and MUST NOT be posted back through the unauthenticated stage or resolve surface.

gate_audience.description: Auth Server audience/origin expected to consume the paired proof.

request_canonical_digest.description: Digest of the canonical request material bound into the pairing proof.

device_metadata.description: User-facing requesting-device hints. Receivers MUST treat this as display metadata and bind the parts shown to the user into the verification transcript.

schemas/device-pairing.schema.json.title: Arkret Device Pairing Short-Link DTOs
schemas/device-pairing.schema.json.description: Closed request and response DTOs for the server-mediated device-pairing short-link handoff (device-lifecycle.md §2.1.1). These endpoints are unauthenticated: staging mints an account-less pending record, and resolve/status exchange the short handle for pairing material without binding or granting anything until an authenticated device authorizes the pairing.

algorithm_list.description: Algorithm ids supported by the target device, sorted by UTF-8 bytewise order and deduplicated before they enter any transcript.

pairing_nonce.description: base64url CSPRNG nonce carrying at least 128 bits of entropy.

gate_audience.description: Origin of the Account Authority gate surface (gate_account_base) this pairing request is bound to. Minted by the staging service; the challenge proof commits to it so a proof cannot be replayed against another Account Authority.

device_pairing_to_device_challenge_trans.description: Transcript inputs the authorizing device forwards for the to-device pairing path, where no server-staged record exists. The Account Authority rebuilds the ak.device-pairing.challenge.to_device.v1 signing input from these values plus its own gate_audience origin and the digest of the submitted new_device_pubkey; it MUST NOT accept a client-supplied gate_audience, because substituting its own origin is exactly what blocks cross-Account-Authority replay. See crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md section 2.1.2.

transaction_id.description: Verification transaction id of the ak.key.verification.request that carried this pairing challenge.

expires_at.description: Expiry the proof committed to. The Account Authority MUST reject an elapsed expires_at before it verifies the signature.

device_pairing_challenge_proof.description: Proof of possession of the staged new_device_pubkey, bound to the server-minted pairing challenge. Signing input is UTF8("ak.device-pairing.challenge.v1\n") || canonical_json({client_nonce, device_pairing_request_id, expires_at, gate_audience, new_device_pubkey_digest, pairing_code, server_nonce}); see crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md section 2.1.2. The proof can only be generated after staging returns, because it commits to server-minted values that do not exist at stage time.

transcript.description: Names the exact signing transcript. ak.device-pairing.challenge.v1 is the server-mediated short-link path and commits to {client_nonce, device_pairing_request_id, expires_at, gate_audience, new_device_pubkey_digest, pairing_code, server_nonce}. ak.device-pairing.challenge.to_device.v1 is the to-device verification path and commits to {expires_at, gate_audience, new_device_pubkey_digest, pairing_code, request_canonical_digest, transaction_id}. A verifier MUST select the member set from this discriminator and MUST NOT accept a proof whose transcript name does not match the path it is verifying.

kid.description: MUST equal new_device_pubkey.kid. The proof is verified with the staged new_device_pubkey and with no other key. This is a device-local ak:device key id selecting the staged key (identity/did-usage-and-verification.md section 2.3), not a DID URL; it is deliberately not named verification_method.

transcript_digest.description: sha256 over the canonical challenge transcript bytes. The verifier recomputes it from its own staged record and rejects a mismatch before checking the signature.

device_pairing_target_attestation.description: Closed possession attestation the target device produces for the accepted_device pairing path, and the only authority for its hpke_key and algorithms: neither the staged record nor the bootstrap carries them, so the approving device reads them here after the signature verifies and copies them byte-for-byte into the ak.device.authorize payload. Signing input is UTF8("ak.device-authorize-accepted-device-possession-proof-v1\n") || canonical_json({algorithms, authorization_binding_kind, device_id, device_key_algorithm, device_public_key, hpke_key, pairing_challenge_transcript_digest}); see crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md section 5.2.2. The object is closed over target-owned material plus this pairing challenge, so the target can build it before it knows which sibling will approve and what principal_id, authorized_by, not_before, expires_at or scopes that sibling will choose; those values are carried by the approving device Event proof instead. It travels only over the out-of-band channel (QR fragment or to-device message) and MUST NOT be posted back through the unauthenticated stage or resolve surface. It is never a wire field of ak.gate.account.command.pair_device: every member is already recomputable there from the request payload and the Account Authority own challenge transcript.

device_public_key.description: Self-describing did:key form of the same Ed25519 key as new_device_pubkey.key. A verifier MUST reject an attestation whose device_public_key decodes to different key bytes than the staged or forwarded new_device_pubkey.

hpke_key.description: Target device X25519 HPKE public key. This attestation is its authority; a service MUST NOT supply or substitute it.

authorization_binding_kind.description: This transcript exists only for accepted_device pairing. registration_anchor and pcr_recovery use their separate full possession objects, and a transcript from one binding kind MUST NOT be accepted for another.

pairing_challenge_transcript_digest.description: MUST equal device_pairing_challenge_proof.transcript_digest of this same pairing challenge. It is the single replay boundary of this attestation: path A commits through it to device_pairing_request_id, pairing_code, gate_audience, expires_at, server_nonce, client_nonce and new_device_pubkey_digest, and path B to transaction_id, request_canonical_digest, expires_at, gate_audience, pairing_code and new_device_pubkey_digest. A verifier MUST recompute the challenge transcript itself and reject a digest that does not match this pairing.

device_signature.description: Ed25519 signature by the private key of device_public_key over the canonical signing input above. The approving device MUST copy it byte-for-byte into device_authorize_payload.device_signature and into the pair_device request device_signature.

public_key.description: Canonical PublicKey shape shared with agent-operations. For a staged device the key material is carried in `key` and `kid` is the target `ak:device:<uuid>` id.

device_pairing_state.description: Lifecycle state of a staged device-pairing short-link record. A staged record starts pending_authorization, flips to authorized once an authenticated device completes ak.gate.account.command.pair_device, and reports expired once its bounded TTL has elapsed.

device_pairing_stage_request_body.description: Unauthenticated stage request that mints a fresh account-less pending pairing record. It carries only the canonical public key and a client nonce: the challenge proof cannot exist yet, because it must commit to the request id, pairing code, expiry, gate audience and server nonce that this call mints. It also deliberately omits hpke_key and algorithms; those reach the approving device inside the signed device_pairing_target_attestation over the out-of-band channel, so the anonymous staging surface never accumulates long-term device key material or a device algorithm fingerprint. The record binds no principal and grants nothing until an authenticated device authorizes it.

device_pairing_stage_outcome.description: Result of staging a device-pairing short-link record. It returns the full server-minted challenge material the new device needs to build the ak.device-pairing.challenge.v1 proof. pairing_code is a short human-carryable secret; both device_pairing_request_id and pairing_code are the query credential for the resolve/status endpoints and MUST NOT be sent in URL path or query string.

device_pairing_resolve_request_body.description: Body-only resolver input for device-pairing short-link handoff. The token is obtained from a URL fragment or equivalent out-of-band channel and MUST NOT be sent in URL path or query.

device_pairing_bootstrap.description: Pairing material handed to an already-authorized device after resolving a device-pairing short link. It carries the server-minted challenge material so the authorized device can recompute the ak.device-pairing.challenge.v1 transcript and verify the proof it received out of band from the new device. It does NOT carry the proof itself, nor the device_pairing_target_attestation, nor the hpke_key and algorithms that attestation signs: the staging surface is unauthenticated and never sees any of them, and mirroring signed values here would only create a second, non-authoritative copy. This is not a session grant, capability grant or long-term secret; the authorized device still drives ak.gate.account.command.pair_device to complete authorization.

device_pairing_status_request_body.description: Body-only poll for the authorization status of a staged device-pairing record. The device_pairing_request_id + pairing_code pair is the query credential and MUST be sent in the JSON body; a record miss and a pairing_code mismatch MUST be indistinguishable (both not_found).

device_pairing_status_outcome.description: Authorization status for a staged device-pairing record. While the record is still open, state is pending_authorization. Once an authenticated device has authorized this pairing, state is authorized and device_id plus authorized_event_ref are present. An open record whose bounded TTL has elapsed reports state expired.

authorized_event_ref.description: Accepted ak.device.authorize Event id. It is the entry point for the mandatory pre-assembly check in crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md section 5.4.1: before the target device assembles the identity locally it MUST fetch this Event and confirm byte-identical device_signature, byte-identical device_public_key, hpke_key and algorithms, and an expected principal_id, or fail closed.

schemas/did-binding-contracts.schema.jso.title: Arkret Verified DID Binding Contracts
schemas/did-binding-contracts.schema.jso.description: Canonical shapes behind identity/did-usage-and-verification.md section 5: the retained evidence receipt whose digest is the binding's evidence_digest, the resolver policy snapshot whose digest is the binding's policy_digest, the mechanically extracted evidence dependency record used for selective invalidation, the limited-trust pin record, and the freshness profile row every authority call site references. These objects are trust-domain-local: the contracts guarantee recomputability and change-sensitivity, not cross-deployment digest equality.

method_token.description: Canonical lowercase DID method token (W3C DID 1.0 method-name), e.g. key, web, webvh.
