evidence_receipt.description: Canonical evidence receipt. evidence_digest = "sha256:" + lowercase_hex(SHA-256(RFC8785_JCS(evidence_receipt))). The receipt MUST be retained so an auditor can recompute the digest; a method without proofs degrades to an empty method_proofs array (a document-bound receipt), never to an implementation-invented placeholder. Unknown method or proof kinds fail closed.

document_digest.description: Digest of the resolver's verified normalized DID Document projection (did-usage-and-verification.md section 5.1); never the raw response bytes (those use the differently named raw_document_digest).

method_proofs.description: Closed per-method proof rows; empty for proofless methods (did:key, bare did:web). v1 registers exactly one row kind (webvh_log); receiving any unregistered proof kind fails closed. Rows never reuse resolver response order: each row kind registers its own canonical sort and duplicate-rejection rules.

webvh_log_evidence.description: did:webvh method evidence row. witnesses are sorted by witness_did (UTF-8 byte order) with duplicates rejected; witness_proofs_digest commits to the canonical raw witness proof set so the receipt stays change-sensitive to any witness signature change.

history_head.description: The verified webvh log head (versionId / entry-hash form) this binding pinned.

witnesses.description: Sorted by witness_did, UTF-8 byte order; duplicates rejected. These rows double as the evidence dependency coordinates for selective invalidation.

resolver_policy_snapshot.description: Canonical resolver policy snapshot. policy_digest = "sha256:" + lowercase_hex(SHA-256(RFC8785_JCS(policy_snapshot))). The snapshot MUST be retainable and rebuildable so auditors can recompute the digest and verify that any security-relevant configuration change necessarily changes it. Enum values MUST use the registered wire tokens below; language-native debug formats are forbidden. accepted_did_methods and trust_roots are sorted by UTF-8 byte order with duplicates rejected; strings receive no Unicode normalization.

policy_profile.description: Registered resolver policy profile id; the schema discriminator for profile_policy. v1 registers ak.did_resolver_policy_profile.base.v1 (empty closed profile_policy). A deployment introducing extra policy dimensions MUST register its own profile with an additionalProperties:false schema listing every configuration field that changes resolution, verification, network boundaries, size limits or degradation behavior as required. Unknown profiles, unknown fields, and missing registered fields all fail closed.

profile_policy.description: Profile-specific dimensions validated by the closed schema the policy_profile registers; the base profile requires exactly the empty object. Any change here changes the digest, so section 5 invalidation obligations are preserved for deployment-specific knobs.

evidence_dependencies.description: Structured dependency record mechanically extracted from the evidence receipt (did-usage-and-verification.md section 5.6). It answers 'which bindings depend on witness X / log head H' — a mapping a digest cannot provide because digests are one-way. Proofless methods produce the empty record.

witness_dids.description: Sorted, deduplicated; empty for proofless methods.

witness_controlling_organizations.description: Sorted, deduplicated; empty for proofless methods.

history_heads.description: Sorted, deduplicated; empty for proofless methods.

limited_trust.description: Per-pin limited-trust record (did-usage-and-verification.md section 5.5). Omitted entirely when both pins are present; when present, each state MUST be consistent with the actual presence of the corresponding pin field. method_unsupported is a legitimate terminal state (did:key has no history); not_surfaced marks a resolver that failed to surface evidence its method supports and is treated as a failure state, not a normal audit note.

freshness_profile.description: One registered freshness profile row (did-usage-and-verification.md section 5.4). Every DID authority call site references exactly one freshness_profile_id through its operation/action registration; natural-language tier guessing is forbidden. Deployments declare their rows in machine-readable form and the declared snapshot enters profile_policy of the resolver policy snapshot, so changing any number structurally invalidates existing bindings. Tier constraints (finite windows, ordering, stale behavior) are normative in section 5.4.

did_method_selector.description: did:<method>: prefixes this row applies to, or the single wildcard "*".

fresh_for_seconds.description: The single freshness threshold: refresh_after = verified_at + fresh_for_seconds, and the authority call's max_age MUST equal the same value — two separately maintained constants are forbidden.

schemas/did-webvh-witness-receipt.schema.title: Arkret did:webvh Witness Receipt
schemas/did-webvh-witness-receipt.schema.description: Arkret-layer, cacheable and auditable record that a named did:webvh witness was observed attesting a specific log version. It is deliberately a separate object family from ak.schema.identity_receipt.v1: that one records a role (writer / witness / replica) inside a DID registry consensus group and binds seq + head_event_digest, whereas this one binds a did:webvh method versionId and a witness did:key drawn from parameters.witness. Overloading one object with both meanings would leave half its required fields meaningless on either branch and force verifiers to guess which sense of the word witness applies. This receipt NEVER substitutes for method conformance: a verifier MUST still fetch and verify the standard did-witness.json proofs, the entry hash chain and the controller proof. See zh/identity/identity-did.md.

schema.description: Closed discriminator. ak.root.identity.receipts.read.list returns a tagged union of receipt families; this constant is what lets a verifier pick the did:webvh method-witness branch instead of the registry consensus branch without guessing.

did.description: Subject DID. Restricted to did:webvh because the object binds method-native did:webvh state; other methods need their own receipt family rather than a widened pattern here.

version_id.description: The exact did:webvh versionId this attestation covers, verbatim from the log entry. Binding to versionId rather than to a digest of the document is what makes the receipt replayable against did-witness.json, whose proofs are themselves keyed by versionId.

log_head_digest.description: Optional digest of the log head the issuer held when observing. Present it when the issuer can commit to the whole log state; it lets a consumer detect a split view that a per-version binding alone would not reveal.

witness_did.description: The attesting witness, which MUST be one of the parameters.witness.witnesses[].id values in force at version_id. did:webvh 1.0 constrains witness identifiers to did:key, so a receipt naming any other form is describing something that is not a method witness.

witness_verification_method.description: The specific verification method inside witness_did whose signature appears in did-witness.json for version_id.

controlling_organization.description: The organization that controls this witness, as resolved by the issuer. Arkret deployment policy counts distinct controlling organizations, not distinct witness keys; without this field an operator running several witness keys would satisfy a two-distinct-organization requirement by itself. A verifier that cannot independently verify this binding MUST fail closed on high-risk paths rather than count the witness.

observed_at.description: When the issuer actually fetched or observed the witness proof. Freshness is evaluated against this instant, not against created_at: an issuer could otherwise re-sign a years-old observation and present it as current.

source.description: Optional origin the proof was read from (the DID's own did-witness.json or a declared mirror). Recorded so a consumer can tell a first-party read from a mirrored one when adjudicating conflicting receipts.

issuer_service_id.description: Stable did_core_id of the Arkret service issuing this receipt. This is the trust root for the receipt itself, and is unrelated to the DID's own controller.

trust_domain.description: Optional trust domain the receipt is scoped to.

audience.description: Optional audience binding (verifier DID, service DID, or domain). When present, verifiers MUST reject the receipt outside that audience context to prevent cross-protocol reuse.

expires_at.description: Required. An Arkret-layer cache record without an expiry becomes indistinguishable from a permanent assertion, which is precisely how stale witness evidence outlives the state it described. MUST be later than created_at, and a consumer MUST treat an expired receipt as absent rather than as weak evidence.

signature.description: Issuer detached proof. payload_digest = sha256(canonical_json(receipt with signature omitted)). The detached JWS signs canonical_json({context:'ak.did-webvh-witness-receipt-proof-v1', payload_digest, issuer_service_id, did, version_id, witness_did, verification_method, created_at, domain?, audience?}); context is a fixed signing-context domain tag and is not a wire field. signature.created_at MUST equal receipt.created_at. signature.verification_method MUST be a currently valid assertion method controlled by issuer_service_id. Receipt audience and proof audience MUST either both be absent or be the same single string; array-valued proof audiences are invalid for this object family.

schemas/direct-conversation-operations.s.title: Arkret Direct Conversation Operations
schemas/direct-conversation-operations.s.description: Closed carriers for the Direct Conversation resolver and single-sided founding. Creation is never carried here: a Direct Conversation Realm is created only by the founder derived from the pair's root Contact basis through the direct_conversation_genesis admission variant of ak.realm.create.

direct_conversation_coordinates.description: Permanent Direct Conversation coordinates. binding_event_ref appears only from found or suspended onward; it is absent while the pair is still provisional.

direct_conversation_founding_acceptance_.description: Source-signed evidence that the founder current Principal Server atomically accepted exactly one Direct Conversation founding unit and closed its local unique slot. It creates no Realm, authorizes no Message and is not a global slot; a second receipt for the same pair and founder but a different unit is direct_conversation_pair_materialization_conflict evidence. proof signs the closed transcript H("ak.direct-conversation.founding-receipt.v1", this object without proof); the receiver recomputes that preimage from the receipt fields and never trusts a carried digest. proof.verification_method resolves to the issuer_service_id current service key at accepted_at and proof.created_at equals accepted_at.

direct_conversation_founding_input.description: Verbatim authoring material for the founding unit the caller is now entitled to author, carried only by the creation_required outcome. Member names equal the DirectConversationFoundingUnitSubmission members byte for byte, so the caller copies them across without any renaming map (service-http-binding.md 2.2.2 echo-container discipline). The caller still authors and signs all three Events itself; this container never carries Event bytes, coordinates or a receipt. Material that the service cannot assemble or verify yields temporarily_unavailable instead of a creation_required outcome without it.

founder_basis_evidence.description: The human branch for a peer Contact founding and the controller_agent branch for an own-Agent founding; the service selects the branch that matches this pair and never returns both.

source_service_binding.description: The founder's current accepted-at binding for this receiving service, as held by the service itself.

direct_conversation_resolve_outcome.description: Closed tagged outcome of ak.self.direct_conversation.read.resolve. Evaluation order is fixed: temporarily_unavailable when the current basis or founder cannot be verified; then creation_blocked, creation_required or awaiting_founder while no Realm exists; then suspended for identity, materialization, terminal or gate conflicts; then provisional while no binding endorsement exists; found last.

active_mls_generation_value_digest.description: SHA-256 of RFC 8785 JCS for the complete currently accepted ak.component.direct_conversation.active_mls_generation.v1 cell value. The Event ref and whole-value digest are supplied or omitted as one pair.
SHA-256 of RFC 8785 JCS for the complete currently accepted active-generation cell value, not a hash of active_mls_generation_ref.
Present with active_mls_generation_ref whenever an accepted active-generation cell exists, including the replacement-repair suspended state.

direct_conversation_resolve_request.description: Closed query body for ak.self.direct_conversation.read.resolve. Creation is never carried here: a Direct Conversation Realm is created only by the derived founder through the direct_conversation_genesis admission variant of ak.realm.create.

direct_conversation_repair_authorization.description: Requester-owned detached authorization over UTF8('ak.direct-conversation-repair-dispatch-v1\n') || RFC8785_JCS({request_id,content}). The branch identity, verification method and authorization Event MUST match the content and the portable evidence byte for byte. The source service session and the outer source-service signature are transport gates, never substitutes for this participant signature.

direct_conversation_repair_requester_evi.description: Portable current requester authority appended by the source Principal Server. The destination independently verifies it and matches every branch field against content, detached authorization, accepted rejoin Event and exact KeyPackage signer evidence; the outer service signature is transport integrity only.

direct_conversation_repair_dispatch_requ.description: Authenticated self command. The requester submits one stable request identity, exact non-authorizing repair content and its own detached authorization. It never enumerates recipient devices; the source service validates current gates and relays the exact request to the peer's current accepted Principal Server.

direct_conversation_repair_relay_request.description: Service-to-service repair relay. The source service copies request_id, content and requester_authorization byte for byte from the accepted self dispatch, appends exactly one portable current-authority evidence branch, then covers the canonical body with RFC 9421 and Content-Digest. The destination independently verifies participant authority and every durable Event gate.

direct_conversation_repair_enqueue_outco.description: Byte-identical terminal outcome proving only that the destination service durably accepted this exact relay and atomically completed exactly one closed recipient target branch. A human principal freezes and enqueues every current authorized device; a Native Agent freezes and enqueues its one current active runtime endpoint from accepted agent-key/session binding and never invents an ak:device identity. The branch-specific digest commits the frozen fanout without disclosing target ids. It is not a repair acknowledgement and says nothing about later Commit, Welcome or activation.

request_digest.description: SHA-256 of the exact canonical direct_conversation_repair_relay_request body.

target_snapshot_digest.description: H('ak.member-repair-target-snapshot-native-agent-v1', {recipient_agent_id,active_runtime_endpoint_ref,message_id}), where the endpoint is the one current accepted agent-key/session binding endpoint.

direct_conversation_send_blocker.description: Closed machine-readable blocker set surfaced by the Direct Conversation resolver. Every value MUST be server-verifiable: the service MUST be able to prove it from accepted authoritative state it may lawfully read, and it MUST NOT guess, decrypt or relay a client self-report. personal_blocked and history_key_unavailable are deliberately absent and MUST NOT be re-added: ak.account.blocklist is holder-private account data that a synchronizing service only ever sees encrypted to holder devices, and whether a historical MLS secret is installed is device-private key state, so a service that answered either one would have to break the encryption invariant or accept an unauthenticated claim as authority. They live in the client-local blocker set of ak.profile.direct_conversation_realm.v1 instead, and a reply carrying either value is a schema_violation the client MUST reject rather than tolerate. presence_offline and keypackage_empty stay here because the service does hold provable facts for them, but they MUST be returned only to an existing exact-pair participant of that very pair; every other caller MUST receive the same opaque failure as for a pair that does not exist, so neither value can be used to enumerate or probe a non-participant. Values never disclose peer presence to non-participants.

schemas/directory-operations.schema.json.title: Arkret Directory Operation DTOs
schemas/directory-operations.schema.json.description: Closed request/response DTOs for Directory discovery search, resolve, private contact discovery, handle lookup, agent selector lookup, and push webhook registration operations.

verification_method.description: DID URL of the issuer key that signed this presentation; its controller MUST equal iss.

source_refs.description: Event ids this entry was derived from, so a consumer can go back to the truth source and verify it. Omit the member entirely when the entry has no Event provenance: an implementation MUST NOT synthesize an id for an Event it never authored, and MUST NOT send an empty array to stand in for one. minItems stays 1 so a present array cannot fake compliance.

verified_badge.description: Public organization verification badge suitable for directory preview rendering.

member_count.description: Public exact organization member count when the organization directory policy permits exact counts.

realms.description: Public Realm ids linked to this organization when the organization directory policy permits Realm fan-out preview.

realm_count.description: Count of public Realm ids linked to this organization.

directory_resolve_handle_request_body.description: Resolve a canonical handle. For restricted handle claims, requester / proofs / claim_presentations / audience / realm_id are authorization inputs; services MUST use indistinguishable denial for anonymous or unauthorized restricted, revoked, rate-limited, and not-found cases.

controller_handle.description: Canonical controller handle string without the @ sigil.

controller_subject.description: Controller principal DID resolved from controller_handle and verified against the selector claim.

subject.description: Native personal agent principal DID selected by (controller_subject, agent_slug).

directory_list_handles_for_subject_reque.description: List currently visible handle claims for a subject. The service MUST apply the same visibility, audience, requester proof, rate-limit, and indistinguishable-denial rules as resolve_handle; absence of a returned handle is not proof the subject has none.

psi_ristretto255_element.description: Canonical unpadded base64url encoding of one 32-byte RFC 9497 ristretto255 element. Decoders MUST additionally reject non-canonical group encodings and the identity element.

psi_voprf_proof.description: Canonical unpadded base64url encoding of one 64-byte RFC 9497 batched DLEQ proof (two 32-byte scalars).

psi_derived_prefix_16.description: Canonical unpadded base64url encoding of the v1 fixed 16-byte derived digest prefix.

psi_response_padding.description: ASCII SP padding. The origin serializes the complete response with RFC 8785 JCS as UTF-8, omits Content-Encoding and applies no content coding, and chooses this value so the HTTP entity body Content-Length exactly equals the phase bucket declared by ServiceDescribe.private_contact_discovery.

psi_batch_id.description: Client-generated UUIDv7 typed batch id correlating the blind and match rounds of one logical PSI query. It is unique within the authenticated device credential and is bound to canonical request digests for replay-safe quota charging.

psi_blind_request_body.description: Round 1 of the §6.2 two-round OPRF set-membership PSI: the client submits blinded connection identifiers. PSI window quota is enforced here; denial is HTTP 429 psi_quota_exhausted in the standard ErrorEnvelope, never a 200 outcome.

ciphersuite.description: Exact RFC 9497 ciphersuite identifier. The ak.private_contact_discovery.v1 profile fixes the separate RFC protocol mode to modeVOPRF (0x01).

blinded_elements.description: Client-padded batch. Cardinality MUST equal ServiceDescribe.private_contact_discovery.batch_item_count; real and dummy elements are indistinguishable to the provider.

psi_match_request_body.description: Round 2 of the §6.2 two-round PSI: the client submits one fixed 16-byte derived digest prefix for every element of the admitted blind batch, preserving cardinality and order. An admitted batch_id MUST NOT be quota-denied at this phase.

derived_prefixes.description: Each entry is the fixed 16-byte prefix of the corresponding unblinded VOPRF output digest. Cardinality and order MUST equal the admitted blind request.

directory_private_contact_discovery_requ.description: Two-round OPRF set-membership PSI request (zh/discovery/discovery-directory.md §6.2/§6.3); the phase field discriminates the round.

invite_consent_handoff_stub.description: Minimal invite/consent handoff stub allowed beside PSI match bits. It declares state or next-step guidance only; it MUST NOT carry a contact request token, reachability proof, profile, membership, or read grant.

state_digest.description: If present, MUST be salted per requester/session or replaced by an audience-bound opaque token per consent-model.md §6.2.

psi_blind_outcome.description: Round 1 success outcome: VOPRF evaluations over the fixed-size submitted batch plus one RFC 9497 batched proof. evaluated_elements MUST be same-length and same-order as the request's blinded_elements.

evaluation_proofs.description: Exactly one RFC 9497 batched VOPRF DLEQ proof covering the entire fixed-size evaluated_elements array. The client verifies it with the public key for this key_epoch from ServiceDescribe.private_contact_discovery.

derived_prefix_bytes.description: Fixed byte length of every round-2 derived_prefixes entry in the v1 profile.

psi_match_outcome.description: Round 2 success outcome: fixed-cardinality hit bitmap (dummy-padded to the provider-enforced batch_item_count). Per-target conditions (nonexistent, undiscoverable, per-target policy-denied, OPRF mismatch) are encoded as unmatched bits and MUST NOT surface as distinct fields, codes, or timing (§6.4 Class A).

handoff_stubs.description: Optional minimal invite/consent handoff stubs. If present, MUST have the same cardinality as hit_bitmap, with dummy stubs (e.g. state="unknown") at unmatched positions so the field shape does not reveal hits.

directory_private_contact_discovery_outc.description: Two-round PSI success outcomes, discriminated by phase. PSI quota denial is NOT an outcome shape: it is HTTP 429 psi_quota_exhausted in the standard ErrorEnvelope at the blind phase, padded to the success-path size bucket and delay class (§6.4 Class B).

trigger.description: Expiry anchor trigger. on_first_read / on_last_read are driven by private read cursor or policy-allowed receipt inputs through anonymous aggregate trigger contributions; expiry metadata MUST NOT expose reader identity.

grace_ms.description: Additional local projection / key-drop grace. Does not extend the Realm policy maximum lifetime.

read_trigger_window_ms.description: Maximum wait window for on_last_read aggregate contributions. If omitted, implementations MUST use max_ttl_ms. This window is metadata-only and MUST NOT expose reader identity or unread reader count.

schemas/draft-sync.schema.json.title: Arkret Draft Sync Account Data
schemas/draft-sync.schema.json.description: Encrypted account-data plaintext shape for ak.profile.draft_sync.v1.

aad_visibility_event_id.description: Normative discriminator for event id visibility in aad. hidden forbids aad.event_id and aad.event_ref_digest; routing_digest requires aad.event_ref_digest and forbids aad.event_id; opaque_id requires aad.event_id and forbids aad.event_ref_digest.

scope_digest.description: Domain-separated commitment to the Event's exact scope_ref under ak.aad-scope-v1 (encryption-and-audit.md 2.3.2). Unconditionally required for every scope so that carrying it never fingerprints one scope kind, and irreversible so the server cannot enumerate Sidecar existence from ciphertext metadata.

oneOf.description: Reference to accepted ak.mls.genesis / winning ak.mls.commit event.

group_state_ref.description: v1 MLS group state lookup hint. MUST point to accepted ak.mls.genesis / winning ak.mls.commit / equivalent group state proof. Does NOT replace MLS transcript verification. See encryption-and-audit.md §4. Ratchet tree material MUST NOT be carried in the per-message envelope; group state changes strand through ak.mls.genesis / Welcome / Commit events.

key_ref.description: MLS group binding hints. Closed object: privacy-sensitive AAD must not be smuggled through here. Forbidden in v1: ratchet_tree, leaf_node, group_info (these MUST NOT be replicated per-message).

purpose.description: AEAD purpose for this domain (encryption-and-audit.md 2.10.2). It is a nonce-derivation and AAD input, so it separates a content nonce from every other AEAD domain under the same key and epoch. Present only for scheme=mls_exporter_aead_v1; mls_rfc9420 derives its message keys from the MLS secret tree and has no exporter AEAD.

aead_profile.description: canonical_id of an ACTIVE row of artifacts/registry/mls-ciphersuite-registry.json. It MUST equal the ciphersuite the MLS group at key_ref.group_state_ref actually negotiated (encryption-and-audit.md 2.10.2, conformance/encoding.md 10.1); a reserved suite, an unregistered suite, an HPKE suite name or any local alias MUST fail closed. It also fixes AEAD.Nk for the content key and N_AEAD for the nonce, so a receiver cannot derive either without it. Present only for scheme=mls_exporter_aead_v1.

schemas/erasure-receipt-operations.schem.title: Arkret Erasure Receipt Operations
schemas/erasure-receipt-operations.schem.description: Typed service-to-service submit, acceptance and retrieval carriers for hard-erasure receipts and their exact retained verification stubs.

erasure_receipt_package.description: Self-contained acceptance package. retained_stub is always present on this carrier even when receipt.retained_stub is omitted. If receipt.retained_stub is present, its canonical bytes MUST equal retained_stub. receipt_digest = H('ak.erasure-receipt.v1', receipt); retained_stub_digest MUST equal SHA-256(RFC8785_JCS(retained_stub)).

erasure_receipt_submit_request_body.description: Canonical body of ak.peer.erasure_receipt.command.submit. Idempotency-Key is a required signed HTTP header and is not duplicated in the body.

erasure_receipt_acceptance.description: Receiver-signed acceptance. proof signs H('ak.erasure-receipt-acceptance.v1', this object without proof). A duplicate reuses the original accepted_at and byte-identical acceptance object.

erasure_receipt_resource.description: Result of ak.peer.erasure_receipt.resource.get. The package is byte-identical in semantic content to the accepted submit package; no later lookup may substitute another retained stub.

schemas/erasure-receipt.schema.json.title: Arkret Erasure Receipt
schemas/erasure-receipt.schema.json.description: Signed attestation that an issuer completed, partially completed, or blocked a hard-erasure request within a declared storage boundary. It proves the issuer's deletion action and retained verification stub, not disappearance of independent third-party copies.

scope.description: Boundary in which deletion was attempted. This MUST be narrow enough for an auditor to tell which service/storage class made the claim.

retained_stub_digest.description: Hash of the retained verification stub after erasure: hash(canonical_json(retained_stub)). The stub verifies typed-reference structure, redundant digest consistency, receipt/stub binding, and linkage to retained external proof, Seal, redaction-authorization, and legal-hold evidence. It does not independently verify erased canonical Event bytes.

retained_stub.description: Optional in-band verification stub. When omitted, the issuer MUST expose the same canonical stub via its erasure receipt endpoint; retained_stub_digest still binds the exact bytes.

fanout_status.description: Cross-Principal-Server erasure receipt fanout aggregate status tracked by the issuing server (models/realm-and-space.md §2.6.2). 'pending' = peers still within erasure_propagation_window_ms and not all acknowledged; 'complete' = every peer that ever held this Realm's content returned a receipt; 'incomplete' = at least one peer failed to acknowledge within erasure_propagation_window_ms. The issuing server MUST surface 'incomplete' to audit/UI and MUST NOT silently swallow it. Absent on receipts that do not drive fanout tracking.

peer_receipts.description: Per-peer fanout acknowledgement records maintained by the issuing server: one entry per peer Principal Server that ever held this Realm's content. Each entry records that peer's acknowledgement status and time, backing the aggregate fanout_status.

status.description: 'pending' = awaiting this peer's feedback receipt; 'acknowledged' = peer returned a receipt (regardless of its outcome); 'failed' = peer reported a non-completed feedback outcome (partially_completed / blocked_by_legal_hold); 'timed_out' = no feedback within erasure_propagation_window_ms.

receipt_id.description: The peer's own feedback receipt id, when received.

schemas/erasure-verification-stub.schema.title: Arkret Erasure Verification Stub
schemas/erasure-verification-stub.schema.description: Minimal retained verification stub bound by erasure-receipt.retained_stub_digest. It preserves event graph, proof, seal, redaction, legal-hold and receipt linkage evidence without retaining erased plaintext.

event_digest.description: Optional redundant digest for an Event subject. Its suite and all 32 digest octets MUST exactly match the suite wire code and digest carried by subject.subject_ref. If omitted, the suite and digest are recovered from the Event ID. This field and the Event ID preserve consistency evidence; neither independently verifies erased canonical Event bytes.

events.description: Canonical set projection of covered Event canonical digests. Bare event IDs are forbidden because they do not bind Event content. Items MUST be strictly increasing by the UTF-8 bytes of canonical_json(item); producers sort and deduplicate before signing, and receivers reject a non-canonical wire array before digest verification.

proofs.description: Detached receipt proofs sign canonical_json({context:'ak.receipt-proof-v1', payload_digest: receipt_digest, issuer, verification_method, created_at, domain?, audience?}); context is a fixed signing-context domain tag, not a wire field.

allOf.$comment: A PCR genesis receipt is a canonical set containing exactly one realm create and one founding device authorize item. Array position has no domain meaning.

A device re-anchor receipt is a canonical set containing exactly one reanchor and one replacement authorize item. The issuer compares scope.reanchor_digest with the item whose kind is ak.device.reanchor and scope.replacement_authorize_digest with the item whose kind is ak.device.authorize; array position has no domain meaning.

device_reanchor_scope.description: Durable acceptance evidence for the PCR-policy re-anchor unit. Authority is selected by the exact authority instance plus the PCR-local monotonic device generation CAS; the base branch carries no DID version, registry head or publication material, and a receiver MUST NOT synthesize either from the generation refs. Every authority field MUST equal the corresponding field of the covered ak.device.reanchor payload.

authority_instance.description: Exact authority instance re-anchored by this unit. It MUST reverse-bind principal_id and realm_id and MUST equal the covered ak.device.reanchor payload authority_instance field-for-field including authority_instance_digest. A same-core instance carrying a different principal_server_id, pcr_realm_id or principal_genesis_receipt_digest is a different PCR and MUST be rejected.

previous_device_generation.description: MUST equal the covered ak.device.reanchor payload previous_device_generation.

new_device_generation.description: Accepted monotonic successor generation. It MUST equal the covered ak.device.reanchor payload new_device_generation and MUST be the immediate successor of previous_device_generation. It is a PCR-local ref and MUST NOT be derived from or rendered as a DID versionId.

reanchor_digest.description: MUST equal event_digest of the unique events[] item whose kind is ak.device.reanchor.

replacement_authorize_digest.description: MUST equal event_digest of the unique events[] item whose kind is ak.device.authorize.

pcr_genesis_scope.description: Durable acceptance evidence for the create-once PCR genesis unit. Envelope digests are calculated only after both Events are fully formed and never enter either Event preimage.

did_version_id.description: The exact did:webvh inception versionId pinned by the identity-root control proof and used to initialize current_device_generation_ref.

log_head_digest.description: The exact DID inception log head digest accepted for this PCR genesis.

control_key_digest.description: Digest of the inception identity-root update key pinned by the control proof.

registration_evidence_digest.description: SHA-256 digest of RFC 8785 JCS of the complete accepted registration_did_evidence relayed to the Principal Server.

create_digest.description: MUST equal event_digest of the unique events[] item whose kind is ak.realm.create.

founding_authorize_digest.description: MUST equal event_digest of the unique events[] item whose kind is ak.device.authorize.

schemas/event-envelope.schema.json.title: Arkret Event Envelope
schemas/event-envelope.schema.json.description: Single canonical wire object for durable and actor-private Events. kind + schema-validated payload is the only producer-authored business fact; reducer cell targets and lattice operations are derived from the registered reducer contract and never supplied on wire. DataEvents carry seal_ref/auth_context; Control Moves carry seal_basis and optional preconditions. proof.event_digest hashes canonical producer bytes after removing proofs, unsigned, and the sole reducer-stamped top-level field actor_kind. Signed scope_ref is included in the digest and is independently checked against payload-derived security scope. Signal uses signal-envelope.schema.json; point-to-point device verification and secret distribution use device-message.schema.json.

kind.description: Standard ak.* Event kinds MUST appear in artifacts/registry/event-kind-registry.json. State convergence is defined by the registered pure reducer over kind + payload; producers do not submit cell writes.

scope_ref.description: Required producer-signed security scope. It enters proof.event_digest and E2EE AAD. Reducers independently derive the Realm/Circle scope from the schema-validated payload and accepted references; missing dependencies, an underivable scope, realm_id mismatch, or any unequal field is fail closed. Exact product targets remain inside recipient-visible ciphertext.

actor_id.description: Principal whose Realm/cell state the Event mutates and to whom the durable fact is attributed. When executed_by is absent, the proof signer maps to actor_id. When executed_by is present, actor_id remains the principal of record while the actual executor and proof signer map to executed_by.

executed_by.description: Optional actual executor DID for a delegated write. This covers both an agent/applet/service acting for a controller actor and a controller acting under explicit managed-principal delegation to write an Agent principal's control state. actor_id is always the principal of record; executed_by is the principal that issued and signed the wire write. When present, MUST appear together with authorization_ref. Applet delegated writes also MUST carry applet_id. Enters canonical event bytes, event digest, and E2EE AAD. Receivers MUST verify the proof's verification_method maps to executed_by (not actor_id) and MUST NOT synthesize an actor_id signature.

authorization_ref.description: Optional. Required when executed_by is present. Prefer a materialized ak:grant:* id; an event id is allowed only when it points to the accepted grant/delegation event that produced the effective authorization; a DID-document delegation URL (did_delegation_ref) is allowed when the delegation is expressed in the principal DID document; realm_authority_root_ref designates this Realm's registered authority-root cell. Exactly two non-grant profile sources are admitted here: direct_conversation_participant_authority_ref, paired with one critical refs[] role=direct_conversation_binding Event reference, and direct_conversation_bootstrap_authority_ref, paired with one critical refs[] role=direct_conversation_founding_unit Event reference for the pre-binding founding phase. An arbitrary Event/cell MUST NOT be treated as participant authority. When executed_by is present, authorization_ref binds the executor delegation instead and the DM profile source is evaluated as an independent conjunctive profile gate.

applet_id.description: Optional signed Applet provenance. Required by ak.profile.applet_* when the Event is introduced by an Applet, Ghost Actor, bridge, or delegated applet path. Enters canonical event bytes and therefore is covered by proof.event_digest. When present, authorization_ref MUST also be present and MUST bind this applet_id and registration_epoch per zh/extensions/applet-integration.md section 11.

external_ref.description: Optional signed external provenance reference for Applet / bridge-originated Events. It is covered by event_digest and MUST NOT be carried only in unsigned when used for loop prevention, audit, or external-message idempotency. Must not contain unauthorized external plaintext.

actor_kind.description: Reducer-stamped projection of the actor_id Actor Profile's actor_kind at write time (see zh/models/event-and-patch.md and zh/models/actor.md). Lets audit/forensic/offline readers classify the event without resolving Actor Profile. Does NOT include 'device': a device is not an actor principal and never appears as actor_id; device actions are attributed to the owning user/org principal DID. MUST NOT appear in actor-supplied submit payload (schema_violation reason=actor_kind_reducer_managed); reducer stamps it during accept. Immutable once written and excluded from producer proof.event_digest.

hlc.description: Advisory hybrid logical clock. INCLUDED in canonical bytes for signing and event digest (so it is integrity-protected and cannot be rewritten by relays), but semantically advisory: used only as a deterministic tiebreaker for timeline display when two events are causally unreachable. MUST NOT influence authorization, lattice join, Control Move precondition comparison, or Seal finality. See encoding.md §7 and event-auth-state-resolution.md §3 rule 1.

prev_refs.description: Actor-chain causal predecessors as complete Event IDs. Each Event ID carries the digest suite code and all 32 digest octets and is committed by this Event's digest preimage. For semantic refs (authorized_by, after, state_witness, inclusion_proof, ...), use refs[].

refs.description: Semantic refs with role. did_recovery_anchor is reserved exclusively for ak.device.reanchor and is enforced bidirectionally below; all other common roles remain open extension tokens.

causal_refs.description: DataEvent semantic causal predecessors by event_digest. A DataEvent carrying payload.patch MUST provide at least one causal_ref and MUST identify exactly one accepted base-head digest for every target cell; the per-cell uniqueness and post-state reconstruction checks are reducer semantics. Other DataEvents may use this field for business causality. These refs are not global completeness proofs.

preconditions.description: Control Move only. Pre-state predicates that must hold under the seal_basis governance view; if any fails, the entire event fails. DataEvents MUST NOT carry preconditions.

seal_ref.description: DataEvent only. Accepted control-plane Seal id used as the authorization basis. Receivers verify identity/key/capability validity at this seal and apply revocation freshness rules.

auth_context.description: DataEvent only. Pins the signing DID and key epoch used to verify authorization at seal_ref. Effective capabilities are derived from the accepted governance basis, never selected by the producer.

seal_basis.description: Control Move only. Signed governance basis for preconditions and reducer derivation. The canonical sorted Seal leaves are the sole producer commitment; receivers resolve and verify each Seal and deterministically recompute the covered control set and joined state. Seal roots remain on the Seal itself and are not copied into the Event.

unsigned.description: Local / transport-only metadata (server-derived hints, redaction reason, age). NOT covered by signature or event digest.

proofs.description: Detached signatures over the canonical proof binding object. proof.event_digest is computed from canonical producer event bytes excluding proofs, unsigned, and reducer-stamped actor_kind; signed scope_ref and advisory hlc are included. Seal signatures live on the Seal object.

requirements.description: Schema, feature, and critical-extension requirements declared by this event. All sub-fields enter the canonical event bytes and the proof event_digest. Reducer selection is derived from the Realm reducer-profile control cell, never declared by an ordinary Event. Receivers MUST fail closed on any unknown critical entry.

schema.description: Schema profile ids this event depends on.

features.description: Features this event requires; receiver MUST fail closed if any is unknown.

critical_extensions.description: Critical extension declarations; each entry MUST have id, extension_scope, fail_closed=true.

allOf.$comment: A patch-bearing DataEvent is identified by its required seal_ref and payload.patch. It needs at least one causal base; exact per-target-cell matching remains a reducer check.
Signed Applet provenance invariants. external_ref is only meaningful when bound to a signed applet_id, and Applet-originated writes must cite the accepted authorization/delegation grant.

Closed direct-conversation participant authority reference. Direct participant writes cite the registered source token and one exact critical binding Event evidence ref. Delegated Agent writes use authorization_ref for the executor delegation and satisfy participant authority independently in the profile evaluator.

Closed direct-conversation bootstrap authority reference. Pre-binding founding-phase writes cite the registered bootstrap source token and one exact critical founding-unit Event evidence ref, because no binding Event exists yet to cite.
Known active non-reducer Event kinds MUST NOT carry CBA fields: preconditions/seal_ref/auth_context/seal_basis.
Signal payload type names are not Event kinds and MUST NOT appear in durable history. They exist only inside encrypted Signal payload. To-device kinds use device-message.schema.json.

Known active reducer-input event kinds MUST carry exactly one CBA basis shape: DataEvent (seal_ref + auth_context, no preconditions/seal_basis), Control Move (seal_basis, no seal_ref/auth_context), the ak.realm.create genesis bootstrap shape, OR a Realm bootstrap follow-up shape (same submit batch after create; batch context is enforced by admission, not JSON Schema). Reducer writes are derived from kind+payload and the registry contract. Unknown extension kinds must declare their own critical extension requirements and are not matched by this branch.

oneOf.$comment: ak.strand.create may be the third item of the exact Direct Conversation founding unit, where it is that Realm's main Strand and no accepted Seal exists yet to reference. JSON Schema permits the no-basis shape; batch admission MUST reject it anywhere else, so every ordinary Strand still carries seal_ref and auth_context.
ak.device.authorize may be the second item of the exact PCR bootstrap or device re-anchor atomic unit. JSON Schema permits the no-basis shape; batch admission MUST reject it anywhere else.

allOf.$comment: Conflict-recovery event detection: any precondition with op=head_in implies conflict recovery semantics. When triggered, refs[] MUST contain BOTH a state_witness and an inclusion_proof (event-auth-state-resolution.md §8.1). Schema-level enforcement; reducer-level verify re-checks.
MUST contain at least one state_witness ref
MUST contain at least one inclusion_proof ref
ak.device.reanchor is the only event allowed to carry did_recovery_anchor, and it must carry exactly one critical ref whose id has did:webvh versionId shape.
Count the reserved role independent of critical so one critical plus one non-critical duplicate cannot pass.

Any Event carrying did_inception is confined to the closed self-principal PCR-genesis shape and carries exactly one critical ref. A delegated Agent PCR create intentionally carries no did_inception; batch/reducer admission distinguishes self-principal genesis from delegated Agent genesis by comparing actor_id, executed_by, authorization_ref, PCR binding and DID subject, which JSON Schema cannot express.
Count the reserved role independently so a critical ref plus a non-critical duplicate cannot pass.

A managed_agent_control Realm create without did_inception is syntactically reserved for delegated managed-principal genesis. Requiring the delegation pair prevents a self-principal caller from falling through to ordinary realm.create capability admission; the delegated_pcr_genesis verifier performs the actor/DID/service/realm comparisons that JSON Schema cannot express.

Reject these top-level field names. The Event Envelope root is closed (additionalProperties=false); extension data belongs in payload or requirements.critical_extensions. The root field names type / auth_refs / target_ref / operation_id are dropped and MUST NOT appear at the root; use kind / refs[role=authorized_by] / payload.* fields / SDK-internal id instead (see operations-sync.md §5).

anyOf.$comment: auth_refs is dropped; it MUST NOT appear at the root, use refs[role=authorized_by]

allOf.$comment: zh/models/realm-and-space.md section 2.5.0: ak.realm.create MUST omit realm_id and use the realm_genesis scope. Collaboration realm_id is derived from this Event's event_id; PCR realm_id is derived from the signed actor DID. The uniform omission leaves one receiver-derived genesis form and avoids the collaboration digest cycle. Every other kind MUST carry realm_id.

external_ref.description: Signed external provenance. Extension profiles define exact field vocabulary; common fields include protocol, network_id, instance_id, user_id, location_id, event_id, external_id, and url. Implementations MUST preserve all fields in canonical bytes and MUST NOT use unsigned.external_ref for security decisions.

canonical_event_timestamp.description: Canonical Event Envelope/proof timestamp. UTC Z form with exactly three millisecond digits; whole-second shorthand, finer fractions, and numeric offsets are forbidden.

oneOf.description: Native controller-and-owned-Agents private scope. It is not a Circle and has no editable membership.

Genesis scope for ak.realm.create only. It carries no realm_id because the receiver derives the Realm id: from this Event for collaboration, or from the signed actor DID for PCR (zh/models/realm-and-space.md section 2.5.0). The uniform omission also prevents the collaboration digest cycle.

profile_ref.description: Profile that defines this extension's semantics when schema_ref is not the exact governing profile.

parameters.description: Closed extension-specific parameter bag. Unknown top-level fields are forbidden; extension-defined data belongs here and is interpreted only after id/schema_ref support is sealed.

material_digest.description: Optional digest of out-of-band extension material when parameters would be too large for the event envelope.

event_ref.description: Complete Event reference carrying the suite wire_code and all 32 digest octets. It is suitable for authorization, equality, deduplication, Seal coverage, and exact replay after normal recomputation and acceptance checks.

did_delegation_ref.description: DID URL of a non-device controller/organization authority entry that designates executed_by for an operation profile. Principal device authorization never uses this DID-document branch: it resolves through accepted PCR evidence. Historical DID authority is resolved at the Event accepted-at basis.

realm_authority_root_ref.description: Designates the registered authority-root cell of the envelope's own realm_id. This is a closed constant, not a general cell_ref: only the singleton ak.component.realm.authority_root.v1 cell carries Realm owner authority, and widening it to an arbitrary cell_ref would let any projected cell be presented as an authorization source. Reducer MUST resolve it against that cell in the Event's authorization basis and verify controller_id == the authorizing principal, plus the cell's capability_action_registry_digest and authority_generation. Inside the ak.realm.create genesis batch the staged root value is used and the Event MUST descend from the same batch's create Event through prev_refs; outside that batch an accepted-Seal inclusion proof is required and a staged proof MUST be rejected. See zh/models/realm-and-space.md section 2.5 and zh/authz/capabilities.md section 3.2.

direct_conversation_participant_authorit.description: The daily profile-scoped non-grant authorization source accepted by Event.authorization_ref. It is meaningful solely in ak.profile.direct_conversation_realm.v1 and requires one critical refs[] role=direct_conversation_binding Event reference. The evaluator rederives the pair's unique immutable binding, exact-two participant membership, Realm/Strand/MLS cross-binding, lifecycle, both directional Contact heads/scopes and action-specific gates without consulting Consent; this constant never authorizes arbitrary Realm or third-party writes.

direct_conversation_bootstrap_authority_.description: The pre-binding profile-scoped non-grant authorization source accepted by Event.authorization_ref, meaningful solely in ak.profile.direct_conversation_realm.v1 between an accepted founding unit and the first legal binding endorsement. It requires one critical refs[] role=direct_conversation_founding_unit Event reference pointing at the accepted ak.realm.create of that unit. The verifier recomputes which of the two mutually exclusive phases applies from accepted facts and MUST NOT let the producer choose: provisional_history_send applies only to the founder while the active-generation cell has not passed generation 0, and exact_pair_founding_completion applies once the selected group state holds exactly the pair's authorized leaves and no legal endorsement exists yet. Both phases permanently retire once the first legal ak.direct_conversation.bound endorsement is accepted, after which only direct_conversation_participant_authority_ref remains. Neither phase authorizes policy, grant, a third participant, another Strand or ordinary membership writes. See zh/identity/contact-and-direct-conversation.md section 7.2.

membership_compensation_delegation_ref.description: Content-addressed accepted-at membership compensation delegation. It is valid only for ak.member.state leave/remove submitted with the matching closed membership_compensation_evidence sidecar and registered single-use evaluator.

role.description: Common roles include authorized_by, attestation, parent_event, after, audit_pair, recovery_capability, state_witness, inclusion_proof, did_inception, and did_recovery_anchor. did_recovery_anchor is reserved to ak.device.reanchor by kind dispatch.

proof.description: Optional inline proof material. Used for inclusion_proof role: carries the Merkle audit path defined by event-auth-state-resolution.md §6.2.1 / §6.2.2 that proves a leaf belongs to a witness state_root. May be omitted when id alone is a content-addressed reference to a separately stored proof object.

kind.description: detached_jws = actor / device / service signature over canonical proof binding object: canonical_json({context:'ak.event-proof-v1', event_digest, actor_id, verification_method, created_at, domain?, audience?}). event_digest excludes proofs, unsigned, and reducer-stamped actor_kind; signed scope_ref and advisory hlc are covered. Ordering authority signatures are carried by Seal.

verification_method.description: DID URL of the Event-signing key. Generic verification extracts the canonical bare full_id base under the active method adapter, validates that method history/key, projects the base full_id to did_core_id, and compares the result byte-for-byte with executed_by when present or actor_id otherwise; a did_core_id is never concatenated into a DID URL. For principal device proofs the fragment MUST be the full device_id (`ak:device:<uuidv7>`), so receivers can resolve `(actor_id, device_id)` through the device directory. The sole exception is an Event whose selected admission variant is did_root_anchor: its closed verifier MUST instead require verification_method to equal an active controller-proof verification method from the one critical did_inception/did_recovery_anchor entry and verify the controller proof/update authority against that referenced did:webvh history; a root did:key controller is not rewritten to the principal actor_id. This exception cannot apply to any other Event.

proof_purpose.description: Optional role discriminator for handle-claim proofs. Generic proof consumers ignore it unless their object-family contract makes it required.

proof.description: Generic detached-JWS proof shape reused by non-Event schemas (snapshot signature, snapshot witness attestations, identity receipts, handle claims, etc.). MUST NOT be used as the shape of Event Envelope `proofs[]` — Event proofs reference $defs/event_proof and bind canonical Event bytes via `event_digest`. Non-Event signed objects MUST define an object-family signing-context constant and include it in the canonical proof binding object with payload_digest; the context constant is not a wire field in this generic shape. drift detection: `payload_digest#event_proof` in forbidden-wire-fields.json is the hard-reject mirror of this rule. New non-Event signed objects MAY $ref this shape; new signed Event-shaped objects MUST instead $ref event_proof.

kind.description: Generic detached JWS proof over a canonical non-Event payload binding object that includes an object-family context constant.

verification_method.description: DID URL of the signing key for this non-Event detached proof. Same pattern as $defs/event_proof.verification_method; semantics are decoupled from Event proof (see $defs/event_proof for the Event-only shape).

payload_digest.description: Generic non-Event detached-proof hash. This $defs/proof shape is reused by non-Event schemas; Event.properties.proofs references $defs/event_proof and MUST use event_digest instead.

proof_purpose.description: Optional role discriminator for non-Event proofs. handle-claim.schema.json requires binding_state=verified claims to carry at least one proofs[] entry with proof_purpose=holder_acceptance; without this optional field that requirement was unsatisfiable under additionalProperties:false. governance_authorization marks a resource-governance-key authorization (directory withdraw/takedown-appeal, discovery-directory.md 8.7.1). Generic proof consumers ignore it unless their object-family contract makes it load-bearing.

schemas/event-payload.schema.json.title: Arkret Standard Event Payloads
schemas/event-payload.schema.json.description: Definitions bundle for common payload contracts used by registered ak.* Event.kind values. The root schema is intentionally generic and MUST NOT be used as a complete payload validator. Event validators MUST validate the full Event Envelope and dispatch by Event.kind to the matching $defs payload class using artifacts/registry/event-kind-registry.json.

not.$comment: The event-payload schema root is a definition-bundle diagnostic only. Standard payload validation MUST select one explicit kind-bound schema ref from the event kind registry.

account_blocklist_payload.description: Payload for ak.account.blocklist. Holder-private personal blocklist state; it never enters shared Realm state or federation payloads.

version.description: Monotonic whole-value CAS revision. The next accepted ak.account.blocklist payload MUST use current version + 1; ak.account_data.set for key ak.account.blocklist uses expected_revision against the same counter. Omitting an entry in the next revision removes it, and entries=[] clears the list.

mode.description: block denies a new holder-facing interaction on the selected surfaces and filters shared durable content only after canonical receive/store; mute keeps content visible but suppresses attention surfaces; hide keeps canonical content but omits it from default holder rendering/search. None of the modes revokes a Realm capability or rewrites shared history.

account_data_set_payload.description: Payload for ak.account_data.set. Writes one holder-private account-data key; the value may be plaintext inside an already private envelope, encrypted account-data material, or a tombstone. Every key is a compare-and-set whole-value register per zh/models/account-data.md §5: expected_revision is the revision the writer believes is current (0 to create), and the accepted revision is expected_revision + 1.

expected_revision.description: Compare-and-set precondition against the accepted per-key revision. A mismatch MUST be rejected with cas_conflict and MUST NOT be stored; the revision counter is a high-water mark that never goes backwards, so a stale offline retry cannot resurrect a superseded value.

body.description: Caller-supplied opaque account-data value. Any JSON value.

account_id.description: Opaque service-account identifier. It is the ak.component.account.status.v1 cell subject; accounts bound to the same principal_id are evaluated independently.

reason_code.description: Machine-readable account status diagnostic. Values that cross service or federation boundaries MUST be registered in error-code-registry.json reason_codes (for example deactivation_federation_incomplete).

supersedes_status_event_id.description: Event id of the ak.account.status event being superseded. Required by zh/identity/account-lifecycle.md §3 rule 2 when lowering severity (e.g. back to active after appeal). MUST NOT be used to downgrade erasure_pending (reason_code erasure_pending_is_terminal).

actor_profile_create_payload.description: Initial actor profile payload. The materialized resolution projection is reducer-managed from the PCR resolution cell and is forbidden on this authoring surface. id/updated_by/updated_at are likewise materialized fields, not create input.

actor_profile_update_payload.description: Actor Profile patch payload. resolution and every resolution.* descendant path are reducer-managed projections of the PCR resolution cell and are forbidden on this generic profile write surface.

agent_action_approve_payload.description: Payload for ak.agent.action_approve. Controller approval binds the draft/action request, target, approved payload digest, expiry, and single-use nonce.

agent_action_reject_payload.description: Payload for ak.agent.action_reject. Controller rejection terminates a draft/action request without shared Realm side effects.

agent_action_request_payload.description: Payload for ak.agent.action_request. Actor-private request for controller approval before a shared Realm write is emitted.

agent_action_target.description: Minimal target descriptor for an actor-private agent draft or approval. It identifies the eventual shared write surface without disclosing private draft content.

agent_deactivate_payload.description: Payload for the single terminal ak.self.agent.deactivate Control Move. At the accepted Seal covering this Move, every verifier mechanically AND-gates all subordinate Agent runtime-key authorizations, sessions, pairing handles, capability grants, KeyPackages, presence and future submissions on lifecycle=active. Historical child Events remain auditable; explicit child revokes are not prerequisites and are reserved for targeted revocation while the Agent is non-terminal. The lifecycle state witness is sufficient transition evidence for every derived ineffective child.

previous_status.description: Controller lifecycle intent at deactivation time. Generic Agent status has only lifecycle, readiness and presence; pairing-poll runtime_state is operation-local and never appears here (key-management.md §3.6.1).

agent_draft_propose_payload.description: Payload for ak.agent.draft.propose. Actor-private proposal that may materialize into controller-owned encrypted draft account data after policy checks.

agent_key_approval_evidence.description: Evidence that authorized this agent key. Durable grant/approval/proposal/policy evidence carries ref so it can be replayed at the event frontier; the short-lived pairing_request branch instead binds pairing_request_id, request_canonical_digest, and approved_by and MUST omit ref.

pairing_request_id.description: Optional profile-local, short-lived pairing artifact id. Required by the agent-key pairing acceptance flow and MUST equal the pairing_request_id in the accepted request; it is not a durable protocol object ref.

agent_key_authorize_payload.description: Payload for ak.agent.key.authorize. Binds one concrete agent signing key to an accountable principal, explicit agent_key_scope, audience, validity window, approval evidence, and both the service-surface and content-capability ceilings that later agent_key_proof sessions must narrow from.

public_key_digest.description: SHA-256 of the decoded 32-byte Ed25519 public key behind verification_method, computed with agent_signing_public_key_digest. Native Agent authorization always commits this raw-key digest; it is distinct from the private runtime-request PublicKey DTO digest.

signing_key_binding_digest.description: sha256 over the canonical agent-signing binding core containing schema, agent_id, agent_key_id, verification_method, public_key, public_key_digest, issued_at, optional expires_at, and controller_id, but excluding agent_key_authorize_event_id and controller_proof. The complete accepted Event ID and controller proof are appended only when materializing the public ak.schema.agent_signing_key_binding.v1 object. Including this Event's not-yet-derived identity would create an impossible digest fixed point. A service MUST recompute the core digest before appending the verified accepted Event identity and MUST NOT substitute another disclosure.

expires_at.description: Optional: absent means the key authorization is non-expiring and governed solely by revocation (ak.agent.key.revoke / lifecycle cascade).

supersedes.description: Exact set of every active Agent-key authorization dot observed immediately before this controller-signed authorization is accepted during runtime re-pairing. Each entry binds both the key id and the authorization Event that introduced the active dot. The array MUST be omitted only for first pairing, when the authoritative active set is empty. Every replacement MUST set-equal the complete pre-accept active authorization set, including an old dot with the same key_id as the new authorization; a stale, partial, extra, or implicit map overwrite fails closed. Acceptance atomically removes these dots with reason superseded_by_repairing and adds this authorize dot, so no server-forged ak.agent.key.revoke Event is required.

revocation_check_ref.description: Optional freshness source for revocation checking. When expires_at is absent, authorization lifetime is governed by the canonical revocation chain and lifecycle cascade; this field may identify the freshness source used for that check.

runtime_attestation.description: Optional runtime / workload attestation captured at pairing approval time. v1 enum includes self_asserted as baseline; future profiles MAY register TEE / SLSA / SPIFFE attestation kinds. Implementations encountering an unknown kind MUST fail closed.

kind.description: v1 enum. Future profiles MAY extend via accepted attestation taxonomy.

attestation_digest.description: Optional digest of verifiable attestation material when kind is not self_asserted.

attestation_ref.description: Optional external verifiable attestation reference (TEE quote, SLSA provenance, etc.).

agent_key_id.description: Stable key identifier within the agent DID. Prefer the DID URL verification method id when available.

agent_key_revoke_payload.description: Payload for ak.agent.key.revoke. The or_set cell subject is (agent_id, key_id); future protocol proofs from this key fail closed once this event is covered by an accepted Seal. The authoring basis is the Control Move envelope seal_basis; the payload carries no frontier field.

agent_key_scope.description: Agent scope object with two uses. In POST /_arkret/self/agents requested_scope it is the required immutable global Agent ceiling; in ak.agent.key.authorize it is a per-key ceiling that MAY be narrower but MUST be an actions/resources/constraints subset of the provision ceiling. It is never a capability grant. actions may contain service operation ids and content action tokens; an omitted action can never be restored by a key, Realm grant or session. resources constrain the service surface and may optionally narrow later content resources, but never authorize content by themselves. Provisioning and pairing do not materialize capability grants from this object; effective authority is the intersection of provision ceiling, key ceiling, independent Realm-scoped grants, session request, membership and policy, with participation applied as an additional deny gate.

actions.description: Literal action ceiling. Every downstream key scope, grant or session action MUST appear here; action families, prefixes and subsumption do not widen it.

resources.description: Selector ceiling, not authorization. Each downstream selector must be covered by a parent selector. operation/service parents cover the same kind and matching explicit field and cannot carry content fields. The content-kind vocabulary is the ResourceSelector vocabulary except '*'; kind=realm covers every Realm-local content kind in the matching Realm and other content kinds cover only the same kind. Omitted parent realm_id is a cross-Realm ceiling wildcard and omitted exact ref is a same-kind/same-Realm wildcard. With no content selector, later Realm grants still choose concrete resources and no content wildcard is granted.

constraints.description: Global mandatory constraints. Every effective key/grant/session evaluation MUST retain and AND these constraints; downstream scopes may add stricter constraints but MUST NOT omit or relax provision constraints.

agent_pause_payload.description: Payload for ak.self.agent.pause. The status cell is keyed by agent_id and moves from active to paused. Authorization is evaluated against the Control Move envelope seal_basis; the reducer accepts the transition only under the accepted current control frontier.

agent_resume_payload.description: Payload for ak.self.agent.resume. Authorization is evaluated against the Control Move envelope seal_basis, and reducers re-check controller, agent, key, capability, Realm policy, and accountability grant against the accepted current control frontier before returning the agent to active. Sidecar desired membership is derived afterward and is not carried in this payload.

agent_sidecar_exchange_control_payload.description: Outer payload for ak.agent.sidecar.exchange.control. sidecar_id and source_context_ref route the Event inside a native Sidecar scope; encrypted_payload plaintext MUST validate as agent-sidecar-exchange-control.schema.json. Admission MUST require matching scope_ref.kind=sidecar and actor_id equal to the Sidecar controller.

agent_slug.description: Controller-scoped native personal agent selector slug used by @<controller-handle>/<agent_slug>. Not a global handle or authorization subject.

applet_bridge_error_payload.description: Payload for ak.applet.bridge_error. Durable Realm-history Event recording a bridge / external-network failure. Field table: zh/extensions/applet-schema.md §7. MUST bind realm_id, failed_transaction_ref, retriable, and visibility_scope; missing any required field MUST be rejected as schema_violation. MUST NOT inline unauthorized external plaintext.

failed_transaction_ref.description: Reference to the failed transaction / source Event. MUST NOT inline unauthorized external plaintext.

error_class.description: Closed error category for aggregation / alerting. See zh/extensions/applet-schema.md §7.

visibility_scope.description: Closed visibility scope enum for the error event. Clients MUST honor it and MUST NOT expose bridge-internal detail to unrelated members.

external_ref.description: External network reference (protocol / network id). MUST NOT contain unauthorized external plaintext.

message.description: Human-readable summary. MUST NOT leak unauthorized external plaintext.

retry_after_ms.description: Suggested retry delay; meaningful only when retriable=true.

applet_registration_payload.description: Payload for ak.applet.registration. Durable Realm-history Event registering an Applet (bridge / bot / Ghost Actor namespace). Field vocabulary: zh/extensions/applet-integration.md §4 and zh/extensions/applet-schema.md §1 (the authoritative machine schema is applet.schema.json, which documents the applet object snapshot; the wire Event payload is this closed class). An Applet's capability to enter a Realm MUST be granted by that Realm's owner / admin / authorized registry-authz service; a self-signed registration alone MUST NOT write to a Realm (reason=applet_registration_unauthorized). registration MUST be signed by the controller DID (proof per models/event-and-patch.md §3).

applet_id.description: Stable applet identifier: a DID or the typed-id form ak:applet:<uuidv7>.

service_id.description: DID of the service hosting the applet runtime.

controller_id.description: DID of the Applet controller / external system; signs the registration.

claimed_profiles.description: Canonical Applet implementation profiles copied from the accepted package. These durable claims are the authority source for profile-bound grant rules.

namespaces.description: Applet namespace claims (actors / realms / handles patterns). Namespace match alone never grants write capability.

webhook_auth.description: Transaction push HTTP signature policy copied from the Applet package. webhook_auth.key_ref is the Applet service DID URL used as the app/bridge->arkret inbound source signature anchor and is bound to this registration_epoch; node->Applet pushes verify the Arkret source service DID from Source-Service-ID instead.

manifest.description: Applet manifest snapshot (capability requirements, supported intents, etc.).

proof.description: Controller-DID detached signature over the canonical registration object (excluding proof). An empty proof object MUST be rejected as schema_violation; required proof fields per models/event-and-patch.md §3.

audit_accessed_payload.description: Strict payload for ak.audit.accessed. It records a specific access or paired privacy-sensitive write. Reducers MUST reject business events that require an audit pair unless this payload identifies the same writer, target, and object/cell in the same ordered submit batch, equivalent control transaction, or an accepted pre-read event with RYW receipt.

late_recovery_original_event_id.description: Required when access_kind=e2ee_late_recovery; identifies the original encrypted event whose plaintext became available through late key recovery.

ryw_required.description: When true, plaintext release or privileged projection MUST wait for an accepted-history RYW receipt before disclosure.

audit_applet_binding_create_payload.description: Genesis payload for ak.audit.applet_binding.create. binding_id, initial active status, creator, and creation time are derived from the accepted Event envelope. Policy fields are immutable; changing them creates a new binding so historical release eligibility cannot be silently expanded.

activation_frontier_digest.description: Accepted Seal coverage digest at which this binding/policy became member-visible. Release requests MUST NOT cover messages or epochs before this coverage point.

first_auditable_epoch.description: First MLS epoch eligible for this binding. Reducers MUST verify it is the epoch created by a ak.mls.commit covering activation_frontier_digest; earlier epochs are permanently ineligible.

retroactive_release.description: v1 audited E2EE never permits a later binding or policy expansion to make pre-activation messages auditable.

eligibility_basis.description: A message is eligible only if it was encrypted after a commit covering this binding/policy frontier.

max_lookback_ms.description: Optional maximum age, measured from session request/authorization time, for otherwise eligible material. Later policy changes may narrow this for future messages but MUST NOT expand already encrypted messages.

max_epoch_span.description: Optional cap on the number of sealed historical epochs a single session/release may cover.

allowed_target_kinds.description: Optional target class allow-list for targeted_evidence_release.

audit_applet_binding_state_payload.description: Lifecycle-only transition for an existing Audit Applet Binding. Scope and release policy cannot be edited by this Event; a policy change requires a new binding genesis.

audit_release_payload.description: Payload for ak.audit.release. A sealed audit release manifest for a bounded historical window. It appends to the control-plane ordered log ak.component.audit.release.v1 keyed by session_id only while the accepted session FSM head is notice. Same-basis close dominates and rejects the release. The payload records release metadata and wrapped material digests only; plaintext MUST NOT be inlined.

recipient_public_key_ref.description: Release material encryption target. MUST equal the authorize payload's approved_recipient_public_key_ref and resolve to recipient_audit_actor_id's authorized audit-release key.

eligibility_proof.description: Proof summary that the requested release is inside the binding activation frontier, first_auditable_epoch, release_window_policy, and the targets' encryption-time eligibility snapshots.

activation_commit_ref.description: ak.mls.commit that covered the activation frontier and created first_auditable_epoch, when the release covers MLS epoch material.

policy_snapshot_digest.description: Digest of the binding/release window policy snapshot used when authorizing this release.

target_eligibility_digest.description: Digest of the deterministic per-target/per-epoch eligibility set proving no pre-activation material is included.

audit_session_contract.description: Shared payload class for ak.audit.session.request / authorize / notice / close. The session_state field is the target state of the control-plane FSM cell ak.component.audit.session.v1 keyed by session_id. Initial state is request; legal main-path transitions are request->authorize->notice->close, with request->close and authorize->close allowed for aborted sessions. Close is terminal; same-basis conflicting siblings produce Bottom.

approved_recipient_audit_actor_id.description: Audit subject approved to receive release material. Required on ak.audit.session.authorize; ak.audit.release.recipient_audit_actor_id MUST match it byte-for-byte.

approved_recipient_public_key_ref.description: Audit release recipient key approved by ak.audit.session.authorize. MUST resolve to approved_recipient_audit_actor_id's authorized audit-release key; ak.audit.release.recipient_public_key_ref MUST match it byte-for-byte.

board_space_id.description: A Space with kind=board. Pattern matches any ak:space:; kind invariant enforced by reducer/profile.

call_participant.description: A single participant value added by ak.call.state.payload.roster_delta. See crypto-media/call-state.md §4/§4.1.

foci_preferred.description: Client-local ordered focus preference list used for the session_focus election (see crypto-media/call-state.md §4.1 and media-service-binding.md §5).

participant_identity.description: Required for sfu/mcu roster joins; MUST be absent for a direct p2p/mesh leg.

participant_binding.description: Required for sfu/mcu roster joins; MUST be absent for a direct p2p/mesh leg. The containing call focus.mode selects the semantic branch.

call_recording_start_payload.description: Typed payload for ak.call.recording.start. recording_id is a stable opaque ASCII handle (1–128 bytes, [A-Za-z0-9._-]) that feeds the recording key exporter Context byte-for-byte and MUST NOT be normalized by receivers. capture_kind selects recording vs transcription so both lifecycles share one start event kind. See crypto-media/call-state.md §5 / §5.1.

recording_id.description: Stable opaque recording / transcript lifecycle handle. Canonical byte-for-byte; receivers MUST NOT normalize (case-fold, NFC/NFKC, trim, re-encode) because it is a cross-implementation key-derivation input.

capture_kind.description: Whether this start event opens a recording or a transcription segment. REQUIRED: it selects the target capture cell family (ak.component.call.recording.v1 vs ak.component.call.transcript.v1) in the registered cell contract, so it MUST NOT be inferred from a missing-field default.

visible_notice.description: Asserts the initiating client will display the capture-in-progress notice to all participants.

result.description: Initial immutable capture evidence. retention.consent_confirmed=true closes the pre-capture consent gate before the FSM enters a capturing state. This wire payload MUST NOT carry recording_start_event_id or transcript_start_event_id: the accepted Event identity is derived only after digesting this payload, and the reducer stamps that identity into the projected result cell.

call_create_payload.description: Genesis payload for ak.call.create. call_id is omitted and derived by retyping the accepted Event id. Signaling, media tokens, Morph bindings, and state deltas MUST reference only an already accepted create.

call_state_payload.description: Typed delta payload for ak.call.state. Every present field maps to one or two explicit registered cell effects; omitted axes produce no effect.
