Removing a DID in a later policy_revision revokes it for every later claim re-check; no separate tombstone exists. Reducers MUST evaluate the current accepted bundle cell on a fresh basis before accepting ak.invite.claim.

realm_policy_server_payload.description: Closed payload for ak.realm.policy_server. A declaration writes the complete direct Realm binding; {tombstone:true} is a durable value tombstone that removes the direct binding from effective queries without erasing the cell history.

leakage_class.description: Machine-readable search leakage class. ak.profile.search.blind_index.v1 uses deterministic_token; ak.profile.search.forward_private.v1 requires forward_private; access_hiding is reserved for explicit PIR/ORAM-backed profiles.

token_rotation_cadence_ms.description: Maximum intended interval between search token generations for profiles that rotate index keys or OPRF blinds.

realm_set_default_strand_payload.description: Payload for ak.realm.set_default_strand. Sets / changes the Realm's authoritative default discussion Strand pointer. Reducer projects strand_id into the Realm projection default_strand_id (single authoritative pointer; avoids multi-default dirty state). Reducer MUST verify strand_id references a projected, non-tombstoned Strand in this Realm; a dangling reference MUST be rejected with failed_precondition. The Strand projection is_default is a derived marker (strand_id == realm.default_strand_id), never independent storage. expected_default_strand_id compiles to a cell head_eq precondition for optimistic concurrency (CAS). Absent and explicit null are normalized to the same null value before comparison, so omission asserts head_eq null and is only valid while the cell is still in its initial no-default state; once a default is set the field MUST be present, otherwise the reducer MUST reject with failed_precondition and MUST NOT overwrite unconditionally.

expected_default_strand_id.description: Optimistic-concurrency guard compared as a whole value after absent and explicit null are normalized to null. The reducer accepts the write only if the Realm's current default_strand_id equals this value (null asserts no default is currently set). Omission therefore asserts head_eq null and MUST fail once a default exists. Mismatch MUST be rejected (failed_precondition).

realm_upgrade_state_payload.description: Realm reducer-profile upgrade payload. target_reducer_profile is the new value written to the Realm reducer-profile singleton control cell. The Event's standard head_eq precondition binds the current cell value.

target_reducer_profile.description: Registered reducer profile id this Realm upgrades to.

relation_create_payload.description: Relation creation. The payload carries the whole relation object under `relation`: the registered effect_projection is set value = payload.relation, and event-and-patch.md 2.4.2 permits a projection to move an existing root path wholesale but never to assemble one, so a flat {relation_id, kind, from_ref, to_ref} form has no derivable cell value.

relation_tombstone_payload.description: Payload for ak.relation.tombstone. relation_id is the sole target carrier for the irreversible active -> tombstoned transition; target_ref and update-style patch fields are forbidden. When supplied, reason is retained on the Event and is not copied into the materialized Relation object.

expected_state_digest.description: Optional optimistic concurrency guard. When present it MUST equal the writer-observed digest of the frozen pre-state this patch was computed against; a mismatch MUST fail closed. Registered as the apply_patch projection's expected_prestate source in contract-registry.json.

resource_discovery_state_payload.description: State payload for actor, applet, and handle discovery declarations. resource_id is the stable cell subject; value carries the schema-versioned discovery state.

rsvp_encrypted_response.description: Encrypted RSVP response envelope. The content_type is pinned so a receiver can route the ciphertext to exactly one decrypted schema; the plaintext MUST validate against rsvp_response.

rsvp_entry.description: Complete RSVP cell value. The whole entry is the mv_register set value, so every head independently carries the schedule the responder observed plus the response itself.

schedule_basis_refs.description: Non-empty schedule revision frontier the responder actually observed, as event_digest values sorted in ascending canonical UTF-8 byte order. MUST be a subset of the envelope causal_refs[], which caps it at the same 128 entries. A frontier larger than 128 MUST fail closed with schedule_frontier_too_large rather than being truncated.

response.description: Plaintext response branch. Only admissible when the target Strand effective scope encryption floor permits plaintext and the receiving service declares the rsvp_response plaintext data class.

encrypted_response.description: Encrypted response branch; content_type is pinned to application/vnd.arkret.calendar-rsvp-response+json and the decrypted plaintext MUST validate against rsvp_response. Required when the effective scope encryption floor is e2ee_required.

rsvp_response.description: RSVP response object. Used directly by rsvp_entry.response and as the decrypted plaintext of rsvp_entry.encrypted_response, whose content_type is application/vnd.arkret.calendar-rsvp-response+json. status and comment always share one encryption boundary; a plaintext status with an encrypted comment is not a valid shape.

comment.description: Optional responder comment. An empty response is expressed by omitting the field, never by an empty string.

event_ref.description: Calendar event Strand id; encoded as a ak:strand: typed id.

occurrence.description: JSON null for the whole series, or the canonical recurrence instance key: YYYY-MM-DD for all-day events and YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS[Zone] for timed events. The date component MUST be a real proleptic-Gregorian date, not merely match the digit pattern. The producer MUST canonicalize before signing; receivers MUST reject non-canonical keys instead of rewriting them.

schema_define_state_payload.description: Schema definition state payload. schema_id is the stable definition cell subject.

sidecar_context_attach_payload.description: Controller-signed versioned attachment of a source Realm context to an existing native Sidecar. It creates no Strand or Relation protocol object.

sidecar_create_payload.description: Minimal native Sidecar genesis intent. sidecar_id is derived from the Event id; realm_id, controller_id, state and timestamps are reducer-derived from the accepted envelope and MUST NOT appear here.

participant_authority_digest.description: Digest of the exact Sidecar identity, controller, and the Realm-scoped desired Agent roster derived from accepted ownership, lifecycle, and Realm membership facts.

control_frontier.description: Sorted accepted refs that materialize Sidecar genesis, ownership, lifecycle, authorization, Realm participation and key readiness. No Circle membership or Sidecar selection Event may appear.

sovereign_did_policy_state_payload.description: Sovereign DID policy state payload. trust_domain is the deployment-scoped replay-boundary subject.

space_create_payload.description: Create payload uses the full Space object schema for wire validation. Semantic validation MUST require payload.object.created_by to match the top-level actor_id and payload.object.created_at to match the top-level created_at before acceptance.

not.$comment: zh/models/common-fields.md: the object id is derived from this create Event's own event_id; carrying it in the payload is schema_violation reason object_id_not_event_derived.

space_object_tombstone_payload.description: Payload for ak.space.tombstone. Realm tombstone uses its separate Realm lifecycle payload; Space tombstone targets payload.space_id.

space_patch_payload.description: Payload class for ak.space.update. Patches Space metadata (title, rank, kind-specific fields) on the Space identified by space_id. Per operations-sync.md §7.3 / §9.3 and realm-and-space.md §3.3, ak.space.update only mutates the Space's own metadata; it MUST NOT PATCH top-level state (archive/restore go through ak.space.archive / ak.space.restore) and MUST NOT move Strands (ak.strand.move / ak.strand.reorder). Reducer rejects update on a non-active Space (reason=space_not_active) — see conformance-vectors.md §6.7.

space_state_transition_payload.description: Payload for ak.space.archive and ak.space.restore. The target Space is expressed on payload.space_id; top-level target_ref is a rejected field on Event envelopes.

state_conflict_recovery_payload.description: Control cell bottom recovery. zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 9.5 resolves a bottom=reject cell that has joined to Bottom back to a single legal value. The authorization and the pre-conflict anchor are not payload fields: they are refs[] entries with role=recovery_capability and role=state_witness.

target_cell.description: The cell being recovered. It MUST be in Bottom when the reducer applies this Event; on any other cell state the write MUST be rejected. This is the only registered kind whose write target is resolved from the payload rather than from a literal cell_family in the registry, because a recovery addresses one cell of an arbitrary family.

resolved_value.description: The single legal value the cell resolves to. Section 9.5 requires the Move to declare it, so it is signed payload, never reducer-synthesized.

realm_moderation_policy_state_payload.description: Closed payload for ak.realm.moderation_policy. The complete moderation-policy document is carried only in value; state and reason are not policy carriers.

strand_create_payload.description: Create payload uses the full Strand object schema for wire validation. Semantic validation MUST require payload.object.created_by to match the top-level actor_id and payload.object.created_at to match the top-level created_at before acceptance.

not.$comment: zh/models/common-fields.md: the object id is derived from this create Event's own event_id; carrying it in the payload is schema_violation reason object_id_not_event_derived.

board_space_id.description: Board Space that owns the position edge; deduplication key (board_space_id, strand_id) MUST be unique among active edges.

from_space_id.description: Source List Space (optional; reducer infers from current active edge if omitted).

target_space_id.description: Target List Space after move. This is the ONLY payload-level field for the destination; the reducer compiles it into the cas_register cell value as 'list_space_id' on the cell at ak:cell:ak.component.strand.position.v1:<board_space_id>:<strand_id>. Writers MUST NOT put 'list_space_id' directly on the ak.strand.move payload (additionalProperties=false enforces this) — there is exactly one destination input field on the wire.

strand_patch_payload.description: Payload class for ak.strand.update. Patches ordinary Strand fields on the Strand identified by target_ref.

space_id.description: List Space within which the reorder happens.

strand_stage_set_payload.description: Payload class for ak.strand.stage.set. Mutates Strand.stage / Strand.stage_changed_at. Intentionally carries no reason field — see the shared stage-set contract in zh/models/common-fields.md §5.3 and zh/models/strand-and-message.md §3.2.

not.$comment: Stage-set guard shared by the concrete Strand and Morph payload classes. Reason-style fields are forbidden; rationale belongs in a discussion-track Message.

strand_watch_set_payload.description: Payload for ak.strand.watch.set. Writes the (strand_id, watcher_actor_id) watch cell. The new cell value is computed from payload.level + payload.level_public: when level is null the effect is set null (clear, equivalent to mentions_only); when level is a string the effect is set { level, level_public? }. Reducer invariants: (1) watcher_actor_id MUST equal envelope.actor_id unless writer holds ak.strand.watch.set.others; (2) when watcher_actor_id != envelope.actor_id (.others write), level MUST be one of {mentions_only, participating, all} and level_public MUST be omitted or false — writing muted or level_public=true on behalf of another actor MUST failed_precondition; (3) .others writes MUST carry refs[role=audit_pair] to a same-batch ak.audit.accessed event whose payload access_kind=watch_set_others identifies writer / target / cell / before-after heads. See models/strand-and-message.md §8.4.

level.description: Watch level. Required. null clears the cell (equivalent to mentions_only / no record); in that case level_public MUST be omitted.

level_public.description: Opt-in publication of the level value to non-self projection consumers. Default false. muted MUST NOT be exposed even with level_public=true. MUST be omitted when level is null.

expected_value.description: Compiles to cas_register head_eq precondition. Whole-value compare against the cell pre-state: either null (assert no prior record) or { level, level_public? } matching the prior cell value exactly. When omitted, reducers MUST treat it as head_eq null: only the initial write may pass; an existing cell MUST fail_precondition. Omission MUST NOT disable CAS or imply last-write-wins.

allOf.description: level_public MUST be omitted when level is null (clearing a cell does not carry a public-level setting).

track_name.description: Strand track key for Message payloads. Mirrors message.schema.json#/properties/track_name: v1 Message payloads are restricted to 'discussion'.

verification_method.description: DID URL of a concrete verification method. Bare DIDs are not valid where a key binding is required.

expected_state_digest.description: Optional optimistic concurrency guard. When present it MUST equal the writer-observed digest of the frozen pre-state this patch was computed against; a mismatch MUST fail closed. Registered as the apply_patch projection's expected_prestate source in contract-registry.json.

view_reconcile_payload.description: Payload for ak.view.reconcile. view_id is the ak.component.view.reconcile.v1 cell subject; definition is the whole View definition object being synced (zh/models/views.md section 3.2). Reconcile is neither ak.view.create's object snapshot nor ak.view.update's patch: it replaces the definition wholesale, so it MUST NOT be dispatched to the shared view_payload, whose definition branch does not even require view_id.

relation_create_object.description: Relation create input. Same shape as object_snapshot minus the id: the relation id is derived from this create Event's event_id (zh/models/common-fields.md); `type` stays banned because the object kind comes from the typed-id prefix.

schemas/events-subscribe-frame.schema.js.title: EventsSubscribeFrame
schemas/events-subscribe-frame.schema.js.description: Closed frame union emitted by ak.self.events.stream.subscribe over NDJSON or as the payload of an Arkret WebSocket channel frame.

registry_id.description: Versioned registry symbol for a dependency, payload schema, or conformance vector.

retrieval_url.description: Optional retrieval hint only. The registry_id plus digest, not this URL, identifies the referenced content.

schemas/federated-device-signing-key-evi.title: Arkret Federated Device Signing Key Evidence
schemas/federated-device-signing-key-evi.description: Portable PCR-anchored device-key authorization evidence. A destination independently verifies registration-time DID evidence, the signed PCR genesis receipt, every accepted device authorization hop, and the Seal that covers the target authorization. Current DID resolution is neither required nor accepted as a substitute for historical evidence. Transport-only: this object never enters another Event digest, reducer, Seal, or timeline.

verification_method.description: The registered adapter MUST project the bare-DID portion of this DID URL to actor_id, and the fragment MUST equal device_id. It need not use the current full_id: historical proofs retain their original DID URL after a valid resolution update. The stable actor_id is a did_core_id and MUST NOT be used as a DID URL prefix.

device_signing_key.description: MUST equal the target authorization Event payload device_public_key.

authority_instance.description: MUST reverse-bind actor_id and the principal genesis receipt below. A business relation that supplied an expected authority instance compares all fields byte-for-byte before accepting the device key.

registration_did_evidence.description: Frozen evidence for the registration accepted-at position. A verifier MUST NOT replace it with a current DID Document, current webvh head or current controller key.

principal_genesis_receipt.description: A verified receipt whose scope.kind is pcr_genesis_unit and whose principal/device commitments match the first two authorization_chain Events.

authorization_chain.description: Complete ordered PCR control-state history needed to rederive the target device projection at accepted_seal, starting at root-signed genesis and including every relevant authorize, revoke, reanchor and device-list move. For accepted_device hops the Event proof signer MUST be payload.authorized_by (a current active device), while payload.device_signature proves possession by the new device. range_completeness_evidence proves that reducer inputs were not omitted.

accepted_seal.description: Accepted Seal whose recursively covered control Event set includes every authorization_chain Event digest and whose Realm id equals authority_instance.pcr_realm_id and the realm id committed in principal_genesis_receipt. Verifiers MUST NOT recompute a PCR realm id from the principal DID.

current_device_projection.description: Deterministic projection rederived from authorization_chain at accepted_seal. The outer source assertion is not authority; any mismatch with replayed history fails closed.

range_completeness_evidence.description: Signed ak.attestation.range_completeness Event envelopes whose verified scopes cover the PCR range from genesis through accepted_seal. The verifier checks roots, actor-seq ranges, witnesses required by Realm policy, and rejects gaps or witness disagreement.

registration_did_evidence_draft.description: Client-authored historical DID evidence before Account Authority acceptance. control_proof signs canonical_json({context:'ak.registration-did-evidence-control-proof-v1',principal_id,full_id,adapter_version,method_history_head,version_id,control_key_digest,method_evidence_digest,verification_method,created_at}); method_evidence_digest is sha256 over RFC 8785 JCS of method_evidence. accepted_at is deliberately absent: the Account Authority adds it only after the exact did_operation has been accepted by the registry.

registration_did_evidence.description: Account-Authority-accepted form of registration_did_evidence_draft. accepted_at is assigned after the registry accepts the exact did_operation, MUST be no earlier than control_proof.created_at, and is not retroactively inserted into the client signature. The pcr_genesis_unit receipt commits the canonical digest of this complete object.

control_proof.description: Registration control signature whose transcript digest is committed by the pcr_genesis_unit receipt.

schemas/file-transfer.schema.json.title: Arkret File Transfer Account Data
schemas/file-transfer.schema.json.description: Plaintext shape that MUST be encrypted before writing ak.profile.file_transfer.v1 account-data values.

content_digest.description: Digest of the stored blob bytes. For encrypted file transfer this is the ciphertext digest and MUST NOT be a plaintext file hash.

blob_size_bytes.description: Size of the stored blob bytes, usually ciphertext plus AEAD overhead.

media_type.description: Original file media type. This field lives inside encrypted account data; encrypted blob metadata SHOULD use application/octet-stream.

plaintext_size_bytes.description: Original file byte length before client-side encryption.

oneOf.$comment: whole-file AEAD form: single nonce, no stream segment parameters
streaming chunked AEAD form: nonce_prefix and fixed segment parameters, no whole-file nonce

content_key.description: Fresh per-transfer content key carried only inside encrypted account-data plaintext.

oneOf.$comment: whole-file file-transfer key message: single nonce, no stream segment parameters
streaming file-transfer key message: nonce_prefix and fixed segment parameters, no whole-file nonce

enc.description: HPKE KEM encapsulated key for the recipient device.

schemas/grant-constraint.schema.json.title: Arkret Grant Constraint
schemas/grant-constraint.schema.json.$comment: Property ordering is grouped by constraint family to match capabilities.md §6 (the human-readable family map): discriminator/meta, then temporal, field_access, kind_restriction, scope_limitation, authority_control, quota, claim_based, confidentiality, then the moderation cache-invalidation hint. Canonical JSON re-sorts keys lexicographically so this ordering is presentation-only and does not affect the wire (see C13-07).

constraint_id.description: Optional stable identifier of this constraint within the grant; used for diagnostics and overrides.

constraint_kind.description: Constraint family discriminator. v1 collapses what were 15 types into 8 by absorbing narrowly-scoped types into their conceptual parent: edit_window → temporal; container_move → scope_limitation; rate_limiting + resource_limit → quota; approval_workflow + accountability + device_session → claim_based (with constraint_subkind); encryption_requirement + visibility_control → confidentiality (with constraint_subkind). Use the optional 'constraint_subkind' field to indicate the original specialization where evaluation logic differs.

evaluation_class.description: Cacheability/dependency hint for the authorization evaluator. stateless = pure function of (constraint, op, now); grant_local = depends on the grant object only; realm_state = depends on Realm frontier (membership, policy_version, etc.); external = depends on data outside the Realm causal frontier (claim revocation status, rate-limit history counts, async approval). Each constraint_kind has a canonical evaluation_class declared in constraint-schema.md §2.3; implementations MAY tighten (e.g. grant_local → stateless) but MUST NOT loosen (e.g. external as stateless). Auth evaluators SHOULD use this hint to gate fast-path caching.

constraint_subkind.description: Optional discriminator within a constraint_kind. Standard values: claim_based.{claim,approval,accountability}; quota.{rate,resource}; confidentiality.{encryption,visibility}; temporal.{window,edit_window,redact_window,session}; authority_control.{applet_authority}. Per constraint-schema.md §2.2, device/session binding is NOT an independent constraint_subkind: it is the claim_based constraint_subkind=claim sub-case expressed via an accepted PCR device issuer. Implementations MAY require constraint_subkind for these families and fail closed on unknown values.

applies_to_actions.description: Optional restriction of a temporal constraint to specific capability actions (e.g. ['ak.message.revise.own', 'ak.message.redact.own']). Action mismatch is neutral in the effect fold: satisfied for effect=allow and not matched for deny/quarantine/require_review.

recurrence.description: Recurrence rule for temporal constraints. Used by constraint-schema.md §3.1.

expires_after.description: ISO 8601 duration; used by approval_workflow constraint instead of expires_after_ms.

condition.description: Conditional predicate for field_access and similar constraints. The `kind` value is a registered named condition from constraint-schema.md §4.1; unknown kinds MUST fail closed. Implementations MUST NOT introduce ad hoc string DSL predicates.

allowed_space_kinds.description: Allowed Space kinds (e.g. 'board', 'list', or profile-registered kinds like 'swimlane', 'calendar_bucket'). Reducer/profile MUST validate kind value.

allowed_circle_ids.description: Limits Circle-scoped capability actions to the listed Circle ids. Used by ak.circle.manage / ak.circle.member.manage style grants; unconstrained Realm-wide Circle management grants are not a normal permission shape.

allowed_session_ids.description: Limits applet interop-session operations to the listed applet-defined session correlation ids.

blob_presign_scope.description: Scope limiter for ak.self.blob.command.presign grants: allowed purposes plus optional blob/realm restrictions.

allowed_data_labels.description: Data classification labels this grant may read, export, transform, or send to external endpoints.

allowed_endpoints.description: Allowed outbound endpoint origins or deployment-approved endpoint patterns for applet / agent / connector operations.

max_authority_depth.description: Maximum remaining authority hops. Bounded by the canonical authority-chain depth ceiling (4) defined in zh/conformance/scalability-constraints.md §3 and zh/authz/capabilities.md §10.2; reducers MUST reject grants declaring a larger value at accept time rather than only truncating during DFS.

applet_id.description: authority_control(constraint_subkind=applet_authority) binding to the accepted Applet registration.

executed_by.description: authority_control(constraint_subkind=applet_authority) binding to the concrete Applet service, bot, or provisioned ghost actor did_core_id that may execute the grant. Its proof verification_method remains a full DID URL and MUST project to this value through the registered method adapter.

registration_epoch.description: authority_control(constraint_subkind=applet_authority) binding to the canonical Applet registration epoch.

blob_presign_max_ttl_seconds.description: Maximum TTL, in seconds, that this grant permits for ak.blob.presign. The service must clamp requested max_age_seconds to the smaller of this value and deployment policy.

max_artifact_bytes.description: Maximum artifact size in bytes for applet / agent / export operations.

max_operations.description: Maximum number of distinct accepted idempotency identities in one UTC epoch-aligned fixed period. Enforcement is a linearizable check-and-reserve at one logical quota authority shared by every node in the enforcing service; per-node duplicated budgets and overshoot are forbidden.

period.description: ISO 8601 duration. For quota constraints, a stricter conditional schema permits only a non-zero fixed-length week/day/hour/minute/second duration; year/month durations are forbidden so every authority derives the same UTC epoch-aligned window id.

burst.description: Optional token-bucket capacity at the same logical quota authority, capped by max_operations and refilled at max_operations/period. It never increases the fixed-window total budget.

constraint_scope.description: Closed v1 quota counting scope. Unknown values are schema violations and MUST fail closed. Quota counters are actor-bound; the enum selects the additional slicing dimension: actor only, actor+space, actor+realm, or actor across all nodes/regions of the enforcing service's global quota domain. global is not an implicit federation-wide counter. Every node in the service domain MUST share one logical linearizable quota authority.

required_claims.description: Conditional claim requirements. resource-selector-grammar.md §3.3 caps this array at 32 entries as a normative DoS guard; the schema enforces maxItems:32 so condition-selector grants cannot smuggle in unbounded claim objects.

subject_matches_actor.description: If true, the credential subject did_core_id MUST match the actor did_core_id after each proof's full DID is independently validated and projected through its registered method adapter.

value_constraints.description: Per-field equality / membership constraints on credential claims.

min_encryption_level.description: confidentiality(constraint_subkind=encryption) static floor: the minimum content-encryption mechanism the grant requires. Values mirror Realm/Circle encryption_profile. Pure static declaration evaluated as stateless unless cross-checked against the Realm's current encryption_profile (see constraint-schema.md §12).

plaintext_fallback_allowed.description: confidentiality(constraint_subkind=encryption) static flag: whether the grant permits plaintext when the encryption floor cannot be met. See constraint-schema.md §12.

audit_trail_required.description: confidentiality(constraint_subkind=encryption) static flag: whether the grant requires an audit trail (e.g. active Audit Applet Binding). See constraint-schema.md §12.

depends_on_moderation_state.description: Cache-invalidation hint: when true, this grant's authorization decisions depend on the ak.component.moderation_state.v1 cell (see policy-server.md §7.1 and capabilities.md §18.1) and the grant's cache entry MUST be invalidated when that cell changes. Default false: ordinary grants (ak.strand.update / ak.message.create / org membership grants) do NOT take a cache hit on every moderation decision. v1 capabilities.md §18.1 lists three conditions where MUST be explicitly true (moderator-role grants, condition-selector subjects referencing moderation state, constraints referencing moderation queue / cell). Schema-side enforcement of condition (2) is in capability-grant.schema.json via if/then on actions[]; conditions (1) and (3) are reducer-side lint. Cache invalidation hint outside the eight constraint families; it does not participate in allow/deny evaluation and is documented in capabilities.md §6 / constraint-schema.md.

allOf.$comment: constraint-schema.md §2.2 / §2.3: claim_based, confidentiality and quota families have NO valid no-constraint_subkind form — every row in the §2.3 evaluation_class table carries a constraint_subkind (claim/approval/accountability; encryption/visibility; rate/resource). Without this gate a {"constraint_kind":"claim_based","effect":"allow"} with no constraint_subkind passes schema validation, letting weak implementations cache an external (claim-revocation) constraint on the grant_local fast path (see C05-03 fail-open). temporal is intentionally excluded: a temporal constraint with no constraint_subkind is the valid ordinary time-window form.
Rate quotas need an explicit counting scope; otherwise SDKs cannot derive a stable counter key.
Applet delegated grants must carry the complete grant-local registration binding. effective_scope is represented by the enclosing capability grant resources[] selector and is not duplicated here.
Applet binding fields are reserved for the registered authority_control.applet_authority shape; partial or cross-family use is invalid.
quota constraint_subkind=rate is a complete hard-quota tuple; partial rate constraints are invalid.
burst is a modifier of a complete rate quota and cannot stand alone.
Cumulative resource quotas need an explicit counting scope; single-operation fields such as blob_max_bytes do not.
Cumulative resource-count quotas need an explicit counting scope.
Quota periods must have a fixed duration so all nodes derive the same UTC epoch-aligned window. Calendar years/months and zero/empty durations are not valid quota periods.
An edit window is only interoperable when its canonical action gate is explicit.
temporal constraint_subkind=edit_window requires the edit duration field.
A redact window is only interoperable when its canonical action gate is explicit.
temporal constraint_subkind=redact_window requires the redact duration field.
redact_after_window_allowed modifies message_edit_window and is invalid without it.

schema.description: Canonical schema discriminator. Aligned with schema-registry.json; lets validators / contract-registry consumers disambiguate this claim from other DID-bearing envelopes.

handle_aliases.description: Interop aliases such as RFC 7565 acct:. Aliases are never canonical; verifiers MUST normalize to handle before cache lookup, proof comparison, or delivery_binding construction.

subject.description: Stable holder/principal did_core_id for a user/principal handle; it is not a server-local account_id, administrative identifier, service identity, or generic resource id.

issuer.description: Stable did_core_id of the handle authority. Bare hostnames are discovery inputs, never proof issuers; proof verification resolves a full DID URL separately and requires its registered adapter projection to equal this issuer.

issuer_service_id.description: Stable service did_core_id that signed, served, or vouched for this handle claim when distinct from issuer.

claim_kind.description: Protocol-level kind of holder/principal handle claim. v1 intentionally does not allow the earlier draft service_handle value: service-readable names or resource labels need their own service/resource schema, while organization-assigned user/principal handles use organization_handle.

visibility.description: Default disclosure boundary for this handle claim.

audience.description: Audience binding for the claim. For handle claims used to build a Realm delivery_binding, audience is the target Realm ID, the inviting service DID, or another verifier domain the proofs explicitly bind to. Verifier MUST reject claims whose audience does not match the current invocation context.

claim_scope.description: Optional claim_scope such as organization_id, realm_id, purpose, or allowed operations.

member_delivery_binding.description: Single source for the Principal Server service DID and delivery parameters this handle claim offers to the membership builder. Top-level delivery shortcuts are forbidden; use member_delivery_binding.recipient_service_id, member_delivery_binding.service_acceptance_ref, and member_delivery_binding.policy_event_ref.

service_resolution.description: Signed first-hop resolution material for recipient_service_id.

schemas/high-risk-authority-proof.schema.title: Arkret High-Risk Authority Proof Family
schemas/high-risk-authority-proof.schema.description: Shared authority proof family for service operations that key-management.md designates as high-risk material destruction or equivalent (first consumer: active-series key backup tail deletion, key-management.md section 7.8). Exactly one closed branch: principal_signing, device_quorum, or trusted_recovery_service, discriminated by `kind`. Every branch reuses the common detached-JWS leaf (event-envelope.schema.json#/$defs/proof) over the operation's single canonical delete-intent transcript; branches never restate the leaf fields. An ordinary current-device session proof is deliberately NOT a branch of this family — operations that accept it for low-risk paths must say so in their own normative text.

detached_proof.description: Common detached-JWS leaf. `payload_digest` MUST be the digest of the operation's canonical transcript (for key backup deletion: the delete-intent transcript of key-management.md section 7.8.1); `created_at` MUST fall inside the server-issued challenge window when the operation binds one.

principal_signing_proof.description: Principal-control-key proof. The proof's verification_method MUST be a principal-grade DID-control verification method whose controller DID is byte-identical to the transcript's principal_id, and that key MUST be a currently accepted principal control key at proof.created_at. Device keys, service keys and retired keys MUST be rejected.

proof.description: Detached-JWS leaf whose verification_method MUST resolve, at proof.created_at, to an authorized non-revoked device key of exactly this device_id under the transcript's principal_id. Every quorum member signs the same canonical transcript bytes.

device_quorum_proof.description: Device-quorum proof. The schema enforces only the minimum wire shape (threshold>=2, signatures.minItems=1). Verification is normative in the consuming operation's text: (a) every signature MUST verify over the same canonical transcript; (b) signatures MUST be deduplicated by device_id; (c) the count of valid deduplicated signatures MUST be >= threshold; (d) threshold MUST equal the currently accepted recovery policy device-quorum k — a smaller issuer-supplied threshold MUST be rejected as failed_precondition. A deployment whose policy k is below 2 cannot use this branch and must use principal_signing or trusted_recovery_service instead; a single current device proof is not a high-risk quorum.

threshold.description: The quorum threshold the issuer claims to satisfy. MUST equal the principal's currently accepted recovery_policy device-quorum k; receivers MUST cross-check per description rule (d).

signatures.description: minItems=1 is the schema floor only; receiver-side verification requires deduplicated valid signature count >= threshold per description rule (c).

trusted_recovery_service_proof.description: Trusted recovery service proof. The verification_method of `proof` MUST be controlled by service_id, and service_id MUST be authorized as a trusted recovery service by the recovery policy / DID delegation snapshotted into the referenced recovery session. The session MUST be unexpired, unconsumed for this purpose, and MUST have been established by principal_signing, recovery unlock or device_quorum — the service alone is never a sufficient factor.

recovery_session_id.description: Verified, unexpired, unconsumed recovery session authenticated by principal_signing, recovery unlock or device_quorum. A service-only session is not a second factor.

attestation_ref.description: Optional attestation object for service_id. If present, receivers MUST resolve it in the same trust_domain as the operation and reject cross-domain attestations.

schemas/ice-config-response.schema.json.title: Arkret Media ICE Config Result
schemas/ice-config-response.schema.json.description: Result shape for the WebRTC media service ICE config endpoint. Used by ak.profile.webrtc_media.v1; see crypto-media/webrtc-signaling.md §4.

realm_id.description: Echo of the request Realm id. Bound into the signature to prevent cross-Realm replay.

call_id.description: Echo of the request call id. Bound into the signature to prevent cross-call replay.

actor_id.description: Stable actor did_core_id that may use this ICE configuration. Bound into the signature.

device_id.description: Device that may use this ICE configuration. Bound into the signature.

ice_servers.description: STUN / TURN server entries the client may use during this call.

ttl_seconds.description: Validity window for the issued credentials in seconds. Clients MUST refresh before this expires; servers SHOULD pick a value <= 1 hour for normal calls.

refresh_lead_seconds.description: Minimum lead time before ttl expiry at which the client SHOULD initiate refresh. refresh_lead_seconds MUST be strictly less than ttl_seconds (servers MUST NOT issue refresh_lead_seconds >= ttl_seconds, otherwise the client would judge the credential stale at issuance and storm refresh). Defaults SHOULD be ttl_seconds / 4. The recommended floor (60s) applies only when ttl_seconds is large enough that floor < ttl_seconds still holds; for small ttl (e.g. the 60s minimum) the server MUST shrink refresh_lead_seconds below ttl_seconds (see webrtc-signaling.md §4.2). Required so all clients refresh at consistent cadence and servers can plan secret rotation grace windows.

issued_at.description: Server-issued timestamp (RFC 3339 UTC). Bound into the ICE config signature.

issued_at_bucket.description: Coarse UTC bucket start used for TURN pseudonym derivation. MUST equal floor(issued_at / bucket_seconds) * bucket_seconds. Bound into the signature so TURN usernames cannot be correlated across buckets by rewriting metadata.

bucket_seconds.description: TURN pseudonym bucket size in seconds. v1 fixes the default and interoperable value at 300s; clients SHOULD refresh before crossing the next bucket.

expires_at.description: Convenience field equal to issued_at + ttl_seconds. MUST match within signature validation.

turn_required.description: When true, clients MUST disable host/srflx ICE candidates and only relay through TURN. Used by high-privacy Realms to prevent IP leakage.

next_retry_at.description: Set when the response is a soft failure (e.g. turn_credential_expired). Clients MUST NOT retry before this time.

signature.description: Detached signature by the media service DID over the canonical bytes of this response (excluding `signature`).

urls.description: STUN/TURN server URL(s). Schemes: stun:, stuns:, turn:, turns:.

username.description: TURN ephemeral credential username. v1: <expiry-unix>:<per-call-pseudonym>. MUST NOT contain principal DID, handle, email, or any cross-call stable identifier.

credential.description: TURN ephemeral credential password (HMAC-SHA256 of username with per-tenant turn shared secret in REST-style).

kid.description: DID URL of the concrete media-service verification method. Bare DID is not accepted because the response must pin one already accepted service key binding.

signature_algorithm.description: Signature algorithm. Values MUST be active alg entries supporting detached_jws in signature-alg-registry.json. Default v1 deployments use Ed25519; stronger or deployment-specific profiles MAY require another registered algorithm while preserving the exact signing input defined in webrtc-signaling.md §4.1.

signature_input.description: Domain-separation label prepended to the ICE config signing bytes. v1 fixes this to ak.media.ice_config.v1 and it MUST NOT be reused for participant binding signatures.

payload_digest.description: SHA-256 digest of the RFC 8785 canonical ICE config response object with the top-level signature field removed. This is the canonical payload covered after the signature_input label and 0x00 separator.

sig.description: base64url-encoded detached signature over canonical response bytes.

schemas/identity-link.schema.json.title: Arkret Minimal-Metadata Identity Link
schemas/identity-link.schema.json.description: Encrypted application-message or MLS private-extension payload that binds a Realm-scoped pairwise actor did_core_id to the real principal did_core_id for ak.profile.mls.minimal_metadata_realm.v1. The binding is scoped to both realm_id and trust_domain so the same pairwise mapping cannot be replayed across deployments. This object is never written to public Realm history unless a separate disclosure policy explicitly permits it.

pairwise_actor_id.description: Realm-scoped pairwise actor did_core_id used byte-for-byte in Event.actor_id and the MLS BasicCredential identity. Its Event proof verificationMethod controller is a did:key full_id whose registered adapter projection MUST equal this value.

principal_id.description: Real principal DID that controls or has disclosed the pairwise DID.

trust_domain.description: Deployment-scope trust domain. Receiver MUST require this value to match the current Realm / service trust_domain before accepting a pairwise DID -> principal DID mapping.

strand_id.description: Optional application-message context marker for the Strand carrying the identity link. It does not create independent membership or key scope; key scope is determined by effective_scope.

track_name.description: Optional display-track context marker for application routing. Track names do not create independent membership, policy, or MLS key scope.

mls_group_id.description: Optional MLS group identifier (base64url RFC 9420 GroupID) for diagnostic / cross-implementation correlation. NOT used by the reducer for authorization — authoritative MLS group state lives in ak.mls.genesis / ak.mls.commit events. Provided here so audit projections can quickly correlate an identity-link with its MLS group without replaying the full epoch chain.

verification_method.description: DID URL of a key controlled by principal_id or by a disclosure proof accepted by Realm policy. Fragment is REQUIRED (this is a DID URL, not a bare DID). DID method-name normalized to lowercase per W3C DID 1.0.

payload_digest.description: Hash of canonical input bytes: utf8('ak.identity-link-v1\n') || canonical_json(identity-link object with proof.signature omitted). The signed object includes trust_domain.

schema.description: Canonical schema discriminator. Aligned with schema-registry.json; lets validators distinguish identity registry receipts from other receipt envelopes (e.g. audit-ryw-receipt, event-batch-receipt).

did.description: Method-native bare full DID whose registry log position is attested by this receipt. This field intentionally remains a full DID because seq and head_event_digest identify that DID method history; it is not a stable Arkret business identity field.

registry_service_id.description: Stable did_core_id of the registry service issuing the receipt. The detached proof verification_method remains a full DID URL and MUST project to this value through the registered method adapter.

witness_role.description: Issuer's role in the DID registry consensus group. Required so verifiers can apply role-specific freshness / quorum rules; an absent role would force the verifier to guess writer vs replica semantics.

audience.description: Optional audience binding (verifier DID, service DID, or domain). When present, verifiers MUST reject the receipt outside that audience context to prevent cross-protocol reuse.

signature.description: Registry detached proof. payload_digest = sha256(canonical_json(receipt with signature omitted)). The detached JWS signs canonical_json({context:'ak.identity-receipt-proof-v1', payload_digest, registry_service_id, did, verification_method, created_at, domain?, audience?}); context is a fixed signing-context domain tag and is not a wire field. signature.created_at MUST equal receipt.created_at. signature.verification_method MUST be a currently valid full DID URL assertion method whose bare full_id is independently validated and projected to registry_service_id by the registered method adapter. Receipt audience and proof audience MUST either both be absent or be the same single string; array-valued proof audiences are invalid for this object family.

schemas/identity-resolution.schema.json.title: Arkret Identity Resolution
schemas/identity-resolution.schema.json.description: Canonical did_core_id/full_id resolution state, owner-published evidence and service-route bootstrap contracts. A full_id is a standard bare DID and a did_core_id is the stable Arkret business identity projected by a registered DID method adapter.

method_evidence_boundary.description: Inclusive adapter-defined history interval covered by this evidence. For a method without native history the from and to values are identical synthetic values for the one verified state.

webvh_method_history_evidence.description: Bounded did:webvh log, proof and witness material routed to adapter did:webvh:1.0. Canonical encoded evidence MUST NOT exceed 1 MiB; a larger history is split into separately verified bounded responses.

evidence.description: Closed canonical evidence receipt for exactly the inclusive boundary. method MUST be webvh and method_proofs MUST carry the matching webvh_log row; the public evidence evaluator checks its history_head against boundary.to_method_history_head.

did_web_method_history_evidence.description: Bounded current DID Document retrieval evidence routed to adapter did:web:1. The boundary endpoints MUST be identical synthetic values. Canonical encoded evidence MUST NOT exceed 1 MiB.

evidence.description: Closed canonical document-bound evidence receipt. method MUST be web and method_proofs MUST be empty; document_digest and boundary synthetic head are cross-checked by the public evidence evaluator.

did_key_method_history_evidence.description: Bounded deterministic local expansion evidence routed to adapter did:key:1. The boundary endpoints MUST be identical synthetic values. Canonical encoded evidence MUST NOT exceed 1 MiB.

evidence.description: Closed canonical local-expansion evidence receipt. method MUST be key and method_proofs MUST be empty; the public evidence evaluator recomputes document_digest and the synthetic boundary directly from full_id.

method_history_evidence.description: Adapter-routed evidence. adapter_version and evidence_kind are a closed discriminator pair; unknown adapters or mismatched pairs fail closed.

resolution_commitment.description: Owner-committed current full_id and method-native history position. For a deterministic method, method_history_head and version_id use the adapter-defined deterministic canonical values; they are never omitted.

principal_resolution_update_payload.description: Payload for ak.identity.resolution.update in the actor's Principal Control Realm. Admission projects full_id to the envelope actor_id and performs a strict CAS against both predecessor fields before accepting a method-valid successor.

principal_genesis_event.description: The accepted identity-control Realm genesis Event. It is resolution history head 0 and commits the initial resolution; its derived Realm id, actor, purpose and initial projection are cross-bound by the principal resolution evidence evaluator.

resolution_update_event.description: One accepted post-genesis resolution successor Event. Its exact resolution-cell head_eq precondition and predecessor fields are mandatory under Event dispatch.

resolution_cell_proof.description: Merkle inclusion proof that the singleton PCR resolution cell has the stated current value under accepted_seal. The cell_ref is always ak:cell:ak.component.identity.resolution.v1:null.

principal_resolution_evidence.description: Portable resolution-only evidence bound to one exact PrincipalAuthorityInstance, its complete signed PCR genesis receipt and its current singleton resolution cell. It intentionally excludes unrelated PCR device, recovery and session history. The verifier recomputes the authority instance digest, verifies the receipt and its reverse bindings, derives the PCR Realm, validates purpose/actor/kind and every supplied contiguous resolution-history segment, validates accepted Seal coverage and cell inclusion, then independently resolves method evidence for the current full_id. Omitted older history never becomes an absence claim.

authority_instance.description: Exact PCR authority selected by the required authority_instance_digest query. Its principal_id and pcr_realm_id MUST equal the response fields; principal_server_id MUST equal principal_genesis_receipt.issuer; and principal_genesis_receipt_digest MUST equal the canonical SHA-256 digest of the complete principal_genesis_receipt.

principal_control_realm_id.description: Realm id derived from principal_genesis_event under the registered PCR derivation rule; it is not a producer-selected alternate scope.

principal_genesis_receipt.description: Complete signed pcr_genesis_unit receipt. Its issuer and scope MUST reverse-bind authority_instance, principal_id, principal_control_realm_id and principal_genesis_event; consumers MUST verify its proof rather than trusting the producer's index.

predecessor_resolution_events.description: Selected post-genesis resolution update Events preceding current_resolution_event, ordered from the current event's immediate predecessor toward older events and contiguous for the supplied range. The genesis Event is carried separately and MUST NOT be repeated here. If the selected range does not reach head 0, the oldest supplied Event's guarded predecessor projection is the next audit cursor; omitted history is unknown rather than absent.

service_resolution_record_core.description: Signed first-hop service route material. It lets a consumer map a stable service did_core_id to a candidate full_id; it is not an endpoint authorization by itself.

service_kind.description: Registered ServiceDescribe role selected at this route. The describe request MUST use this value when the base URL hosts multiple roles.

resolution_event_ref.description: Adapter-canonical service control-state reference. It MUST equal the active adapter row's service_resolution_event_ref_rule for this full_id and method_history_head: did:webvh maps to did-webvh-entry-sha256, did:web maps to did-web-document-sha256, and did:key maps to did-key-full-id-sha256.

record_sequence.description: Exact signed-record sequence within one service did_core_id. The first record is 0; every accepted same-core successor is exactly the immediately previous record_sequence plus one. Gaps, reuse and rollback fail closed.

previous_record_digest.description: sha256 over RFC 8785 JCS of the immediately previous complete signed ServiceResolutionRecord, including proof, or null exactly when record_sequence is 0.

current_record_url.description: No-redirect HTTPS current-record URL. It MUST equal canonical base_url plus _arkret/open/services/{RFC3986-percent-encoded service_id}/resolution. A fetched successor's independently verified signed value becomes the next refresh URL; an old record or redirect cannot retarget it. Fetchers apply SSRF, DNS-rebinding, response-size and timeout controls and trust only verified record bytes.

base_url.description: Canonical first-hop HTTPS base: lowercase scheme and host, normalized path, no query or fragment, exactly one trailing slash. The consumer resolves _arkret/describe relative to this value without following cross-origin redirects and cross-checks the returned binding.

describe_digest.description: sha256 over RFC 8785 JCS of {service_id, service_kind, service_resolution, http_json_base_url} projected from ServiceDescribe. Dynamic capabilities, limits, rate policy and x_* fields are intentionally excluded.

issued_at.description: MUST be <= refresh_after and strictly earlier than expires_at.

refresh_after.description: MUST satisfy issued_at <= refresh_after < expires_at. At or after this time a cache refreshes current_record_url before a security-sensitive use.

expires_at.description: MUST be later than refresh_after. An expired record is never routable; current_record_url may provide a verified successor with the same service_id.

service_resolution_record.description: Portable signed ServiceResolutionRecord. Its record digest is sha256:<lowercase-hex SHA-256 of RFC 8785 JCS of this complete object including proof>. Separately, payload_digest is sha256 over RFC 8785 JCS of record. The detached proof signs canonical_json({context:'ak.service-resolution-record-proof-v1', payload_digest, service_id, service_kind, full_id, method_history_head, version_id, resolution_event_ref, record_sequence, previous_record_digest, current_record_url, base_url, describe_digest, issued_at, refresh_after, expires_at, verification_method, created_at, domain?, audience?}) under a service control key accepted at method_history_head; proof.created_at MUST equal record.issued_at. The verifier also enforces project(full_id)=service_id, the adapter-canonical history/version/event-ref mapping, record_sequence=0 iff previous_record_digest=null, exact plus-one same-core succession, and the timestamp ordering declared by the record fields.

service_route_handover_notice_core.description: Portable future-route sidecar bound to one current ServiceResolutionRecord. It never changes the current route, never consumes record_sequence and never authorizes Realm, device, KeyPackage, repair or other business payload bytes. The evaluator enforces issued_at <= not_before <= cutover_at < grace_until <= expires_at for scheduled notices; candidate_record_url is the mechanical no-redirect service-resolution path below canonical candidate_base_url. A receiver accepts the candidate only after it returns the exact same service_id/service_kind, record_sequence=from_record_sequence+1 and previous_record_digest=from_record_digest in a formally verified ServiceResolutionRecord followed by describe reverse binding.

handover_id.description: Service-local UUIDv7 identity. It is stable across every scheduled update and cancellation in one notice chain.

notice_revision.description: The first notice is revision 0. Every accepted update or cancellation is exactly predecessor revision plus one.

from_record_digest.description: Exact complete signed-record digest at the notice basis. It MUST equal the receiver's durable last-seen/current digest for from_record_sequence; a stale or unrelated basis is never accepted silently.

not_before.description: Before this instant only bounded public record/describe preflight is allowed and it cannot update route state or carry business bytes. Clock skew may delay local use but cannot advance it.

previous_notice_digest.description: Null exactly for notice_revision 0; otherwise the digest of the immediately previous complete signed notice.

service_route_handover_proof_transcript.description: RFC 8785 canonical detached-signature transcript. payload_digest is over the complete notice core. Optional candidate/time members are present exactly for state=scheduled. The evaluator also requires proof.created_at=issued_at and resolves verification_method through the notice service's current method history; a mirror key is never valid here.

service_route_handover_notice.description: Complete target-service-signed handover artifact. Its notice digest is SHA-256 over RFC 8785 JCS of this complete object including proof. Publishing or mirroring it does not make candidate_base_url current and cannot replace a formally verified successor ServiceResolutionRecord.

service_resolution_mirror_artifact.description: Closed exact-one carrier for target-signed route material. A peer or mirror transports the selected artifact byte-for-byte and cannot replace it with a self-signed URL assertion.

service_resolution_artifact_key.description: Canonical durable-ledger key for one mirrored artifact family.

service_resolution_publish_request.description: Publishes exactly one target-signed record or notice into a Realm-scoped peer mirror. The authenticated Source-Service-ID, not an untrusted body field, supplies source_service_id. artifact_digest is over the exact complete selected artifact. The receiver validates current federation-peer authority, target visibility/delegation, target proof, basis, chain, freshness and bounds before any durable write.

service_resolution_publish_ack_core.description: Receiver-authored durable exact-digest acknowledgement. Transport idempotency is keyed by (source_service_id, realm_id, request_id) and binds request_digest: an exact retry returns the original ack and a different request digest is duplicate_conflict. Artifact integrity is independently keyed by (source_service_id, realm_id, artifact_key): the same artifact key with another artifact_digest is duplicate_conflict with zero overwrite, while a new request_id for identical artifact bytes may receive a new ack cross-bound to that request.

request_digest.description: SHA-256 over RFC 8785 JCS of the complete service_resolution_publish_request.

service_resolution_resolve_request.description: Realm-scoped anti-enumeration query for target-signed successor material. requester authority comes from the authenticated peer service and current Realm relationship. target_service_id must already be visible to requester through an effective member delivery binding, sync_endpoints or explicit service delegation. Unknown, unauthorized, invisible and not-held outcomes are externally indistinguishable.

service_resolution_resolve_outcome.description: Bounded continuous target-signed successor supply. successor_records begins exactly at known_record_sequence+1 with predecessor known_record_digest and remains plus-one/digest-contiguous. handover_notice, when present, is the single active non-expired target notice on the returned/current basis. has_more never permits accepting a gap. The canonical response is at most 256 KiB. The requester independently verifies every target proof, method history, time, chain and describe binding; same sequence with different valid target-signed digests is a route fork and enters quarantine, never a majority or reachability choice.

has_more.description: True only when more continuous target-signed records are held beyond the bounded response. The caller continues from the last verified record; it never skips the omitted segment.

service_resolution_last_seen_floor.description: Durable remote ServiceResolutionRecord anti-rollback floor, distinct from route cache and service_route_notice_state. It survives process restart and cache eviction. The record floor advances only after target proof, exact successor chain, method history, freshness and describe reverse binding all pass. Same record sequence with a different valid target-signed digest is a fork quarantine, not last-writer-wins.

service_route_notice_state.description: Durable accepted handover-notice state, independent from the ServiceResolutionRecord floor and TTL route cache. It survives restart and is retained until cancellation, formal successor completion or signed expiry. A scheduled entry is usable only while state=scheduled and now<expires_at, and only against the exact from_record floor. A cancelled entry remains durable evidence that the candidate must not be used. Same revision with another digest is a fork quarantine.

service_route_cache_entry.description: Replaceable TTL performance cache derived from one already verified durable floor. It is not authority and MAY disappear on restart. Cache freshness never permits accepting a sequence below service_resolution_last_seen_floor, extending signed expires_at, bypassing describe, or turning a notice candidate into a current route.

version_id.description: Native DID-method version coordinate copied from the exact verified signed ServiceResolutionRecord; cache replacement cannot infer or refresh it independently.

refresh_after.description: Signed record refresh trigger; it does not extend expires_at or authorize a future candidate.

expires_at.description: Signed ServiceResolutionRecord hard expiry. The cache is never routable at or after this instant.

cache_expires_at.description: Local TTL no later than the signed record expires_at. Implementations enforce cache_expires_at <= expires_at and refresh_after < expires_at.

route_mirror_hint.description: Transport-only hint for one route-mirror service. mirror_service_id is only a stable lookup identity and MUST be paired with independently verifiable service_resolution first-hop material; neither the did_core_id nor the carrier authorizes target-service routing or Realm access.

mirror_service_id.description: Stable did_core_id of the candidate route-mirror service. A bare did_core_id is never a route or authority.

service_resolution.description: Verifiable first-hop carrier for the mirror itself: either an inline signed current record or its current_record_url locator. A naked URL is forbidden. The target service route still requires Realm-scoped resolve authorization and target-signed material.

route_assistance.description: Optional short-TTL, transport-only route recovery hints for invite locator, invite delivery, or Contact bootstrap. At least one member is required. Effective usability is bounded by the earliest containing locator/invite/contact bootstrap expiry and each fetched record or signed notice expiry. This object MUST NOT enter Event canonical bytes, a Realm member cell, capability or authorization state. Its notice and mirror carriers never extend an outer token/receipt TTL and never authorize delivery, route switching or Realm access.

handover_notice.description: At most one complete target-signed active handover notice. It is only a candidate-discovery hint; the receiver still requires a basis-matching formal successor ServiceResolutionRecord and describe verification.

mirror_hints.description: At most four independently routable mirror hints. Each item carries the mirror did_core_id together with a service_resolution_carrier; bare URLs and bare core ids are not valid items.

current_record_url.description: Directly dereferenceable stable HTTPS URL for the current signed record. Redirects are not followed unless the redirected origin is independently authorized. Fetchers enforce SSRF, DNS-rebinding, size and timeout policy.

pinned_record_digest.description: Optional sha256 over RFC 8785 JCS of the complete signed record expected for the version that produced this carrier. It pins that version only; a later refresh may return a different digest after the fetched same-core successor independently verifies.

schemas/inclusion-list.schema.json.title: Arkret InclusionList
schemas/inclusion-list.schema.json.description: FOCIL-style control-plane inclusion list. A non-proposer notary signer lists pending Control Move digests that passed its local verification; the next Seal MUST include, signed-reject, or prove batch pre-state verification failure for every listed digest, otherwise receivers MUST reject that Seal (authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.3). single_did notary profiles cannot provide this mechanism. The list is an accountability object, not a Seal: it never advances governance state by itself.

signer_id.description: Notary signer issuing the list. MUST be an eligible non-proposer signer of the Realm's multi-signer notary profile at issue time.

list_seq.description: Per-signer monotonic inclusion-list sequence. Two different canonical lists from the same signer with the same (realm_id, list_seq) constitute equivocation evidence under the section 7.1 slot rule.

event_digests.description: Canonical ascending list of pending Control Move event digests that passed the issuer's local verification and hold a valid receipt.

expiry_seal_count.description: Number of subsequent Seals within which the obligation must be discharged. Default deployment value is 1 (the next Seal).

payload_digest.description: Hash of canonical InclusionList bytes with signature omitted.

schemas/invite-delivery-request.schema.j.title: Arkret Invite Delivery Request
schemas/invite-delivery-request.schema.j.description: Private service-to-service request used by an inviter-side Principal Server to deliver a Realm invite to the invitee-side Principal Server. The request carries an explicit invite address and introduction evidence; raw locator tokens are never written into durable Realm events.

invite_event.description: The ak.invite.create EventEnvelope or equivalent accepted event view being delivered.

subject_id.description: Stable principal did_core_id of the invite recipient.

recipient_service_id.description: Stable Principal Server service did_core_id that accepts invite delivery for subject_id.

route_assistance.description: Optional transport-only hints for recovering the same recipient_service_id route. This field is outside invite_event canonical bytes and MUST NOT be copied into invite_delivery_target or any Realm member cell; it does not extend invite/locator TTL or authorize delivery.

recipient_service_kind.description: v1 only allows Principal Server invite delivery. Omit by default; if present, the value MUST be principal_server.
v1 only allows Principal Server invite delivery. Omit by default; if present, the value MUST be principal_server.

consent_grant_ref.description: Event ref of the invitee-issued ak.consent.grant (scope invite or any) that authorizes the inviter to send Realm/Strand invites. High-trust evidence: it is material the invitee actively issued to the inviter, equivalent in trust to a locator_ref.

consent_id.description: Optional consent cell id locating the holder consent cell, to speed up receiver verification of the active grant dot.

handle.description: Canonical handle string the inviter used as the human-readable entry point.

handle_claim.description: Verified handle claim proving that handle resolves to invite_address.subject_id. The receiver MUST verify binding_state, proofs, expiry, issuer trust, visibility/audience policy, and that handle_claim.handle equals handle.

member_delivery_binding_candidate.description: Optional builder evidence returned by a Directory or trusted issuer for intent=invite. When present, verifiers MUST check subject_id, handle, recipient_service_id, audience, issuer_service_id, expiry and proofs against this delivery.

resolved_by.description: Optional stable Directory or issuer service did_core_id that supplied the handle resolution.

status.description: Generic receive status. It MUST NOT reveal whether subject_id exists or whether policy quarantined/dropped the invite. A holder-quarantine outcome MUST be reported as deferred with no disclosed_outcome. Only a receiver policy disclosure level of outcome may add disclosed_outcome, and only with delivered|blocked.

disclosed_outcome.description: Optional graded-disclosure result, closed to delivered|blocked. Present ONLY when the subject's receive policy disclosure level for this introduction trust tier is 'outcome' and the subject did not block the issuer; omitted (opaque) otherwise. delivered: the invite reached the holder surface awaiting acceptance; blocked: rejected by block list or policy. A holder-quarantine outcome MUST NOT be disclosed: it reveals holder-private consent state (identity/consent-model.md 6.1.1) and MUST be reported as status='deferred' with no disclosed_outcome, in the same response and timing equivalence class as rate-limit silent drop, timeout drop, holder-not-found and holder policy deny.

schemas/invite-receive-policy.schema.jso.title: Arkret Invite and Contact Receive Policy
schemas/invite-receive-policy.schema.jso.description: Subject-private policy used by a Principal Server to decide which invite delivery or first-contact request introduction evidence may notify the holder. This policy is not written into the target Realm durable event log or the public contact fact log.

subject_id.description: Stable principal did_core_id whose private invite receive policy this object configures. A long-lived principal MUST originate from did:webvh; only ak.profile.ephemeral_pairwise_principal.v1 admits a did:key principal. did:web is never a principal method.

holder_allowed_introduction_kinds.description: Allowlist of introduction evidence kinds that may reach holder notification or review.

explicit_address_behavior.description: Default behavior for explicit_address evidence. Deployments SHOULD default to quarantine or drop, not notify.

handle_claim_behavior.description: Default behavior for handle_claim evidence. Omitted means quarantine. A subject MAY set notify to allow verified handle-based requests to reach the holder, but the effective value is capped by receive_policy_constraints.

unknown_invites.description: Behavior for invite/contact delivery requests without compliant introduction_evidence.

allowed_handle_domains.description: Optional subject-private allowlist for canonical handle domains accepted as handle_claim evidence. Empty or omitted means no subject-level domain restriction; deployment constraints may still restrict the effective set.

denied_handle_domains.description: Subject-private denylist for canonical handle domains. Matches are rejected before allowed_handle_domains is evaluated.

trusted_handle_issuers.description: Optional subject-private allowlist of handle claim issuers accepted for handle_claim evidence.

trusted_directory_services.description: Optional subject-private allowlist of Directory service DIDs accepted as resolved_by for handle_claim evidence.

denied_subjects.description: Per-subject block list (peer principal DIDs). Invite delivery whose inviter is in this list MUST be dropped, and disclosure MUST be forced to opaque regardless of the disclosure policy, to avoid leaking the block via a side channel.

disclosure.description: Graded disclosure policy. Controls whether the invite/contact delivery outcome reveals a real result (delivered/blocked) to the requester, by introduction trust tier. Holder quarantine is never disclosable at any tier: it maps to status=deferred with no disclosed_outcome. Omitted means the default: high_trust=outcome, discovery_trust=opaque, low_trust=opaque.

domain_name.description: Canonical IDNA A-label domain. Subdomains are not implied; list each accepted domain explicitly.

disclosure_level.description: opaque: only a generic accepted-for-processing status is returned, indistinguishable across exists/not-exists/policy outcomes. outcome: the real delivered|blocked result is disclosed to the inviter. Neither level ever discloses holder quarantine.

high_trust.description: Disclosure level for the high-trust introduction tier: consent_grant, locator_ref, shared_realm. Default outcome.

discovery_trust.description: Disclosure level for public or restricted discovery evidence: handle_claim. Default opaque.

low_trust.description: Disclosure level for the low-trust introduction tier: same_principal_server, explicit_address, and missing/non-compliant evidence. Default opaque.

receive_policy_constraints.description: Deployment/admin upper bound applied to subject-private receive policies. The effective receive policy is the intersection of the subject policy and these constraints; constraints can only make a subject less reachable, never more reachable.

applies_to.description: Surfaces governed by this constraint object. Omitted means both invite_delivery and contact_request.

deployment_allowed_introduction_kinds.description: Maximum set of introduction evidence kinds this deployment permits. Omitted means no deployment-level kind cap.

handle_claim_max_behavior.description: Maximum behavior allowed for handle_claim evidence using the order drop < quarantine < notify.

explicit_address_max_behavior.description: Maximum behavior allowed for explicit_address evidence using the order drop < quarantine < notify.

allowed_handle_domains.description: Deployment-level allowlist for handle domains accepted as handle_claim evidence. Empty means no handle domain is accepted.

invite_delivery_target.description: Public durable target for private invite delivery. invitee is the subject; this object carries only the recipient Principal Server service DID.

introduction_evidence_digest.description: Digest of private invite delivery introduction_evidence. Raw locator tokens and receive-policy state MUST NOT appear in durable Realm events.

updated_by.description: Reducer-derived actor that produced the most recent invite state update.

third_party_invite.description: Wire-level 3PID/OOB invite binding. No plaintext email/phone/SMS code is allowed here. `oob_code_kind` distinguishes offline high-entropy token validation from server-side lookup short-code validation.

display_name_hint.description: Non-identifying UI hint only; MUST NOT contain plaintext 3PID.

token_commitment.description: Salted commitment to a high-entropy invite token. Required for offline_token mode.

token_salt_id.description: Opaque handle for the verification service's private salt record. The salt value itself MUST NOT appear on wire.

lookup_table_ref.description: Opaque verification-service lookup table reference for short-code mode. The raw short code MUST NOT appear on wire.

pepper_id.description: Server-private pepper generation identifier for lookup mode; the pepper value itself is never on wire.

oob_code_kind.description: offline_token means the out-of-band code is itself >=128-bit entropy and validated against token_commitment. lookup means the human-readable code is only an index into a server-private lookup table protected by rate limits and pepper/HMAC storage.

token_entropy_bits.description: Required for offline_token mode. Entropy estimate excluding separators.

verification_public_key.description: Ephemeral public key or DID verification method used by the verification service to sign claim results.

schemas/join-policy-operations.schema.js.title: Arkret Candidate Join Policy Operation DTOs
schemas/join-policy-operations.schema.js.description: Closed profile-private DTOs for ak.profile.candidate.join_policy.v1. These objects are carried only by the registered join-application HTTP operations; candidate_kind is never an Event.kind and none of these receipts enter shared Realm history.

server_protected_body.description: Private record for a non-E2EE Realm. The service MUST encrypt this object at rest and authorize every read; it is never copied to shared Realm history or ordinary sync.

reviewer_envelope_body.description: Opaque E2EE application body encrypted to eligible reviewer devices. The server validates recipient capability/device bindings but cannot inspect plaintext answers.

application_receipt.description: Applicant-signed application receipt. application_receipt_digest is sha256:JCS of this object with application_receipt_digest and proof omitted. proof signs the ak.join-application-receipt-proof-v1 transcript.

review_receipt.description: Reviewer-signed decision receipt. review_receipt_digest is sha256:JCS of this object with review_receipt_digest and proof omitted. proof signs the ak.join-application-review-receipt-proof-v1 transcript.

cancel_receipt.description: Applicant-signed cancellation receipt. cancel_receipt_digest is sha256:JCS of this object with cancel_receipt_digest and proof omitted. proof signs the ak.join-application-cancel-receipt-proof-v1 transcript.

schemas/key-backup-active-series.schema..title: Arkret Key Backup Active Series Record
schemas/key-backup-active-series.schema..description: Signed principal-control record selecting the canonical backup series for one (actor_id, backup_kind). This closes the rollback gap when multiple series exist after compromise rotation or migration. Receivers MUST verify this record before choosing a series from list results.

series_pointer_version.description: Strictly monotonic per (actor_id, backup_kind). The first record is 1 and every successor is previous+1; receivers reject rollback, gaps and same-version forks.

previous_series_ids.description: Retained old series used only for read-old-data or erasure transition. MUST NOT be treated as a primary recovery source.

frontier_ref.description: Principal Control Realm frontier and current identity-root device generation under which active_series_id was selected.

signature.description: base64url signature over canonical_json(record without auth_data.signature).

device_authorize_event_id.description: Accepted current-generation ak.device.authorize Event anchoring the device that signed this active-series selection.

schemas/key-backup-plaintext.schema.json.title: Arkret Key Backup Plaintext Keybag
schemas/key-backup-plaintext.schema.json.description: Canonical plaintext carried inside ak.schema.key_backup.v1 ciphertext after AEAD/HPKE open. The public envelope contents[] is only an index; this keybag is the import truth source.

secret_b64u.description: base64url(no padding) encoded secret bytes. The item_kind and metadata define how receivers import the bytes.

managed_principal_binding.description: Required for controller-custodied Native Personal Agent PCR MLS material and MUST byte-for-byte match the corresponding public contents[] binding and AEAD AAD canonical binding set.

schemas/key-backup-unlock-proof.schema.j.title: Arkret Key Backup Unlock Proof
schemas/key-backup-unlock-proof.schema.j.description: Proof presented before a recovery strand downloads or unlocks a key-backup envelope. It binds a backup read/decrypt action to one recovery_session_id, requesting device, backup object, selected series, ciphertext digest, and the proof transcript accepted by the recovery session.

proof_digest.description: Digest of the canonical recovery proof transcript that moved the session to verified.

challenge.description: Optional echo of the recovery-session challenge; when present it MUST match the session snapshot.
