The client MUST decode these exact bytes, add only a controller proof over event_digest, and return the resulting signed Event. The service MUST reject any other unsigned bytes or digest.

principal_service_binding_prepare_reques.description: Request a service-generated frozen binding core. Omitting expected_current_binding_digest is a create-if-absent CAS; supplying it is a same-service replacement CAS for the same PrincipalAuthorityInstance. The service reads the authenticated principal's accepted PCR authority and its own current service-key evidence; it does not resolve current human DID authority.

principal_service_binding_prepare_outcom.description: Durable single-use challenge plus the exact binding core the principal authorizes. binding_draft.authorization_challenge equals challenge_id byte for byte and is covered by binding_digest. accepted_at and not_before equal issued_at byte for byte. expires_at bounds challenge use, not binding validity; optional binding_draft.expires_at is independently chosen by service policy. Exact request_id replay returns the same unconsumed outcome; same request_id with different intent is duplicate_conflict.

principal_service_binding_commit_request.description: Commit the exact frozen draft. The verifier loads challenge state, recomputes binding_digest and verifies principal_authorization_proof against a current accepted device/recovery authority in binding_draft.authority_instance. Current DID control is neither required nor sufficient. The client never submits a service proof or reconstructed binding object.

schemas/principal-service-binding.schema.title: Arkret Principal Service Binding
schemas/principal-service-binding.schema.description: Portable accepted-at binding between exactly one PrincipalAuthorityInstance and its Principal Server. It is not a global current-service pointer and cannot be continued to another PCR or Principal Server.

accepted_at_service_binding_core.description: Frozen accepted-at binding core returned by ak.self.principal_service_binding.command.prepare. binding_digest = H('ak.principal-service-binding.v1', the RFC 8785 canonical object formed by every property here except binding_digest). authority_instance selects one PCR; authority_evidence describes only the service signing key, never principal authority. A same-service renewal stays inside the same authority instance.

authority_instance.description: principal_id MUST equal authority_instance.principal_id and service_id MUST equal authority_instance.principal_server_id.

endpoint_origins.description: Canonical HTTPS origins sorted by unsigned UTF-8 bytes. Paths, queries and fragments are forbidden by semantic validation.

service_resolution.description: First-hop route material for service_id. An inline record MUST name the same service_id; a referenced record MUST be fetched and independently verified before endpoint use.

authorization_challenge.description: Opaque service-generated challenge copied from the durable prepare record and included in binding_digest. It is never caller-selected or reused across distinct binding drafts.

predecessor_binding_digest.description: Exact current accepted binding digest replaced by this same-service renewal. Omitted only for the first accepted binding.

accepted_at_service_binding.description: Closed accepted-at snapshot installed by the two-phase self binding operation. principal_authorization_proof is made by a current accepted device/recovery authority from authority_instance and is independently replayable through principal_authorization_evidence; it is never a current DID-controller proof. service_acceptance_proof uses the service key. Neither proof enters binding_digest.

principal_authorization_evidence.description: Must match authority_instance byte-for-byte and authorize principal_authorization_proof at accepted_at.

schemas/public-key.schema.json.title: Arkret Canonical Public Key DTO
schemas/public-key.schema.json.description: Canonical wire shape of a public key carried in Arkret DTOs. It is defined in its own document so that device, agent and account surfaces reference one shared definition instead of reverse-referencing each other's bundles. Prose examples MUST use this exact shape: kty/kid/algorithm/key, no public_key alias.

public_key.description: Canonical public key. key carries the base64url key material; kid is the typed identifier of the key holder (for a device key, ak:device:<uuidv7>). There is no public_key member: that spelling is not canonical wire and MUST be rejected.

schemas/push-operations.schema.json.title: Arkret Push Gateway Operation DTOs
schemas/push-operations.schema.json.description: Closed request and response DTOs for ak.edge.push.command.register_device, ak.edge.push.command.unregister_device, and ak.push.notify.

push_target_id.description: Typed pairwise pseudonym for one (recipient_service_id, principal, device, push_route) tuple. It MUST NOT be a DID, DID URL, Realm id, Strand id, Message id, Event id, or stable cross-Realm correlation key.

push_route_token.description: Opaque service-generated routing token. It MUST NOT contain, encode, or be reversibly derived from a DID, DID URL, Realm id, Circle id, Strand id, Message id, Event id, handle, platform push token, or stable cross-context correlation key.

registration_id.description: Push gateway local registration id. It is not a registered ak:<kind> protocol object id.

badge.description: Coarse unread indicator. Under blind_wakeup it MUST NOT carry a plaintext absolute unread count (activity side channel); only a boolean presence flag or a policy-declared bucket string is allowed. See push-notifications.md §5.1.

missed_call.description: Coarse missed-call indicator. Under blind_wakeup it MUST NOT carry a plaintext absolute count; only a boolean presence flag or the policy-declared bucket string is allowed. See push-notifications.md §5.1.

target_route_token.description: Gateway-internal mention-redirect routing token for this device route. Paired with notification.route_tokens.mention_redirect_target_route_tokens to drive the fail-closed per-device routing gate. MUST be stripped before any provider call; MUST NOT be forwarded to a provider. See push-notifications.md §4.5 / §5.1.

visible_notification_opt_in.description: Receiver device authorization state for ak.profile.push_gateway.visible_notification.v1. Missing or false means this device MUST receive only blind_wakeup output even if the caller service is plaintext-visible; visible metadata requires an explicit per-device opt-in.

route_tokens.description: Gateway-internal opaque routing fragment shared by blind and visible notifications. Every field here drives gateway-side routing / dedup / circuit-breaker state and MUST be stripped before the gateway calls any push provider; it MUST NOT be forwarded to a provider. Tokens are issued by the recipient Sync or Principal Service and bound to recipient_service_id, push gateway service DID, purpose, scope, and salt epoch.

realm_route_token.description: Opaque token for Realm-level routing / dedup / circuit-breaker keying.

scope_route_token.description: Opaque token for the effective Realm or Circle scope of this wakeup.

mention_redirect_target_route_tokens.description: Mention-redirect routing allow-list. When non-empty, each device's device_route.target_route_token MUST appear here or that device is failed closed (no provider call, no body decryption). Gateway-internal; MUST be stripped before any provider call. See push-notifications.md §4.5.

delivery_binding_frontier_token.description: Opaque token representing the receiver's delivery-binding frontier for stale-route detection.

audit_envelope.description: `ak.audit.accessed` envelope routing fragment carried alongside a notify request. When present, the request is an audit-pipeline event (e.g. an `e2ee_late_recovery` access notice), not a push notify: the gateway writes the audit event, acks 200, and skips the push pipeline.

access_kind.description: ak.audit.accessed.access_kind. The gateway branches on `e2ee_late_recovery` to skip the push pipeline.

late_recovery_original_event_id.description: REQUIRED (at the application layer) when access_kind == e2ee_late_recovery. References the original event the late recovery targets.

timing_profile_hint.description: Closed timing/profile hint from Sync Service. traffic_metadata_hardened means the source Realm or route declares ak.profile.traffic_metadata_hardened.v1 and the Push Gateway MUST use a 300s or coarser provider-visible timing bucket. Gateway-internal; MUST be stripped before any provider call. See push-notifications.md §2.4 / §4.5 / §5.1.

push_hint.description: Sanitized hint sentinel. When the value is "l10n_key" the actual localization key MUST be carried in push_hint_l10n_key (this enum value is a form selector, not a literal display token). See push-notifications.md §5.1 / §4.5.

push_hint_l10n_key.description: Localization key value, only present (and required) when push_hint == "l10n_key". MUST be an l10n key token, never plaintext body or any identifying metadata.

evaluation_locus_unresolved.description: Set true when the client has been woken but server-side rule matching is not yet resolved (E2EE client-side rule fallback). Pure local-evaluation signal; carries no metadata. See push-notifications.md §4.5.

devices.description: Input device routes for this notification. device_id MUST be unique across the array: the input is a set, not a multiset. uniqueItems only rejects byte-identical entries, so the gateway MUST additionally reject a repeated device_id that differs in push_key or any other field. This uniqueness is what lets the response conserve exactly one outcome per input device. See push-notifications.md §5.1.

timing_profile_hint.description: Closed timing/profile hint from Sync Service. traffic_metadata_hardened means the source Realm or route declares ak.profile.traffic_metadata_hardened.v1 and the Push Gateway MUST use a 300s or coarser provider-visible timing bucket. Gateway-internal; MUST be stripped before any provider call. See push-notifications.md §2.4 / §4.5 / §5.1.

push_hint.description: Sanitized hint sentinel. When the value is "l10n_key" the actual localization key MUST be carried in push_hint_l10n_key (this enum value is a form selector, not a literal display token). See push-notifications.md §5.1 / §4.5.

push_hint_l10n_key.description: Localization key value, only present (and required) when push_hint == "l10n_key".

evaluation_locus_unresolved.description: Set true when the client has been woken but server-side rule matching is not yet resolved. See push-notifications.md §4.5.

devices.description: Input device routes for this notification. device_id MUST be unique across the array: the input is a set, not a multiset. uniqueItems only rejects byte-identical entries, so the gateway MUST additionally reject a repeated device_id that differs in push_key or any other field. This uniqueness is what lets the response conserve exactly one outcome per input device. See push-notifications.md §5.1.

push_notify_request_body.description: Closed Arkret notify body. Product-private notification bodies, provider adapter payloads, APNs/FCM/WebPush data dictionaries, `content`, `content_*`, `provider_payload`, DND/snooze state, and push-rule plaintext are outside this wire surface and MUST be consumed before this body is built. Provider-facing payloads are reconstructed by the gateway from this closed shape and MUST strip route_tokens / reason_code / event_kind / audit_envelope before provider dispatch.

event_kind.description: Originating Event kind (e.g. `ak.message`) used by the gateway to route Phase-P2 `ak.agent.*` lifecycle / actor-private kinds to a no-fanout aak. Coarse routing selector; carries no Realm / sender / event identifier.

reason_code.description: Caller-supplied wire-safe reason code. The well-known value `historical_only` marks a diagnostic replay that MUST NOT trigger a fresh push fanout (the gateway answers a 200 idempotency-style ack). Other values are honored only where the operation defines them.

push_notify_device_outcome.description: Gateway acceptance result for exactly one input device route. Identity is the (push_target_id, device_id) pair already carried by the request; no third route identifier exists. Provider delivery state, provider message ids, raw push tokens and token hashes MUST NOT appear here.

gateway_status.description: Closed gateway acceptance result. accepted = this request durably took the device route over. duplicate = an earlier request already took it over and this request produced no new delivery. rejected = the gateway did not take it over. accepted and duplicate both mean the caller MUST NOT resend this device; only rejected may be resent, and only when retry_after_ms is present. See push-notifications.md §5.2.

reason_code.description: Closed rejection reason, all registered in error-code-registry.json. The first four are target-level or policy rejections; push_token_unknown / push_token_invalid tell the caller to drop this device registration; the last two are the only caller-retryable reasons. REQUIRED when gateway_status=rejected and MUST be absent otherwise.

retry_after_ms.description: Caller-facing backoff. Present only when the gateway did not take the route over AND the reason is one the caller can retry; its presence is the sole wire signal that the caller — not the gateway — owns the next attempt. A durably accepted route is retried by the gateway and never carries this field.

push_notify_outcome.description: Closed notify response. outcomes[] is conserved against notification.devices[]: every input device_id appears exactly once, no device_id appears twice, and no device_id appears that was not requested. A target-level failure is expanded into one same-reason rejected outcome per input device rather than collapsing into a second response shape, so the conservation invariant holds unconditionally. Counts, if a deployment surfaces them, are derived from outcomes[] and are never an independent truth source.

push_target_id.description: Echo of notification.push_target_id. MUST equal the request value.

outcomes.description: One entry per unique device_id in notification.devices[]. device_id MUST be unique across the array.

schemas/query.schema.json.title: Arkret Query / Search Request Shapes
schemas/query.schema.json.description: Canonical wire schema for client query / projection and search request bodies and their reusable building blocks (filters, sort, relation query). The OpenAPI document references these $defs so there is a single source of truth. Human-readable semantics: zh/conformance/query-schema.md. facet_name / view_renderer are copies of the shared OpenAPI enums (kept local so this file is self-contained); the authoritative facet / renderer enums also live in the OpenAPI components and MUST stay in lockstep.

context_ref.description: Optional timeline / renderer context object reference. This is not a Seal.

schemas/range-completeness-attestation.s.title: Arkret Range-bound Completeness Attestation
schemas/range-completeness-attestation.s.description: A range-bound completeness attestation. Event kind: ak.attestation.range_completeness (active in event-kind-registry; the event kind itself carries NO .v1 suffix). Payload schema id: ak.schema.range_completeness_attestation.v1 (schemas keep the .v1 versioning). The attestation asserts that the issuer (and any witnesses) have observed every reducer-input event in a declared range — (from_frontier, to_frontier) bounded by explicit per-actor seq intervals — where each frontier is a Realm-scoped frontier (property name realm_frontier; the security/replication boundary for completeness in v1 is the Realm, not an in-Realm Space container). Distinct from ak.event_batch_receipt (set-bound integrity over an arbitrary chosen subset) and ak.audit.ryw_receipt (per-event RYW hint). Used when verifiers need a completeness claim — i.e., 'no event has been silently withheld from this range' — not just 'the events given are unmodified'. Standalone single-issuer attestations are NOT sufficient for sovereign / multi-writer trust models; deployments requiring strong completeness MUST use a witness_attestation block following the ak.audit.ryw_receipt model (zh/crypto-media/audited-e2ee.md §4.1.1).

schema.description: Payload schema id (versioned). The owning Event kind in event-kind-registry.json is ak.attestation.range_completeness (NO .v1 suffix on the event kind).

from_frontier.description: Lower bound of the range (exclusive). The attestation covers events causally after this frontier.

from_seq_exclusive.description: Per-actor seq lower bound (exclusive). -1 means 'from actor genesis'.

to_seq_inclusive.description: Per-actor seq upper bound (inclusive). Issuer asserts completeness of every actor_seq in the half-open interval (from_seq_exclusive, to_seq_inclusive].

actor_seq_ranges.description: Per-actor seq intervals attested. Silent forks frequently appear as a missing slice in a single actor's seq sequence while the global frontier still advances monotonically — explicit per-actor ranges close that gap. MUST cover every actor that produced reducer-input events in (from_frontier, to_frontier].

root.description: Canonical Merkle root over the sorted set of (actor_id, actor_seq, event_id, event_digest) tuples for every reducer-input event in scope. Digest algorithm agility per Realm.digest_algorithm.

count.description: Number of reducer-input events in scope. MUST match the number of leaves used to compute root.

observed_at.description: When the issuer finished observing the scope and computed the attestation.

kind.description: Same semantics as ak.audit.ryw_receipt.witness_attestation: 'federation_witness_attested' requires witnesses[].length >= 2 with pairwise-distinct issuer/controlling_organization/verification_method, each listed by Realm policy in audit.range_completeness_witnesses[]. 'single_source' is the honest declaration for self-attested deployments. Mismatch between kind and witnesses[] cardinality / distinctness / policy listing MUST be rejected. Receivers SHOULD treat single_source attestations as advisory only and not as a sovereign-grade completeness proof.

verification_method.description: DID URL of the key the witness used to sign. MUST be distinct from other witnesses' verification_method values for 'federation_witness_attested' to be valid.

schemas/read-cursor-operations.schema.js.title: Arkret Read Cursor Self-Management Operation DTOs
schemas/read-cursor-operations.schema.js.description: Closed request/response DTOs for the self-surface read cursor operations (ak.self.read_cursor.*). Advance carries the authenticated holder's exact signed ak.read_cursor.advance actor-private Event; the service validates and forwards it without rebuilding or co-signing. The durable cursor object model and read_scope / position field shapes are read-cursor.schema.json. See spec/v1/zh/discovery/read-receipts.md.

read_cursor_advance_request_body.description: Carries one caller-signed ak.read_cursor.advance Event and nothing else. The Event payload is the complete ak.schema.read_cursor.v1 object; actor_id is both envelope ownership and payload ownership, while payload device_id must equal the authenticated session device. The service MUST submit these exact bytes through ordinary Event admission and MUST NOT mint the cursor id, choose updated_at, rebuild the payload, or sign under a service identity.

kind.description: Read-scope object kind per zh/models/private-objects.md §2.2. Track-scoped read cursors use kind='strand' plus track_name. Thread cursors use kind='thread' with container_ref = the thread root message id (zh/discovery/read-receipts.md §5); thread is a projection selector over the reply sub-timeline, not a first-class protocol object. Shares the read-scope discriminator family with read-receipt.schema.json; each schema declares its own supported subset.

container_ref.description: Required when kind is circle, space, strand, or thread; omitted for kind='realm'. Thread read scopes reference the root message.

track_name.description: Required when kind='strand' AND the cursor scopes a single track (e.g. 'discussion', 'synthesis', or any profile-registered track name). Track names MUST match the Strand's registered tracks; unknown tracks MUST be rejected with schema_violation.

schemas/read-cursor.schema.json.title: Arkret Read Cursor
schemas/read-cursor.schema.json.description: Actor-private multi-device read cursor. Stored in encrypted account data or actor-private stream; NEVER published into a shared Realm Event history. Bound to (actor_id, realm_id, read_scope, position, HLC, device_id) per zh/discovery/read-receipts.md §6.6. Multi-device merge is causal-first per §6.5: the position that causally dominates wins regardless of HLC; HLC max decides only causally concurrent positions, and device_id only breaks equal HLCs.

device_id.description: Originating device. Required for multi-device convergence: when two devices race on the same (actor_id, realm_id, read_scope) the receiver first picks the causally dominating position; only for causally concurrent positions does it pick the greater HLC, and device_id provides a deterministic actor_id-scoped tiebreaker when those HLCs are equal. device_id MUST NOT be used to select a position that another position causally dominates.

schemas/read-receipt.schema.json.title: Arkret Read Receipt Signal Plaintext
schemas/read-receipt.schema.json.description: Closed decrypted Signal plaintext payload profile for ak.receipt.read, carried only inside ak.schema.signal_envelope.v1 with signal_class=session. It is a Strand timeline UI hint, NOT canonical truth, NOT a durable Event, and NOT a multi-device cursor (see read-cursor.schema.json for that). MUST NOT generate push notifications. Realm scope, sender identity and send time come from the enclosing signed envelope and are not duplicated here. Privacy is governed by Realm policy: Realms MAY allow public, members-only, or actor-private receipt sharing. See zh/discovery/read-receipts.md sections 2.1 / 6.2 and zh/sync/signal.md section 1.1.

payload_sequence.description: Strictly increasing but non-contiguous u64 within (sender_device_id, canonical scope_ref). Arbitrary forward gaps are accepted; a repeated or lower value is stale.

event_id.description: ID of the most recent Event the actor has read. Causality implies all causal predecessors are also read.

hlc.description: Optional. HLC of the read position; required when Sync Service must compare receipts under merge / debounce rules across devices for the same actor.

kind.description: Read-scope discriminator from the same family as read-cursor.schema.json; each schema declares its own supported subset (receipt additionally supports view/message/morph; cursor additionally supports circle/space). kind='thread' selects the reply sub-timeline rooted at a message (zh/discovery/read-receipts.md §5); thread is a projection selector, not a first-class protocol object.

object_ref.description: Required when kind is anything other than 'realm'. Thread read scopes reference the root message.

track_name.description: Required when kind='strand' and the receipt scopes a single track.

track_scope.description: Only valid when kind='strand'. Use track_scope='all' for an entire Strand regardless of track.

genesis_salt.description: Canonical unpadded Base64URL encoding of exactly 32 CSPRNG octets. It distinguishes event-derived creation intents and has no replay, ordering, authorization, freshness, or winner semantics.

founding_device_descriptor.description: Human Principal Control Realm genesis only. The identity root commits to the exact founding device material and the canonical founding authorize payload digest. The enclosing pcr_genesis_unit requires it; managed Agent PCR genesis MUST omit it.

initial_resolution.description: Root-committed initial full_id and DID method history position for a Principal Control Realm or managed Agent control Realm. The admitting service MUST verify that project(full_id) equals the genesis actor_id before accepting the closed genesis unit.

allOf.description: founding_device_descriptor is exclusive to human Principal Control Realm genesis. managed_agent_control, collaboration and direct_conversation genesis MUST omit it. genesis_salt is required for every purpose since PCR genesis is event-derived like any other Realm.
Only identity-control Realm genesis carries initial_resolution, and every such genesis carries it. Collaboration/direct-conversation Realms MUST omit it.
Human Principal Control Realm genesis uses the independently closed human-principal DID method set.

Managed Agent PCR genesis commits the already accepted did:webvh inception head. The later PCR service binding update is continuous from this head and does not participate in the create Event preimage.
Ephemeral pairwise did:key actors are MLS LeafNode-bound Realm-local authors and never create a PCR.

founding_device_descriptor.description: Closed founding-device commitment embedded in the root-signed human Principal Control Realm genesis payload and required by pcr_genesis_unit. It is not an independent signed object. Managed Agent PCR creation omits this human-device descriptor.

founding_authorize_payload_digest.description: Canonical digest of the proof-free founding ak.device.authorize payload. It MUST NOT be an Event id or envelope digest.

schemas/realm-join-candidate.schema.json.title: Arkret Realm Join Candidate
schemas/realm-join-candidate.schema.json.description: Time-bounded routing hint for submitting Realm join, invite-accept, knock, or restricted-join material through a qualified Realm service. This object is not membership authorization and is distinct from member_delivery_binding.

realm_id.description: Realm this candidate is bound to. Verifiers MUST reject a candidate used for any other Realm.

service_id.description: Stable service did_core_id that can receive or relay join-side submissions for this Realm.

service_resolution.description: First-hop signed ServiceResolutionRecord material for service_id, inline or through current_record_url. Callers MUST validate the record proof, method-native history, project(full_id)=service_id, freshness, canonical base_url and route-binding projection before transport, then use GET /_arkret/describe only as second-hop capability/metadata confirmation.

service_kind.description: Service class. principal_server is the normal candidate; sync_node and notary are allowed only when Realm policy authorizes them to receive join-side submissions.

role.description: Routing role within the Realm candidate set. This is a hint for ordering and diagnostics, not an authorization grant.

endpoint.description: Optional non-authoritative endpoint hint. Callers MUST NOT route from this field or a DID Document endpoint; they MUST obtain and validate service_resolution, use its canonical base_url for first transport, and confirm capabilities through GET /_arkret/describe.

operations.description: Endpoint-callable operation ids available at this candidate. Join-side routing requires ak.events.submit.

join_methods.description: Join-side strands this candidate claims to support for this requester and Realm.

priority.description: Lower values are preferred. Ties are broken deterministically by service_id.

source.description: Where this routing hint came from. Receivers still validate current Realm policy and the signed ServiceResolutionRecord; route authority comes from the validated record, while GET /_arkret/describe is only second-hop capability and metadata confirmation.

source_refs.description: Realm or directory source events that justify this candidate, such as discovery, service-binding, or sync endpoint state.

frontier_ref.description: Optional digest of the candidate service's advertised Realm frontier at as_of; used only to detect stale hints.

seal_basis.description: Full single-leaf Control Move basis for the candidate service's current accepted Realm Seal at as_of. Principal-server candidates MUST include this so pre-join Realm join / invite-accept Control Moves can be signed without a separate membership-gated frontier read. This is a routing/anchoring hint, not membership authorization: the receiving service still validates the submitted basis and invite.

as_of.description: Time when the issuer observed or refreshed this candidate.

expires_at.description: Time after which clients MUST NOT use this candidate without re-resolving the Realm.

proofs.description: Optional proof set binding realm_id, service_id, role, operations, join_methods, as_of, and expires_at. Required when the candidate is carried outside a freshly resolved Directory response.

schemas/realm-link-operations.schema.jso.title: Arkret Realm Link Self-Management Operation DTOs
schemas/realm-link-operations.schema.jso.description: Closed request/response DTOs for the self-surface cross-Realm link operations (ak.self.realm_link.*). Each write carries the caller-signed ak.realm.link Move and the service submits those exact bytes through ordinary Event admission, so the reducer still validates self-reference, link kind and the FSM transition. General link-graph cycles are legal; traversal uses a visited set and does not reject a write merely for forming a cycle. The durable link payload is the canonical ak.realm.link; see spec/v1/zh/models/realm-links.md.

link_kind.description: Core value or machine-registered extension kind using x.<reverse-dns>.<name>; unregistered extension values fail closed.

commitment.description: Optional opaque commitment / proof reference linking this edge to an external attestation.

realm_link_event_submission.description: Shared submission shape for both cross-Realm link writes. Create and tombstone are the same Event kind writing the same (realm_id, target_realm_id, link_kind) FSM cell, so they share one submission def and differ only in the status their payload names. Edge fields MUST be carried inside the caller-signed Event; accepting them directly for a service-added signature is forbidden by capabilities.md sections 118/361 and key-management.md section 411. The source Realm is single-sourced by event.realm_id and MUST equal the path realm_id; the rest of the edge is event.payload (realm_link_payload). The service MUST submit these exact bytes through ordinary Event admission and MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event; admission MUST verify that event.actor_id is the authenticated caller, and rejects self-reference with schema_violation + realm_link_self_reference and an illegal FSM transition with failed_precondition + realm_link_invalid_transition. Because the payload names the status the edge is moving to, a concurrent write on the same triple makes the later submission fail its transition check rather than silently overwriting.

realm_link_create_request_body.description: Carries the caller-signed ak.realm.link Move and nothing else. target_realm_id, link_kind, status and the optional label / commitment all live in link_event.event.payload.

link_event.description: Closed ak.realm.link Event authored and signed by the authenticated caller.

realm_link_delete_request_body.description: Carries the caller-signed tombstoning ak.realm.link Move and nothing else. The edge is single-sourced by link_event.event.payload: target_realm_id MUST equal the path target_realm_id, and link_kind is named there rather than in a query parameter, because a query parameter is outside the bytes the caller signs. Deleting an edge is the same durable Event kind as creating one -- every peer has to converge on the removal too -- so this operation keeps its event_log effect.

link_event.description: Closed ak.realm.link Event authored and signed by the authenticated caller, with payload.status pinned to tombstoned.

realm_effective_policy_outcome.description: Merged effective policy after walking governed_by / inherits_policy_from ancestors per the Realm's ak.realm.inheritance_policy declaration.

inheritance_mode.description: explicit when the Realm has projected a ak.realm.inheritance_policy; none otherwise (implicit inheritance is forbidden).

schemas/realm-organization-operations.sc.title: Arkret Realm Organization-Relationship Read Operation DTOs
schemas/realm-organization-operations.sc.description: Closed response DTO for the self-surface Realm organization-relationship read operation (ak.self.realm_organization.read.list). Returns the projected ak.realm.organization statements (active / revoked / expired) for a Realm plus the declared owning_organizations hints that have no verified statement. The verified rows mirror the canonical realm_organization_payload field order; lifecycle_phase is reducer-derived. A row here is a projection only: an organization relationship is only verified when lifecycle_phase=verified_active, and actual Realm control still requires the corresponding Realm policy / notary / capability / service-binding event. See spec/v1/zh/models/realm-and-space.md §2.3.0 and schemas/event-payload.schema.json#/$defs/realm_organization_payload.

lifecycle_phase.description: Reducer-derived lifecycle phase of the projected statement. verified_active = latest accepted statement for (organization_id, relationship) is status=active and within its validity window. revoked_or_expired = the relationship has been revoked or is outside its not_before/expires_at window. Declared-only organization hints with no statement are carried in declared_organization_hints, not as rows.

delegation_ref.description: Resolved authorization.delegation_ref for delegated issuer roles (governance_service / account_authority).

relationships.description: Projected ak.realm.organization statement rows (verified_active and revoked_or_expired), latest-per-(organization_id, relationship).

declared_organization_hints.description: owning_organizations declared hints (realm-and-space.md §2.3.0) that have NO verified ak.realm.organization statement. These are unverified claims and MUST NOT be rendered as official / governed / endorsed.

schemas/realm-policy-server-operations.s.title: Arkret Realm Policy-Server Self-Management Operation DTOs
schemas/realm-policy-server-operations.s.description: Closed request/response DTOs for the self-surface Realm policy-server config operations (ak.self.realm_policy_server.*). PUT carries the caller-signed durable ak.realm.policy_server Move; DELETE carries the same kind with payload {tombstone:true}. Both MUST carry head_eq for the complete settled value when the direct cell already holds one, and the caller attaches that precondition because it is inside the bytes it signs. An existing tombstone is an idempotent empty success, while a never-written or inherited-only direct cell returns not_found. Both mutation operations require ak.policy.manage; see spec/v1/zh/authz/policy-server.md §2.

from_org_fallback.description: True when the config was resolved via the governed_by / org-fallback chain rather than a row on the Realm itself.

realm_policy_server_event_submission.description: Shared submission shape for both policy-server writes. Replace and delete write the same CAS-register cell with the same Event kind, so they share one submission def and differ only in whether the payload is a declaration or the value tombstone. Declaration fields MUST be carried inside the caller-signed Event; accepting them directly for a service-added signature is forbidden by capabilities.md sections 118/361 and key-management.md section 411. The Realm is single-sourced by event.realm_id and MUST equal the path realm_id. The service MUST submit these exact bytes through ordinary Event admission and MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event; admission MUST verify that event.actor_id is the authenticated caller and that the caller holds ak.policy.manage. When the direct cell already holds a settled declaration or tombstone, the Event MUST carry a head_eq precondition on ak:cell:ak.component.realm.policy_server.v1:null naming that complete value; the caller attaches it because preconditions are inside the signed bytes, so a concurrent write makes the later submission fail its precondition rather than silently clobbering the cell.

realm_policy_server_replace_request_body.description: Carries the caller-signed ak.realm.policy_server declaration Move and nothing else. The whole declaration is policy_server_event.event.payload (realm_policy_server_declaration_payload), which is the durable value the reducer stores -- there is no narrower REST projection of it left to drift.

policy_server_event.description: Closed ak.realm.policy_server Event authored and signed by the authenticated caller, whose payload is a declaration.

realm_policy_server_delete_request_body.description: Carries the caller-signed value-tombstone ak.realm.policy_server Move and nothing else. The payload is exactly {"tombstone":true}. This is a DELETE with a request body -- the same shape ak.self.keys.backups.resource.delete already uses -- because the durable removal is a signed Event and no signature fits in a bodyless request.

policy_server_event.description: Closed ak.realm.policy_server Event authored and signed by the authenticated caller, with payload pinned to the value tombstone.

schemas/realm-read-operations.schema.jso.title: Arkret Realm Read + Moderation-Policy Operation DTOs
schemas/realm-read-operations.schema.jso.description: Closed request/response DTOs for the self-surface Realm read operations and moderation-policy management (ak.self.realm.*). Realm read returns the lifecycle projection; export returns a full event-log + operation dump; effective moderation-policy returns the organization-inherited merged view; the moderation-policy override write carries the caller-signed ak.realm.moderation_policy Event. See spec/v1/zh/models/realm-and-space.md and spec/v1/zh/governance/content-moderation.md.

operations.description: Operation dump rows {operation_id, realm_id, object_kind, operation_type, payload, created_at}.

events.description: Event-log dump rows {event_id, realm_id, event_kind, operation_type, operation_id, sender, payload, created_at}.

realm_effective_moderation_policy.$comment: Open extension surface: the merged moderation-policy view carries deployment-defined organization/realm policy layers and fanout metadata; additionalProperties intentionally true so servers may surface implementation-specific layer detail without a wire-breaking change.

inheritance_chain.description: Organization DIDs (or deployment-local organization identifiers) contributing policy layers, parent-first.

realm_moderation_policy_event_submission.description: Caller-signed ak.realm.moderation_policy Control Move. event.realm_id MUST equal the path Realm and event.actor_id MUST equal the authenticated session actor. The service forwards the exact submission through ordinary Event admission and MUST NOT author, rebuild, co-sign or append a precondition. Admission requires ak.realm.moderation_policy or ak.policy.manage according to the capability registry; Realm ownership alone is not an authorization rule. The Event MUST contain exactly one signed head_eq precondition for ak:cell:ak.component.realm.moderation_policy.v1:null, comparing the complete settled cell value or null when absent. The payload is the closed realm_moderation_policy_state_payload and carries the policy document only as payload.value. Exact byte replay of an accepted Event returns the byte-identical stored outcome; the same event identity with different bytes, a stale head, a Bottom cell or a second applicable CAS guard fails closed without another write.

realm_moderation_policy_replace_request_.description: Carries the caller-signed ak.realm.moderation_policy Event and no unsigned policy fields.

realm_moderation_policy_document.description: Projection of the accepted moderation-policy Event: realm_id is event.realm_id, policy is event.payload.value, updated_by is event.actor_id, and updated_at is event.created_at.

realm_lifecycle_event_submission.description: Shared submission shape for the four Realm lifecycle Moves. The Event payload MUST be carried inside the caller-signed Event; accepting it directly for a service-added signature is forbidden by capabilities.md sections 118/361 and key-management.md section 411. The Realm is single-sourced by event.realm_id and MUST equal the path realm_id. The service MUST submit these exact bytes through ordinary Event admission and MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event; admission MUST verify that event.actor_id is the authenticated caller and that the lifecycle transition is admissible from the Realm's current state. Because these payloads describe a transition out of state the caller has to read first, a concurrent lifecycle write makes the later submission fail its precondition rather than silently reordering: that is the intended outcome, not a regression.

realm_archive_request_body.description: Carries the caller-signed ak.realm.archive Move and nothing else. The archived flag and optional reason live in lifecycle_event.event.payload (realm_archive_payload).

lifecycle_event.description: Closed ak.realm.archive Event authored and signed by the authenticated caller.

realm_freeze_request_body.description: Carries the caller-signed ak.realm.freeze Move and nothing else. The frozen flag and optional reason live in lifecycle_event.event.payload (realm_freeze_payload).

lifecycle_event.description: Closed ak.realm.freeze Event authored and signed by the authenticated caller.

realm_tombstone_request_body.description: Carries the caller-signed terminal ak.realm.tombstone Move and nothing else. Its payload (realm_tombstone_payload) requires reason and successor_realm_id, so the signed Event is the whole record of who ended the Realm and where it continues.

lifecycle_event.description: Closed ak.realm.tombstone Event authored and signed by the authenticated caller.

realm_destroy_request_body.description: Carries the caller-signed terminal ak.realm.destroy Move and nothing else. Its payload (realm_destroy_payload) requires reason and may pin retention_policy_id and verification_stub_required.

lifecycle_event.description: Closed ak.realm.destroy Event authored and signed by the authenticated caller.

anyOf.$comment: forbidden Realm authorship field; canonical name is created_by
forbidden Realm addressing field; the only alias carrier is the ak.realm.alias Event (ak.component.realm.alias.v1). See zh/discovery/object-addressing.md section 3.3.

forbidden Realm policy field; the E2EE history sharing policy is the ak.realm.history_sharing_policy facet cell, and the two profiles that can never emit that Event take a profile-fixed baseline instead: ak.profile.principal_control_realm.v1 and ak.profile.direct_conversation_realm.v1. See zh/governance/history-visibility.md section 3, zh/models/realm-and-space.md section 2.8.1 and zh/identity/contact-and-direct-conversation.md section 6.2.
forbidden Realm policy field; the only carrier is the ak.realm.plaintext_visible_services facet cell. See zh/sync/service-surface.md.

id.description: Present on the materialised object. MUST be absent from the create Event payload: zh/models/common-fields.md derives it from the create Event's own event_id (retyped), so a payload-supplied id would be a second, forgeable truth.

security_class.description: Optional security class. 'high_assurance' forbids federation_policy=open and SHOULD use stricter resolver/E2EE/audit defaults. Omitted = 'standard'.

trust_domain.description: Immutable deployment trust domain captured by ak.realm.create. Receivers MUST require this to match the current Realm trust domain before accepting cross-domain replay-sensitive proofs.

owning_organizations.description: Declared or projected organization principals associated with this Realm. Each DID MUST resolve to an Organization principal. This field alone is not a verified ownership/governance endorsement; clients and directories MUST require an active ak.realm.organization statement for verified badges or organization-controlled semantics.

fields.description: Product/profile fields. Security-relevant discriminators such as purpose in {principal_control, managed_agent_control} and collaboration_role=direct_conversation are schema constrained below; other product fields remain extension-defined.

relation_profiles.description: Optional Relation cardinality and conflict profiles declared by this Realm schema/profile.

on_conflict.description: Conflict handling for mutually unreachable Relation candidates. deterministic_winner selects the candidate with the bytewise-greatest canonical event_digest per the single canonical tie-break rule (zh/conformance/encoding.md §4.2); it MUST NOT use HLC, actor id, event_id, local receive order, database id, or service insertion order.

preview_policy_id.description: Optional materialized pointer to the effective preview / peek policy. Canonical writes use ak.realm.preview_policy; absence means directory card / stripped state only, no history stub/snippet preview.

default_strand_id.description: Optional / nullable. AUTHORITATIVE single pointer to the Realm's default discussion Strand (last value projected from ak.realm.set_default_strand; cell ak.component.realm.set_default_strand.v1, cas_register, bottom=reject). A single pointer avoids multi-default dirty state. null / absent means the Realm has no designated default Strand. The reducer rejects a set_default_strand whose strand_id does not resolve to a projected non-tombstoned Strand in this Realm (failed_precondition), so this pointer never dangles. The Strand projection's derived is_default flag is computed as strand_id == this value; clients discover the default Strand deterministically from this field (or the Strand is_default marker) and MUST NOT rely on any Strand-reuses-Realm-token implementation detail. See zh/models/strand-and-message.md (default-Strand discovery).

reducer_profile.description: Materialized value of the Realm reducer-profile singleton control cell. ak.realm.create supplies its genesis value; only ak.realm.upgrade may change it.

content_scheme.description: Content-envelope encryption scheme for MLS-backed Realms (crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md §2.10). Orthogonal to encryption_profile, which only declares whether an MLS group exists. mls_rfc9420 = MLS PrivateMessage (per-message forward secrecy, NOT shareable to later joiners; only valid with history_visibility=joined/restricted on MLS-backed Realms). mls_exporter_aead_v1 = MLS-Exporter-derived per-epoch history_secret AEAD (history shareable to authorized later joiners via ak.realm_key.share; per-epoch forward secrecy; does not itself force pre-join delivery). Because it changes historical key access, it MUST enter security_frontier_digest so receivers can determine, per epoch T0, which scheme applies. Absent: mls_rfc9420 for encryption_profile=mls_rfc9420 Realms; not applicable when encryption_profile=none/external.

content_encryption_floor.description: Realm-wide content encryption floor (models/circle.md §7, models/realm-and-space.md §4). This is the Realm's actual content-encryption on/off switch. When e2ee_required, the effective_scope of Strand / Message / Morph / Blob content MUST be MLS-backed (Realm-default MLS or Circle MLS); reducer MUST failed_precondition (reason=content_encryption_floor_violation) on plaintext content. Independent of encryption_profile, which only declares the encryption MECHANISM (whether an MLS group exists), not which Arkret fields enter ciphertext. One-way ratchet: once the effective value has reached e2ee_required, a later policy write lowering it back to allow_plaintext MUST be rejected with content_encryption_floor_downgrade. Defaults to allow_plaintext when absent.

metadata_encryption_floor.description: Realm-wide metadata encryption floor (models/circle.md §7), binary and symmetric with content_encryption_floor. allow_plaintext lets user-readable metadata stay wire-plaintext; e2ee_required forces it into encrypted_metadata. Comparison order allow_plaintext < e2ee_required. Effective floor = max(parent Realm value, Circle metadata floor, object profile requirement); any write below the effective floor MUST failed_precondition (reason=metadata_encryption_floor_violation). MUST NOT be relaxed by Circle, Space, or object profile. Space does not carry a metadata floor value. One-way ratchet: once the effective value has reached e2ee_required, a later policy write lowering it back to allow_plaintext MUST be rejected with metadata_encryption_floor_downgrade. When absent, reducers default to e2ee_required for mls_rfc9420 or content_encryption_floor=e2ee_required Realms, otherwise allow_plaintext.

agent_participation.description: Realm five-bit native Agent participation ceiling. It may only tighten the target-service safety ceiling and is itself the parent of Circle and Strand ceilings.

durability_policy.description: Realm Recovery Key (RRK) durability policy (models/realm-and-space.md §2.3.1, crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md §2.10.8). Declares who can recover Realm history after all member devices are lost or all members leave. Confidentiality-axis durability, orthogonal to notary / notary.recovery_* (finality axis: who signs Seals). Recovery recipients are offline HPKE public keys, NOT MLS members. Only effective (mode != none) when content_scheme=mls_exporter_aead_v1; declaring mode != none on an mls_rfc9420 Realm MUST failed_precondition (durability_scheme_incompatible). Granularity = organization composition (point a sensitive Realm's owning_organizations at a finer org), not a per-Realm knob; parent-org retention = list the parent org RRK in recovery_recipients (explicit, member-visible). Written via Event kind ak.realm.policy_bundle.

mode.description: none = no organizational recovery path (total member loss = permanent loss). org_recovery_key = single org RRK. threshold = k-of-n recovery recipients.

recovery_recipients.description: Recovery recipients (RRK holders). MUST be non-empty when mode != none. Each verification_method MUST point to a verification method designated by an active ArkretRealmHistoryRecoveryKey service entry published by principal_id, domain-separated from the principal's backup-HPKE key (key-management.md §3.3 backup_hpke_ikm, wire name recovery_public_key).

threshold.description: k-of-n threshold parameters, required when mode=threshold. k <= n and n MUST equal len(recovery_recipients).

then.$comment: The arithmetic rule 1 <= k <= n == len(recovery_recipients) is reducer/conformance validation because JSON Schema cannot compare threshold.n to array length portably.

sync_endpoints.description: Realm-level service binding list for shared notary / sync / mirror / federation peer surfaces. Directory resolve responses expose a requester-filtered join_candidates projection for join-side ingress; raw sync_endpoints are not a public candidate list. Member-level delivery_binding remains on ak.member.state and MUST NOT be inferred from this list.

notary_profile.description: Create-locked Seal finality profile. single_did and threshold deployments require signed Seal single-chain uniqueness; open_set deployments allow multiple Seal leaves and deterministic joined control views; mixed deployments use a primary notary plus fallback recovery notary.

availability_policy.description: Realm policy component governing independently signed byte-availability receipts before Seal inclusion and before snapshot/backfill availability claims. Absent means {min_holders:1, holder_roles:['notary'], applies_to:['seal_include']}. Holder roles are resolved from the accepted notary/service-binding state at the Seal basis; a self-asserted role is insufficient.

audit_policy.description: Realm policy component for range-completeness and seal-transparency witness admission. If absent, receivers MUST NOT accept a seal-transparency auditor attestation as verified v1 evidence, and federation_witness_attested range completeness has no admissible witness set.

digest_algorithm.description: Digest suite (canonicalization x hash tuple) used for DataEvent ids, Control Move ids, Seal ids, state_root, and Merkle leaves within this Realm. It is locked at create except for ak.realm.digest_suite_transition under ak.profile.hash_transition.v1. Defaults to sha256. Value space is the active rows of artifacts/registry/digest-suite-registry.json (this enum MUST be regenerated when a row flips active, e.g. cbor.sha256); bare ids denote canonical-JSON canonicalization, dotted ids denote alternate canonical encodings. Exactly one live suite per Realm; migration uses the control-plane transition Move and dual-root Seal defined by event-auth-state-resolution.md §9.3.2.

notary.description: Genesis value for the Realm notary cell. Subsequent changes are Control Moves finalized by the previous notary. For single_did profiles, recovery_members and controller organization evidence are required so reducer/authz can reject single-organization recovery setups.

forensic_attribution.$comment: Required for type=threshold (enforced by allOf below). MUST be quorum_intersection when 2*threshold > members.length (two conflicting quorums then intersect in at least one attributable double-signer; see authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.1 and BFT Protocol Forensics). MUST be waived when 2*threshold <= members.length, declaring that automatic culprit attribution is unavailable. JSON Schema cannot compare threshold against members.length, so the arithmetic side is reducer/conformance validation (ak.vector.cba_lattice.threshold_forensic_attribution.v1).
forensic_attribution.description: Equivocation culprit-attribution mode for threshold notary committees: quorum_intersection (2k>n, automatic attribution available) or waived (k<=n/2, deployment explicitly waives automatic attribution and relies on committee-level handling).

controller_organization.description: DID of the organization controlling the primary notary, when the resolver or deployment policy can derive it. Required for single_did profile so recovery diversity can be verified.

recovery_controller_organizations.description: Organization DIDs controlling recovery_members. Reducer MUST verify at least one differs from controller_organization for single_did profile.

capability_action_registry_digest.description: Create-locked genesis capability-action registry basis for this Realm: the JCS SHA-256 digest of the complete canonical capability-action-registry.json snapshot the creator adopted. The ak.realm.create reducer copies this signed value into the ak.component.realm.authority_root.v1 cell; it MUST NOT infer the digest from its own embedded registry, because that would make genesis state_root depend on the receiver's software version. Changing the basis afterwards is a root-control Move, not a Realm update.

revocation_freshness_window_ms.description: Realm-level maximum control-plane seal distance/time window for accepting DataEvents whose seal_ref predates an observed revocation seal. Receivers evaluate this window by seal topology and policy (the notary-committed seal-time delta along the Seal DAG per authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 4.3), not by unverified event signing time. risk_tier=high capabilities get no grace (effective 0). High-risk Realms SHOULD use a short value or move the affected cell family to control plane.

recovery_witness_freshness_window_ms.description: Maximum signed Seal.sealed_at distance from the conflict-detecting frontier to a state_witness used by a conflict-recovery Move. Receivers compute the non-negative DAG time delta from the witness Seal to the recovery Move's seal_basis leaves; exceeding this value fails closed with recovery_witness_revoke_lagging.

proposal_intake_sla_ms.description: Realm-level deadline within which a submitted control-plane Control Move MUST receive a signed Control Proposal Ack or signed ingress rejection (authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.2). This acknowledgement phase is separate from the Control Proposal Ack's bounded decision window. Silent omission past this SLA is governance-health evidence.

proposal_decision_window_ms.description: Realm-level default first decision window for an acknowledged Control Move. A Control Proposal Ack commits decision_due_at = received_at + an effective window no greater than this value and the protocol hard ceiling of 24 hours. The deadline requires a verifiable decision (include in an accepted Seal, signed reject, or bounded signed defer); it is not an acceptance or finality SLA.
proposal_decision_window_ms.$comment: Reducer/conformance validation MUST enforce proposal_decision_window_ms <= proposal_absolute_deadline_ms. If max_proposal_defers > 0, the inequality MUST be strict so at least one strictly later decision_due_at remains representable. JSON Schema cannot compare sibling numeric properties.

proposal_absolute_deadline_ms.description: Realm-level absolute proposal decision horizon measured from the Control Proposal Ack's signed received_at. absolute_due_at MUST equal received_at plus an effective value no greater than this field and the protocol hard ceiling of 72 hours. Signed defers MUST preserve absolute_due_at and cannot extend this horizon.
proposal_absolute_deadline_ms.$comment: Reducer/conformance validation owns the sibling-field ordering rule documented on proposal_decision_window_ms.

max_proposal_defers.description: Maximum cumulative number of signed defers for one acknowledged Control Move. The protocol hard ceiling is two. Every defer carries a closed reason code, increments defer_count by exactly one, advances decision_due_at without exceeding absolute_due_at, and preserves the Control Proposal Ack's absolute_due_at.
max_proposal_defers.$comment: When proposal_decision_window_ms equals proposal_absolute_deadline_ms this field MUST be 0; otherwise the declared defer count is not realizable.

seal_compaction_max_interval_ms.description: Structural obligation, not advisory: maximum interval between compaction Seals (Seals carrying covered_event_digests[] or an equivalent verifiable full-coverage manifest). Because the cumulative control-plane covered set is defined recursively from predecessor_refs + delta, compaction Seals are the only bounded bootstrap points for new verifiers; a notary that exceeds this interval degrades bootstrap to walking the chain to genesis. open_set deployments MUST use <= 86400000 (24h); threshold deployments MUST use <= 604800000 (7d); single_did SHOULD use <= 86400000. Receivers SHOULD raise governance health alarms when the live chain exceeds the declared interval. See authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 6.2 and conformance vector ak.vector.cba_lattice.seal_compaction_interval_enforced.v1.

max_authority_lifetime_ms.description: Realm-level maximum lifetime window used when an otherwise unbounded parent grant first delegates. Reducers freeze authority_expiry_seal = first_delegation_sealed_at + effective max_authority_lifetime_ms and MUST NOT refresh it on re-delegation. Effective value is the minimum of this field and any stricter grant, policy, deployment, or profile override. Defaults to 86400000 ms (24h). See zh/authz/capabilities.md §10.1.

bottom_escalation_after_ms.description: Optional timeout after which unresolved bottom diagnostics should be escalated to recovery governance. Expiry does not choose a winner automatically.

cell_lattices.description: Optional Realm-specific lattice declarations for extension cell families.

allOf.$comment: single_did notary profiles bind one DID as the primary notary. controller_organization / recovery_controller_organizations / recovery_members are required ONLY when the deployment can derive a controlling organization (see notary.controller_organization 'when ... can derive it'; decisions/0003 §7 — personal / orgless Realms legitimately omit them and fall back to per-user recovery). When a controller_organization IS declared, an explicit recovery-notary diversity path MUST accompany it. The distinct-controller arithmetic stays semantic/reducer validation because JSON Schema cannot compare DID-controller derivations across resolver evidence.
Org-controlled single_did Realms MUST declare the recovery-notary diversity path alongside the controlling organization.

Threshold notary committees must declare their equivocation culprit-attribution mode at Realm create time. The arithmetic rule (quorum_intersection iff 2*threshold > members.length) is reducer/conformance validation; see notary.forensic_attribution $comment.

Principal control Realms are ordinary ak.schema.realm.v1 objects, but the profile discriminator must be closed at schema level: fields.purpose and schema_refs must appear together, the Realm MUST be MLS-backed, and both encryption floors MUST be pinned to e2ee_required (key-management §4.1 / §5.0.1, realm-and-space §2.8.1). There is no plaintext-floor PCR in v1.
The inverse guard prevents a profile-tagged Realm from omitting the machine-readable purpose discriminator, and pins the encryption floors symmetrically with the forward guard.

Direct Conversation Realms are ordinary Collaboration Realms with a closed machine role. The discriminator and profile must appear together; create-locked Realm security fields are pinned here while the exact-two membership, participant identity, no-Space and main-Strand rules are reducer/profile invariants.
The inverse Direct Conversation guard prevents a profile-tagged ordinary Realm from omitting its collaboration role discriminator.
Principal Control and Direct Conversation are mutually exclusive Realm roles.
content_scheme is only meaningful for MLS-backed Realms. Plaintext or external encryption Realms MUST NOT declare an MLS content envelope scheme.

recipient_id.description: Realm-unique stable id for this recovery recipient.

principal_id.description: Principal holding the RRK private key. SHOULD resolve to an Organization Principal for org_recovery_key/threshold; MAY be a personal principal for personal Realms.

verification_method.description: Reference to a verification method in principal_id's DID Document designated by an active ArkretRealmHistoryRecoveryKey service entry (identity/identity-did.md §8.3). The RRK HPKE public key; history-recovery domain, separate from the backup-HPKE key derived per key-management.md §3.3.

controller_organization.description: Organization DID controlling this recovery recipient, when derivable; receiver MAY use it to verify org attribution.

sync_endpoint.description: Realm-authorized shared service binding. service_id is the stable business identity; service_resolution supplies independently verifiable current route material. A bare endpoint URL is never an authority root.

cell_role.description: Semantic role declared by Realm schema. Security-root roles are restricted to control-plane lattice semantics by the allOf rules below.

plane.description: CBA plane for this cell family. authorization_root / policy_root / notary_root / membership / lifecycle MUST be control. Ordinary content / draft / cosmetic cells SHOULD be data unless sealed=true.

sealed.description: Opt-in control-plane finality for an otherwise data-like cell family. When true, plane MUST be control. A data-like family reused as an authorization input for any risk_tier=high capability MUST set sealed=true; ordinary authorization_root declarations are already required to use plane=control.

initial_value.description: Optional cell schema initial value (cas_register only). When defined, the cas_register `join` algorithm initialises `current` to this value (rather than null) before applying any Move. Combined with a `head_eq: <initial_value>` predicate on the first set Move, this implements singleton-once-set cells via the empty sentinel pattern. See event-auth-state-resolution.md §9.3.1.

sentinel_writers.description: Optional companion to `initial_value` (cas_register only). When `initial_value` is declared, set ops whose effect equals the sentinel are rejected by default (initial_value_reserved). Listing event_kinds here permits those event_kinds to write the sentinel back — typically the cleanup event_kind in a singleton-once-set / explicit-reset workflow. Capability authorization remains a separate independent check. See event-auth-state-resolution.md §9.3.1.

allOf.$comment: Security-root roles are always control-plane.
sealed=true is the explicit data-to-control opt-in.
initial_value is only defined for cas_register (see event-auth-state-resolution.md §9.3.1). Other lattices reject the field.

sentinel_writers is the companion of initial_value; it only makes sense on a cas_register cell that has declared initial_value. Reject declarations on other lattices, and reject declarations on cas_register cells that lack initial_value (since there is no sentinel to authorise writing back).

schemas/recovery-authority.schema.json.title: Arkret Recovery Completion Carriers
schemas/recovery-authority.schema.json.description: Closed recovery completion attestation and Standard-grant issuance carriers. Device recovery is authorized by the accepted PCR recovery policy; an optional DID-root proof is only one explicitly enabled factor.

canonical_public_material.description: Typed public material plus the exact canonical bytes persisted by the coordinator. canonical_bytes_base64url MUST decode to the canonical JSON/CBOR representation of value and digest MUST recompute over those bytes.

initial_session.description: The Standard grant to issue after recovery. device_id MUST equal the attested replacement device and the RFC 7638 thumbprint of session_public_key MUST equal the Bound AccountHandoff and HTTP DPoP key.

canonical_request_digest.description: SHA-256 of JCS(request object with only canonical_request_digest omitted). The Bound AccountHandoff authorization and RFC 9449 HTTP DPoP proof authenticate the account and holder outside this closed business body.

recovery_completion_attestation.description: Coordinator-signed proof created atomically with the durable completed RecoveryTransaction. It is the only offline completion evidence accepted by the Account Authority when issuing the post-recovery Standard grant.

schemas/recovery-policy.schema.json.title: Arkret Recovery Policy
schemas/recovery-policy.schema.json.description: Normative grammar for a principal's PCR recovery policy. Bound to one Principal Authority Instance through signed control events; receivers reject recovery and pcr_recovery device authorization whose proof family, threshold or optional DID-root factor is not allowed by the currently accepted policy.

version.description: Monotonically increasing counter scoped by principal_id. Receivers MUST reject a publish whose version is not strictly greater than the currently accepted policy.

supersedes.description: Predecessor policy_id. Null only for the genesis policy of a principal.

trust_domain.description: Deployment-scope trust domain identifier the policy applies to. Cross-domain proofs MUST fail.

allowed_proof_kinds.description: Which proof families authorize PCR device re-entry. did_root is optional and revocable; omitting it guarantees current DID control alone cannot recover this authority instance.

publication_authorization_rules.description: Signed deterministic projection inputs for PCR recovery publication. Exactly one rule per allowed proof kind; a revoked policy carries an empty array.

threshold.description: Threshold-recovery configuration. Required when allowed_proof_kinds contains 'threshold_recovery'.

k.description: Minimum share count required to reconstruct the recovery secret. MUST be >= 2; threshold=1 is forbidden because it collapses to a single-holder bearer.

n.description: Total number of shares issued. MUST equal shares.length and MUST be >= k.

vss_root_commitment.description: Optional VSS root commitment binding all shares' polynomial commitments. SHOULD be present for Feldman / Pedersen schemes.

reshare_policy.description: Proactive secret sharing / re-share cadence. Holders MUST be able to refresh shares without reconstructing the secret. Implementations SHOULD re-share at least once per `max_share_age_seconds`.

device_quorum.description: Device-quorum configuration. Required when allowed_proof_kinds contains 'device_quorum'.

authorization_verification_method.description: Exact verification method authorized by this accepted PCR recovery-policy rule. DID-root methods are valid only for proof_kind=did_root; service and quorum rules derive from their own accepted policy basis.

trusted_recovery_services.description: Recovery services explicitly declared in the principal's DID Document (or sovereign trust seal). Required when allowed_proof_kinds contains 'trusted_recovery_service'.

recovery_keys.description: Recovery signing keys this principal authorizes for 'recovery_unlock' proofs and for the single publication signature produced after 'threshold_recovery' secret reconstruction. Each entry binds a verification method (24-word Recovery Key derived signing key, or hardware-released equivalent) to the principal. A recovery_unlock proof's recovery_secret_ref, and a threshold_recovery publication rule's issuer set, MUST resolve to active entries in this array; the proof signature MUST verify under the selected entry's public key. Required when allowed_proof_kinds contains either 'recovery_unlock' or 'threshold_recovery'. See identity/key-management.md §7.5.2 and crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §14.4 / §15.

recovery_key_agreements.description: Backup-only HPKE recipient keys. These entries are cryptographically and semantically distinct from recovery_keys[] signing keys. key-backup encryption.recipient_key_ref resolves only here in the envelope's referenced accepted policy, never to a DID Document-only key agreement or a recovery signing verification_method.

approval_requirement.description: Two-person rule / cooldown enforcement layered on top of cryptographic proofs.

cooldown_seconds.description: Minimum wall-clock window between recovery announcement and effective key change. Receivers MUST reject control-stream Events whose accepted_at is earlier than announcement_at + cooldown_seconds.

announcement_required.description: When true, recovery MUST be announced on the principal control stream and visible to authorized devices before effective key change.

audit.description: Where the recovery strand MUST emit auditable records (recovery announcement, holder participation, completion receipt).

receipt_required.description: When true, recovery completion MUST produce a ak.schema.recovery_receipt.v1 record.

verification_method.description: DID URL identifying the authorized issuer: founding device after genesis; current-generation accepted device for later updates; identity root for re-anchor; or a coordinator satisfying the superseded policy quorum. Receivers resolve this semantic authority from accepted principal-control state, not from arbitrary DID Document membership.

recovery_policy_set_payload.description: Canonical ak.policy.set payload for recovery-policy publication. policy_id MUST equal value.policy_id; state and reason are intentionally unavailable on this operation.

recovery_policy_publish_request.description: Recovery policy publication through the ordinary first-publication Event ingress. Cross-field validation additionally requires payload.policy_id=value.policy_id and actor/scope/lease to bind value.principal_id's Principal Control Realm.

recovery_key_entry.description: A recovery signing key the principal authorizes for 'recovery_unlock' proofs and post-reconstruction 'threshold_recovery' publication signatures. The verification_method is the stable recovery_secret_ref and publication-rule issuer; public_key_multibase carries the actual signing public key so principals do not depend on a DID Document verificationMethod. key_agreement_ref pairs this signer with a distinct backup-only recovery_key_agreements[] entry.

verification_method.description: DID URL (e.g. `did:webvh:...#recovery-1`) identifying this recovery signing key. This is the value a recovery_unlock proof carries in recovery_secret_ref / verification_method and a threshold_recovery publication rule carries in issuers[].verification_method; it MUST be unique within recovery_keys[].

public_key_multibase.description: Multikey for the recovery proof signature algorithm. MUST NOT equal or be converted into the paired HPKE key.

key_agreement_ref.description: MUST identify exactly one non-revoked recovery_key_agreements[] entry in the same policy.

signature_algorithm.description: Signature algorithm used by the recovery key. Values mirror active signature-alg-registry rows; ML-DSA-65 use additionally requires the corresponding PQ-capable implementation profile.

not_before.description: Earliest instant this recovery key may authorize a recovery_unlock proof or threshold_recovery publication signature.

expires_at.description: Instant after which this recovery key MUST NOT authorize a recovery_unlock proof or threshold_recovery publication signature.

revoked_at.description: When set, the entry is revoked from this instant onward and MUST NOT satisfy any recovery_unlock proof or threshold_recovery publication signature whose binding time is at or after it.

recovery_key_agreement_entry.description: Dedicated X25519 HPKE recipient for key-backup envelopes. It cannot verify recovery_unlock or authorize DID/Event operations.

key_agreement_ref.description: Stable identifier used by key-backup encryption.recipient_key_ref.

recovery_policy_summary.description: Read-model summary of the currently accepted recovery policy. `policy` carries the original ak.schema.recovery_policy.v1 object when the service can disclose it to the caller.

acceptance_basis.description: Immutable accepted CBA basis whose control state commits this exact recovery policy version.

recovery_policy_ref.description: Convenience tuple equivalent to `{policy_id, policy_version: version}`. When present, it MUST match policy_id/version.

policy.description: Full accepted ak.schema.recovery_policy.v1 object. Omitted only when the caller is authorized to learn that a policy exists but not to receive holder/share details.

control_frontier.description: Optional principal control-stream frontier under which the active policy was observed.

recovery_policy_active_outcome.description: Response for ak.root.identity.recovery_policy.resource.get. `active_policy=null` is a successful read meaning no accepted recovery policy currently exists for the resolved principal.

principal_id.description: Resolved principal. Required when the request used an explicit principal_id selector; SHOULD be present on all authenticated reads.

recovery_policy_ref.description: Convenience tuple for the active policy. MUST be absent or null-equivalent when active_policy is null, and MUST match active_policy.policy_id/version when active_policy is present.

recovery_policy_publish_outcome.description: Response for ak.root.identity.recovery_policy.command.publish after accepting a ak.schema.recovery_policy.v1 publish or rotation.

acceptance_basis.description: Immutable accepted CBA basis whose control state commits this exact recovery policy version.

holder.description: DID of the share holder. MAY be a user, a hardware module identified by did:key, or a custodial service. The holder DID does NOT inherit any business capability of the principal.

schemas/recovery-receipt.schema.json.title: Arkret Recovery Receipt
schemas/recovery-receipt.schema.json.description: Signed completion receipt for a principal recovery strand. Bound to the recovery_session_id, identity model, model generation, accepted device authorization path, every proof, backup unlock, and MLS Welcome replay action. Formal recovery receipts are signed only after the recovering device has been accepted via ak.device.authorize; pre-authorization failures use server outcome/audit evidence instead. See crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §15.

transaction_id.description: RecoveryTransaction that reserved this receipt id. It MUST equal the transaction whose binding.terminal_receipt_id is this receipt_id, which is what lets a verifier holding only the receipt resolve the authorizing transaction; binding.terminal_receipt_id alone is one-way. See zh/identity/security-transactions.md section 2.

transaction_request_digest.description: Stable request_digest of the RecoveryTransaction. It is signed by the replacement device so the terminal attestation cannot be rebound to a different transaction plan even if an identifier is substituted.

prepared_plan_digest.description: Digest of the closed typed prepared_plan stored by the RecoveryTransaction. It MUST equal transaction.prepared_plan_digest and is signed to prevent substituting different prepared bytes under the same reserved ids.

recovery_session_id.description: Stable session identifier used by every proof transcript, backup decrypt proof, and MLS Welcome replay during this recovery. A byte-identical resubmission of an already accepted receipt is idempotent and MUST return the stored receipt; only a SECOND, DIFFERENT receipt for the same session id and principal is a conflict. Rejecting the byte-identical replay would make a lost response unrecoverable, which zh/identity/security-transactions.md section 1 invariants 3 and 4 forbid.

recovery_authority_kind.description: did_root is valid only when the accepted PCR policy explicitly enabled that optional factor.

previous_model_generation_ref.description: PCR device generation snapshotted at recovery-session creation.

result_model_generation_ref.description: Accepted monotonic PCR device generation after completion.

proof_digest.description: Canonical-JSON digest of the proof transcript used to satisfy the active recovery policy. Auditors recompute against the originating proof event to verify.

quorum_participant_count.description: Required for device_quorum and threshold_recovery; equals the number of participating members / shares.

share_ids.description: When kind=threshold_recovery, the share_ids that participated. MUST be a subset of the active policy's shares[].

welcome_count.description: Number of MLS Welcomes successfully replayed for the recovering device.

outcome_reason_code.description: Free-form reason code; MUST be present when outcome != 'completed'.

verification_method.description: DID URL of the new_device_id's accepted device key. Receivers MUST resolve it through the principal control stream and verify that ak.device.authorize for new_device_id was accepted before this receipt was signed; service keys and unauthorised fresh-device keys MUST NOT sign a formal recovery_receipt.

signature_algorithm.description: v1 fixes the recovery-strand replacement device possession proof to Ed25519 (zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md sections 5.2 and 15). The three-algorithm set in zh/identity/key-management.md section 7.9 belongs to recovery_policy.recovery_keys[].alg and MUST NOT be reused as a reason to widen this one.

schemas/recovery-session.schema.json.title: Arkret Recovery Session
schemas/recovery-session.schema.json.description: Wire contract for the device recovery session state machine. The root object is the recovery session state shape; request body/result helper shapes and kind-specific recovery proof transcripts live in $defs. See zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §15.

challenge.description: base64url(no padding) encoding of 256 bits from a CSPRNG. The value is single-use and bound to one recovery_session_id.
