identity_model.description: The v1 base recovery model: an accepted PCR recovery policy directly authorizes the next device generation. Current DID control is not implicit.

proof_digest.description: Digest of the canonical recovery proof transcript that satisfied this session.

publication_authority_context.description: Server-snapshotted accepted PCR recovery authority for publishing the re-anchor unit. It never grants the replacement device a generic lease issuer role.

current_device_generation_ref.description: Reducer-managed PCR device generation snapshotted at session creation.

registry_head.description: Digest of the accepted identity-registry head snapshot.

publication_authority_context_digest.description: SHA-256 of JCS(publication_authority_context). Recovery proof transcripts and RecoveryTransaction session snapshots bind this exact digest.

transaction_id.description: Unique durable RecoveryTransaction bound by CAS after verification. Absent until transaction create succeeds.

rejection_reason_code.description: Closed enum. proof_failed: proof verification failures reached the server policy limit; operator_rejected: explicit operator/admin rejection; risk_policy: server risk policy rejection; superseded: replaced by a newer recovery session for the same principal/device.

expires_at.description: Session expiration. Default TTL is 900 seconds; deployments MAY shorten it and MUST NOT lengthen it unless a future recovery_policy field explicitly permits the override.

created_at.description: Recovery session creation/signing time. This is the created_at value used in the recovery proof transcript.

expected_recovery_policy_ref.description: Optional client CAS hint. Servers MUST snapshot the currently accepted policy; if this hint is present and differs, the request fails with recovery_policy_mismatch.

challenge.description: Echo of the server-issued session challenge. Mismatch fails as recovery_session_challenge_mismatch.

verification_method.description: Current DID-root verification method, accepted only when the frozen PCR recovery policy explicitly enables this revocable factor.

recovery_secret_ref.description: DID URL or recovery-policy key ref for the recovery key entry authorized at the session's created_at.

unlock_commitment.description: Public binding hash over the session transcript and recovery_secret_ref. Possession is proven by signature; this commitment prevents proof-shell substitution.

attestation_ref.description: Reference to service attestation evidence when required by the active recovery policy.

transcript_digest.description: Digest of the holder's share release transcript bound to share_id, holder, recovery_session_id, requesting_device_id, audience, and issued_at. For threshold_recovery / recovery_unlock the requesting device may be a not-yet-authorized new device; holder validation binds proof-of-possession and the recovery session instead of requiring an existing device record.

proof.description: Kind-specific recovery proof. Receivers reconstruct the canonical transcript from stored session state and the proof body, then verify that the active recovery policy allows this proof kind and its threshold/service/share constraints.

model_generation_ref.description: Accepted PCR generation fenced by this recovery. DID method versioning is orthogonal.

created_at.description: Session creation/signing time, not client proof creation time.

generic_recovery_transcript.description: Canonical transcript field set shared by recovery_unlock, device_quorum, trusted_recovery_service, and threshold_recovery proofs before adding kind-specific proof_body. Producers and receivers MUST bind exactly this session tuple.

model_generation_ref.description: Accepted DID versionId that anchors the current device generation.

proof_body.description: The selected proof object with signature bytes omitted where the kind-specific verification rule says so.

scope_circle_id.description: Optional intra-Realm Circle (models/circle.md) defining this Relation fact's effective scope, supplied in the submit payload. For confidential_discussion_of it points to the private Strand's Circle. For structural relations the resulting effective_scope MUST NOT be wider than the narrowest participating endpoint scope (circle.md §6.1). Sidecar context mappings are native sidecar.context cells, not Relation objects.

effective_scope.description: Read-only immutable effective scope of this Relation fact, materialized from the accepted Event.scope_ref after the receiver verifies it against scope_circle_id and endpoint pre-state (circle.md §6.1-§6.2). For structural relations it MUST NOT be wider than the narrowest participating endpoint scope. It remains immutable across any later scope rebind and MUST NOT appear in actor-supplied content payload (reason=effective_scope_reducer_managed).

relation_kind.description: Relation semantic. The standard kind vocabulary (kind list, cardinality class, truth-source class, weak_semantic flag) is machine-indexed in artifacts/registry/relation-kind-registry.json; detailed dedupe/scope/conflict semantics in models/relation.md §3-§6. Cross-Realm constraint: structural relations 'contains' and 'belongs_to' MUST NOT cross Realm (resolved from_ref and to_ref MUST share the same realm_id); weak_semantic=true kinds per the registry MAY cross Realm subject to two-sided authorization. Stays a free string so extension profiles can add kinds; unregistered kinds are opaque edges (unknown_relation_kind), never container/visibility semantics.

rank.description: Top-level rank string for ordered relations (e.g. contains-list-strand position). Encoding follows conformance/encoding.md §9. Aligned with Space.rank so all rank-bearing canonical objects expose rank at the top level instead of fields.rank.

fields.description: Edge metadata. MUST NOT contain a 'rank' key — rank moved to the top level in v1 to align with Space.rank.

state.description: Relation state. 'tombstoned' covers both deletion and redaction; the originating reason is preserved on the ak.relation.tombstone / ak.redaction event, not on the materialized object.

state_changed_at.description: Reducer-derived timestamp of the most recent state transition. MUST be set when state != 'active'; MUST be the created_at of the corresponding ak.relation.tombstone / redaction Event. Aligns with Space.state_changed_at and the common-fields rule in models/common-fields.md §3.

object_ref.description: Typed canonical reference. Allowed kinds: realm, space, actor_profile, strand, message, morph, relation, event, view, blob metadata ID, content-addressed blob ref (active digest suites per artifacts/registry/digest-suite-registry.json; v1: sha256 / blake3), or DID. Space is a valid Relation endpoint (board/list containers, e.g. board --contains--> list). The blob ref suite set is aligned with blob.schema.json and notification.schema.json so any content-addressed blob ref accepted in those schemas is also accepted as a Relation endpoint.

relation_conflict_diagnostic.description: Projection-only conflict diagnostic emitted for deterministic_winner losers and require_review output. reducer_input MUST be false; MUST NOT be treated as canonical event bytes or dedupe authority. See zh/models/relation.md §6.

dedupe_key.description: Canonical projection of the dedupe key under which these candidates collided.

winner.description: The deterministic winner (event_digest bytewise-greatest per the single canonical tie-break rule, zh/conformance/encoding.md §4.2), or omitted-equivalent for require_review where no canonical winner is projected.

losers.description: Conflict losers retained for audit and explicit repair. Bounded by the conflict fanout limit (v1 public profile: 16 total candidates including the winner).

event_digest.description: Canonical signed Event digest (<digest-suite>:<hex>), the bytewise tie-break key.

reason.description: Optional reason code for this candidate's disposition (e.g. relation_conflict_fanout_exceeded).

object_ref.description: Canonical object reference. Acceptable typed-id kinds match the v1 resource selector kind enum (see resource-selector-grammar.md §3.1). Notably MUST NOT include 'actor_profile' (use the 'actor' selector with did pattern), nor non-canonical 'board' / 'list' / 'card' / 'subject' / 'room' kinds — board / list / swimlane / calendar bucket are Space objects and MUST use the 'space' kind together with the 'allowed_space_kinds' constraint to restrict which Space kinds the grant covers.

actor_id.description: Concrete principal / service / agent did_core_id. v1 forbids actor:*; actor selectors MUST NOT use a wildcard subject.

match_scope.description: Selector match breadth. exact matches only the named resource; children matches immediate children; subtree matches descendants including nested children; realm_wide is valid only when realm_id is present and limits matching to the named Realm. The normative algorithm is zh/authz/resource-selector-grammar.md ?6.

allOf.$comment: resource-selector-grammar.md §3.1: notification / read_cursor selectors are realm-scoped and the object part is *-only (notification:<realm>:* / read_cursor:<realm>:*). A bare {"kind":"read_cursor"} with no realm_id would otherwise match every principal's read cursors across all Realms (see C04-07). Force realm_id and forbid a precise object id (no notification_id / read_cursor_id field exists; selection is realm-wide *-only).
resource-selector-grammar.md ?3.1/?4.2/?6: space and circle selectors are Realm-scoped in v1; wildcard space/circle selectors MUST carry realm_id to avoid cross-Realm authorization expansion.

Realm-local resource kinds always carry realm_id, including exact-id selectors. This prevents a schema-valid bare kind selector from matching every Realm and keeps authorization scope explicit in signed grant bytes.

resource-selector-grammar.md §4.8/§8.1: actor:* is forbidden and an actor selector MUST carry a concrete principal DID. Force actor_id present so a bare {"kind":"actor"} is rejected at the schema layer rather than only at the reducer (selector_actor_wildcard_forbidden).

schemas/sdk-conformance-claim.schema.jso.title: Arkret SDK Conformance Claim
schemas/sdk-conformance-claim.schema.jso.description: Signed, artifact-bound SDK release claim. The proof covers RFC 8785 JCS bytes of the object with proof omitted, prefixed by the UTF-8 domain separator arkret-sdk-conformance-claim-v1 followed by LF.

build_variants.description: Optional per-build profile inventory for source or multi-variant SDK distributions. Variant IDs MUST be unique and each feature_set_digest binds the exact normalized feature/configuration set used to produce that variant.

schemas/seal-transparency.schema.json.title: Arkret SealTransparency
schemas/seal-transparency.schema.json.description: Seal transparency wire objects (authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.4): an append-only log entry binding one accepted Seal tuple, and an independent auditor attestation over a log range. The log makes split-view attacks (showing different Seal chains to different receivers) detectable: an operator must either publish consistently or fork the log, and a log fork is provable from two signed entries with the same log_index. Top-level object is a log entry; auditor attestations use #/$defs/auditor_attestation.

log_id.description: Stable identifier of the transparency log (operator URL, DID, or registry name).

log_index.description: Zero-based append-only position. Two differently-signed entries with the same (log_id, log_index) are a provable log fork.

prev_entry_digest.description: Digest of the previous entry's canonical bytes (hash chain). null only for log_index 0.

auditor_attestation.description: Signed statement by an independent auditor (peer Realm or third party) that it verified the log range [from_index, to_index]: append-only consistency, Seal signature validity, and control/completeness monotonicity along every Seal DAG predecessor edge represented in the range. Log-index-adjacent concurrent leaves are not compared. A client accepts this as verified v1 evidence only when a concrete operation/profile carries it and the deployment policy's required attestation count is met.

head_entry_digest.description: Digest of the entry at to_index, binding the attested range head.

checks.description: All checks MUST be true. dag_edges_verified means monotonic checks were performed along every represented predecessor edge, not by log_index adjacency; an auditor that cannot assert a check MUST NOT issue the attestation.

payload_digest.description: Hash of canonical entry / attestation bytes with the signature field omitted.

schemas/seal.schema.json.title: Arkret Seal
schemas/seal.schema.json.description: Wire shape of a Arkret CBA Seal. It finalizes only control-plane Events. `delta[]` is the canonical set of new control-plane event_digest values introduced by this Seal; cumulative coverage is derived recursively as covered_set(S)=set(S.delta) union covered_set(predecessor_refs[]). `control_event_set_root` authenticates that recursive covered_set and is used for basis, inclusion and non-membership proofs. Optional data_* roots are observational only and MUST NOT gate DataEvents. Identity & signature model (see zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md §6): the typed `id` (`ak:seal:<algo>:<hex>`) is content-derived — its hex equals H(seal_canonical_bytes) under the Realm digest_algorithm. Seal canonical bytes are the canonical JSON of every signed top-level field EXCEPT id and notary_signature. The `notary_signature` is NOT part of canonical bytes. Receivers MUST recompute H(seal_canonical_bytes) and verify the notary signature over the same bytes.

id.description: Content-derived typed reference. hex part MUST equal H(seal_canonical_bytes) under the Realm digest_algorithm, where seal_canonical_bytes is the canonical JSON of every signed body field EXCEPT `id` and `notary_signature`. Receivers MUST recompute and verify; mismatch → digest_mismatch. NEVER include `id` in the hash input — that would create a self-reference.

delta.description: Canonical bytewise-sorted set of new control-plane event_digest values introduced by this Seal. DataEvent digests MUST NOT appear here. Receivers MUST reject the Seal if any delta entry is already covered by a predecessor, if any entry is not a known valid Control Move digest, or if the list is not canonical sorted and duplicate-free.

control_event_set_root.description: Authenticated root over the recursive covered_set of this Seal. Default construction is RFC6962 Merkle root over canonical bytewise-sorted covered_set(S); inclusion uses Merkle audit path and non-membership uses sorted-neighbor proof. The root is not computed over delta[] alone.

state_root.description: Merkle root of control-plane cell state only.

completeness_root.description: Control-plane per-actor interval / chain-head completeness commitment. It does not prove absence of unknown actors.

notary_seq.description: Per-signer or committee slot sequence used for equivocation detection. Same signer and same realm_id MUST NOT sign two different canonical Seal bodies with the same notary_seq.

data_view_root.description: Optional observational root of KeyView records keyed by data cell id. It is not a DataEvent admission gate.

data_event_set_root.description: Optional observational root over DataEvent digests seen in this seal window. Missing DataEvents are not invalid.

coverage_scope.description: Optional observational coverage declaration for data_view_root / data_event_set_root. The object is intentionally closed only by deployment profiles; core verifiers treat it as signed diagnostic material.

covered_event_digests.description: Optional compaction materialization of the full recursive covered_set(S), canonical bytewise-sorted and duplicate-free. When present, receivers MUST verify it equals set(delta) union all predecessor covered sets and that control_event_set_root is computed over this exact set. Non-compaction Seals normally omit it.

previous_state_root.description: Hash-algorithm transition only: present iff this Seal is a Transition Seal under ak.profile.hash_transition.v1. It commits the governance view before the transition Move is applied, computed with previous_digest_algorithm. state_root commits the post-transition governance view with the new suite. See event-auth-state-resolution.md §9.3.2.

previous_digest_algorithm.description: Profile id of the previous hash algorithm. Required iff previous_state_root is present; absent on non-transition Seals.

notary_signature.description: Signature over seal_canonical_bytes (every signed body field EXCEPT `id` and `notary_signature`). MUST NOT enter the canonical bytes itself — signatures never sign themselves. Seal is not an Event Envelope, so its signature uses the generic non-Event proof field `payload_digest`; that value MUST equal H(seal_canonical_bytes) under the Realm digest_algorithm. Event Envelope proofs use `event_digest` instead.

sealed_at.description: Normative notary commit timestamp covered by the Seal signature transcript. It is the time input for revocation_freshness_window_ms, recovery_witness_freshness_window_ms, proposal_intake_sla_ms, and reducer-derived projection timestamps. It MUST be >= every predecessor Seal.sealed_at. A value beyond verifier wall time + hard_future_skew_ms produces non-terminal seal_deferred_future_skew and MUST be retried as the clock advances; it is not a permanent rejection or a lattice winner input.

verification_method.description: DID URL of the signing key. Bare DID is not valid for signatures because verifiers need a stable verification method, not only a controller DID.

payload_digest.description: Hash of seal_canonical_bytes for this non-Event Seal signature. Do not rename to event_digest: event_digest is reserved for Event Envelope proofs.

leakage_class.description: Machine-readable search leakage class. ak.profile.search.blind_index.v1 uses deterministic_token; ak.profile.search.forward_private.v1 requires forward_private; access_hiding is reserved for explicit PIR/ORAM-backed profiles.

token_rotation_cadence_ms.description: Maximum intended interval between search token generations for profiles that rotate index keys or OPRF blinds.

schemas/security-transaction.schema.json.title: Arkret Security Transaction
schemas/security-transaction.schema.json.description: Closed durable RecoveryTransaction and SecurityRotationTransaction resource. Binding, prepared plan and accepted outputs are separate protocol states.

prepared_plan_digest.description: Digest of canonical prepared_plan bytes. Implementations MUST recompute it and persist both bytes and typed value before the first side effect.

attestation_digest.description: SHA-256 of JCS(artifact). The coordinator MUST recompute it from the received typed artifact bytes.

prepared_event_submission_batch.description: Exact typed account-client Event publication batch and its persisted canonical bytes.

prepared_event_unit.description: Exact typed Event submit request and persisted canonical bytes. A PCR recovery unit contains reanchor plus replacement authorize for the same authority instance/session/generation CAS; candidate possession is verified through the unit-local overlay before mutation and never by resolving current human DID.

request.description: Typed value that MUST independently validate against request_schema. The indirection keeps the transaction schema acyclic while preserving a closed schema identity.

backup_rotations.description: Exactly secret_storage then mls_history in canonical backup_kind order.

erase_confirmation_digest.description: SHA-256 of the non-circular JCS projection {domain=ak.backup_series_erase_confirmation_preimage.v1, transaction_id, series=backup_rotations}.

local_commit_digest.description: SHA-256 of the non-circular JCS projection {domain=ak.security_rotation_local_commit_preimage.v1, transaction_id, new_secret_commitment, backup_rotations}.

backup_rotations.description: Prepared material for the same canonical two backup_kind entries as binding.backup_rotations.

erase_confirmation_digest.description: Must equal the binding's non-circular erase confirmation projection digest.

local_commit_digest.description: Must equal the binding's non-circular local commit projection digest.

schemas/service-describe.schema.json.title: Arkret Service Describe
schemas/service-describe.schema.json.description: Canonical service describe response returned by ak.server.read.describe and per-surface describe operations. It combines stable service metadata (service_id, service_kind, protocol_version, profiles, bindings, auth, limits, plaintext visibility and rate-limit policy) with claim-level partitions: implemented_features, claimed_profiles, verified_profiles, experimental_features and compat_surfaces. The `supported_operations` field MUST list endpoint-callable operation_ids. Constraint: when `development_mode=true`, the service MUST NOT advertise any `verified_profiles` entry, and clients MUST verify the referenced verification artifacts before treating verified_profiles as production conformance. See service-surface.md §3.0.

service_id.description: Stable did_core_id of the service making this describe claim. It cannot be resolved without service_resolution or another verified ServiceResolutionRecord.

service_resolution.description: Read-only current full_id commitment for this service role. Describe is a second-hop endpoint confirmation surface, not a did_core_id resolver: callers already need a candidate URL before fetching it and MUST verify the full_id projection, method evidence and endpoint reverse binding before updating a route cache.

trust_domain.description: Deployment-scope trust domain for this service. Receivers use it as the canonical receive-context replay boundary for cross-deployment proofs and federation transactions.

service_kind.description: One logical role this service plays on the wire. Each ServiceDescribe document describes exactly one role; co-located roles sharing a public binding use separate role-scoped responses selected by GET /_arkret/describe?service_kind=<registered-id>. The value space is registry/service-kind-registry.json filtered to active rows whose valid_in contains service_describe.

supported_reducer_profiles.description: Registered Realm reducer profiles this service can execute. This is a runtime capability set, not a conformance claim and not a selected Realm profile.

profile_bindings.description: Profile-specific carrier declarations keyed by profile id. A profile that mandates one interoperable private carrier must bind it here rather than relying on a product-local route.

supported_operations.description: operation_ids that this endpoint can actually be invoked with. Element format SHOULD match the canonical operation_registry ids (e.g. `ak.self.events.command.submit`).

supported_bindings.description: Transport binding declarations for this service.

supported_features.description: Feature identifiers (`ak.feature.*`) the service supports. Distinct from profile claims.

calendar_tzdb_versions.description: IANA TZDB release tags this service can execute for calendar schedules, taken from calendar-timezone-registry.json. Required when the service claims a calendar profile. A schedule whose signed tzdb_version is absent here MUST fail closed with calendar_tzdb_mismatch or project its instants as unresolved; the service MUST NOT fall back to a nearby or newer release.

auth_metadata.description: Authentication and session metadata needed by clients before calling protected operations.

methods.description: Authentication methods offered for this principal/account surface. Methods describe proof providers, standard discovery, and the proof kind accepted by the Account Authority. Arkret gate/account routing is always derived from account_authority.

limits.description: Operational limits such as body size, batch size, TTL, pagination or retention bounds.

mls_governance_proof.description: Required with these exact v1 interoperability bounds when supported_operations contains ak.self.events.read.mls_governance_proof.

plaintext_visibility.description: Plaintext boundary declaration. Omission is not allowed: callers use this object to decide whether the service may be registered as plaintext-visible. An empty object means the service claims no plaintext classes; Realm plaintext_visible_services entries MUST match non-empty data_classes here.

data_classes.description: Closed machine-checkable classes of plaintext or reversible derived content this service is implemented to receive.

max_visibility.description: Maximum plaintext visibility class the service claims it can receive. Omitted is treated as none unless data_classes is non-empty.

privacy_derivation.description: Machine-readable privacy-preserving identifier derivation claims. Secret material is never published here; only profile and epoch metadata needed for audit and rotation checks.

secret_scope.description: The HMAC salt/pepper is unique to this service context and MUST NOT be shared across Principal Servers, organizations, or push routes.

salt_epoch_id.description: Opaque public epoch label for the active secret. This is not the secret salt value.

receive_policy_constraints.description: Deployment/admin upper bound for subject-private invite/contact receive policies. Principal Servers SHOULD expose this in describe so clients can show which user reachability preferences are capped by server policy.

rate_limit_policy_id.description: Identifier for a cacheable, verifiable rate-limit policy object with the same minimum fields as rate_limit_policy. See zh/sync/api-conventions.md §8.

rate_limit_policy.description: Inline rate-limit policy. If the service can return rate_limited, entries[] MUST expose at least endpoint or operation_id, rate_limit_scope, a window/limit tuple or a retry hint; an empty entries[] explicitly means no predictable endpoint-level rate limit beyond generic abuse protection.

egress_network_policy.description: Coarse outbound-network policy for SSRF protection. Public describe MAY omit sensitive allowlist entries; authenticated operator describe MAY return the complete policy. Normative semantics are defined in zh/sync/api-conventions.md §11.2.

resource_kinds.description: Directory-service resource classes indexed by ak.find.directory.read.describe. Required when service_kind=directory_service.

discovery_profiles.description: Directory discovery profiles and extension profile ids advertised by ak.find.directory.read.describe. Required when service_kind=directory_service.

private_contact_discovery.description: Complete machine-readable configuration for ak.private_contact_discovery.v1. Required when supported_operations contains ak.find.directory.read.private_contact_discovery; clients MUST fail closed if any field is absent or unsupported.

oprf_mode.description: RFC 9497 modeVOPRF (0x01), distinct from the ciphersuite identifier.

public_key.description: Canonical unpadded base64url encoding of the active 32-byte ristretto255 VOPRF public key. Decoders additionally validate the group encoding and reject the identity element.

key_epoch.description: Epoch accepted for new blind requests. A batch admitted under an older epoch remains bound to its pinned key and cached outcome until its advertised completion TTL expires.

batch_item_count.description: Exact cardinality required for blinded_elements, evaluated_elements, derived_prefixes, hit_bitmap and, when enabled, handoff_stubs. Clients create indistinguishable dummy elements before sending the blind request.

proof_shape.description: One 64-byte RFC 9497 batched DLEQ proof covers the entire fixed-size batch.

handoff_stubs_mode.description: Shape is fixed for the advertised key epoch. always means handoff_stubs is present at every match position with dummy entries where necessary; never means the field is absent for every match outcome.

response_size_buckets_bytes.description: Allowed exact RFC 8785 JCS UTF-8 HTTP entity-body Content-Length buckets for PSI success and Class B failures. The phase uses the smallest bucket that can hold its maximal response shape for the advertised batch_item_count.

blind_response_bucket_bytes.description: Precomputed smallest allowed bucket that holds the largest RFC 8785 JCS body among the maximal legal blind success outcome and every allowed blind-phase Class B error projection for this configuration.

match_response_bucket_bytes.description: Precomputed smallest allowed bucket that holds the largest RFC 8785 JCS body among the maximal legal match success outcome and every allowed match-phase Class B error projection for this batch_item_count and handoff_stubs_mode.

batch_completion_ttl_seconds.description: Exact acceptance interval measured from successful blind admission. The provider retains the pinned key epoch, request bindings and cached outcomes throughout this interval; at or after admission_time + this value it rejects the batch as psi_batch_unavailable.

anti_enumeration_delay.description: Origin-side delay distribution shared by success and Class B paths for the same phase, sampled only after authentication and syntax validation.

restricted_query_proof.description: Whether the directory requires holder-approved proof for restricted or privacy-sensitive query classes.

ingest_modes.description: Directory ingest modes supported by this instance.

accept_policy_kind.description: Directory resource acceptance policy advertised by ak.find.directory.read.describe.

accept_policy_ref.description: Optional human-readable or governance reference describing how a resource obtains directory acceptance.

default_ttl_seconds.description: Default directory entry TTL in seconds.

max_ttl_seconds.description: Maximum accepted directory entry TTL in seconds.

revalidation_grace_seconds.description: Grace period for refreshing indexed resources after TTL expiry.

accepted_resource_kinds.description: Subset of resource kinds accepted by this directory instance.

accepted_did_methods.description: Principal/governance DID methods accepted by this directory instance.

takedown_contact.description: Operator takedown notification or appeal contact, expressed as a DID or URL.

rate_limits.description: Readable per-DID, per-organization or per-IP directory quota limits.

implemented_features.description: feature_ids the service has implementation code for but does NOT necessarily claim conformance for. Tooling that builds a conformance matrix MUST treat this strictly weaker than `claimed_profiles`.

claimed_profiles.description: Profiles the service self-claims membership in. `claim_kind` MUST be `self_claimed`; verified-only assertions belong under `verified_profiles` and MUST NOT appear here.

verified_profiles.description: Profiles for which a Conformance Verifier run (conformance-suite.md §6.2) has produced a passing verification artifact. Each entry MUST identify the verification run, artifact hash, artifact retrieval reference, verifier DID, verifier signature, and verification timestamp. When the service is in `development_mode=true` this array MUST be empty.

artifact_ref.description: URI or transparency-log reference from which the verification artifact can be fetched.

verifier_service_id.description: Stable did_core_id of the Conformance Verifier that signed the artifact statement. The artifact's full DID URL signing key is verified separately and its canonical bare full_id MUST project through the registered adapter to this value.

signature.description: Signature over profile_id, verification_run_id, artifact_digest, artifact_ref, verifier and timestamp.

experimental_features.description: feature_ids that the service exposes but explicitly does NOT promise stable interop for. Clients MUST treat these as non-load-bearing for protocol-level decisions.

compat_surfaces.description: Surfaces this service exposes outside its claimed Arkret v1 conformance: bridged third-party protocols and delegated resolver postures. A service MUST NOT declare its own product-private route root here — a private API is neither a bridged foreign protocol nor a delegation, and declaring one would grant it a conformance-adjacent standing it does not have. The object is closed so such a declaration cannot be smuggled in through extension keys.

kind.description: matrix_passthrough / mimi_passthrough: bridged foreign protocol surface. delegated_resolver: a DID document / key-log surface served on behalf of a canonical authority this service does not claim to be (conformance-profiles.md §9). external_interop: any other non-Arkret interop surface. This list is exhaustive; product-private APIs have no member here.

development_mode.description: Mirror of the service's development_mode flag. When true, `verified_profiles` MUST be empty.

allOf.$comment: A service that claims or verifies a calendar profile MUST publish the TZDB releases it can execute; see zh/models/calendar-event.md.

cidr.description: IPv4 or IPv6 CIDR string. Parsability and address-family semantics are enforced by the egress policy evaluator.

origin.description: Absolute origin of the client-visible Account Authority.

gate_account_base.description: Absolute base URL from which all client-visible /_arkret/gate/account/* endpoints MUST be derived.

schemas/service-operation-dtos.schema.js.title: Arkret Service Operation DTOs
schemas/service-operation-dtos.schema.js.description: Canonical request and response DTOs for service operations. OpenAPI components reference this artifact so SDK and conformance tooling use one schema source.

revoked.description: Whether a live device session was revoked.

redirect_url.description: Deployment-controlled browser handoff URL. This outcome MUST NOT contain SessionGrantOutcome, ak.session.grant, or Principal local session material; client-visible grant issuance is only via SessionGrantRequestBody.proof.proof_kind=oidc_code_exchange.

ActorAggregateFrontierView.description: Read-only actor history aggregate. It has no single sequence or head and cannot be used for Event authoring.

realms.description: Visible Realm frontiers sorted by realm_id with no duplicate realm_id.

grant_chain_terminated.description: Whether the grant rotation chain is now unable to refresh, including the already-terminated idempotent case.

auth_session_logged_out.description: Whether the underlying Auth-side browser/auth session is now logged out, including the already-logged-out idempotent case.

AuthSessionLogoutRequestBody.description: Service-to-service Account Authority to Auth Server request that logs out the Auth-side session owning a ak.session.grant rotation chain.

grant_jwt.description: Session grant used to locate the Auth-side session and its rotation chain.

logout_request_digest.description: Optional digest of the validated client-visible account /logout request that caused this S2S sub-operation.

validated_at.description: When the Account Authority validated the client-visible account /logout request.

reason_code.description: Reason for logging out the Auth-side session. v1 defines only account_logout for this S2S sub-operation.

AuthorizationLeaseIssueIntent.description: Typed authorization target for a registered non-Event operation. The issuer rederives the current authority policy from the accepted basis; this object is not itself an authorization.

AuthorizationLeaseIssueOutcome.description: One authority-issued publication lease per requested Event, preserving request order.

AuthorizationLeaseIssueRequest.description: Exactly one non-empty target array: final signed Events for publication pre-admission, or typed non-Event operation intents. Mixed requests are forbidden.

AuthzCheckOutcome.description: ak.self.authz.read.check diagnostic/preflight decision. See zh/authz/capabilities.md §18. This shape may include freshness and obligation hints, but any obligation that affects reducer admission or external state MUST be re-issued and signed through PolicyCheckOutcome.

decision.description: `allow` / `hard_deny` are terminal decisions. `soft_deny` is an evaluated policy soft refusal. `quarantine` / `require_review` are Policy Server-mediated soft outcomes (the request enters async review). Transient dependency or freshness failures are reported through `freshness_state`, `reason_code`, and `retry_after_ms`, not as policy decision values.

freshness_state.description: Frontier freshness classification for revocation-sensitive decisions; see zh/authz/capabilities.md §18.2.

last_known_frontier_age_ms.description: Age of the newest revocation/auth frontier evidence used for this decision. Present when freshness_state is stale or unknown.

notary_status.description: Coarse status of the notary/frontier source used to diagnose stale or unknown revocation freshness.

reason_code.description: Registered reason code. High-risk stale or unknown revocation freshness returns revocation_freshness_unknown.

retry_after_ms.description: Set when `freshness_state ∈ {stale,unknown}` or a retryable `reason_code` is present; client SHOULD back off this amount before retry.

obligations.description: Policy server obligations (challenge / rate_limit / drop_attachment) the caller MUST satisfy before the action proceeds.

AuthzCheckRequestBody.description: ak.self.authz.read.check input — local capability projection / preflight / diagnostic query. `resource` is optional because some actions (e.g. `ak.realm.create`, identity-scoped actions) have no Realm-bound target. The result is not a signed Policy Server decision and MUST NOT be used as Event auth_context, reducer accept proof, or cross-service authorization fact; dynamic policy obligations use ak.self.policy.read.check.

actor_id.description: Subject did_core_id whose authorization is being checked.

resource.description: Optional resource selector (Realm / Strand / Space / Morph / etc.).

context.description: Optional decision context — claim presentations, frontier reference, request metadata.

url.description: Fully-qualified URL clients can pass to browser primitives. Contains the `presign` query parameter, `blob_ref`, and a presign envelope bound to `realm_id` for Realm-owned blobs.

expires_at.description: Server-determined expiry; SHOULD be earlier than `now() + max_age_seconds`.

blob_ref.description: Target blob. MUST be a content-addressed ref or visible blob metadata id.

realm_id.description: Realm binding for Realm-owned blobs. Servers MUST include the same realm_id in the presign envelope and reject mismatches with blob metadata; only deployment-public/global blobs may omit this field.

max_age_seconds.description: Client-requested TTL upper bound. Server clamps to the smaller of this value, the issuing grant's `blob_presign_max_ttl_seconds` constraint, and the deployment-level cap.

purpose.description: Intended rendering / download mode. Servers MAY apply purpose-specific Content-Disposition or rate limits.

backend_token.description: Opaque to Arkret protocol; type-specific (e.g. LiveKit JWT).

participant_identity.description: SFU-local short handle, scope `(call_id, focus_id, sfu_did)`. UUIDv7-form rtc_participant typed ID.

backend_kind.description: Backend binding type identifier (livekit / arkret_native / etc.).

device_id.description: Stable protocol endpoint identifier. REQUIRED for agent_key_proof and covered by request_canonical_digest; the Account Authority MUST persist and return the same value in the issued grant so Principal Servers can bind MLS KeyPackage ownership, Welcome routing, consume/revoke operations, refresh, and restart recovery to one endpoint. It MUST NOT be derived from a session or grant id.

decisions.description: Verified signed decision chain in ascending defer_count order. Signed-reject is terminal and therefore does not remain in pending_proposals.

retained_faults.description: Deadline faults retained after a late but otherwise valid Seal is accepted. Sorted by (accepted_at, proposal_digest); this is evidence derived from the signed chain, not a second finality source.

message_id.description: Sender-assigned stable identity copied unchanged into DeviceMessageEnvelope.message_id. Reusing the same sender-scoped message_id with different canonical target content MUST fail with duplicate_conflict (reason message_id_conflict).

ok.description: True when the acknowledgement was accepted, including the legal no-op case of re-acking the same or an older token (the acknowledged position MUST NOT move backward).

pruned_count.description: Number of queued messages actually deleted by this acknowledgement.

ack_token.description: Acknowledgement token previously issued to the same (principal_id, device_id) via an account subscribe to_device batch or a device_messages get page. Acknowledgement is cumulative and monotonic: the server prunes all delivered messages up to and including the token's bound queue position. Unknown / expired / cross-bound tokens MUST be rejected with invalid_param (reason invalid_ack_token) without deleting anything. Naturally idempotent; no Idempotency-Key required.

messages.description: DeviceMessageEnvelope items; not Event Envelope objects. This endpoint does not serve the durable Event timeline.

ack_token.description: Server-issued opaque acknowledgement token, REQUIRED whenever messages[] is non-empty. Covers this page plus all previously delivered messages for the authenticated device. Queue deletion happens only through ak.self.device_messages.command.ack with this token, never through the after= read cursor (client-sync.md §10.1).

next_cursor.description: Read-only continuation position; advancing it MUST NOT delete queued messages.

lost.description: SHOULD be true when unacknowledged messages were dropped (expiry or capacity) since the device's last acknowledged position; clients SHOULD trigger key recovery paths.

accepted_at.description: Stable registry decision time for this exact accepted or duplicate operation. A duplicate returns the original acceptance time.

seq.description: New method sequence number when available.

did_method.description: DID method discriminator without the did: prefix (e.g. web, webvh, key). It MUST exactly equal the method component of did; verifiers dispatch method-specific validation only after that equality check.

seq.description: Optional method sequence number when the DID method exposes one.

prev_event_digest.description: Optional previous operation hash / key-log head, when required by the DID method.

operation.description: Complete DID method-native operation, including every controller/update/recovery proof required by that method. This is not a generic JSON Patch. The selected adapter MUST validate the immutable native operation and its full history before any state mutation; transport authentication never substitutes for method-native control proof.

DirectConversationFounderBasisEvidence.description: Closed XOR authorization evidence for one Direct Conversation founding unit, matching the two registered ak.realm.create admission variants. The human branch feeds direct_conversation_genesis; the controller_agent branch feeds direct_conversation_agent_genesis. Carrying both, neither, or mixed branch fields rejects the whole unit.

basis_evidence_bundle.description: Portable evidence for the pair's current Contact basis. The verifier re-derives founder from the root basis, never from this current basis.

root_basis_continuity_chain.description: Ordered tombstone/recontact predecessors from the current basis back to the pair's unique root founder basis, each linked by previous_terminal_basis_id. An empty array means the current basis is itself the root. A break, a cycle, multiple roots or two directional proofs yielding different roots reject the unit.

DirectConversationFoundingAcceptanceOutc.description: Closed outcome of the direct_conversation_founding request branch. status is accepted for the first admission of this unit and duplicate for a byte-identical replay; partial is structurally impossible because the unit is atomic. A slot already closed by a different unit for the same pair returns the slot_already_committed error instead of this outcome.

event_ids.description: The three accepted Event IDs in the same wire order as the request. They are the exact preimage of receipt.founding_unit_digest.

DirectConversationFoundingFederationSubm.description: Direct Conversation founding exception branch of ak.peer.events.command.submit (zh/sync/federation.md section 4.0.4). The Realm does not yet exist at the receiver, so no ordinary federation_peer authority and no Realm-scoped service_binding_ref can be computed; destination binding comes from the section 3 service DID and trust-domain headers plus the source acceptance receipt. This is a registered atomic unit: a missing bounded dependency returns top-level HTTP 409 dependency_missing with zero writes and never a per-item partial.

events.description: The same three founder-signed Events in the same fixed wire order, byte-identical to what the source accepted.

source_service_binding.description: Portable accepted-at binding for source_acceptance_receipt. binding_digest MUST equal receipt.issuer_service_binding_digest, service_id MUST equal receipt.issuer_service_id and authenticated Source-Service-ID, principal_id MUST equal receipt.founder_id, and authority_instance MUST equal the Contact basis frozen instance. Another same-core PCR is rejected.

signer_key_evidence.description: Source-Principal-Server attestation of the founder device keys needed to verify the three original Event proofs. Transport-only evidence covered by the outer HTTP Message Signature.

DirectConversationFoundingUnitSubmission.description: Caller-authored Direct Conversation founding unit submitted to the founder's current Principal Server. The founder authors all three Events itself: realm_id is retype(events[0] Event ID) and main_strand_id is retype(events[2] Event ID), so no party can allocate either coordinate before the canonical preimage exists. The service never allocates, replaces or renegotiates an ID; it only verifies the unit, CAS-closes its local (founder_id, trust_domain_id, pair_key) slot and accepts zero or three Events atomically. See zh/identity/contact-and-direct-conversation.md sections 5.5 and 6.1.

unit_kind.description: Explicit discriminator. Ordinary single and batch submissions forbid this property, so the three request branches are an exact XOR.

idempotency_key.description: Caller-chosen key. The same key with the same founding unit replays the byte-identical receipt without advancing accepted_at; the same key with a different unit is duplicate_conflict with zero writes.

events.description: Exactly three founder-signed Events in fixed wire order: ak.realm.create with an omitted realm_id and a realm_genesis scope_ref, the peer participant's ak.member.state{join}, then ak.strand.create with an omitted strand_id. Reordering, a fourth Event, a missing member join and a missing Strand each reject the whole unit.

source_service_binding.description: Founder-authorized accepted-at binding for the current Principal Server. principal_id MUST equal events[0].event.actor_id, service_id MUST equal the receiving service, and accepted_at MUST be live and no later than the slot transaction. The service verifies both proofs and uses this binding_digest verbatim in its acceptance receipt; it MUST NOT synthesize the principal proof.

cba_proof_bundles.description: Optional receiver-relative dependency bundles for the unit's seal_ref or seal_basis leaves. Bundles are transport evidence, not Event fields.

DirectoryGovernanceProof.description: Single resource-governance authorization proof for directory write surfaces (withdraw, takedown_appeal). Reuses the generic non-Event detached-JWS wire leaf while closing audience, purpose, and domain choices for this object family; canonical binding, signer authority, and freshness rules are defined in discovery-directory.md section 8.7.1.

discovery_event.description: The accepted ak.{kind}.discovery Event itself, delivered in its original signed form exactly as peer contact delivery carries the original ak.contact.* Event. kind MUST correspond to resource_kind and the Event's own proofs carry the resource governance signature, so no second signed copy of the same fact is defined (discovery-directory.md 8.3).

DirectoryTakedownAppealOutcome.description: Signed decision receipt acknowledging an appeal submission per discovery-directory.md §8.7 step 3.

appeal_id.description: Directory-local audit reference for the appeal; not a registered ak:<kind> typed ID.

decision_receipt.description: Signed Directory decision receipt; status pending until adjudicated.

DirectoryTakedownAppealRequestBody.description: Resource-side appeal packet against an operator takedown; the bound fields and governance signature are normative per discovery-directory.md §8.7.

takedown_id.description: The operator takedown_id from the takedown notice.

argument_digest.description: Digest of the appeal argument / evidence bundle (sha256:<hex>).

governance_proof.description: Signature by the resource governance key or an authorized advocate, equivalent strength to withdraw.governance_proof; wire form and binding per discovery-directory.md section 8.7.1.

withdrawal_ref.description: Directory-local audit reference for the withdrawal; not a registered ak:<kind> typed ID.

governance_proof.description: Signature proof by the resource governance key, equivalent strength to announce.discovery_state.proof; wire form and binding per discovery-directory.md section 8.7.1.

EventFederationSubmission.description: Event publication transported between peers. Online federation carries an empty ingress_receipts array and no authorization_lease; explicit delayed/offline federation carries its lease and one or more lease-bound receipts. The receiving peer independently revalidates the Event, current admission, optional delayed evidence and CBA closure.

control_proposal_ack.description: Canonical external-authority receipt set for a federated Control Move. Forbidden for DataEvents.

EventInitialSubmission.description: Initial durable Event publication. Online submission requires only the complete signed Event and performs current-state admission atomically. authorization_lease is optional and valid only for an explicitly requested delayed/offline publication window. Lease and dependency bundles are excluded from the Event digest.

cba_proof_bundles.description: Optional receiver-relative dependency bundles for the Event seal_ref or seal_basis. Bundles are transport evidence, not Event fields.

control_proposal_ack.description: Required external-authority receipt set when a Control Move is submitted to a receiver that cannot itself produce the complete current authority quorum. Forbidden for DataEvents.

EventReadRow.description: A readable event item. Complete EventEnvelope is the only reducer input shape. RedactedEventView and ReferenceLockedEventStub are projection/completeness evidence for callers that may know the source event exists but may not receive its full canonical payload bytes.

EventSealSubmitOutcome.description: Result of ak.self.events.command.submit_seal after full Seal and active-device verification.

accepted_event_digests.description: The Control Events this Seal accepted, as a set: byte-wise ascending and unique, the same normalization Seal.delta carries. Order MUST NOT be read as reducer apply order, which is causal-then-digest-descending and is not observable on this response; a client comparing this array against its own submission order or against a server's apply order is comparing two different sequences.

allOf.description: Actor-supplied ak.self.events.command.submit input envelope. It reuses the base Event shape, including the required producer-signed scope_ref, and forbids the sole reducer-stamped Event field actor_kind. Object payload schemas independently forbid actor-supplied effective_scope where that name is reserved for a read-only materialized object projection.

EventView.description: Result of ak.self.events.resource.get — a single complete Event Envelope, RedactedEventView, or ReferenceLockedEventStub with optional visibility / receipt hints. Redacted / locked variants are projection-only evidence and MUST NOT be used as reducer input.

visibility.description: Caller-visible policy hint for this event (history visibility class, E2EE envelope class).

receipts.description: Event batch receipts witnessing this event, if visible.

EventsActorCasConflictProblem.description: Closed details for an authenticated, visible actor-chain cas_conflict that proves the submitted Event was not accepted and its signed basis is stale.

EventsDependencyMissingProblem.description: Closed ErrorEnvelope.error.details for an atomic federation unit rejected with top-level dependency_missing. The unit performed zero Event, Seal, reducer, projection, or frontier writes.

EventsFrontierAccountClientState.description: Account-client ak.self.events.read.frontier response. For a managed Agent PCR whose accepted Events are ahead of its accepted Seal, frontier remains the last accepted controller-device-signed Seal and receipts includes `{kind: ak.managed_agent_pcr.seal_head.v1, seal: Seal}` so the controller can author the successor; the service must never synthesize that device Seal.

EventsFrontierFederationPeerState.description: Federation peer ak.peer.events.read.frontier response. Requires S2S signed trust-domain headers.

heads.description: Current federation-visible head Event IDs for this Realm.

max_hlc.description: Maximum HLC observed by the issuer at this frontier, when available.

frontier_root.description: Hash commitment returned to an authorized federation peer.

actor_seq_upper_bounds.description: Per-actor sequence upper bounds returned to an authorized federation peer.

witness_receipts.description: Optional witness or receipt-service attestations over the observed frontier.

signature.description: Service signature over the peer frontier response.

EventsQueryOutcome.description: Result of ak.self.events.read.scan. Ordering follows the "近邻先返回" rule unless `order` was explicitly set on the request; see service-http-binding.md §3.3.3.

prev_cursor.description: Absolute-direction cursor toward older events; pass to next request's `before=`.

next_cursor.description: Absolute-direction cursor toward newer events; pass to next request's `after=`.

has_more.description: True if more events remain in the `prev_cursor` (older) direction; SHOULD ignore `next_cursor` direction (subscribe / poll instead).

range_completeness.description: Optional. Present only when the request set include_completeness=true, the service advertises events_query_range_completeness, and at least one ak.attestation.range_completeness attestation covers the returned page's range (service-http-binding.md §3.3.6). Absence means the range is un-attested — neither an error nor a completeness confirmation. Clients verify per operations-sync.md §6.4.4 (root recompute, actor_seq_ranges check, witness_disagreement fail-closed).

attestation_refs.description: Event ids of ak.attestation.range_completeness events whose union of scopes covers the returned page. Over-coverage is legal; clients intersect scopes during verification.

attestations.description: Optional inline complete ak.attestation.range_completeness EventEnvelope objects for the referenced attestations. Every inline event's event_id MUST appear in attestation_refs and clients MUST verify the EventEnvelope signature / event_digest before using its payload. Servers MAY omit this field and let clients backfill the attestation events by id.

EventsQueryPostRequestBody.description: QUERY content for ak.self.events.read.scan and ak.peer.events.read.scan.

realms.description: Filter by Realm IDs. UNION within, intersection with `actors[]`.

actors.description: Filter by Actor DIDs. UNION within, intersection with `realms[]`.

before.description: Return events strictly older than this cursor position (exclusive).

after.description: Return events strictly newer than this cursor position (exclusive).

order.description: Same semantics as the GET form `order` query parameter.

include_completeness.description: Request range-completeness attestation references covering the returned page (service-http-binding.md §3.3.6). Only effective when the service advertises events_query_range_completeness in supported_features; services that do not advertise it MUST ignore this parameter.

EventsResolveOutcome.description: ak.self.events.read.resolve result. `events[]`, optional `seals[]`, and `missing[]` plus optional `unauthorized[]` form a partition of the requested selectors.

seals.description: Accepted Seals covering the returned Events: for each Event, the Seal whose delta[] contains that Event's event_digest. Deduplicated and sorted by Seal id; an Event that is accepted but not yet sealed contributes nothing and the service MUST NOT substitute a later descendant Seal. Supplying a Seal here is not an assertion of trust: a client bootstrapping an MLS governance anchor still has to verify the candidate itself under zh/crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md section 2.5.4.

missing.description: IDs / hashes that were requested but do not exist or are not visible (indistinguishable per visibility rules).

unauthorized.description: Optional split of missing into a separately-named bucket when policy explicitly distinguishes auth failure from non-existence.

EventsResolveRequestBody.description: ak.self.events.read.resolve request body. At least one of event_ids, event_digests, or seal_refs MUST be non-empty.

seal_refs.description: Exact Seal references needed to verify control state and construct publication evidence.

EventsSubmitBatchRequestBody.description: Batch ak.self.events.command.submit request used by account clients.

EventsSubmitFederationBatchRequestBody.description: Ordinary Realm-scoped federation service-to-service ak.peer.events.command.submit request body.

events.description: One Realm-scoped federation transaction. Every nested event.realm_id MUST equal service_binding_ref.realm_id. Control-plane Events MUST precede data-plane Events; relative order within each phase is preserved.

cba_proof_bundles.description: Receiver-relative CBA dependency bundles rooted at nested Events' seal_ref or seal_basis leaves. Each bundle MAY be a bounded verifiable superset; the receiver independently validates all objects and reports exact missing dependencies.

signer_key_evidence.description: Source-Principal-Server attestation of active participant device keys needed to verify original Event proofs. This transport-only evidence is covered by the outer HTTP Message Signature and never changes the Event envelope.

agent_signer_evidence_bundle.description: Portable Native Agent signer evidence for transported Events. The bundle uses the same typed DTO as client sync and is covered by the outer HTTP Message Signature without changing Event canonical bytes.

EventsSubmitFederationRequestBody.description: Closed request union for ak.peer.events.command.submit. The ordinary branch carries a Realm-scoped federation transaction; the direct_conversation_founding branch carries the Direct Conversation founding exception and is discriminated by unit_kind, which the ordinary branch forbids through additionalProperties:false.

EventsSubmitOutcome.description:
Result of ak.events.submit. Tracks per-event acceptance / duplication /
rejection along with the post-write frontier and an optional barrier
cursor for read-your-writes.

accepted.description: Event IDs that entered the accepted set for the first time. Idempotent re-submissions of identical bodies are sealed via duplicate[], not re-listed here.

ingress_receipts.description: Newly issued or byte-identical previously issued receipts for accepted/duplicate Event digests. A service MUST return the stored receipt for an idempotent duplicate; it MUST NOT mint a receipt with a later received_at.

control_proposal_acks.description: Signed bounded-decision receipts for accepted or duplicate Control Move proposal digests. A duplicate MUST return the originally stored byte-identical receipt; a service MUST NOT mint later deadlines. DataEvents never appear in this array.

duplicate.description: Event IDs whose canonical bytes matched a prior accepted event (idempotent no-op).

quarantine.description: Event IDs deferred to async / human verification.

realm_actor_frontiers.description: Post-submit authoring frontiers for accepted or duplicate Events, sorted and unique by (realm_id, actor_id).

realm_frontiers.description: Visible post-submit Realm Seal frontiers sorted and unique by realm_id.

cursor.description: Optional barrier cursor (purpose=barrier) bound to the most recently accepted event.

original_outcome.description: Present only when status="historical_only" (idempotency-cache replay after origin key revoke / binding or peer-policy change, see sync/federation.md section 8.5.1): carries the originally cached outcome verbatim as historical diagnostics. The nested outcome's status MUST NOT be "historical_only"; the top-level accepted[] MUST be empty in that case. Absent for all other status values.

EventsSubmitRejectedItem.description: One rejected submission. When the reason is a missing CBA dependency the receiver reports the exact shortfall so the sender can extend one bundle instead of guessing; a bundle MAY be a bounded verifiable superset, so the receiver never asks for a byte-minimal bundle.

index.description: 0-based position of the rejected item in the request events[] array. Present when the item could be located positionally, which is the only way to report an item whose id failed to parse.

missing_event_ids.description: Exact Event IDs required by prev_refs, causal_refs, or another signed reference. Present only for dependency_missing.

missing_seal_refs.description: Exact Seals the receiver still needs to close this Event's seal_ref or seal_basis leaves. Required whenever the rejection is a dependency shortfall; each retry round MUST strictly shrink this set.

missing_event_digests.description: Exact control-plane Event digests the receiver still needs. Same shrinking obligation as missing_seal_refs.

EventsSubmitRequestBody.description: Closed request union for ak.self.events.command.submit. The single and batch branches carry ordinary Events; the direct_conversation_founding branch is the only carrier for the Direct Conversation founding unit and is discriminated by unit_kind, which the other two branches forbid through additionalProperties:false.

EventsSubmitResponseBody.description: Closed response union for ak.self.events.command.submit. Ordinary submissions return EventsSubmitOutcome; the direct_conversation_founding request branch returns DirectConversationFoundingAcceptanceOutcome, which carries the source-signed founding acceptance receipt.

FederationServiceBindingRef.description:
Request-level service binding snapshot carried by federation
service-to-service ak.peer.events.command.submit calls. This is metadata for the
receiver to verify the sender's delivery decision; client writes omit it.

IdentityDocumentView.description: Result of ak.root.identity.document.resource.get — current DID Document plus normalized view hints.

did_document.description: Raw DID Core document with W3C field names preserved.

normalized_view.description:
Optional Arkret normalized principal view (snake_case) — derived
projection only, NOT a re-publishable DID Document. See
zh/identity/identity-did.md §6.

method_evidence.description: Closed adapter-discriminated proof material (e.g. did:webvh history head and canonical witness receipt). This is the registered supply surface for portable principal resolution evidence.

IdentityLogListOutcome.description: Result of ak.root.identity.log.read.list. Entries are returned in the DID method's own native log form: for did:webvh each entry is a verbatim did.jsonl log entry with its native versionId, entryHash chain and Data Integrity proof. Arkret defines no parallel entry envelope, sequence numbering, hash chain or proof transcript over DID logs — the method already provides all of them, and a second signed representation of the same history could disagree with the first. Methods without a native history (did:web) MUST report that rather than being wrapped in a shape that implies one.

method.description: DID method of the returned log, e.g. did:webvh. Consumers dispatch parsing and verification on this value.

native_history.description: False when the method has no native key history at all (did:web). Such a response MUST return an empty entries array; the server MUST NOT synthesise entries, sequence numbers or a chain the method does not have.

entries.description: Verbatim method-native log entries in method order. Arkret does not reinterpret, renumber or re-sign them; verification follows the method specification.

next_cursor.description: Opaque continuation cursor for the next page when has_more=true.

IdentityReceiptListOutcome.description: Result of ak.root.identity.receipts.read.list. receipts[] is a tagged union over two distinct object families discriminated by their schema constant: ak.schema.identity_receipt.v1 records a role inside a DID registry consensus group (writer / witness / replica) and binds seq + head_event_digest, while ak.schema.did_webvh_witness_receipt.v1 records a did:webvh method witness observed at a specific versionId. The two say different things with the same English word, so the discriminator is mandatory and a verifier MUST branch on it rather than infer intent from which optional fields happen to be present.

threshold_met.description: True when the returned receipt set satisfies the effective witness threshold for the requested head. The effective threshold is the strictest intersection of the method-native parameters.witness.threshold and the deployment / Realm policy minimum (identity-did.md §3.4.2), and distinctness is counted over controlling_organization where policy requires distinct organizations. Omitted when the registry cannot evaluate threshold policy for this query; an omitted value MUST NOT be read as true. A true value is an Arkret-layer convenience and MUST NOT replace verifying the standard did-witness.json proofs.

InitialSessionGrantRequest.description: Initial Standard SessionGrant intent embedded in identity_creation registration. It reuses the DPoP holder key established by account handoff; Account Authority recomputes RFC 7638 thumbprint of session_public_key and requires equality with the handoff/control-proof dpop_jkt. It is not a separate authorization or credential.

session_public_key.description: Exact RFC 8785 JCS public JWK for the existing handoff DPoP holder key. Private members are forbidden.

ManagedAgentPcrSealHeadReceipt.description: Accepted controller-device-signed managed Agent PCR Seal head returned when accepted Events are ahead of Seal coverage. The service relays this exact Seal and MUST NOT synthesize or sign it.

MlsGroupStateMaterialOutcome.description: Exact RFC 9420 public group-state material. *_bytes_b64 use unpadded base64url. Consumers MUST decode, hash raw bytes, compare both explicit digests and the hashes embedded in both ak:blob:sha256 refs, verify GroupInfo and ratchet_tree consistency, then derive leaf_index only from occupied leaves in the verified tree.

MlsGroupStateMaterialRequestBody.description: Read-only service request for the exact public MLS epoch-0 GroupInfo and ratchet_tree bytes committed by one accepted ak.mls.genesis Event. Every selector is copied from that Event; the receiver MUST resolve the Event and compare every field before returning bytes.

status.description: Stored submit outcome. Later queue resolution does not rewrite this response; exact replay returns the byte-identical submitted outcome.

routed_to.description: Stable core_ids selected as moderation routing destinations. MUST be omitted for an ordinary reporter and MAY be serialized only when the caller independently holds moderation/governance capability for the report's exact scope. Endpoint discovery and full-DID verification remain separate resolution steps.

OrganizationControlProof.description: Method-native proof that the caller controls the external Organization DID at the pinned version. proof_kind is a closed discriminator with exactly two members, both of which describe a MATURE, already-published DID. Creating a new Organization DID is a separate inception / governance ceremony and deliberately has no member here: a receiver must never have to guess whether a proof asserts control of existing state or creation of new state. This object never carries an Arkret-issued challenge signature in place of method-native control evidence.

proof_kind.description: resolved_verification_method: a single signature by a verification method that is in the organization DID's control relationship at version_id. governance_quorum: a threshold of signatures from the organization's governance key set. Witness attestation is neither of these and MUST NOT be substituted for control evidence (identity-did.md §8.1).

quorum_threshold.description: Required when proof_kind=governance_quorum and forbidden otherwise. The number of distinct valid governance signatures the organization's own policy demands. proofs[] MUST contain at least this many entries signed by distinct verification methods; JSON Schema cannot compare the two, so the receiver MUST enforce it and fail closed when short.

proofs.description: Detached proofs over canonical_json({context:'ak.organization-registration-control-proof-v1', challenge_id, organization_id, full_id, local_admin_subject, version_id, log_head_digest, verification_method, created_at}). The verifier independently validates the published full_id and requires project(full_id)=organization_id before checking the full DID URL verification_method. Binding the challenge, stable core, full DID, beneficiary admin and exact version together prevents replay across deployments, resolutions or beneficiaries.

OrganizationRegistrationChallenge.description: Single-use control challenge. Every binding field exists to close one replay path: purpose separates this proof from any other signature the organization makes, audience and trust_domain pin it to this deployment, origin pins the HTTP surface, nonce makes it unrepeatable, and the expiry window bounds how long a captured proof stays useful. A registry MUST consume the challenge on the first successful use and atomically persist (challenge_id, canonical_request_digest, outcome). Only a byte-identical retry may return that stored outcome; the same challenge with any different digest is invalid.

full_id.description: Current published bare DID for the external organization. The registry MUST independently validate it and require the registered method adapter to project it to organization_id before issuing the challenge.

purpose.description: Fixed purpose tag, identical to the signing context of OrganizationControlProof.proofs[]. A proof produced for any other purpose MUST NOT verify here.

audience.description: Stable service did_core_id of the issuing registry. A proof bound to one registry MUST NOT be accepted by another; the proof verification method remains a full DID URL projected to this value by the registered method adapter.

local_admin_subject.description: The local principal the requested scopes will be delegated to. It is fixed at challenge time and signed over by the control proof, because a proof that binds only the organization and the version says nothing about who benefits from it: anyone who obtained such a proof could submit ensure naming themselves and receive the organization's administrative scopes. ensure MUST reject a request whose local_admin_subject differs from the one in the referenced challenge.

expires_at.description: MUST be at most 300 seconds after created_at. A longer window buys nothing and widens the interval in which a captured proof remains usable.

OrganizationRegistrationChallengeRequest.description: Request a single-use control challenge for an external Organization DID. Two phases are mandatory: the registry issues the challenge and remembers it, then the caller proves control against it. Folding this into ensure would let the caller supply its own challenge, at which point neither freshness nor single use can be established by the receiver.

organization_id.description: Stable did_core_id of the external Organization to be registered. Resolvability alone confers nothing; this request only opens a proof window.

full_id.description: Current published bare DID submitted for first registration. The registry MUST independently resolve and validate it and require project(full_id)=organization_id.

local_admin_subject.description: The local principal the requested scopes will be delegated to. It is fixed at challenge time and signed over by the control proof, because a proof that binds only the organization and the version says nothing about who benefits from it: anyone who obtained such a proof could submit ensure naming themselves and receive the organization's administrative scopes. ensure MUST reject a request whose local_admin_subject differs from the one in the referenced challenge.

OrganizationRegistrationEnsureRequestBod.description: Register an external Organization identity with this deployment by submitting both its stable organization_id core and current published full_id. Idempotent on organization_id: replaying the same registration returns the existing binding with created=false. This operation registers a reference and a local administrative binding; it does not host the DID's method history, does not make this deployment its controller, and does not create Realm state.

full_id.description: Current published bare DID whose method history and control proof are pinned by this request. MUST equal the full_id bound into the referenced challenge and project to organization_id.

version_id.description: The exact resolved DID version the control proof was made against. Pinning the version is what makes the receipt auditable later: without it, a receipt asserts control at an unknown point in the DID's history.

local_admin_subject.description: The local principal the requested scopes are delegated to. MUST equal the value bound into the referenced challenge and signed over by control_proof; a mismatch means the proof was made for a different beneficiary and MUST be rejected with organization_registration_challenge_invalid.

requested_scopes.description: MUST be identical to the set carried by the referenced challenge; a mismatch means the proof was made for different authority than is being claimed.

handle_attestation.description: Optional supporting attestation only. An organization handle or domain claim may improve discovery and display, but MUST NOT substitute for DID control or quorum proof: whoever operates a domain is not thereby the controller of the organization's DID. Named attestation rather than evidence because it carries exactly one material family (common-fields.md R6).

subject.description: Stable organization did_core_id the handle is claimed for. MUST equal organization_id; the attestation proof's full DID URL is independently projected to its issuer did_core_id.

status.description: The issuer's assertion at signing time. It is a floor, not a guarantee: a receiver MUST still consult the issuer's current revocation state before relying on the handle for display, because a self-asserted active is exactly what a revoked attestation would also carry.

OrganizationRegistrationOutcome.description: Result of every organization registration command and of the read surface. organization_id, registration_generation and version_id MUST exactly equal the corresponding fields inside registration_receipt. created is true exactly on a call that opened a new generation, so an idempotent replay is distinguishable from first establishment or replacement without comparing receipts; JSON Schema cannot express these cross-field invariants, so receivers and conformance runners MUST enforce them.

full_id.description: Published bare DID recorded by registration_receipt. MUST project to organization_id.

registration_generation.description: Monotonic generation of the binding for this organization_id, starting at 1. The organization did_core_id stays the stable key while full_id may refresh within that identity; terminal states are per generation. Revoke ends generation N, and a later ensure opens generation N+1 rather than reviving N or colliding with it. ensure that changes local_admin_subject or the scope set also opens a new generation.

created.description: True exactly when this call opened a new generation: the first registration, a re-registration after revoke, or an ensure that changed local_admin_subject or the scope set. False for a byte-identical ensure retry that matches the consumed challenge's canonical_request_digest and stored outcome, and for every read, refresh and revoke. Reusing the challenge with a different digest is an error, not created=false.

OrganizationRegistrationReceipt.description: Provider-signed record that this deployment accepted an external Organization DID binding. receipt_claims is exactly the object formed by removing registration_receipt_id and proof from the receipt; registration_receipt_id is ak:organization-registration-receipt:<lowercase hex SHA-256(canonical_json(receipt_claims))>. proof.payload_digest hashes the complete receipt after registration_receipt_id is inserted and proof is removed, so neither digest is self-referential. proof is a detached JWS over the ak.organization-registration-receipt-proof-v1 binding object. The receipt proves acceptance of one generation of one local binding and nothing else: it is not a Realm capability, not membership, not a notary designation, and not a service delegation.

registration_receipt_id.description: ak:organization-registration-receipt: plus lowercase hex SHA-256(canonical_json(receipt with registration_receipt_id and proof both omitted)).

full_id.description: Published bare DID whose pinned version and control proof were accepted for this receipt. Consumers MUST independently validate it and require project(full_id)=organization_id.

registration_generation.description: Monotonic generation of the binding for this stable organization did_core_id, starting at 1. A same-core full_id refresh does not create a different organization identity; terminal registration states remain per generation.

control_proof_kind.description: Mirrors OrganizationControlProof.proof_kind so a later auditor can tell which commitment control_key_digest is over without re-fetching the original request.

control_key_digest.description: Under resolved_verification_method, the digest of the active control/update public key at version_id. Under governance_quorum, the digest of the canonical governance key set head that satisfied the threshold. It is never a next-key commitment and never private material.

status.description: Closed lifecycle. active: control evidence is current. stale: the pinned version no longer reflects current control (controller rotation) or the evidence has aged out; low-risk reads may continue but high-risk paths MUST fail closed until a successful refresh. revoked: terminal for this generation, whether withdrawn locally, atomically superseded by a new generation, or forced by deactivation of the external DID.
